**Guaranteed Drop:** Auriza Hero's Grave

  - The player has to navigate the side section that begins in the pit towards the end of the dungeon and trigger a Flame Pillar found at the end of said side section. This will move a statue of Rosus perched on top of said pillar that projects a teleporter sigil into the middle of the hallway where the two chariots patrolling side by side can be found. Causing the third chariot to teleport in the middle of their path, initiating a mass collision that destroys all of them in the process. The player will automatically receive this item (along with  the complete Tree Sentinel Set) in their inventory once the final chariot collides.
  - The player can also more easily trigger this flame pillar without needing to explore the side section. The moment they enter the hall with the two chariots, the player can use Margit's or Mohg's Shackle (as despite doing no direct damage, both of these items sport enormous hitboxes that ignore walls) allowing them to trigger the flame pillar without needing direct line of sight with said pillar.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The  is an optional boss in Elden Ring. It also appears as a field boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The antler-like horns of a long-lived stag continued budding long after death, over and over again, until the beast became an Ancestor Spirit. Ancestral Spirits are a phenomenon that exists beyond the purview of the Erdtree, following the principle that life sprouts from death, just as it does birth, granting power. Its horned remains are found at the southern Hallowhorn Grounds on the bank of the Siofra River, where it lies beneath the false night sky. Its large, antler-like horns sprouted small leafy plants that shone with light, infusing nearby Ancestral Followers with profound spirituality.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
- This boss is optional.
- Furled Fingers or Spirit Ashes can be summoned for this boss.
- Deals  Standard and  Magic damage

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- 13,000 runes
- Ancestral Follower Ashes

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
The horned remains of this Ancestor Spirit are found at the Hallowhorn Grounds in the lower section of the Siofra River, accessible via the Siofra River Well in Limgrave. This ruined structure is situated southeast of the  Siofra River Bank Site of Grace.

In order to face this boss, the player must first light **eight** beacons scattered throughout the area. Each beacon corresponds to a pillar flanking the staircase to the Hallowhorn Grounds. Once all signals are lit, the following message displays: **Power gathers somewhere in horned remains**. The horned remains will burned with blue spectral flames, and agreeing to **Touch horned remains** will grant a supernatural encounter with the spirit.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text:
- HP: 4,393
- Defense: 107
- Stance: 120
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- Cannot be parried
- Ancestor Spirit is scripted to absorb the souls of nearby animal spirits, gaining a new attack based on the aspect. It periodically die, rebirthing itself, losing the move.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: The Ancestor Spirit is able to jump up and hop while mid-air. It can produce a jet of blue spirit vapor from its mouth, both while on the ground and in the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating this boss for the first time unlocks the "Ancestor Spirit" achievement.
- This is the weaker version of the Regal Ancestor Spirit.
- Due to their similarities in design and behavior, Torrent may be a juvenile Ancestor Spirit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - In Norse mythology, four   eat among the branches of the world tree . According to the , the stags crane their necks upward to chomp at the branches. The morning dew gathers in their horns and forms the rivers of the world.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**"Homing Instinct"** is an info item and painting in Elden Ring.
Depicts a distant Minor Erdtree, framed by ancient ruins.

Leads to the Incantation Scarab headpiece.
__TOC__

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Limgrave
- Acquired from interacting with the painting found inside the Artist's Shack located on a hill, past the road north of Waypoint Ruins.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Allows the Player to perceive the soul of a painter and retrieve a unique item from their location.
The location being the point of perspective depicted by the painting itself.

The soul in question can be found near an arch of Ancient Ruins by the cliffs southeast of the First Step (or northwest from the Seaside Ruins) Site of Grace.

The painter is initially invisible when viewed from a distance but will eventually reveal themselves as the player gets physically closer to them. Successfully locating the spirit will make it dissipate before leaving the Incantation Scarab headpiece for the player to pick up from the ground.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This painting's name, "Homing Instinct" is likely a reference to Scarabs instinctively abandoning their rolled clumps, in order to return to their home nest as their lives approach its end.
  - It could also reference the feeling homesickness for Leyndell and the Erdtree displayed by Godrick and his followers. Due to its depiction of a visibly distant Erdtree and said Erdtree being in close proximity to the Tower of Return, which offers the inhabitants of Limgrave a means to quickly travel to the capital, even if the location they end up in is only a small enclosed area of it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Alabaster Lord's Sword** is a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: - Deals an extra 20% damage against Gravity-type enemies.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Lake of Rot
- Defeat the Alabaster Lord in the Lake of Rot (will not drop if the Lord is killed at the same time as the player) to obtain the Alabaster Lord's Sword. He is on top of a large Ancient Dynasty structure.
**Random Drop**:
- Defeat Alabaster Lords in Yelough Anix Tunnel.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.text:
- The Alabaster Lord's Sword is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- The Alabaster Lord's Sword cannot have its affinities changed with Ashes of War or Whetblades.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Unlike Ash of War: Gravitas, which deals entirely Magic damage, this weapon's skill mostly Physical damage with some Magic damage, with roughly the same damage ratio as the weapon itself.
- The shortest among all greatswords.
- The 2-handed charged heavy attacks of this weapon deals damage on par with that of a Colossal Sword while draining much less Stamina than any other greatsword's. 1-handed charge attacks have similar bonuses but much less of a damage increase.
  - To be precise, the 1-handed charged heavy attacks have a roughly 10% higher damage multiplier while the 2-handed charged heavy attack has a 34% damage multiplier, and both cost only 18 points of Stamina where the average stamina cost for greatswords for both is between 35 and 42 points of Stamina for the 1-handed ones and between 38 and 48 for 2-handed ones.
- Despite that being its highest Attribute requirement, its Intelligence scaling is rather subpar.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword
- Onyx Lord's Greatsword

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Agheel's Flame** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Caelid
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Flying Dragon Agheel.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of flames, dealing Fire damage equal to 169% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e., 507% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonfire.
- Compared to Dragonfire, this spell deals 17% more damage but also consumes 38% more FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the third strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 0.5% less damage than Ghostflame Breath and 10% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Borealis's Mist, a weaker Magic damage version of this spell that also inflicts Frostbite
- Dragonfire, a weaker but cheaper version of this spell
- Ekzykes's Decay, a weaker Standard damage of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot
- Ghostflame Breath, a slightly stronger Magic damage version of this spell that also inflicts some Frostbite
- Smarag's Glintstone Breath, a stronger Magic damage version of this spell

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 8,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Calls on a red, crackling spear from above that is then slammed into the ground, hitting with Lightning Attack Power equal to 360% of Incantation Scaling in a small 0.2 meter radius, and creating a shockwave with a 3 meter radius that hits with Lightning Attack Power equal to 285% of Incantation Scaling.

From the point of impact, waves of red lightning are sent out directly ahead and behind, and to the left and right of the caster with Lightning Attack Power equal to 122% of Incantation Scaling in a 2 meter radius from the center of each wave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 29 points of Stamina.
- Deals 17 Stance damage on a direct or shockwave hit and 5 Stance damage on a wave hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- The "direct" hit and the initial area attack cannot hit the same target, though the smaller, weakest waves can hit an enemy that has already been hit if they are either quick or large enough to also be where those are.
- The "spear" is actually flung downwards, meaning it can be used to hit the ground beneath a cliff if the caster is standing on its edge.
- Casts faster than Fortissax's Lightning Spear, but is much weaker overall and per hit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - FP cost was decreased from 30 to 25.
  - Only the direct hit had its Stamina Attack Power increased against guarding enemies, from 100 to 140.

- Patch 1.04 included an undocumented change which reduced the FP cost of this incantation.
  - FP cost was decreased from 42 to 30.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 10,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Sends out rows of bolts in all directions, hitting at regular intervals with Lightning Attack Power equal to 317% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell sends out additional bolts to extend the range slighly and increases the Attack Power of each hit to 379% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 31 points of Stamina. Charging the spell increases the cost to 40 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases this to 9 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 19%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 37%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
  - Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike was charged or not.
- This is one of the game's strongest attacks, capable of dealing over ten thousand damage to larger bosses such as the Dragonlord or the God-Devouring Serpent, even if they are resistant to Lightning, but even smaller, human-sized enemies will take heavy damage in the thousands if hit by just one or two bolts.
- This spell sometimes fails to do anything when cast under low-level roofs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Unlike other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't summon its bolts bolt from somewhere above them, instead creating them from the used Sacred Seal.
- Patch 1.04 decreased recovery time.
- Patch 1.03.3 included an undocumented changed which increased the FP cost of this incantation.
  - FP cost was increased from 27 to 36.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom, another area of effect striking incantation, but with Holy damage
- Death Lightning, a more inaccurate and spread out but stronger version of this spell
- Elden Stars
- Founding Rain of Stars, a sorcery with a similar but much, much weaker damage

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Alexander, Warrior Jar** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Alexander is a living jar who travels the Lands Between, honing his strength to become a great warrior. Alexander was created to be a warrior vessel, and the remains of many great warriors reside within him. He originally came from Jarburg, a hidden village of living jars in Liurnia of the Lakes; however, he vowed never to return, claiming that "the path of champions must be trod alone".

On his journey to become a grand champion, he seeks out Redmane Castle in Caelid, following rumours of a festival of combat. On his way to the festival, he crosses paths with the Tarnished multiple times, often requiring their assistance to get out of unfortunate situations such as being stuck in potholes.

Alexander finally participates in the Radahn Festival, a brawl between several champions and Starscourge Radahn. Alexander survives the ordeal, however, he suffers damage to his body and is forced to hide for the remainder of the battle. Undeterred, he replenishes himself with the bodies of mighty warriors littering the battlefield, vowing to grow even stronger.

Next, Alexander travels to Mt. Gelmir, hoping to temper his body in the sea of fire, such that it would never crack again. Finding the lava to be lukewarm and insufficient to strengthen his vessel, he sets his sights upon the Mountaintops of the Giants, seeking out the flame of ruin.

Alexander travels to the mountaintops, where he witnesses the Tarnished's fight with the Fire Giant. He then finds himself in Farum Azula, where he encounters the Tarnished for a final time. Impressed by his companion's feats of strength, he requests a duel. The Tarnished emerges victorious and Alexander accepts his defeat, asking the Tarnished to take his innards with his final words.

The Tarnished may present these innards to Alexander's nephew, the Jar-Bairn, who vows to become strong like his uncle Alexander.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave (Stormhill)
  - *(Optional)* Alexander can first be found in Stormhill, stuck in a pothole atop a cliff southwest of the Saintsbridge Site of Grace. He will call out once you get close. After talking to him, agree to help him and then stand behind him and hit him. Once you have dealt sufficient damage, he will burst free of the hole. Exhaust his dialogue again to receive an Exhalted Flesh.
1. Limgrave (Gael Tunnel)
  - *(Optional)* Alexander can next be found near the Rear Gael Tunnel Site of Grace, accessible via the Limgrave entrance. By progressing through the dungeon from the Caelid entrance, you will be able to unlock the door blocking Alexander's path. Exhaust his dialogue to continue his questline.
1. Caelid (Redmane Castle)
  - *(Optional)* Alexander will be standing in the plaza as long as you have triggered the Radahn Festival. He is also available as a summon during the Starscourge Radahn boss fight.
1. Caelid (Redmane Castle)
  - After defeating Starscourge Radahn, Alexander can be found near the Site of Grace in the Wailing Dunes. Exhaust his dialogue to progress his questline.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes
  - (Optional) Alexander will be in a pothole on the cliffs above Jarburg, south of the Artist's Shack (Liurnia of the lakes). He will once again ask you to hit him, however doing so will not free him. You must throw an Oil Pot at him, talk to him again, and then hit him several more times to free him. Speak to him again to receive three Exalted Flesh.
1. Mt Gelmir
  - Alexander can be found in a pool of lava south of Fort Laiedd, near a Magma Wyrm encounter. To speak to him without taking damage from the lava, ride Torrent to a sloped rock in front of him and dismount. Speak to him to receive the Jar helmet.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
  - *(Optional)* Alexander can be summoned during the Fire Giant boss fight. His summon sign is just inside the arena.
1. Crumbling Farum Azula
  - Alexander will be standing on a floating platform close to the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace. He will request a duel. After defeating him, exhaust his dialogue and pick up Alexander's Innards and a Shard of Alexander.
  - Alexander's Innards can be given to Jar-Bairn at the end of his own questline.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Altus Plateau** is a region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The **Altus Plateau** is a northwestern region of the Lands Between. It is a region of great significance, for it is here that the Erdtree can be found, as well as Leyndell, the royal capital of Queen Marika. Altus borders Liurnia of the Lakes to the south, and the Forbidden Lands which lead to the Mountaintops of the Giants to the east. Due to its high elevation, Altus is connected to its neighbouring regions primarily through two lifts; the Grand Lift of Dectus to the south and the Grand Lift of Rold to the east. There is another, more dangerous path to Liurnia that goes through the mountains separating the two regions.

Altus is a lush and verdant land, once over-flowing with the bounty of the Erdtree itself. Most of the vegetation that grows in Altus is tinged with the gold of the Erdtree, and flowers that grow on the plateau are prized reagents by Perfumers. The people of the plateau believed that those born at the foot of the Erdtree, like themselves, were blessed. While still beautiful, the land is marred by scars from the Shattering, left over from the many battles waged here. The land is dotted by ruined battlefields and soldier's camps.

The western parts of Altus are mountainous and dominated by the volcanic Mt. Gelmir. At the top of the mountain lies the Volcano Manor, home to the demigod Praetor Rykard. At the foot of the mountain lies bubbling geysers as well as a village of Demihumans.

In the north of Altus, through a deep canyon, lies the Shaded Castle, ancient manor of the Marais family who served as both executioners and castellans of the Shaded Castle for generations. The castle lies in disrepair, haunted by Wraith-Callers and Revenants, and with most of its courtyard sinking into a poison swamp.

The eastern parts of Altus are dominated by Leyndell, Queen Marika's royal capital, built at the foot of the Erdtree. Two primary paths lead into the capital grounds; one from the southwest and one from the northwest. The southwestern path is the main road, a well-maintained and well-guarded highway gloriously decorated with statues of Queen Marika's soldiers. The capital grounds are defended by double ramparts. Within the outer wall, to the northeast, lies a Minor Erdtree. Just outside the outer wall, on an outcropping north of the southwestern highway, lies the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave, final resting place of a hero who fought against the Giants.

The inner wall of the capital is surrounded by a moat, which appears to have mostly dried out, as its waters are now shallow. Within the inner walls, the Royal Capital is bounded by a lake, which serves as yet another layer of protection. The capital is ruled by the Demigod Morgott, known also as the Veiled Monarch.

The location being the point of perspective depicted by the painting itself.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
There is a limited number of Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones that can be acquired each playthrough. As of now, a total number of 13 have been discovered.

- One given by Witch-Hunter Jerren for siding with him against Sellen at the end of her questline.
- One can be purchased from Gostoc at the end of Nepheli's questline for 20000 runes.
- One given by Nepheli Loux at the end of her questline.
- One from Gurranq as reward for finding all 9 Deathroot.
- One dropped by the Night's Cavalry duo miniboss guarding the caravan with the Flowing Curved Sword in it on the Consecrated Snowfield. These also drop the Night Cavalry armor set.
- Two are dropped by two different red lightning dragon minibosses in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancient Dragon Lansseax** is an optional boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Lansseax, sister of Fortissax, was an Ancient Dragon that took the form of a human priestess to commune with the knights of Leyndell's Ancient Dragon Cult. Her most beloved knight was Vyke the Dragonspear, a Tarnished knight of the Roundtable Hold, who was later scorched by the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
Lansseax is first encountered near the  Abandoned Coffin Site of Grace, ambushing the player near the entrance to Altus Plateau from the Ruin-Strewn Precipice. After sustaining enough damage, she abruptly ends the fight by flying away.

Her next encounter is on a hill southwest of the  Rampartside Path Site of Grace, located in eastern Altus Plateau, where she can be defeated for good.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Lansseax has two unique moves that involve her summoning a glaive made of red lightning. One is a diagonal slam which releases waves of lightning across the ground that can be dodged through. The other is a horizontal sweep which also sends out waves.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Ancient Dragon Lansseax was named **Lansseax, Ancient Dragon Progeny** in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ainsel River** is an underground region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Ainsel is said to be the grave of civilisations that flourished before the Erdtree. The eastern side of Ainsel is dominated by the Uhl Palace Ruins, characterised by their mausoleums and statues, and inhabited by the Claymen who served as priests of the ancient dynasty.

Nokstella, one of the Eternal Cities, can be found in the western portion of the subterranean space, inhabited by the Nox who were banished underground by the Greater Will long ago. Deeper still is the Lake of Rot, a putrid underground swamp littered with ancient ruins, where the essence of an Outer God was sealed. At the deepest point is the lair of Astel, a malformed star who once assailed an Eternal City and took away its sky. Beyond Astel is a lift which leads to the Moonlight Altar, provided the Dark Moon Ring has been found.

Ainsel can be accessed via the Ainsel River Well in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. The Ainsel River Main, which encompasses Nokstella, can be accessed via a sending gate in Renna's Rise, after Ranni the Witch gains possession of the Fingerslayer Blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The name Ainsel, meaning My Own Self, is a fairy name from Scottish/Gaelic folklore. The name Siofra has similar origins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader** is a boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Alecto was the ringleader of the Black Knife Assassins, the assailants responsible for the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. She was believed to be a Numen originating from an Eternal City. Alecto was said to have had close ties to Queen Marika herself.

sections.heading: Black Knives
sections.text:
After stealing a fragment of Destined Death, Ranni the Witch performed a dark ritual to imbue its power into mishappen blades. Alecto and her fellow assassins took the daggers, donned silent, silver scale armor, and made their way toward the Royal Capital.

Alecto masked her presence with a concealing veil as she and her co-conspirators entered Leyndell beneath the cover of darkness. When the moment was right, they carved the Cursemark of Death into Godwyn's flesh and slew his soul. Alecto's daughter, Tiche, died protecting her during their ensuing flight from the capital. Alecto herself was later captured and sealed within an Evergaol by an unknown party.

sections.heading: Boss fight
sections.text: She shares a moveset with the Black Knife Assassins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Alecto was likely trapped in the Ringleader's Evergaol by Ranni the Witch or War Counselor Iji.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Alabaster Lord** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A race of ancients with stone skin who are said to have risen to life when a meteor struck long ago. They wield swords made from blue-white meteoric ore, and utilise gravitational powers that pull things in.

Radahn learned how to use gravitational techniques from an Alabaster Lord in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, which allowed him to challenge the stars.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Limgrave: Found on the beach south of Seaside Ruins Site of Grace, itself south of Dragon-Burnt Ruins. Search for a spiritspring to the right of a pillar southeast of the grace to fall down safely and then look for an archway on the middle of the sands.
- Weeping Peninsula: Found in a field with impact craters, close to the Beside the Crater-Pocked Glade Site of Grace that is north of Oridys's Rise.
- Academy of Raya Lucaria: From the Church of the Cuckoo Site of Grace, proceed out into the graveyards and across the bridge to the gate out at the end of the second graveyard. Instead of taking the water wheel upward, proceed straight ahead to an altar with a gravity anomaly beside it.
- Lake of Rot: Found atop a stone structure at the end that has to be raised with buttons, just before the Grand Cloister. To get back up after failing, head up the cliffside on the far left side (right side if coming from the Grand Cloister Site of Grace).
- Yelough Anix Tunnel: Found at the bottom of the Tunnel.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - In Version 1.00 of Elden Ring, the Onyx Lord in the Royal Grave Evergaol was called "Alabaster Lord."

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Academy of Raya Lucaria** is a both a faction, and a legacy dungeon located in Liurnia of the Lakes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Academy of Raya Lucaria sits on a plateau in the middle of the great lake of Liurnia, and is the place of study for glintstone sorcerers of the Lands Between. This area is accessed by using an Academy Glintstone Key to pass through either of the two gates marked with the blue seal.

The Academy offers everything from basic training in sorcerery to advanced, specialized study. Higher learning is accessible to only noteworthy scholars, who are then permitted to don stone Glintstone Crowns, modeled after notable sorcerers in their chosen conspectus. Azur and Lusat, regarded as founding glintstone sorcerers, founded the Karolos and Olivinus Conspectuses, respectively. The majority of Glintstone Crown sorcerers found within the Academy pursue one of these two founding conspectuses.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The founding of the Academy of Raya Lucaria was credited to the primeval sorcerers Azur and Lusat. Their study of the Primeval Current shook the academy when they began to transfigure fledgling sorcerers into Graven Masses—the seeds of stars.

Long ago, Rennala charmed the Academy with her lunar magic. She became the Academy's master and established the house of Caria as royalty. When Rennala assumed governorship over the Academy, she heavily limited the study of the primeval current due the dangers it presented and subsequently exiled Azur and Lusat. This change outraged Sorceress Sellen, who began to transform her peers into Graven Schools. Though the Academy expelled Sellen and denounced her methods, they shared her core sentiment, and their thirst for knowledge would eventually lead to the downfall of the Carians influence over the Academy.

The combined forces of the Knights of the Cuckoo: the Cuckoo Knights, the Raya Lucaria Soldiers and their Foot Soldiers were hired by the Academy at some point. As payment for their service, the Academy taught them martial Glintstone techniques like Scholar's Armament and Scholar's Shield. The design of the Cuckoo bird upon their armor is mused to represent the Cuckoo's refusal to be mere servants of the Academy. The Cuckoo were given free reign to wage war as they pleased by the Academy, and became known for their rapacious ways.

When Rennala's husband Radagon left her to become the second Elden Lord, Rennala's heart went with him. With Rennala a grieving shell of her former self, the Academy then realised that she was no champion after all. She still clutches the amber egg given to her by Radagon, which contains the Great Rune of the Unborn. No longer in any state to defend herself, the Academy took the opportunity to lock Rennala in their Grand Library and staged a rebellion against the Carians, so that they could pursue unlimited study once more. The resulting conflict between the Acadamy's forces, and those of the Carians, waged across Liurnia, becoming an effective Liurnian civil war. Ultimately, the Acadamy would achieve their goals. Without their queen, and her successors absent, the Carians fell into decline, and their influence in the Academy's policies dissipated.

After the Shattering of the Elden Ring, the Academy declared neutrality in the ensuing war and cast repelling seals upon its entrances, blocking outside access to anyone not in possession of a Academy Glintstone Key. Such a key may be found on an island west of the Academy, guarded by Glintstone Dragon Smarag.

sections.heading: Sites of Grace
sections.text:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: A **conspectus** is a field of study within the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Scholars who show particular promise in sorcery are permitted to don a stone glintstone crown and study a particular conspectus. Thus, each conspectus is associated with its own glintstone crown, as well as its own set of glintstone sorceries.

sections.heading: Karolos Conspectus
sections.text:
The oldest and most venerable of the Academy's conspectuses, the Karolos Conspectus was founded by Azur, the primeval sorcerer, and aspires to follow in his footsteps by pursuing the mysteries of comets. Scholars who study the Karolos Conspectus don Karolos Glintstone Crowns and utilise comet-based sorceries.

**Spells:**
- Glintstone Cometshard
- Comet
- Shard Spiral

sections.heading: Olivinus Conspectus
sections.text:
A conspectus begat by the primeval sorcerer Lusat, with a focus on the study of meteors. Sorcerers from Sellia, Town of Sorcery are known to travel to the Academy of Raya Lucaria to study the Olivinus Conspectus. Those who follow this conspectus wear Olivinus Glintstone Crowns and wield sorceries that launch magic shooting stars at their targets.

**Spells:**
- Glintstone Stars
- Star Shower

sections.heading: Twinsage Conspectus
sections.text:
A special, higher conspectus comprised of the Academy's truly elite scholars. Those who study the Twinsage Conspectus wear Twinsage Glintstone Crowns, depicting dual heads, and are permitted to study sorceries from all other conspectuses.

**Spells:**
- Glintstone Cometshard
- Crystal Burst

sections.heading: Lazuli Conspectus
sections.text:
A heterodox conspectus that views the moon as equal to the stars. Scholars of the Lazuli Conspectus study Carian sorceries, and fight using wooden Lazuli Glintstone Swords inlaid with glintstone. They don Lazuli Glintstone Crowns and wear pale Lazuli Robes in the hue of the full moon, signifying their heresy. By their presence at Caria Manor, fighting alongside Carian forces, it seems at least some of these sorcerers chose to side with Carians against the Acadamy during the Liurnian civil war.

**Spells:**
- Carian Greatsword

sections.heading: Haima Conspectus
sections.text:
The conspectus of Haima, the adjudicator of the Academy. Scholars of the Haima Conspectus, known as battlemages, seek to quell conflict through the use of their sorceries of cannon fire and gavel, as well as through the use of their Stone Clubs made from hard glintstone, which allow them to feel the impact of their blows. During times of war, when the Academy seals its gates, only Haima's scholars dare to venture outside. Scholars of the Haima Conspectus wear Haima Glintstone Crowns.

**Spells:**
- Cannon of Haima
- Gavel of Haima

sections.heading: Hierodas Conspectus
sections.text:
The Hierodas Glintstone Crown was granted to observant scholars who engaged in nomadic study away from the Academy, walking the Lands Between in search of knowledge. Notable adherents of this conspectus include the Scholar and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm. Wilhelm, a silent seeker of sorcery who made contact with the primeval current, embraced Night Sorceries, using the Staff of Loss as a catalyst.

**Spells:**
- Starlight
- Glintstone Arc

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: ***Aseo*** is the main character in the manga spinoff **Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree**, taking the role as the playable Tarnished from the original game. The story revolves around his quest to help Melina get to the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
There was one other, a Tarnished of no renown. A wretch of Reedlandish descent, called by Grace, to cross the fog into the Lands Between, to stand before the Elden Ring and succeed Queen Marika, as the Elden Lord.

The Tarnished awoke in the Chapel of Anticipation. After a run in with the Grafted Scion, he ended up in the Stranded Graveyard. The drifting Melina and the Spirit Steed Torrent saw him. Melina was hesitant to choose him but Torrent urged her to. Melina placed healing flasks onto the Tarnished's butt. The amnesiac Tarnished awoke, headed up the stairs and lift and exited the Heroes' Grave, seeing Limgrave, having no memories of his past before arriving at the Lands. He sought not to be Lord, having no purpose, simply a noob. White Mask Varre, a servant of Mohg, mocked the Tarnished, scaring him but informed him to head to Stormveil where Godrick was. Meanwhile Godrick was comparing grafting parts to his subordinates. The Tarnished sees the Tree Sentinel but is knocked onto a stake, the Tree Sentinel shocked that he survived. The lost Tarnished is unable to get anywhere. Melina appears, offering to level him up with his runes in return for taking her to the Erdtree, so she can ascertain her purpose which she has forgotten. The Tarnished realizes that like him, Melina wishes to find her purpose and agrees to help her. As for a name, Melina names him Aseo after the Reedlandish pronunciation of Tarnished, Asebito. Melina hands Aseo Torrent. Aseo attempted to challenge the Tree Sentinel with Torrent but fails. Aseo is unable to make any progress and Patches the Untethered, a bald money motivated merchant (who is free of worldly wants such as greed) and an entity who has a presence in other worlds finds him and takes him under his wing. Aseo sees Patches as a brother and Melina questions why Aseo isn't doing anything to make progress. Patches lets Aseo go on his quest after Aseo refuses to steal from the Nomadic Merchant Kale. However, Patches as a parting gift tricks Aseo into a teleporter chest which takes Aseo into Mistwood Ruins, filled with massive Rune Bears. Patches claiming it's to prepare Aseo for the dangers that lie ahead. Aseo escapes the forest, conversing with Kale, Kale offering Aseo a free crafting kit if he assists Ranni's Shadowbound Beast Blaidd in Mistwood, which Aseo reluctantly does. Blaidd reveals his intentions to kill the Bloodhound Knight Darwil. Aseo and Blaidd befriend and helps Blaidd who has poor directional skills reach Darwil in Forlorn Hound Evergaol where he is imprisoned. Melina translates the fight between Blaidd and Darwil. Both beasts were once allies. Darwil was a Ranni fan and Ranni's adoptive brother Blaidd and him secretly did a Ranni fan club to make Ranni dolls. They even put up a Reedlandish sign for the club. When Darwil decided to give the Ranni dolls maid dresses, this turned them into enemies. Blaidd believes that Darwil being trapped in the Evergaol isn't enough to pay for the crime of what he did to Ranni's dolls. Melina defeats Darwil, sickened at their conversation. Aseo returns to Kale at the Church of Vows, to find Kale sleeping and to see Ranni who claims she is the witch Renna to keep her identity hidden, something Aseo sees through given he had seen Blaidd's Ranni dolls. Ranni gives Aseo a bell to summon spirit summons and also 3 wolf spirit summons which Aseo names Pochi, Shirou and Tarou. Godrick makes plans, wishing to hold a grafting competition. Aseo after some bonding with the wolfs, walks to Stormveil but unlike the previous times the way there is not guarded as Godrick has retracted his troops for the impending competition. Aseo on the way encounters Roderika. Roderika was a noblewoman and a Tarnished, her men were killed by a Grafted Scion, children grafted into monstrous spider like beings by Godrick himself. She has lost any will to survive but Aseo urges her to remain hopeful, sharing his similar experience of being stranded in this strange land. Aseo h

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text:
Aseo possesses the black hair of a Reedlander.

Aseo starts off wearing nothing more than a loincloth and utilizes a Club, he receives a saddlebag to hold items in Chapter 3.

He recieves a Longsword as a gift and Fell Omen Cloak made from Margit ripping a part of his own cloak off in Chapter 8. He later receives the Heater Shield from Bernahl in Chapter 15.

In Chapter 18, Ranni, in an attempt to make Aseo her ally, gifts Aseo a Carian Knight set. He becomes over-encumbered and ditches half the set barring the Gauntlet and Greaves for warmth at night. In Chapter 19, Thops gives him the Glintstone Staff.

Ranni eventually gives him the sword of Night and flame.

He later gets a Jar from Alexander

sections.heading: Personality
sections.text: Aseo can be described as an airhead and lacking intelligence at times, such as asking the Tree Sentinel for a ride to Stormveil Castle, with the Tree Sentintel promptly Shield Bashing him, and sending him flying into a Marika's Cross.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Albinaurics** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The albinaurics are artificial life found across the Lands Between either as a First-Generation Albinauric (including an archer variant) or Second-Generation Albinauric.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Albinaurics are lifeforms made by human hands, forsaken to the Lands Between by the stars. Thus, many believe them to live impure lives, untouched by the Erdtree's grace. They are said to have been created in the Eternal City from a primordial drop of night-tinged dew, and secretly harbour the ability to cast magic using their innate arcaneness. All Albinaurics share a fate; their legs will one day fade, and with them, their lives. This process can be seen most clearly in the bearded Elder Albinaurics that inhabit the Village of the Albinaurics.

Albinaurics are viewed as impure, and are persecuted by the Knights of the Cuckoo for their defiled blood. They seek salvation in Miquella's Haligtree, which they believe to be their chosen land. Aged Albinaurics carry Ivory Sickles in dedication to the Haligtree, despite having never entered its presence.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Albinaurics have silver blood. All first-generation Albinaurics are disabled and have lost the use of their legs. The males appear as withered old men with long beards whose legs are vanishing into shadow. The female archers, who wear blue silver mail born from the same mother as themselves, also lack the functionality of their legs, which they compensate for by riding wolfback. Nonetheless, they were feared as deadly sharpshooters.

Second-generation Albinaurics differ visually from the more humanoid first generation specimens, having heads that resemble those of frogs and protruding bellies. They wield weaponry modelled after the ripples that are said to be the origin of their species, as well as wooden clubs shaped like the Crescent Moon.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
Albinaurics are encountered throughout the Lands Between and Realm of Shadow. A majority may be found in central Liurnia.

No Albinaurics are found in the Eternal Cities or at the Albinauric Rise in the Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.text:
- Their natural Arcaness raises their  Holy defense.
- Large Sanguine Albinaurics at the Mohgwyn Palace turned red and sprouted horns after receiving Mohg's accursed Omen blood and a boon from the Formless Mother. They blow into Curved Great Clubs to summon Tibia's Giant Skeletons. Others sprout piercing bloodthorns whenever they cartwheel, a power of the Blood Star.
- Albinauric's Shack and Commander Gaius are found in proximity to the Scadutree Chalice, suggesting its blessed sap was the amber that catalyzed the origin of their species.
- The  also known as the shinbone or shankbone, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee. The first generation of Albinaurics lost the use of their tibias, and are unable to walk on their own.
- Oracle Envoys, the Putrescent Knight, and the Prince of Death are also legless. The nameless bearded god of the Ancient Dynasty is depicted without legs at the Cocoon of the Empyrean.
- Tibia Mariners and the giant mummified maidens perched atop Chair-Crypts also appear immobile.
- Albinaurics have white blood, though Loretta and Gaius bleed red because they and their non-Albinauric mounts are coded as a single NPC.
- Loretta was absurdly rumored to be an Albinauric.

- Albinaurics were also known as the **Children of Silver** in .
- Cut content: Sorcerer Thops specified the Albinaurics and their curses were born of an Eternal City rite, and warns of their grudges against outsiders. He called Young Albinaurics "Frogs."
- In version 1.00, the Academy of Raya Lucaria produced Albinauric Archers to serve as maids.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Albinauric Archer** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Female Albinaurics that have become masters of archery. They don armor made from blue silver, a material born from the same mother as the archers themselves that provides protection from magic and frost. Some have chosen to compensate for their weak legs by riding on Dire Wolves but even then, they are capable of picking off a target from great distances. Their Albinauric Bow splits their arrows into three magical homing projectiles for extra effect.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
The **Albinauric Archer**s are dangerous and a bit of a nuisance even from a distance they shoot three magical arrows at the player that can deal devastating damage. They are very agile with their wolf and can evade the players attacks their wolf can cause frostbite with their frost breathe.

It’s also important to note that when players do kill their mount the **Albinauric Archer** will still continue shooting their arrows at the player but there are some useful tips for defeating them having a fully upgraded Ballista or crossbow will stagger them allowing the player to get a hit in and repeating the process.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The  also known as the shinbone or shankbone, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee. The first generation of Albinaurics lost the use of their tibias, and are unable to walk on their own.
- Unlike male Elder Albinaurics, female Albinaurics don't appear to suffer from their fatal condition of their legs disappearing.

sections.text:

- *Albinauric* is a constructed term derived from Latin roots *albus* (pale, white) and ** (gold), suggesting an approximation of silver made from gold.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Abductor Virgins**, also known as **Iron Virgins**, are Bosses and Enemies in Elden Ring. They are Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Abductor Virgins are automatons affiliated with the Volcano Manor. Originally designed with the intent of capturing and transposing victims for interrogation, they can be found strewn around the Lands Between. Though the majority have lost their powers of transposition, they will still attempt to fulfill their original directive if approached.

To aid in their task, Abductor Virgins have been outfitted with heavy weaponry on both arms that alter how they approach each target. When a Virgin has approached a target, they will open their chest cavity and attempt to pull them in with serpentine tendrils. Given the loss of their transposition ability, the target will be constricted instead. If they survive this, they will be spat back out.

They are weak to Lightning damage and all damage taken is greatly increased if attacked when their chest cavity is opened during a charge or attempted grab.

Wheel=

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text:
A model with arms that end in great iron wheels, based on the device used by Inquisitor Ghiza. One such model lies at the bottom of the big waterwheel of Raya Lucaria, its transpostitional powers still fully intact.

These variants will often use their wheels by pressing them down on the ground. When placing both wheels at their sides, they will either perform a small spin in place, or a larger spin where they gradually spiral outwards. When there is distance, the Virgin will place both wheels in front and rapidly accelerate forward. Sometimes they will stop before reaching the target and open their chest cavity in an attempt to grab them.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Can include a separate table for a specific instance of this variant's moveset.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text:
A model with arms that end in great scythes on chains that it can extend and retract at will. Though they only have one spin attack, they will often use it to get some distance between them and their target. At the very end, they may throw their scythes at the target. This is something that they will do whenever there is sufficient distance. It is important to be careful after dodging the initial throw, as the scythe may hit when it is being retracted. This is especially true when near the Virgin, as the scythe will spin back around behind it upon return.

It's important to note that the Scythe can sometimes go through walls.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: A unique model of the Iron Virgin that has both the scythe and wheel devices installed. They are capable of using a mixed move-set, often consisting of using the wheel to spin and close distance and the scythe to attack from far away.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A pair of Iron Virgins, one wielding the wheel implements and the other wielding the scythe implements. The latter will make itself known immediately at the start of the fight. Whereas the former will charge at the player from the left side of the cave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - They are immune to all Status Effects like other golems.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancient Dragons** are non-respawning enemies in Elden Ring and bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign. These **Old Dragons** have stone bodies and live eternal lives.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Ancient Dragons have timeless, light-gray bodies made of jagged gravel stone imbued with gold. They are distinguished from lesser dragons by their four legs and four wings with golden undersides. They have long muzzles and broad, flat foreheads that taper to pointed snouts and a wide mouth lined with numerous sharp, interlocking teeth. Deep-set eyes with orange sclera and vertical yellow irises stare forward from beneath heavy bony ridges. A pair of enormous horns rises above the eyes and extends backward, framing the head like a crown. Behind them, a row of eight shorter horn-like spikes stands along the top rear of the skull. Additional spikes jut outward from the sides of their heads near the cheeks, and long, wispy strands of gray hair trail along the ridge of their elongated necks.

They can breathe fire like many of their descendants; however, they possess the legendary ability to summon storms of red lightning and wield it as spears and glaives. They are unaffected by time and are immortal.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Ancient Dragons were immortal beings who ruled in the prehistoric era before the age of the Erdtree. They were ruled over by Dragonlord Placidusax, said to have been Elden Lord in that bygone age, from the royal city of Farum Azula, and it is said that they would protect their lord as a wall of living rock. In Farum Azula, many Ancient Dragons can be found buried in the rock, between the catacombs of the Beastmen and the surface of the city, their bodies still filled with gold.

In the catacombs of the Beastmen under the city, many statues can be found depicting an Ancient Dragon surrounded by Beastmen dressed like clergymen, highlighting the Beastmens' role as priests and servants of the Dragons.

During the reign of Queen Marika the Eternal, the Ancient Dragon Gransax wrought havoc on Leyndell, Royal Capital, the only time in recorded history that Leyndell's walls have fallen. This marked the dawn of the war against the Dragons, during which the Tree Sentinels clad themselves in armor resembling the bodies of malformed dragons to protect the Erdtree. During this conflict Godwyn the Golden fought to the last against Ancient Dragon Fortissax. Godwyn defeated Fortissax, however he befriended his fallen foe, ending the conflict and giving rise to the capital's Ancient Dragon Cult. Worship of the Ancient Dragons does not conflict with faith in the Erdtree, as the Dragons' lightning is imbued with gold, and as such the Cult was permitted within Leyndell. Several ancient dragons assumed feeble human forms to better commune with humans.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: Four can be fought, but spirit ashes can be used only for the first and strongest dragon, which will drop  32,400 runes and an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone when killed. Three weaker variants can be fought, one near the  Crumbling Beast Grave Site of Grace, another one south of the  Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, and one at the  Dragon Temple Rooftop Site of Grace; these will reward  21,600 runes and a [[Smithing Stone 8|Smithing Stone [8]]].

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.text:
There are four total encounters with the three boss variants:
- Ancient Dragon Lansseax
- Ancient Dragon Senessax Shadow of the Erdtree
- Lichdragon Fortissax

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text:
They attack with fire breath and powerful lightning magic.
- Stance: 120 (600 effective)
  - Incoming stance damage to the body is multiplied by ×0.2 (stance damage to the head is multiplied by ×0.4).
- Deals  Standard,  Fire, and  Lightning damage.
- Immune to  Sleep.
- Strong vs:  Lightning damage
- Weak vs:  Pierce damage
- Ancient Dragons are susceptible to Anti-Dragon effects.
- Weak spot: Head (+100% damage, +100% stance damage)
- Parryable attacks: No
- This enemy is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Many four-winged ancient dragons can be seen flying throughout Crumbling Farum Azula, though they cannot be interacted with.
- Ancient dragons maintained Placidusax's favor by relinquishing their sleep to him and remaining awake.
- The ancient dragons' immortality robbed them of the ambition and fierceness of spirit needed to destroy Bayle the Dread themselves.
- Ancient dragons who wielded branching red lightning sided with Bayle against Dragonlord Placidusax.
- Ancient dragons seemingly lose their gold tinge after death; they revert to inanimate stone before crumbling away. Ancient dragon corpses present at the Church of Dragon Communion, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion, and the Dragon Temple may represent those who assumed human form to share Dragon Communion with humanity.
- The larger ancient dragons embedded within Farum Azula retain their gold and likely represent an older generation of dragons, as their morphology more closely that of Placidusax than living ancient dragons, whose internal names are "GuardianDescendant". Ancient Dragon Lansseax was named "Lansseax, Ancient Dragon Progeny" .
- The Draconians were the people of the ancient dragons and were known for their brief lifespans.
- Humans could become everlasting ancient dragons by consuming Rock Hearts, the original form of Dragon Communion.

sections.text: - Internal name: **GuardianDescendant** (ID: 4510)

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ancestral Follower Warriors** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Having abandoned steel, the weapons they wield consist of repurposed animal parts.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text:
The most common are those that wield the Jawbone Axe and are capable of performing swift attacks with both the weapon and their free hand.

The most dangerous and notable of these warriors are the hunters that wield the Horn Bow, capable of firing Dwelling Arrows with near-perfect precision, even over great distances. If the player is spotted, they will relentlessly fire arrows, but if they are approached, they will switch to an axe for melee combat.

Others wield either the Greathorn Hammer or the sacred Winged Greathorn, and attack slower but deal much more devastating blows. The Followers that wield the latter weapon are capable of performing its Unique Skill: Soul Stifler.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text:
A spectral variant of the Ancestral Followers. Like similar phantom variants, they can briefly appear and disappear.

They are still immune to Status Effects.

sections.heading: Notes

  - Their bodies were covered in pustules and they had the ability to spew a stream of scarlet rot.

sections.text: The **Abandoned Cave** is a Location and Sites of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A cave set into the cliffs of central Caelid, situated above the ravine containing the Deep Siofra Well. It lies south of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, north of the Swamp of Aeonia, and just northwest of the Sellia Evergaol. It is located east of the nearest Site of Grace:  Smoldering Wall. The entrance is reached by crossing a tree root spanning the canyon from the west, beyond an Abductor Virgin.

Within, Abandoned Cave opens into a rot-blighted swamp where aged Servants of Rot cultivate Miranda Flowers. Geysers of Scarlet Rot erupt intermittently from the ground. Several broken Abductor Virgins lie scattered throughout. In the innermost chamber lurk two Cleanrot Knights—remnants of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's forces who opposed the Redmanes in the Battle of Aeonia during the Shattering.

sections.heading: Abandoned Cave
sections.text: The  **Abandoned Cave** Site of Grace is found inside the cave, just beyond the entrance. It is the only grace at this location.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Arcane** (神秘, *Shinpi*) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Arcane stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Arcane scaling. Increasing Arcane will also increase Discovery, which increases the chance of finding drops from enemies. It will also contribute to the Tarnished's Holy Defense and Vitality, which increases resistance to Death Blight. Increasing Arcane also affects weapons with Blood Loss, Poison, Madness and Sleep build up, increasing the rate at which they inflict status effects.

The Tarnished can level Arcane by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. The Tarnished has a base discovery rate of 100, with each level in Arcane increasing Discovery by 1. Increasing Holy Defense has soft caps at 20, 35 and 60 Arcane. Vitality increased through Arcane has soft caps at 15, 40 and 60 Arcane.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Altus Tunnel** is a Location and Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A crystal mine in central Altus Plateau south of the Minor Erdtree (Altus Plateau). The mine is populated by crystal miners, who appear to be overseen by marionettes.

The tunnel is connected to the Perfumer's Grotto, with a large cavern joining the two dungeons. A malformed creature from the stars dangles from the ceiling in this space. It is not possible to reach the Perfumer's Grotto side of the cavern from Altus Tunnel, however.

sections.heading: Altus Tunnel
sections.text: Found at the bottom of the lift at the start of the dungeon.

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.text: - Crystalian (Spear) & Crystalian (Ringblade)

- Avionette Soldier
- Crystal Snail
- Withered Astel

- Arsenal Charm +1

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Albinauric Rise** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A sorcerer's rise on the east side of Consecrated Snowfield, the Albinauric Rise was the tower of an Albinauric who studied the Primeval Current. It contains a Graven Mass, a conglomerate of lesser sorcerers said to be the seed of stars. The entrance to the tower is sealed, and a puzzle must be solved to open it. Phantom Imps will spawn continuously around the outside of the tower.

A statue depicting two fighting imps offers a clue to the solution. Using a Bewitching Branch or several Crystal Darts on one will cause it to become hostile towards the other Imps, causing them to fight, unlocking the door. Alternately, the Fanged Imp Ashes can be used to summon a spirit Imp to fight the others, also resulting in the door becoming unsealed.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Elder Albinauric
- Heretical Rise
- Mirage Rise
- Pidia, Carian Servant

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ainsel River Main** is a subregion in Elden Ring. It is found along the underground Ainsel River.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The northern area of Ainsel River, which encompasses Nokstella, Eternal City. The Ainsel River Main is the beginning of the path leading to the Moonlight Altar, a key location in Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Connected areas
sections.text: This area can be reached in two ways. Progressing Ranni the Witch's storyline until the Fingerslayer Blade to her will unlock Renna's Rise, which houses a portal to this location. Otherwise, a coffin found on the southern shore of the shallow lake in Deeproot Depths will let one arrive here without helping Ranni.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**"Champion's Song"** is an info item and painting in Elden Ring.
Depicts the scene of a Hero's Grave with the razor sharp rocks of Mt. Gelmir looming in the distance, with Volcano Manor as its crown.

Leads to the Harp Bow.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Altus Plateau
- Acquired from interacting with the painting found in a wooden structure north of the Shaded Castle Ramparts Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Allows the Player to perceive the soul of a painter and retrieve a unique item from their location.
The location being the point of perspective depicted by the painting itself.

The soul in question can be found east of the Sainted Hero's Grave on a hill facing west above the Rampartside Path Site of Grace.

The painter is initially invisible when viewed from a distance but will eventually reveal themselves as the player gets physically closer to them. Successfully locating the spirit will make it dissipate before leaving the Harp Bow for the player to pick up from the ground.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - This painting's name, "Champion's Song" is likely a reference to its reward, the Harp Bow. *"Troubadours sing tales of champions, both in the honorable service of the Erdtree, and the one who spurns honor for blasphemy."* Befitting of its depiction of a mausoleum for heroes who served the Erdtree and the visage of Volcano Manor, a site of blasphemous recusants.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Affinities** are a mechanic in Elden Ring that alters a weapon's properties after applying Ashes of War.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.text:
All Affinities except for Standard, Heavy, Keen, and Quality (the "basic four") will prevent Weapon Buffs from being applied to a weapon (except for those applied via a skill), and will also limit the amount of compatible skills.
- More specifically:
  - Magic and Cold skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Magic or Cold affinity.
  - Fire and Flame Art skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Fire or Flame Art affinity.
  - Lightning and Sacred skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Lightning or Sacred affinity.
  - Poison, Blood, and Occult skills and affinities are only compatible with affinities and skills of the "basic four" affinities or those of Poison, Blood, or Occult affinity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Standard** is an affinity in Elden Ring.

This is the default affinity of all infusable weapons except for the Butchering Knife, which is Sacred by default. It provides a weapon's default scaling modifiers, a mix of Strength-scaling and Dexterity-scaling.

The Standard Affinity is compatible with all Skills by default, even without any of the Whetblades. It is the affinity of all Ashes of War exclusive to ranged weapons (Light Bows, Bows, and Greatbows), and to Perfume Bottles Shadow of the Erdtree and Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree weapons.

It's also the affinity of the vast majority of shield and parry Ash of Wars (mostly exclusive to Small Shields, Medium Shields, Greatshields, and Thrusting Shields, though the latter two cannot accept parry-based ashes) except for Ash of War: Carian Retaliation and Ash of War: Thops's Barrier (both Magic affinity), and Ash of War: Golden Parry, Ash of War: Holy Ground, and Ash of War: Vow of the Indomitable (all three Sacred affinity).

sections.heading: Locked weapons
sections.text:
A few weapons are upgraded with regular Smithing Stones but cannot have their affinity changed from Standard.

These include the Crystal Knife and Ivory Sickle Daggers, the Ripple Blade Axe, the Troll's Hammer Colossal Weapon, the Treespear Great Spear, and the Ripple Crescent Halberd Halberd.

sections.heading: Bullet skill-scaling
sections.text: For any skill with damage separate from the weapon itself, such as Skill: Beast's Roar and Skill: Flame of the Redmanes, it provides neutral scaling for Intelligence-, Faith-, and Arcane-scaling skills but slightly decreased scaling for Strength- and Dexterity-scaling skills.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Arena Combat** is a mode where players can compete against other players in ritual combat. There are different modes and venues to chose from and the more Victories a player claims, the higher they'll increase in rank, though there are currently no practical rewards for competing in Arena Combat. Players have some control of whom they can connect with through the use of passwords.

sections.heading: Colosseums
sections.text:
There are three colosseums scattered across the Lands Between, each provide their own mode, their own respective venue to fight in and each venue has it's own music track playing in the background.

After interacting with each colosseum's respective registration altar, players can freely access each venue and each mode from the Roundtable Hold by interacting with Marika's Effigy, it is found next to the fireplace in the same room as the Table of Lost Grace.

sections.heading: Arena Ranks
sections.text:
Each Colosseum have ranks that track the results of combatants for Duels, United Combat/Combat Ordeal and Spirit Ashes allowed.
There are five ranks for each mode. A combatant's rank will be displayed next to their character's name, it can also be found outside of combat, in the Arena's lobby menu.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Patch 1.09 added invulnerability-frames as combatants re-spawn after death.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Acquired by choosing the *Age of the Stars* when completing the game.

To unlock this ending, complete Ranni the Witch's questline by placing the Dark Moon Ring on her finger at the Moonlight Altar. After winning the Final Battle, touch the blue Summoning Sign that appears next to Fractured Marika.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Ranni's Summoning Sign is unavailable if the player has been embraced by the Three Fingers. To lift the restriction, use Miquella's Needle when prompted to at the arena of Dragonlord Placidusax.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Acquired after defeating the Ancestor Spirit in the Southern Hallowhorn Grounds of Siofra River.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **ancient ruins** (古遺跡, *Furui Iseki*), also known as **giant ruins** (巨大な古遺, *Kyodai na Furui Iseki*), are recurring structures found throughout the Lands Between in Elden Ring. They were seemingly built by the ancient civilization associated with the ruins at **Rauh** (ラウフ, *Rau**fu**,* possibly *Lauf*).

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The ancient ruins are enormous megastructures scattered throughout and incorporated into the Lands Between. They typically consist of repeating octagonal pillars and arches made from black stone that is generally darker than the surrounding natural rock formations. Many of these ruins are so deeply embedded within the earth that they seem to predate the very lands above them, suggesting that parts of the Lands Between rest atop artificial platforms. Though the Ancient Ruins of Rauh are the most intact of these structures, other examples are found throughout Limgrave, Caelid, and the Mountaintops of the Giants, within the Ruin-Strewn Precipice, and at the Rauh Base. The Divine Towers and even the pillar that the Forge of the Giants rests upon use the same architectural style.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The ancient ruins are remnants of a prehistoric empire that spanned the entire Lands Between. The Rauh civilization predated the hornsent and was one of the earliest in the realm, rivalling the Ancient Dynasty and Farum Azula. According to hornsent scholars, the inhabitants of Rauh practised a form of spiritual manipulation, with their most well-known artifact being the Spritestone, which could manipulate the moment when a spirit vanished. These were crafted from Rauh Burrows, stones with small, nest-like holes meant to be inhabited by tiny spirits called 'sprites', enabling them to function as ritual implements. The Rauh people also used Dewgems as an ingredient in sprite medicine. These secrets were thought lost to time until their rediscovery at Rauh by hornsent archaeologists.

Statues of a mysterious woman with a great octagonal crown are prominently featured throughout the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to this goddess-like figure. The Verdigris Discus can be found under one of these statues. The Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook 2 and the Bondstone are located beneath another, held by the corpse of a hornsent. In addition, female figures with pointed headpieces and long side veils are represented in other artistic reliefs at the Rauh ruins.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Highroad Cave — a Guardian Golem protects black stone structures buried in the earth. These structures are built at the junction where the inland sea meets the Murkwater river that runs south through Agheel Lake and feeds into the sea via another set of Rauh arches.

- Limgrave — structures are found along the southwest coast of Limgrave, bridging the chasm that separates the region from the Weeping Peninsula.

- Weeping Peninsula — a row of black stone structures cross through Tombsward Ruins in western Weeping Peninsula.

- Wailing Dunes — large arches of black stone emerge from the plateau, running east into the sea. This structure was likely once continuous with the corresponding sections at the Mohgwyn Palace deep underground.

- Ruin-Strewn Precipice — appears to be a great dam positioned at the point where the Altus Plateau meets Liurnia of the Lakes. It is connected to the Seethewater river, which originates in Gelmir and floods the lower region.

- Mountaintops of the Giants — black stone megastructures are present along the stretch of the frozen river that crosses the Mountaintops of the Giants and a valley in the Consecrated Snowfield where a large number of Guardian Golems protect it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Rauh civilization created colossal golems from stone and lava. These Guardian Golems are commonly found near their ruins. Their great arrows are imbued with ancient magic and generate tempestuous gusts of wind.
- Flowing water is a persistent motif in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The location features numerous Dewgems and waterfalls, and irrigation channels bisect its paved roadways.
  - The Guardian Golem at Highroad Cave drops the Blue Dancer Charm related to the blind swordsman who defeated the ancient rot god.
  - The giant stone arches may have been constructed to divert rivers or regulate water flow, possibly to mitigate the impact of erosion or prevent the accumulation of stagnant water.
- The Rauh civilization used heftiness to represent the burden of the strong to protect others.
  - "Heft" was later used to describe the Giant's Red Braid, Thorned Whip, Prelate's Inferno Crozier, and Giant-Crusher, among others. The Fire Prelates, who revered the Fire Giant, used heftiness to symbolize the weight of their duty. Many Fire Monks later abandoned their posts to serve the "weighty" Black Flame.
- Rauh is internally referred to as モヘンジョダロ, *Mohenjo-Daro*, an ancient ruin of the real-world Indus Valley Civilization, one of the earliest cities ever built.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **ancient dynasty** was a faction mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Ancient dynastic ruins are white stone structures with rectangular floorplans and simple rounded columns with square pedestals and Corinthian capitals. The dynasty produced a large variety of obelisks and other stelae depicting trees, beasts, and seated ancestors. Other artifacts featured stone coffin arks and bulls bearing great rings upon their backs. The ancient dynasty erected countless statues of a one-eyed, bearded elder clutching a stone tablet engraved with a tree, while another bearing a sun or star-shaped map lay discarded at his feet.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
In times of old, long before the age of the Erdtree, a great tree-tending dynasty flourished in the Lands Between. They emphasized ancestor observation and the cultivation of trees, and venerated a bearded elder who discarded one of two stone tablets. Their civilization constructed significant landmarks along the banks of the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers, such as the Grand Cloister, Uld Palace Ruins, and Mohgwyn Palace.

The ancient dynasty documented the enormous stone coffins that washed ashore the Cerulean Coast, arriving since the era when Death was burned in ghostflame. The vessels featured pallbearers, statues of the dynastic god, and heroic scenes, though the tainted heroes interred within had congealed into a putrescent liquor. The remains were given equal treatment in death by the Deathbirds, until the practice ended.

Claymen armed with blue glowing weapons fashioned from sharpened meteoric ore served the ancient dynasty. These priests searched for revelations on behalf of their masters, casting magical bubble sorceries. They once received oracles through their bubbles.

The ancient dynasty eventually collapsed, buried in the lightless depths deep underground. Their ancient bowers petrified, turning to stone. Despite their masters' absence, the Claymen priests—warped and bowed with age—continued searching their bubbles for lost oracles as the world carried on without them.

The dynastic ruins were later inhabited by Ancestral Followers and Kindred of Rot. During the Shattering, Luminary Mohg sought to establish his own Mohgwyn Dynasty at the Mohgwyn Palace.

sections.heading: Members
sections.text:
- Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statue, clutching a tablet
- Clayman
- Putrescent Knight
- Putrescent Rotmound
- Putrescent Skeleton

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The one-eyed Bearded Elder presumably founded the dynasty. His statues are found on stone coffins and in the ruins of dynastic sites. None of the Hallowhorn Grounds in the Siofra River area contains bearded elder statues; instead, they venerate hallowed Horned Remains of long-lived stags.
- Their use of fishing equipment like Clayman's Harpoon indicates they lived along a body of water.
- The dynasty either arrived in the Lands Between in the stone coffins or sent them off to sea. Claymen either formed from putrescence or became putrescent over the ages, respectively.
- The Claymen priests presumably search for Oracle Envoys, whose appearance heralds the arrival of a new god or age. Oracle Envoys blow into golden horns to produce music and golden bubble magic. The Envoy's Greathorn casts Unique Skill: Great Oracular Bubble, which has the same title as the Great Oracular Bubble spell cast by Claymen.
  - They likely also search for Metyr, Mother of Fingers, who communicated with the Greater Will through her bubble-like microcosm before she was broken and went into hiding long ago.
  - Ancestral Followers use Greathorn Hammers and Winged Greathorns in their rituals, linking the term to ancient dynastic sites.
- Ancient dynasty ruins stood above ground in the past because they grew trees, and the "lightless depths" are their grave. They may have had a long-forgotten conflict with Astels, as they used meteorites and an Alabaster Lord and Withered Astel dwell within the Lake of Rot and Uhl Palace Ruins (south), respectively.  Astel, Naturalborn of the Void (grace) can only be reached by descending the waterfall at the Grand Cloister and traveling further downstream. It's also possible the ruins were buried at the same time as the nearby Eternal Cities.
- The obelisk scenes with the elder reaching into the branches of the tree to present something to a maiden also appear at the center of Erdtree Greatshields, carried by the Tree Sentinels. The Erdtree Greatshield condenses two frames into a single image, depicting an elder and a maiden beside a tree. The elder reaches his right arm into the boughs, his left hand resting on the pommel of a sword that serves as a cane.
- The Four Belfries bear carvings of the Bearded Elder emerging from leafless branches. These structures are more architecturally sophisticated than those of the ancient dynasty.
- The Suppressing Pillar uses ancient dynasty architecture.
- Miranda Blossoms are sometimes found in their ruins.
