sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Below the rest of the Realm of Shadow, hidden under a sprawling canopy that blots out the light of the sky, a thick swampy woodland corrupted by Madness. The Hornsent Inquisitors stand guard against the horrors within, and the atmosphere is so harrowing that Torrent refuses to be summoned out of fear. Messages on the ground warn about beings lurking in the woods, creatures that cannot be touched and can kill one with a glance.

The Abyssal Woods can only be accessed by navigating through Darklight Catacombs at the base of Recluses' River in Scadu Altus.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ancient Dragon Cult**, also simply known as the **Dragon Cult**, is a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The ancient dragon cult is devoted to the worship of the ancient dragons. The religion plays a deep, long-standing role in the history of the Beastmen of Farum Azula, while its practice amongst humans was established more recently. The cult was based in Leyndell, Royal Capital, and championed by Godwyn the Golden in collaboration with Ancient Dragon Lansseax and Dread Fortissax after the conclusion of the war between Leyndell and the Ancient Dragons. Its equipment and incantations heavily base themselves on the Ancient Dragons and emulate their ability to conjure lightning.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The gold-worshipping capital of Leyndell was attacked by a legion of Ancient Dragons, led by the colossal Ancient Dragon Gransax. Gransax's assault would be the only time in the historical record that Leyndell's walls had fallen and marked the dawn of the war against the ancient dragons. This brutal war ended with Godwyn's triumph over and immediate peacemaking with Ancient Dragon Fortissax.

The implementation of the faith in Leyndell would be supported largely by the arguement that the worshipping of the ancient dragons did not clash with belief in the Erdtree, as the very scales of the ancient dragons, and lightning itself, were both imbued with gold. Ancient Dragon Lansseax, sister of Fortissax, assumed the form of a humanoid priestess to teach the blessings of the Ancient Dragons to Leyndell's inhabitants, bolstering its defenses with lightning.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Age of the Duskborn** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Age of the Duskborn represents a potential future for the Lands Between in which the Rune of Death is restored to the Elden Ring by the Elden Lord. This allows for the integration of Those Who Live in Death into the Golden Order.

This is made possible through the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince gestated by Fia, Deathbed Companion, after transferring her accumulated heroic lifeforce to the Prince of Death—the soulless body of Godwyn the Golden.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Age of the Duskborn is an "Elden Lord" ending and will unlock the Elden Lord achievement.
- This ending is achieved by completing Fia's questline and using the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince to finish the game at Fractured Marika.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Age of Order** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Age of Order envisions a future for the Lands Between in which the Golden Order is perfected. By incorporated the Mending Rune of Perfect Order into the Elden Ring, the Elden Lord establishes a harmonious and immutable Order to govern all.

This ending is made possible by the revelations of Goldmask, a noble philosopher who attained enlightenment and uncovered the means to achieve this absolute state of Order.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Age of Order is an "Elden Lord" ending and will unlock the Elden Lord achievement.
- This ending is achieved by completing Brother Corhyn and Goldmask's questline and using the Mending Rune of Perfect Order to finish the game at Fractured Marika.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Age of the Stars** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The "Age of the Stars" ending sees The Tarnished aid Ranni the Witch in ousting Marika and remaining at her side as Ranni's first Elden Lord.

The Tarnished helps Ranni fulfill her vision of a Lands Between without the Golden Order by allowing her to replace Marika in godhood and takes the role of her consort. Ranni ushers in a new order not of gold, but of the stars and moon of the chill night. Rather than make herself and her order objects of worship, she chooses instead to keep her order and the Lands Between at a great divide, removing the certainties of faith that had existed during Marika's rule.

The Tarnished and Ranni leave the Lands Between, embarking on a thousand-year voyage into darkness under the wisdom of the Dark Moon. Even if life and souls are one with the order, it will be out of sight, emotion, faith, and touch.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - If Ranni's blue summon sign is present at the Stone Platform and selected instead of Fractured Marika, the Age of the Stars ending will begin.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancient Dragon-Man** is an Invader and optional Enemy boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Ancient Dragon-Man is enountered twice in the Gravesite Plain—once as an Invader and once as a formal boss. His Invasion triggers on the road southwest of the  Pillar Path Waypoint Site of Grace. He is fought up the hill past Igon, who audibly cowers on the ground. The boss version is encountered at the bottom of the Dragon's Pit. Defeating him opens the path to the Foot of the Jagged Peak, which connects to Charo's Hidden Grave and the Jagged Peak.

Formerly a drake warrior who hunted colossal dragons, the Ancient Dragon-Man partook in the original form of Dragon Communion by consuming a jagged Rock Heart. He took on the stony form of a small, bipedal ancient dragon and became the arbiter of those worthy to devour Bayle the Dread.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
- Wields the Dragon-Hunter's Great Katana and Dragon Communion Seal.
- Uses the Magma Breath and Dragonmaw Incantations.
- Prefers two-handed jumping attacks and Dragonwound Slash.
- Has transformed using a Rock Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Ancient Dragon-Man has a single Flask of Crimson Tears.
- He has 0 Poise and 0% Damage Negation for each Damage Type.
- Draconic Tree Sentinels also became dragons to better fight dragons.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
It is possible to defeat the Ancient Dragon-Man without having leveled up or upgraded one's Weapons, Flasks and even Scadutree Blessings with relative comfort through the use of spamming the crouching light attack from Whips. As its long reach, fast attack-speed, low stamina-consumption and early stamina-regeneration, combined with the Ancient Dragon-Man's non-existent poise, allows the player to consistently harass him from a relatively safe distance without needing to worry about him trying to excessively dodge and then rush the player down like conventional projectiles from spells or bows would.

The player can increase their un-upgraded weapon's damage-output through the use of Blood Loss, Frostbite and Poison procs that are then immediately followed by the use of the Skill, The Poison Flower Blooms Twice as a third source of blood loss-like burst-damage.

The most efficient set-up for this would be to have two different whips they can alternate between. Hoslow's Petal Whip and Thorned Whip are excellent choices as they can both have their Affinities changed through the use of Ashes of War, while at the same time preserving their innate blood loss buildup no matter what affinity is chosen. So one Poison whip with Ash of War: The Poison Flower Blooms Twice and a Cold whip with almost any ash of the user's choosing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - His humanoid appearance is that of a bald, middle-aged man with a wide jaw-line, while also carrying many visual traits distinctive to the Draconian race, such as their stone-black skin and eyes with grey irises and blood-red sclera.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ancient Ruins of Rauh** (ラウフの古遺跡, *Rau**fu*** *no Furui Iseki*, possibly Lauf), also known as the **Rauh Ruins**, is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Ancient Ruins of Rauh is an area defined by verdant life and flowing water. It features numerous waterfalls and pools where Dewgems grow in abundance, and its paved roadways are bisected by irrigation channels. This massive stone complex was once part of a ancient civilization that spanned the entire Lands Between, but it has since flooded, split in half, and became overgrown with plants and wildlife.

The Ancient Ruins of Rauh is perched high above the Rauh Base, and connected via bridge to the Shadow Keep in the east. It comprises the upper section of the Rauh Ruins, located within the Land of the Tower.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The ancient Rauh civilization predated the hornsent, and rivaled the Ancient Dynasty and Farum Azula as one of the earliest cultures to emerge in the Lands Between. The primordial Crucible of life flourished and likely originated in Rauh, and, according to legend, the "mother of all Crucibles" first appeared on the Giants. Its influence mutated the local wildlife to grow aspects of other creatures, such as horns and feathers. The area was suffused with such potent spirituality that an acrid Spirit Calculus formed on its inhabitants over time.

According to hornsent scholars, the inhabitants of Rauh practiced a form of spiritual manipulation. Their most well-known artifact was the Spritestone, also known as "bondstone," which could manipulate the moment when a spirit vanished. These spritestones were crafted using Rauh Burrows, oval-shaped stones modeled with small, nest-like holes at their center to be inhabited by spirits, enabling them to function as ritual implements. Bondstones were large burrowstones with a white gem obtained from polishing a special crystal. These were used to control the explosions of spiritual powers, thus determining the moment when the bond with the spirit would be broken.

For unknown reasons, the civilization of Rauh collapsed, and the city fell into ruin. It was split in two by a great chasm and became flooded and densely overgrown with vegetation. The secrets of spiritual bonding were lost to time.

sections.heading: Hornsent
sections.text: After their rise to power, the hornsent made expeditions to the Rauh ruins. They sought to understand the secrets of antiquity because these ruins were strongly associated with the Crucible that they held sacred. They erected the Church of the Bud in the Rauh ruins. The structure was known for its flowers and featured a large ornamental bud and stone platform for viewing adjacent Belurat and Enir-Ilim. Whether intentional or not, it was constructed atop a divine element. Later, hornsent archaeologists rediscovered the process for making spritestones and other forgotten spiritual arts.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.text:
During Messmer's Crusade, his army marched toward Enir-Ilim through the ruins of Rauh. They razed the Church of the Bud and installed the Sealing Tree on the stone platform. However, the ruins were preserved due to the intervention of Fire Knight Salza, who defied orders to burn them. Messmer's forces collected large horned beasts and tanglehorned giants from the ruins for the Specimen Storehouse instead.

As the Church of the Bud burned around her, Romina sat on the ground, clutching the bud in speechless silence. She discovered a twisted divine element in the ashes and modified it into the scarlet rot. After the Battle of Aeonia, Romina summoned and soothed Malenia's unwanted butterflies, who allowed her to practice an ancient purification ritual once lost to time. Her actions imbued the church's flowers with scarlet rot, caused local Spider Scorpions to grow in size, and transformed the landscape surrounding the Church of the Bud into a scarlet rot swamp.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text: The ruins are a lush oasis of green in the dour Realm of Shadow. Their sanctity is ensured by Fire Knight Salza, who guards the west entrance to the city. The eastern section of the complex is home to many Bloodfiends and horned beasts. The subterranean structures are excavated by Shadow Undead in search of the secrets of Rauh. The western half of the ruins are dominated by a Servants of Rot cult led by Romina, Saint of the Bud. The waters in this section are stagnant, festering pools of rot. Like the Scarlet Buds of the Church, the bodies of the Kindred of Rot have turned bright scarlet, indicating their acceptance by Romina. The ruins are also home to many Spider Scorpions and other creatures touched by the Crucible.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- **Internal Name**: モヘンジョダロ, *Mohenjo-Daro*, an ancient ruin of the real-world Indus Valley Civilization.
- A small portion of this area is accessible early by traveling through the Sending Gate at the Fifth Belfry, located behind Castle Ensis on the Scadu Altus.
- Statues of a mysterious woman wearing a great octagonal crown are prominently featured throughout the ruins. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to the "Rauh goddess" figure. The Verdigris Discus can be found under one of these statues, while the [[Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook 2|Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook [2]]] and the Bondstone are located beneath another, held by the corpse of a hornsent. In addition, female figures with pointed headpieces and long side veils are represented in other artistic reliefs in the architecture.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword** is a Colossal Sword, a melee armament in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Ruined Forge of Starfall Past
- The Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword is obtained upon examining the forge altar at the Ruined Forge Starfall Past.
- The altar is found on the second level. To reach the altar, you must pull the lever to make the iron door rise, and use it as a platform to jump across to the second level where the altar is.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot be buffed or infused.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This weapon is buffed by the Magic Scorpion Charm however it should be noted that it only increases the innate magic damage present on the weapon and not the full damage produced by the White Light Charge skill.

- It makes a great use of the Spear Talisman since its moveset consist of many trusting attacks.

- Leans slightly more towards Strength than Faith, though Faith scaling becomes stronger than Strength after the latter reaches 60. Additionally, Holy damage is easier to increase than Physical.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Likely inspired by , wherein Neolithic stone tools were mistaken for the weapons of the gods by later discoverers, unaware of human prehistory.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Aged One's Exultation increases attack power by +20% for 30 seconds when madness is triggered near the player.
  - This buff may be stacked with Black Dumpling and Madding Hand for a total of +41.9% attack power.
  - This buff is reduced to +12% in PvP.
- It is highly effective against enemies that induce Madness.
- Pairs well with builds utilizing frenzy-inducing abilities or spells.
- The buff persists after removing the talisman.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ailment Talisman** is a talisman in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Ailment Talisman is found in the Gravesite Plain at the Abandoned Ailing Village. It is located on a corpse at the edge of an unfinished wooden bridge.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Ailment Talisman provides ~+350 resistance to a specific status effect after being afflicted.
  - Poison / Scarlet Rot resistance lasts for 120 seconds.
  - Frostbite resistance lasts for 45 seconds.
  - Hemorrhage, Sleep, and Madness resistance last for 30 seconds.
  - Death Blight is not affected, as its onset kills the player.
- The buildup or duration of the triggering ailment is immediately reduced by a certain amount.
- This talisman is especially useful in areas or encounters where specific ailments are prevalent.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Prior to Update 1.13, the buildup of a status effect was not reduced when the Ailment Talisman was triggered.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **lightless abyss**, also known as the **lightless void** or the **lightless dark**, is an unseen location in Elden Ring. It exists outside the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A lightless void lay at the end of the primeval current, deep within the cosmos beyond the Lands Between. The Greater Will's vast darkness held the many-colored remnants of countless shattered stars, and from it were born Astel and the Fallingstar Beasts.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This void was likely also the birthplace of Maris, Fathom of Night, Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and the Elden Beast.
- Metyr was once able to communicate with the Greater Will directly through the power of her microcosm.
- It may be the origin point, or end, of the Primeval Current.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The lightless abyss may be a black hole or a cosmic void.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancient Dragon Gransax** was a character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Gransax was an enormous ancient dragon who wielded a great spear modeled after a spiraling bolt of yellow lightning.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: During the early Age of the Erdtree, Gransax attacked Leyndell, breaching the walls of the Royal Capital and triggered the War of the Ancient Dragons. During his assault, the knights of the Erdtree employed Golden Lightning Fortification, an Erdtree Worship incantation, to shield themselves from his red lightning. Gransax was ultimately defeated, frozen in place at the Fortified Manor. In the aftermath, a faction of Tree Sentinels concluded that the only way to protect the Erdtree was to transform into dragons themselves, becoming the malformed Draconic Tree Sentinels.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Gransax's immense stone body lies where he fell in Leyndell, Royal Capital, at the Fortified Manor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- It is unclear what exactly prompted Gransax and the ancient dragons to descend from Farum Azula and attack the Royal Capital.
- Gransax is approximately 328 meters in length—nine times larger than the standard ancient dragon.
- Gransax's body is partially buried in ash in Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Bolt of Gransax is one of the legendary armaments required for the achievement.
- Gransax (~328m) dethroned the Dragon God (182m) from *Demon's Souls* as the largest dragon in a FromSoftware game. However, with the release of Shadow of the Erdtree, Gransax lost this title to the colossal drake (~392m) located at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ancient Dragon Knight** is an unseen character in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The nameless ancient dragon knight was a Leyndell Knight who joined the Ancient Dragon Cult that formed in Leyndell following the War of the Ancient Dragons. This cultist was privy to the surreptitious secrets of the ancient dragons' red lightning.

After Godwyn the Golden transformed into the Prince of Death, his personal guard journeyed to the Realm of Shadow in search of a cadaver surrogate. The ancient dragon knight followed the Death Knights on their quest to bring about the coming Age of the Duskborn.

The ancient dragon knight authored the Ancient Dragon Knight's Cookbook, which documented techniques for crafting Red Lightning Pots, Dragonbolt Grease, and Drawstring Dragonbolt Grease. Pages of this tome are found in the Fog Rift Catacombs and Scorpion River Catacombs.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **ancestral followers**, also known as the **horned folk**, are a faction in Elden Ring. They reject the advancements of society and worship the ancestral spirits.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The blue-eyed ancestral followers are robust, brawny humanoids with bluish, bruise-colored skin and silvery gray hair. Their muscular bodies outsize their heads and their faces are brightly painted white with red designs. While they do not exhibit the natural horn growth they venerate, they emulate its presence with headbands.

The horned folk do little to modify what nature had given them, using minimally-procesed organic materials like bone and animal pelts for their  weapons and attire.Their great horned headbands were spoils harvested from dead beasts. Warriors carry hefty weapons imbued with ancient spiritual power, taken from the remains of herbivorious beasts. They do not sharpen their crushing jawbone axes and their arrows capitalize on the natural puncturing ability of animal fangs.

They wear protective necklaces and horn charms to boost their focus and ward off disease and other maladies. Mottled accrouments with vivid and varied coloration are most precious to the followers. The Shamans wear Shining Horned Headbands adorned with fingerprint talismans, likely made from putrescence or Silver Tears.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
<section begin="Bio" />The horned folk rejected writing and metalworking in all its forms, living in primitive hunter-gatherer communities among dynastic ruins and ancient bowers. They worshipped the spirits of herbivorous beasts, a deeply-rooted faith that operated beyond the purview of Marika's Golden Order. They distanced themselves from the Erdtree, waiting for new buds to sprout in the Lands Between.<section end="Bio" />

The horned folk recognized Death as a means to gain power. They knew life sprung forth from both birth and death, and that it could bud from their very souls. They revered the radiant antlers of long-lived stags, from which which new life blossomed endlessly until the beast became an Ancestor Spirit.

The rituals of the followers tapped into the spiritual energy that dwelled within the bones of beasts. In these ceremonies, they stamped their feet in syncopation with a beautiful lullaby sung by exalted shamans. The head of an ancestral infant was swung like a censer to produce a mist of blue spirit vapor that sapped souls and siphoned vitality. Any life that showed no signs of budding was culled in the miasma by warriors wielding greathorns that resembled the wings of an envoy.

The ancestral followers were master hunters who shared a bond with beasts. Normally timid creatures, such as deer and sheep, remained unafraid in their presence. Many animals accompanied them as they foraged through the wooded areas. Living in idyllic harmony with herbivorous creatures, they made their home among the underground ruins of the ancient dynasty along the banks of the Siofra River.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The ancestral followers near the Hallowhorn Grounds (South) are spectral and glow with blue light. They are invisible to those far away.
  - The blood of the ancestral followers is red, however, the blue spirit followers bleed white.
- The song of the shamans draws blue spirit energy into the bodies of nearby followers. The horns of those who hear it siphon spirit energy and illuminate with blue light whenever the follower damages an enemy.
- It can be inferred that they value the Crucible due to their reverence for horns and the spiral.
  - Their practices are similar to the Horn-Calling of the Horned Warriors, but they seem to focus on imbuing the horns with power instead.
  - The ancestral followers once cultivated close ties with a Tarnished and gifted them a Spiralhorn Shield.
  - Despite their indifference the Erdtree, they pray towards the Minor Erdtree in east Liurnia; the local Erdtree Avatar does not attack them.
- The followers distanced themselves from gold, silver, and the ancient smithery, rejecting metalworking altogether.
- The winged greathorn ritual implement is selected for its resemblance to a life-reaping winged envoy.
  - Like Lichdragon Fortissax, this design may echo the wings of the Death Rite Birds. The greathorn hammer vaguely resembles the winged scythe, which is said to depict white-winged maidens, who are also messengers of Death.
- The ancestral shamans cradle an infant in their arms, similar to the Abductor Virgins, catacombs sorcerers, the twinned armor, the Gloam-Eyed Queen, and the statue of Marika in the Shadow Keep.
- Blue Spectral Ancestral Followers appear alongside similarly ghostly trees in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ancestral Follower Shamans** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Each cradling an Ancestral Infant's Head, female Ancestral Followers sing to Horned Remains that sprout fresh buds until they become Ancestor Spirits. Brawny, bruise-colored humanoids dressed in primitive animal furs and sandals, Ancestral Follower Shamans have red painted third eyes and wear their long white hair in single uncut braids. Six small fingerprint talismans dangle from their ceremonial antlers, which produce buds that shine with potent spiritual energy.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
The Ancestral Follower Shamans are primarily found near the Hallowhorn Grounds (North) in the  Ancestral Woods section of Nokron, Eternal City. One Shaman is found in the Consecrated Snowfield at the base of a petrified minor Erdtree.

Rotten Ancestral Follower Shamans can be found in unmarked camps throughout the Rotted Woods in Limveld.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Their song provides a buff to nearby Ancestral Follower Warriors that causes their horns to absorb spiritual energy and briefly glow whenever they deal damage. If the song is interrupted or if the Follower strays too far, the bonus is immediately dispelled.
- Unlike the aggressive, bull-like charge of the Warriors, Ancestral Follower Shamans move with a calm and deliberate pace.
- The fingerprint talismans hanging from their antlers are most likely made from putrescence.
- The blue shining buds on the Shamans' headbands are very similar to those found within Night Giants. The giants are also adorned with fingerprint whorls.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - "AncestorBelieverFemale" is the internal name for the Ancestral Follower Shamans.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Age of the Elden Ring** was a time period prior to the events of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The age of the Elden Ring likely refers to an era of Golden Order Fundamentalism spearheaded by Queen Marika the Eternal and her second Elden Lord, King Consort Radagon. This era was marked by worship of the Golden Order and its key fundamentals—the Law of Causality and the Law of Regression.

The cursed twin Demigods Miquella and Malenia were born during this time.

This era ended when Marika shattered the Elden Ring, triggering the Shattering.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Alternatively, the "age of the Elden Ring" may broadly refer to the full span of time between the Elden Beast becoming the Elden Ring and when it is Shattered by Marika.
- Churches dedicated to Radagon, such as the Church of Pilgrimage and Bellum Church, were likely built or converted during this time.
- The Night of Black Knives occured during this time period.

These dire wolves serve as loyal mounts for first-generation Albinauric Archers, who gain mobility by climbing onto their backs.

sections.heading: Notes

- Lobo was the loyal partner of Latenna the Albinauric. He was mortally wounded by Ensha of the Royal Remains on the orders of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.
- Latenna can mount these wolves when she is summoned with her Spirit Ashes. She can only tame unmounted wolves.
- A pack of dire wolves patrol the upper courtyard of Caria Manor, near Royal Knight Loretta.
- The Archers' Wolves may be synonymous with the snow-wolves encountered by Kaiden Sellswords.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Adel, Baron of Night**, also known as **Gaping Jaw**, is a Nightlord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign, encountered on the third night of the Gaping Jaw Expeditions.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adel was a marvel of the natural world—immense, regal, and unrivaled atop his perch. But when the Night's Tide drenched the old island in azure rain, all life withered and perished. Starved of prey, Adel was consumed by an insatiable, ravening hunger that grew into madness.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
He is a monstrous black dragon with a sideways jaw and a bottomless appetite. He harnesses the power of violet-purple lightning during his second phase. As an Everdark Sovereign, Adel moves at light speed and whips up a massive cyclone.

Adel deals  Standard damage on all moves during the first phase. During phases two and three, he can also deal  Lightning damage. He inflicts heavy  Blood Loss buildup on its biting grab attack.

Adel is resistant to  Fire,  Lightning, and  Blood Loss, and fully immune to  Madness. He is vulnerable to  Scarlet Rot,  Frostbite, and  Sleep; however, he is particularly affected by  Poison damage. When the effect is procced, Adel receives the full sum of the damage-over-time upfront, and the next round of status buildup can be applied sooner than usual. However, Adel creates a  Poison hazard by vomiting up the contents of his stomach.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- Night of the Baron (first victory)
- Random Relics
- Murk
- Sovereign Sigils (Everdark Sovereign)

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
- HP (solo): 13,140
- HP (trio): 39,420
- HP (Everdark Sovereign): +25%
- Defense: 100
- Stance: 150
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- Cannot be parried
- Vulnerable to Anti-dragon effects
- Weak spot: Head ≈ +50%
- Gains a temporary Attack Power Up effect after finishing a successful grab attack, indicated by a red aura
  - Adel deals 112% damage for 30 seconds; the effect is increased to 115% damage during the Everdark Sovereign phase 3
- Adel is scripted to stagger when  Poisoned during Phase 1 only. Poison no longer staggers Adel during Phases 2 and 3.
- Grab attack inflicts heavy  Blood Loss buildup and partially restores Adel's HP
- Button-mashing does not help end Adel's grab attacks early

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Damage Types
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (  ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
- Phase 1: No lightning, staggered by  Poison
- Phase 2: Lightning, not staggered by  Poison

sections.heading: Everdark Sovereign
sections.text:
The Everdark Sovereign version of Adel, Baron of Night begins with Phase 2 and transitions to an empowered "Phase 3" fight. Adel gains jagged purple horns on his left and right jaws and is more challenging, utilizing a fully-upgraded moveset.
- This version of the boss does not have the scripted weakness to  Poison because it starts in Phase 2.
- When he reaches 60% HP, Adel teleports uncontrollably, then strikes the earth in a flash of lightning, creating a raging tornado and starting Phase 3.
- Tornado deals  Lightning damage to players outside its ring; the eye of the storm is only safe zone.
- The tornado can be passed through, but it deals damage; use Spiritstreams to jump in unscathed.
- Tornado lasts 60 seconds, and has a 60-second cooldown; it can be activated once every 120 seconds.
- The hurtbox of several attacks is expanded during Phase 3.
- Prefers the triple ground pound over single ground pounds during Phase 3.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Stack  Lightning damage negation.
- Eat nine Stanching Boluses to gain a +9 Resistance to  Blood Loss.
- Hurl Fetid Pots from behind, never near the mouth.
- During the second phase, watch for and avoid spots where the lightning will strike.
- Jump right before the delayed lightning eruption to avoid all earthquake attacks.
- When fighting the Everdark Sovereign, use the Spiritstream jumps to enter the eye of the storm from above. They appear simultaneously with the tornado.
- One of Adel's attacks displaces him far from his target. If he leaves the tornado ring, avoid chasing after him.
- Allies can be freed from Adel's biting grab attack by breaking his stance
- Guardian, Raider, and Wylder can survive the full grab attack.
- During Phases 2 and 3, Adel gains access to a variation of the grab that lasts longer and deals additional damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Age of Plenty** was an era mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.text:
- After: War Against the Giants
- Concurrent: Age of the Erdtree
- Next: Erdtree Worship

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The age of Plenty was a time of bountiful grace and prosperity for the Erdtree civilization at Leyndell, Royal Capital. It was the beginning of Queen Marika's reign as a god.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
When the new age began, the Erdtree flourished with abundance. It secreted primordial life energy in the form of sacred sap, which hardened into an amber that was treasured as the most precious of jewels. These blessings fell like golden tears from its boughs, pooling in flasks or large collection basins. Queen Marika personally bestowed them to her Elden Lord and a chosen few.  These Sacred Tears were worshipped and used to spread the faith in churches across all lands.

During these early days, the Erdtree radiated the gentle warmth of the sun and healed all who basked in its golden glow. Its bark at this time was brown, much like the Minor Erdtrees.

It was thought that the blessed sap of the Erdtree would drip from its boughs forever, but that era of blind belief swiftly came to an end. It was only for a fleeting moment, as is the course of all life. Over time, the Erdtree became more an object of faith.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Gloam-Eyed Queen's god hunt may have occured during the Age of Plenty.
- Messmer's Crusade may have occured toward the end of the Age of Plenty.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Ancient Bowers are enormous stone trees that are found above and below ground, scattered throughout the Abyssal Woods, Consecrated Snowfield, Mohgwyn Palace, and Siofra River. They are varied in size, though each was large enough to be drawn on the world map, with some individuals rivaling Minor Erdtrees in stature. They are the petrified remains of trees grown long before Queen Marika's Erdtree, likely cultivated by the Ancient Dynasty in times of old, given the sacred tree-tending scenes recorded on nearby Obelisk Beacons. Albinaurics, Ancestral Followers, and Spark Orbs commonly dwell among the ancient bowers.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Abyssal Woods
- Ancestral Woods - a sunless forest that still retains a thick canopy of dead branches.
- Consecrated Snowfield - a chill forest of ancient trees accented by red flowers and clusters of Rimed Crystal Buds.
- Mohgwyn Palace - petrified stumps, slacked with the Formless Mother's accursed blood, sprout fresh green buds.
- Siofra River
- Worshipper's Woods

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Japanese kanji for  is also used for the Red-Feathered Branchsword's **ancient** death rituals, the Death Ritual Spear's priests of **old**, and the Flowerstone Gavel's **ancient** flower, which all seem to correspond with the time when Death was burned in Ghostflame.
- "Bower" is derived from the Old English *būr* ("private room/abode/dwelling").
  - Ancestral Follower Warriors often hunt near these trees with Dwelling Arrows.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bandai Namco Entertainment** is a Japanese video game development and publishing company. headquartered in Minato-ku, Tokyo. Bandai Namco Entertainment was formed on March 31, 2006. They are the seventh largest video game development company in the world, in terms of revenue. They are also the publishers of Elden Ring, as well as other FromSoftware titles.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
<noinclude>

The **Bloody Wolf** was one of the five playable characters . Unlike the Prophet and Warrior origins, Bloody Wolf, along with Champion and Enchanted Knight, would not appear in the final game.

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.text:
Though this class isn't available in the final release of the game, it can be recreated.

The weapon and the shield can be acquired early, as the Bastard Sword is bought from the Nomadic Merchant at the  Castle Morne Rampart Site of Grace in the Weeping Peninsula and the Iron Roundshield is bought from the Nomadic Merchant outside of Coastal Cave in western Limgrave.

The Armor Set and the Skill's Ash of War require access to Leyndell, Royal Capital and thus need 2 Great Runes.

<font color="red">WARNING:</font> Both the Armor Set and the Ash of War becomes inaccessible after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade unless you start a new Journey.
The Raging Wolf Set requires completion of the first two invasions as part of Tanith's questline at Volcano Manor to gain the Letter to Bernahl and be able to invade Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm inside of the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital and gain the set.
Ash of War: Thunderbolt meanwhile is dropped by a Teardrop Scarab west-northwest of the  Avenue Balcony Site of Grace, in the courtyard hidden under the gigantic wing of Gransax and is guarded by a Black Dumpling Albinauric.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.text:
The Vagabond origin is arguably the most well-suited for this purpose as it has stats that are very similar to the Bloody Wolf's, can wield the Bastard Sword two-handed without any additional stats (and can wield it one-handed with 2 more points in Strength) and the Iron Roundshield one-handed, and wears an armor set of similar weight. It does however need at least 2 more points in Endurance to wield the weapon and the shield with either Armor Set, without even including Talismans.

The Hero origin, while not quite as suited stat-wise and having worse armor, is still decently suitable as it only needs 1 more point in Dexterity to wield the Bastard Sword and can comfortably wield the weapon and shield without having to increase its Endurance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bloodhound Knights** are enemies and bosses in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Bloodhound Knights are trained as hunters and are known to be unshakable trackers. Without language, they choose their own master whom they will stay loyal to for the rest of their life.

They wield a Bloodhound's Fang alongside a Bloodhound Claw that allows them to slip past an enemy's guard. They use the Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step to either move out of harm's way or to close the gap between them and their opponent quickly.

Lesser variants can be found as non-respawning enemies guarding corpses in the overworld. One is found atop a wall near the gate past the Isolated Merchant at Academy of Raya Lucaria, another is in one of the rooms past the illusory wall in Volcano Manor, a third is guarding Eternal Darkness in Swamp Lookout Tower atop the gate wall near Sellia, Town of Sorcery, and a fourth is guarding the Gelmir Knight Set inside of Gelmir Hero's Grave in a room reached by dropping onto rafters below the Chariot's path.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Bloodhound Knight was found at the Lakeside Crystal Cave exit. It appears to be guarding the location of Latenna the Albinauric, forcing her to stay until the location of the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) has been revealed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wears Bloodhound Knight Helm, Bloodhound Knight Armor, Bloodhound Knight Gauntlets, and Bloodhound Knight Greaves
- Wields Bloodhound's Fang and Bloodhound Claws
- Uses Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step
- The emblem on their cape is a wolf's head surrounded by concentric thorned rings.

sections.text: **Beastman of Farum Azula** are enemies and bosses in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Azula beastmen are anthropomorphic, bestial creatures who reside in Crumbling Farum Azula. They fight using heavy, curved weapons forged from dull iron, and some use shields made from earthenware jars, which are created to make shields. The crumbling ruins of Farum Azula are said to be the remains of a giant mausoleum enshrining an Ancient Dragon, and certain Beastmen, who wield weapons clad in lightning, are chosen to guard it.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Lightly-armored Beastmen clad in ornate golden jewellery. Patches of their flesh are missing, exposing parts of their bones. They can be found wielding curved swords, jar-shields, or sickle-like throwing blades. Grey-haired Beastmen wield Clawmark Seals, which they use to cast lightning incantations. Some beastmen wield weapons imbued with red lightning, which deal lightning damage.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Much larger than the standard variety, these Beastmen are clad in plate armour and wield vast, curved cleavers.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: An armored, cleaver-wielding Beastman found in the Groveside Cave in Limgrave. It is encountered in a wide cavern littered with dead Godrick Soldiers, who appear to have set up a camp before falling victim to the Beastman.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Two Beastmen are encountered in Dragonbarrow Cave in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. One fights from range, using paired throwing knives, while the other uses a large cleaver.

**Astrologer** is one of the starting origins in Elden Ring.

Consider this origin very carefully. While melee and bow fighters are spoiled for choice of weapons and equipment very early on from both loot and stores, you will not get access to effective equipment for spellcasting until you are past at least two major bosses of Margit, the Fell Omen and Godrick the Grafted, where you will be finally able to buy the equipment listed below that the Astrologer starts with. The Sorceress Sellen who will be your main spell teacher is also locked behind a boss fight. Even if you heavily prefer melee or bow combat, it might be worthwhile taking the Astrologer anyways just for the early tactical option of the spells.

When choosing to be an Astrologer i.e. spellcaster, you're going to have to force your "hand preference" and controls based on your intended combat style due to two key spells that hard-force whether your Staff can be in your Right or Left hand, with such spells being blocked from firing in the opposite orientation. Note that the handedness has no effect on the raw strength of spells, nor does 2-handing a staff.

- Scholar's Armament forces you to have the staff in the Left hand in order to be able to enchant a weapon on the Right.
- Scholar's Shield forces you to have the staff in the Right hand in order to be able to enchant a shield on the Left.

Given that you can't have the same staff equipped twice in two different weapon slots and that it is not economical to keep Strengthening two separate staffs as you level up, it is suggested to stick with just one of the above. If you truly detest melee combat except as a last resort and want to stick with spells as much as possible, go with a Right-handed staff to be able to use the shield buff for more defense (which is the Astrologer's default setup when you first start the game). Otherwise, switch the staff to the Left hand and get used to the different activation keys so that you can use the surprisingly powerful weapon buff.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.text: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, the Astrologer is the best choice for essentially any build which focuses mainly on Intelligence, and more specifically the Sorceries. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Intelligence-Strength-Dex
sections.text:
The main goal of this build is to give the Astrologer access to the very powerful spells while simultaneously giving some tactical flexibility in melee and the ability to lure/damage enemies at a range beyond what their spells can reach via a Longbow. If you get your Strength to 20 and Dexterity to 14, you can fully use the Longbow and the Pike, as well as several of the shields that have a 100% Physical damage reduction through guarding like the Heater Shield. However, as an alternate option you can stick with the Pike and Staff build for liberal use of Scholar's Armament, and then you can easily have both spells and melee attacks happening interchangeably along with relying on dodge rolls for defense. In this instance, just remove the shield to reduce your Equip Load; remember that a Shield only helps you, in any way, if you Guard with it. They do not give any bonus passive defenses just from wearing them like Armor does, so you may be better off saving the weight of the Shield and wearing a stronger Armor instead.

You won't really need to push either stat much further than this for a LONG time. Then you can pile on Intelligence, as well as the occasional Vigor, Mind and Endurance for improved HP, FP and Stamina capacity; keep Vigor and Mind up enough so that your HP and FP max capacities are just slightly above what a Flask charge can restore, growing as you upgrade the Flask strength.

Make liberal use of the auto-targeting feature and your range. While not having a particularly fast damage output, Glintstone Pebble is extremely FP-efficient against single targets. Glintstone Arc has identical damage per shot as Pebble but with a higher FP cost and slightly less range, however it can hit small groups of enemies simultaneously which is where it truly shines. Combine these with a careful evasive ranged combat style and a decent Summon, and you can do VERY well for quite some time before you even find another reasonable spell.

Once you've gotten comfortable with the attack patterns of certain enemies you can easily switch to melee with the ultra-long Pike (using the Spear beforehand which is acquired earlier), allowing for efficient kills without burning through too much FP.

One additional benefit of this playstyle is that the equipped weaponry and staves of Magic Users tends to be fairly light, since they can use spell selection to give them a spread of short range and long range combat options. This in turn allows magic users to wear heavier, more protective armor than melee fighters normally would at the same load limit and still maintain good mobility.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Ashes of War** are special items in Elden Ring that can be used to modify the Skills of certain armaments, and (optionally) infuse them with one of a selection of possible Affinities. With any Whetblade, they can be applied to compatible armaments while resting at a Site of Grace, or by Smithing Master Hewg.

Ashes of War are not consumed when applied; rather, they are slotted into the armament, and can be removed at any time.

sections.heading: Usage & Application
sections.text:
Each Ash of War corresponds to a specific Skill, and can only be applied to armaments compatible with that skill; for instance, Ash of War: Piercing Fang can only be applied to weapons capable of thrusting attacks, but Ash of War: Kick can be applied to any melee weapon. Ashes of War also cannot be applied to any weapon that is upgraded using Somber Smithing Stones.

Ashes of War also each have a corresponding "native" Affinity; for instance, Ash of War: Bloody Slash has the Blood affinity. When being applied to an armament, this Affinity can optionally be infused to change the weapon's base damage values, damage scaling, and/or status effect buildups; alternatively, the armament can be left with the Standard affinity to keep the default scaling, and other affinities can be chosen if corresponding Whetblades are held.

Ashes of War can be freely removed from weapons — refunding the Ash and reverting the weapon to its default Skill — or directly transferred between weapons. They can also be duplicated by Hewg with Lost Ashes of War — whether in the inventory or already on a weapon — consuming them in the process.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Ashes of War are most commonly obtained as a drop from certain Teardrop Scarabs; however, they are sometimes contained in chests, sold by merchants, dropped by certain enemies such as Night's Cavalry or the unique Godrick Knight in Fort Haight, or occasionally are available as potential rewards from boss Remembrances — for example, Ash of War: Waves of Darkness from the Remembrance of the Naturalborn.

Additionally, some weapons have Ashes of War pre-equipped on acquisition, such that they can be applied to other weapons or duplicated from them. For example, the Nagakiba has Ash of War: Piercing Fang equipped on acquisition, despite having Unsheathe as its base skill when Piercing Fang is removed; and Backhand BladeShadow of the Erdtree has Ash of War: Blind Spot pre-equipped while simultaneously having Blind Spot as its underlying base skill. This often occurs when the Ash is otherwise impossible to obtain naturally.

sections.heading: Skill Scalings
sections.text:
It depends on the Ash of War individually if the Skill it grants scales with the weapon's attack rating, or your character's stats and the weapon's upgrades.

For example: Ash of War: Lion's Claw will deal over 1000 damage on a Keen-infused +25 Flamberge equipped to a character with 20str/40dex and less than 1000 if the Ash of War's default Heavy-infusion was chosen instead; meanwhile, Ash of War: Ground Slam will deal less damage if any infusion option other than Heavy is chosen, even if the weapon's attack rating would be higher with something else.

sections.heading: Number of Ashes
sections.text:
There are a total of 91 Ashes of War in the Elden Ring base game:

Standard 12, Keen 11, Quality 12, Lightning 3, Magic 10, Sacred 11, Heavy 14, Fire 3, Blackflame/Flame Art 2, Poison 2, Cold 3, Blood 4, Occult 4

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bloody Finger Nerijus** is a mini-boss NPC invader in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A member of the Bloody Fingers, Nerijus is a Tarnished driven mad by bloodlust and in service to Mohg, Lord of Blood.prowls along a shallow river in Limgrave, waiting to ambush Tarnished. When Nerijus attempting to ambush a Tarnished by invading them outside the cave, Yura, who knew him by name, came to the Tarnished's assistance.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.text:
Nerijus will spawn in Limgrave along the riverbed beneath the bridge where the Night's Cavalry spawns at night, just as one nears the Murkwater Cave entrance. Like other NPC invaders, when he arrives, the Tarnished will be unable to use Torrent, leave the immediate vicinity, or enter the cave. He'll spawn at the far end of the riverbed and start running towards the player.

It's recommended to either clear out all Those Who Live in Death near the bridge before spawning Nerijus, as they can be a nuisance while fighting him, You can also avoid them by keeping to the other end of the riverbed, closer to where Nerijus spawns in.

Nerijus is aggressive and armed with a pair of Reduvia daggers that give him a mix of quick ranged and melee attacks that all inflict bleed buildup. However, he is fairly easy to knock around with a two-handed or heavy weapon; his poise is low due to his light armor set. If needing assistance, run back towards the bridge area to buy some time for Bloody Finger Hunter Yura to spawn in, who'll help assist in fighting Nerijus, though he can still be killed by Nerijus. The two of you together can keep him stunlocked with ease.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Bloody Finger Nerijus was named **Nerijus** in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bloody Finger Hunter Yura** is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A ronin warrior in an iron kasa reminiscent of the straw hats worn in the Land of Reeds, Yura was a hunter of Mohg's Bloody Fingers. He understood the hidden dangers of Dragon Communion and was once close to Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, a former Drake Knight for whom he harbored deep feelings. He wielded the unblockable Piercing Fang technique with deadly precision.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
Yura can first be found resting beneath a fallen ruin south of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins in Limgrave. He warns the Tarnished to stay away from Agheel Lake, where Flying Dragon Agheel roosts. However, he offers his aid if the player is brave enough to hunt the mighty dragon. If the Tarnished slays Agheel, Yura speaks of the island Church of Dragon Communion, and cautions against Dragon Communion's corrupting influence.

When the Tarnished is ambushed by Bloody Finger Nerijus on the Murkwater River, Yura intervenes to thwart the invasion. Later, Yura travels to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, where the Tarnished may repay his aid by assisting him against a Ravenmount Assassin. There, Yura urges them to avoid Eleonora, the deadliest of all Bloody Fingers.

Yura ultimately tracks Eleonora to the Second Church of Marika on the Altus Plateau. In their final battle, he suffers a mortal wound to sever the Bloody Finger from her hand. As the Tarnished arrives too late, Yura implores Eleonora to renounce the cessblood before dying in their presence.

After his death, Yura's body becomes host to Shabriri, who claims that Yura willingly surrendered his vessel.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. *(Optional)* Limgrave
  - The following two steps can be completed in either order. His dialogue will vary depending on where he is met first.
  - Yura can be found under a fallen Azula ruin near the  Seaside Ruins site of grace, southwest of Agheel Lake. Exhaust his dialogue and his summon sign will appear in Agheel Lake to assist against Flying Dragon Agheel. Speak to him again after defeating Agheel for further dialogue.
  - Enter the Murkwater River, the ravine north of Agheel Lake, and head towards Murkwater Cave. Bloody Finger Nerijus will invade you. After fighting Nerijus for a while, Yura appears to assist you. After defeating Nerijus, continue along the ravine to find Yura under a bridge. Exhaust his dialogue.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes
  - A red summon sign can be found northeast of the  Raya Lucaria Main Gate. Interact with it to assist Yura in defeating Bloody Finger Ravenmount Assassin. After defeating the foe, Yura can be found on the bridge near where the summon sign was. Speak to him to receive a [[Smithing Stone 5|Smithing Stone [5]]].
1. Altus Plateau
  - Travel to the Second Church of Marika, located northwest of the  Altus Highway Junction site of grace, where Yura lies on the ground. Speak to him, and then pick up the Nagakiba. Shortly after, Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger will invade. Defeat her to receive Eleonora's Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
  - Once you travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, Yura's quest will be locked regardless of which steps have been completed. Shabriri will be waiting near the  Zamor Ruins site of grace, in possession of Yura's reanimated body. The Nagakiba can be found on the ground in whichever location he would have been at, depending on how far into his questline you have progressed.

sections.text: **Black Knife** is a melee armament found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Received upon defeating the Black Knife Assassin in front of Sainted Hero's Grave located in Altus Plateau.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Technically leans towards a pure (80) Dexterity build with its scaling, but practically speaking a hybrid (45/45) Dexterity/Faith build gains about as much Attack Power (AP) while also making the skill stronger since it only scales with weapon upgrade level and the user's Faith.
  - Effectively, the hybrid build loses about 2% AP compared to the pure build (494 AP vs 503 AP) in exchange for gaining about 13% more AP for the initial hit of the skill (969 AP vs 856 AP).
- Despite its often resisted Holy damage this weapon still pulls its weight well due to the percentage-based damage effect its skill also causes, even when dodged through.
  - This health drain effect triggers even when rolled through so to fully avoid it can't be allowed to touch your body when dodged.
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Blade of Calling, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword.
  - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2 due to hitting twice.

The finger bones extend from a starry, knot-like cluster of blue, green, and purple orbs. Wispy white filaments trail from the clump, and a small bony spur sprouts from its surface like a horn. A procession of stars follows from the mass, culminating in dark concentric rings.
  - The orange-hued stars likely represent primordial gold and amber-hued stars, which dictate the fates of the gods.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Azur's Glintstone Staff** is a Glintstone Staff and catalyst found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Found in a secluded room on the highest level of the Church of the Cuckoo. The level can be accessed via the rooftops of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

From the Debate Parlor site of grace, go outside to the left until you meet two Raya Lucaria Sorcerers. Jump down on the stairs next to them. Continue forward until you can jump onto the rooftops. Then, proceed further and go up the ladder at the end of said rooftops.

After the sorcerer, go down on the rooftops again, until you can see a dome-like structure that has windows. Go through one of the windows, and descend onto the lower floor. One of the exits leads to a enclosed bridge, with a High Page guarding the secluded room. The staff is in the room behind him, in front of the inactive School of Graven Mages.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Increases FP cost of Sorceries by 20%, in exchange for speeding up their casting time even more than the Radagon Icon.
  - Casting speed is decreased for any spell cast when this staff is held in one of a character's two active hands, even if this staff isn't used to cast it.
  - Adds 40 "virtual" Dexterity for the purpose of improving casting speed.
  - The casting speed decrease applies to both Incantations and Sorceries but the FP cost increase only applies to Sorceries. This means that Incantation users can keep this Staff in the off-hand with no penalty aside from its weight and taking up an active hand-slot.
- A +10 Azur's Glintstone Staff gains 254 Sorcery Scaling with minimum stats (52 Intelligence), 279 Sorcery Scaling at 60 Intelligence, 320 Sorcery Scaling at 70 Intelligence, and 362 Sorcery Scaling at 80 Intelligence.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Scions of the Eternal Cities, the Black Knife Assassins were a group of women with close ties to Queen Marika the Eternal. Led by Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader, they were coconspirators of Ranni the Witch, who robbed the Rune of Death from Maliketh, the Black Blade. She imbued it into Blades of Calling, fashioning a set of god-slaying Black Knives. The Assassins carried out the Night of Black Knives, carving Cursemarks of Death into Ranni and Godwyn the Golden. They wore silent, silver scale armor and used Concealing Veils to mask their presence, rendering them effectively invisible.

Presently, they are scattered throughout the Lands Between, and can be found in many different regions.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Twenty Black Knife Assassins appear in *Elden Ring*.
  - x2 Malefactor's Evergaol (Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader and Black Knife Tiche)
  - x1 Deathtouched Catacombs
  - x1 Sage's Cave
  - x1 Sainted Hero's Grave
  - x1 Black Knife Catacombs
  - x1 Queen's Bedchamber
  - x1 Ordina, Liturgical Town
  - x1 Ordina, Liturgical Town (dead)
  - x4 Ordina, Liturgical Town (spectral, inside evergaol)
  - x3 Kingsrealm Ruins (slain by War Counselor Iji during his quest)
  - x4 Ranni's Rise (slain by Blaidd the Half-Wolf during his quest)
- At least four Assassins appear around Limveld in Elden Ring Nightreign. Two stalk the streets of Noklateo, the Shrouded City, one roams near the easternmost evergaol, and another acts as the central castle boss.

sections.heading: Overview

sections.heading: Background

This assassin sustained a grievous wound, retreating deep within the Deathtouched Catacombs. Uniquely, her health bar has already been partially depleted before the player arrives so that she starts at 60% HP. She is the only wounded Black Knife Assassin. Although red blood stains her armor, she bleeds darkness on hit.

She drops the Assassin's Crimson Dagger, a Talisman which allows the player to recover HP after performing a critical hit.

sections.heading: Background

An assassin hiding in a small chapel within the Catacombs, concealed behind an illusory wall. As well as dropping the Assassin's Cerulean Dagger, which allows the player to recover FP from critical hits, she also leaves behind a Black Knifeprint, which can be given to Sorcerer Rogier to progress his questline.

D, Hunter of the Dead can be summoned for this fight.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Astel, Naturalborn of the Void** and **Astel, Stars of Darkness** are Bosses in Elden Ring. **Naturalborn of the Void** is a Boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: <section begin="background"/>Far beyond the Lands Between, within the Greater Will's lightless abyss, the many-colored debris of ancient stars coalesced into a malformed creature. A falling star of ill omen, Astel arrived long ago. It assailed an Eternal City with a barrage of meteors, sealing it deep underground, away from the true night sky. The destroyed Nameless Eternal City is probably Noklateo, the Shrouded City.<section end="background"/>

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: <section begin="characteristics"/>A procession of multi-colored orbs, Astel is an aberrant, cosmic entity that resembles a Great Dragonfly. It has a humanoid skull with large mandibles and a large blue eye emerging from a crack in its forehead. It has four translucent insect wings and six skeletal arms that end in human-like hands, the forelimbs each possessing six fingers. Its long tail ends in a spiny scorpion stinger, wielded as a flail. It also casts gravity-based magic and can warp to other parts of the arena.<section end="characteristics"/>

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
Astel, Naturalborn of the Void=

This is an optional boss, but is required to reach Moonlight Altar and achieve a certain ending.

sections.text: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void is encountered in a cavern beyond the Lake of Rot, accessed via a coffin in the Grand Cloister. It makes use of a variety of gravity-based attacks, and can warp to other parts of the arena.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The Fallingstar Beasts are likely another variant of Astel. They have the same head and tails, but the ferromagnetic beasts are covered in stone and iron filings.

- Astel has an unused animation in which it fell from the sky, crashing to the earth like a meteor. This move is used by Starscourge Radahn.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Blaidd the Half-Wolf** is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A guarded and boorish yet fiercely loyal half-wolf, Blaidd was a shadowbound beast, created by the Two Fingers to serve Lunar Princess Ranni when she was chosen as an Empyrean. The wolf was the beast of the Carian royal covenant and irrefutably symbolized the moon's pride, and so he was approved and raised by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon as Ranni's stepbrother.

Blaidd was Ranni's unwavering blade. Like all shadowbound beasts, he could not truly die and was incapable of treachery against his master, compelled to enact her will. Unbeknownst to him, however, an accursed failsafe within shadows overrode this directive should their master turn against the Two Fingers; should Ranni rebel against her prescribed fate, Blaidd’s unwavering loyalty would twist into madness, becoming a Baleful Shadow—a dire threat to Ranni herself.

When Blaidd swore an oath to serve no master other than Ranni the Witch and her Dark Moon, a cold frost magic graced his Royal Greatsword. The cold bothered him, nonetheless.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text: Blaidd searched the Mistwood Ruins for a traitor named Darriwil, and the passage to Nokron, Eternal City, a long-lost ruin said to be banished underground by the Greater Will. He travels to Redmane Castle to participate in the Radahn Festival.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave (Mistwood Ruins)
  - Blaidd can be heard howling in Mistwood. After hearing the howl, speak to Merchant Kalé and select "**About the howling in Mistwood.**" This will unlock the "Finger Snap" gesture.
  - Use Finger Snap at the Mistwood Ruins near the ruined tower adjacent to the slumbering Runebear to cause Blaidd to jump down. Talk to him and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Limgrave (Forlorn Hound Evergaol)
  - Enter the Forlorn Hound Evergaol in Limgrave and defeat Bloodhound Knight Darriwil. Blaidd will be available as a summonable cooperator during this fight.
  - After defeating Darriwil, Blaidd appears outside the Forlorn Hound Evergaol. Speak with him to earn a [[Somber Smithing Stone 2|Somber Smithing Stone [2]]].
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Ranni's Rise)
  - After entering Ranni's service, a projection of Blaidd appears in Ranni's Rise and offers dialogue. This step is skipped if Starscourge Radahn has already been defeated.
1. Siofra River
  - Blaidd moves to the base of an enormous ruined bridge on the bank of the Siofra River, located between the  Siofra River Bank and  Worshipper's Woods Sites of Grace. He will suggest asking Preceptor Seluvis about how to reach Nokron, Eternal City. This step is skipped if Starscourge Radahn has already been defeated.
  - (Optional) After speaking to Seluvis about Nokron and then speaking to Sorceress Sellen, return to Blaidd and exhaust his dialogue. He will move to Redmane Castle afterwards.
1. Caelid (Redmane Castle)
  - Blaidd will appear in the  Redmane Castle Plaza when the Radahn Festival begins. He also appears as an optional summon in the fight against Starscourge Radahn.
1. Caelid (Wailing Dunes)
  - (Optional) After defeating Radahn, speak to Blaidd next to the  Starscourge Radahn Site of Grace. He will mark the location of the *Starfall Crater*—entrance to Nokron, Eternal City—on your map.
1. Limgrave (Forlorn Hound Evergaol)
  - (Optional) Interact with the Forlorn Hound Evergaol to speak to Blaidd. Either choose to release him or leave him.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Three Sisters)
  - After giving Ranni the Dark Moon Ring, Blaidd will appear as a hostile NPC outside Ranni's Rise, surrounded by the bodies of slain Black Knife Assassins. Defeat him to receive his armor and weapon.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Kingsrealm Ruins)
  - (Optional) Speak to War Counselor Iji to deliver the news of Blaidd's death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wields the Royal Greatsword and wears Blaidd's Armor, Blaidd's Gauntlets, and Blaidd's Greaves.
- Similar to the Beast Eye, Blaidd’s eyes are violet. His left eye is partially shut.
- Blaidd revives himself if killed prematurely because he is a Shadowbound Beast; however, he remains hostile until the player uses Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows.
- Blaidd is friends with Merchant Kalé.
- Blaidd rarely interacted with Tarnished before meeting the player.
- During Ranni’s questline, the Tarnished confronts a Baleful Shadow in Nokstella, Eternal City, one of the assassins dispatched by the Two Fingers. This shadow takes Blaidd’s form, though it is not actually him.
- Blaidd kills several Black Knife Assassins during an offscreen ambush at the Three Sisters, which triggers when the player gives Ranni the Dark Moon Ring.
- Baleful Shadows sent after Ranni assume Blaidd's form and appearance.
  - A corpse near Ranni's Rise holds a Black Wolf Mask, nearly identical to Blaidd’s head. The mask likely belonged to an assassin who attempted to approach Ranni by impersonating Blaidd.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Boc the Seamster** or **Demi-Human Boc** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He offers the player the ability to modify their garments, free of charge.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Boc is a demi-human seamster from Limgrave. He was very close to his mother, a seamstress, until her passing. Inspired by her, Boc aspired to follow in her footsteps and inherited her sewing kit. He lived with a demi-human tribe in a Coastal Cave on the western coast of Limgrave, but at some point, he was cast out by his kin. Lost and isolated, Boc was transformed into a bush by a spell.

A Tarnished came across Boc and broke the spell, freeing him. Grateful, Boc offered to sneak back into the cave where he had been exiled to retrieve something precious with which to repay his champion. However, his former tribe discovered him and beat him mercilessly. When the champion found Boc again, he warned them not to enter the cave. Ignoring his warning, the champion avenged Boc and recovered his mother's cherished sewing needle. Moved by their kindness, Boc vowed to become a seamster like his mother.

Boc next encounters the champion in Liurnia of the Lakes, where he humbly offers his services as the champion's personal seamster. He will trace the champion's footsteps, following them to the Altus Plateau and the Royal Capital. Boc remains in awe of his master, and as the Tarnished champion draws closer to the throne of the Elden Lord, Boc will begin to refer to them as a lord.

Even though Boc is given a golden needle worthy of a master seamster, allowing him to perform modifications to the grab of the demigods themselves, Boc remains terribly self-conscious and bothered by his appearance. He asks his master whether they think he is ugly and expresses an interest in being reborn by Queen Rennala. Should the Tarnished champion aid Boc in fulfilling his wish to be reborn, Boc will travel to the Academy of Raya Lucaria and will be reborn a human through her powers. However, like many of those reborn by Rennala, the process goes awry, and Boc dies shortly thereafter.

Instead, the Tarnished champion may find a Prattling Pate which speaks with the voice of Boc's deceased mother, and tells him he's beautiful. Upon hearing this, Boc will be contented and will continue faithfully serving his lord.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave
  - Boc can be found in the form of a small tree near Gatefront Ruins. He will call out until you attack or roll into the tree, reversing the illusion and causing him to transform back.
1. Limgrave (Coastal Cave)
  - Boc can be found lying on the ground beside the Site of Grace at the start of the dungeon. Defeating the Demi-Human Chief dual boss of the area will reward you with the Sewing Needle, which can be given to Boc.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Lake-facing Cliffs)
  - *(Optional)* Boc will be next to the Site of Grace. He will offer to make alterations to your equipment free of charge.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (East Raya Lucaria Gate)
  - *(Optional)* Boc can be given the Gold Sewing Needle, which allows him to alter Demigod equipment. He can be given the item in subsequent steps of his questline instead if this step is missed.
1. Altus Plateau (Altus Highway Junction)
  - *(Optional)* Boc will ask if he can call you Lord at this point if he has already been given the Gold Sewing Needle. Agreeing will unlock the "My Lord" gesture.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (East Capital Rampart)
  - If Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon has been defeated, Boc will ask for a Larval Tear.
  - Giving him a Larval Tear will move him to Raya Lucaria Grand Library. He will appear kneeling on the ground in human form, unresponsive. Upon reloading the area, he will be dead.
  - Refusing to give him a Larval Tear will unlock the dialogue option "What do you really think?". Selecting this option will cause him to die just outside Raya Lucaria Grand Library.
  - Instead of selecting either option, using Prattling Pate "You're Beautiful" in front of him will prevent him from dying. He will remain at East Capital Rampart for the rest of the game.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Boc does not require an Academy Glintstone Key to reach the Raya Lucaria Grand Library.

sections.text:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Aspects of the Crucible: Breath** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Aspects of the Crucible: Breath is acquired upon defeating Tanith's Knight, which can be fought after killing Tanith in Rykard's arena in the Volcano Manor, at the end of her questline.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Creates a large pouch on the caster's neck before breathing out tongues of flame with Fire Attack Power equal to 98% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast.
- Attack Power is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
- Doesn't immediately start to consume FP for the upkeep cost, instead only starting after about 2-3 seconds. This seems to coincide with the initially created throat pouch shrinking to roughly the width of the character's torso.
- The caster must always move forward at a walking pace as long as this spell is being channeled.
- Decent in PvP as a "wake-up" attack (i.e., after an attack that has knocked down an opponent, such as a Critical Attack), since it has a relatively short start-up animation and a wide attack area, which can cause the additional damage needed to finish off a target.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is used by Crucible Axe Knights (except for the two found in Limgrave).
- Aspects of the Crucible: Breath creates a throat pouch similar to those of the basilisks.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Aspects of the Crucible: Horns** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Aspects of the Crucible: Horns is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight in Stormveil Castle, down the outer western rampart. From the Rampart Tower Site of Grace, head north to the walkway with the Warhawks, and drop down to the left at the guard tower. Continue dropping down until you reach a breakable cliff and fall through it to arrive on a cliffside with the Crucible Knight.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
The caster crouches slightly and creates a horn on their shoulder before dashing a few steps forward, hitting with Standard Attack Power equal to 277% of Incantation Scaling upon contact with the horn.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 327% of Incantation Scaling and greatly increases the distance charged, to about three times the previous amount, launching any human-sized foes that are hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 38 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 49 points of Stamina.
- Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 18%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 36%.
- Deals 16 Stance damage when uncharged and 30 Stance damage when charged.
- The charged version of the spell is generally much better than the uncharged version, primarily due to the increased distance traveled and the ability to launch smaller foes into the air.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is used by Crucible Tree Knights, though they summon it on their arm.
  - Despite this, the spell is dropped by a Crucible Axe Knight.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - FP cost was reduced from 20 to 18, and damage to Stamina of guarding enemies was increased from 200 to 240 for the uncharged version and from 260 to 300 for the charged version.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost, increased cast speed, increased the distance traveled when not charged, and made it easier to cause enemies to flinch when charged.
  - FP cost was reduced from 30 to 20.
