sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Aspects of the Crucible: Tail** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is an Erdtree incantation.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Aspects of the Crucible: Tail is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight trapped in the Stormhill Evergaol, located in Stormhill.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Creates a tail that swings in front of the caster with Standard Attack Power equal to 202% of Incantation Scaling.

If charged, it adds a second, larger swing, dealing Standard Attack Power equal to 274% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 42 points of Stamina to cast, whether charged or uncharged.
- Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 36%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 56%.
- The first swing deals 13 Stance damage, and the second swing deals 39 Stance damage.
  - This means that the charged version of the spell can deal up to 52 Stance damage, greater than even a hammer-type Colossal Weapon's charged heavy attack, allowing it to break the stance of many enemies within two hits.
- The spell goes through obstacles, making it decent for ambushing foes by using thin walls as cover.
- It is a bit slow to cast and has about a second of recovery time after the spell finishes casting.
- Launches smaller foes backward if it hits them.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This is the spell used by Crucible Axe Knights.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - FP cost was reduced from 22 to 20, and stamina damage to guarding enemies was increased from 180 to 200 on the first swipe and from 240 to 270 on the second swipe.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost.
  - FP cost was reduced from 32 to 22.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Assassin's Approach** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Starting spell for the Confessor origin.
- Sold for  2,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Assassin's Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Assassin's Approach applies a Buff that silences footsteps and prevents all non-lethal fall damage for 30 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  15 FP per cast.
- Costs  13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Non-lethal fall damage is only negated for falls between 16 and 20 meters, meaning this incantation does not prevent guaranteed deaths from falls of 20 meters or more.
- Overrides and is overridden by Soft Cotton.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text: - Generally outclassed by Soft Cotton, which is an easy-to-acquire consumable tool that costs no FP to activate. However, Soft Cotton lasts only 20 seconds and cannot be crafted during combat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Update 1.03 (undocumented) increased FP cost from 12 to 15.
- Update 1.07 extended the duration of this spell from 20 seconds to 30 seconds.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Darkness
- Longtail Cat Talisman, a talisman that eliminates non-lethal fall damage
- Miriam's Vanishing
- Shadow Bait
- Unseen Form

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Barrier of Gold** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Guaranteed Drop:** Leyndell, Royal Capital
- Drops from an invisible Scarab rolling back and forth on the path patrolled by a Crucible Tree Knight, north of the Erdtree Sanctuary Site of Grace, past the elevator downwards.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> If Maliketh, the Black Blade is defeated before this incantation is acquired it becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Magic damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for caster and allies within a 6 meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 13 points of Stamina to cast.
- Overall a very strong defensive incantation, if one that comes a bit late and will most likely come after the Magic-heavy area of Liurnia of the Lakes, with only the Astels and Loretta being the major Magic damage bosses left.
- Since it doesn't actually apply a flat increase to damage negation, just the damage taken, the actual effective new damage negation (the one shown on the character screen) can be calculated with the following formula: 1 - (1 - (current Magic damage negation)/100) * (1 - 0.60).
  - As an example, if Magic damage negation before casting the incantation is 25.000 the result becomes this: 1 - (1 - 25.000/100) * (1 - 0.60) = 0.7, or 70.0% Magic damage negation.
  - Against other players, simply replace the 0.60 with 0.20 for a new end result of 40.0% Magic damage negation.
- Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher Magic damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell the less effective it may appear to be in the statistics.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Golden Lightning Fortification, a variant that reduces Lightning damage.
- Magic Fortification, a weaker, personal version of this incantation
- Protection of the Erdtree
- Spelldrake Talisman, a talisman granting Magic damage negation
- Spellproof Dried Liver, a consumable item granting much weaker damage negation at no cost except materials

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bestial Vitality** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Bestial Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Quest Item:** Bestial Sanctum, Greyoll's Dragonbarrow
- Bestial Vitality is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the third Deathroot.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Infuses the body with bestial vigor to grant health regeneration to them, healing 5 HP per second for 120 seconds (600 HP in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  18 FP per cast.
- Costs  10 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to equip.
- Can move slowly during casting.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text: - Old Lord's Talisman extends both the duration and total healing by 30%, increasing the total HP restored to 780.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The HP regeneration effect stacks with the Blessed Dew Talisman and Icon Shield, but not with Blessing's Boon, Blessing of the Erdtree, or Crimsonburst Crystal Tear.
- This is the only HP regenerating incantation that is caster-only, but it's also the most FP-efficient one, letting the caster slowly regain their health during their travels (or simply cower in a corner over the fairly long duration).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Flame, Grant Me Strength has the same icon for its spell scroll, just red instead of beige.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Blessed Dew Talisman, a Talisman that also grants a weak, stackable health regeneration effect
- Crimsonburst Crystal Tear, a Crystal Tear that also grants a self-only HP-regeneration effect

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bestial Constitution** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Bestial Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Guaranteed Drop:** Greyoll's Dragonbarrow

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Removes any Blood Loss and Frostbite build-up on the caster, and removes any applied Frostbite.

sections.heading: Notes

- Costs  10 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to equip.
- Can move slowly while casting.

sections.heading: Strategies

sections.heading: See also

- Lord's Aid, another incantation that can remove Blood Loss, in addition to Poison and Sleep
- Speckled Hardtear, a Crystal Tear that removes all Status Effects and build-up

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bestial Sling** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Bestial Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Quest Item:** Greyoll's Dragonbarrow
- Bestial Sling is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the second Deathroot.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Throw out a fistful of stone shards with Standard Attack Power equal to 87% of Incantation Scaling.

Hits twice at melee range.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  21 points of FP to cast.
- Costs  19 points of Stamina to cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 4 Stance damage.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text: - Range is slightly increased by the Arrow's Reach Talisman, decreasing damage fall-off.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Has Attack Power equal to 174% of Incantation Scaling (not accounting for flat defence) at melee (Daggers) range due to hitting twice there.
- Deals pretty low damage but is excellent for harassing passive or low-health enemy players.
- Since it casts so quickly it can easily be spammed against an opponent to force them on the back foot.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Used by Gurranq, Beast Clergyman.
- Patch 1.12 (PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments): Decreased poise damage.
  - Poise damage against other players was decreased from 54 to 26.
- Patch 1.08: Reduced the poise damage of the Incantation Bestial Sling.
  - This update actually had no effect.
- Patch 1.07: Reduced the stone fragment scatter randomness. Increased stamina attack power against guarding enemies. Reduced between two hits and adjusted the detection so that two hits are always made at close range. Decreased poise damage.
  - Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 40 to 60.
    - Against guarding players the Stamina Attack Power was instead increased to 75.
  - The incantation can now hit twice at very short melee range.
  - Only Stance damage was decreased, from 5 to 4. Poise damage was increased from 50 to 54.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Rock Sling, a sorcery counterpart, if with larger and stronger projectiles
- Stone of Gurranq, a considerably larger rock-throwing incantation

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Black Blade** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Summons a red, spectral version of Maliketh's Black Blade, then jumps and spins forwards with the blade to hit for Holy Attack Power equal to 225% of Incantation Scaling while also sending out a wave with Holy Attack Power equal to 162% of Incantation Scaling.

If the incantation is used again immediately afterwards, the second sword's Attack Power is increased to 232% of Incantation Scaling while the beam's Attack Power is increased to 169% of Incantation Scaling for the second cast.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 44 points of Stamina to perform, with the follow-up costing the same amount of Stamina for a total of 88 points of Stamina if both parts are used.
- The sword part deals 9 Stance damage and the beam part deals 4 Stance damage.
- Both the sword itself and the wave it sends out can hit the same target at melee range, meaning that the first cast effectively can have Attack Power roughly equal to 387% of Incantation Scaling while the follow-up cast can have Attack Power equal to 401% of Incantation Scaling.
- The beam attack applies two debuffs: the first deals damage equal to 0.1% of the target's maximum HP + 1 every 0.1 seconds for 2 seconds (total damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20) while the second debuff lowers the target's maximum HP by 10% for 15 seconds, signified by a part of their health bar being blocked out with grey.
  - The debuff that lowers maximum HP doesn't stack with the Maliketh's Black Blade's skill Destined Death similar debuff, but it does stack with the one inflicted by the Black Knife's skill Blade of Death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.08 fixed a bug that prevented the follow-up attack from occurring when the Black Sword Incantation was activated with a Sacred Seal in the left hand.
  - Black Blade is incorrectly referred to as Black Sword in this patch note.
- Patch 1.07.1 the incantation Black Blade is currently missing its follow up attack when cast from the left hand. This issue will be corrected in a future update.
  - The issue was fixed with Patch 1.08.
- Patch 1.07 reduced stamina consumption, improved turning performance and shortened recovery time, the sword and the wave attack have been changed so that they hit at the same time. Attack power, stamina attack power, and poise damage of each part have been decreased, decreased the number of times the wave part hits large enemies.
  - Prior to this only either the sword attack or the beam attack could hit an enemy.
  - The Attack Power of the first sword and beam was decreased from 290% of Incantation Scaling and 252% of Incantation Scaling to 225% and 162% of the same respectively, and the Attack Power of the follow-up sword and beam was decreased from 297% of Incantation Scaling and 260% of Incantation Scaling to 232% and 169% of the same respectively.
  - The Stamina damage to guarding opponents for the first sword and beam was decreased from 190 and 150 to 145 and 115 respectively, and the same for the follow-up sword and beam was decreased from 220 and 150 to 160 and 125 respectively.
    - The Stamina damage to guarding players was split from the PvE values and increased at the same time, going to 181 and 143 for the first sword and beam, and to 200 and 156 for the follow-up sword and beam.
  - The Stance damage of sword attacks and beam attacks were decreased from 10 and 7 to 9 and 4 respectively. The Poise damage of sword attacks and beam attacks meanwhile was actually increased, not decreased, going from 100 and 70 to 243 and 108 respectively.
- Patch 1.04 decreased Stamina consumption and decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Black Flame** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Godskin Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Create a small ball of Blackflame to throw, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 244% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting a Blackflame effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 300% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 25 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 33 points.
- Deals 9.1 Stance damage on hit. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 11.83.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 23%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 41%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Godslayer's Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- An very strong yet simple spell due to a combination of fast casting speed and percentage-based damage.
  - Since it deals at least 2% of a target's health per cast it can kill anything damageable in 50 casts, though most often much quicker due to the Fire damage it also deals.
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- 1.07: Increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 100 to 150 for the uncharged version, and from 160 to 210 for the charged version.
    - Against players the Stamina Attack Power was instead increased to 187 for the uncharged version and to 262 for the charged version.
- 1.04: Increase damage and the spell can break enemy’s guard more easily.
  - Attack Power was increased from 214% of Incantation Scaling for the uncharged version to 244% of the same, and from 248% of Incantation Scaling for the charged version to 300% of the same.
  - Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 91 to 100 for the uncharged version, and from 118 to 160 for the charged version.
- Patch 1.03.3 seems to have included an undocumented change which increased the FP cost of this incantation from 15 to 18.

sections.text:
- Fire Serpent, a tracking, Messmerfire variant
- Flame Sling, a Giants' Flame variant

sections.heading: Acquisition

- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Quickly sheathe the right-hand weapon with Blackflame, granting Fire Attack Power equal to 85% of the seal's Faith-based Incantation Scaling and inflicting an effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds.

Lasts for 7 seconds and counts as a Weapon Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 10 points of Stamina to cast.
- Despite being one of the Godslayer Incantations, this spell, like other spell-based weapon buffs, does not get bonus damage from its associated seal (the Godslayer's Seal for this one).
- Can have its extremely short duration extended by 30% by the Old Lord's Talisman, to 9.1 seconds.
- The Blackflame effect is also applied to target's hit by Skills of the buffed weapon, even if those skills don't involve the weapon, such as with Skill: Thunderbolt or Skill: Flame of the Redmanes.
- Casts considerably quicker if used immediately after a roll, jump, or attack, or when sprinting, letting the user get more out of its short duration.
- The additional damage from the Blackflame effect will at most be 9% of target's maximum HP + 90 (11.1% + 110 if the Old Lord's Talisman is used). Practically though, the bonus damage will probably be around 5% + 50, presuming the user is able to keep on the offense.
  - It's important to note that the duration of Blackflame effects doesn't stack, instead the duration is reset if another hit is landed during an ongoing burn.
  - Due to the extremely short duration of this buff, it's important to keep on the offensive if possible after casting the spell.
- Should ideally be cast just before an opening in a boss's attacks happens.
- Outmatched in added Fire Attack Power (i.e. not counting the added Blackflame effect) by Drawstring Fire Grease below 170 Incantation Scaling and by Drawstring Messmerfire Grease Shadow of the Erdtree below 208 Incantation Scaling.
  - Note that both of these consumable items last considerably longer than Black Flame Blade, even if the Old Lord's Talisman is equipped. More specifically, Drawstring Fire Grease lasts for 10 seconds and Drawstring Messmerfire Grease lasts for 25 seconds.
- Can be used with a quick weapon such as the Dagger, even if it's unupgraded, to deal heavy damage to high-health bosses.
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Uses the same casting animation as Drawstring Greases, and also share their very short duration (though Black Flame Blade's duration is shorter than even theirs).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Bloodflame Blade, the other, weaker but much longer lasting Fire-based Weapon Buff
- Drawstring Fire Grease/Drawstring Messmerfire Grease Shadow of the Erdtree, similarly quick-casting Weapon Buffs but with longer durations and non-scaling damage
- Skill: Black Flame Tornado, a skill that also deals Blackflame damage

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Black Flame Ritual** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Guaranteed Drop:** Mountaintops of the Giants
- Black Flame Ritual is received upon defeating the Spiritcaller Snail boss in Spiritcaller Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This Snail summons the spirits of a Godskin Apostle and a Godskin Noble.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Summon a circle of Blackflame around the caster for about 4 seconds, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 106% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting an effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds, if an enemy touches them.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 109% of Incantation Scaling and creates the circle a bit further away from the caster.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 39 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 51 points.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 6.5 per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 3%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 18%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Godslayer's Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- The ring can hit an enemy up to 4 times, effectively granting it Attack Power equal to 424% of Incantation Scaling (436% if charged), not accounting for flat defence, and dealing additional damage equal to 5% of target's maximum HP + 20 (since hitting with a new Blackflame effect will just reset the duration of the debuff).
  - This makes the incantation surprisingly usable for attacking, at least against large opponents such as Trolls, since enemies can be tricked into standing inside of the flames.
  - An older instance of Black Flame Ritual isn't removed when a new is cast, though their damage won't stack as efficiently against opponents compared to when their casts are more separated.
  - Significantly harder to use against other players, being primarily useful for forcing them to stay away from the caster or to obscure the caster's other attacks. Be wary of opponent's jumping over the flames or simply running through them, as well as the fact that the charged version's pillars being further out means it's possible to stand close to the caster without being damaged.
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- 1.06: Fixed a bug which caused the charged version of “Black Flame Ritual” to consume the same amount of stamina as the normal version
- 1.04: Reduced FP cost and increased damage.
  - FP cost was decreased from 36 to 30.
- Patch 1.03.3 seems to have included an undocumented change which increased the FP cost of this incantation from 24 to 36.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Black Flame's Protection** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold
- Acquired from Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing after selecting the "about the secret medallion" dialogue option. This option will only appear after the player has obtained both the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) and Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
- Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 2,500  Runes should the player not talk to Gideon about both medallions before unleashing the Rune of Death.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Physical damage taken by 35% (15% in PvP) while also decreasing all healing received by 20% for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  30 FP per cast.
- Costs  13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces Physical damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *PhysicalFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
<math>TotalPhysicalReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {PhysicalDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {PhysicalFortification}) )</math>
  - For example, if physical damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
<math>PhysicalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 36.25%:
<math>TotalPhysicalReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.15) ) = 36.25%</math>

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The reduction in healing effective lowers the effectiveness of this spell to only lowering Physical damage taken by 18.75% (and increasing the effective damage taken in PvP by 6.25%), assuming that healing will be used and not accounting for it helping the player survive hits that otherwise would have killed them.
  - Effectively still has its full PvP strength of 15% in no-healing scenarios such as semi-formal duels in the open world or via a Duelist's Furled Finger, and the Duel Arena Combat mode available through the Royal Colosseum in Leyndell, Royal Capital or via Roundtable Hold.
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as physical damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple physical negation sources.
- This incantation is valuable whenever available since the vast majority of areas will have most of the damage inflicted by enemies as various types of Physical damage. The biggest exception is Liurnia of the Lakes, where Magic damage shares the spotlight.
- Black Flame's Protection offers greater physical protection than Boiled Crab (35% vs. 20%) and has a slightly longer duration (70 vs. 60 seconds). This spell requires 30 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 30 FP to cast, while the Crab only requires 600 Runes per piece bought.
  - The Boiled Crab is preferable for PvP encounters, as Black Flame's Protection's effect is reduced to 15%.
  - Though Boiled Crab (and the slightly weaker Boiled Prawn) are potentially accessible much earlier, it's possible to not gain access to them should Blackguard Big Boggart be killed before any of either has been bought from him.
- The reduction in healing for the Flask of Crimson Tears specifically can be countered with either the Crimson Seed Talisman or Crimson Seed Talisman +1, setting healing effectiveness to 96% and 104% respectively.
  - Note that this only helps with the flask, as the Heal spells are not affected by either talisman but is affected by the healing reduction.

- Dragoncrest Shield Talismans, a type of talisman granting additional Physical damage negation
- Flame Fortification, effectively a Fire damage negation version

- Magic Fortification, effectively a Magic damage negation version

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
The caster kneels in prayer, granting health regeneration to themselves and allies within a 15-meter radius, healing 12 HP per second for 90 seconds (1080 HP in total).

Nearby Revenants and Revenant Followers lose 3% of their maximum HP plus 10 per second for 30 seconds (90% of their maximum HP + 300 in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  60 FP per cast.
- Costs  30 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to equip.
- The effect can be delayed indefinitely by holding the casting button, which is useful if an ally is not yet within range.
- Bandai Namco Entertainment rated it on the first place of the top 5 incantations.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text: - Old Lord's Talisman extends both the duration and total healing by 30%, increasing the total HP restored to 1404.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The HP regeneration effect stacks with the Blessed Dew Talisman and Icon Shield, but not with Bestial Vitality, Blessing's Boon, or Crimsonburst Crystal Tear.
- Blessing of the Erdtree offers the highest healing per second, 50% greater than the second strongest health regeneration buff. However, its high FP cost makes it relatively inefficient.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Increases the damage of charged heavy melee attacks by 10%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Doesn't enhance the Dark Moon Greatsword's charged heavy attacks when they're buffed by its Unique Skill: Moonlight Greatsword.
- Doesn't work with the projectiles launched by the charged heavy attacks of the Frozen Needle or Wing of Astel.
- Has strong synergy with the Roar Medallion if using a skill that boosts heavy attacks.
  - Skill compatible with both are Barbaric Roar, Braggart's Roar, Shriek of Milos, and War Cry.
- Synergy with the Spear Talisman with weapons that have charged heavy attacks that deal Pierce damage.
  - Weapon types that primarily have thrusting heavy attacks are Great Spears, Spears (except for the Death Ritual Spear, Partisan, and Spiked Spear), Heavy Thrusting Swords (except for the Great Épée), Thrusting Swords (except for the Estoc), and Straight Swords (except for the Broadsword, Cane Sword, Carian Knight's Sword, and Lazuli Glintstone Sword).
  - Other notable weapons are the Claymore, Lucerne, Nagakiba, Pickaxe, Rusted Anchor, Warpick, and the Zweihander and Troll's Golden Sword.
- Works well with the unique charged heavy attack of the Iron Cleaver and Celebrant's Cleaver, since while they are weaker than the usual Axe charged heavy attack they also include a run-up that potentially let's them be used from a safe distance to close in.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Avionette Soldier Ashes** is a spirit ash in Elden Ring.

- Have a surprising amount of mobility due to their flight, though this mostly matters for reaching a foe rather than maneuvering around it since it's only in straight lines.
- Like their hostile counterparts they will sometimes go berserk when hit, greatly increasing damage due to their increased attack rate. Unlike their hostile counterparts they generally have enough HP to survive through the attack and the cooldown period, and potentially trigger another berserk phase.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Banished Knight Engvall** is a spirit ash in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Dropped by Grave Warden Duelist in Murkwater Catacombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.
- Summons a Banished Knight that wields a halberd with a more mobile variant of the Stormcaller skill on it.
- Deals Standard and Pierce damage.
- A slow, tanky summon that can hit decently hard and is available very early on, Engvall's main drawback is his huge FP cost which puts him out of range of most early builds that aren't focused on magic. This makes him an ideal companion for a caster that doesn't mind devoting all or most of a cerulean flask to him.
- Though he is quite durable, he is quite expensive, FP-wise, to summon. His halberd gives him wide-sweeping attacks for cleaving through crowds, while his Stormcaller has good AOE and can knock many enemies flat. Still, he is greatly outclassed by Banished Knight Oleg due to the latter's greater damage potential: Oleg tends to move and attack faster with in longer combos, while Engvall is a bit slower and also isn't quite as good at keeping foes staggered.

sections.heading: Trivia

- The Japanese name of these knights is 失地騎士 (shicchi kishi); knights who have lost their land to an enemy. The implication is they are "Banished Knights" because they have been driven from their homeland by force.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

- Deals Slash damage and inflicts slight Blood Loss build-up with both weapons.
- As a red-eye Spirit Ash, this knight will remain at the spot where they are summoned and pursue any encroaching enemies aggressively. Quite fitting for the masterless knight known as the Rabid Stray.
- Like other, hostile Bloodhound Knights, Floh is quite fragile and reliant on being able to chain staggers and Blood Loss to burst down foes without being killed. Due to this, Floh is best used by a build that can keep attention away from them and that can take advantage of the additional Blood Loss build-up to more easily cause the status themself.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The name Floh seems to stem from the name of the prehistoric Floian period, a trait shared with Bloodhound Knight Darriwil, who in turn seems to be named for the Darriwilian period.
  - The only other enemy with this etymological origin are the three named Crucible Knights: Ordovis, Siluria, Devonia.
  - Crucible Knight Floh was the boss of the Erdtree-Gazing Evergaol in early development. This location was renamed Forlorn Hound Evergaol and now contains Bloodhound Knight Darriwil.

- The "Rabid Stray" seeking a lord of true caliber may reference the ancient Greek philosopher —known for his futile search for a wise (honest) man and later  of , the most powerful man in the world.
  - Diogenes was nicknamed a “barking dog” for his  and austere lifestyle. Some accounts claim he died from a dog bite.
  - *"At the approach of so many people, Diogenes sat up a little and fixed his eyes on Alexander. When the king greeted him and asked if there was anything he wanted, Diogenes replied, 'Yes, that you should stand a little out of my sun'. It is said that Alexander was so impressed by this—and by the arrogance and grandeur of spirit of a man who could treat him with such disdain—that he said to his courtiers, who were laughing and joking about the philosopher as they walked away, 'But I'll tell you this: if I were not Alexander, I would be Diogenes!'"* — Plutarch, Alexander, XIV

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ashen Remains**, also referred to as **Spirit Ashes**, are items in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree that allow players to summon spirits to assist in combat.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
There are two main types of Ashen Remains. **Ashes** are used to summon basic allies while **renowned ashes** call forth mighty heroes from the past. Each Spirit Ash can be upgraded to a maximum of +10 by Roderika, Spirit Tuner by trading her Glovewort flowers. Spirit ashes may be improved further with Revered Spirit Ashes; however, their bonus is only applied to the Realm of Shadow. Once the first Revered Spirit Ash has been collected, their Shadow Realm Blessing may be strengthened at any Site of Grace.
- Grave Glovewort is used to improve standard Ashes
- Ghost Glovewort is used to improve special Renowned Ashes
- Revered Spirit Ash is used to improve the Shadow Realm Blessing

sections.heading: How to use Spirit Ashes
sections.text:
To summon spirits, players must possess the Spirit Calling Bell and be within the radius of a Rebirth Monument. The desired ash can then be activated directly from the inventory. Most spirit ashes require either FP or HP to summon, and only one ash can be summoned at a time.

Rebirth Monuments are small obelisks scattered throughout the Lands Between. They are required to summon spirit ashes, and their presence is indicated on the screen with a specific icon. These monuments are commonly found near boss arenas or areas with dense clusters of enemies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Black Knife Catacombs** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

It is found by heading east from the Church of Vows and taking the south path in the north-south split road. From there, follow the road until another north-east split happens and head north again before the cliffside splits east and follow it.

The entrance to the catacombs is guarded by a Mausoleum Knight.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A catacomb in the north-eastern area of Liurnia, inhabited by Necromancers and Skeletons. The catacombs are said to contain a knifeprint which hides the truth of the conspiracy of the Night of Black Knives.

Skeletons in this dungeon cannot be killed normally after being defeated unless using special weaknesses of Those Who Live in Death. Instead, nearby Commoners wielding special staves have to be killed to finished them off normally.

The entrance to the main boss arena can be found just after the Site of Grace at the entrance. Head left to find a split in the route, with a Stonesword Key-locked room to the left that holds 2 Skeletons and the Rosus' Axe.

To continue, head forward instead of to the left and run into a large room with 3 guillotines.

sections.heading: Main boss route
sections.text:
Run through the guillotine to a ladder and climb down. Straight ahead is the dungeon lever, guarded by 2 Giant Crabs that pop up from the back and the front as you approach.

Return to the entrance and head through the now unlocked door to arrive at the boss, a Cemetery Shade who is accompanied by 2 sword-wielding Skeletons and 2 bow-wielding Skeletons. Since this can be a very overwhelming fight it is recommended to bring a Spirit Ash to distract at least some of the foes, or otherwise bring a strong anti-undead attack such as the skill Sacred Blade to deal with the mobs.

sections.heading: Secondary boss route
sections.text:
After the second or third guillotine blade has fallen down in the large room they can be stepped onto and ridden to a ledge above. Following through the door leads to more regular enemies as well as a corridor that seemingly ends with a small hole to the right to drop down to the lever below. If one instead attacks the wall straight ahead another fog wall for a boss will be revealed, along with the summon sign for D, Hunter of the Dead should he be alive.

Since the Black Knife Assassin within is a very agile foe capable of making lunges across the rather small arena, it is advisable to summon D or a Spirit Ash to help keep the assassin's attention on someone else and get a safe moment to heal.

Jump from the southwestern part of the elevator to a doorway just above the bottom floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- While its Faith-scaling is technically the strongest its Dexterity-scaling is effectively almost equal to it because the dagger's Physical base Attack Power is higher than its Holy base Attack Power.
  - An equal split between Dexterity and Faith will give the most Attack Power (AP), though a pure Dexterity build or a pure Faith build will get only about 5% less AP.
  - Since the skill scales with weapon upgrade level and Faith but not Dexterity or Strength, it can be beneficial to lean into the pure Faith build, or even a 45/45 or 30/60 Dex/Fth split.
  - A pure Faith (80) build gives 1138 Holy Attack Power, 13% more Attack Power on the skill than hybrid Dexterity/Faith (45/45) build's 1010 Holy Attack Power and 5.5% more Attack Power than the skill of a Faith-leaning Dexterity/Faith (30/60) build's 1079 Holy Attack Power.
- Unfortunately generally outclassed by the Black Knife. While this weapon is 0.5 units lighter, has better scaling, and its skill deals more outright damage at a lower FP cost, the Black Knife will always have more AP due to higher base Attack Power, is attainable much earlier in the game, and the skill is often more damaging due to part of its damage being percentage-based.
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword.
  - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2 due to hitting twice.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information

- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base Attack Power while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base Attack Power: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire Attack Power, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning Attack Power, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy Attack Power, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic Attack Power.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Blackguard Big Boggart** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Boggart is an ex-convict who was called to the Lands Between by the Guidance of Grace. At some point in the past he was imprisoned in the same gaol as the Dung Eater, and saw first hand the ways he defiles and kills people.

The Tarnished first encounters him in Liurnia of the Lakes, where they confront him over the theft of a necklace belonging to Rya. Despite his foreboding first impression, Boggart gives the Tarnished the opportunity to buy back the necklace, and offers to sell them some cooked crawfish.

Boggart then journeys to Altus Plateau, setting up camp beside a river outside the capital, where he catches and cooks crabs. Here, he warns the Tarnished about the Dung Eater. Should the Tarnished ignore his warnings and release the killer from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, Boggart will become his latest victim.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Boilprawn Shack)
  - Head north-west from the Site of Grace to find Rya the Scout inside a gazebo and talk to her.
  - Move to north-west again from here to find Blackguard Big Boggart at the Boilprawn Shack and talk to him: select **Give me the necklace** and then **Deal** to be able to buy Rya's Necklace from him for 1000 Runes.
  - After purchasing the item, he'll start selling an infinite supply of Boiled Prawns. Purchase at least one to progress his questline: you'll receive the "Spread Out" gesture and, in turn, Boggart's summon sign will appear at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook to aid you against Magma Wyrm Makar.
1. Altus Plateau
  - After resting at a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, Boggart will move to the outer moat along the northern wall of Leyndell, Royal Capital in the Capital Outskirts (due west from the Capital Rampart Site of Grace).
  - You may now purchase an infinite supply of Boiled Crabs.
  - Exhaust Boggart's dialogue about Dung Eater. After freeing Dung Eater from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning Grounds, Boggart will have some additional dialogue.
1. Altus Plateau
  - After hearing Boggart's final piece of dialogue about Dung Eater, warning you that Dung Eater is lurking nearby, reload the area to find Boggart bound to a chair. Speak to him to trigger an invasion from Dung Eater.
  - Defeat Dung Eater and return to Boggart, who is now dead. Loot his equipment, as well as the Seedbed Curse.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Blackguard, alt. Blaggard, is an old term for scoundrel.

sections.heading: Overview

sections.text: The **Bloodstained Dagger** is a Dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:

  - One can point asleep next to the bridge west of the South of the Lookout Tower Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Strong Strength- and Arcane-scaling.
  - Surpasses all daggers except the rather unusual Wakizashi for raw damage on a Heavy affinity and has the highest Strength-scaling of them all, just short of an S-rating.
  - Second or third strongest dagger on the Occult affinity, though it will only slightly outmatch the Reduvia (only by 1 point) and the latter will have more Blood Loss build-up.
  - Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
  - Despite this its Heavy affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).
- The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
  - While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.
- The only dagger with a Strength focus on its Cold affinity instead of a Dexterity focus.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:

- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A Hero's Grave tucked away on the outer north-eastern wall of Leyndell, Royal Capital. Automated chariots move along the corridors, and there are many Basilisks throughout. At the end of the dungeon awaits one of the two leaders of the Crucible Knights.

The chariots are summoned by sigils projected onto the ground by statues; one such statue is attached to a fire-breathing pillar. Raising the pillar will move the sigil up onto the same track as the other two chariots; approaching the sigil in its new location to summon this chariot will then result in the chariots colliding, destroying them. Once all three chariots are destroyed, Ash of War: Holy Ground and the Tree Sentinel Set are granted.

The pillar can be raised from afar with Margit's Shackle to avoid a significant amount of effort.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The  was an unseen character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The blind swordsman was an ancient nomadic warrior, clad in sturdy leather and blue fabrics symbolizing waters as brisk and fluid as the blade in his hand. According to legend, he received a curved sword patterned after rushing waters from a fairy, represented by the Dancer in Blue.

The ever-drifting hero traveled the Ainsel River to the Lake of Rot, where still waters grew stagnant with scarlet rot in the presence of a great scorpion. Blade in hand, he confronted the outer god of Rot with the fluidity akin to a dance—allowing his foe to strike, then exploiting the opening with a well-timed counterattack. The blind swordsman defeated the ancient god and sealed away its divine essence.

During the age of the Elden Ring, the Blind Swordsman encountered the young Demigod Malenia and became her mentor. Despite being born into the accursed rot, she gained wings of unparalleled strength. However, Malenia would eventually abandon her pride to meet General Radahn's measure during the Battle of Aeonia, producing in the Swamp of Aeonia.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Blind Swordsman invented the Guard Counter technique, the art of allowing one's opponent to strike to leave them vulnerable to a well-timed reply.
- The Prosthesis-Wearer Heirloom depicts the Blind Swordsman clasping left hands with Malenia; both figures wear prosthetic right arms.
- Wore the Blue Cloth Set, which is used by the Warrior starting origin. This armor set bears a striking resemblance to the Blue Dancer Charm fairy.
  - The blue color of the set symbolizes brisk waters, emphasizing flow, and stresses the need to remain ever drifting. As such, the Blind Swordsman may be related to the nomadic warriors who wear the Blue Cloth set.
- The hero's Flowing Curved Sword is housed within a Great Coffin in the Consecrated Snowfield.
- The Blue Dancer Charm and Shamshir are found among ancient ruins in Highroad Cave.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The fairy that bestowed the flowing sword on the blind swordsman is sometimes speculated to have been the spirit of the Siofra River, 'Síofra' being an Irish name meaning "elf" or "changeling," derived from *síobhra*, the older Gaelic word for "elf" or "fairy".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Blood Loss** is a status effect in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Blood Loss is usually caused by serrated, thorned, exremely sharp, or bloodstained weapons. Spells and items affiliated with the Lord of Blood also cause this status effect.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.text:
Deals a combination of flat and percentual damage when inflicted and humanoid or smaller enemies, and Tarnished, are slightly staggered. The flat damage is usually 100, but increases to 200 when done by Somber Smithing Stone-upgraded weapons with innate Blood Loss and Arcane-scaling or by regular Smithing Stone-upgraded weapons with innate Blood Loss and with the Blood-affinity. The percentual damage depends on the enemy: normal ones and Tarnished take 15% damage, bosses and enemies that directly accompany them take 10.5% damage, and the Lord of Blood takes 7.5% damage.

Additionally, the blood loss inflicted by Mohg's Nihil attack is unique and only inflicts percentual damage, roughly 33% damage on each of the first two pulses and about 66% on the final pulse. Using the Purifying Crystal Tear greatly reduces this damage to about 5% on the first two pulses and 10% on the final one.

Blood loss can also be inflicted on someone in the middle of invincibility frames, such as a roll, though this only causes the stun and not the damage.

sections.heading: Buffs related to Blood Loss
sections.text: There are certain equipment that gives the player buffs when blood loss has been inflicted in the general vicinity, they do not discriminate between what has been bled in order to activate, it can be friend, foe and even oneself and generally lasts for around 20 seconds since the last blood loss infliction.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Banished Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Knights who, whether by misfortune or misdeed, were forced to abandon their homes.  Most were sent to the fringes, forced to start anew with only despair for company. Many of them wear helms adorned with sculptures of dragons, although some cover their helms with deep red scarves to protect themselves from the biting winds of the fringes.

The Banished Knights wielded the power of the storm and practiced Dragon Communion. They are predominantly found in Stormveil Castle, Castle Sol, and Crumbling Farum Azula, often accompanied by Exile Soldiers. Spectral versions of these knights can be encountered at Castle Sol on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

Two notable Banished Knights are Oleg and Engvall, referred to as the Wings of the Storm. After their banishment, they were extended invitations by the Grace-Given Lord. While Oleg accepted this invitation and later earned Erdtree Burial, Engvall rejected it and instead chose to watch over a masterless castle, gaining reknown as a hero of the fringes.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Banished Knights clad in ornate armour, found defending Stormveil Castle. They fight using greatswords and halberds, and can utilise storm-based combat arts in battle.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Banished Knights who wear red scarves over their helmets. Some of these knights are capable of using Dragon Communion Incantations, such as Dragonfire, while others utilize storm arts. Spectral versions of these knights can be found in Fringefolk Hero's Grave in the Stranded Graveyard within Limgrave.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text:
An spectral variant of the Banished Knights. Phantom Banished Knights can only be encountered in Castle Sol, at the Mountaintops of the Giants. Additionally, Commander Niall, the boss at this location, can summon two of these spirits, one wielding a halberd and the other dual swords.

These enemies can disappear and reappear. Some cannot be snuck up on, and will teleport behind the player, even when attacked from distance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Horns emerge from the right pauldron worn by Banished Knights.
- The Banished Knight Helm (Altered) displays a four-legged dragon.
- One of Fia's Champions is a Banished Knight, though they use the player model.

- The Japanese name 失地騎士 (*shicchi kishi*) literally means "knights who have lost their land to an enemy", indicating the Banished Knights were driven from their homeland by force.

**Bell Bearings** are Key Items in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree that can be given to the Twin Maiden Husks to expand their inventory. There are **51** to collect in the base game and an additional **10** to be found in the DLC.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Merchants usually drop their respective Bell Bearings when they die, either from being killed by the player or from scripted events. When given to the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold, the bearing will grant access to the inventory they used to sell.

Some other Bell Bearings can be found scattered throughout the Lands Between, or dropped by certain enemies such as the Bell-Bearing Hunter upon defeat. They can also be found in the Land of Shadow, hidden in hanging jars  that must be destroyed with ranged attacks to release the bearings.

The benefits of generic Bell Bearings given to the Twin Maiden Husks will carry over into New Game Plus. However, those of named characters, such as Iji's Bell Bearing, will not carry over. These may be collected again when the character dies.

sections.text: **Astel, Naturalborn of the Void** is an optional Boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is encountered within a secluded, starlit cavern somewhere along the underground Ainsel River, beyond the Lake of Rot. This area is accessed by entering the Transportation Coffin overlooking a chasm at the Grand Cloister. The elevator Astel blocks is the only path to the hidden Moonlight Altar, a necessary step for Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
- HP (solo): 11,170
- Defense: 114
- Stance: 120
- Deals  Standard and  Magic damage
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to a Critical Hit after being stance broken
- Weakness: Gravity effects
- Weak spot: Head

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- 80,000 runes
- Remembrance of the Naturalborn

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating Astel, Naturalborn of the Void for the first time unlocks the "Astel, Naturalborn of the Void" achievement.
- Defeating this boss is optional, though it is mandatory for the "Age of the Stars" ending.
- Astel resembles a Great Dragonfly.
- Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is the boss of the Grand Cloister, an area populated by insect-like Kindred of Rot.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This boss was named **Astel, Misbegotten of the Void** in . At the time, the Misbegotten were referred to as "Aberrations."
- Astel has an unused animation in which it fell from the sky, crashing to the earth like a meteor. This move is used by Starscourge Radahn.
- The internal data Astel's boss arena includes spawn markers for an Ancestor Spirit and its spirit animals, suggesting the Grand Cloister boss was reassigned to Astel from a third Ancestor Spirit encounter.
  - It is also possible that one of the Ancestor Spirit boss rooms was duplicated and used as a template.

sections.text: The **Badlands** are a mentioned location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
After his banishment from the Lands Between, Lord Godfrey led his kinsfolk, the Tarnished, on a Long March, after which he divested himself of kingship and once again became a simple warrior. As Hoarah Loux, Godfrey became a chieftain of the Badlands, inspiring many brave warriors to follow his example.

Exalted Flesh is considered to be a delicacy in the Badlands, eaten by its heroes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A Spirit Jellyfish found in the Stargazer's Ruins on the Mountaintops of the Giants. She is waiting for her sister, Aurelia, with whom she promised to see the stars when they turned fourteen.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. When approaching Stargazers' Ruins, Aureliette's voice can be heard from inside the main building.
1. Use the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes obtained from Roderika, Spirit Tuner in front of Aureliette.
1. After a brief dialogue, she will disappear, and the seal blocking access to the cellar containing the Primal Glintstone Blade will be gone.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Two gravestones can be found north-east of Stargazers' Ruins. Interacting with them will reveal the message *"Here lie Aurelia and Aureliette, who never saw the stars"*
- "Aureliette" likely comes from the common jellyfish species aurelia aurita, also known as "moon jellies", which the Spirit Jellyfish greatly resembles.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Basilisks** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Basilisks are amphibious creatures that haunt many regions of the Lands Between, favoring places tainted by Death. These squat, finned quadrupeds move in short hops and lash out with claws or sudden leaps, but their most significant threat is the black fog they exhale, which spreads Death Blight. The grotesque, bulbous eyes on their heads are a deception—the true eyes are small and set far back near the snout. These false eyes resemble the Prince of Death's, with similar pupils appearing in the tainted roots that wind through graveyards and catacombs.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Ainsel River – in dark cave areas
- Ancient Ruins of Rauh – summoned by the Divine Beast Dancing Lion
- Auriza Hero's Grave
- Deeproot Depths – found in and around the Nameless Eternal City
- Lake of Rot – submerged in the scarlet rot
- Mt. Gelmir – along and to the north of the Seethewater River
- Rauh Base – north of Temple Town Ruins
- Scorpion River Catacombs
- Subterranean Shunning-Grounds
- The Shaded Castle
- Volcano Manor

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Resistant to most Status Effects
- Vulnerable to  Fire and  Slash damage
- Cannot be Parried
- Can be Stance-Broken, but cannot be Critical Attacked
- Affected by Beast-Repellent Torch and Beastlure Pot
- The Prince of Death—the soulless body of Godwyn the Golden—has finned forelimbs, much like a Basilisk.
- Basilisk statues in Scorpion River Catacombs inflict  Death Blight via line of sight.
- In Elden Ring Nightreign, Basilisks populate the sewers of Noklateo, the Shrouded City.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Basilisks are a recurring enemy in the *Dark Souls* franchise, having appeared in all three games. Typically, Basilisks inflict Curse or petrify the player. Although these status conditions do not appear in *Elden Ring*, their Death Blight-inflicting clouds work similarly.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This page is mostly based on the Bestiary Index from the English Official Elden Ring Strategy Guide by Future Press  for both how enemy variants are distinguished between each other and their listed names. However, it's important to note that the strategy guide should not be considered complete, un-arguable gospel, as it features a couple writing mistakes of it's own both when it comes to it's own naming format for alternate variants (for example: the format goes from *"Omen (Axe) (Strong Curse)"* back to *"Omen (Cleaver, Strong Curse)"* in the naming format) and does not even feature all the same enemies or variants that the Japanese guide did, nor some of what we've noted down ourselves during the making of this wiki. Missing enemies/variants include:
  - The mechanical chariots patrolling the halls of several Hero's Graves.
  - The Lightning Balls floating around Siofra River.
  - and several more.
- This means that if we were to only follow the guide, some enemies would not have an official English name at all.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Bloody Fingers** are a covenant of invaders from Mohg the Lord of Blood's burgeoning Mohgwyn Dynasty. By his will, these bloodthirsty Tarnished hunt their own.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
This group of Tarnished is similar in practice to the Recusants of the Volcano Manor, in that Bloody Fingers seek out and kill other Tarnished throughout the Lands Between. However, they seem to differ in long-term goals as well as rites of induction. To become a Bloody Finger, one must be inducted via a process overseen by a White Mask, such as Varré. The first step is to prove their dedication to their Lord's cause by hunting fellow Tarnished, using fetishes made from Furled Fingers blackened with blood congestion, to invade their worlds as blood-red phantoms; these seem to have been chopped off rather unceremoniously. Killing one Host of Fingers, or attempting to do so at least three times, is enough to pass this step. Next, the inductee must stain a special cloth, the Lord of Blood's Favor, in the blood of a Tarnished's Finger Maiden. One need not necessarily kill a maiden, let alone their own maiden, to do so, as long as they can obtain the blood. With this done, it can be brought to the White Mask.

The initiate, now a formal Bloody Finger, is then given one last blessing: the Lord of Blood's own glistening blood, siphoned into the nail of their finger. This Bloody Finger's skin becomes sickly pale and loses feeling, although the nail aches with sweetest pain. The process is agonizing, but it gives the ability to invade other worlds as often as they like without the need for the consumable fingers. Over time, the inductee begins to fall to "cessblood", an infection-like condition that causes an onset of bloodlust and insanity, removing any inhibition that would prevent the Bloody Finger from killing their fellow Tarnished with a zealous devotion to Mohg.

The new Bloody Finger may also be given a Pureblood Knight's Medal, with the power as to gain an audience with Mohg himself, when the time is right; obtaining one sometimes requires the White Mask to go out of their way to obtain it.

There are those that hunt the Bloody Fingers in return, however: Yura is one such warrior seeking to put an end to their cessblood. The group has taken notice of this, however, and sent assassins after him.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: Sanguine Nobles, who have ties to the Bloody Fingers and Mohg, are noted to have curly black horns similar to his coming from their head and their feet, as well as sporting claws. Given that Cessblood seems to use his blood, this process appears capable of partially transforming someone, over time, into an Omen or at least taking on Omen traits.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bayle the Dread** is an optional boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Enemy of the Dragonlord
sections.text: Bayle the Dread was a legendary black dragon who is said to be the ancestor of the drakes or lesser dragons. Long ago, Bayle betrayed the Ancient dragons and clashed with Dragonlord Placidusax. Their vicious battle ended in stalemate and left both dragons with grievous injuries and loss of body parts, with Bayle losing his two winged arms, his pair of wings on his back and his left leg, with the dreaded dragon fleeing to the Jagged Peak soon afterwards.

sections.heading: Dragon Communion
sections.text:
As punishment for his betrayal, Placidusax created the art of Dragon Communion, sending his followers to shepherd humanity into hunting Bayle and his descendants. As reward for felling the drakes, the dragon hunters consumed their hearts in order to gain their power.  Bayle was pursued by Florissax, a servant of Placidusax who sought to recruit mortals in the hunt for Bayle.

Dragonslayer Igon, a particularly obsessive drake warrior, was one such mortal. Igon faced Bayle, but was left broken in both body and spirit by their battle.

sections.heading: Drake Warrior
sections.text:
Igon was stumbled upon by a Tarnished champion, and begged them to summon his spirit to face Bayle once more. Together, the pair succeed in slaying Bayle.

If Bayle's heart is eaten at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion, his willpower will one day consume the body and soul of the drake warrior.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text: Bayle is weakest against piercing damage, Dragon Communion Grease, and Igon's Harpoons.

sections.heading: Phase One
sections.text: Bayle is stuck on the ground. He commands a unique power that combines fire and lightning damage.

sections.heading: Phase Two
sections.text: Bayle summons an extra set of wings made from red lightning. He is able to fly.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Two of Placidusax's lost heads can be found still clinging onto the upside of Bayle's neck.
- The ancient dragons who sided with Bayle against Placidusax wielded the branching red lightning.
- Drake Warrior Igon may be summoned inside the area if the player has received his Furled Finger.
- Igon and Florissax will reward the player after Bayle is defeated.
- Bayle is the only boss in the game who displays the text 'Legend Felled' when defeated who does not drop a Remembrance. Rather, he drops the Heart of Bayle, which functions similarly, with some differences.
  - The Heart of Bayle cannot be redeemed for an item by meeting with Finger Reader Enia. Rather, it must be redeemed at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion.
  - The Heart cannot be consumed to receive Runes, nor duplicated.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Bayle's name is a corruption of "bale," which refers to a destructive and evil force.
- Bayle's name and moniker "The Dread" may also be a reference to the dragon *Balerion*, *The Black* *Dread* from author and the base game's co-writer George R. R. Martin's fantasy novel series, *A Song of Ice and Fire*.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom is found in the upper sections of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. From the Rauh Ancient Ruins, East site of grace, head across the bridge just to the west, then drop down to a slightly lower bridge section at the end.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Sprouts a flower from the user's chest, creating a rain of light around them that lasts for 4 seconds and has Holy Attack Power equal to 80% of Incantation Scaling per hit.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power per hit to 100% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 26 points of Stamina.
- Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 44%.
- Can deal decent damage against large foes such as Dragons, but more mobile or smaller foes will likely only be hit once or twice for minimal damage.
- There is about a 2-second delay before the rain of light begins after casting the spell.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is very similar to the light spell used by Miranda Blossoms, Melina, and the cut Miranda's Prayer tool. However, this spell creates a flower at the beginning of its cast.
- Patch 1.14 increased attack speed, increased the size of the hitbox, and shortened the recovery time between using this incantation and follow-up actions.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns is acquired by defeating the Golden Hippopotamus boss found just inside the main gate of Shadow Keep on Scadu Altus.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Sprouts spines from the back and rolls sideways on the ground, throwing them around the user, dealing Pierce Attack Power equal to 45% of Incantation Scaling per hit, hitting up to 10 times (450% of Incantation Scaling in total).

The spell can be charged to spin twice, increasing the maximum number of hits to 15 and moving forward. These extra attacks deal Attack Power equal to 120% of Incantation Scaling per hit (600% of Incantation Scaling for the extra hits or 1000% of Incantation Scaling in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 29 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 38 points of Stamina.
- Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 122%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 156%.
- The very low height of the user when casting this spell means that high-centered thrusting or horizontal attacks can easily miss them.
  - The charged version's increased forward momentum makes it even better at evading attacks.
- Since this Incantation deals Pierce damage, it will occasionally deal a Counter Hit against an attacking foe, increasing the Attack Power of that specific hit by 30%.
  - Note that this will most likely result in an overall 2-3% damage increase per Counter Hit since each is only a portion of the total damage.
  - Since this isn't a weapon, it does NOT benefit from the Spear Talisman.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.14 increased attack power and stamina attack power against guarding enemies. The close-range hitbox now follows the movement of the player.
  - The attack power was increased from 40% of Incantation Scaling to 45% for the uncharged hits and most of the charged hits, while the increase was from 70% to 120% of Incantation Scaling for the stronger charged hits.
  - Stamina attack power against guarding enemies was only increased for the charged hits, going from 50 to 85 against PvE enemies and from 62 to 106 against other players.

sections.text: The **Blessing of Despair** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord and adds the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse to the Elden Ring, bringing about an accursed world where defilement becomes the norm. All will become cursed in the *Blessing of Despair* ending. Thus, none can be scorned, fulfilling the Dung Eater's twisted vision.

Curse life itself; the world's children, grandchildren, and every generation hence, will be its pustules. And yet with Order itself defiled, defilement will be defilement no more, and every Seedbed Curse will be a cursed blessing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Blessing of Despair is an "Elden Lord" ending and will unlock the Elden Lord achievement.
- This ending is achieved by completing the Dung Eater's questline and using the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse to finish the game at Fractured Marika.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bayle's Flame Lightning** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Summons one of Bayle's arms to slam down with, causing an explosion around the point of impact. A direct hit deals Standard damage equal to 250% of Incantation Scaling, Lightning damage equal to 280% of the same, and Fire damage equal to 220% of the same, while an enemy that isn't directly hit but moves into the point of impact afterward is dealt Lightning damage equal to 200% of Incantation Scaling and Fire damage equal to 150% of the same.

Enemies just outside of the hit area take Fire damage equal to 30% of Incantation Scaling and Lightning damage equal to 15% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes

- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Has some Hyperarmor when cast, and can thus resist a hit or two from most foes before being knocked down on the ground.

  - This increased the damage of the initial hit, with the Lightning attack power going from 250% of Incantation Scaling to 280% of the same and the Fire attack power going from 190% of Incantation Scaling to 220% of the same.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **base serpent** or **abyssal serpent** is a character in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Long ago, the abyssal serpent was a powerful snake in the Lands Between. It was separated from its light, although it is unclear by whom, when, or why. If it was not so already, it henceforth became a wicked entity.

Messmer, son of Queen Marika, was born cursed with the essence of the base serpent stirring within him. His mother's fear drove her to suppress its power, so she replaced his right eye with a golden Scarseal of Grace. Later, she trapped him within the Realm of Shadow on an endless crusade against those stripped of her Grace. The abyssal serpent slowly consumed Messmer's Kindling, but its influence was limited by his constant companions, the winged serpents.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Information regarding this character is limited.
- If the base serpent did not possess Messmer from birth, then it was placed there by Marika herself.
- It is unclear whether the shed snakeskin near the Bonny Village belonged to the base serpent.
  - The skin is adjacent to the O Mother statue, implying a connection to Messmer. However, its appearance more closely resembles the flayed snake found in the Temple of Eiglay than the attacks of Base Serpent Messmer.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Messmer refers to the Base Serpent as "光無き、深淵の蛇が" that can be translated as "the Lightless, Serpent of the Abyss", without the idea that it was "shorn of light" but rather that it had always been lightless (光無, Hikarina, lit. "Without light").
- Messmer unleashes the base serpent by divesting himself of his mother's light.
  - Marika's actions ironically led to the base serpent's unsealing.
- In the Japanese version, the "base serpent" is called 邪な蛇 (*"Wicked Snake" or "Evil Snake"*).
  - The English word "base" is used to express a deficiency in character or status (*ignoble, baseborn, base instincts*).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Beastmen** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The beastmen were bestial humanoids who served the ancient dragons in ages past, wielding weapons clad in red lightning. They inhabited Crumbling Farum Azula, the ruined city in the sky, and were once granted five fingers of intelligence. Many were honored warriors of the Sun Realm, while others were chosen to guard the giant mausoleum of Dragonlord Placidusax.

The beastmen forged heavy yet balanced curved weapons from dull iron, and fired earthenware jars specifically to make shields. Despite their crude works, they possessed knowledge beyond human understanding.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text: True to their name, Beastmen appear to be half-man, half-canid humanoids with sharp claws, furry tails, and large snouts full of sharp, bloodstained teeth. Their skin is covered with scraggly dark gray fur, with bare patches exposing raw flesh and even bones, most notably on their lipless, skull-like faces. Although most Beastmen dress in little more than ragged wrappings and loincloths, stronger warriors can be seen clad in iron armor and chainmail, and all Beastmen decorate their bodies with unalloyed gold jewelry, including bracelets, crowns, and necklaces adorned with precious stones. They can be found wielding curved swords, jar-shields, or sickle-like throwing blades. Grey-haired Beastmen wield Clawmark Seals, which they use to cast lightning incantations. Some beastmen wield weapons imbued with red lightning, which deal lightning damage.
