sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bloodfiends** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Long ago, a subjugated tribe was saved from the ravages of war when they encountered the Formless Mother, who transformed them into bloodfiends.

The bloodfiends make offerings of blood to the Formless Mother, sometimes even spilling their own blood in devotion. Their sacred spears are central to their rituals, serving as instruments of communion with the mother of truth, an outer god who desires a wound. From her wound, Sacred Bloody Flesh may fall—a raw, blood-soaked meat that never dries or rots, valued as a delicacy by the bloodfiends.

The bloodfiends cultivate Sanguine Amaryllis, blood-red flowers with meaty petals, grown in pools of blood. These flowers may reflect their admiration for the beauty of blood.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Some of their weapons, sanctified through blood rituals, are capable of spraying stored blood when executing strong attacks.

; Bloodfiend (fork)

; Purple Bloodfiend
Bloodfiends carrying arms and forks found in the Stone Coffin Fissure. Their weapons and breath inflict sleep build-up.

; Large Bloodfiend
A gigantic bloodfiend that wields a massive arm pulled from its fellows.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Boc's mother** or **Mum** was an unseen character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Boc's mother was a highly skilled demi-human seamstress whose dedication to her craft left a lasting impact on her son. Her ability to create garments from scratch surpassed even the royal seamsters of the Erdtree capital. Among the sewing tools Boc inherited, her curved needle—shaped like a fang—stood out as a cherished symbol of her craft and the deep bond they shared. She taught him the art of tailoring, inspiring his deep desire to follow in her footsteps.

Though Boc struggled with his appearance, his mother was the only one who called him beautiful, giving him a sense of self-worth that he clung to throughout his life. Her memory drove him to perfect his skills, always striving to live up to the talent and kindness she embodied.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Boc's mother was a demi-human with deft hands. Her compassionate voice was recorded by a Prattling Pate, which can be found in the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Her unconditional affection for Boc was immortalized in the wistful Prattling Pate, which captured her tender words: *"You're beautiful."*
- Boc's mother was likely a member of nobility. She possessed specific knowledge of the royal seamsters, who repaired the clothes of the demigods.
- The lattice ornamentation featured on her sewing needle is identical to the stitching on the Mask of Confidence. Both designs are simplified version of the trellis of Radagon's Rune, and the seals on the Academy of Raya Lucaria gates and the Erdtree itself. The lattice design represents the threaded needlework both characters are known for.
  - Boc later trades in his mother's needle for the golden sewing needle once owned by Radagon of the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Black Knights** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Black Knights are an order of knights who are devoted servants of Messmer the Impaler, serving as the primary force in his army. Having absolute loyalty to their master, the Black Knights possess an iron conviction to their Crusade, and they never yield nor doubt their purpose, being strongly dedicated to purging the Realm of Shadow,

Wearing black armor ornamentally and etched in gold, they carry weapons and shields of black steel, decorated with golden embellishments, and are imbued with Erdtree incantations. The Black Knights also seem to emit a rotten odor from their gauntlets and greaves. The cause may be from the tainted nature of the blood that stains their armor, or it may stem from their blackened souls, which fester as a result of endless slaughter.

Despite their devoted loyalty, however, not all Black Knights serve Messmer without doubt; both Black Knight Commander Andreas and his son and second-in-command Black Knight Captain Huw rebelled against Messmer upon learning of his serpentine nature. For their betrayal, they were ultimately imprisoned in underground tombs.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Bestial incantations**, also known as **beast incantations**, are a type of Incantation in Elden Ring. They are used primarily by Gurranq, Beast Clergyman and the Vulgar Militia. These incantations harness the primal power of beasts, focusing on robustness, healing, and delivering devastating physical attacks. The Clawmark Seal and Cinquedea both increase the effectiveness of offensive bestial incantations.

They all have a very low Faith requirement.

sections.heading: Boosting Bestial Incantations
sections.text:
<section begin="Bestial Boost"/>
- Bloodboil Aromatic increases Physical Attack Power by 30% (20% in PvP) for 60 seconds as a Body Buff.
- Blue Dancer Charm increases Physical Attack Power by up to 15% at low carried Equip Load values.
- Cinquedea increases Attack Power by 10% when held in an active hand, and by 21% when wielded in each hand (stacks with Clawmark Seal).
- Clawmark Seal increases Attack Power by 10% when held in an active hand, and by 21% when wielded in each hand (stacks with Cinquedea).
- Exalted Flesh increases Physical Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 30 seconds as a Body Buff.
- Flame, Grant Me Strength increases Physical Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 30 seconds as a Body Buff.
- Uplifting Aromatic increases Physical Attack Power 10% (7.5% in PvP) for 40 seconds as an Aura Buff.
<section end="Bestial Boost"/>

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Blackflame**, also known as , is a type of flame in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Blackflame was weighty, alluring fire conjured by Godslayer incantations. Drawn from faith and the power of the Rune of Death, its black-and-white flames could burn away the very gods in ancient times.

Following the War Against the Giants, the beguiling blackflame enthralled Amon and other Fire Monks loyal to the Giants' Flame. Those who fled their duties formed the Blackflame Monks, aligning themselves with the  Empyrean Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Godskin Apostles. Together, they launched a violent god hunt, during which the black flame was their armor within. However, Queen Marika commanded her Shadowbound Beast and half-brother, Maliketh, to defeat the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles. She removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it in his black blade. The Golden Order was born, and the true power of the black flame was lost.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
All offensive Black Flame attacks deal  Fire damage and apply a special effect that inflicts additional damage equal to 20 + 2.0% of the target's maximum HP over 2 seconds.
- The effect does not stack, though further hits refresh its 2-second timer.
- All bosses in the Realm of Shadow resist this percentage-based damage, taking only 10 + 1.0% of their maximum HP over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler (Base Serpent Messmer), Bayle the Dread, and Promised Consort Radahn (Radahn, Consort of Miquella) take even less: 7 + 0.7% of their maximum HP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Gloam-Eyed Queen channeled Black Flames through her Godslayer's Greatsword.
- The flames of Destined Death are red, indicating blackflame may be drained of its former color. That said, the  Blackflame Monk's Seal is a colorless Giant's Seal and other Godskin paraphernalia likewise reflect the current color of blackflame.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Battle of Aeonia** was an event that occurred during the Shattering in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Battle of Aeonia was the infamous final act of the Shattering, which decimated the central region of Caelid, now known as the Swamp of Aeonia. The conflict arose when Malenia the Severed confronted General Radahn regarding Miquella's vow. Malenia and her undefeated Cleanrot Knight army marched southward through Liurnia of the Lakes and Limgrave to reach Caelid, where they met Radahn's Redmane forces in battle.

The Demigods were evenly matched, fighting to a standstill in a field southwest of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. The stalemate ended when Malenia, in an attempt to kill Radahn, snapped her Unalloyed Gold Needle by stabbing herself, whispering in her rival's ear: *"Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."* This act triggered her very first rotflower bloom, unleashing the baleful scarlet rot she had fought her whole life to contain. Although the Empyrean gained tremendous strength, Malenia was unable to kill Radahn and quickly succumbed to a deep, coma-like slumber.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text:
Malenia and Radahn's duel ended in a stalemate. Her Scarlet Aeonia scattered Aeonian butterflies and terraformed the landscape, driving back the Redmane Knights, but their leader survived. Radahn's Great Rune burned to resist the scarlet rot, though his mind was quickly consumed, reducing him to no more than a wandering, feral beast. In defeat, the Redmanes likewise burned the Red Lion crest on their left breasts to indicate their resolve, vowing to remain behind to act as a smoldering bulwark against the encroaching scarlet rot. Miquella of the Haligtree rescued Redmane Freyja from the Swamp of Aeonia, cured her rotting sickness, and charmed her into his service.

The festering Swamp spawned pests and other Servants of Rot, though Malenia would not embrace them. She lingered for a time before Cleanrot Knight Finlay pulled her from the bog and carried her back to the Haligtree. However, Malenia's daughters later emerged from the swamp, each child taken in by Sage Gowry. Romina, Saint of the Bud reached out to the abandoned scarlet butterflies and drew some of them to the Realm of Shadow.

Ultimately, none of the Demigods succeeded in becoming Elden Lord or the God of a new era, and they were abandoned by the Greater Will. Some time later, the guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who were called back to the Lands Between to claim the Great Runes, become Elden Lord, and restore the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Assault on Volcano Manor** was an event that occurred during The Shattering in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A gluttonous serpent dwelled on Mt. Gelmir in ancient times, feeding on human sacrifices provided by its followers. Although the Serpent-God was slain long ago, Praetor Rykard, a Demigod, later rediscovered the ancient hexes of the mountain. Despite being a ruthless justiciar, who mercilessly prosecuted—and tortured—those accused of heresy and other crimes, he grew disillusioned with the Golden Order.

In the wake of the Shattering, Rykard and his siblings each claimed shards of the great Elden Ring. Discontent with struggling over Queen Marika's scraps of power, he viewed the abasing war with total contempt. Believing that the gods were no different, Rykard turned to taking by force, launching a blasphemous insurgency against the Erdtree and the Greater Will. Many knights believed his ambitions are noble and made him worthy of sovereignty, pledging their support to his cause.

sections.heading: Assault
sections.text:
A war with no glory, the Assault on Volcano Manor is said to have been the most appalling battle in the Shattering. The conflict took place on Mt. Gelmir, between Rykard's army and the forces of Leyndell. The squalid, the sick, and the blasphemous are said to have participated in the battle, which went on without end. The attackers brought the Jar Cannon to the assault, however it was discovered that nobody knew how to use it.

Rykard would eventually feed himself, great rune and all, to the great serpent, known as the God-Devouring Serpent, an ancient traitor of the Erdtree, and he became one with the serpent. With his own lofty ambition turning into gluttonous depravity, Rykard began devouring on his own champions, feeding them to the bowels of the God-Devouring Serpent. The devoured champions would then become part of Rykard's "family" so they can devour the gods together. Disturbed by what their lord had become and the battles waged in his name being costly, Rykard's own men deserted him, no longer able to abide the consequences of his blasphemy. Those who remained came to be known as Recusants.

Psychologically affected by their experience in the assault, most of the soldiers in Leyndell's army eventually became afflicted by Frenzy - leaving them in a state of madness - and seemingly resorted to cannibalism, consuming the bodies of the dead, which became a sickening reality across the battlefields.

  - Two Cuckoo birds crowns the symbolic , implying the Academy of Raya Lucaria's hands in the crafting of the talisman.
- The black moon may be related to the Eternal Darkness spell of Sellia, Town of Sorcery.
- It is possible the large hole in Nokstella's ceiling was once filled by the black moon.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The blood star is an occult entity whose power is channeled by Faith-based Thorn Sorceries. It exists beyond the Lands Between and may only be glimpsed by those deprived of light. It is deeply tied to Blood Loss and the Briars of Sin.

The Guilty Sorcerers and other exiled criminals beheld the blood star after their eyes were gouged out during the War Against the Giants. Soon after, they began issuing blood sacrifices to weave bloodthorn spirals with aberrant sorceries.

Despite its cosmic origin, sorcerous practices involving the blood star were prohibited by the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Heretics who pursued it, such Mad Tongue Alberich, produced a special red glintstone saturated with blood. Such a power is comparable to that of Death hexes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Knight Bernahl's nameless Finger Maiden threw herself into the Forge of the Giants. According to unused concept she had detailed appearance and failed to become a kindling maiden. In full release, she only be mentioned in Beast Champion Set’s description and her ritual is presumed successful, considering that Bernahl's golden summon sign in the Crumbling Farum Azula requires no prerequisites.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: - Her presumed charred remains kneel in Dejection at the Shack of the Lofty on the Mountaintops of the Giants. Looting them grants the Traveling Maiden Hood, Traveling Maiden Robe, Traveling Maiden Gloves, and Traveling Maiden Boots. This finger maiden is also suspected of being Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood‘s maiden.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- An NPC version of Bernahl's Finger Maiden was planned for the Smoldering Church in Caelid, but was ultimately scrapped prior to the  and may no longer be canonical.
  - Only her face data, equipped armor, initial location, and Japanese dialogue subtitles made it into the game; information about this version of her character is based on an unofficial translation of the Japanese script and may contain inaccuracies. An official English source text has yet to emerge or does not exist.
  - She wore the Bloodsoaked Mask, Finger Maiden Robe (Altered), Traveling Maiden Gloves, and Traveling Maiden Boots. She was bald with golden eyes and burns covering her face.
  - She asked to be burned with various flames to become a Kindling Maiden, but was ultimately unfit. The Giants' Flame would not find purchase within her in the way it does Melina, whose story she paralleled.
  - This NPC was replaced with Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater, a false Finger Maiden who invades at the Smoldering Church. Anastasia also invades near the Volcano Manor, which was where Bernahl went after his maiden perished.
  - Bernahl's Finger Maiden described the Fire Monks as giant.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Asimi, Silver Tear**, later known as **Asimi, Eternal King**, was a Silver Tear character that was  cut from Elden Ring. They asked to enter the player's body to aid them on their quest. Information about them is limited and may no longer be canonical.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Asimi was located at the Artist's Shack in Limgrave.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Asimi was a silver tear that gained sentience and the ability to speak, living in fear of death. An arcane creature of mimicry, they came from a mother chalice in the Eternal City—the cradle of their kind—with dreams of one day becoming Sovereign Eternal.

sections.heading: Asimi's Quest
sections.text:
Asimi would have identified the Tarnished as the one fated to become Elden Lord, offering power in exchange for protection. Should the player accept, Asimi was inhaled through a kiss, living inside their new host.

Upon hearing the great underground rivers of their home, Asimi would have urged the player to visit the Eternal Cities, where special chalices could be found. Asimi wished to quench their thirst by drinking from these cradle chalices to become a more perfect whole. After collecting the tears from each chalice, Asimi likely exited the Tarnished to follow their footsteps.

Asimi likely morphed into the Tarnished and attacked them, much like the Mimic Tear and Stray Mimic Tear bosses.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- A unique "kissing" animation would have triggered when the player accepted Asimi inside.
- Melina offered unique dialogue if Asimi was present inside the Tarnished.
- They likely dropped or granted the Mimic Tear Ashes.
- The mother chalice was the most sacred to Asimi, and the cradle of their kind. It was suffused with the blessings of the stars.
- Radagon of the Golden Order also sought to become a perfect whole and reign for eternity.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Asími (ασήμι) is a Greek word for "silver".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Astrologers** were a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
At some point long before the rise of the Erdtree, the ancient astrologers established themselves in the Mountaintops of the Giants, the highest peaks of the Lands Between, where they dwelled at the Stargazer's Ruins and read fate in the stars. They considered the Fire Giants their allies and lived in peace alongside them.

One astrologer glimpsed the Primeval Current, and the stars showered the Lands Between with their amber: Glintstone, a crystalline substance bearing the vitality of the stars. This revelation gave rise to the first glintstone sorcery, the legendary Founding Rain of Stars. From then on, astrologers embedded glintstone at the tips of their staves, using them as catalysts for sorcery. In doing so, they became the precursor to the modern Glintstone Sorcerers, who continued their traditions. Some among them even fashioned Primal Glintstone Blades, slicing open their own hearts to bind their souls to primal glintstones before death.

Among the astrologers was Rennala, who spent her youth gazing at the night sky and following the stars. One day she beheld the Full Moon upon the Mountaintops, and from that moment she was set upon her path. Rennala later enchanted the Academy of Raya Lucaria with her moon magic and rose as a champion. There she became master of the academy and queen of Liurnia of the Lakes, establishing House Caria as royalty.

The Carians continued the astrologers’ legacy, constructing immense telescopes to chart the heavens. Yet with the coming of the Age of the Erdtree, the Golden Order supplanted the fate once governed by the stars, and Carian astrology fell into decline. Even so, the Carians preserved their heritage: Caria Manor safeguarded the Sword of Night and Flame as a relic of their ancient alliance with the Fire Giants, their preceptors wore wide hats inscribed with the motions of the stars, and the Stargazer Heirloom, commemorating Rennala’s legend, passed into the keeping of her daughter, Ranni the Witch.

sections.text: ***Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues***, unofficially referred to as *Elden John*, *Fellden John*, *Ancient Dynast*, *Ancient Dynasty God*, *Bearded Elder*, *Uhl King*, *Uld King*, and other names in the community, are objects in Elden Ring. All information about the statues and unseen character they depict is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The old statues portray a bald-headed elder with a long, braided beard and a missing right eye, dressed in a hooded robe and holding a stone tablet to his chest with elongated arms, though individual examples vary. Those on stone-coffin ships show him in his most human form, flanked by maiden-and-lord pairings, and may be among the earliest. Works attributed to the Ancient Dynasty give him a damaged right eye and arboreal traits—most notably a root-like beard—and depict him embracing one half of a broken tablet with tightly crossed arms, the discarded half placed at his feet; the held fragment bears a tree, while the other contains a ringed world map or sun. Statues at the Cocoon of the Empyrean omit the rejected tablet and replace his legs with roots. The figures at The Four Belfries, likely the most recent, emphasize his emergence from dense roots or dead branches. His robes have extended sleeves, and he raises his hands to his chest. His legs and both tablets are absent.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A bearded man was revered in the Ancient Dynasty that existed long before the age of the Erdtree. His heroic followers were sent off with Great Grave Glovewort in great stone coffin ships for burial at sea, drifting towards the Lands Between. When the massive arks finally washed up on the Cerulean Coast, their contents had putrified into a viscous sludge of bruise-colored putrescence. Though tainted and impure, the Deathbirds nonetheless cleansed the putrid remains in their ghostflame kilns, until they one day stopped.

His followers established a series of palaces along the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers, where claymen priests used crude weapons made from shards of fallen meteorites, which also arrived from outside the realm. They constructed the Hallowhorn Grounds, Uhl Palace Ruins, Uld Palace Ruins, Lake of Rot, Grand Cloister, and Mohgwyn Palace, and later The Four Belfries. At some point, their ancient dynasty collapsed, and the tablet-clutching god's name was forgotten.

The Ancestral Followers later worshipped Ancestor Spirits among the dynastic ruins. Their ritual implements evoked the power of horns, trees, and Deathbirds. The followers' faith existed beyond the influence of the Erdtree, asserting that new life arises from death, and from Death, one gains power.

After the outer god of Rot was sealed away in the Grand Cloister, the Kindred of Rot prayed toward scarlet rot-infested statues of the bearded man.

The Mohgwyn Dynasty worshipped a large statue of the bearded man at the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, which faced the Cocoon of the Empyrean, where eight smoldering statues of the bearded man portray him without legs, rising upward.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Some Ancient Dynasty stelae depict him tending tall trees.
- Rugs and folding screens in Leyndell, Royal Capital depict clones of the bearded elder growing like fruit on a tree, suggesting a link between the Ancient Dynasty and the Golden Lineage. It also indicates that the statues may not all depict the same individual.
- He may be related to the Suppressing Pillar because of its similarity to ancient dynasty architecture.
- His context connects him to various outer gods, including Death, Night, the Fell God of Fire, the Formless Mother, and even the Greater Will.
  - He has only one eye, but plenty of facial hair, similar to the Fell God.
  - His likeness seemingly appears with and without the hood on the Winged Scythe, linking him to Ancient Death. This weapon symbolizes white-winged maidens, who are said to be Death's gentle envoys.
  - The Putrescent Knight's head seems to contain starlight.
  - Mohg, whose Omen blood was aflame by the Formless Mother, seeks to establish a Mohgwyn Dynasty within the Ancient Dynastic ruins.
  - After the crusade ravaged the hornsent, they found the Formless Mother in the shadow of their ancestor, and transformed into Bloodfiends. Some sought out eternal rest from St. Trina in the Stone Coffin Fissure.
  - He may be related to Metyr, Mother of Fingers, who once communed with the Greater Will through her bubble-like microcosm, as Claymen Sorceries produce Magic bubbles within which oracles were once found, and Oracle Envoys use holy bubbles to herald the arrival of a new god. Maris, Fathom of Night, also known as the Augur and "master of bubbles," is another likely candidate.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The discarded tablet texture is sourced from the  (also known as the *Imago Mundi* or *Mappa mundi*)—the earliest known world map—which depicts ancient , often dubbed the “cradle of civilization,” as a sun or star-shaped region with two major rivers.
- Both tablets display a tree on one face, and a map on the other, but their reverse sides are not visible in regular play; they most likely share textures for performance and storage efficiency.
- The Bearded Elder shares many traits with , the All-Father from . Most notably are his association with trees, missing right eye, and role as a .
- The figure and his paired tablets also allude to , who received two  inscribed by the . His appearance on stone coffins also likens him to  because "Noah's Ark" are their filenames.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
<noinclude>

The **Champion** was one of the five playable characters . Unlike the Prophet and Warrior origins, Champion, along with Bloody Wolf and Enchanted Knight, would not appear in the final game, though its armor and weapon would be inherited by the Hero origin and the shield would end up being carried by the Samurai origin.

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.text:
Though the class isn't fully available as a starting Origin, even with the Hero carrying a majority of its equipment, it can be recreated.

The weapon and the shield, Battle Axe and Red Thorn Roundshield, can be gained by either starting as a Hero (this is also the only way to have 2 of them) or buying it from the Twin Maiden Husks and by starting as a Samurai or buying it from the Nomadic Merchant at  Castle Morne Rampart in Weeping Peninsula, for the axe and shield respectively.

The Armor Set is more out of the way if not gained by starting as the Hero origin, as it's bought from the Nomadic Merchant in southern Caelid, southwest of the  Southern Aeonia Swamp Bank Site of Grace and on the road split leading towards Redmane Castle.

The Finger Seal is bought from the Twin Maiden Husks or by starting as either either the Prophet or the Confessor origin, while Dragonfire requires a Dragon Heart (most easily gained by defeating Flying Dragon Agheel) and then sacrificing it at either the Church of Dragon Communion found past Coastal Cave in Limgrave or at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in southern Caelid.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.text:
The Hero origin is obviously a good start if trying to recreate this class, seeing as it wears the correct Armor Set and both has a Battle Axe and is the only way to get two of them without starting another Journey. It will need 7 points in Faith and 1 in Arcane to cast Dragonfire but will probably be better off by switching the Finger Seal for a Clawmark Seal to better synergize with the Strength/Faith build it's more naturally set up for.

The Prophet origin could also be a decent base since it can wield the Battle Axe one-handed with only 1 more point in Strength and cast Dragonfire with 1 more point in Arcane, but will lack any fitting equipment to start with.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.text: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, Confessor is objectively the worst choice. Origins become more efficient when they have lower stats as this means the low stat can be ignored and the points can instead be invested in attributes that the build makes use of. With Confessor's lowest stat values being a 9 in Intelligence and a 9 in Arcane, the origin only has a maximum of 2 points it can potentially save when compared with Wretch. Even in a build where none of its other points are wasted, Prophet, Hero and Vagabond save more stat points overall than Confessor, as their lowest stats are all at 7 which grants them far more build potential. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Sword of Night and Flame
sections.text: Despite the issues inherent to confessor it has one single solitary niche, being one of the two most optimal origins to build for the Sword of Night and Flame. It shares this tie with Astrologer and both origins save 1 stat point on this build when compared to Wretch. The only notable difference between the two options is that Confessor has 2 less Mind than Astrologer. This gap in FP does not affect the number of times you are able to use the sword's weapon skill, meaning that Confessor is overall the most optimal origin if you specifically do not want to cast spells as part of this build, or invest in being able to cast the weapon skill more often.

sections.text:
The caster sacrifices their own blood to summon swirling vines of bloodthorn around themselves. This spell can be recast up to 2 additional times, with increasing intensity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Catch Flame** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  600 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
- Starting equipment for the Prophet Origin.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Conjure a small burst of flames from the hand, that has Fire Attack Power equal to 225% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  10 FP per cast.
- Costs  17 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 7 Stance damage.
- Can be chain-cast continuously, provided the player has sufficient amounts of FP.
- Casting this incantation directly after a roll, jump, or backstep makes the casting time slightly shorter, making it much more dynamic than many other, slower spells.
- Moves the caster slightly forward with each use.
- Despite using the Giants' Flame, this spell does not generate a spell sigil when cast, making it ineligible for a boost from the Giant's Seal.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- With its rapid casting time, Catch Flame excels as a quick, close-range option for dispatching enemies. However, its small area of effect and short range make it less reliable against agile or fast-moving targets.
- A potent damage-dealing spell throughout the game thanks to its more than decent damage and extremely quick casting time, and available on a lot of Incantations build with only a minimal amount of Faith.
  - It is especially potent as an early-game tool for players who can manage the low FP cost compared to their meager FP pool.
  - Highly efficient as a melee spell for pure Faith builds.
- Casting Catch Flame immediately before Magma Breath significantly reduces the cast time of the latter, enabling quicker execution in combat.
  - When chained into Magma Breath mid-air, Catch Flame modifies the casting animation into a faster, more fluid spray, allowing players to seamlessly chain another Magma Breath cast.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Like Fire's Deadly Sin and Flame Sling, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.
<section begin="Corhyn"/>* Brother Corhyn was one of the prophets exiled for glimpsing the forbidden flame of ruin, a transgression that led to banishment.<section end="Corhyn"/>
- Catch Flame closely resembles the Combustion spell from the *Dark Souls* series.

- Bloodflame Talons, another variant of this spell
- Fire's Deadly Sin, another ominous prophecy spell
- Flame Sling, another ominous prophecy spell
- O, Flame!, a larger variation of this spell

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Astel, Naturalborn of the Void** is a Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Tiny stars fill a grand subterranean cavern downstream the Ainsel River, which serves as the boss room for Astel, Naturalborn of the Void. This area can only be reached by entering the Transportation Coffin at the edge of a scarlet rot waterfall. The player awakens in the green glow of a small chamber containing bioluminescent fungi.

The  Site of Grace unlocks after the boss is defeated. Proceed through the tunnel opposite the entrance and take the lift up to reach the Moonlight Altar. This is the only path to the Moonlight Altar.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The Transportation Coffin will not carry the player back to the Grand Cloister.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The internal data Astel's boss arena includes spawn markers for an Ancestor Spirit and its spirit animals, suggesting the Grand Cloister boss was reassigned to Astel from a third Ancestor Spirit encounter.
  - Astel has an unused animation in which it fell from the sky, crashing to the earth like a meteor. This move is used by Starscourge Radahn.
  - It is also possible that one of the Ancestor Spirit boss rooms was duplicated and used as a template.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Broadsword** is a straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Starting equipment for the Confessor class.
- Nomadic Merchant southeast of Coastal Cave, beneath the collapsed structure.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
- Always has the highest Attack Power (AP) of all regular Straight Swords, with the exception of the Quality Affinity, primarily due to its high base damage being able to compensate for its somewhat mediocre scaling.
  - Since it's acquirable extremely early, as soon as the tutorial is completed, this weapon is a useful tool for potentially the entire game.
- Surprisingly, compared to its predecessors from previous game, this weapon isn't short but merely of average length.
- Leans towards Strength for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities.
- Despite having the highest damage and scaling on its Heavy affinity it actually gives slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).
- Has a unique heavy attack and rolling attack, shared with the Cane Sword, replacing the usual thrusts with a broad, sweeping strike and an upward cut specifically.
  - This is mostly a disadvantage. While the unique heavy attack is mostly good, it lacks the Pierce damage of the usual Straight Sword heavy attack and thus can't counter-hit attacking foes, while the unique rolling attack is very lacking in reach.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Carian Knight's Sword** is a straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Held by a Carriage located in the northwest region of Liurnia of the Lakes, between the Northern Liurnia Lake Shore and The Four Belfries Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The locked, innate skill, Carian Grandeur, while not unique and reliant on its weaker Intelligence-scaling, is still very strong if it can hit. Best used as a replacement for a Critical Attack or while lying in ambush since it charges somewhat slowly.
- Gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Intelligence build (616 AP from having 45 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 45 Intelligence), a bit less from a pure Strength build (609 AP from 80 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 18 Intelligence), and far less from a pure Intelligence build (576 AP from 10 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 80 Intelligence).
  - Note that since the skill's damage is entirely reliant on the character's Intelligence and the weapon's Intelligence-scaling, the skill will be weaker on the pure Strength build compared to the other two builds.
  - Since the Carian Knight's Sword innate Intelligence-scaling is fairly poor, strengthening the skill and the sword's Attack Power together is somewhat difficult, with only the ease of upgrading weapons with Somber Smithing Stones over those needing Smithing Stones keeping it in front of regular Magic affinity weapons with this skill equipped.
- Has a unique blocking heavy attack, shared with the Lazuli Glintstone Sword. While this can make attacking into an attacking foe a bit less punishing, the resulting Stamina damage that will be taken if hit can prevent the user from attacking or rolling away.
  - While the brief hit-stun taken by shields isn't suffered when hit, the low Stability means that using the unique heavy attack is highly likely to result in a stun from being guardbroken.
  - Stability can be increased by 10% via two-handing and then further by the Greatshield Talisman.
  - While the uncharged unique heavy attack deals the same amount of Stance damage as a normal uncharged heavy attack, the charged version only deals 1.5 times more Stance damage instead of the regular straight sword charged version which deals 3 times more Stance damage.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A veteran of a battle that took place in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid. He continued to brandish his flag in the rot-eaten battlefield even after his lord fled. He wears the same armor and wields the same standard as Commander Niall, the leader of an army of no nation situated in Castle Sol.

In battle, Commander O'Neil summons the spirits of Exile Soldiers. Initially, he will summon five regular soldiers, and will summon three large soldiers after his health has been reduced to half. His attacks inflict Scarlet Rot.

O'Neil is in possession of the Unalloyed Gold Needle, which is required by Sage Gowry to stanch Millicent's Rot.

Polyanna, Adopted Daughter can be summoned for this fight.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Commander Niall** is an optional boss in Elden Ring. Defeating him will unlock the Commander Niall achievement.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Commander Niall, a veteran general of Castle Sol, offered his prosthesis in exchange for the lives of imprisoned knights, forming an army of no nation. A lone survivor, Niall commands the spirits of deceased knights to defend his master, who has long passed. Niall guards a chest containing the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left), one-half of the Medallion required to gain access to the Consecrated Snowfield, the land of Miquella's Haligtree.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: At the beginning of the fight, Niall summons the spirits of two Banished Knights, one with a sword and shield, and the other wielding dual swords. Niall will be relatively passive while the knights are alive, instead buffing them until they have both been defeated or his health has been reduced to half. Both Banished Knights will inflict Frostbite with their attacks. Niall himself uses a mixture of lightning and frost-based attacks. He can imbue his prosthesis with lightning and perform kicks and stomps, and he can use his halberd to generate frost.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **OldGeneral** (ID: 3050)
- The Japanese description for Veteran's Prosthesis states Niall offered his leg, rather than his prosthetic, in exchange for his knights.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Borealis the Freezing Fog** is an optional Great Enemy boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Borealis the Freezing Fog was one of the ice dragons, who were lords of the Mountaintops before the Fire Giants chased them from the peak.

The dragon Borealis patrols the frozen expanse of the Freezing Lake in the northeastern Mountaintops of the Giants. He emerges from a thick white fog, which he exhales clouds that inflict Frostbite.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Borealis the Freezing Fog is located in the Mountaintops of the Giants, patrolling the frozen lake southeast of the  Freezing Lake Site of Grace. The nearest Grace is  Spiritcaller Cave.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: - Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will award one  Dragon Heart,  100,000 Runes, and will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
Instead of flames, Borealis exhales Dragonice and Borealis's Mist.
- Borealis inflicts Frostbite with his breath attacks and roars. His attacks include:
  - Frost Breath: Borealis exhales a cone of freezing fog, which lingers and applies Frostbite.
  - Frost Stomp: Stomps on the ground, creating a shockwave of ice that deals AoE damage and builds Frostbite.
  - Frost Wing Sweep: Swings his massive wings, releasing icy projectiles that track players in the area.
  - Roar: Releases a deafening roar that briefly staggers players and applies frost buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Borealis the Freezing Fog counts as a Dragon-type enemy and is vulnerable to anti-dragon effects.
- Furled Fingers and Spirit Ashes are allowed in this encounter.
- Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Borealis is the only ice dragon in the game.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Borealis's Mist** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of frozen mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 158% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 110 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. 474% of Incantation Scaling and 330 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonice.
- Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Dragonice, and Ghostflame Breath), this is the most expensive one, but it effectively combines the high Frostbite build-up of Dragonice with the higher Magic damage of Ghostflame Breath.
  - Compared to Dragonice, this spell deals 17% more damage but also consumes 38% more FP.
  - Compared to Ghostflame Breath, this spell deals 6% less damage and consumes 17% more FP but causes 100% more Frostbite build-up.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 168 FP: 2*48 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 91 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the second weakest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 16% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath and 7% less damage than Agheel's Flame (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals only 2% more damage than Ekzykes's Decay.
  - However, the Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Agheel's Flame, a stronger Fire damage version of this spell
- Dragonice, a weaker but cheaper version of this spell
- Ekzykes's Decay, a weaker Standard damage of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot
- Ghostflame Breath, a slightly stronger Magic damage version of this spell that inflicts less Frostbite
- Smarag's Glintstone Breath, a stronger Magic damage version of this spell that doesn't inflict Frostbite

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Castle Morne** is a location in Elden Ring. Found at the southernmost point in the Lands Between, it overlooks the southeastern shore of the Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Castle Morne once belonged to the Stormveil faction that later fell to the Erdtree long ago. A clan of warriors rose against Queen Marika, only to be vanquished. The lone survivor, burdened by anger and regret, collected their swords and reforged them into a single Grafted Blade Greatsword. Morne was the site of their legendary showdown with Godfrey, First Elden Lord, commemorated by a nearby Sword Monument. Although the hero swore an Oath of Vengeance, they were ultimately defeated by the Elden Lord, and their sword became a treasure of the keep.

After the Shattering, this fortress fell under the control of Godrick the Grafted, a distant scion of the Golden Lineage, who ruled Limgrave from Stormveil Castle. He appointed Castellan Edgar to oversee the castle and its Godrick Soldier garrison; however, by the time the player arrives, it has fallen to an uprising by its maltreated Misbegotten servants. Edgar's blind daughter, Irina of Morne, fled the castle, but her Great Coffin escort was overtaken by Misbegotten on the road near the Bridge of Sacrifice. Edgar is bound by duty to maintain his post until the sword of Morne is reclaimed from the Leonine Misbegotten.

sections.text:

- The large Moangrave may represent the revenger or their clan.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In heraldry, *morné* (or *morne*) describes a beast, typically a lion, depicted standing fiercely on one hind leg with its forepaws elevated, without teeth, claws, or a tongue. The term derives from the Old French *morner* ("to blunt"), representing a defanged, defeated, or stripped-down state. The name "Castle Morne" likely describes the castle's recurring themes of loss and diminished power, including the golden lion emblazoned on the vanquished revenger's Grafted Blade Greatsword, the rebellion of the oppressed Leonine Misbegotten who seized that weapon, the prior conquest of the castle by Godfrey, and the suppression of Godfrey's true ferocity by Serosh, Lord of Beasts. It may also allude to Stormveil stormhawks or Elder Lions, whose respective talons and horns were amputated by Godfrey's Golden Lineage. Although stormhawks are absent from the castle, their likeness appears on palisades throughout its grounds.
- Mentioned in *Dark Souls III*, Morne was a knight who served the goddess of tears.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Castellan Edgar**, later known as **Edgar the Revenger**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Edgar was one of the Banished Knights, members of a defeated army who were driven from their home and sent to the fringes of the Lands Between. During or after the Shattering, he was appointed commander of Castle Morne by Godrick the Grafted, the Lord of Limgrave, who entrusted him with safeguarding its storied sword. Edgar lived there with his daughter, Irina, until the Misbegotten servants rebelled and overran the castle. Irina and a number of other inhabitants fled the keep, but Edgar and a retinue of Godrick Soldiers stubbornly stayed behind to prevent the Grafted Blade Greatsword from falling into the wrong hands.

The Tarnished may arrive at Castle Morne at the behest of Irina. Once the Misbegotten rebels are vanquished and the treasured weapon is reclaimed, Edgar is no longer bound to the castle. He soon departs, promising to spend the rest of his days with Irina, only to find that the Misbegotten have murdered her before he arrives. A grief-stricken Edgar vows to punish those responsible for his daughter's killing.

Edgar hunts the Misbegotten across the continent on his quest for vengeance, and eventually succumbs to madness. He later invades the Tarnished at the Revenger's Shack in Liurnia of the Lakes as an invader. Upon his death, Edgar bequeaths his Shabriri Grape, the eyeball of one consumed by frenzy.

sections.heading: Questline Progression

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Castellan Jerren**, also known as **Witch-Hunter Jerren**, is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Jerren is the elderly castellan of Redmane Castle. In the past, Jerren was a nomadic warrior who became a guest of the Carian Royal Family. There, he became acquainted with General Radahn, the son of Radagon and Rennala, the Carian queen, who would later challenge the stars and arrest their movements, halting fate. He was considered an eccentric by Smithing Master Iji, the troll war counselor of the Carians. During this time, Jerren made a promise to kill Sellen, the Graven Witch, a sorceress who had long been a hindrance to the Carians.

After spending time as a guest of the Carians, Jerren served as a guest commander under General Radahn, and the two swore an oath of honourable death to one another. During the Shattering, Radahn fought Malenia, Blade of Miquella in the Battle of Aeonia, and in the aftermath was driven mad by Malenia's rot, cursed to wander the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike. Jerren convened the Radahn Festival to give Radahn a warrior's death.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
He attracted champions from across the Lands Between to participate in a battle against the Red Lion General and a chance to claim his Great Rune. Among the champions who converge upon Redmane Castle to participate in the festival is the Tarnished who succeeds in defeating Radahn, giving him an honourable death.

With Radahn dead, the stars are once again set into motion, and Sellen is dispossessed of her immortality. Finally able to uphold his old promise, Jerren travels to Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, where Sellen is bound by the Academy's shackles. When he arrives, he finds her as a husk, her soul having seemingly already fled. Suspecting Sellen to still be alive somewhere, Jerren continues his hunt, eventually tracking her down to the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He vows to kill her and crush her Primal Glintstone, which facilitated her survival. Should the Tarnished aid him in defeating Sellen, he will thank them before departing, promising to meet them again at the next tournament.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. *(Optional)* Redmane Castle (before Radahn Festival)
  - Jerren can be encountered in Redmane Castle before initiating the Radahn Festival, sitting on a chair inside the church just beyond the Redmane Castle Plaza. Speaking to him here will unlock some additional dialogue with War Counselor Iji.
1. Redmane Castle (Radahn Festival)
  - When the Radahn Festival commences, Jerren can be found on a podium overlooking the plaza. Speak to him and select "Ready as I'll ever be" to trigger a cutscene. After the cutscene, wait for Jerren to finish speaking to receive the "Heartening Cry" Gesture. Next, go into the church behind Jerren and take the elevator down. Use the sending gate at the bottom of the elevator to reach the Wailing Dunes
1. Wailing Dunes
  - Defeat Starscourge Radahn.
  - *(Optional)* Castellan Jerren's summon sign will appear mid-fight during Radahn's second phase.
1. *(Optional)* Redmane Castle (after Radahn Festival)
  - Jerren can be spoken to once more after the Radahn Festival, in the same location he was in before the festival. After exhausting his dialogue he will disappear.
1. Witchbane Ruins
  - After following Sellen's questline up until she gives you Sellen's Primal Glintstone, reload and return to Witchbane Ruins to find Witch-Hunter Jerren. Exhaust his dialogue to progress to the next step.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
  - After transplanting Sellen's Primal Glintstone into the puppet in the cellar beneath Three Sisters, there will be two summon signs outside the door to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library. To progress Jerren's questline, interact with the red summon sign. You will be summoned to assist Jerren in defeating Sellen. Defeat Sellen to receive the Witch's Glintstone Crown and Sellen's Bell Bearing. After the fight, speak to Jerren, who will be just outside the room. Exhaust his dialogue to receive an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Witch-Hunter Jerren replaced Redeemer Guilbert, a cut character from an early, prelease version of *Elden Ring*.
- Jerren's mask and hood bear a resemblance to Slave Knight Gael, an NPC and boss in *Dark Souls III*, who shares his name with Fort Gael in Caelid. In this area there is a Stranded Soul NPC who makes reference to Jerren.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Coded Sword** is a straight sword in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: The Coded Sword can be found on the upper floor of the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital, in the room that mirrors the one that the Two Fingers of the Roundtable Hold can be found it. This weapon cannot be acquired once the Tarnished has defeated Maliketh.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- As the name suggest, the skill, Unblockable Blade, will pierce through all the damage negation from a blocking shield or weapon. It also has a very wide reach since it's a sweeping attack and deals Stance damage on par with a Straight Sword's charged heavy attack, meaning it can break the Stance of most enemies within 2 hits and most bosses within 3 or 4 hits.
- Unlike all other weapons, this weapon doesn't bounce away from any shield when wielded one-handed, not even when hitting the Ant's Skull Plate or sturdy enemies such as Miners.
  - Since this weapon has no Physical damage and instead is fully elemental, and its skill fully ignores all the damage negation of a block, it's not very wise to try to block it.
- Since this weapon deals pure Holy damage it benefits fully from Holy-Shrouding Cracked Tear but is also heavily weakened if the fought enemy has high Holy Damage Negation, something that becomes increasingly common among Bosses after entering Leyndell, Royal Capital, with most of them having 40% Holy damage negation and 3 (technically 2) late-game bosses having 80% Holy damage negation.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:

- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Brother Corhyn** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring. He can be given prayerbooks to access an array of Incantations.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order. At some point, Corhyn made his way to Roundtable Hold, where he teaches the incantations of the Two Fingers to Tarnished of the Roundtable, hoping that one of them might one day claim the title of Elden Lord, so that Corhyn might council them. When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable, Corhyn introduces himself to them, and offers his tutelage. Corhyn will even teach the champion heretical incantations, from outside the line of the Erdtree, though he does so reluctantly.

After the Tarnished champion opens the way to the Altus Plateau, Corhyn announces that he is departing the Roundtable to search for the legendary Goldmask, an eminent scholar of the Golden Order. While searching for Goldmask, Corhyn continues his own investigations into the nature of the Golden Order, and while he makes some advancements, he also becomes aware of how little he truly knows. With guidance from the Tarnished champion, Corhyn is united with Goldmask.

Corhyn takes it upon himself to become Goldmask's disciple and to chronicle his wisdom, deciphering the meaning behind every minute movement made by the mute Goldmask. The process goes well, until Goldmask's movements suddenly cease, as he is confounded by the nature of Radagon. The Tarnished champion may solve the riddle, revealing to Goldmask that Radagon and Queen Marika the Eternal are in fact one and the same, allowing Corhyn to continue his work.

Goldmask leads his disciple to the Forbidden Lands and the Mountaintops of the Giants, where none may tread. Corhyn continues his duty, but begins to doubt his master. He detects in his movements that Goldmask has begun to suspect the holism of the Golden Order, an unacceptable heresy in Corhyn's mind. Corhyn continues to serve his master, but is tormented by doubt.

After the Tarnished champion unleashes the flame of the giants to burn the Erdtree, Corhyn is found in the ashen ruins of Leyndell, Royal Capital. Corhyn denounces his master as nothing more than a madman, who rejected the perfection of the Golden Order and sought to replace it with his own "perfected" order. As the Erdtree burns above him, Corhyn loses his mind. Alternatively, Corhyn may be offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, causing him to remain in the Mountaintops, seemingly unaware that Goldmask has returned to Leyndell.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Corhyn can be found in the central chamber of Roundtable Hold, where he will offer to teach you several Incantations. His shop inventory can be increased by giving him prayerbooks.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - After reaching Altus Plateau, Corhyn will express an interest in searching for Goldmask.
1. Altus Plateau
  - Corhyn can be found north of the the Altus Highway Junction Site of Grace.
  - Talking to him here after finding Goldmask will allow you to reveal Goldmask's location to him.
1. Altus Plateau (Forest-Spanning Greatbridge)
  - Corhyn will now appear next to Goldmask. The pair will now travel together.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital
  - Corhyn and Goldmask can be found near the colosseum. Corhyn will express frustration at Goldmask's current obsession with Radagon.
  - After using Law of Regression in front of the Radagon statue past the lift near Erdtree Sanctuary, talk to Goldmask to reveal Radagon's secret and then talk to Corhyn.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
  - Corhyn and Goldmask will move to the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins. Corhyn can be offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, which will affect the end of his questline.
  - If offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, Corhyn will remain in this location after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade after Goldmask leaves. After reloading the area, he will have disappeared, leaving behind his flail, robe, and bell bearing.
1. Leyndell, Ashen Capital
  - If Corhyn was not offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, he will appear in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, close to the giant Bolt of Gransax after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. After exhausting his dialogue and resting at a Site of Grace, he will be gone.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Corhyn will refuse to take the Tonic of Forgetfulness if offered to him and it will remain in your inventory. Despite this, the act of offering it to him will influence the outcome of his questline. This choice will not affect the outcome of Goldmask's questline, however.

sections.text: The **Consecrated Snowfield** is a subregion located on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A snow-swept, misty area to the west of the Mountaintops of the Giants. The Consecrated Snowfield is final trial for those who seek Miquella's Haligtree, and can only be accessed by uniting the two halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, found in the Village of the Albinaurics and Castle Sol, and bringing them to the Grand Lift of Rold.

Visibility is limited in many parts of the snowfield. Small, golden lights illuminate the path from the upper section to the broad, snowy plane below, through which a frozen river runs. In the south-west are the Yelough Anix Ruins, consumed by the Flame of Frenzy. Far to the north lies the Apostate Derelict, where the gentle yet towering sister of Latenna the Albinauric resides. South-east of there is Ordina, Liturgical Town, which hides the entrance to the Haligtree. There is also a waygate, tucked away on the western cliffs, which leads to Mohgwyn Palace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Castle Sol** is a landmark in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Castle Sol is a castle in the northern Mountaintops of the Giants.
- Wandering Mausoleum outside
- Elder Lions inside the main courtyard
- Banished Knight spirits with unique movesets inside
- Boss: Commander Niall

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Castle Sol was an old fortress built on the northernmost tip of the Lands Between, belonging to those who later became Banished Knights. These drake hunters would gift an Icerind Hatchet, made from a scale of Borealis the Freezing Fog, to Liurnia of the Lakes as part of their diplomatic relationships.

In the distant past, a frigid, awe-inspiring eclipse mesmerized the knights of Castle Sol. Drained of its color, the lusterless sun repelled Destined Death and granted life to the soulless. The castle's inhabitants gathered at its Church of the Eclipse, where they used the storied Eclipse Shotel in worship of the dreadful celestial event.

In a later age, when veteran Commander Niall and his men were garrisoned at Sol, another force defeated them in battle even though they wielded storm and lightning-clad weapons. In exchange for the captured lives of his fallen men, Niall offered his right leg. Unable to die, and with nowhere to fade to, Niall eternally led the summoned spirits of his army of no nation.

Following the Night of Black Knives, Sol's inhabitants fervently prayed for another eclipse, hoping to call a spirit into the soulless demigod interred with their mausoleum. The Mausoleum Knights, who beheaded themselves to protect their masters as spirits, displayed the Eclipse to ward off the Destined Death of Godwyn the Golden.

Later, Miquella the Kind visited to castle and petitioned the master to return the life of his comrade. He bestowed half of a secret medallion to the master that would allow him to access the then-upcoming Haligtree if he had succeeded in his task. However, the awaited eclipse never came to pass, making the master of the castle unable to visit the Haligtree as he wasn't able to fulfill his duty, thus he lost hope and perished. Niall, the commander of Castle Sol, left alone in the castle to protect his long-passed master, continue commanding the nationless spirits of his Banished Knight army.

sections.text: Castle Sol is situated on the northern edge of the Mountaintops of the Giants, north  Snow Valley Ruins Overlook. It is accessed from the east, after traveling down from the graveyard with Giant Skeletons. The path is guarded by a Tibia Mariner and Death Rite Bird.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Cleanrot Knights were fierce warriors who remained devoted to Malenia, Blade of Miquella, even as her scarlet rot consumed their bodies. Their winged helms and sword insignias embodied the unyielding resolve of their Empyrean master. They stood in arms with Miquella's followers within Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

They fought under Malenia's command throughout her undefeated campaign in the Shattering, which culminated in the fateful clash against General Radahn's Redmane army in Caelid. A majority of the knights fell at the Battle of Aeonia, their spirits locked in eternal combat in the War-Dead Catacombs. The few survivors wandered the resulting Swamp of Aeonia, while others traced the footsteps of Cleanrot Knight Finlay, who bore the sleeping Malenia all the way back to the Haligtree, passing through the Shaded Castle along the way.

sections.heading: Chacteristics
sections.text: All Cleanrot Knights wear golden armor and wield a Cleanrot Knight's Sword as a secondary weapon to complement their polearms. This allows them to land multiple attacks in quick succession, triggering the Talisman's blessing to strengthen them even further. Most Cleanrot Knights wield a Cleanrot Spear, which bears a small shield on its shaft. They will imbue their spear with gold before performing their more deadly attacks, such as grabbing their enemy with the spear tip and infecting them with Scarlet Rot, and summoning forth a golden palisade from the ground. They can also brace their spear with their sword to absorb an incoming blow and quickly retaliate with their own. Cleanrot knight commanders wield the Halo Scythe. They prefer ranged combat, repeatedly firing rings of Miquella's light from a distance. In close quarters, they may vomit Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text: Cleanrot Knights are resistant to  Slash and  Holy damage, taking 35% and 40% less damage from these types. They receive flat damage from  Pierce and  Lightning damage, but take 20% extra damage from  Fire attacks; however, the scythe-wielding variant can nullify this vulnerability by casting an incantation.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A lone Cleanrot Knight, encountered in an alcove at the very end of Stillwater Cave that has been partially flooded in poisonous waters.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
Most of the room is full of poisonous water, so it's advisable to quickly run to the small island of safety just left of the boss, in the middle left to far left section of the room.

Since this boss is the spear-wielding variant and this fight will most likely happen early in the game, it's critical to avoid its Scarlet Rot-inducing, charging grab attack (signified by its spear glowing a bright gold). This is most easily accomplished by rolling diagonally forward to reach the other side of the boss. Since the boss is vulnerable to backstabs

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Cleanrot Knight and its commander, both encountered in an alcove at the very end of Abandoned Cave that has been partially flooded by scarlet rot. The remains of numerous Abudctor Virgins lay scattered around the arena.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
As the fight starts, only the spear-wielder is present, with the scythe-wielding commander rising from the rot pool to the left within 12 seconds of starting the battle. As such, it is best to spend that opening either summoning a Spirit or rushing down the spear knight to try and at least severely wound it before the scythe knight can join the fray.

Of the two combatants, the spear knight is more aggressive and will try to restrict player movement with its Sacred Phalanx and inflict Scarlet Rot with its charge. In contrast, the scythe knight will harass from afar with Miquella's Ring of Light and buff both of them with a unique combination of health regeneration and extra Fire resistance to cover for one of their weaknesses.

If fighting alone, try to pull the spear knight to the right so that the hill blocks the light rings and buys extra time to kill it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Church of Vows** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
An old, crumbling church on the eastern side of Liurnia of the Lakes. The Church of Vows was the site of the marriage between Rennala, Queen of Caria, and Radagon, the red-haired champion of the Golden Order, uniting the houses of the Erdtree and the Moon following their conflict during the Second Liurnian War. Several of Radagon's personal effects are found at this location, seemingly abandoned as part of his vow.

The aged tortoise pastor, Miriel, oversees the church despite its dilapidated state. He has in-depth knowledge of the history of Liurnia and the Carian Royal Family, which he is happy to divulge if spoken to.

sections.heading: Basin of Atonement
sections.text:
At the back of the church stands a Nox Swordstress statue and an ornate Basin of Atonement. It is said that Radagon repented his territorial aggression by cleansing himself with dew in this pool. The player may replicate this act here by offering up Celestial Dew, performing an Absolution.

Absolution simply reverts any NPCs that have been attacked and made hostile back to their original, non-hostile state. It will not render passive any characters that are hostile by default, nor will it revive those who have died. It will not restore Melina as a traveling companion, even if the Frenzied Flame has been suppressed with Miquella's Needle.

- Miriel is absent while the Bell Bearing Hunter event is active.
- The Church of Vows was presumably used by the Nox prior to their banishment underground.
  - The architecture at the church matches the Cathedral of Manus Celes and the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, implying all three buildings were constructed by the Nox.
    - The windows at these locations are paned with the same horseshoe-shaped "Two Fingers" motif.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Chapel of Anticipation** is a legacy dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Chapel of Anticipation is the first location the player explores when they begin the game. It consists of a small chapel connected by rope bridge to a wide-open courtyard featuring a large statue of Queen Marika. The path to Stormveil Castle and the rest of Limgrave has crumbled away, and a Grafted Scion is prepared to ambush any Tarnished who enter the courtyard.

After crossing the Sea of Fog, the Tarnished awakens beneath a maiden statue in the chapel. Their ill-starred Finger Maiden is slumped against the south wall, lying in a pool of her blood. Her body holds the Tarnished's Wizened Finger. An encouraging Message on the floor reads *"Though the path be broken and uncertain, claim your place as Elden Lord."* The room is exited through an operable door nearby.

sections.heading: Leaving
sections.text:
There are three ways to leave the Chapel of Anticipation:
1. Defeat the Grafted Scion
1. Be killed by the Grafted Scion
1. Fall from the cliff by walking near the Nascent Butterflies

Upon doing so, the player is transported to the Stranded Graveyard, where they are by rescued by Melina and Torrent.

sections.heading: Second visit
sections.text:
The player may revisit the area later via the *"Precipice of Anticipation"* Sending Gate at The Four Belfries in Liurnia of the Lakes. However, the teleporter must first be activated with an Imbued Sword Key. The destination point is on the side opposite the initial spawn point.

If the Grafted Scion was not defeated previously, it can be challenged once more. Additionally, the door at the side of the chapel will now be unlocked, allowing the player to collect Stormhawk Deenh and The Stormhawk King.

While most of the churches throughout the Lands Between are affiliated with the Golden Order, others serve the followers of other Outer Gods, and pagan religions founded prior to Queen Marika's rule.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This weapon is wielded by the young maidens who play a central role in the festival.
- Grants 10 Runes every time an enemy is hit.
- The strongest dagger for the Keen affinity, with its A being just on the verge of an S-scaling. Otherwise somewhat subpar or average when it comes to damage, including the otherwise Dexterity-scaling Lightning and Cold affinities.
  - Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
  - Pairs well with non-physical affinities such as Magic since those are usually already only partially negated by guarding and the ignored guarding damage negation applies to all forms of damage, not just Physical.
  - As a dagger it will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A large, dilapidated cathedral sitting atop the Moonlight Altar, a vast plateau overlooking Liurnia. The cathedral is guarded by Adula, a dragon in the service of Ranni the Witch. Within the cathedral itself, a large number of Starlight Shards can be found. Near the back of the church, there is a hole which leads to a small cavern, where Ranni's doll can be found sitting atop the corpse of her Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The name "Manus Celes" means "Hidden Hand" or "Celestial Hand" in Latin, though *Celes* is not a standard Latin word. It is derived from *manus* ("hand") and *cēlēs* ("to conceal, cover, or hide"), *caeles* ("deity, god; heaven-faring"), or *caelestis* ("heavenly, celestial").
  - *Cælestial* is an archaic spelling of *celestial*.
  - Its meaning may be intentionally ambiguous, as multiple interpretations supported by contextual evidence.
    - The "Hidden Hand" reading may allude to the hidden presence of the Two Fingers beneath the cathedral.
    - The "Celestial Hand," "Heavenly Hand," and "Hand of God" interpretations are supported by the abundant Starlight Shards in the area and the Two Fingers' association with Metyr, Mother of Fingers and the Greater Will.
