sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Carian Study Hall** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Carian Study Hall is a building on the eastern coast of Liurnia, to the north of Jarburg. It is connected to the Divine Tower of Liurnia by a great bridge, though it is not accessible initially.

The Study Hall consists of a vast library spanning multiple storeys, accessed by an elevator from a chapel-like entrance hall. The study hall is patrolled by Preceptor Miriam, a sorceress who calls upon blue, spectral nobles and prefers to fight from a distance using magical projectiles.

The hall hides a secret, which is revealed when a Carian Inverted Statue is placed onto a pedestal of a celestial globe in the entrance hall. Doing so flips the entire building upside-down, leading to another encounter with Miriam and revealing the entrance to the Divine Tower of Liurnia.

The player receives the Carian Inverted Statue from Ranni the Witch after bringing her the Fingerslayer Blade. The Divine Tower beyond the study hall hides Ranni's true body, which bears the Cursemark of Death.

sections.heading: Study Hall Entrance
sections.text: Found in the entrance chamber at the start of the dungeon.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.text:
For both versions of the area, the greatest danger will be dangerous ranged Magic attacks, so bringing some way to counteract that (such as Spellproof Dried Liver, Magic Fortification, or Spelldrake Talisman) is useful.

Normally only the Standard version is accessible but both versions can be freely switched between after acquiring the Carian Inverted Statue.

sections.heading: Standard version
sections.text:
From the only Grace, ignore the altar and walk around it. Take the elevator up to a split with stairs to a bridge on the left and a sidepath on the right. At the end of the sidepath is a Golden Rune [3] and picking up spawns two puppet Estoc variant Wandering Nobles.

Walking up the stairs spawns two more puppet Nobles and Preceptor Miriam. Hitting Miriam once or twice causes her to teleport further away, a behavior that will continue for the rest of the area until she is killed (though do note that she can skip over spots if enough damage is inflicted in one go). On the bridge itself 5 more Nobles will spawn as you approach Miriam on the other side, while she will snipe at you with Loretta's Greatbow.

The stairs at the other side of the bridge has Miriam and another puppet Noble and 2 more Nobles will spawn upon approaching a small raised stone section with the Carian Glintstone Staff. Further along and to the right is an elevator to the second floor.

The first level of the second floor is essentially a circular balcony where you play a game of ring-around-the-rosie with Preceptor Miriam and occasionally spawning puppet Nobles, now also with the sorcerer variant. Miriam will alternate between either using Loretta's Greatbow or Magic Downpour while teleporting clockwise around the area if you approach closely while she isn't charging a spell, so try to either attack her as the spell is being charged up or use a ranged weapon like a Bow. Since the puppets don't respawn until resting at a grace one may want to focus their first lap in killing them. Killing her gives the Magic Downpour sorcery and a Golden Rune [4] can be found on the ring.

To the left of the elevator used to come up and two lengths of the railing along is a ladder to the lower rafters. There is no item on the lower level but there are to Giant Rats, one straight ahead and one far to the right. Additionally there is another ladder up to the upper rafters, with 3 more Giant Rats and also the Cerulean Seed Talisman.

sections.heading: Inverted version
sections.text:
Using the Carian Inverted Statue on the altar instead changes the path behind it. The elevator well is now fall onto a ledge around a hole in the floor, and beyond it is a thin hole with 1 small Fingercreepers with another 2 flanking it on the walls.

Entering into the bridge room, which is now a set of walkways with a platform in the middle. Take a left to drop down to a nook with the Mask of Confidence while dropping down on the right takes you to 2 small Fingercreepers. Since Preceptor Miriam will be standing on the central platform and bombard you with Loretta's Greatbow and Magic Downpour, stick close to the wall when approaching. Two more small Fingercreepers are on the same platform and a spear-wielding Raya Lucaria Soldier puppet hides around a corner to support her. Reducing Miriam to half health causes her to teleport further away.

The Preceptor will stand across the gap, now unrestricted by cover, so keep an eye on her while dealing with the new enemies. Moving forward and to the right is a bridge with 2 Fingercreepers on it and a nook with a Fingercreeper to the right. Guarding Miriam final location will be 2 sword-wielding Raya Lucaria Soldiers that may have to be dealt with first. Defeat her to get Lucidity.

Since there are no more doors forward you instead have to either drop down to either the middle chandelier below you and then one below that or fall of the right side to the wooden walkway around the area. Either way lets you drop down to the rafters and some Giant Rats. The lower level of the rafters holds some Glintstone Fireflies on the central ring and a few Holyproof Dried Livers one the lower left offshoot beam (seen from Miriam's last spot).

Drop down into the elevator and use it to go down to access the door to Divine Tower of Liurnia.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bosses** are powerful enemies that can be encountered in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Bosses can be found roaming the overworld or inside one of the many locations in the Lands Between. There are in total **238** bosses.

Several key indicators can identify a boss fight. Firstly, the music changes to a more intense or dramatic score. A health bar and the boss's name appear prominently at the bottom of the screen. Bosses yield a larger amount of Runes when defeated, and their items rewards are added directly to the inventory. Unlike common enemies, bosses are not revived when the player rests at a Site of Grace.

Some bosses appear out in the open world and will attack the player if they wander too close. These field bosses may be disengaged and fled from. The player can lead them a short distance away from their spawn points. Certain field bosses only appear at night: Deathbirds, Death Rite Birds, and Night's Cavalry.

If the player challenges the dungeon boss, they are trapped within the room by a fog wall until the boss is defeated. If the player is defeated, they may be required to pass through a fog gate to rechallenge the boss. Some difficult bosses may be encountered early on, which can drive player exploration.

sections.heading: Mandatory bosses
sections.text:
Over two hundred bosses are available to fight, but only a few must be beaten to finish the game. These bosses are encountered after acquiring two Great Runes and gaining access to Leyndell, Royal Capital.

The boss fights that are not optional and must be beaten to progress include:

1. Any two shardbearers: Godrick, Mohg, Rennala, Rykard, or Radahn
1. Draconic Tree Sentinel or Fia's Champions
1. Godfrey, First Elden Lord
1. Morgott, the Omen King
1. Fire Giant
1. Godskin Duo
1. Maliketh, the Black Blade
1. Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing
1. Godfrey, First Elden Lord
1. Radagon of the Golden Order
1. Elden Beast

Two bosses must be defeated in order to access the *Shadow of the Erdtree*:
1. Starscourge Radahn
1. Mohg, Lord of Blood

Similarly, the bosses mandatory for completing the *Shadow of the Erdtree* are:
1. Messmer the Impaler
1. Romina, Saint of the Bud
1. Promised Consort Radahn

sections.text:

Enemies in this cave do not drop Items. It is unknown if this is intentional, or an oversite.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Carian Royal Family** was a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Members of the Carian royal family were prolific Sorcerers and erstwhile heads of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, who were famous for developing their own glintstone sorceries. They originated from the mist-laden region in the west of the Lands Between, known as Liurnia of the Lakes.

The Carian royal family would reach its peak under Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. In her youth, she was a prominent champion who would go on to charm the academy with her lunar magic, becoming its master. She also led the Glintstone Knights and established the house of Caria as royalty.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Carian Royals have always been closely associated with the western coast of Liurnia, which is the location of their estate, the Caria Manor, as well as the Three Sisters immediately behind it. Another location of importance was the Carian Study Hall, a large library in eastern Liurnia that connects to the region's Divine Tower.

The Carian royals were served by magic preceptors notable for large hats with the movements of the stars drawn on the inside of the brim, as well as on their bright blue gowns. All glintstone sorcerers are the descendants of astrologers, a fact that the Carians remained aware of. The astrologers preceded the sorcerers and had established themselves in mountaintops that nearly touched the sky, and considered the Fire Giants their neighbors. They would read fate in the stars, but alas, the night sky no longer cradles fate.

However, the Carian royal family were mostly known for the famous enchanted knights that served them. These enchanted knights, anointed by the Lunar Queen, were heroes of the highest honors, and served as direct retainers to the kingdom's princesses. Their swords were embedded with blue glintstone, and could serve as catalysts, letting them wield sorcerous battle skills. Despite numbering fewer than twenty, this power made them a match for even the champions of gold in battle. They combined this art with their swordsmanship to maintain pressure upon their foes, striking in waves of steel and sorcery. The Carian knights never wavered, and even had sorceries that could alleviate the buildup of sleep or madness. There were also enchanted troll knights among their number, comrades of young Rennala, bound by oath. They were called into service when the Queen invoked an oath they swore. These trolls were treated as true knights of Caria, and would fight arm in arm with their human comrades.

The famous Loretta was once a royal Carian knight, and served as a personal guard to Carian royalty. Despite fighting mounted and using a war sickle, her favored weapon was said to be the bow, and she developed sorceries imitating the power of a greatbow. She would leave her service in search of a haven for Albinaurics, but an apparition of her remains to defend Caria Manor to this day. Several Albinauric mages, such as Pidia, remained as servants to the Carian royal family, seemingly facing less persecution there then in other parts of the Lands Between.

The oldest sorcery devised by the Carians would conjure a Magic Glintblade, and it would serve as a prototype for more enhanced sword-phalanx sorceries wielded by royal enchanted knights. They also created sorceries that would conjure magic swords that could sweep, slice and pierce their enemies. Some sorceries were said to have been taught to them by the enigmatic Crystalians, to mark the swearing of an old concord.

Due to the influence of the Carians, the study of the primeval current was forbidden at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. However, the Lazuli Conspectus would eventually develop in the academy. The scholars of this conspectus sought to master Carian sorcery, and viewed the moon as equal to the stars. This would be seen as a heterodox pursuit, or even outright heresy, by their colleagues at the academy.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
When Queen Marika the Eternal established her new Age of the Erdtree, she dispatched a champion known as Radagon to lead her armies against the lands of Liurnia. Not much was known about Radagon before he joined the ranks in the Liurnian Wars, but he was seen as a great champion with flowing red locks, and he would lead a great golden host to Liurnia, where he would meet Rennala in battle.

Radagon would fight two wars against Rennala and the Academy, both of which saw no clear victor. Instead, Radagon eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, swore his love to Rennala and became the husband of the Carian Queen.

He married her at the Church of Vows, and it would be this matrimonial union, and reconciliation between the houses of the Erdtree and the Full Moon that would eventually have grave consequences for the Carians, as it was during the age of the Erdtree that Carian astrology withered on the vine, as the fate once writ in the night skies had been fettered by the Golden Order.

Rennala would bequeath Radagon with a greatsword, to honor a long standing tradition in which a Moon Greatsword is bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse. Upon entering into marriage with Rennala and joining the Carian line, Radagon would order Carian magic preceptors to don masks of confidence, to make it clear that all of their matters were to be kept strictly private. While husband to Rennala, he studied glintstone sorcery taught at the Academy. Together, Radagon and Rennala would go on to have three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.

After Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon left Rennala to become the second husband and King Consort of Queen Marika, and would receive the title of second Elden Lord. Queen Marika made Radagon's and Rennala's children her demigod stepchildren. When Radagon left, Rennala's heart left with him. Realizing their heartbroken queen was no champion at all, the Academy rebelled against the Carian royal family and Rennala would find herself under the assault of her own students, who would eventually lock her away in the grand library.

Liurnia decended in civil war, with the Carians and their retainers on one side, and the Academy and its Knights of the Cuckoo on the other. The soldiers of Raya Lucaria were known as the Cuckoos, as their symbol was a peering cuckoo bird, the bird's shrewd gaze an expression of their refusal to be mere servants of the academy. They were given free rein by the scholars of the academy to wage war as they pleased, and they were infamous for their rapacious ways*.* The Knights of the Cuckoo would use "faux sorceries" and would be taught lesser spells by the academy as payment for their contract. Meanwhile, the Carian royal family had secretly been preparing against the disloyalty of the academy by devising sorceries that could dispel incoming spells and retaliate with glintblades. The moon and stars would go their separate ways.

The war would eventually lead to the Siege of Caria Manor. The Carians were taken off guard, but their strength had not yet fully waned, and they managed to repel the onslaught by conjuring a powerful enchanted snare that remains potent to this day.

sections.heading: Current Events
sections.text: As the Lands Between fell into disarray, the last Carian Princess, Ranni, made her way back to her family's ancestral home, where she would gather her allies and vassals in order to set her own plans into motion. Her vassals included her faithful shadow, the Half-Wolf Blaidd, her families old troll blacksmith Iji, who was now her war counsellor, as well as Seluvis, a preceptor in the sorcerous arts. She also won the loyalty of Glintstone Dragon Adula who swore a knightly oath to her and now guards the path to her tower. The Tarnished can join the group and eventually become her consort as she ushers in her Age of the Stars.

sections.text:
<noinclude>
**Claws** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text:
Claws are hand-held weapons consisting of one or more blades extending from the knuckles of the wielder. They are similar to Fists in terms of their attack patterns and range, though they scale primarily with Dexterity rather than Strength. Though they are shorter than most blades (ranging between that of Daggers and Straight Swords) and deal modest damage per hit, Claws excel at delivering rapid-fire, close-range slashing attacks that rend flesh easily. With the exception of the Venomous Fang, all Claws feature innate Bleed Damage.

Each Claw comes in a set of two, with the Tarnished wielding one on each hand when equipping a Claw "two-handed" without taking up both hand slots. When equipped one-handed, the Tarnished will hold one claw in one hand while the other is left tied to their belt.

sections.heading: Pros/Cons
sections.text:
- + Lightweight
- + Fast/high DPS
- + Can proc Blood Loss and other status effects quickly (if applied)
- + Paired Weapons - can be wielded in both hands with only one slot
- - Short Reach
- - Only four kinds available/cannot be farmed within the same playthrough (I.E. if a player wants to dual-wield two sets of the same type of Claws, they will have to wait until NG+ to acquire another)
- - Few Ashes of War available

**Colossal Swords** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
They have excellent reach and area coverage, along with high damage against both health and poise, at the cost of their high weight and slow attack speed. Its one-handed moveset's slow speed is at risk of getting parried; however, most moves of its two-handed moveset are completely un-parriable.

Most Colossal Swords require a decent amount of investment into the Strength attribute in order to be wielded; however, it's possible to still wield a colossal sword with less strength than listed through two-handing, as two-handing increases the player's effective Strength by 50%.

sections.text: **Commoners**, also known as , are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Lower-class citizens of Lands Between, commoners can be found in most major settlements. They no longer have their wits about them, and are typically hostile towards the Tarnished.  They are most often seen wearing boards around their neck depicting a sprawling tree, with holes formed by its roots. This is a self-imposed shackle representing a voluntary display of allegiance to the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Commoners dressed in plain garb, bearing evidence of their devotion to the Erdtree on the boards hung around their necks. They fight using weathered straight swords, and will sometimes throw Fire Pots and Ruin Fragments.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Maddened commoners found in places touched by the frenzied flame, which can be seen burning in their eyes. They are found in the Ailing Village, Frenzied Flame Village, and Yelough Anix Ruins. They fight using swords and spears, and can harness the power of the frenzied flame to unleash Madness-inflicting attacks.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: White-haired necromancers found only in the Black Knife Catacombs. They dress in similar garb to commoners, but with black tunics, and they carry torchpoles blazing with a pale flame. They have the ability to continuously resurrect nearby Skeletons by preventing them from being permanently killed unless holy damage is used. If the necromancer is killed, all of the skeletons connected to them will also die.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Commoners clad only in ragged loincloths and headbands, found exclusively in Volcano Manor. They wield swords, torches, and spears, and will use Fire Pots, Poison Pots, Oil Pots and Ruin Fragments.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Commoners dressed similarly to necromancers, but with the addition of a veil. They are only found at the Minor Erdtree (Capital Outskirts), surrounding an Omen which, like the commoners themselves, can cast Fia's Mist.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Catacombs** are recurring Landmarks in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Catacombs are maze-like, subterranean dungeons that include puzzles and have at least one Boss. They are accessed by locating and opening a door at their entrances in the overworld and descending elevators. They are almost always filled with traps and require the player to pull a lever to unlock the large door to the boss's arena, which bears a relief of a tree with corpses within its roots. They are typically guarded by Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, their Imp underlings, and Grave Warden Duelists.

These burial grounds were constructed in proximity to Greattree roots and often contain Glovewort and Spirit Ashes. Usher of Death, Rosus guides the spirits of the dead back to the roots. Interacting with a statue of Rosus produces a trail of blue light that indicates the entrance to the nearest catacombs, provided the player has not already discovered the landmark.

sections.text: There are 18 Catacombs to find in the Lands Between and three more to discover in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Catacombs contain unique statues of Skeletal Grave Wardens, Imps, Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, Basilisks, and more. Grave Warden statues carry croziers.
- Torrent cannot be summoned inside Catacombs.

sections.heading: Overview

The Chest is a separate Inventory that holds items. Its menu is accessible at any Site of Grace by selecting **Sort Chest**.

Collected items that exceed their alloted carry capacity are automatically transferred to the Chest. Consumable items are refilled when the player rests at Sites of Grace, though this feature may be toggled for individual items.

Stackable items may be stored to a maximum amount, typically 600 or 999.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Bols, Carian Knight** is an optional boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A hulking troll knight clad in heavy armor and wielding a massive greatsword, Bols was one of the Trolls called into service by the Carians, fighting as a true enchanted knight alongside human comrades. Bols was imprisoned within the Cuckoo's Evergaol in western Liurnia of the Lakes by the Knights of the Cuckoo during the Liurnian Civil War.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: A towering troll knight with slow, sweeping greatsword attacks that create shockwaves. His size makes it easy to pass between his legs and circle to his back. He can summon Greatblade Phalanx blades overhead.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: - Cuckoo's Evergaol (Liurnia of the Lakes)

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
- HP: 5,109
- Defense: 110
- Stance: 65
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
- Cannot be Parried
- Strong vs  Magic and  Frostbite
- Weak to  Slash,  Poison,  Scarlet Rot, and  Blood Loss
- Closest Site of Grace:  Revenger's Shack
- Multiplayer is not allowed; Spirit Ash summons are disabled

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Bols, Carian Knight deals  Standard damage,  Slash damage,  Pierce damage, and  Magic damage.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Use his size: dodge between his legs and stay on his back side.
- Keep him in view; he can pivot quickly into a follow-up.
- Stay close even for ranged builds; create distance only to reset spacing.
- When he casts Greatblade Phalanx, sprint toward him so the blades pass overhead.
- Shockwaves from slams fan out in front; positioning behind him mitigates most follow-ups.

sections.text: A chilly catacombs in the south-eastern Consecrated Snowfield. The dungeon contains two pillars that emit jets of Frostbite-inflicting mist, which can be disabled by hitting them. There are also Erdtree Burial Watchdogs and Cleanrot Knights scattered throughout.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Cave of the Forlorn** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: An icy cave in eastern Consecrated Snowfield, on the north bank of the frozen river. The two levels are separated by a thick sheet of ice, allowing one to glimpse the lower level from above. The cave is inhabited by Misbegotten and hostile Spirit Jellyfish. At the bottom is a Misbegotten Crusader who wields a Golden Order Greatsword once owned by Radagon of the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Caelid Colosseum** is a Location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
An old Colosseum located in northern Caelid, accessed from the Siofra River via the Deep Siofra Well, then traveling north through a ravine. The path is guarded by massive Guardian Golem Archers who fire blue Golem's Magic Arrows.

This arena once hosted gladiatorial combat in honor of the Erdtree during the reign of Lord Godfrey. It was closed during the time of Lord Radagon, and its Duelists were exiled.. However, it is possible that either the colosseum of Caelid managed to remain open or that General Radahn revived the practice of gladiators' fights, since Redmane Freyja was once a gladiator herself and was chosen by Radahn after witnessing her valor in the arena.

The towering Great Jar stands before the arena. Various Knights of the Great Jar may be challenged via red Duelist summon signs. Defeat three champions without dying to unlock the door to the Caelid Colosseum. Interact with the statue of Marika to unlock the activity.

sections.heading: Colosseum PvP
sections.text:
Online player-vs-player battles at the Caelid Colosseum allow the use of Spirit Ashes. All three game modes are available:
- Combat Ordeal – Timed free-for-all deathmatch
- Duel Mode – One-on-one duel; no respawns
- United Combat – Timed team deathmatch

sections.heading: Characters

- Knight of the Great Jar x3

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Interacting with the Marika statue for the first time also unlocks the activity queue at the Roundtable Hold.
- When playing online, the pregenerated Knights of the Great Jar are replaced with computer-controlled copies of random players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The colosseum interior was inaccessible prior to the December 7th, 2022 update. The door could not be opened in earlier versions of the game.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Acquired after defeating Commander Niall in the Castle Sol.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Colossal remains**, also known as **giant skeletons**, **titans**, and other unofficial names, are objects in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
]]
The colossal remains are mountainous skeletal vestiges of a long-extinct species of giant, whose sheer size far surpassed that of Trolls and even Fire Giants. Their immense skulls feature hollow eye sockets large enough to accommodate roosting Giant Crows, and their bones have hardened into solid stone.

These skeletons are embedded into the earth throughout Caelid and the Mountaintops of the Giants. In Caelid, the remains are deeply overgrown with large wooden roots and covered in a thick layer of fungal growth. In contrast, those found in the Mountaintops are fully exposed.

Most of the Mountaintops' colossal skeletons are located on Flame Peak. Two notable examples can be found within a fissure between the  Foot of the Forge Site of Grace and the Fire Giant's boss arena.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Only the upper torso and skulls are exposed.
- The skeletons found in Caelid are much larger than those on the Mountaintops.
- The cause of the colossal giants' extinction remains unknown.
- Due to the enormity of their size, it's possible these colossal giants were the original architects of the ancient ruins like the Rauh Ruins along with other landmarks that share the same architectural style, such as the Forge of the Giants and the Divine Towers.
- The giants are the only known creatures large enough to have used the arrowhead that became the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword. It is possible they were the old gods.
- Shadowy titans of similar proportions appear in Limveld on the second Noontide. These colossi appear to be formed from woody vines, and lack bones and upper skulls. Heolstor the Nightlord can reincarnate as one of these arboreal Night Giants.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In Norse mythology, the  Vafþrúðnir claims the earth was formed from the body of .
- In the *Elden Ring* Closed Network Test, heads of similar proportions were present in Limgrave when viewed from Stormveil Castle. Deep lacerations were carved into their stone flesh, which burned like coals.
- A cut dialogue from Enia describes Radahn solely as "the slayer of giants." It is possible the remains in Caelid may once have been related to this cut aspect of his character.

sections.page: Chapter 1: You Thought This'd Be Serious. Didn't You?
sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **You Thought This'd Be Serious. Didn't You?** is the 1st chapter of the 1st volume of the *Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree* manga, written and illustrated by Nikiichi Tobita.

sections.page: Chapter 1: You Thought This'd Be Serious. Didn't You?
sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
<onlyinclude>The story of the Death of Godwyn, the Shattering War and several Tarnished rising to the call of grace is told. A girl and a steed, Torrent, arrive in a cave in search for a potential Elden Lord, with an unconscious tarnished lying naked, on the floor. She leaves behind two sacred flasks in the hopes that they'll serve him on his journey. The tarnished is next seen exiting a mausoleum to be greeted by White Mask Varré, who's unusual mannerisms unnerve him. Varré recommends that the tarnished starts his journey to Stormveil, an advice he takes openly and proceeds to attempt asking the nearby golden knight for a ride to the castle, only to be met with violence. Meanwhile in Stormveil Castle, Godrick the Grafted is judging recent grafting as presented by Gatekeeper Gostoc. Finding them lackluster, Godrick urges the servants to work more collaboratively in creating new designs before leaving. The tarnished is then seen despairing over the ruthlessness of every living thing he comes across only to be met by the girl who left him the flasks, Melina, offering him an accord.
</onlyinclude>

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Confessors** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The confessors were Tarnished who once received the guidance of grace, but willfully ignored the path it laid before them. In doing so, they lost the ability to perceive it again. Though their grace was never restored, they found renewed purpose as covert operatives serving the Two Fingers at the Roundtable Hold.

These assassins operated in darkness, tasked with eliminating other Tarnished who had strayed from grace. Their covert missions often led them beyond the Lands Between, where they served churches aligned with the Fingers’ doctrine as wandering priests and spies.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Dressed in black leather to blend seamlessly into the night, confessors use their talents to eliminate enemies of the Fingers and rogue Tarnished alike. They employ subterfuge to distract and confound their enemies, setting the stage for a deadly ambush.  Using ritual implements, they masked the sound of their movements, causing many paranoid Tarnished to dread total silence.

One of the most prominent head confessors, Crepus, wielded a long-range black-key crossbow, fitted with spiral-tipped bolts that injected scarlet rot deep into his targets. Another assassin, Rileigh the Idle, also used the black-key crossbow along with a dagger fashioned from the stinger of a great scorpion.

The confessor emblem is a black-key.

sections.text:
- Confessor (player origin)

- Rileigh the Idle

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The confessors' logo is called the Black-Key.
- Many of the Confessors' Two Fingers incantations were preserved in assassin's prayerbooks.
- Shadow Bait is found on a corpse representing a confessor in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.
- The Confessor origin starts with a Broadsword, Finger Seal,  and Blue Crest Heater Shield. They cast Urgent Heal and Assassin's Approach.
- The Two Fingers similarly used Baleful Shadows to pursue rogue Empyreans.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Buffs** are effects applied by a Tarnished to either themself or to themself and their allies, and are used to strengthen offence or defence.

They primarily come in three categories: Weapon Buffs, Body Buffs, and Aura Buffs.

sections.heading: Weapon Buffs
sections.text:
All Weapon Buffs are self-targeted, and almost all of them have only offensive benefits, with very few exceptions. They cannot be applied to any type of ranged weapon or casting implement, and only a few specific ones can be used on shields.

It's possible to keep two weapons buffed at the same time by two-handing the left-hand weapon and using either a Grease or a Skill on it, then stopping the two-handing so that the right-hand weapon also can be buffed with either a Grease or a Skill. It isn't necessary to use the same buff category for both weapons.

Some weapons are buffable and some aren't. As a general rule, weapons upgraded with Smithing Stones are buffable while weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones aren't buffable unless their innate skill grants them a weapon buff. Exceptions to this rule are the Crystal Knife and Ivory Sickle, two Smithing Stone weapons that aren't buffable, and the Bloodhound's Fang and Varré's Bouquet, two Somber Smithing Stone weapon that are buffable.

Additionally, weapons equipped with affinities that aren't either Standard, Heavy, Keen, or Quality also aren't buffable except for with the Skills that are compatible with those affinities, with no exceptions.

For Weapon Buffs that are also either Sorceries or Incantations, they can only be cast on right-handed weapons (or left-handed shields for the shield-specific ones).

sections.heading: Body Buffs
sections.text: Most Body Buffs are self-targeted and defensive in their benefits, but some, primarily those that are the upgraded form of weaker Body Buffs, also grant their benefits to nearby allies. A scant few are instead focused on increasing the caster's offensive strength.

sections.heading: Aura Buffs
sections.text: All Aura Buffs target both the caster and their nearby allies, and most, with the exception of some offense-only Aura Buffs, provide both offensive and defensive benefits.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Chaos Followers are the names given to those who have fully succumbed to madness and the allure of the Frenzied Flame. They have found the pain of living too much to bear, to the point where many wish they were never born and so they now yearn for the arrival of their lord, who may incinerate all that divides and distinguishes, so that none may be born to face the suffering of the world ever again. They have two established settlements in the Lands Between; Callu the Ailing Village in the Weeping Peninsula and the Frenzied Flame Village of Northeast Liurnia.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Commander Gaius** is an optional boss in Shadow of the Erdtree encountered outside the backdoor of the Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Commander Gaius was a noted warrior and military strategist who rode a giant boar as his steed. Gaius studied gravitational magic from an Alabaster Lord. He was a fellow student of Radahn, a future demigod. He also befriended Messmer the Impaler, as both had in common that they were cursed from birth. The pair were as elder brothers to Radahn, with whom Gaius had formed a friendly rivalry.
When Messmer embarked on the purge of the Land of Shadow on Queen Marika the Eternal's orders, Gaius would join him and serve as the commander of his soldiers. He was never without his boar. Even when Marika abandoned Messmer, Gaius remained steadfast, guarding the backdoor of Shadow Keep. It was here that he would meet his end at the hands of a Tarnished champion.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text: Commander Gaius is an albinauric without legs who rides a heavily armored, great-tusked boar. Gaius wears black iron armor patterned to represent fallen seeds and wields the Sword Lance. He was cursed by his Albinauric heritage and as such was doomed to lose the use of his legs.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text: Commander Gaius will charge with his boar to try to run you over. This can be dodge by jumping over with torrent or dodging at a very exact moment. He also uses gravity magic to attack enemies that are too far away.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wears Gaius's Helm, Gaius's Armor, Gaius's Gauntlets, and Gaius's Greaves
- Wields Sword Lance
- Casts Blades of Stone
- Gaius serves as a foil to Royal Knight Loretta, who hid her Albinauric nature from her compatriots.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Briar Set** is an armor set in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Each piece can be purchased from Finger Reader Enia after defeating Elemer of the Briar in The Shaded Castle.
- The regular chestpiece can be bought for 6,000 runes and the other 3 pieces cost 4,000 runes each, for a total cost of 18,000 runes for the entire set.
- The altered chest piece can be attained by altering the regular chest piece with the Tailoring Tools.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The set has good overall physical defenses, with a slight weakness toward Strike damage, and good Fire defense, mirrored by a significantly lower Lightning defense. It also offers strong resistance against Blood Loss and Frostbite due to its high Robustness, with decent resistance against Poison and Scarlet Rot from its somewhat lower Immunity.
- Each armor piece causes a small amount of damage (25 points from either chest piece and 18 from each other armor piece, for 79 damage total when the whole set is worn) when the wearer touches an enemy while rolling or using the skills Quickstep or Bloodhound's Step.
  - Note that this is before any damage reduction is applied, usually resulting in less than 15 damage being dealt when the whole set is worn.
  - While the damage is extremely low, it still has significant utility: weaker enemies can be lightly staggered by the damage as if they were hit by a Dagger or Straight Sword, and other players can be finished off or have their Opaline Bubbletear effect removed.
  - The effect stacks with the Mantle of Thorns sorcery, which will also add some minimal Blood Loss build-up to rolls.
- The total Poise of 47 is just short of the common PvE breakpoint of 51 to resist lighter enemy attacks. Swapping out a piece or two to reach that level is a good idea unless the damage from dodging is extremely attractive to you.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Cleanrot Set** is an armor set in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- The regular pieces drop at a 3% rate from Cleanrot Knights.
  - The altered head and chest pieces are gained by altering the regular version with the Tailoring Tools.
  - An early farming spot with a lot of Knights is the Heart of Aenoia Site of Grace in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid, where large groups are hidden to the south and to the southwest.
  - The shortest farming route is the lone Cleanrot Knight outside of the Prayer Room Site of Grace in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The 58 Poise this Armor Set has (53 if using the Altered pieces) is just above the minimum 51 Poise breakpoint required to prevent being staggered by about half of all resistible attacks.
- Excellent Immunity and Robustness grants high resistance to Poison, Scarlet Rot, Blood Loss, and Frostbite.
- Excellent Strike and Pierce defense, the former of which is quite unusual on a metal armor set.
- Surprisingly enough the Set doesn't carry any of the Fire weakness the associated enemies have. Additionally, it only has a minor weakness to Lightning compared to other sets made of metal.

sections.heading: Summary

**Carian Sorceries** (カーリア王家の魔術, *Kāria Ōke no Majutsu*), also known as **Glintblade Sorceries** (輝剣の魔術, *Kiken no Majutsu*), are a school of magic in Elden Ring. They are favored by the Carian Royal Family, which this collection of sorceries have been named after. Carian sorceries come in various shapes and sizes, several being favored by particular groups within the monarchy.

A majority of these spells conjure some form of weapon out of magic, most of them swords of varying shapes and sizes, which is favored by the knights and other oathsworn servants. One knight in particular, Loretta, would favor greatbows made of magic. Many Carian sorceries are not mutually exclusive to a particular group, and individuals have been known to incorporate the tools of other Carian groups into their own arsenal.

The only spells that are truly unique to an individual are the moon sorceries, as each are exclusive to their own chosen princess.

All offensive Carian sorceries deal pure Magic Damage and have an Intelligence requirement.

sections.text: **Charo's Hidden Grave** is a subregion in Shadow of the Erdtree, located in the Realm of Shadow. This area is accessible via Dragon's Pit after defeating the Ancient Dragon-Man. From the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion site of grace, head southwest along the foot of the massive dragon, then turn west to reach the area.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Charo's Hidden Grave is a plateau on the southern shore of the Gravesite Plain, where a sacred field of glowing red blossoms grows. The plateau overlooks the Cerulean Coast, contrasting with the solemn blue field below. The area also features peaceful rivers, waterfalls, gravestones, and Those Who Live in Death.

The original grave keepers rest amidst this crimson sea of lilies. Legend has it that the wizened Tibia Mariner's ancient skulls still retain the power to summon the dead. A rare gravesite flower, the Ghostflame Bloom, is said to grow in here, blossoming into the cold ghostflame. This barely tangible flower silently burns and is the sister to the spirit-calling Grave Violet.

- Charo's Hidden Grave features many  (*Lycoris radiata*), also known as "death flowers" or "corpse flowers." In Japanese culture, these poisonous flowers, commonly planted in cemeteries, symbolize death, final goodbyes, and the passage to the afterlife.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Charo** was an character mentioned in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The final resting place of Charo was concealed on the southern shore of the Gravesite Plain, among a hallowed field of crimson lilies overlooking the solemn Cerulean Coast.

Charo's Hidden Grave was shared with the wizened Tibia Mariners, first of all grave keepers, who guided Those Lost in Death long after withering away. A rare gravesite flower was also said to blossom there into cold ghostflame. The silent-burning, barely-tangible ghostflame bloom was sister to the spirit-calling grave violet.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - It can be inferred that Charo was the founder or patron of the Tibia Mariners. His may also be the first grave they were keeping.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Charo's name is a corruption of , the ferryman of the dead in Greek myth. Charon was said to transport the souls of the dead down the  in the .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The *'Chair-Crypts* (椅子廟, *Isubyō*)' are objects in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The chair-crypts are towering stone thrones of religious significance constructed by the Nox in ancient times. They appear in the Eternal Cities and Sellia, Town of Sorcery. These chairs are carved from stone and decorated with ornamental floral patterns, including a large inverted flower on their backrests. Some are occupied by giant mummies. Beneath each throne lies a chamber containing a chest with valuable Nox relics. Occupied chair-crypts also contain a Great Ghost Glovewort.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
There are four chair-crypts in the Lands Between:

1. Sellia, Town of Sorcery ( Chair-Crypt of Sellia) — an unoccupied throne guarded by a Nox Swordstress & Nox Monk; contains Lusat's Glintstone Staff
1. Nokron, Eternal City ( Night's Sacred Ground) — an occupied throne guarded by a Troll Mimic Tear and several Mimic Tears; contains the Fingerslayer Blade and a Great Ghost Glovewort
1. Nokstella, Eternal City ( Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella) — an occupied throne guarded by Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella; contains a Great Ghost Glovewort
1. Nokstella, Eternal City ( Nokstella, Eternal City) — an unoccupied throne guarded by a Nox Swordstress and two Mimic Tears; contains the Moon of Nokstella
1. Noklateo, the Shrouded City () — an occupied throne guarded by a Naturalborn of the Void; contains the Favor of Noklateo, the Shrouded City

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The chair-crypt was a symbol of the Nox and appears behind crossed staves in the spell sigil Night Sorceries.
  - The same symbol is also used for Claymen Sorceries despite them being the priests of the Ancient Dynasty.
- Nameless Eternal City lacks a chair-crypt.
  - The Prince of Death's Throne is located in the Nameless Eternal City close to the roots of the Erdtree.
- The unoccupied chair-crypts are smaller, implying that they were made with smaller beings in mind.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.text: The **Cerulean Coast** is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Cerulean Coast is located on the Southern Shore of the Realm of Shadow. It is connected to Charo's Hidden Grave, Foot of the Jagged Peak, Gravesite Plain, and the Stone Coffin Fissure. The area is revealed on the Shadow Realm map when Map: Southern Shore has been collected.

The Cerulean Coast is accessible via the  Pillar Path Cross south of Castle Ensis. Adventurers can traverse this region by heading north to cliffs, descending via rock formations, and proceeding south through Ellac River Cave. Glowing blue flowers and massive stone arks signify the Cerulean Coast.

The northeast Cerulean Coast contains the Finger Ruins of Rhia, and the Southern Nameless Mausoleum lies on an island to the west. A rocky southern peninsula hides a deep tunnel leading to the Stone Coffin Fissure legacy dungeon, which remains locked by a Miquella's Haligtree seal until Miquella discards his Great Rune. This story event is triggered by entering the Shadow Keep or crossing the bridge east of Bonny Village.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A somber field of ephemeral blue lilies blooms among beached coffin-ships from beyond the Lands Between. These stone vesels house the Congealed Putrescence of ancient, tainted life, once purified in ghostflame by the deathbirds long ago. The blue flowers are contrasted by a sea of luminous crimson lilies on the plateau above, said to be the home of the Tibia Mariners and the hidden grave of Charo. Deep underground, below both fields, wilts St. Trina's Garden of Deep Purple.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Church of the Bud** is a Site of Grace in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Church of the Bud is a sacred site of unclear purpose constructed by the Hornsent within the western half of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The church features distinctive spiral pillars topped with decorative buds. The Scarlet Buds found here were originally a different color, untainted by the scarlet rot. Behind the church, a stone platform supports the Sealing Tree that veils Enir-Ilim in shadow. This tree can only be burned with Messmer's Kindling.

The church was the only building in Rauh to be razed by Messmer's army during the crusade. Romina sat on the ground in shock, clutching the bud, as the church burned around her. In her despair, she uncovered a divine essence within the ashes and weaved it into the scarlet rot. Her actions imbued the church's flowers with scarlet rot, caused local Spider Scorpions to grow in size, and transformed the landscape surrounding the Church of the Bud into a scarlet rot swamp. After the Battle of Aeonia, Romina summoned and soothed Malenia's unwanted butterflies. Now, she uses her Poleblade of the Bud to perform a long-forgotten purification ritual.

The Site of Grace is unlocked after Romina, Saint of the Bud is defeated.

sections.text: **Castle Ensis** is a legacy dungeon in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Castle Ensis is a medium-sized fortification within the Realm of Shadow, connecting the Gravesite Plain to the Scadu Altus. Located north-northeast of the  Three Paths Cross Site of Grace, the castle lies east of Belurat, Tower Settlement, across the Ellac Greatbridge. Castle Ensis is adjacent to the Fog Rift Fort and the Fifth Belfry.

Castle Ensis is the stronghold of Rellana, a princess of the Carian Royal Family. Rellana and her oathsworn followed Messmer the Impaler on his crusade against the hornsent. As a result, the castle is populated by the enchanted knights of Caria, Lazuli Sorcerers and many Messmer Soldiers.

sections.text: The **Cocoon of the Empyrean** is a Site of Grace in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: It is found in the boss arena of Mohg, Lord of Blood atop the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum. It is revealed after Mohg is slain, and the Tarnished, Needle Knight Leda, and Miquella's Followers touch Miquella's withered arm to enter the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Cocoon of the Empyrean rests within an enormous pelvic girdle and contains the Empyrean body of Miquella.
After the Battle of Aeonia long ago, Miquella placed a powerful charm on the Demigod Mohg. cut Miquella from the roots of the Haligtree and stole him from the city of Elphael. Mohg carried him across the Consecrated Snowfield and brought him to his Mohgwyn Palace in the ruins of the Ancient Dynasty. Mohg has been sharing his accursed blood with Miquella in an attempt to ascend the dormant Empyrean into godhood and take his side as the next Elden Lord.

Sir Ansbach, commander of the Pureblood Knights, challenged Miquella in an attempt to dispel the charm cast on Mohg. Although he managed to wound the fearsome Empyrean, he, too, fell under his spell.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **colossal dragon** is an object in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The colossal dragon's immense body lies at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion near the Foot of the Jagged Peak. It was killed long ago by a corroded metal rod that pierced the back of its skull. Its heart was presumably devoured in Dragon Communion as retribution for the actions of Bayle the Dread.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Unlike modern drakes, the colossal dragon has featherless, leathery wings.
- Dragon Communion Harpoons are embedded in the dragon's wings.
- The  rod that killed the colossal dragon is covered in , implying it was delivered with lightning.
- The nearby Dragon Communion Priestess implies Dragonlord Placidusax felled the colossal drake and devoured its dragon heart. However, the Dragonlord does not utilize metal rods in combat against the player.
- The dragon does not show signs of decomposition.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The aged claymen assumed crude human forms to serve the Ancient Dynasty, a civilization that flourished underground the Lands Between long before the age of the Erdtree. Hunched and sluggish muddy men with stalactite beards, they sharpened glowing meteoric ore and bound it with rope to form makeshift harpoons, daggers, and bolas. They were employed as priests to pursue revelations through magical bubble sorceries requiring both intelligence and arcane.

After their civilization fell to ruin, they began an endless search for long-lost oracles within their bubbles.
By the end of the Shattering, the claymen were largely all that remained of the lost civilization, still infesting its underground ruins in large numbers.

  - The ancient dynasty is connected to the stone coffins on the Cerulean Coast, which contained Putrescent Knight.
  - Claymen Sorcery and putrescence-based Death Sorceries require Arcane.
  - Claymen and Night Sorcery share the Chair-Crypt spell sigil.
    - Despite the fact that the Claymen served the Ancient Dynasty this might imply a collaboration between the two cultures in their creation.
  - The Eternal Cities later created Silver Mimic Tears.
- Clayman Ashes summons the spirits of two Claymen with Harpoons.
- The oracles presumably search for Oracle Envoys, bubble magic-users whose appearance heralds a new age. Their golden bubbles deal  Holy damage.

sections.text: **Bonny Village** is a location within the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Bonny Village is located in eastern Scadu Altus, accessible through the fissure in the Moorth Ruins. Entry into the village requires descending into the pit, landing on a slanted structure, and navigating through a collapsed building and tunnel. A ladder leads up to a well that emerges near the  Bonny Village Site of Grace.

A shallow ravine divides the village, with the remains of a collapsed bridge at its center. The eastern and western halves are densely packed with greatjars and numerous hanging pots. The hornsent inhabitants conducted rebirth rituals, sealing shamans and other undesirables into jars.

North of the village, on the western side, a headless statue stands before a dead tree in a clearing. The O Mother gesture can be found at its feet. Nearby, the shed skin of a large serpent is present, resembling the snake at the  Temple of Eiglay. A bridge to the south leads to the Bonny Gaol, where the potentates stored their Jar Innards. To the east, another bridge leads to the Whipping Hut, with a road extending northward toward the Cathedral of Manus Metyr and the Shadow Keep, Church District.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Butterflies** are a concept in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Butterflies were thin-feathered insects known for their large, often brightly colored wings and fluttering flight. An aspect of the primordial Crucible, they held divine significance for the denizens of the Lands Between, and were used in purification rituals at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh in antiquity.

Each connected to a Demigod child of Queen Marika and Radagon, four strains of sacred butterfly appeared during the age of the Erdtree: Black Pyrefly (Messmer), Smoldering Butterfly (Melina), Nascent Butterfly (St. Trina and Miquella), and Aeonian Butterfly (Malenia).

When Malenia unleashed the scarlet rot at the Battle of Aeonia, scarlet butterflies emerged and became her wings, granting immense strength. Despite this, she later rejected them, just as she did the Servants of Rot. Only upon her transformation into Malenia, Goddess of Rot—when the Scarlet Aeonia blooms a second time—do butterflies return as her wings. The forsaken scarlet butterflies were left to roam the Swamp of Aeonia or were taken in by Romina, Saint of the Bud, who summoned scarlet rot after Messmer's crusade reached the Church of the Bud. Like the Kindred of Rot, these butterflies turned bright pink when they were embraced by Romina.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The butterfly aspect may have first appeared on the Giants.
- The Fine Feather Crucible Talisman boosts backstepping.
- Nascent Butterflies boost Status Resistances, and cure Ailments in Elden Ring Nightreign.
- Smoldering Butterflies boost Attack Power and  Fire Attack Power in *Elden Ring Nightreign*.
- Romina, Saint of the Bud, has grown her own set of insect wings; the scarlet butterflies do not serve as her wings.
- Similar to Aeonian butterflies, the Servants of Death collectively form the wings of Death Rite Birds.

sections.text: **Candletrees**, also known as **candle-trees**, are objects in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Candletrees are leafless, incorporeal saplings with wick-like branches that resemble candelabras. They emit a white glow, and orange flames silently flicker from four of their nine ghostly candles.

These trees appear regardless of time of day in specific locations around the Lands Between. Activating one summons a golden Wandering Noble spirit to slowly lead the Tarnished to an unexplored point of interest. As it walks, the phantom leaves behind a trail of golden footprints.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Candletrees guided the spirits of the Lands Between, and the candlestands at Elphael were made in their image. The candle-tree design was banned during the age of the Erdtree due to perceived similarities to the prophesied cardinal sin. However, it was later adopted by Miquella the Kind for use in Haligtree Town.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Candletrees do not disappear once the associated points of interest are cleared; however, the trees may no longer be activated.
- Physical candlestands identical to Candletrees light up Haligtree Town and Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. They are often placed near silk cocoons and statues of a shrouded figure brandishing a great needle.
- The Candletree Wooden Shield, Silver-Pickled Fowl Foot, Nascent Butterfly, and Black Hood are looted from a pair of treasure chests in Sage's Cave, guarded by Skeletal Bandits. The boss Necromancer Garris associates the area, and the Candletree, with the ancient Death culture.
- This tree might be related to or synonymous with the Helphen, the guiding lampwood of the spirit world.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Cardinal Sin** is an event in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Burning the Erdtree is the first cardinal sin. The War Against the Giants was fought by Elden Lord Godfrey to prevent the Giants' Flame from burning the Erdtree. Despite her efforts, Queen Marika was unable to destroy the Fell God's Flame, so she sealed it away and appointed the Fire Monks to guard it. This marked the beginning of her Age of the Erdtree.

Despite its suppression, the Flame lurked within her Golden Order. Many prophets glimpsed a sinister, recurring prophecy: The kindling would one day ignite the Erdtree and end the Order. They were branded heretics and banished to the fringes of society. In secret, Marika gave purpose to her daughter Melina, that she would be the kindling maiden who would awaken and use the flame of ruin to burn the Erdtree. The Two Fingers, and, according to them, the Greater Will, forbid the cardinal sin.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text:
When Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, the entrance to the Erdtree was sealed by its impenetrable thorns.  The player Tarnished commits the first cardinal sin by sacrificing a kindling maiden or using the Frenzied Flame to awaken the Giants' Flame at the Forge of the Giants. They are then transported to Crumbling Farum Azula to unbind the Rune of Death. Once they do so, Flame engulfs the tree and burns away the obstructive thorns.

Burning the Erdtree coats it in crimson flames. Tiny red embers fall in all overworld areas of the Lands Between, including Crumbling Farum Azula. The Roundtable Hold is tied to the Erdtree's Grace, and burns alongside the Erdtree. Smithing Master Hewg and Finger Reader Enia are both affected by the burning of the Roundtable.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Burning the Erdtree for the first time will unlock the "Erdtree Aflame" achievement.
- The Scadutree has two intertwining trunks. The Sealing Tree that obscures Enir-Ilim resembles one of those trunks. Like the golden Erdtree, it must be burned with a special flame: Messmer's Kindling.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Carian Knights**, also known as the **enchanted knights**, are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Carian Knights were loyal vassals to the Carian royal family and the moon. They styled themselves in silver armor with lapis-lazuli capes, and served as retainers to the lunar princesses. Though they were only twenty strong, they were highly skilled in fighting and Carian sorceries, making them terrifying opponents. They held off Radagon and the Golden Order's warriors in the two Liurnian Wars, which culminated in the marriage of Rennala and Radagon.

A group of Carian Knights led by Lunar Princess Rellana joined Messmer the Impaler on his crusade against the hornsent in the Realm of Shadow.

Following the departure of Radagon, Queen Rennala fell into a deep depression. The Academy of Raya Lucaria betrayed the Carians and locked their Queen in the Raya Lucaria Grand Library. Their counterparts, the Cuckoo Knights, sided with the academy and later attacked Caria Manor. They succeeded in trapping Bols, Carian Knight in the Cuckoo's Evergaol and destroying the Kingsrealm Ruins, but were unable to claim Caria Manor.

sections.text: **Chalices**, also known as **Vessels**, are Items in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Chalices are vessels used at the Relic Rites station to equip three Relics. Their slots are color-coded and only accept Relics of the same color. However, white-colored slots accept any color Relic. Additional Chalices are unlocked by completing Remembrance Quests or purchased from the Small Jar Bazaar.

The vessel slots are color-coded by their  Characteristic:
- slots equip red Relics, such as Burning Scenes.
- slots equip green Relics, such as Tranquil Scenes.
- slots equip blue Relics, such as Drizzly Scenes.
- slots equip yellow Relics, such as Luminous Scenes.
- White slots equip any standard Relic.

Slots 1, 2, and 3 accept standard Relics. Slots 4, 5, and 6 accept Depths Relics and only activate during the Deep of Night.

- Grails only accept Relics of a single characteristic and can be simultaneously assigned to multiple Nightfarers.
- Depths Relic slots unlock after completing the Deep of Night Expedition for the first time. Relics assigned to these slots do not provide their bonuses during other Expeditions.
- Sealed Urns use the same relic color combination as normal urns but with a different slot order, allowing players to adjust which effect takes priority without changing their overall build.

Giant Tree Grail, matching the format of the Sacred Erdtree Grail's Japanese name, 黄金樹の聖杯 (*Ougonju no Seihai*).
  - It is likely that 霊樹 (*Reiju*) refers to the spectral tree which enwraps the Spirit Shelter, and possibly that 巨人樹 (*Kyojinju*) refers to the shadowy giants with tree-like bodies that can be seen from the second Noontide; the Giant's Cradles all-blue slot configuration may reference the glowing blue branches seen within the bodies of these creatures.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Collector Signboard** is an object in Elden Ring Nightreign,

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Collector Signboard is a small shrine featuring a round wooden disk carved with a scarab beetle brandishing its prized ring. As scarabs near death, they abandon their rolled treasures and return to their home nest. The Nightfarers receive these treasures from the Collector Signboard. A catalogued inventory is pinned to the disk above a shallow offering bowl.

The Collector Signboard functions as a merchant, trading Relics, Chalices, and Garb for Sovereign Sigils. It also provides services such as selecting a specific Shifting Earth event or altering the appearance of the Great Site of Grace at the Roundtable Hold. Sovereign Sigils are earned by completing Everdark Sovereign Expeditions.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Collector Signboard is located outside the Roundtable Hold, along its western exterior wall. Exit the building through the south entrance, then turn right and proceed north, turning right again. It is tucked behind a corner, adjacent to a stone balcony with an inoperable door.

sections.heading: Options
sections.text:
- **View Catalog**
  - Browse and purchase a selection of Relics, Chalices, and Garb with Sovereign Sigils
- **Give Cracked Witch's Brooch**
  - Replaces the Cracked Witch's Brooch with the Witch's Brooch in exchange for **3** Sovereign Sigils
- **Conjure a shift in the earth**

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Briars of Sin**, also known as the **thorns of sin** and the **thorns of punishment**, are supernatural vines in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Briars of Sin are creeping, thorned vines that draw blood by impaling sinners from below or by squeezing them in their tight embrace. They could even enter the body, dismembering their victims in the process. Thorny, stake-like trees grew from the corpses of Fire Giants killed by the Briars.

By offering their own blood in sacrifice, practioners of thorn sorcery can manifest the Briars as crimson bloodthorns.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Briars of Sin punishing criminals and sinners in the Lands Between by crushing their eyes, permanently branding them as the Guilty. These crimson thorns inflicted Blood Loss and shared ancient ties with the Giants' Flame and blood star. During the War Against the Giants, Queen Marika's forces used the briars to impale and destroy the Fire Giants, swiftly ending the conflict with the fell god at the dawn of the age of the Erdtree.

Those who survived the briars were exiled from the Altus Plateau. A group of Guilty maidens dwelled in eternal darkness before beholding the heretical blood star, which revealed the aberrant secrets of Faith-based thorn sorcery. They produced bloodthorns by impaling sacrifices with smoldering, withered saplings, turning blood into red glintstone. They revered a maiden whose eyes were crushed by Briars of Sin before her rebirth in the Lands Between, and integrated with the Fire Monks, whose Prelates cracked crimson Thorned Whips to incite religious fervor. Horned Sanguine Albinaurics produce bloodthorns during their cartwheels.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.text:
- Blackflame Sorcerers (formerly)
- Elemer of the Briar (Bell-Bearing Hunter)
- Fire Monks
- Fire Prelate
- Guilty (Thorn Sorcerers)
- Mad Tongue Alberich

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Only visual and contextual evidence supports their role in the War Against the Giants. It is unclear who wielded the briars, though the Trolls' betrayal was a noted turning point in the war.
- The "thorn trees" seen impaling Fire Giants also appear near Fire Monk camps and Guardians' Garrison.
- Every Fire Giant slain by the Briars of Sin has white hair, as if drained of their iconic flame-red color. It is unclear whether this change was directly caused by the thorns or if their hair is drained of its color upon their deaths.
- The Briars of Sin may be linked to the Impenetrable Thorns of the Erdtree and Scadutree, as well as the mottling thorns afflicting Exile Soldiers and the ruins of Stormveil Castle.
  - Both Guilty and Exiled Soldiers drop Smoldering Butterflies, which are associated with Melina and the flame of ruin.
- Elemer of the Briar, also known as the Bell-Bearing Hunter, hailed from Eochaid, an ancient realm of the Lands Between.
- Criminals marked for death by the Erdtree were bound in iron briars, while those accused of lesser crimes wore wreathes of sharpened branches.
- Although Maliketh, the Black Blade sinned in the past and has gouged-out eyes, it is unclear whether the briars blinded him.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The maiden represented on the Shield of the Guilty was explicitly a goddess in ; however, the item did not mention the Briars of Sin at the time. Her identity is unknown, though she may be Melina, the Gloam-Eyed Queen, the Fell God, or someone else. She is unlikely to be Queen Marika because "maiden" specifically refers to an unmarried young woman, and Godfrey was Marika's Lord by the time of her decree at the First Church of Marika.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Chair-Crypt Mummies**, also known in the community as **Nox Giants** or **Nox Gods** are deceased characters in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text: They have long been dead, but their giant mummified corpses can still be found still sitting in the Chair-Crypts of the Night's Sacred Ground in Nokron, Eternal City, Nokstella, Eternal City, and Noklateo, the Shrouded City. Under their corpses Great Ghost Glovewort were placed, to give comfort to their heroic spirits and as tribute for dying glorious deaths, as ancient custom.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The chair-crypt mummies are not referenced in any item description or dialogue, leaving their nature and origins open to interpretation.
- The symbol depicted on their robes is the same used by the Nox on the capes of their Night Maidens and Swordstresses
- These bodies are of similar size and proportions to the Rauh giant mummy at Specimen Storehouse and Giant Skeleton enemies, possibly making these bodies contemporaries/descendants of the giants inhabiting the ancient civilization of Rauh.
  - Both Nox descendants and Marika's tribe, the Shamans, are Numen, hinting at a common ancestry.
  - Their fresh robes and mummified bodies are reminiscent of the shugendō practice of sokushinbutsu, wherein the mummified bodies of shugendō practitioners are enshrined and regularly given fresh robes.
    - This same practice is found in the Tutelary Deities and Curseblades of Hornsent society, the latter being explicitly referred to as shugendō practitioners in the Japanese script. Notably, Hornsent society is heavily focused on the study of Rauh, which could indicate a shared origin between the Crypt-Chairs and Tutelary Deities in the customs of the ancient civilization.

sections.text:
The Church of the Cuckoo is a small prayer room with pews and birdcages at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. The Knights of the Cuckoo and scholars venerated the Cuckoo within this nave.

A single Glintstone Sorcerer stands near the altar at the far end of the church, and two pairs of Marionette Soldiers drop from the ceiling to ambush players. A corpse propped up against the altar can be looted for a [[Golden Rune 2|Golden Rune [2]]], while another on the floor behind it grants a [[Somber Smithing Stone 3|Somber Smithing Stone [3]]].

An Illusory Wall in this area can be dispelled by striking it, revealing an adjoined burial chamber. It is the first panel along the right wall in the back of the room. The hidden side room contains scholarly stone coffins. Loot the corpse here for a Rune Arc.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Demi-Human Chiefs** are a duo boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Demi-Humans are typically small in stature and bestial in appearance, often possessing fur, canine faces, and pointed ears. Although they are intelligent and capable of speech, as exemplified by Boc the Seamster, they are typically violent and brutish, particularly at night when their blood boils and they turn feral.

Demi-Humans wield a variety of weapons, such as falchions, daggers, and clubs. Those considered to be the toughest wield spiked clubs, which they believe to be a badge of honor.

Demi-Human society appears to be hierarchical, with the lesser Demi-Humans following much larger Demi-Human Chiefs. Demi-Humans lose hope if their leader dies, causing them to panic and stop attacking. At the top of the Demi-Human hierarchy are the Queens, who are capable of wielding rudimentary sorceries via their staves.

Despite their violent demeanour, Demi-Humans are capable of fostering diplomatic relations with humans, with Kenneth Haight building an alliance with a group of Demi-Humans in Fort Haight.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text: Larger, more bestial Demi-Humans that serve as leaders of their smaller brethren. Fierce Demi-Human walk on all four legs, and carry bloodstained daggers in each of their front paws.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Two demi-human chiefs encountered in a large cavern within the Coastal Cave They appear to be the leaders of their accompanying pack of regular demi-humans. Boc the Demi-Human was exiled from their tribe. They kept possession of his mother's sewing tools.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Any nearby demi-humans will become demoralized and stop fighting after these bosses die.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Cure Poison** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Cure Poison is sold for  800 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: The caster bows in prayer, cleasing themselves of Poison and its buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  7 FP per cast.
- Costs  10 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- The caster can walk slowly while casting this incantation.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- This spell is niche but useful against most Miranda Blossoms or in poison-filled areas like the swamps near Castle Morne, Village of the Albinaurics, and The Shaded Castle.
  - Given its limited use, it is best to equip this incantation only when needed for these areas.
- This spell is a reusable alternative to Neutralizing Boluses.
- Very helpful when using Fetid Pots to cleanse self-inflicted Poison buildup.
- Only the Prophet, Confessor, and Wretch starting origins can use this incantation with their base attributes. However, the Two Fingers Heirloom allows the other origins to meet the low Faith requirement.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Flame, Cleanse Me – An upgraded version that also removes Scarlet Rot and fully applied Frostbite.
- Lord's Aid – A broader version that also affects nearby allies and removes Blood Loss and Sleep.
- Neutralizing Boluses – A consumable alternative to this incantation.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Dragonfire** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Creates a dragon head before breathing out a wave of flames, dealing Fire damage equal to 144% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e., 432% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast, with an additional 40 points required upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Agheel's Flame.
- Compared to Agheel's Flame, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 30% less FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 104 FP: 2*28 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 53 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains, as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the second strongest "default" dragon breath attack, dealing 9% less damage than Glintstone Breath if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation are equal.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 decreased the power of the following incantations in PvP.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Agheel's Flame, a stronger but more expensive version of this spell.
- Aspects of the Crucible: Breath, a weaker, smaller, but more mobile version of this spell.
- Dragonice, a weaker Magic damage version of this spell that also inflicts Frostbite.
- Ghostflame Breath
- Glintstone Breath, a slightly stronger Magic damage version of this spell.
- Rotten Breath, a weaker Standard damage version of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot.
