sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Crucible Knight** is a non-respawnable enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Crucible Knights served Godfrey, the First Elden Lord. They were led by Crucible Knight Ordovis and Crucible Knight Siluria, two honored as the foremost amongst the Crucible Knights. Their armor holds the power of the crucible of life. In time, their strength, even their appearance, was seen as chaotic and deserving of scorn.

Crucible Axe Knight=

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Crucible Knights led by Ordovis. Their armor adorned with the axe ornamentation that is his mark. They wield a greatsword modeled after the Ordovis's Greatsword and carry a Crucible Hornshield in their off-hand. When facing a tough foe, they are capable of interweaving their attacks with Aspects of the Crucible: Breath and Aspects of the Crucible: Tail incantations.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
The following moves are unique to the Crucible Axe Knight in Farum Azula and Siofra River (the one encountered by entering the portal at The Four Belfries). It is also used by Tanith's Knight.

The following move is unique to Tanith's Knight and Crucible Knight Ordovis.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Crucible Knights led by Siluria. Their armor adorned with the great tree ornamentation that is her mark. They wield a greatspear modeled after Siluria's Tree, which itself is modeled after the crucible of the primordial form of the Erdtree.. When facing a tough foe, they are capable of interweaving their attacks with Aspects of the Crucible: Horns.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Crucible Knight immured in an Evergaol for unknown reasons.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Joins the Leonine Misbegotten when it reaches half-health. Disappears alongside the Leonine Misbegotten once the Radahn Festival begins, but will re-appear after its conclusion.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Allied with the Volcano Manor, they silently stand by Tanith as her guardian. See her questline for more details on how to trigger the invasion.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Spirit-Caller Snail at the Road's End Catacombs summons the spirits of two Crucible Knights.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Although not technically a boss, Devonia is a unique NPC enemy that appears in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. She uses a unique Greathammer and it is said that she is looking for the origins of the Crucible itself.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Two can be found in Stormhill.
- Three can be found along the Siofra River.
- Two can be found in Liurnia.
- One can be found in Caelid.
- One can be found on Mt. Gelmir.
- Four can be found on the Altus Plateau.
- Two can be found in Crumbling Farum Azula.
- One can be found in the Deeproot Depths.
- Crucible Knight Devonia can be found at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
- Executor is a playable character in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- According to the Closed Network Test description for Ordovis's Greatsword, there were 16 Crucible Knights of Godfrey. Though the description has been changed, this is still the case for the final version of the base game. However, additional Crucible Knights were introduced in Shadow of the Erdtree and Elden Ring Nightreign.
- The Crucible Knights are meant to be a relic of the prehistoric era of the Crucible, which came long before the Age of the Erdtree, and their names are a deliberate reminder of their ancient origins. The names of the Crucible Knights all find their roots in the naming conventions of Earth’s prehistoric periods, specifically during the Paleozoic Era:
  - Ordovis is named after the Ordovician, which lasted from 485.4 million years ago to 443.8 million years ago.
  - Siluria is named after the Silurian, which followed the conclusion of the Ordovician and lasted until 419.2 million years ago.
  - Devonia is named after the Devonian period, which was about 419.2 million to 358.9 million years ago
  - This is not a trait wholly unique to the Crucible Knights: Bloodhound Knight Floh and Bloodhound Knight Darriwil seem to be named after the Floian period and the Darriwilian period, respectively, both of which are stages of the Ordovician period. Unlike the Crucible Knights, there doesn't seem to be any particular reason why they are named after these periods.
- The Crucible Knight with the spear was named **Crucible Knight (Great Spear)** in .

sections.text: The **Crystal Knife** is a Dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found in a chest inside the Raya Lucaria Crystal Tunnel located in Liurnia of the Lakes. After taking the first elevator after the Site of Grace down and walking across a wooden beam it is inside the second room on the right, guarded by two distracted Marionette Soldiers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed.
- The scaling favors an equal split between Strength and Intelligence, with the higher Physical base damage making the Strength-scaling more equivalent to the technically higher Intelligence-scaling.
  - Surprisingly only 20 points/5% of total Attack Power behind when focused purely on Strength or Intelligence, or hybridizing Strength/Intelligence, Strength/Dexterity, or Dexterity/Intelligence.
- Decent raw damage but the unusual, for a dagger anyway, lack of a critical multiplier means it ends up being outclassed by all of the other daggers, especially the Dagger and the Miséricorde, for the purpose of critical hits.
- Pairs well with a Magic or Cold affinity Bloodstained Dagger due to its also scaling well with Strength.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Despite the description mentioning that this weapon is used to remove to remove glintstones, it's never seen being used that way.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Dagger** is a Dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- 1 sold by the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold for 400 Runes
- 4% drop chance from dagger-wielding enemies (Highwaymen, Godrick Foot Soldiers, Raya Lucaria Foot Soldiers, Radahn Foot Soldiers, Leyndell Foot Soldiers, Haligtree Foot Soldiers, and Messmer Foot Soldiers).
  - A good early farming spot is all the Highwaymen at the beginning of Murkwater Cave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Together with the Rapier this weapon has the second strongest critical multiplier at 130 (the Miséricorde has the highest, at 140).
- Has low enough requirements to be used with any starting class's default attributes and is fairly common, making it a decent secondary weapon for backstabbing and other critical hits, especially for those who don't have the stats to wield the Miséricorde.
- Generally Dexterity-leaning on its affinities and performs best on a Keen affinity (having scaling just short of S-tier scaling) but also works surprisingly well with the Occult affinity, even if it lacks any of the innate Status Effects required to truly take advantage of this.
  - Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- The shortest of all daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.text: **Crucible Knight Ordovis** is an optional duo boss in Elden Ring. He is encountered alongside another Crucible Knight at Auriza Hero's Grave.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Ordovis was a leader of the Crucible Knights who served Lord Godfrey. He was one of the order's two most-renowned knights, and his men bore the mark of the axe.

Like his men, Ordovis was possessed of the strength to channel the ancient powers of the Crucible. His greatsword was forged with primordial gold, and is imbued with its holy life energies. As the Erdtree flourished and its origins became a distant memory, the Crucible Knights were viewed with scorn.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Crystalians** are Enemies and Bosses in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Crystalians are humanoid beings with inorganic, crystalline bodies. Chiseled from pure blue glintstone, they wear red capes and wield crystal weaponry.

In combat, Crystalians are initially highly resistant to attacks; however, breaking their stance will lower their defense, rendering them significantly more susceptible to all forms of attack, and prevent most weapons from bouncing of them. Keep in mind that backstabs are still available even if the Crystalians are armored so dashing in for a Critical Attack with a Strike weapon is very useful to make sure one dies as quickly as possible.

Putrid Crystalians are infected by Scarlet Rot. Although their movesets are identical to the standard variations, they also inflict  Scarlet Rot buildup.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Crystalians cleave close to the ideals of the primeval current and are regarded as guests by the sorcerers. They possess a form of cognition known as the "wisdom of the stone", and bear the sole purpose of safeguarding their crystals until the end. They wield weaponry fashioned from crystal, a deed impossible for a human, and are believed by some to await the return of their creator who will craft them new brethren.

sections.heading: Crystalian (Spear) Description
sections.text: Spear-wielding Crystalians capable of rapid, successive thrusting attacks. Spiritcaller Snails in Miquella's Haligtree may summon these enemies. A putrid version can be found at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Crystalian (Staff) Description
sections.text: Staff-wielding Crystalians capable of using offensive sorceries. Spiritcaller Snails in Miquella's Haligtree may summon these enemies. A putrid version can be found at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Crystalian (Ringblade) Description
sections.text: Crystalians who wield a pair of circular blades; one large and one small. They fight acrobatically, using a variety of spinning attacks. Spiritcaller Snails in Miquella's Haligtree may summon these enemies. A putrid version can be found at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

Since this Crystalian is encountered on its own, jumping heavy attacks may safely break its Stance. Remain wary of the Crystalian's ranged attacks as they can hit at inopportune times.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Decaying Ekzykes**, also known as the **Dragon Communion Revenger**, is an optional Great Enemy boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The dragon Ekzykes harbored deep resentment toward the Drake Warriors who feasted upon Dragon Hearts through Dragon Communion. He brought bale upon these dragon hunters, denying their entry to the Cathedral of Dragon Communion.

In the aftermath of the Battle of Aeonia, most dragons abandoned Caelid to evade the creeping scarlet rot. Ekzykes, however, chose to remain. Driven by his unrelenting vengeance, he ensured the drake warriors could not perform their Communion. Ultimately, Ekzykes succumbed to the rot, leaving behind nothing but his seething hatred and gravel stone heart.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Decaying Ekzykes is a putrid dragon found in southern Caelid, near the Cathedral of Dragon Communion. He patrols a field northwest of the Cathedral, nearest the  Caelid Highway South Site of Grace, guarding the path to the Dragon Communion altar.

- His stomps also produce a small cloud of Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Death Rite Birds** are optional recurring bosses in Elden Ring. They only appear at night and are a more powerful version of the deathbirds.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Death Rite Birds are gigantic decaying birds with incrusted corpses over their body, partially covered in ghostflame and guarded by the spirits of the servants of death inside their wings. All Deathbirds are said to be the offspring of an entity called the twinbird, which is an envoy of an outer god. Their purpose was to tend the ghostflame by raking out the ashen remains of the death from their kiln. Because of this, they were called graveyard fire keepers and used to be widely active before the Erdtree existed, although regarded as malevolent deities by some. Through the ancient act of the rite of Death, priests of old were permitted to come among the deathbirds and become their guardians, an act which serves as an oath sworn to their distant resurrection. Such priests can be seen inside their wings as spirit beings wielding death ritual spears.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text:
The Death Rite Bird often spawns from a giant ball of Ghostflame up in the sky.

It is possible to lock onto either the boss's head or the spine. It takes extra damage when hit in the head, but due to how much it moves, it can disorienting and result in getting dead-angled when blocking, so it's usually safer to lock into the spine or not at all.

While it is possible to fight this boss on horseback, it is not recommended. The safest place to be in melee range is behind its legs, where neither the weapon swings, nor the beak can hit you.

This boss can be staggered when dealt enough damage, giving you a window to land a Critical Attack on its head.

sections.heading: Weaknesses
sections.text: As they count as Those Who Live in Death they are weak to Holy damage and extremely weak to specific anti-undead weapons. Ash of War: Sacred Blade and Holy Water Pots are useful tools to make short work of these enemies, even if the user doesn't have a lot of Faith.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
The first phase is very similar to a normal Deathbird fight, with the difference that its melee attacks deal both physical and ghostflame damage, making shields somewhat less effective although blocking is still preferable to receiving the damage directly.

Death Rite Birds also uses Ghostflame Ignition, the unique ash of war of the Death's Poker.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Dragonlord Placidusax** is a Remembrance Boss in Elden Ring, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Dragonlord Placidusax is a quadrupedal dragon with two wizened heads and a grievously wounded gravel stone body. The scales protecting his head and back are drained of color, while those on his underbelly are vibrant gold. Each of his craggy, horn-strewn faces has yellow eyes, paired crown horns, and a large horn on the snout. They both have long strands of white hair that continue down the full length of their necks. In his prime, Dragonlord Placidusax had five heads, each emerging from the vortex-like swirl at the base of his neck, though now only two remain. He also had two pairs of wings in the past, but has since lost the rear set. His exposed flesh is red and gold.

Placidusax summons Red Lightning and can assume the form of a storming thundercloud. He can fire beams of golden flame from his both mouths.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
In the prehistoric era, eons before the age of the Erdtree, the Lands Between were ruled from Farum Azula by Dragonlord Placidusax, the Elden Lord and many-headed king of the beastmen and undying Ancient Dragons. However, after he lost a head and his god fled, but likely before the meteorite struck his flying royal city, Placidusax retreated to the storm beyond time to dream in eternal anticipation of his god's return. He required his followers to render up their sleep and remain ever-awake, so that he might find solace in slumber. The timeless ancient dragons, to whom the passing of many lifetimes had rendered notions of ambition, hunger, and fierceness of spirit as utterly unfathomable, received his blessings and grace in return.

In time, the drake dragons—paltry, mortal offspring of the ancient dragons—rebelled, and Placidusax was betrayed by one of his own: Bayle the Dread. The old dragons formed a living wall of rock to protect their Dragonlord, but not before Bayle inflicted mutual, dire wounds upon the Dragonlord, claiming two of his heads and fleeing to the Jagged Peak. In retaliation, the Dragonlord marked Bayle and his bloodline for death. He reportedly slew the colossal drake and devoured its Dragon Heart, consummating the first Dragon Communion. He sent his followers to introduce Dragon Communion to mankind, within whom he recognized the mad hunger and fiery drive necessary to destroy Bayle.

Farum Azula became a mausoleum enshrining Placidusax, guarded by his chosen beasts. Despite his severely weakened condition, Placidusax continued to grant blessings to his followers. Several of Placidusax's Gravel Stone scales were disseminated throughout the world. They were used as smithing stones, said to allow for the creation of god-slaying weapons by lightly twisting time.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
Dragonlord Placidusax can be found in the storm beyond time at Crumbling Farum Azula. The nearest site of grace is  Beside the Great Bridge, from which it can be reached by traveling north and down the slope. The player needs to jump down from a broken section of the bridge to reach his mausoleum complex. Once inside, activate the empty beastman to lie down. The storm rewinds time, and the Dragonlord appears.

The arena is a large, circular platform with pillars around its perimeter. These can be destroyed by Placidusax's attacks. The size of the arena gives ample room to avoid his area of effect or dodge his divebomb attacks.

Defeating Dragonlord Placidusax unlocks the  Dragonlord Placidusax site of grace, which appears inside the arena.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text: Placidusax will begin the fight by summoning a storm of red lightning bolts which rain down on the arena for a few seconds. During his first phase, he will primarily use lightning claw attacks if the player is in front, a slam attack with his wings if they are to either side, and a tail sweep if they get behind him. He also has fire breath attacks which cover a large area in front of or around him. He has an area of effect attack which involves summoning a large lightning bolt and thrusting it into the ground, creating a massive explosion after a short delay. When he performs this attack, the music will briefly get quieter and red waves will emanate from where the lightning bolt hits, providing an indicator for the range of the explosion.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: Placidusax now gains the ability to disappear in a cloud of fog. If he floats into the air before doing so, he will reappear in a stationary or moving thundercloud above the arena, before emerging and diving down at the player. He also gains the ability to disappear and reappear in quick succession, unleashing attacks with his lightning claws in between.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating Dragonlord Placidusax for the first time unlocks the "Dragonlord Placidusax" achievement.
- Dragonlord Placidusax is not classified as a Dragon or Ancient Dragon for the purpose of Anti-Dragon effects because he is the origin of Dragon Communion. Unlike Dragon Communion Incantations, Placidusax's Ruin does not scale with Arcane.
- According to the Remembrance of the Dragonlord, Placidusax was an Elden Lord before the era of the Erdtree, making him the earliest known Elden Lord.
- Placidusax's five heads once corresponded with the five-fingers of intelligence granted to beasts in ancient times.
  - One of Placidusax's heads was lost prior to Bayle's betrayal. The Old Lord's Talisman depicts him with four heads and both sets of wings. Four fingers were seen as a sign of good luck.
  - Two of the Dragonlord's lost heads, as well as parts of their respective necks, can be found on the body of Bayle the Dread, still biting into the drake's neck.
- Part of a dragon’s body (an arm, wing, and head) resembling Placidusax can be seen sticking out of a body of rock in Farum Azula prior to reaching his arena. These were the old dragons who protected him as a living wall of rock in the prehistoric era.
- The Dragon Communion Priestess implies Placidusax felled the colossal drake at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion and consumed its heart, but Placidusax does not wield metal rods against the player.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Placidusax's design is most likely modeled after King Ghidora from the *Godzilla* franchise.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Divine Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Guaranteed Drop:** Weeping Peninsula
- Divine Fortification is obtained upon defeating the Teardrop Scarab found atop a fallen ruin near the Tombsward Ruins.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Divine Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Holy damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  20 FP per cast.
- Costs  13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces holy damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *DivineFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
<math>TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {HolyDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {DivineFortification}) )</math>
  - For example, if holy damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
<math>TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
<math>TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%</math>

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as holy damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple holy negation sources.
- Divine Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
- This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Holy damage in the game, particularly when facing enemies like Cleanrot Knights, Erdtree Avatars, Miranda Blossoms, and Oracle Envoys, especially while exploring Miquella's Haligtree.
- Divine Fortification offers the same holy protection as Holyproof Dried Liver (35%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
  - The Holyproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.
  - Holyproof Pickled Liver

sections.heading: Overview

Crabs are commonly found around the coastlines, rivers, and lakes of the Lands Between. They vary in size, with the larger varieties being far more aggressive.

Baby Crab=

sections.heading: Variant Description

A common variety of crab. They do not typically pose a threat. A maggot-ridden variation can be found in the Black Knife Catacombs. sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
POWER (uncharged): 13.5% SS per bolt, 6 shots total (81% full barrage)

POWER (charged): 13.5% SS per bolt, up to 23 shots total (310.5% at 48 FP full barrage)

An astoundingly poor spell in PvE, without charging it has a terribly high cost for utterly miserable damage that's barely over half that of a single Glintstone Pebble, and if waiting to charge it this is extremely slow; simply spamming other spells will heavily outdamage it over time. Charging the attack does not increase the damage, it merely extends it for more shots at an additional 2 FP per shot, up to 17 extra bolts total.

The one notable exception would be in Invasion situations, both players and NPC Bloody Fingers. Such highly evasive opponents would find it rather difficult to evade the entire barrage of a fully charged shot.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Creates a 5-meter radius cloud of darkness at the caster's location for 5 seconds. Any enemies that come into contact with it are blinded for 7 seconds, temporarily rendering them non-hostile.

- Useful for setting up Backstabs against powerful non-boss enemies, such as knights, or for escaping large groups of enemies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Death Lightning** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

- Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Sends out Lightning bolts that hit randomly around the caster, inflict 50 Death Blight build-up and hit with Attack Power equal to 513% of Incantation Scaling, and leave behind clouds inflicting 30 of Death Blight build-up every 0.2 seconds for 3 seconds (450 build-up in total from the clouds).

Charging this spell sends out more bolts over a larger area and increases the Attack Power of them to 564% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina. Charging the spell increases the cost to 42 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases this to 9.25 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 9.9%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 26%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- This spell is notoriously unreliable, capable of dealing great damage but hitting only rarely against smaller foes and being fairly inaccurate even against massive bosses.
  - Generally outclassed by Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike, though that spell is acquired a good bit later.
- This spell sometimes fails to do anything when cast under low-level roofs.

sections.heading: Trivia

  - FP cost was decreased from 32 to 28.
- Patch 1.04: Decreased FP cost, Increased the duration of death-accumulating smoke.
  - FP cost was decreased from 46 to 32.

sections.heading: Acquisition

**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants

  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> If Corhyn dies before this incantation appears in his inventory then it will become unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Throws out a ring of light with Holy Attack Power equal to 150% of Incantation Scaling and going through foes, stopping when it reaches its maximum range or hits an object.

The ring begins to return to the caster shortly after arriving at its destination, having the same Attack Power for its attack against all foes it passes through.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
  - Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
- Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%.
- Effectively has Attack Power roughly equal to 300% of Incantation Scaling per cast since it will very often hit the main target on the way back.
- Several rings can be out at the same time, making the spell very spammable.
- Pairs well with the Erdtree Greatshield's skill Golden Retaliation and the Ash of War: Carian Retaliation since the timing of the returning ring is very predictable and will trigger the spell-parry-into-projectile part of those skills.
- Can be cast while riding Torrent, further extending the incantation's usability and ability to be spammed.
- The caster takes a short step forwards each time the spell is cast. While many steep falls prevent a character from stepping over them from movement caused by Skills, Spells, and Weapons, it's still good to be a bit careful.
- Though it goes through all enemies it will not ignore the damage reduction from an enemy that is keeping its guard up if they are guarding in the direction it's flying from.
  - Note that it will still fly through said guarding enemy and will hit their unprotected back when returning unless said enemy turns around in between the two hits.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 reduced FP and stamina consumption, increased the range, speed, and duration of the halo, and increased casting speed.
  - Decreased FP cost from 9 to 3.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost, increased damage, and cast speed.
  - Decreased FP cost from 11 to 9. Attack Power was increased from 114% of Incantation Scaling to 150% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Summons a crackling aura that increases the resistance to all Status Effects by 30 and causes the one-handed light attacks of non-Great or Colossal weapons to be deflected. This also reduces the caster's Lightning Damage Negation by 35% and counts as a Body Buff, and lasts for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Deflects the one-handed regular light attacks of Daggers, Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Straight Swords, Thrusting Swords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Curved Swords, Backhand Blades, Katanas, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Twinblades, Axes, Spears, the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear Shadow of the Erdtree Great Spear, Halberds, Reapers, the Katar and Pata Shadow of the Erdtree Fists, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree.
  - Unarmed attacks are also deflected.
  - One-handed regular light attacks from Staves, Sacred Seals, Torches, and Small Shields are also deflected.
  - Fists besides the Katar and Pata aren't deflected.
  - For Daggers, Thrusting Swords (except the Estoc and Noble's Estoc, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Heavy Thrusting Swords (except the Sword Lance Shadow of the Erdtree, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Twinblades, Axes (except the Iron Cleaver and Celebrant's Cleaver, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Spears, the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear, Reapers, the Katar and Pata, Claws, and Beast Claws, one-handed regular heavy attacks and running light attacks are also deflected.
  - For Katanas, running light attacks are also deflected.
  - For Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, one-handed regular heavy attacks are actually deflected.
  - For Thrusting Swords, running heavy attacks, rolling light attacks, and backstep light attacks are also deflected.
  - For Heavy Thrusting Swords, rolling light attacks and backstep light attacks are also deflected.
- Combines well with the Skill: Raptor of the Mists since that skill will also make the user dodge an attack that would have hit them, thus preventing the damage, while the slight stun of the Dragonbolt Blessing can make it easier to land the attack.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Dragonice** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of frozen mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 135% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 110 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 405% of the same and 330 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 48 points of Stamina to cast, and another 48 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast in midair, unlike Borealis's Mist and Ghostflame Breath.
- Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Borealis's Mist, and Ghostflame Breath), this is the most cost-effective for inflicting Frostbite, but causes less damage than the other two breaths.
  - Compared to Borealis's Mist, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 29% less FP.
  - Compared to Ghostflame Breath, this spell deals 20% less damage but consumes 17% less FP and causes 100% more Frostbite build-up.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 120 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 65 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the second weakest "default" dragon breath attack, dealing 15% less damage than Glintstone Breath and 6% less damage than Dragonfire (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals only 3% more damage than Rotten Breath.
  - However, the Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**D, Hunter of the Dead** is an NPC in *Elden Ring.*

He is also possible to summon as a cooperator in Black Knife Catacombs.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Darian, more commonly known as D, Hunter of the Dead is an undead hunter and an ally of Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Darian has a twin brother by the name of Devin, who was also called D. While Darian and Devin had different minds and bodies, they shared a single soul, and were reviled as cursed beings. The twins found sanctuary in the Golden Order, the only institution to accept them.

Darian befriended the spellblade Rogier, with whom he shared an interest in Those Who Live in Death. The two friends eventually parted ways, each coming to their own conclusion about the undead.

Darian became a proponent of Golden Order fundamentalism and a hunter of Those Who Live in Death, seeking to stamp out defilement and preserve the perfection of the Golden Order. Darian encountered and became an ally of Gurranq, who bid him to weed out Deathroot, a plant which caused the emergence of Those Who Live in Death, so that he might feed it to him.

Following the traces of death, Darian came upon Summonwater Village, where a Tibia Mariner had set up shop. In the outskirts of the village, he encounters a Tarnished champion and warns them to stay away from the village. After the champion defeats the Mariner and weeds out the Deathroot, Darian offers them a deal; to take his place as Gurranq's servant, in exchange for Gurranq sharing with them the strength of beasts.

With other matters to attend to, Darian relocates to Roundtable Hold. After the Tarnished takes him up on his offer, he declares them brothers-in-arms and teaches them the fundamentalist techniques wielded by the hunters of the dead. Another resident of Roundtable Hold and associate of the Tarnished champion is Fia, a deathbed companion and servant of the Prince of Death. Fia gives the Tarnished a dagger, asking them to find its rightful owner. After the Tarnished shows Darian the dagger, he offers to return it to its owner.

Shortly thereafter, Darian is murdered by Fia. The Tarnished champion may retrieve Darian's armor and find his twin. Devin will don the armor, and avenge his brother, finding Fia at the foot of the Prince of Death and murdering her.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave
  - *(Optional)* D can first be encountered close to Saintsbridge in Limgrave. He will warn you about Summonwater Village, which is overrun by Those Who Live in Death, including a Tibia Mariner.
  - *(Optional)* After defeating the Tibia Mariner in Summonwater Village, D will appear appear in the village and offer to introduce you to Gurranq.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - D will appear in Roundtable Hold regardless of whether he was encountered in Limgrave. If you have at least one Deathroot and did not complete step 1, he will offer to introduce you to Gurranq.
  - D will begin selling Incantations after you have met Gurranq. He will also become available as a cooperator in Black Knight Catacombs as well as against the Tibia Mariner in Liurnia of the Lakes.
  - After progressing Fia's questline, the Weathered Dagger can be given to D.
  - After reloading the area, Fia can be found standing over D's corpse in a previously inaccessible room in Roundtable Hold.

The **Dragoncrest Shield Talisman** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

It gives +10% physical damage reduction. This talisman has 4 variants, including Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman, only one of which can be equipped at a time.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Obtained from a corpse that lies on the ground, near Bestial Sanctum, in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Equipping the Longtail Cat Talisman here, or using Soft Cotton is very helpful, as there are several parkour drops coming up that will deal unavoidable damage, and there are Bat enemies in the area. From the front door of the sanctum, head southwest around the side of the sanctum, until reaching a cliff that overlooks a large tree root, close enough to drop to. Drop from here to the branch, to another branch, to a domed rooftop, and then to the first of 3 ring structures, jutting out from the cliffside. Jump up to the ledge surrounding the nearby pillar, walk across the buttress to the next pillar, drop to the lower ledge, jump to another lower ledge on the first pillar, and drop down to the second ring. Jump to the next-lower ledge on the outer pillar, walk across the buttress, and jump to a ledge that sticks out from the wall below. At this point, it is recommended to mount Torrent, as the final jump is extremely difficult to make on foot, while almost trivial to make with Torrent's double-jump ability. The third ring below is just barely beyond the instant-death threshold for falling, so instead, aim for the ledge on that outer pillar, just a few feet above the ring. After finally reaching the third ring, head northeast along it to find the corpse.

sections.text: - Obtained from a corpse in Auriza Hero's Grave in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. Make your way to the area where two chariots ride side-by-side, up and down a slope. At the bottom of this slope is a corpse, hanging off of a ledge above a pit. Drop into the pit from where this corpse lies to land on a beam, and continue dropping down into this pit, until landing on the top of a thin stone archway. Walk to the end of this archway and climb a ladder to reach another ramp, guarded by a single chariot. While it is possible to reach the bottom of this ramp without dying, it is extremely difficult, as it involves either taking a hit from the chariot without dying, or using a movement ability, like Bloodhound Step, along with excellent timing. The far easier thing to do is to proceed up the ramp until reaching a moving, fire-breathing pillar, which can be raised by hitting it. After raising the pillar, die or teleport to return to the ramp with two chariots. The raised pillar will now be shining a chariot-spawning circle of light onto the middle of this ramp, which will cause a chariot to spawn that collides with the others, destroying them all. The door at the bottom of the ramp leading to the corpse can now be safely reached.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Deathbird** is a recurring boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
All Deathbirds are said to be the offspring of an entity called the twinbird, which is an envoy of an outer god of Death. In the time when there was no Erdtree, Death was burned in ghostflame, and the Deathbirds were the keepers of that fire. They were graveyard fire keepers and were said to rake out the ashen remains of the dead from their kiln. From the cinders of the dead burned with ghostflame arose vengeful spirits.  The Deathbirds were regarded as malevolent deities by some. Through the ancient act of the rite of Death, servants of Death were permitted to come among the Deathbirds and become their guardians. This act serves as an oath sworn to their distant resurrection. Such priests can be seen inside the wings of the Death Rite Birds as spirit beings wielding Death ritual spears.

These recurring optional bosses only appear at night, descending from the sky. They are gigantic decaying birds with bodies composed of smaller corpses. They count as Those Who Live in Death despite predating the Deathroot.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text:
- Stance: 120
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to effects that target Those Who Live in Death
- Weak spot: Head

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Deathbirds usually rely on melee attacks, which can be either dodged or blocked, except for their peck and grab attacks. It's recommended to avoid being under its head to avoid getting pecked.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
- Defense: 105

Found at night, northwest of Castle Morne, on top of the cliff. Walk near the Fallen Ruins to make it appear.

There are Tarnished Golden Sunflowers where it spawns that can be used to make Holy Water Pots (recipe from Missionary's Cookbook 1, bought from Merchant Kalé).

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Found at night and spawns when near the fallen ruins that are very close and northeast of the  Scenic Isle grace.

sections.heading: Background

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Deathbirds' red-feathered wings might be associated with the Twinbird's red half.
- Corpses can be seen in its chest.
- As they count as Those Who Live in Death, they are weak to Holy damage and extremely weak to specific anti-undead weapons. Ash of War: Sacred Blade and Holy Water Pots are valuable tools to make short work of these enemies, even if the user doesn't have a lot of Faith.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Crumbling Farum Azula** is a subregion of the Lands Between in Elden Ring. This legacy dungeon is accessible after burning the Erdtree at the Forge of the Giants found on Flame Peak in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Farum Azula is a giant temple in the sky, located above the sea to the east of the Lands Between. Once a royal city of the Ancient Dragons and the seat of the Dragonlord Placidusax, Farum Azula has been crumbling since time immemorial. Now, all that remains is a mausoleum guarded by chosen Beastmen, who wield weapons clad in Red Lightning. The storm beyond time rages in the center of the crumbling city, and at its heart is the Dragonlord's seat, where he awaits the return of his god.

In Farum Azula, many Ancient Dragons can be found buried in the rock, between the catacombs of the Beastmen and the surface of the city, their bodies still filled with gold. It is said that they formed a living wall of rock to protect the Dragonlord long ago.

As well as Beastmen, Farum Azula is still home to a number of Ancient Dragons, who roost on the floating fragments of the city. There is also a population of Wormfaces dwelling in one of the lower levels of the city. It appears that Deathroot has spread throughout parts of the city as well.

Farum Azula is the dwelling place of Maliketh, the Black Blade, the protector of the Rune of Death. It is here that the Tarnished finds themselves after the Erdtree is set aflame, and where they finally unbind the Rune of Death, releasing it upon the Lands Between.

When crafted, 5 are made at a time.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text:
:''Throwing knife chiseled from impure crystal.
Craftable item.''
:*Consumes FP. Throw at enemies to deal magic damage.*
:*Long ago, it is said that a golem crafter employed a similar crystal tool.*

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
A certain number of Crystal Darts will cause golem enemies to "malfunction", stagger, and attack one another (shown by blue sparks around their heads). These enemies include:

- Imps
- Erdtree Burial Watchdogs
  - Especially useful when encountered in a duo or when accompanied by Imps.
- Guardian Golems
  - Note that many Golems can already damage each other, this just means that they may do so by aiming for them rather than by clipping them when aiming for someone else.
- Golem Smiths Shadow of the Erdtree

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Deals Magic damage.
- The FP cost is very low and will most likely not cause complications unless there is only barely enough FP to cast a spell or use an Ash of War several times in a row.
- Causing an enemy to malfunction will most likely not make it turn against it allies immediately, as it only makes them viable targets and The Tarnished (Protagonist) will most likely be the last target to damage them.
- Malfunctioning enemies cannot only attack other enemies, but can also be attacked by other enemies.
  - Malfunctioning enemies will also attack each other.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Deeproot Depths** is an underground region of the Lands Between in Elden Ring. This area of the map is revealed by collecting Map: Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Deeproot Depths is an enormous cavern deep below the Altus Plateau. It is the source of the Ainsel and Siofra Rivers, and the furthest downward the Erdtree roots extend. The network of Greattree roots that spread throughout the Lands Between also begins here.

Below the  Prince of Death's Throne, a nameless Eternal City lies in ruins, with many of its buildings sinking into a mire of milky liquid. In the northwestern area, a Wandering Mausoleum prowls, surrounded by Mausoleum Soldiers and Knights. To the far west, Siluria, one of the two leaders of the Crucible Knights, awaits at the hollowed-out trunk of a dead oak tree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Nameless Eternal City was destroyed by Astel, Naturalborn of the Void long ago.

After Godwyn the Golden was murdered on the Night of Black Knives, his body was buried in the Erdtree's roots. His malformed body, corrupted by Death, can be found to the north of the cavern. It is here that Fia resides after fleeing Roundtable Hold.

This area can be reached by either defeating the Valiant Gargoyle duo boss in Siofra Aqueduct or by finding an illusory wall at the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription, found behind a movable wall guarded by Mohg, the Omen at the bottom of the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.

An abandoned coffin found along the southwestern shore of the shallow body of water allows travel to Ainsel River Main, the northern part of Ainsel River.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Dragon King's Cragblade** is a melee armament found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This weapon's Guard Counters become Thrusting Counterattacks.
- Has a 30% damage boost against Dragons and a 15% damage boost against Ancient Dragons.
  - Since this weapon primarily deals Pierce-type damage, which is most dragons weakness, it is well suited to this anti-dragon role. Be aware that Borealis, the Freezing Fog, is a Pierce-resistant dragon and that all Ancient Dragons resist the secondary Lightning damage.
- The Dexterity-scaling is responsible for increasing both the Physical damage and the Lightning damage.
  - The Physical/Lightning split is roughly 60%/40%.

- Scales best with Dexterity, up to the 80 point softcap.
- The skill is chargeable, benefiting from the Godfrey Icon.
- Has a unique heavy attack, shared with the Bloody Helice. In comparison with the default one, found on the Godskin Stitcher, the regular heavy attack has longer reach, the charge heavy attack is a lunging thrust instead of a short-ranged double thrust, and the feint (done by dodging when charging a heavy attack).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.04 decreased the skill's cost from 35 FP to 28 FP, decreased its recovery time, and decreased the damage of the uncharged version of the skill. Also increased skill cast speed.
- Patch 1.07 increased the directional control of the skill.
- Patch 1.08 reduced the speed of crouching light attacks and the stagger of two-handed jumping heavy attacks, and also the poise damage of all attacks in PvP.

sections.text: **Dragonkin Soldier** is a reoccurring boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Draconic beings born from Gravel Stone in the Eternal City, Dragonkin Soldiers never knew true sky or true lightning, and so they wielded ice lightning as their weapon. They never achieved immortality, and perished as decrepit imitations of true Ancient Dragons.

They have humanoid bodies, with lanky arms and legs, and their chests have large, gaping cavities. They wear minimal armour, and red-and-black capes with golden embroidery.

Spectral Dragonkin Soldiers appear in the Consecrated Snowfield. They will disappear if the player gets too far away, and spawn continuously.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **D, Beholder of Death** is an NPC and co-operator in *Elden Ring.* He can be summoned for the Valiant Gargoyles boss in Nokron.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Devin, more commonly known as "D", is the twin-brother of Darian, who is also known as D. The two twins had separate minds and bodies, but shared a single soul. For this, they were reviled as accursed beings, but found solace in the Golden Order, which accepted them both.

At some point, Devin traveled deep below ground to the roots of the Erdtree, where he met with the Prince of Death. The encounter appears to have nearly shattered Devin's mind, as he came to dwell in the Siofra Aqueduct, barely able to speak.

Later, his brother Darian is murdered by Fia, Deathbed Companion, and his Twinned Set finds its way to Devin. Seemingly acknowledging that Darian had died, but still barely able to speak, Devin gathers himself, and if requested, helps the Tarnished champion clear the way to the Deeproot Depths.

After Fia is given the other half of the Cursemark of Death, allowing her to lay with the Prince of Death in order to produce a Mending Rune, Devin will finally find her, and kill her. The Tarnished champion can find Devin gloating and taunting the Prince of Death, cursing him and the murdered Fia. Having avenged his brother, Devin declares he has no more regrets and prays for the honeyed rays of gold to deliver his spirit, so that he may once again look his brother in the eye.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Nokron, Eternal City
  - Devin can be found outside the Valiant Gargoyles' duo boss arena beyond Hallowhorn Grounds (north). He can be given the full Twinned Set if you obtained it at the end of D, Hunter of the Dead's questline.
    - (Optional) He is available as a summon for the Valiant Gargoyles duo boss after being given the Twinned Set and reloading the area.
  - If D, Beholder of Death, was given a Twinned Set that was obtained by directly killing D, Hunter of the Dead, then he will be hostile the next time the area is loaded. He will drop both the Twinned Set and the Inseparable Sword upon death, immediately ending his questline right there.
1. Deeproot Depths
  - After completing Fia, Deathbed Companion's questline and obtaining the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince, D can be found standing over Fia's slain corpse. After reloading the area, he will be gone, and the Inseparable Sword and Twinned Set can be found nearby.

sections.text: - D, Beholder of Death was named **D, Hunter of the Dead** in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Dragon Communion Seal** is a Sacred Seal in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Dropped by a spectral Banished Knight located in the Fringefolk Hero's Grave in Limgrave. To find it, start at the Stranded Graveyard Site of Grace and head down the first two ramps in the Grave, then head right in the split to go up another two ramps. The Knight is inside a small room at the end of the ramp and is quite tough for the early game. The Chariot in the dungeon can be used to help kill it, though that comes at considerable risk to the player as well.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This Sacred Seal is best used for split Arcane/Faith builds, with an even split being slightly more favorable over one more biased towards Arcane.  It can also be used for a pure Arcane build but that alternative is slightly weaker, by about 7-8%.
  - For comparison: a 45/45 Arc/Fth split gives 336 Scaling at +10, a 60/30 Arc/Fth split gives 333 Scaling at +10, and a 80/10 Arc/Fth split gives 310 Scaling at +10.
- Holding a Dragon Communion Seal (DCS) in one of your active hands will boost the damage of directly damaging Dragon Communion Incantations by 15%.
  - Holding a DCS in each active hand (that is, two Seals that are each held in separate hands) will increase the damage boost to 32.25% (1.15*1.15=1.3225).
  - The damage boost is still granted if the other piece of equipment is two-handed.
  - This bonus stacks with the 20% damage boost granted when reactivating the Rock Heart.
- Any incantation that inflicts Poison (except for Poison Armament), Madness, or non-bloodflame Blood Loss build-up and is cast using this Seal will have their Status Effect scale with the wielder's Arcane stat.
  - This status build-up bonus is equivalent to a fifth of the regular Weapon Scaling bonus from Stat Scaling, meaning that with a +10 DCS's scaling with Arcane being at 2.25 this caps at 45% (0.2*2.25=0.45).
  - Of the Blood Loss-inflicting incantations only Swarm of Flies inflicts any direct Blood Loss-build up (70 build-up out of its total 150 build-up) as direct status build-up instead of as part of a non-scaling bloodflame effect.
  - It would theoretically also scale the amount of Sleep build-up of any incantation that inflicts such a Status Effect. However, no incantation that inflicts that status effect exists.
  - Curiously Scarlet Rot build-up doesn't scale with Arcane, even though the spell type can inflict that status effect.
- The weight being 0 means and the existence of Physical Dragon Communion Incantations such as Dragonmaw and Rotten Breath means this Seal works well with the Blue Dancer Charm weight-based increase to Physical damage.
  - This synergy is further enhanced by the existence of the Rock Heart, essentially a 0 weight armor set that can increase the damage of Dragon Communion Incantations even further.
- This Seal is very unsuitable for casting Weapon Buff or direct healing spells as those depend entirely on the Faith portion of the used Seal's scaling, and this Seal only have about a third of the Faith scaling that pure Faith scaling Seals such as the Finger Seal and Erdtree Seal have.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.04 decreased the scaling of status effect build-up from spells and incantations of Albinauric Staff and Dragon Communion Seal.
  - Previously both of these casting implements full Arcane-scaling would apply to the Status Effects build-up of spells cast with them. For a +10 Dragon Communion Seal, this meant that almost the full S (2.25) would be applied thus resulting in roughly 3 times the Status Effect build-up on builds with high Arcane which would often result in instant or near instant application of Madness with spells such as Frenzied Burst.

sections.text:
<noinclude>
**Daggers** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Daggers generally have very short reach and low damage against both health and poise, but compensates for this with their fast attack speed and sometimes higher than average damage on Critical Attacks, making several of them (particularly the Dagger and especially the Misericorde) powerful tools for Backstabs and Ripostes.

Their fast attack-speed and high number of hits-per-second makes them good at building up Status Effects like Poison and Blood Loss.

As they have low weight, they also make excellent catalysts for certain Ashes of War and Skills, providing a stat-efficient means of casting status buffs like Golden Vow or Shared Order with no need for high investment in certain attributes, while specific daggers such as Reduvia and the Black Knife have exceptionally strong ranged Skills that only they posses (Reduvia Blood Blade and Blade of Death respectively).

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
The moveset for Daggers consists mostly of rapid slashes, with the exception of one- and two-handed rolling and heavy running attacks, two-handed heavy attacks, and dual wield backstep attacks, which are all thrusts.

Some daggers have different standing heavy attacks: Glintstone Kris, Main-gauche, Miséricorde, and Scorpion's Stinger have thrusts, and Black Knife, Blade of Calling, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword have a quick, double-hit slash.

The dual-wield moveset is notably quite quick and both the backstep attack and the jumping attack are excellent due to their reach and speed respectively. The first attack in the dual-wield attack chain is surprisingly slow due to being composed of 3 separate hits, making it somewhat difficult to use since Daggers won't stagger most foes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Discovery** is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Discovery affects their ability to find drops from defeated enemies. Discovery has a base level of 100 for the Tarnished, and Discovery can be raised by 1 for each point of Arcane taken while leveling up. Equipment can also boost Discovery while worn. Additionally, Discovery can be boosted temporarily by using a Silver-Pickled Fowl Foot consumbale item.

An item with a P% drop rate is actually found with probability as follows, if you have Discovery *D*:

<math>\begin{align}
Chance &= \frac{100\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}{1000+ \left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor-10P} \\
&= \frac{100}{1+\frac{1000-10P}{\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}} \\
&= \frac{10}{\frac{1}{10}+\frac{100-P}{\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}} \\
&\approx \frac{100}{1+\frac{10000-100P}{PD}} \\
\end{align}</math>

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Demigods** (デミゴッド, *Demigoddo*) are special beings found in the Lands Between. They are the majority of the primary characters in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Lands Between are ruled by a family of demigods, heroes with an especially powerful blessing received from the blood of Queen Marika the Eternal. They are immortals due to their fated deaths being removed from the Elden Ring when Queen Marika created the Golden Order by sealing the Rune of Death.

During the Night of Black Knives, a fragment of the Rune of Death enabled the murder of Godwyn the Golden. This was the first death of a demigod in all history, and it was after this that the demigods began to fall. At an unknown period, Queen Marika told her demigod children to make of themselves that which they desired, whether it be a Lord, or a God. However, she also declared that if they failed to become anything at all, they would be forsaken, and amount only to a sacrifice.

These events were precursors to the shattering of the Elden Ring, whereupon several of the demigods inherited Great Runes, becoming known as Shardbearers. The mad taint of the strength granted by their Great Runes triggered the Shattering, a war in which the demigods fought for control of the Lands Between. However, no lord arose from the Shattering, and the demigods were abandoned by the Greater Will.

Upon their return to the Lands Between, the Tarnished were impelled by the Two Fingers to seek out the demigods and relieve them of their Great Runes. At least three of the demigods were slain by The Tarnished in their quest to become Elden Lord.

sections.heading: The Golden Lineage
sections.text:
The first Demigods were Godfrey, First Elden Lord and his descendants, known as the Golden Lineage. The confirmed members of the Golden Lineage are Morgott, the Omen King, his twin Mohg, Lord of Blood, Godrick the Grafted, Godefroy the Grafted, and the Grafted Scions. Godwyn the Golden's name, title, and the pattern on his clothing suggests his descendancy from the Golden Lineage.

Godrick the Grafted was only a distant relation, his divine blood linking him to Marika sorely diluted, indicating unseen generations of Golden Lineage demigods. According to Kenneth Haight, Godrick is the last of the Golden Lineage, but the Grafted Scions are also suggested to be the dregs of the Golden Lineage.

When Godfrey was divested of his Grace, he became Tarnished, and lost his demigod status.

sections.heading: Carian Royal Family
sections.text: After Godfrey was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon became King Consort and second Elden Lord by marrying Queen Marika. This led to the children he conceived with Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon becoming demigod stepchildren, including Starscourge Radahn, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and Ranni the Witch.

sections.heading: Messmer and Melina
sections.text:
Messmer and Melina are both children of Marika.
- It is often speculated that the Kindling Maiden Melina may be a demigod, as she is called "DaughterMarika" internally and states her mother is inside the Erdtree. Furthermore, she is bound by Grace, quotes ancient words of Marika, and implied to be the younger sister of Messmer the Impaler. Like Messmer, Melina is associated with a butterfly and is fated to fulfill a purpose.

sections.heading: Twin Prodigies
sections.text: The union of Radagon and Marika led to the birth of at least two more demigods, the twins Miquella of the Haligtree and Malenia, Blade of Miquella, however they suffered afflictions from birth; the former was born with a curse of eternal childhood, and the latter harbored Scarlet Rot within.

sections.heading: Soulless Demigods
sections.text: The Wandering Mausoleums found throughout the Lands Between cradle the corpses of soulless demigods. At least eight demigods became these soulless demigods, and at least one of them is an unwanted child of Queen Marika's. They are guarded by the Mausoleum Knights, who watch over a soulless demigod until their resurrection.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- According to Finger Reader Enia, the demigods are each and all the direct offspring of Queen Marika.
- According to the Overview Trailer, the demigods are "those who have inherited the blood of Queen Marika the Eternal."

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- According to game director Hidetaka Miyazaki, the main demigod bosses of the game were initially written by George R. R. Martin. As part of the creative process, Martin wrote the initial characters as grand heroes, and FromSoftware took them developed the way in which their Great Runes misshaped and distorted them.
- Localisation Notes
  - Rather than "unwanted child", the soulless demigod(s) of the mausoleum is referred to as Queen Marika's "ugly bastard" or "ugly spawn." (醜い落とし子, *Minikui otoshi-ko*.)

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Demi-humans** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Demi-Humans are typically small in stature and bestial in appearance, often possessing fur, canine faces, and pointed ears. Although they are intelligent and capable of speech, as exemplified by Boc the Seamster, they are typically violent and brutish, particularly at night when their blood boils and they turn feral.

Demi-Humans wield a variety of weapons, such as falchions, daggers, and clubs. Those considered to be the toughest wield spiked clubs, which they believe to be a badge of honor.

Demi-Human society appears to be hierarchical, with the lesser Demi-Humans following much larger Demi-Human Chiefs. Demi-Humans lose hope if their leader dies, causing them to panic and stop attacking. At the top of the Demi-Human hierarchy are the Queens, who are capable of wielding rudimentary sorceries via their staves.

Despite their violent demeanour, Demi-Humans are capable of fostering diplomatic relations with humans, with Kenneth Haight building an alliance with a group of Demi-Humans in Fort Haight.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Demi-humans of average build, who wear rags. Demi-humans are bestial in appearance, often characterized by fur, elongated faces, and pointed ears. They exhibit a blend of human and mammalian features, yet all share the common trait of possessing five fingers and toes. While typically shorter than the Tarnished, demi-humans vary greatly in size—some are as small as children while others are of towering stature. Demi-humans wield a variety of weapons, including falchions and clubs; some carry rickety shields. Many demi-humans carry string. As night falls, demi-humans become increasingly feral and aggressive, their eyes glowing a menacing red.

sections.text: **Cuckoo Knight** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Knights of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. They wear red-and-blue armour emblazoned with a peering cuckoo, whose shrewd gaze is thought to represent the knights' refusal to be mere servants of the Academy. In payment for their contract with the Academy, the knights were taught glintstone sorceries such as Scholar's Armament and Scholar's Shield.

When the Academy turned against the Carian Royal Family, the Cuckoos launched an assault on Caria Manor, declaring their enemy to be none other than Caria itself. However, they were caught in an enchanted snare, and the Raya Lucaria Soldiers were turned into spectral puppets.

They are sometimes found riding horses.

sections.text: The **Divine Towers** are recurring landmarks in Elden Ring. There are six to find in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
There are **six** divine towers in the Lands Between, each corresponding with a different shardbearer. A pair of Two Fingers lies dormant atop each tower, except the Divine Tower of Liurnia. Devoid Great Runes can be restored by interacting with these Two Fingers.

The massive towers share structural similarities with ancient ruins and the Forge of the Giants, with certain areas containing glowing meteorite ore. Their origin and purpose remain unknown.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The pedestals at the top of each Divine Tower contain a chunk of meteorite ore encircled by a pattern that resembles the eye of the Fell God.
- A layer of hardened rock coats one side of each tower.
- The original body of Ranni the Witch rests at the top of the Divine Tower of Liurnia.
- A Divine Tower is the brace for the Spirit Shelter in Elden Ring Nightreign. Additional Divine Towers appear in the Great Hollow.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Dexterity** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Dexterity stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Dexterity scaling. Increasing Dexterity will also decreased the Tarnished's casting time with spells as it raises. Fall damage will also be reduced as Dexterity raises past 21 Dexterity.

The Tarnished can level Dexterity by spending Runes at Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Crystal Tears** are Key Items in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
When resting at a Site of Grace, up to two Crystal Tears can be mixed into the Flask of Wondrous Physick to bestow temporary buffs when the physick is consumed. These buffs vary in both effect and duration depending on the Crystal Tears used.

They are acquired by defeating minibosses near Minor Erdtrees (especially Erdtree Avatars), found in stone receptacles across the Lands Between, or dropped by Furnace Golems in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Dragons are the mortal descendants of the Ancient Dragons, who once ruled the Lands Between during a prehistoric era. Unlike their predecessors, their fleshy hides bore no Gravel Stone scales. They possessed fewer limbs and flew on feathered wings. Their snouts were more narrow and terminated in diminutive maxillary beaks.

The dragons were idolized by humans for their sheer strength and sublime beauty. However, the ancient dragons viewed them as lowborn, paltry imitations. While the drakes inherited the fiery breath of their forebears, they could not channel their red lightning. Yet, their vivacious red hearts were covered in sacred gravel stones.

sections.heading: Dragon Communion
Later events

Well before the first astrologers and the Erdtree, ice dragons held dominion over the Mountaintops. Some time later, they were defeated by the Fire Giants, who drove them the Flame Peak.

Many dragons in the current age descend from Elder Dragon Greyoll, a mother drake of colossal size. Following the Battle of Aeonia, Greyoll and her offspring fled the Scarlet Rot by settling on a plateau in the northern reaches of Caelid, later known as Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.

sections.heading: Flying Dragon
sections.text:
; Flying Dragon Description
Dragons who settled in northern Caelid with their mother, Elder Dragon Greyoll.

- There are six red-eyed Flying Dragons surrounding Greyoll. Greyoll will lose 20% of her health with each Dragon killed, meaning that killing five will cause Greyoll to die.

sections.heading: Glintstone Dragon
sections.text:
; Glintstone Dragon Description
Dragons imbued with glintstone roost atop the Moonlight Altar in western Liurnia of the Lakes. They can exhale Glintstone Breath, which inflicts magic damage.

- These Dragons do not respawn when killed.

sections.heading: Flying Dragon Agheel
sections.text:
; Flying Dragon Agheel Overview
Wandering Nobles in the ruins around the lake chant Agheel's name, praying that it will burn them to ash. Flying Dragon Agheel is encountered in Agheel Lake in southern Limgrave, northwest of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins. It appears by flying down from above, torching a congregation of Wandering Nobles with dragonfire.

- Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is available as a summon for this fight, after speaking to him under the ruin south of the lake.

- After taking a critical hit, the target receives an additional 20% standard damage for the remainder of the fight.

- Defeating Flying Dragon Agheel will unlock Agheel's Flame, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

; Moveset

sections.heading: Flying Dragon Greyll
sections.text:
; Flying Dragon Greyll Overview
A Flying Dragon encountered on the Farum Greatbridge (bridge south of Bestial Sanctum), on the northern peninsula of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Greyll is identical to Agheel in both appearance and ability. However, the bridge gives the player much less room to maneuver.

; Moveset

sections.heading: Glintstone Dragon Smarag
sections.text:
; Glintstone Dragon Smarag Overview
A devourer of sorcerers, whose body gradually became corrupted by the glintstones of those he ate. Smarag is encountered near an island west of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and north of the Temple Quarter, guarding a corpse that holds the Academy Glintstone Key. Note that it is **not** necessary to kill this dragon to get the Academy Glintstone Key; it can be retrieved by either sneaking behind it or rushing beyond it before it's fully awakened to get at the corpse.

- Smarag is able to fire Glintstone Cometshards from his mouth, and can also unleash magic breath, akin to the fire breath of other Dragons.

- Defeating Glintstone Dragon Smarag will unlock Smarag's Glintstone Breath, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

; Moveset

sections.heading: Glintstone Dragon Adula
sections.text:
; Glintstone Dragon Adula Overview
A devourer of sorcerers, whose body became corrupted by glintstone. Adula was once bested by Ranni the Witch and subsequently swore a knightly oath to her Dark Moon.

- Adula is first encountered outside Ranni's Rise in the Three Sisters, north of Caria Manor. After a brief fight, it disappears, only to reappear at the Moonlight Altar outside the Cathedral of Manus Celes.

- Adula can use magic breath, much like Smarag. However, it can also utilize Adula's Moonblade, conjuring a magic blade in its maw mid-flight and unleashing a wave that inflicts Frostbite.

; Moveset

sections.heading: Decaying Ekzykes
sections.text:
A Dragon plagued by scarlet rot, encountered north-west of the Cathedral of Dragon Communion. Also known as the **Dragon Communion Revenger**, Ekzykes did not forget his hatred even as he succumbed to the rot.

Instead of flames, Ekzykes breathes toxic clouds that inflict Scarlet Rot, covering a large area and taking a few seconds to dissipate. Its stomps also produce a small cloud of Scarlet Rot.

Defeating Decaying Ekzykes will unlock Ekzykes's Decay, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Borealis the Freezing Fog
sections.text:
One of the ice dragons, who were lords of the Mountaintops before the Fire Giants chased them from the peak. Borealis is encountered on the frozen lake in the northeast of the Mountaintops, emerging from a thick white fog.

Borealis exhales clouds that inflict Frostbite. Its stomps also produce small clouds of Frostbite.

Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Elder Dragon Greyoll
sections.text:
Greyoll is known as the mother of the lesser dragons. She is a massive but stationary dragon encountered in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, just south of Fort Faroth. She is immobile, either having grown too weak to move or as a result of having fused with the surrounding rocks, but can still let loose fearsome roars to weaken her enemies.

- Defeating any of the six lesser dragons surrounding her will cause large amounts of damage to her, and killing them all will kill her.

- Defeating Elder Dragon Greyoll will unlock Greyoll's Roar, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for three Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Deep Siofra Well** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
An ancient structure in a deep ravine in northern Caelid. Inside is a lift which connects Caelid to Siofra River. As the ravine is inaccessible from the rest of Caelid, the only way to access this area is by taking the lift up from beside the Below the River Well Site of Grace in northeastern Siofra River, requiring two Stonesword Keys to activate it.

The ravine branches in two directions from the well. Travelling south will lead to a one-way drop to the Swamp of Aeonia, while the western path leads to the Great Jar and the Caelid Colosseum.

sections.heading: Deep Siofra Well
sections.text: Found just outside the entrance to the well.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.text:
Upon entering the Dragonbarrow location several passive Standing Sentry Stones will be found crowding the path, while Explosive ones dot the lower parts. Just around a corner is a Golem with a magical greatbow guarding the way, with another waiting far behind it to support. Since the second Golem will attack you when near the Great Jar and the first one will you near the second golem, it is best to take care of both before approaching.

Additionally, Gravel Stones dot the ground just before the stone the first Golem is standing on.

For the encounter with the gigantic Living Jar at the end, see the Great Jar page.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Dominula is a village situated on a hill in the northern Altus Plateau, north of the Woodfolk Ruins. A number of wooden crosses shaped like Marika's Rune and adorned with pink floral wreathes are erected around the village. Flowers also rest on the heads of the villagers, who wear white robes stained with dried blood. The celebrants dance barefoot beneath the windmills, twirling in place as part of their ancient tradition.

Most of the dancers are too caught up in the festivities to attack the player. Those who are not dancing will attack on sight, however, and will alert the rest of the villagers to attack. The eyes of many villagers glow red. On the south side of the village, a Stranded Soul cowers in fear of a festive melody, pleading to not be skinned.

At the top of the hill upon which the village stands is a Godskin Apostle, a member of a group that once hunted and flayed the gods.
