sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
The **Erdtree** (黄金樹, *Ōgonju*; lit. "Golden Tree") is a giant, gold-colored
tree that towers above the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Erdtree is the heart of the Golden Order, and a divine blessing and direct product of the Elden Ring.

The Altus Plateau was regarded as the realm of the Erdtree, and its people believed that those blessed to be born at its foot held a special significance. The blessing granted by the Erdtree and consequently the Elden Ring, is represented by a golden light in the eyes of the inhabitants of the Lands Between, known as the Grace of Gold. Upon their deaths, the remembrances of demigods and greater champions, and other such powerful beings are hewn into the Erdtree.

The entrance to the Erdtree is currently sealed by a latticework of Impenetrable Thorns in the shape of Radagon's Rune.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Crucible of life was the primordial matter that became the Erdtree and the place where all life was once blended together. It was said to be close in nature to life itself, and was represented by gold with a reddish tint—primordial gold. Queen Marika transformed the Crucible into the Erdtree under the guidance of the Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.text:
The birth of the Erdtree coincided with the War Against the Giants. Following the defeat of the Fire Giants and their Fell God, and the confinement of the Flame of Ruin, Queen Marika declared the beginning of a new epoch, glistening with life, known as the Age of the Erdtree.

Although the Erdtree came from a blending of all life, many cultures were deemed vulgar under Marika's regime. In the time of Lord Godfrey, everything once stood in opposition to the Erdtree. Through countless victories in war, it became the embodiment of Order, and defeated were eradicated, enslaved, or banished to the fringes.

sections.heading: Age of Plenty
sections.text:
When the new age began, the Erdtree flourished with abundance. It secreted primordial life energy in the form of sacred sap, which hardened into an amber that was treasured as the most precious of jewels. These blessings fell like golden tears from its boughs, pooling in flasks or large collection basins. Queen Marika herself personally bestowed them to her Elden Lord and chosen few.  These Sacred Tears were worshipped and used to spread the faith in churches across all lands.

During these early days, the Erdtree radiated the gentle warmth of the sun and healed all who basked in its golden glow. Its bark at this time was brown, much like the Minor Erdtrees.

It was thought that the blessed sap of the Erdtree would drip from its boughs forever, but that era of blind belief swiftly came to an end. It was only for a fleeting moment, as is the course of all life. Over time, the Erdtree became more an object of faith.

sections.heading: Erdtree Burial
sections.text: Erdtree burial was an honor awarded to heroes as a proper death meant returning to the Erdtree. The remains of such champions were deposited within the catacombs built around the Greattree roots that once connected to the Erdtree. Indeed there were once heroes abundantly blessed by the Erdtree who upon earning their honors simply died. Statues of Rosus, Usher of Death, were erected in order to guide the dead who lose their way during their return to the Erdtree roots.

sections.heading: Age of the Elden Ring
sections.text: On the Night of Black Knives, a stolen fragment of the Rune of Death was used to murder Godwyn the Golden. As a hero and the first demigod to die, Godwyn's body was buried deep beneath Leyndell in the Deeproot Depths overlooking the Nameless Eternal City. Although his soul has perished, his body did not, and his Erdtree burial enabled the Rune of Death to spread throughout the great tree roots, sprouting in the form of Deathroot across the Lands Between. Deathroot violated the catacombs and gave rise to Those Who Live in Death, who refused the Erdtree's call to return. At some point, either before or after the Elden Ring was shattered, the connection between the Erdtree and the great tree roots was severed.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text:
s were released when the Elden Ring was shattered]]

Minor Erdtrees were considered to be the offspring of the Erdtree. After the Elden Ring was shattered, golden seeds flew from the Erdtree and scattered across the Lands Between, as if life itself knew that its end had come. It used to be believed that Erdtree seeds could not exist, as the Erdtree was once perfect and eternal. Erdtree Avatars emerged following the shattering of the Elden Ring, determined to protect the withering Erdtree's offspring. Illusory trees, or phantom trees, also grew from the scattered golden seeds. Additionally, the Wrath of Gold incantation was discovered, and feared as a sign of the Erdtree's wrath.

Queen Marika was imprisoned inside the Erdtree after she shattered the Elden Ring. At some point following the shattering of the Elden Ring, the entrance to the Erdtree was blocked by impenetrable thorns, emblazoned with the seal of King Consort Radagon, which prevent access to anyone outside. The Flame of Ruin was capable of burning the Erdtree and destroying the impenetrable thorns, but doing so was long held to be the first cardinal sin.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
]]
After the defeat of Morgott, the Omen King, The Tarnished attempted to enter the Erdtree to repair the Elden Ring, become Marika's consort, and ascend as Elden Lord. However, they were unable to enter due to the impenetrable thorns. The Tarnished then traveled to the Mountaintops of the Giants to rekindle the Flame of Ruin and burn the Erdtree, either by sacrificing Melina (as was her duty as the kindling maiden) or by using the Frenzied Flame. This journey eventually led them to Crumbling Farum Azula, where the defeat of Maliketh, the Black Blade unbound the Rune of Death, enabling them to enter the burning Erdtree.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The fate of the Erdtree is dependent on the player's ending choice.
- The Scadutree is the "shadow of the Erdtree."
- Miquella's Haligtree was meant to succeed the Erdtree.
- The Erdtree's presence facilitates interaction and harmony with Demi-Humans.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

- The Erdtree is evidently inspired by the  motif found in various mythologies around the world.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Elden Lord** is a title held by multiple characters in Elden Ring. It refers to individuals with great power who have stood before the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
]]
The title of Elden Lord was given to the consorts of Queen Marika the Eternal. What power and authority the Elden Lord wields is unclear, as is the nature of the relationship between an Elden Lord and their deity. In the case of the consorts of Queen Marika, they appear to have been able to wield the power of the Elden Ring to an unknown extent.

The most ancient known holder of the title is Dragonlord Placidusax, said to have been Elden Lord in the time before the Erdtree. Despite this, Godfrey is referred to as the first Elden Lord, being the first consort of Queen Marika.  After Godfrey was banished from the Lands Between, King Consort Radagon left his wife Rennala and returned to Leyndell, becoming Marika's second husband and taking the title of second Elden Lord.

After the Shattering of the Elden Ring, Marika and Radagon were both imprisoned within the Erdtree. The Demigods, tainted by the strength of their Great Runes, went to war over the title of Elden Lord, but none succeeded. Subsequently, the Tarnished were called back to the Lands Between, guided by Grace, to seek the shards of the Elden Ring and claim the title of Elden Lord.

If the Tarnished succeeds in accessing the Erdtree and opts to repair the Elden Ring, they will become Elden Lord, joining Marika as her consort. However, Marika is found in a shattered and unresponsive state, seemingly merely a shell containing the Elden Ring. The Tarnished may choose to imperfectly restore the Golden Order and rule over an Age of Fracture, or add one of three Mending Runes to establish a new Age.

sections.heading: Similar Titles
sections.text:
Certain characters hold titles reminiscent of Elden Lord, often in the service of other powerful entities.
- Dragonlord: The ruler of the Ancient Dragons.
- Dreglord: Traitorous Straghess, a revenger against the Night.
- Lord of Blasphemy: The Demigod who fed himself to the God-Devouring Serpent that intends to consume the world.
- Lord of Blood: The Demigod Mohg seeks to ascend his half-brother Miquella to godhood and hopes to rule at his side as consort.
- Lord of Frenzied Flame: The **Lord of Chaos**; a blasphemous figure touched Three Fingers who may one day restore the One Great with the power of the Frenzied Flame.
- Lord of Night: The figure who is to usher in the coming Age of the Stars awaited by the Nox of the Eternal Cities.
- Nightlord: The lord of Night that threatens Limveld
- Ensha: An ancient, soulless lord of the lost and desperate, whose bones form the Royal Remains Armor.
- Prince of Death: Fia, Deathbed Companion and Those Who Live in Death await the second life of Godwyn the Golden's soulless corpse.
- Storm Lord: A figure defeated by Godfrey during his campaigns; possibly the former ruler of Stormveil Castle.

The **Enchanted Knight** was one of the five playable characters . It served as designated sorcerer class for the Network Test. Unlike the Prophet and Warrior origins, Enchanted Knight, along with Bloody Wolf and Champion, would not appear in the final game.

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.text:
Though this class isn't available in the final release of the game, it can be recreated.

All items are found in either Limgrave or Liurnia of the Lakes.

The Winged Spear (or rather the Spear, as it's known in the released game) can be gained by either farming spear-wielding Exile Soldiers, with one of them being found up the stairs just south of the  Rampart Tower Site of Grace in Stormveil Castle or killing Patches for his +7 Spear (found at either Murkwater Cave in Limgrave or the  Scenic Isle Site of Grace in southern Liurnia) while the Carian Glintstone Shield (Carian Knight's Shield in the released game) is dropped by Moongrum, Carian Knight near the top of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

For the skills, Ash of War: Determination is dropped by a Scarab found on the bridge at the northern edge of Agheel Lake (southeast of  Agheel Lake North Site of Grace which itself is east of Gatefront Ruins in Limgrave). As Sorcerer Hunter (Skill: Carian Retaliation in the released game) is not an innate skill anymore, Ash of War: Carian Retaliation can be bought for  3,000 Runes from Pidia, Carian Servant at the end of Caria Manor after defeating Royal Knight Loretta.

The Carian Sorcerer Staff (Carian Glintstone Staff in the released game) can be found in the regular version of the Carian Study Hall along the eastern edge of Liurnia of the Lakes, on a small altar at the end of the first floor just before the elevator. Glintstone Pebble can be gained by either starting as the Astrologer Origin, or by buying it for  1,000 Runes from either Sorceress Sellen in Waypoint Ruins or Sorcerer Thops at Church of Irith. Carian Piercer is dropped by a Scarab found on the ground level of Caria Manor, just around the first pillar on the right of the stone path.

The entire Carian Knight Set can be found in the graveyard about halfway up Academy of Raya Lucaria. Past the  Church of the Cuckoo Site of Grace, heading out into the graveyard and past the rope bridge keep to the right and look over the edge for a lower platform where 3 Magic Putrid Corpse are praying in front of a small monument which the entire armor set can be found in front of.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.text:
Prisoner is the generally most suitable Origin as it only needs 1 more points in both Strength and Dexterity to wield the weapon and 1 more point in Intelligence to cast all spells and wield the shield (or 10 more points in Intelligence to wield the staff). Additionally, 3 more points in Endurance is needed to carry all the gear with a medium load, not counting any Talismans.

Astrologer exchanges some physical stats in exchange for immediately being able to cast the spells, though will still need 8 more points in Intelligence to wield the staff. They can wield the weapon two-handed with 3 more points of Dexterity and will need 2 more points in Strength to wield the shield one-handed or 4 more points to wield the weapon one-handed. Finally, 5 more points in Endurance are needed to carry all the gear with a medium load, not counting any talismans.

Samurai is a surprise contender since it's the only starting Origin able to wield the weapon one-handed but is generally very lacking in Intelligence, needing 6 more points just to wield the shield (or 5 points to  justuse the sorceries or 15 points to wield the staff). Only 2 points in Endurance are needed to carry the gear at a medium load.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Finger Seal** is a Sacred Seal and catalyst in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 800 Runes.

Obtained by default if selecting the Confessor or Prophet origins.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Used to cast Incantations. No bonus to any spells, including Two Fingers Incantations.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- At 249% Faith scaling this Seal is technically the third strongest in the game, and the strongest if your Faith is between 10 and 26. Do note that it is outclassed by any Sacred Seal with a bonus to certain spells if those spells are being cast.
  - At 10 Faith it has 126 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 20 Faith it has 156 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 30 Faith it has 188 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 40 Faith it has 221 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 50 Faith it has 254 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 60 Faith it has 286 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 70 Faith it has 305 Incantation Scaling.
  - At 80 Faith it has 329 Incantation Scaling.
- Consistently 3-5 points behind the Godslayer's Seal after reaching 27 Faith and above, making it quite viable to keep the Finger Seal upgraded for regular use if you have already invested in it and are somewhat lacking in regular Smithing Stones.
- Actually stronger than the Erdtree Seal until 66 Faith, and thereafter it becomes outclassed, which in combination with the latter requiring the much more common Somber Smithing Stones makes the latter option much more favorable.
- No bonus to any incantations, not even the ones granted by the Two Fingers, a trait shared only with the Erdtree Seal among the Sacred Seals

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The maidens live to serve a chosen Tarnished, sharing their guidance and the wisdom of the Two Fingers.

Long ago, it was promised that the guidance of grace would ensure that the pair be brought together.  Nonetheless, some never saw such guidance.

They can turn rune fragments into strength. However, not much else is known about them.

- **Finger Maiden Therolina** never met her Tarnished to guide, and was at some point captured by Seluvis and added to the collection of puppets in his secret chambers. Her puppeted form is present for the Radahn Festival at Redmane Castle and can be summoned to assist in fighting General Radahn.

- **Irina of Morne** is never identified as a Finger Maiden, but can be killed in order to advance White-Faced Varré's quest line.
- **Lightseeker Hyetta** seeks to become a Finger Maiden, but follows Three Fingers instead.

  - The double-dipping effectively pulls it B-scaling on Faith-scaling affinities to the equivalent of an S-scaling.
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Fire Knight's Shortsword.
  - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.
- If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats.
  - In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities is only shared with the Clayman's Harpoon while the DLC adds the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, Fire Knight's Greatsword, and Fire Knight's Shortsword, weapons which all have the same quality.
- Due to a bug this weapon actually doesn't have an actual Arcane-scaling on Poison, Blood, and Occult affinities.

sections.text: **The Deep of Night**, also known as the **Deep Night** is a gameplay mode in Elden Ring Nightreign, included in an update that launched on September 11, 2025.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Deep of Night is a ranked game mode that offers greater challenges with increasing difficulty to veteran Nightfarers who have braved the Night's Tide many times. Enemies are stronger than usual, the target Nightlord cannot be specified, and Shifting Earth changes are not reflected. Exclusive rewards such as Depths Relics and weapons with multiple additional but also detrimental effects can appear. Difficulty increases with each descent, and ratings fluctuate with wins and losses, directly influencing the **Depth** (levels 1 through 5). Increase rank through victory and journey deeper into the infinite Night.<section begin="Summary"/>

sections.heading: Key Features
sections.text:
- **The Deep of Night is a high-difficulty ranked challenge mode**
- Progress through 'Depths' levels 1 through 5, each rank increasing difficulty
- 'Depths' 4 and 5 function as an "endless mode"
- Ratings fluctuate according to wins and losses; reaching 1,000 increases your Depth.
- Fully-randomized Nightlords
- Fully-randomized Shifting Earth events
- Stronger, tankier 'Red' Enemies and Bosses, identified by veiny red visual effects, that drop potent
- When the mode is unlocked, every Chalice for each Nightfarer gains three extra Relic slots (a total of six per vessel) dedicated to special Depths Relics.
- **Depths Relics**: powerful relics touched by the Deep of Night that only activate in the Deep of Night game mode. They provide both positive and negative effects.
- : powerful weapons found in the Deep of Night that have two positive effects and one adverse effect; otherwise equal to  in terms of gameplay
- New beneficial Effects unique to Depths Relics and .<section end="Summary"/>

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: are special Demigods with the potential to reach full godhood and forge a new Order. They are hand-selected by the Two Fingers to succeed the current god as vessel for the great Elden Ring. As such, they are important characters in the world of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Empyreans can ascend to godhood through different methods. Marika was able to ascend using the Gate of Divinity, gathering the Runes of thousands of hornsent sacrificed to form it. Miquella was also able to use the Gate after divesting his physical body and Great Rune before performing a secret rite involving Radahn as his Lord. Malenia could ascend by letting her Rot bloom three times. while Ranni finds her Order by "[going] to the night sky." They fully consummate their godhood by becoming the vessel of the Elden Ring. Their chosen consort confers Great Runes and brandishes the Elden Ring, becoming the Elden Lord.

Empyreans are served by warrior vassals of unerring loyalty, which may come in the form of wolves. Shadowbound beasts, sometimes simply referred to as "shadows," are custom-tailored by the Two Fingers to ensure the Demigod follows the right path. Though incapable of treachery towards their Empyrean, should their master resist the will of the Two Fingers, they will descend into madness, becoming a curse rather than a protector.  The three known shadowbound beasts are: Maliketh, who serves Marika; Blaidd, who serves Ranni; and the Baleful Shadow, which had no Empyrean master and served the Two Fingers directly. There are also many aspects that an Empyrean can possess.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The most prominent Empyrean was Queen Marika, a golden-haired Numen from the Shaman Village. A descendant of denizens of another world, she was selected and guided by the Two Fingers toward true godhood. Through seduction and betrayal, Marika ascended at the Gate of Divinity, located atop the tower of Enir-Ilim. There, she acquired threads of the Elden Ring, became its vessel, and created her Order. She later used a Golden Seed to transform the Crucible into the Erdtree, and eventually shattered the Elden Ring. Her shadow was Maliketh and her consorts were Lord Godfrey and Serosh, and later her other half, Lord Radagon.

Another Empyrean, known as the Gloam-Eyed Queen, wielded the god-slaying black flame and raised the Godskin Apostles. She challenged Marika's established Order by leading her followers on a god hunt. However, she was defeated in battle by Marika's shadowbound beast, Maliketh, the Black Blade. Marika then extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and Maliketh sealed it within his Black Blade. This act severed the source of the Gloam-Eyed Queen's power and created the Golden Order. The identities and deeds of her shadow and consort remain unclear.

During the Age of the Erdtree, three Empyreans were named as Marika's potential successors: Miquella, Malenia and Ranni. Miquella and Malenia were twins born of a single god, being the children of both Marika and her second consort Radagon. Their powerful lineage made them prime candidates for Empyrean. Ranni, on the other hand, was the daughter of Radagon and his former wife, Queen Rennala of the Full Moon, prior to his union with Marika. This demonstrates that being the child of two full gods is not a strict requirement to become an Empyrean, as Ranni herself was only a demigod. Miquella saw a tender kindness in General Radahn and made a vow to select him as his future consort.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text: Miquella himself was able to ascend to godhood, but was defeated by the Tarnished before he could reach Fractured Marika and bring about his envisioned Age of Compassion. Unlike her brother, Malenia rejected her destiny and abandoned the Servants of Rot. However, she would briefly ascend as the Goddess of Rot during her battle with the same Tarnished warrior but was similarly defeated, yet fated to bloom once more. As for Ranni, she has the potential to bring about her Age of Stars with the assistance of the Tarnished, who she makes her consort. The Tarnished can become Marika's third consort, using her imprisoned form to bring about the Ages of Fracture, Order, Age of the Duskborn, or introduce the Blessing of Despair.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Each Empyrean typically bonds with their Lord consort near their ascension to godhood.
- Whether all Empyreans are granted a Shadow is unclear, as there is no concrete evidence of Miquella, Malenia, nor the Gloam-Eyed Queen receiving shadowbound beasts.
- Mohg, Lord of Blood wished to be Miquella's consort but was used to house the soul of Radahn instead.
- Dragonlord Placidusax's unnamed god is presumed to be an Empyrean who was once a vessel to the Elden Ring, apropos to his own title as Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- "" refers to the highest heaven in ancient and medieval cosmology, usually consisting of fire or light. It can also refer to the firmament (the heavens) or an ideal place or state. In Japanese, Empyreans are referred to as 神人 (*Shinjin*; lit. "Divine Person", "God-like Person").
- Miquella has cut dialogue phrased similar to the speech given by Ranni the Witch during her Age of Stars ending.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Elden Beast** is the final Boss of Elden Ring, encountered on the Stone Platform inside the Erdtree at Leyndell, Ashen Capital, fought directly after Radagon of the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: A long-necked, aquatic creature, the Elden Beast is a living constellation of shimmering Amber Starlight suspended in a translucent silhouette. Its narrow head lacks a traditional face, instead containing a single ball of glowing white light. It has a golden spine, an elongated body, and, along its back, long, tapering fins flare outward like fingers of radiant gold. Behind the torso trails a long, tapering tail that ends in a rich golden rootstock. The Elden Beast has two arms and two legs, with five-fingered hands. A glowing crack like shattered glass graces its chest.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Sent upon a golden star by the Greater Will, the arrival of the Elden Beast was one of the earliest events known to have occurred in the Lands Between. It was the vassal beast of the Greater Will and the living incarnation of the concept of Order. At some later point in the primordial past, the Elden Beast was forged into the great Elden Ring. The Empyrean consort of Dragonlord Placidusax became its vessel, becoming a god and making the ancient dragon the first known Elden Lord.

After untold ages, the Numen Marika, an Empyrean, became the new goddess and the vessel of the Elden Ring. Her Golden Order established her as the one true god to rule over the Lands Between. However, Marika eventually shattered the Elden Ring, leading to her imprisonment at the Stone Platform within the Erdtree.

The Tarnished enters the Erdtree where they find the shackled Marika, and face Radagon, Marika's male other self and the reigning Elden Lord, the two of them sharing the same body. After his defeat, the Elden Beast emerges from Radagon, transforming his defeated body into a large sword. The Elden Beast reverts to the Elden Ring upon defeat.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
- Nearest Site of Grace:  Elden Throne

The Elden Beast appears immediately after Radagon of the Golden Order is defeated. If you die to the Elden Beast, you are required to fight Radagon again before rechallenging it.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
- HP: 22,127
- Defense: 121
- Stance: 150
- This boss cannot be Parried.
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
- Deals  Standard and  Holy damage
- Immune to all Status Ailments

Elden Beast is the second half of the final boss fight with Radagon of the Golden Order. The Elden Beast uses a combination of physical sword attacks and golden Holy attacks.

The arena is a large, flat body of shallow water. Although it appears endless, the arena does have invisible walls surrounding it. The Elden Beast will regularly swim away from the player, or disappear underwater before emerging, meaning that the fight often requires one to chase or wait for it. Unlike the previous fight, it is possible to summon Torrent.

When its health reaches around 80% it will fly up into the air and create a golden ring which closes in on the player before exploding. This can be avoided by jumping over the ring as it closes in. It will also begin to use additional attacks, such as Elden Stars or Spear Showers. At around 30% health, it will perform the Golden Ring attack again, but this time it will generate three rings that each close in on the player.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
Its normal sword attacks are fairly easy to dodge, with perhaps the repeating stabs being an exception. The Golden Rings can be jumped over to preserve your momentum and get out of them quicker, while the Spear Showers can be avoid by running while zig-zagging.

Elden Stars, if it cannot be interrupted by a stagger, is quite dangerous due to the consistent damage over time it can inflict and because it will gain speed to chase if allowed to travel with minimal turning. A way to fairly easily dodge it is to circle the Elden Beast counter-clockwise (that is, heading around it to your right before circling left to run out the duration.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- It is heavily implied that the Elden Beast was the being who imprisoned Marika inside the Erdtree based on one of its attacks where it attempts to grab the player and lift them up in the air to crucify and then pierce them with a barrage of golden spears, similar to how Marika was seen in the cutscene before the final boss battle.
- Its tail resembles a network of golden roots and is comparable to those of Astels and Fallingstar Beasts.
- The properties and appearance of the Elden Beast may have differed when it contained the Rune of Death and various Great Runes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Elden Beast is internally referenced as the *"NebulaDragon"*.
- It resembles the dragon associated with the alchemical , paralleling Marika and Radagon. The Rebis represents a single entity split into male and female halves, later reunited as a transcendent being empowered by a dragon.
- It was not possible to summon Torrent when facing the Elden Beast prior to Version 1.12.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The  is a boss in Elden Ring. He is encountered at Flame Peak on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This encounter is **not** optional as it must be completed to unlock Crumbling Farum Azula and advance the main storyline.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Fire Giant is a gargantuan, red-haired humanoid with a slumbering, bearded face on its front torso. Its flame-red hair is worn in many braids, each with at least one beard bead. They worshipped the Fell God of Flame, and could borrow from it to achieve near-godlike power. The Fire Giants viewed smithing as a divine rite, and even their descendants, the Trolls, wielded hammers patterned after the fell god's eye. The association between smithing and divinity reaches back to the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, whose anvils were shaped like altars and used in sacred forges.-->

Long before the Erdtree, the Giants claimed the inhospitable northern mountains after driving away the Ice Dragons that once ruled them. They worshipped their Fell God and tended its Flame within the Great Forge. Their astrologer neighbors dwelled among the high peaks, while the Zamor Knights were their eternal enemies.

When Queen Marika the Eternal ushered in the Age of the Erdtree, she ordered her consort Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, to wage the War Against the Giants, fearing that their flame could burn her Erdtree. Despite their might, the Giants were said to have been slain by Godfrey and his Crucible Knights, while Marika herself was rumored to have struck down the fell god. They were punished by the Briars of Sin, yet their inextinguishable Flame endured. Marika sealed it away, reducing its once-roaring blaze to embers and cursing the last Fire Giant to tend it for eternity.

After untold ages, the last Fire Giant's labor was interrupted by a Tarnished seeking to harness the flame to burn the Erdtree. In battle, the Giant's leg brace was shattered, and in agony he tore off his own foot to sacrifice it to the fell god. Even empowered by divine flame, he was finally struck down—his death releasing him from the eternal curse.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
Alexander, Warrior Jar is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been met at Mt. Gelmir. His summon sign is just inside the western boss gate. Torrent can also be used during this fight.

The arena is a large snowfield with craggy, uneven terrain. The field slops upwards from the entrance, and the Giant begins the fight at the top of the slope. Torrent can be called during this fight, and is useful for covering distance and avoiding the avalanche by jumping.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
During phase 1, the Fire Giant will fight using a large, circular dish. Although he is fairly slow-moving, he is able to cover distance using his roll. He also possesses the ability to launch an avalanche straight towards the player. Initially, the majority of his attacks involve slamming the dish into the ground.

The objective initially is to attack the red braids wrapped around his left leg. After enough damage has been dealt, the braids will fall off, uncovering his injured ankle. At this point he will roll three times in succession, and then reach into the mouth on his abdomen, coating his hand in flames. He now gains the ability to use two fire-based abilities- a fast-moving fireball, and a large, slow-moving fire orb that homes in on the player.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: Once his health drops below 47%, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. The Fire Giant has now lost the large dish as well as his left leg, and is forced to kneel on the ground. He is less mobile during this phase, however he can still roll. He now has a greater variety of fire spells. He may summon pillars of fire that erupt from the ground around him, breathe fire, or spew molten rocks that rain down on the arena. His weak spot is now on his left forearm.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Fire Giants came in a range of sizes. Some were smaller than the Fire Giant, while others were larger. Even the largest known Fire Giants were smaller than the skulls of the colossal remains.
- Each Fire Giant killed in the War Against the Giants is tangled in the Briars of Sin and has white hair rather than red, as if drained of color. It is unclear whether this change was caused by the thorns or occurs naturally upon a Fire Giant's death.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ekzykes's Decay** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Caelid
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Decaying Ekzykes in Caelid.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a heavy, rotting mist, dealing Standard damage equal to 155% of Incantation Scaling and causing 65 Scarlet Rot build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 465% of the same and 195 build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
  - Note that while the Dragon Communion Seal scales with Arcane, Scarlet Rot will not scale with that so Ekzykes's Decay gains no innate benefit except for the damage boost.
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Compatible with the Blue Dancer Charm, even more so since its two primary boosting items, the Dragon Communion Seal and Rock Heart, are weightless.
- The Scarlet Rot deals damage roughly equal to 1170 + 29.7% of the target's maximum health over the course of 90 seconds.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.
- The total Scarlet Rot build-up is 390 if using both breaths, enough to afflict many vulnerable enemies and bosses with the Status Effect and most non-resistant ones within two full casts.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Rotten Breath.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 168 FP: 2*48 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 91 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Compared to Rotten Breath, this spell deals 18% more damage but also consumes 40% more FP.
- This is the weakest "named" dragon breath attack, but it's also the only one that deals Physical damage.
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased. Reduced Scarlet Rot status effect buildup.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.
  - The status build-up per hit was decreased from 130 to 65 (total build-up reduced from 780 to 390).
  - Prior to Patch 1.07, this amount of build-up was twice as much, 780 in total, letting it Rot most non-resistant enemies and bosses in one full cast.

sections.text: **Elden Stars** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

**Loot:** Deeproot Depths
- Elden Stars can be looted from a body at the end of a cave filled with giant ants in the Deeproot Depths, located immediately west of the Great Waterfall Crest grace, after climbing up one of the large roots.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: This spell sends out a golden orb that tracks its target while shooting out small projectiles with Holy Attack Power equal to 20% of Incantation Scaling. Upon making contact with a surface or enemy, the orb explodes, dealing Holy Attack Power equal to 199% of Incantation Scaling and hitting a 4.2-meter radius around the point of impact.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  47 FP per cast.
- Costs  48 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Deals 14 Stance damage with the explosion and 0.5 Stance damage per mini-projectile that hits.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The small projectiles sent out by the main orb deal extremely low damage and are mainly useful for harassing other players with constant incoming damage ticks.
  - The reason that the damage is so much lower than the difference in Attack Power suggests is because defense reduces the damage of attacks with relatively lower Attack Power much more than those with relatively high Attack Power.
- Generally a rather ineffective spell that is mostly useful for pressuring other players in PvP scenarios.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Elden Beast uses this spell.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption from 47 to 41.
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Electrify Armament** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Grants the right-hand weapon a Weapon Buff giving bonus Lightning Attack Power equal to 75% of the Faith-based Incantation Scaling of the Sacred Seal used to cast it for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 10 points of Stamina to cast.
- Despite being a Dragon Cult Incantation, this spell, like other spell-based weapon buffs, does not get bonus damage from its associated seal (the Gravel Stone Seal for this one).
- This is generally the strongest Faith-based weapon buff: Order's Blade requires a light Intelligence investment and grants the more often resisted Holy, Black Flame Blade has a very short duration of 7 seconds (9.1 seconds with Old Lord's Talisman) even with it dealing damage based on the target's maximum HP, and Bloodflame Blade only grants Fire Attack Power equal to 40% of Incantation Scaling.
- Like with all spell-based Weapon Buffs, it can only be cast when a weapon is held in the right hand and the casting implement in the left hand.
- Outmatched by Lightning Grease and Skill: Lightning Slash below 114 Incantation Scaling and by Dragonbolt Grease Shadow of the Erdtree below 160 Incantation Scaling.
  - Though they cast much quicker and last for a shorter duration, Drawstring Lightning Grease is stronger below 147 Incantation Scaling while Drawstring Dragonbolt Grease Shadow of the Erdtree is stronger below 180 Incantation Scaling.
  - Lightning Slash has the advantage of also being usable for weapons with the otherwise unbuffable (not counting other skills) Lightning and Sacred Affinity weapons.

sections.text: **Fire's Deadly Sin** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Painting Item:** Altus Plateau
- Left behind by the spirit of an artist located near the southern cliffs at the top of Dominula, Windmill Village, south of the Windmill Heights Site of Grace after acquiring "Flightless Bird" Painting.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Slam down on the ground do hit with Fire Attack Power equal to 183% of Incantation Scaling with a 3 meter radius and gain a Body Buff that hits 4/s with 45 Fire Attack Power with a 2 meter radius while ignoring Guarding. Lasts for 40 seconds and damages the caster for 6/s (240 damage total).

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the initial fire explosion to 212% of Incantation Scaling and the Body Buff's Attack Power per tick to 59. Self damage is increased to 8/s (320 damage total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  10 FP per cast.
- Costs  28 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 36.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- The initial fire explosion deals 7 Stance damage while the ticks from the Buff deals 0 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage of the initial explosion to 10.
- The self damage is technically 3/0.5 seconds for the uncharged version and 4/0.5 seconds for the charged version.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- Old Lord's Talisman increases the duration of this spell from 40 to 52 seconds.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 16% for the explosion and by 31% for the ticks, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 33% for the explosion and by 51% for the ticks.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The Attack Power is too low to reliably defeat most enemies without additional sources of damage.
- Fire attacks cleanse targets of their Frostbite buildup, resetting the status effect. This spell synergizes particularly well with Frostbite builds by allowing them to trigger Frostbite damage more frequently than usual.
- The constant HP drain from this spell can be mitigated by using the Blessing of the Erdtree or Blessing's Boon incantations, the Crimsonburst Crystal Tear; the Blessed Dew Talisman, the Icon Shield, or the Royal Remains Armor. Equipping the full Royal Remains Set will completely offset the damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Like Catch Flame and Flame Sling, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.

- In a prior version of Elden Ring, this spell could guarantee the activation of the Erdtree Greatshield's Golden Retaliation skill, triggering its golden projectile whenever used.
- Additionally, this spell used to inherit the on-hit effects of active Weapon Buffs. Most notably, this included the Blood Loss buildup from Bloodflame Blade and the Death Blight effect from the Eclipse Shotel's Death Flare skill, resulting in devastating consequences.
- Patch 1.03: Fixed a bug which causes Fire's Deadly Sin incantation to have different effect.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Elemer of the Briar** is a reoccurring boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Elemer of the Briar, also known as the **Bell Bearing Hunter**, originally hailed from Eochaid, a land of proudly solitary ascetics. He wears iron armor wrapped in iron thorns, which are a mark of the guilty and of those sentenced to death. He was slated for execution at the Shaded Castle, home of the family of House Marais, however he evaded death by snatching the sword from the site of his looming execution and furnished it with battle skills from his homeland. He gained the moniker "Bell Bearing Hunter" by killing numerous merchants and instructors, and taking their Bell Bearings.

Elemer can be encountered in the Castellan's Hall of the Shaded Castle, the site of his failed execution. He can also appear in various locations throughout the Lands Between, typically in places where merchants can be found.

The Bell-Bearing Hunter will only appear when resting at night; to make him reappear after being defeated yourself, rest at the grace and set the time to night and then rest again.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Can include a separate table for a specific instance of this variant's moveset.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
- Try to stick close to him as his ranged sword swipes are much wider and generally harder to predict.
- It is possible to bait him into a cycle of repeated shield slams by getting behind him and only landing one attack (lighter weapons can possibly use an uncharged heavy attack and some skills are quick enough to also be used) after each slam. Be aware that he can also follow up with an explosion sometimes, so take a moment to see if the shield begins to glow red as he is about to pull it up.
- The grab is rather hard to dodge and very delayed. Wait until his hand begins to move towards you before dodging. It is also possible to dodge by running far enough away or by being behind him.
- The blade drill is hard to avoid if rolling to the right and has some reach so try to roll forward and to the left.
- His shield charge is very quick so try to stay relatively close as to not provoke it.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Elemer is encountered in the hall at the top of the Shaded Castle. He can channel energy through his sword, allowing him to send it towards the player and control it at a distance, or fire a red beam by rotating it quickly.

The first time he is encountered he will be facing the painting at the end of the room, making a heavy initial attack such as a charged heavy attack more possible. On subsequent attempts he will be facing the entrance.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Bell Bearing Hunter appears in Warmaster's Shack at night. He will only spawn if the player has talked to Knight Bernahl and exhausted his dialogue. Bernahl will not be present while the Bell Bearing Hunter is spawned, but will reappear if the player dies or if they defeat the boss.

sections.heading: Background

Miriel will not be present when the Bell Bearing Hunter appears, but will reappear if the player dies or if they defeat the boss.

sections.heading: Background

This version is actually stronger than Elemer's own fight.

This version is actually the strongest of all the Bell-Bearing Hunter encounters and has twice the health of Elemer's own, named encounter.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fia, Deathbed Companion** is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Fia is initially located at the Roundtable Hold in the room adjacent to Smithing Master Hewg. She may be hugged to gain a Baldachin's Blessing. At a certain point during her questline, she moves to the  Prince of Death's Throne at the Deeproot Depths.

Fia's quest intersects with the questlines of D, Hunter of the Dead; D, Beholder of Death; Ranni the Witch; and Sorcerer Rogier.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Fia was once a Deathbed Companion. She would receive the warmth and vigor from champions, and then lay with the remains of an exalted noble, to grant him another chance at life. This was the sole purpose of Fia's existence, and was considered a sacred act in her homeland.

However, before Fia could bear the noble into new life, she was awakened by the guidance of grace, and chased from her birthplace, travelling to the Lands Between. At some point she met a chivalrous knight by the name of Lionel the Lionhearted. Upon meeting the exiled Fia, Lionel declared himself to be her father, and became her loyal companion.

Fia found herself in Roundtable Hold, where she continued to perform her role as a Deathbed Companion. Here, she encountered Rogier, a spellblade obsessed with Those Who Live in Death, and a Tarnished champion seeking to become Elden Lord. Rogier began an investigation into the events surrounding the Night of Black Knives, which had led to the death of Godwyn, aided by the Tarnished champion. Fia subtly aided the pair in their investigation, pointing them towards the Black Knifeprint, and granted her services to the Tarnished champion, taking their warmth and vigor in exchange for her blessings.

Unbeknownst to the other Tarnished of Roundtable Hold, Fia was the companion of Godwyn, the Prince of Death, and wished to become a mother to Those Who Live in Death. After asking the Tarnished to return a Weathered Dagger to D, Hunter of the Dead, Fia kills D, who was in possession of one half of the Cursemark of Death,  and returns the Cursemark to the malformed corpse of Godwyn in Deeproot Depths. She then solicits the assistance of the Tarnished in retrieving the other half of the Cursemark, which she uses to gestate a Mending Rune that can embed the principle of Life in Death into Order.

D, Beholder of Death, seeking revenge for his brother, D, kills Fia after she creates her Mending Rune.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
Fia's questline ties into the questlines of several other NPCs, and is required in order to achieve the Age of the Duskborn ending.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Fia can be found in her room in Roundtable Hold. Initially she will be available to provide a Baldachin's Blessing.
  - After Rogier comes to Roundtable Hold and discusses the Night of Black Knives, Fia will provide a Knifeprint Clue. The Black Knifeprint must be obtained and given to Rogier.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - After triggering the Radahn Festival, Fia will ask you to return the Weathered Dagger to its rightful owner. You must give this to D, Hunter of the Dead, and reload the area.
  - Fia can now be found in a previously locked room, standing over D's corpse. Exhaust her dialogue and she will disappear.
1. Deeproot Depths
  - Defeat Fia's Champions and rest at the Site of Grace. Fia will be sitting in front of Godwyn's corpse. She will offer you the opportunity to kill her. To continue her questline, select "No, I want to be held." Selecting "That's right" will not lock you out of the rest of the questline, and you can change your mind by speaking to her again.
  - While being held, choose "Talk in Secret" to learn about the Cursemark of Death.
1. Divine Tower of Liurnia
  - In order to access the Divine Tower of Liurnia, you need to have progressed Ranni the Witch's quest and received the Carian Inverted Statue. Use the statue on the pedestal in the first room of the Carian Study Hall and progress through the area to the Divine Tower.
  - Retrieve the Cursemark of Death from the top of the tower.
1. Deeproot Depths
  - Speak to Fia again and select "Talk in Secret" until you receive the option to hand Fia the Cursemark of Death.
  - Exhaust her dialogue once again and reload the area to find her sleeping.
1. Deathbed Dream
  - Interact with Fia's body to enter the Deathbed Dream. Defeat Lichdragon Fortissax to return to Deeproot Depths.
1. Deeproot Depths
  - Loot the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince from Fia's body. This will allow you to achieve the Age of Duskborn ending.
  - Reload the area to find Fia dead, with D, Beholder of Death standing over her.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Fia will not fight you if attacked, however skull-like projectiles resembling those summoned when casting Rancorcall will spawn above her head and target you. Her dialogue when attacked implies that Godwyn is the source of these projectiles.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Drawing-Room Key** is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- Opens the doors within the Volcano Manor in the hallway adjacent to Tanith's throne.
- Triggers Knight Bernahl's relocation from the Warmaster's Shack of Limgrave to the eastern quarter of the manor.
- Expands Knight Bernahl's shop inventory with Ash of War: Eruption and Ash of War: Assassin's Gambit.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Volcano Manor, Mt. Gelmir
- Received from Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress upon selecting **Join Volcano Manor**.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This item is part of Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress's questline.
- If Knight Bernahl is killed prior to acquiring this key, the Twin Maiden Husks will offer his expanded stock via Bernahl's Bell Bearing.
- If Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is defeated by bypassing the Volcano Manor through the Abductor Virgin in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, this item will be found on Tanith's chair.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Fingerslayer Blade** is a Key Item in Elden Ring. It is part of Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- The Fingerslayer Blade must be given to Ranni the Witch at Ranni's Rise to advance her questline.
- In exchange, Ranni will reward the player with the Carian Inverted Statue, which opens the path from the Carian Study Hall to the Divine Tower of Liurnia.
- Grants access to the Cursemark of Death and the Stargazer Heirloom.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Night's Sacred Ground
- The Fingerslayer Blade is found inside a treasure chest at the base of the Chair-Crypt in Nokron, Eternal City. The chest is guarded by a Mimic Troll and multiple Silver Mimic Tears.
- The locked Nox treasure chest containing the Fingerslayer Blade only opens for Ranni's followers. "**You are not destined to open this**" displays if the player tries to open it before agreeing to serve Ranni the Witch at Ranni's Rise.
- Nokron, the upper Eternal City section of the Siofra River, becomes accessible after defeating Starscourge Radahn at the Wailing Dunes. The death of the Red Lion General releases certain stars from his gravitational grip, resuming fates held in stasis since the Starscourge Conflict. A falling star crashes to the earth in Limgrave, setting Ranni's Empyrean destiny back into motion. The starfall crater enables passage to the long-lost Eternal City.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The misshapen Fingerslayer Blade has a spiraling, crescent-shaped blade that faintly glows at its tip. Its crossguard bends in a downward arch, similar to the Rune of Death.
- It strongly resembles the Sacred Relic Sword fashioned from the extracted remains of Radagon of the Golden Order, suggesting it was once a vessel that held the Elden Ring.
  - As per its reveal, only the Elden Beast can transform gods into armaments.
  - The Fingerslayer Blade is unlikely to originate from among the known cast.
- Nox conspirators who wore Nox Mirrorhelms wielded the Fingerslayer Blade, likely against Metyr, Mother of Fingers, the daughter of the Greater Will who retreated beneath the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. This act triggered the invasion of Astel and the downfall of the Eternal Cities.
- Later, Ranni the Witch can use the Fingerslayer Blade against her Two Fingers, hidden beneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
- The Fingerslayer Blade, an item with which treacherous War Counselor Iji is well-versed, is guarded by a Troll.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Iji's Mirrorhelm – Another instrument of high treason.
- Night — The Outer God
- Ringed Finger – Another relic of high treason.
- Sword of Milos – Another weapon made from a corpse.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Finger Reader Enia** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Enia is a long-lived Finger Reader, much like the Finger Reader Crones scattered across the Lands Between. She interprets the words of the Two Fingers, envoys of the Greater Will. Enia remains in Roundtable Hold alongside the Two Fingers, offering words of wisdom throughout the Tarnisheds' journeys.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
The Tarnished meets Enia in the Two Fingers' audience chamber in Roundtable Hold after claiming a Great Rune, where she imparts the wisdom of the Two Fingers upon them, revealing that they must gather more Great Runes to repair the shattered Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. In addition to her guidance, Enia offers to grant the Tarnished the power housed within the Remembrances they gain from killing powerful foes.

After the Tarnished defeats Morgott, the Omen King and finds the way inside the Erdtree blocked by  impenetrable thorns, the Two Fingers begin their long communication with the Greater Will. Enia, discovering that the Tarnished intends to burn the Erdtree and unleash the Rune of Death, Enia forewarns them of the dangers of the first cardinal sin, telling them that the Two Fingers and Greater Will would not approve of this course of action. With the Fingers dormant, Enia ultimately advises the Tarnished to do what they think is right.

After the Rune of Death is unleashed, Enia goes dormant along with the Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Power from Remembrance
sections.text: The following are items that can be obtained in exchange for the Remembrances of major bosses. The required Remembrance will be removed from the player's inventory once an item is purchased, however they can be duplicated using Wandering Mausoleums.

sections.heading: Equipment of Champions
sections.text: The following are items that can be purchased after defeating certain bosses.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Enia can first be spoken to in Roundtable Hold, in the door west of the Table of Lost Grace, after defeating a Shardbearer. Exhaust her dialogue to unlock her two shop inventories.
1. After defeating two Shardbearers, speak to Enia again to receive a Talisman Pouch.
  - If you defeat Morgott, the Omen King before speaking to Enia during this step, the Talisman Pouch will be available to purchase from the Twin Maiden Husks.
1. After defeating Morgott, the Omen King and attempting to access the Erdtree, speak to Enia again for some additional dialogue.
1. After gaining access to Crumbling Farum Azula, speak to Enia again for some additional dialogue.
1. Enia will narrate the cutscene that plays after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. She will now be dead upon returning to Roundtable Hold, however her shop inventories can still be accessed by interacting with her corpse.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Elden Remembrance** is a Remembrance, a type of consumable Tool in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- Consume to gain  50,000 runes
- Tradeable; speak with Finger Reader Enia and select "**Receive power from remembrance**" to gain either Marika's Hammer or Sacred Relic Sword.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Stone Platform (Leyndell, Ashen Capital)
- The Elden Remembrance is obtained upon defeating the Elden Beast at the Stone Platform within the burning Erdtree, accessible via the Elden Throne at Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Once acquired, this Remembrance can be duplicated at any Wandering Mausoleum without a bell.
- While Remembrances can be duplicated more than once through different duplicators, they cannot be exchanged for additional copies of an item already obtained in the same playthrough.
- Max held: 99
- Max stored: 600
- Sell value:  50,000 runes

sections.text: **Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree** is a legacy dungeon in Elden Ring. It is accessible after defeating Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree in Miquella's Haligtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: It is an optional endgame locations that can only be reached by descending from Miquella's Haligtree, past Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree. The boss at the end of this area is Malenia, Blade of Miquella.
