sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: This page provides an overview of the **endings** in Elden Ring. Players have six options to conclude the game: the *Age of Fracture*, *Age of Order*, *Age of the Duskborn*, *Blessing of Despair*, *Age of the Stars*, or the *Lord of Frenzied Flame*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The various endings in Elden Ring are tied to choices made by the player throughout their journey, as well as optional questlines. These outcomes define the fate of the Lands Between, and the role the Tarnished assumes as Queen Marika's Elden Lord or otherwise. Each ending represents the Tarnished brandishing the Elden Ring and ushering in their new Age.

**Note**: Receiving the Flame of Frenzy from the Three Fingers in the Frenzied Flame Proscription will **lock** the player out of all endings except the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending. This restriction can be lifted by using Miquella's Needle when prompted at Dragonlord Placidusax's boss arena, however, doing so will **permanently lock** the player out of the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending.

sections.heading: Choosing an Ending
sections.text:
After defeating the final boss, the Tarnished will return to a room containing Marika's statue and a nearby Grace. If Ranni's questline has been completed, her summon sign will also appear near the Fractured Marika statue. At this point, the player can choose an ending by interacting with either Marika's statue or, if available, Ranni's summon sign.

If the Tarnished possesses the Frenzied Flame, Ranni's summon sign will not appear unless the Frenzied Flame has been removed using Miquella's Needle. In this scenario, the only option is to interact with Marika's statue, which automatically triggers the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending, offering no alternative choices.

Without the Frenzied Flame, interacting with Marika's statue presents the option to select one of three possible mending runes obtained during the Tarnished's journey. Choosing a rune initiates the corresponding ending: *Age of Order*, *Age of the Duskborn*, or *Blessing of Despair*. Alternatively, players can choose to "Mend the Elden Ring" without a rune, resulting in the *Age of Fracture* ending.

If Ranni's summon sign is present and selected instead of Marika's statue, the *Age of the Stars* ending will begin.

Regardless of the choice, the nearby Site of Grace allows the player to teleport elsewhere and return later, postponing the ending and enabling continued exploration.

To start a New Game Plus, an ending must be selected. After the end credits, players can choose "Begin Journey X" or return later to the Roundtable Hold Grace to initiate the new playthrough.

sections.heading: Elden Lord
sections.text: The *Age of Fracture*, *Age of Order*, *Age of the Duskborn*, and *Blessing of Despair* endings all result in the Tarnished becoming Marika's new Elden Lord. Each offers a different interpretation of Marika's vision for the Golden Order, mending the Elden Ring and ushering in their new Age of choice to rule over.

sections.heading: Age of Fracture
sections.text: In the *Age of Fracture* ending, the Tarnished becomes Elden Lord without adding any special Mending Runes to the Elden Ring. In doing so, they fulfill the Two Fingers' plans of using the Tarnished to restore the sense of stability not felt since the Elden Ring was shattered. The Golden Order remains in the truest state possible to what it once was and the status quo is restored.

sections.heading: Age of Order
sections.text: The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, fulfilling Goldmask's idea of a "Perfect" Golden Order based on his research into how it had fallen to its current state. Realizing that the Golden Order's imperfections stemmed from the fickleness of the gods, who, in fact, were no better than men, Goldmask's new transcendental ideology attempts to bring true order to the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Age of the Duskborn
sections.text: The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, wielding the rune born from Fia and the Prince of Death's union. Just as the Golden Order had been created by confining the Rune of Death, the Tarnished creates a new order of death restored. The principle of life in death is embedded within this order, and Those Who Live in Death are allowed to live in peace. Thus begins the *Age of the Duskborn*.

sections.heading: Blessing of Despair
sections.text: The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, bringing about an accursed world where defilement becomes the norm. All will become cursed in the *Blessing of Despair* ending. Thus, none can be scorned, fulfilling the Dung Eater's twisted vision.

sections.heading: Age of the Stars
sections.text: In the "Age of the Stars" ending, the player Tarnished summons Ranni the Witch to succeed Marika in godhood. Ranni ushers in her vision of a new order not of gold, but of the stars and moon of the chill night. Rather than make herself and her order objects of worship, she chooses instead to keep her order and both the Lands Between and the cycle of life and death at a great divide, removing the certainties of faith that had existed during Marika's rule. The Tarnished takes the role of Ranni's Elden Lord consort, and they leave the Lands Between together, embarking on a thousand-year voyage into darkness under the wisdom of the Moon.

sections.heading: Lord of Frenzied Flame
sections.text:
The "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending, triggered by the possession of the Frenzied Flame, overrides the possibility of any other ending. The Tarnished disregard the notion of becoming Elden Lord, becoming the Lord of Frenzied Flame instead and incinerating everything that came before. Rather than become Elden Lord, The Tarnished becomes the Lord of Frenzied Flame, fulfilling the machinations of Shabriri, and the Three Fingers' will. The Tarnished is left almost completely alone, the Frenzied Flame rapidly consuming everything in existence.

If Melina was not sacrificed, she is seen vowing to hunt down and kill the Tarnished for not heeding her earlier warnings. For The Tarnished to separate themselves from the Frenzied Flame's influence after it being inherited, they must acquire Miquella's Needle and follow its specific conditions of use. Once the Frenzied Flame is suppressed, it can not be reclaimed in any way, preventing the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Age of Fracture is the simplest to obtain, only requiring the player to finish the game, while all others demand completion of their respective side quests beforehand.
- The *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending has an additional bonus ending cutscene if Melina was not sacrificed as a maiden. It shows her finding the burned Spectral Steed Whistle in the ashen ground and stating that she will now follow through with her vow to kill The Tarnished with Destined Death for becoming the Lord of Frenzied Flame.
  - If Melina was sacrificed and The Tarnished became the Lord of Frenzied Flame afterward, the bonus cutscene would simply not play.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- An unused variant of the *Age of Order* ending was titled the *Age Absolute*.
- The *Age of Fracture* has an unused alternate introduction.
- Among the cut content surrounding Miquella the Kind, there was at one point an ending associated with him. Miquella would have offered his dew to the Tarnished and requested their share in his dream. He would have a world where "all things will flourish, whether graceful, or malign."  This may imply that this version of Miquella envisioned a world where even marginalized groups, such as Albinaurics and Misbegotten, would thrive.
  - The term "malign" in the English translation does not perfectly align with the Japanese text, which is translated literally as "not-so-graceful."
- The English dialogue for the *Age of the Stars* ending has been debated for its interpretative differences compared to the Japanese script. Some suggest that a more literal translation may provide additional clarity and preserve the nuances of the original text, as discussed here.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ensha of the Royal Remains** is an NPC in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Ensha is the unspeaking adherent of Sir Gideon Ofnir, typically found leaning on the wall outside his master's study in Roundtable Hold. Ensha wears armour graced with golden human bones, which are said to have belonged to a soulless king, the lord of the lost and desperate, known as Ensha.

After the Tarnished obtains one half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Ensha invades them in Roundtable Hold. After killing Ensha, the Tarnished confronts Gideon, who claims that Ensha got ahead of himself.  As an apology, Gideon furnishes the Tarnished with advice regarding the whereabouts of the medallion's other half.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Talk to him to receive the "What do you want?" Gesture.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - After retrieving the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) from Old Albus in the Village of the Albinaurics, or the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left)from Castle Sol, Ensha will invade the player. Upon death, he drops the Clinging Bone and his Royal Remains Set can then be collected from his original spot outside Gideon's room.
  - Afterwards, Gideon will have a new dialogue option **About Ensha** and, once exhausted, **About the secret medallions**.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Elder Lions**, also known as **Guardian Lions**, are non-respawning Enemies in Elden Ring and Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Elder Lions are beasts blessed with spiritually-infused horns by the primordial Crucible of life. Valued by the hornsent, lion pelts adorned the bodies of chosen Divine Beast Warriors who invoked divinity to perform tempestuous, cavorting lion dances. Serosh, Lord of Beasts—the hornless golden lion—later became Lord Godfrey's Regent, and symbolized the noble Golden Lineage.

Battered Elder Lions equipped with curved swords once engaged in gladiatorial combat at the colosseums, but the practice died out by the time of Lord Radagon. However, lions were later utilized by various military groups during the Shattering, some supporting lordsworn forces stationed at Leyndell, Redmane Castle, Stormveil, and Castle Sol. Starscourge Radahn, the Red Lion General, and his famed Redmanes practiced the Lion's Claw technique, a battle art that imitated the light-footedness of lions.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
A massive lion with a dark gray coat and fierce yellow eyes, its silvery-white mane decorated by broken horns. Two pairs of manacles are nailed cruelly into its forelimbs, and a curved blade fixed to the right serves as a prosthetic weapon. Bearing the scars of many battles, the chained beast moves with brutal grace, somersaulting forward to cleave its prey with precision.

Elder Lions patrolling Castle Sol can exhale a freezing fog.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
Elder Lions are often found in areas associated with the Banished Knights, Starscourge Radahn, and the Golden Lineage.
- Altus Plateau
- Castle Sol
- Fort Gael
- Leyndell, Royal Capital
- Redmane Castle
- Stormveil Castle
- Swamp of Aeonia: Southern shore

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Lion's Claw and Savage Lion's Claw techniques used by General Radahn and the Redmanes visibly emulate the movement of the Elder Lions' somersault strike.
- The Elder Lions have five claws, a celebrated symbol among the Beastmen of Farum Azula, who consider it a sign of the intelligence once bestowed on their kind.
- Golden lions symbolized the Golden Lineage of Elden Lord Godfrey and his Beast Regent, Serosh.
- The Divine Beast is represented by a horned lion.
  - Statues of horned lions line Belurat, Tower Settlement and Enir-Ilim.
  - The sculpted keepers of the tower wore lion pelts to invoke divinity. Enormous lions were used to create the Divine Beast Dancing Lion.
  - The ritual of the lion dance in particular was revered for its divinity, fury, and light-footed beauty.
- Leonine Misbegotten have the appearance of a lion and some imps wear lion masks.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Elder Lions are internally named "**OldLionOfArena**" (ID: 4270).
- There are disabled spawn markers for lions at the Colosseums. An elder lion would have battled a Grave Warden Duelist at the Royal Colosseum, a concept likely recycled for the Onestrike Warrior and Blinding Elder Lion encounters in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Evergaols** are a recurring type of location in the Lands Between.

Evergaols appear as a circle in the ground made of gray bricks. Interacting with the symbol at the center will allow you to enter the Evergaol where you will have to fight its inhabitant in a 1-on-1 duel. Once entered, you may not exit an Evergaol without either dying or defeating the boss within.

Ordina, Liturgical Town is an exception, as it uses the Evergaol mechanic for the area's puzzle, rather than the Evergaol containing a boss.

With the exception of summoning Blaidd the Half-Wolf inside of the Forlorn Hound Evergaol, it's impossible to summon anyone, cooperator or Spirit Ash, inside of an Evergaol.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - "Gaol" is an older way to spell "jail." Evergaol is pronounced "everjail."

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Eternal Cities** are landmarks in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Eternal Cities of the Lands Between are buried deep underground. The city of Nokstella rests along the Ainsel River Main, while Nokron is perched on a plateau overlooking the Siofra River. These cities are inhabited by the Nox and their Silver Tears, or patrolled by scouting Fallen Hawks. An uninhabited, third nameless Eternal City lies in ruins below the  Prince of Death's Throne in the Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: List of Eternal Cities
sections.text:
- Noklateo, the Shrouded City
- Nokron, Eternal City
  - Siofra Aqueduct
- Nokstella, Eternal City
- The Nameless Eternal City

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
]]

The Eternal Cities were built by the Nox, who were devoted to the starry night sky. These cities contained massive stone Chair-Crypts that seated giant maidens. The Nox used weapons forged from the liquid metal of Silver Tears, which could mimic other forms. They used these Mimic Tears in an attempt to create their own Lord.

Long ago, the Nox conspired against the Greater Will. They donned Nox Mirrorhelms to repel its light and used the Fingerslayer Blade to inflict a grievous wound upon a vassal of the Greater Will. As punishment for their blasphemy, they were banished deep underground. The Black Moon that hung over Nokstella was shattered into Memory Stones, and Astel, Naturalborn of the Void was unleashed upon one of their cities and it stole its false night sky. Although the nameless Eternal City was completely leveled, the others were left mostly intact. Although the efforts of the Nox all ended in failure, they continued to believe a Lord of Night would one day come to usher in an Age of the Stars.

Eternal City architecture also appears in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, Ordina, Liturgical Town, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and the Ainsel River Main.

sections.heading: Inhabitants
sections.text:
- The Eternal Cities were home to the Nox clergy, which included Nox Monks, Nox Swordstresses, and Night Maidens.
- Silver Tears are found throughout Nokron and Nokstella.
- The Fallen Hawks now wander Nokron and the Siofra Aqueduct.
- The Dragonkin Soldiers, who wielded ice lightning, were born in the Eternal Cities after they were sent underground.
- The Nox of the nameless Eternal City crafted Valiant Gargoyles with Corpse Wax.
- War Counselor Iji wears a Mirrorhelm, the description of which either implicates his involvement in the plot to use the Fingerslayer Blade or his knowledge of it and his blasphemous desire to use it for Ranni's plans.
- The nameless Eternal City is populated by Basilisks, Mausoleum Knights and Mausoleum Soldiers and Gargoyles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Many of the buildings constructed by the Nox, such as the Siofra Aqueduct, appear inverted, hanging like stalactites from the cavern ceiling. It is unclear whether these were built after their banishment.
  - The Carian Study Hall was built with a similar design.
- Eternal City ruins are strewn about the Ainsel River Main near Nokstella. This area is red with scarlet rot and prowled by a Baleful Shadow during Ranni the Witch's questline. An aqueduct drains water from the Ainsel into the stagnant lake.
- Sellia, Town of Sorcery was founded in Caelid. Many notable glintstone sorcerers came from Sellia, including Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, who went on to found the Olivinus conspectus at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. The Sellians were known assassins who utilized night sorceries to hunt their peers. The secret chair-crypt at this location is vacant.
- The Eternal Cities were likely buried after the ancient dynasty ended, as they are found surrounded by their underground ruins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Fire** is a Damage Type in Elden Ring.

This damage type has the additional property of removing fully applied Frostbite status, removing its debuffs.

sections.heading: Fighting Against Fire
sections.text:
- Flame Fortification/Flame, Protect Me, increases Fire damage negation by 35%/60% (10%/20% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user, lasting for 90 seconds/70 seconds. Flame, Protect Me, additionally grants the buff to nearby allies. Requires 10 and 24 Faith to cast.
- Protection of the Erdtree, increases Fire damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user and nearby allies for 70 seconds. Also increases Magic damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount. Requires 35 Faith to cast.
- Flamedrake Talisman/Flamedrake Talisman +1/Flamedrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Fire damage negation by 13%/17%/20% (4%/5%/6% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time.
- Pearldrake Talisman/Pearldrake Talisman +1/Pearldrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Fire damage negation by 5%/7%/9% (2%/3%/4% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time. Also increases Magic damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount.
- Fireproof Dried Liver, a consumable and Body Buff that increases Magic damage negation by 15% (10% in PvP). Lasts for 120 seconds.
- Pest's Glaive, a Halberd that increases Fire damage negation by 2%. Also increases Magic damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount. Only works if held in an active hand and does not stack with another Pest's Glaive.
- Being in rain or standing in a body of water increases Fire damage negation by 10% for both the Tarnished and their enemies. Also decreases Lightning damage negation by the same amount.

sections.heading: Fighting With Fire
sections.text:
- Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear, increases Fire damage dealt by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes when used with the Flask of Wondrous Physick.
- Fire Scorpion Charm, a Talisman that increases Magic damage dealt by 12% (8% in PvP) while increasing Physical damage taken by 10% (15% in PvP).
- Flame, Grant Me Strength, an Incantation and Body Buff that increases Fire (and Physical) damage by 20% (15% in PvP) and stamina recovery speed by 5/s for 30 seconds. Requires 15 Faith to cast.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Endurance** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Endurance stat directly affects their Stamina totals. Leveling Endurance will also increase the Tarnished's Robustness, which increases their resistance to Hemorrhage and Frostbite. Finally, Endurance also affects the Tarnished's possible Equip Load, increasing it as Endurance increases.

The Tarnished can level Endurance by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Endurance has three soft cap points for increasing Stamina, at 15, 30 and 50, with increases seeing dimishing returns after these points. Increasing Robustness sees two soft caps, 40 and 60, with gains from increasing Endurance not beginning until 31 Endurance. Increasing Equip Load sees soft caps at 25 and 60 Endurance.

sections.text:
;Directly
- Imp Head (Wolf), increases Endurance by 2.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Faith** (信仰, *Shinkō*) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Faith stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Faith scaling.

It's the stat primarily associated with Incantations, as well as with the Fire and Holy elements.

The Tarnished can level Faith by spending Runes at Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **FP** is one of the stats in Elden Ring. It represents the energy to use spells or skills. The Tarnished must have enough FP to cast a spell or to properly perform a weapon skill. It is represented by a blue square (  ).

sections.heading: Increasing FP
sections.text: The total FP can be increased by leveling the Mind attribute. However, the game applies soft caps beginning at level 15, 35 and 60. Soft caps modify the amount of points gained per attribute level up.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Equip Load** is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Equip Load affects their movement speed, and increases as the Tarnished equips more items in their equipment slots. It will also affect the amount of invincibility frames and recovery frames, with heavier equipped loads affecting them negatively. More specifically, Light Load rolls and Medium Load rolls are equally effective and have the same recovery time, but the former will roll a longer distance. Heavy Load rolls meanwhile face an almost twice as long recovery animation, leaving the Tarnished very vulnerable to follow-up attacks.

Equipped items totalling less than 30% of the maximum equip load is considered a Light Load. Greater than 30% and less than 70% is considered a Medium Load. Greater than 70% is considered a Heavy Load. The game menu will display the Tarnished's current load type directly under the numerical weight totals.

Exceeding 100% weight load will result in being Overloaded, rendering the Tarnished unable to roll or backstep, instead only staggering forward slightly with no benefit.

Equip Load exceeding 70% also increases the time it takes to recover Stamina as well and increases harm caused by fall damage.

The Tarnished can increase their maximum Equip Load by leveling Endurance. Equip Load experiences soft caps at 25 and 60 Endurance, resulting in diminishing returns as leveling increases past these points.

A Prophet has the lowest starting equip load due to its starting Endurance of 8, while the Samurai has the highest due to its Endurance being at 13.

While all other classes start in Medium Load thanks to their starting equipment, the Vagabond is the only class to start in Heavy Load due to its heavy equipment.

The scaling is strongest early on, around 1.5-1.6 per point of Endurance below 26 points in the Attribute before falling off from 26 to 38 Endurance before recovering and averaging 1.5 from 39 to 60 Endurance before falling down 1.0 Equip Load per point of Endurance above 61.

sections.text:

- Arsenal Charm, increases maximum Equip Load by 15%.
- Arsenal Charm +1, increases maximum Equip Load by 17%.
- Great-Jar's Arsenal, increases maximum Equip Load by 19%.
- Erdtree's Favor, increases maximum Equip Load by 5%.
- Erdtree's Favor +1, increases maximum Equip Load by 6.5%.
- Erdtree's Favor +2, increases maximum Equip Load by 8%.
- Winged Crystal Tear, increases maxiumum Equip Load by 450% for 3 minutes upon use if Flask of Wondrous Physick.

;Indirect (the two Radagon's talismans cannot be worn at the same time)
- Imp Head (Wolf), helm that increases Endurance by 2 levels with Equip Load affected accordingly.
- Hierodas Glintstone Crown, helm that increases Endurance by 2 levels while also increases Intelligence by 2 and lowering FP by 10%.
- Radagon's Scarseal, talisman that increases Endurance by 3 levels while also increasing Vigor, Strength, and Dexterity by 3 levels and increasing damage taken by 10%.
- Radagon's Soreseal, talisman that increases Endurance by 5 levels while also increasing Vigor, Strength, and Dexterity by 5 levels and increasing damage taken by 15%.
- Godrick's Great Rune, increase Endurance by 5 levels upon using a Rune Arc if equipped and until the Tarnished's next death, with Equip Load affected accordingly.
- Unique Skill: Oath of Vengeance, available on the Grafted Blade Greatsword, raises all Attributes (including Endurance) by 5 levels upon use for 60 seconds with Equip Load affected accordingly.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Finger Maiden Therolina** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Therolina is a Finger Maiden who never met the Tarnished she was meant to guide,  even though it was promised that the guidance of grace would ensure that the pair be brought together. At some point, she met her end at the hands of Preceptor Seluvis, being turned into one of his puppets. Her puppet will attend Radahn's Festival, presumably under the control of Selivus, to give a lending hand in felling the demigod. Before battling the demigod, Therolina's puppet can be spoken to, but only responds in a silent polite bow.

Upon delivering Seluvis's Potion to any of the potential targets for Selivus, and then discovering his secret chambers, the Tarnished can chose to receive Therolina's puppet as a gift, or purchase it for 2 Starlight Shards. She uses healing incantations and Holy Water Pots, but she is not a fighter by nature and is ill-suited to battle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Despite Therolina's puppet already attending the Radahn Festival, the protagonist can also summon their own separate version of Therolina's puppet if they received it from Selivus beforehand.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fallingstar Beast** is a reoccurring boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Fallingstar Beasts are creatures formed of shiny black rock. They have spiky tails, patches of white fur, and insect-like mandibles. They are found in craters, likely indicating that they plummeted onto the Lands Between from a great distance.

The more mature Full-Grown Fallingstar Beast have greater magical abilities, able to control gravity in their vicinity and unleash great magical beams akin to Comet Azur.

They can use Gravity-based abilities, much like other enemies associated with meteors and fallen stars such as Alabaster Lords, Onyx Lords, and Withered Astel. Much like those other enemies, they are also weak to gravity-based sorceries. Additionally, extraterrestrial weapons such as the Wing of Astel and the Alabaster Lord's Sword and gravity imbued weapons such as the Starscourge Greatsword and Radahn's Spear greatarrows deal bonus damage to these foes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Fallingstar Beast found in a crater in Altus Plateau, south of the steps leading to Capital Outskirts, and south-east of the Altus Highway Junction Site of Grace. The route leading to it is pockmarked with smaller craters, and there are several Starcallers and Leyndell Soldiers nearby.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Fallingstar Beast found in a cave at the end of Sellia Crystal Tunnel in Caelid.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A large Fallingstar Beast encountered in a crater on Mt. Gelmir, accessed via a ladder or a spirit spring near the Ninth Mt. Gelmir Campsite Site of Grace. It has a blue orb resembling an eye emerging from the fur on its face, reminiscent of the eye visible through the crack in Astel's skull.

It also has an additional phase when falling below half health, unleashing a lifting gravity wave in an area around itself and being able to shot sweeping beams of magic.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Found in *Shadow of the Erdtree* at the northmost part of the Finger Ruins of Dheo.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fire Monk** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Warrior-monks who reside in the Mountaintops of the Giants. During the War Against the Giants, the Fire Monks fought on behalf of the Erdtree. They devised "Flame, Protect Me", an incantation which shielded the champions of the Erdtree from the Giants' Flame. After the war had concluded, the flame of ruin was sealed away, and the Fire Monks were appointed to watch over it. They were led in this ordeal by the Fire Prelates, and in turn led the Guilty; exiled criminals who wielded thorn sorceries.

After many years, the Fire Monks succumbed to the allure of the flame of ruin, beguiled by it. Wielding fire-based incantations, the Fire Monks continued to keep watch over the flame, bearing the likeness of the fell god upon their chestplates.

At some point, the incantation "Flame of the Fell God", which had been kept secret by Chief Guardian Arghanthy, was stolen by a thief named Adan. Several Fire Monks travelled to Liurnia of the Lakes to seek him out, erecting camps in the lands on either side of the lake while they searched.

A Flame Monk named Amon fled his duty to watch over the Giants' Flame out of cowardice, instead swearing fealty to the god-slaying black flame. He was followed by others, enthralled by the black flame, who became known as Blackflame Monks.

sections.text: **Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A Tarnished sorcerer and scholar of the Academy of Raya Lucaria who engaged in nomadic study away from the Academy, donning the Hierodas Glintstone Crown. Wilhelm was a silent seeker who at one time made contact with the primeval current, and became one of the first Tarnished to visit Roundtable Hold. He befriended Vargram the Raging Wolf, however confrontation let them into violence, and Wilhelm was imprisoned in Roundtable Hold.

The Tarnished encounters Vargram and Wilhelm together in the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital, during a joint mission with Knight Bernahl on behalf of the Fortified Manor.

sections.text:

  - After joining the Volcano Manor and eliminating Old Knight Istvan and Rileigh the Idle under Tanith's request, talk to Recusant Bernahl in the eastern quarter of the manor to receive Letter to Bernhal, unlocking Wilhelm's invasion sign in Leyndell.
  - Once Wilhelm and Vargram, the Raging Wolf are defeated, awarding you with the Raging Wolf Set, return to Bernhal to receive Gelmir's Fury.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fallen Hawk Soldiers** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Fallen Hawks are company of slaves from Stormveil once ordered to explore the Eternal City. When the last of their embers had been used up, they resorted to burning the bones of their fellows for light. This led to them acquiring Ghostflame, but sealed their fates as dwellers of the underground rivers for eternity. An upside-down, perpetually falling hawk serves as their emblem.

The soldiers are pale and skeletal in appearance, lacking armour aside from a few who wear crude helmets. They are missing eyes, and their noses have worn away. They appear to have holes drilled into their heads. The soldiers wield a variety of armaments, including spears, swords, greatshields, heater shields, ghostflame torches, and bows that fire arrows tipped with ghostflame. Their methods are somewhat crude, yet they work well together as a squadron.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Headless Fallen Hawk Soldiers populate Noklateo, the Shrouded City and an area of the Great Hollow  in Elden Ring Nightreign.
- Several Silver Tears mimic Fallen Hawk Soldiers at Night's Sacred Ground.
- The Archer Ashes found in Nokstella imply that some Fallen Hawks also reached the other Eternal City.
- Due to the demoralizing name and imagery of their emblem, the Fallen Hawks were once the original members of Stormveil before the Storm Lord's defeat at the hands of Godfrey and the Golden Order's seizure of their castle.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
The **Elden Ring Closed Network Test** was a Demo intended to stress test Elden Ring's online matchmaking servers. This version of the game is also known to have some slightly different assets and code, which have been used by fans to show differences between planned content and the final release of the game.

sections.text: This page lists licensed adaptations of the Elden Ring universe.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: *Elden Ring* has many official adaptations, including manga, books, and other games. These derivative works are mainly commissioned by Kadokawa, which owned more than 60% of FromSoftware by 2024 and usually explore either the story or gameplay of the game. The manga tries to recreate the player's journey through the game, while Tabletop RPGs try to adapt their gameplay loop.

sections.heading: Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree
sections.text: *The Road to the Erdtree* is a comedic manga adaptation published digitally and in print. While the original work is in Japanese, it has also been translated into English, French, Italian, and Spanish.

sections.heading: Elden Ring: Become Lord
sections.text: *Elden Ring: Become Lord* was announced as a fully-colored Kadokawa's *Tatesc*, a Japanese webcomic format meant to be read by scrolling on a phone. The work promises a more serious tone and will be published both digitally and in print. Only the Japanese version was mentioned in the product announcement.

sections.heading: *See You at the Grace After Work*
sections.text: *See You at the Grace After Work* is a light novel that tells the story of two coworkers who get to know each other due to Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Elden Ring TRPG
sections.text: *Elden Ring: TRPG* is the official tabletop roleplaying adaptation of *Elden Ring*. At release, the three tomes were only planned to be released in Japanese and sold via Amazon Japan and Kadokawa Store.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Eochaid** was an unseen location mentioned in Elden Ring. Little is known of its people and customs.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Eochaid was a lesser foreign kingdom located outside the Lands Between. Its people were proud ascetics who practiced a distinct form of magic and lived solitary lives. By using copper as a conduit, those from Eochaid willed their blades to pirouette through the skies. The state of Eochaid and its people vanished long ago.

After the Shattering war subsided, a man in iron armor from Eochaid began amassing Bell Bearings, stalking numerous merchants and instructors and killing them with violent corkscrew attacks. When captured, the Bell Bearing Hunter’s crimes warranted the death sentence, and he was bound in winding, rusted iron thorns. Before his execution at The Shaded Castle, Elemer of the Briar seized the ceremonial copper Marais Executioner's Sword, furnishing it with battle skills from his homeland, and drove Castellan Maleigh Marais from the castle, claiming both for himself.

sections.heading: Characters from Eochaid
sections.text: - Elemer of the Briar, also known as the Bell Bearing Hunter

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- It can be inferred that the people of this land view companionship, collaboration and other benefits gained from social interactions as a form hedonistic indulgence that must be discarded in order to focus on the self and better pursue spiritual goals.
- The distinction between copper and rust was of importance to those from Eochaid.
- Likely associated with the Briars of Sin and guilty criminals

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **fallen ruins** are massive fragments of Crumbling Farum Azula, the ancient city in the sky.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The royal city of the Ancient Dragons travels across the sky in the storm beyond time. In prehistoric times, Farum Azula was destroyed when struck by a meteorite. In the many ages since, its ruins have crumbled and fallen down. These fragments are found embedded in the ground, littered throughout the Lands Between.

The ruins are broken pieces of a massive mausoleum enshrined around Dragonlord Placidusax. Many of these ruins contain the interred remains of the Beastmen.

The fallen ruins are primarily found throughout Limgrave and Liurnia of the Lakes. They are consistently surrounded by a decent quantity of Ruin Fragments and in rarer cases Sanctuary Stones.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The fallen ruins are made from solid stone. Only the outer layer has been worked.
- Many ruins are bleached white, while others feature faintly colored stones.
- During the night, Deathbirds spawn at certain fallen ruins.
- There are no fallen ruins in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **fell god**, also known as the **one-eyed god**, is a character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The nameless god of fire is the source of the Giants' Flame and Giants' Flame incantations. While this character is never officially labeled an outer god, it operates in much the same manner as one; however, it interferes with the Lands Between more directly. It is an ancient, malformed deity that was said to possess curled horns and thick braids of bright red hair. It has a single eye with a fiery-orange iris that swirled like an inferno. Surrounding its central pupil is a ring of eight smaller pupils.

It physically manifests as a grotesque visage on the torso of Fire Giants, channeling its immense power through them. Its great flames erupt from a gaping mouth on the host's stomach, unleashing destructive fire upon its enemies.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The fell god of fire has been around for a long time and predates the Erdtree. It was a malevolent figure in the old hornsent legends of Enir-Ilim. The Fire Giants were its followers, and tended the god's undying flames housed within the great black Forge anchored to the Flame Peak atop the Mountaintops of the Giants. Though it was feared, the sparks of its flame could fertilize even frozen lands, leading to the growth of half-ashen and smoldering flowers called Fire Blossoms.

The Fire Giants considered smithing a divine ritual, and even the Trolls, their descendants, wielded hammers as ceremonial tools for smithing, crafted with the same pattern of the fell god's eye. The connection of smithing to divinity dates back to the Forges of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, where Anvil Hammers were shaped like altars and used in ancient divine rituals.

The fell god was also considered evil by Queen Marika, as its Flames were capable of burning her Erdtree. Thus, she waged a bloody War Against the Giants for the sake of her new Age of the Erdtree. However, during this conflict her priests would be forced to use the very power they were fighting against to protect the champions of the Erdtree from the flames of the Fire Giants, creating the first incantation of the Fire Monks.

It is said that Queen Marika personally slew the fell god, but once the Fire Giants were defeated, she realized the flame of their forge could not die and thus sealed it away, reducing its once formidable fire into mere embers and cursing the last surviving Fire Giant to keep them so for all eternity. The power to fully burn the Erdtree was lost when the Rune of Death was sealed in Maliketh's Black Blade.

However, the fell god was not destroyed. Though dormant, it continued to lurk  within its subjects, on the cusp of being awakened at any moment with a sufficient sacrificial offering. The fell god's allure swayed even the Fire Monks that were tasked with keeping watch over the Flame.

sections.text:
; a concentric ring of eight dots surrounding a larger central dot]]

- It is unclear whether the fell god is one of the outer gods. Though the power of their flames can certainly be described as divine and they operates like one, it is never explicitly stated to be an outer god.
  - Erdtree prophets glimpsed its flame within their faith, implying this power currently exists within the Golden Order.
  - This can be explain by the fact that the forces of the Erdtree were forced to create incantations that channeled the flame of the fell god through faith to protect themselves from that power, thus integrating the laws of another god into the Order. This is something that, according to Sorcerer Rogier, the Golden Order of the past was already capable of doing.
  - In addition, the Erdtree was once as warm as the gentle sun, a power possibly related to those of the fell god
- It currently manifests as a grotesque face on the torsos of Fire Giants.
- In addition to the Fire Giants, the Fell God dwells within the Flame of the Fell God. This spell is a massive ball of fire,  not unlike a sun. This ability is most similar to the Messmer's Orb.
- The inhabitants of the Lands Between have produced a number of objects that invoke the fell god's image.
  - The Furnace Golems are colossal wickermen filled with burning bodies. Their faces are Furnace Visages—stone masks depicting the fell god as a bronze sun, with a mane of eight curled horns. It looms high above the Fire Giant faces attached to the golems' knees.
    - Its opens one or both eyes when taking damage or during certain attacks.
    - The sun medallion on the Dung Eater's Omen Armor resembles the Furnace Visage.
  - The leader of the Fire Monks, Chief Guardian Arghanthy, uses a One-Eyed Shield that expels flame from its mouth. The large swirl along below the barrel is flanked by eight smaller swirls.
  - The Fire Monk Armor portrays a cyclopian face on the torso in imitation of Fire Giants.
- The fell god is represented by a ring of eight small circles surrounding a larger central circle.
  - This pattern appears on the One-Eyed Shield, Furnace Visage, Verdigris Armor, and Verdigris Greaves.
  - This distinctive pattern appears on the Divine Towers, with some pillar reliefs featuring central cavities filled with glowing meteorite ore.
  - The Troll's Hammer, used by giants during an age when smithing held divine significance, also features eight circles orbiting a central circle.
  - The Verdigris Discus shares this pattern with the fell god's eye. Verdigris, believed to be a gift from an outer god, also appears on the talismans and great dish carried by the Fire Giant.
  - St. Trina's prophesied adult form shared many physical traits with the fell god.
- The fell god's red hair grows on its followers, such as the Fire Giants, Monks, and Prelates.
  - Radagon, Messmer, Rykard, Radahn, Ranni, Malenia, Millicent, and Millicent's Sisters all have the same red hair. Melina's hair is much more faded than the rest.
  - Red hair also appear on every single Fire Knight, those who had received inside them the flame of Messmer, who had visions of the Flame burning the Erdtree and the kindling inside him.
  - Radagon resented his own red hair, which was a curse of the giants.
  - Misbegotten, especially Misbegotten Warriors, have red hair and fur.
  - Red is a color strongly associated with life and the Crucible, and is the color of the horned Great Red Bears.
  - Red hair appears to seep from the severed Omen horns protruding from the Dung Eater's armor.  The only opening in the Omen Helm is a large crack near the right eye.
  - Although inaccessible through normal gameplay, the Dung Eater has faded red hair and is only character modeled to have a deformed facial appearance.
  - The blind Lamenter has horns, red hair, and a dormant face resting on its back. Though its blissful state was a true form of enlightment, the fearful horsent refused to accept it and foolishly buried it deep und

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In the Japanese localization for Burn, O Flame!, the Fire Giant is singular rather than plural, implying the fell god did not curse them prior to the War Against the Giants, rather it was the curse that Queen Marika the Eternal imposed on the last of their kind, as confirmed in the Remembrance of the Fire Giant's description.
- While the English localization claims that the Hornsent's sagas were "haunted" by the Fell God, the Japanese description simply claims it was "An evil god of fire of the legends of the horned people" (角人たちの伝承にある、火の悪神である). The Hornsent were aware of the Formless Mother and Shadow Undead at the Abandoned Ailing Village cast Swarm of Flies, an incantation associated with the Formless Mother, they used Rot for purification rituals through Romina, Saint of the Bud and kept Gravebirds inside Belurat and Enir-Ilim, golems crafted as kindreds to the Deathbirds. The god of fire being considered as "fell" (evil) could be attributed to Messmer's soldiers who built the Furnace Golem, as the people of Erdtree viewed all deities other than Marika negatively and had a tradition of addressing the deity as "fell" through multiple artifacts.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Dryleaf Dane** is an NPC in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Dane is a member of the Dryleaf Sect, an order of spiritual seekers who chose to serve a new god after seeing the decline of the Erdtree in the fallen leaves. Dane fights using an unarmed technique which focuses on kicks.

Dane is a compatriot of Needle Knight Leda, and has been in the service of Miquella even longer than she has. He seldom speaks, and even Leda has never heard his voice. The The Tarnished may challenge him to a duel in Scadu Altus, after which he will grant them access to Dryleaf Arts.

Dane discovers the sealing tree in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and deduces that it must be burnt using the flame of Messmer the Impaler. After it has been burnt, Dane joins Leda in Enir-Ilim, where they face off against the Tarnished. Upon his defeat he finally breaks his silence, offering a plea for Miquella to rise to godhood.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Dane's signature appears on the Ancient Ruins Cross Message and Monk's Missive. He also left a Message beneath a waterfall at Recluse's River.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Fire Knight's Shortsword** is a dagger melee armament found in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: 4% chance to be dropped by dual dagger-wielding Fire Knights.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Generally leans towards Dexterity-scaling over Strength-scaling.
- Despite the description this dagger actually has higher Faith-scaling and raw Attack Power (AP) on a Sacred affinity than on a Flame Art affinity. It's also outclassed in raw AP by a Flame Art affinity Erdsteel Dagger.
  - However, the Fire Knight's Shortsword's Flame Art affinity usually has higher effective damage than the Sacred affinity due to only having to bypass 2 flat defences rather than 3, and the Fire damage will be higher on its own than either the Sacred affinity's Holy damage or the Flame Art Erdsteel Dagger's Fire damage.
- Surprisingly enough, since this weapon is themed after Faith and Fire, it actually has the strongest Intelligence-scaling of all Daggers on the Magic and Cold affinities.
- Though the innate Fire damage is low on all but the Fire and Flame Art affinities, simply having it means it will immediate reset fully applied Frostbite on the next hit if on a Cold affinity or using Frostbite-causing skills such as Chilling Mist. It will also stun enemies that are extremely vulnerable to fire, such as Fingercreepers and Miranda Sprouts and Blossoms
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger.
  - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.
- If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats.
  - In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities was only held by the Clayman's Harpoon and the Erdsteel Dagger, while the DLC added the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, and Fire Knight's Greatsword, weapons which all have the same quality.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

This legacy dungeon is accessible after using Messmer's Kindling to burn the Sealing Tree at the  Church of the Bud in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Once unsealed, it can also be reached by climbing the ladder in the  Divine Beast Theatre.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Finger Readers** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The finger readers are oracles who interpret the words spoken by the Two Fingers in their language of light. By reading one's fingerprint to provide hints about quests yet to be undertaken.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The finger readers were oracles who interpreted the language of light spoken by the Two Fingers. They acted as mediums through whom the Fingers communicated the wisdom of the Greater Will.

They were said to live life eternal. However, many dead Finger Reader Crones can be found between the Erdtree Sanctuary and Queen's Bedchamber in Leyndell, Royal Capital, presumably having died of unnatural causes.  Those still alive may have served their Fingers at the Divine Towers, but since they are all dead, the crones have lost their purpose, which is why they desperately wish to read someone's fingers. The only named one is Enia, found in the Roundtable Hold, and she is the only one who is still interprets the words of her Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The finger readers are shriveled old hags who sit on chairs in a bizarre posture. They clutch staves adorned with bell bearings.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Fire Knight Queelign is an invader encountered at the graveyard in Belurat, Tower Settlement and at the Church of the Crusade. After both invasions have been thwarted, he may be found again as a friendly NPC at Shadow Keep, Church District.

Queelign is a Fire Knight who dreams of becoming a second Impaler after Messmer. Like his master, he eventually questions his blind faith in Marika.

sections.heading: Questline steps
sections.text:
1. Belurat, Tower Settlement or Church of the Crusade
  - Defeat Queelign's first invasion
1. Belurat, Tower Settlement or Church of the Crusade
  - Defeat Queelign's second invasion
1. Prayer Room of Shadow Keep's Church District
  - Exhaust dialogue and give either an Iris of Grace or an Iris of Occultation

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Electrocharge** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Fog Rift Catacombs
- Found by dropping down a hole in the second cubicle on the left at the third dropping spike-roof and then taking a left twice to find it in the same rooms as a Catacombs Sorcerer, some Fulgurbloom, and a few Skeletal Slimes.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Summons a lightning bolt down onto the user, damaging nearby enemies with Lightning Attack Power equal to 213% of Incantation Scaling.

For 45 seconds, the user is granted a Body Buff that has Lightning Attack Power equal to 45% of Incantation Scaling in a small area around the user every 1 second.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the initial bolt to 262% of Incantation Scaling and the Attack Power of the Body Buff's pulses to 59% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast. Cost is increased to 36 points of Stamina if charged.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the bolt by 23% and the Attack Power of the lingering effect by 31%, this leads to a total Attack Power increase of 41% and 51% respectively.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- The initial bolt deals surprisingly good damage, if only in a very small area around the user, while the buff deals minuscule amounts of damage.
  - While the damage over time is very small, it is still somewhat useful for things that only require any amount of damage without having to "waste" a hit, such as killing Skeletons before they can resurrect or breaking the damage-reducing bubble from Opaline Bubbletear or a Uplifting Aromatic (including the one used by Perfumers).
  - Annoyingly enough, this lingering damage effect will not prevent the Stance of any enemy from recovering.
  - The lingering damage effect from the Buff completely ignores Guarding, fully piercing through Guarded Damage Negation.
- Since this incantation grants a Body Buff, it will remove many strong defensive buffs such as Barrier of Gold and Fireproof Dried Liver. While there isn't a lot of overlap between these spells' uses (Electrocharge is more suited for use against many smaller enemies, while most defensive buffs are better against tougher foes), this is still a downside to trying to use the initial bolt offensively.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Fire Knights were an order of warriors who answered directly to Messmer the Impaler. Each knight descended from noble families of the Erdtree's high society but was exiled from their homes after pledging loyalty to Messmer. They alone understood their master's cursed serpent-like flames and the Base Serpent that consumed him.

Although they made use of their fire to commit atrocities and destruction in the crusade into the Realm of Shadow, they successfully convinced their lord to preserve the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and its artifacts. The Fire Knight would guard and manage the Storehouse inside the Shadow Keep where ancient specimens and relics were conserved and studied.

After the Elden Ring was shattered and its effects were felt in the Shadow Realm too, the Fire Knights would discover and use the Wrath from Afar incantation that replicated the golden shockwave feared as a sign of the Erdtree's wrath but still used the ancient sigil of the primordial Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Fire Knights are tall and lanky, with red hair like Messmer, and a trace of soot covering their otherwise unblemished faces.

They wear bright crimson pointed hoods and cloaks, with dark red underarmor. Their chestpieces are engraved with fingerprint-like whorls, while their black scale skirts are lined with gold. They wear braided cord aprons and cuts of rope, both depicting spirals. Their capes bear the emblem of Messmer's Army in gold, over which hangs a large coiled snake and three sets of triplet bells, fastened to the twin golden serpents forming a ring around their necks—symbolic of their bond to Messmer.

In battle, Fire Knights specialize in wielding fire for their master's cause. They fight with greatswords and shortswords, whose slender, spiraling blades undulate like flame. When not striking with steel, they rely on Messmer's Flame and Erdtree incantations, often channeling them through the sacred seal, which strengthens their pyromancies.

sections.text: **Fire Knight Wego**, or **elder Wego**, is an enemy character in Shadow of the Erdtree. He is a Fire Knight found in the Church District at the Shadow Keep and attacks using Messmer's Flame incantations. He does not respawn after being defeated.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Wego was a venerable leader among the Fire Knights who served directly under Messmer the Impaler. This order was known for their crimson cloaks and golden twin serpents coiled around their necks, symbols of their bond to their master. Like his juniors, old Wego understood Messmer's cursed, serpent-like flames and the torment that consumed him. Wego was once a member of one of the esteemed noble families of the Erdtree's high society but was exiled after pledging his loyalty to Messmer.

Wego’s helmet was unique, adorned with two death masks layered one upon the other. Following the Crusade, Wego turned to the spirituality of Messmer's flames to escape his growing loneliness. He performed rites to resurrect the dead, but the soulless beings he revived offered no comfort to his poor heart.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Greyoll is revered as the mother of many lesser dragons. She appears as a colossal, immobile dragon in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, just south of Fort Faroth.

Her body is bent with age, her scales are grey, and silver hairs grow from her jaw like a wizened beard. Though incapable of movement, she lets loose fearsome roars that damage nearby foes. Greyoll depends on her brood for protection and will perish if they are slain.

sections.heading: Locations

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- While the intended method of defeating her is by killing the surrounding lesser dragons, killing Greyoll herself directly through another method, such as Blood Loss, will also kill these smaller dragons.
  - This method will grant all  67,350 Runes at once, making this an excellent place to use a Gold-Pickled Fowl Foot for more Runes early on.

- Defeating Elder Dragon Greyoll unlocks Greyoll's Roar, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for three Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- While the English localization claims that Greyoll was the mother of "all" dragons, the Japanese description simply claims she was a "great mother of dragons" (竜の大母).
  - This same term, 大母, is also used for the Grandmother.
- Elder Dragon Greyoll was originally intended to be fought more directly. However, attempting to view this moveset results in heavy lag and slowdown which is presumably why it wasn't implemented.
- Greyoll was initially conceived as an Ancient Dragon, with her concept art depicting her as such and the Chinese CNT version of Greyoll's Roar describing her as an "ancient dragon" and a stony mountain. It's likely that this late-stage script revision is the reason she uses a scaled up drake model rather than having a unique design.

Revealed on December 12, 2024, the game was released on May 30, 2025, for , , , , and  via .

sections.heading: Plot
sections.text:
s approach the Night Lord]]
*Nightreign* takes place in the Lands Between on a timeline parallel to the events of *Elden Ring*, branching from the Shattering. The Night's Tide, an encroaching wall of violet flames and relentless rain, threatens the land of Limveld and its Roundtable Hold. A Priestess in a hooded white robe and silver mask urges the Nightfarers to unite and prevent an impending catastrophe. Players must survive two nights before facing the Nightlord beyond a door on a petrified tree.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
*Elden Ring Nightreign* delivers a fast-paced roguelike experience, playable solo, duo, or in groups of three.
 Players select one of eight unique classes and must survive two perilous nights in a procedurally generated world before confronting the Night Lord. The game combines cooperative survival with a shrinking safe zone, blending elements of *Elden Ring's* iconic design with new features to enhance replayability. The compact game world draws inspiration from *Elden Ring's* Limgrave and features randomized elements, such as structure layouts, enemy placements, and environmental modifiers. Special map events, including meteoric impacts, ant swarms, and volcanic eruptions, create dynamic scenarios. Sites of Grace and Runes return, allowing players to level up and gain abilities as they progress or fail. Additional mechanics, such as powerful ultimate abilities and new traversal options, expand gameplay possibilities. Players can summon a spectral bird to glide through the sky or scale walls by jumping.

Each of the three nights lasts approximately 10 to 15 minutes. Players begin each run at level 1, simplifying progression and encouraging quick engagement without build optimization. The Night's Tide shrinks the safe zone each night and recedes at dawn. Players caught in the rain take damage, and while daytime deaths allow respawning, nighttime deaths do not.

sections.heading: Key features
sections.text:
- **Offline solo or online co-op** - Join forces with up to two other players or venture solo with scaled difficulty.

- **Playable heroes** - Select from one of eight different characters, each with their own story, strengths, and weaknesses. Team composition and coordination will play a key role in determining success.

- **Fast-paced roguelike** - Inputs for movement and combat are more fluid and agile. Players run faster and may wall-jump, vault ledges, and glide around the game world.

- **Dynamic, compact world** - The game world is smaller and will reshuffle with each new run, randomizing locations and encounters.

- **Survive the night** - Each night culminates in a shrinking safe zone and a challenging, randomized boss fight, offering rare loot and selectable rewards.

- **Simplified inventory** - The inventory screens will be color-coded and streamlined, and most items will not persist between runs.

- **Near-Death** - Players are downed and can be revived after their HP drops to 0.

sections.heading: Playable characters
sections.text:

*Nightreign* will offer ten playable Nightfarers with unique abilities and impactful ultimates, each named for their character class. These classes are beginner-friendly and more easily defined, but their facial appearance may not be adjusted with the character slider. However, the armor of these characters may be customized with various cosmetics. Each hero has a custom storyline; characters that were not selected can be interacted with at the Roundtable Hold.

sections.heading: Bosses and enemies
sections.text:

The game will feature eight new bosses. Among the new additions is Gladius, a monstrous hound with three heads. Several enemies and bosses return from the original game, such as the Zamor Knights, Godrick Knights, and Demi-Human Swordsmen. Margit, the Fell Omen pursues players across the map and grants a powerful Favor of the Night buff if defeated. In addition, the Centipede Demon, The Duke's Dear Freja, and Nameless King return from *Dark Souls,* *Dark Souls II,* and *Dark Souls III*, respectively. All encounters are randomized, and defeated enemies are not reset upon resting at a Site of Grace. The Night Lord is selected at the Roundtable Hold before the start of each run.

sections.heading: Inventory changes
sections.text:
Items and gear are color-coded based on rarity. New items and weapons are available, including lootable skills, upgrades, and stat buffs. Rather than using a generic ball of light, these items are rendered as generic, glowing objects that indicate their item type.

The inventory screens are simplified, and up to three weapons can be equipped in each hand. Randomized passive bonuses from special weapons persist when the item is in the inventory. Weapon weight penalties and stat requirements are removed, but some items have level requirements. Basic loot is shared between players, but special item drops are not.

Items may be purchased from Nomadic Merchant spirits scattered around Limveld. They sit beside a campfire and a smithing anvil. Armaments may be improved with Smithing Stones at these workbenches.

Most items do not persist between runs. Murk can be used to purchase unlockable items that persist between runs, such as cosmetics, emotes, and build-defining Relics. Relics are also obtained at the end of each run, regardless of victory.

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.text: *Nightreign* is primarily designed for 3-player co-op, but offers single-player and two-player modes with reduced enemy scaling. The password system will return to handle private matchmaking. Multiplayer activities are no longer limited by in-game items or confined to a single area or dungeon. Players may communicate through a more robust gesture and ping system. Downed players are revived after taking enough damage from their teammates, but the game ends when all players are downed simultaneously. Unsuccessful runs will spawn Red Phantoms in the worlds of others that may be defeated for valuable loot. Basic loot is shared with teammates, but special boss loot is not. The game will not include player-versus-player (PvP) elements.

sections.heading: *The Forsaken Hollows*
sections.text: *Elden Ring Nightreign: The Forsaken Hollows* is a paid DLC expansion for *Nightreign* that launches on December 4, 2025. First revealed on November 11, 2025, it includes new Nightfarers, Nightlords, Expeditions, Enemies, and minor Bosses.

sections.heading: Development
sections.text: *Nightreign* is directed by Junya Ishizaki, a veteran of FromSoftware since *Dark Souls*. The game retains the franchise's hallmark epic battles while introducing a faster-paced combat system. The project was green-lit by Hidetaka Miyazaki, who gave creative control to Ishizaki. , who was heavily involved in the development of *Elden Ring*, did not provide additional contributions for *Nightreign*. The game was conceptualized while *Elden Ring* was still in development.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- *Nightreign* will be a standalone, premium-priced game; it will not be free-to-play. It does not require *Elden Ring* or Shadow of the Erdtree to be owned or installed. It is not a live service and will not feature a battlepass or microtransactions.
  - All planned DLC expansions are included with the Digital Deluxe edition.
- Cross-platform multiplayer will not be available.
- The game will not offer difficulty options.
- The Roundtable Hold is the pre-game lobby. It includes a training room, loadout customization, non-player characters, and a lore codex of characters and enemies.
  - Change heroes by interacting with the altar.
  - Start exploration by interacting with the Table of Lost Grace and selecting a target Night Lord.
- Up to six Relics may be equipped at once, and each grants a powerful bonus to attributes or damage from specific sources. Relics are placed on pedestals at the Roundtable.
- Players initially drop into the world at a location of their choosing on a Spectral Hawk. They can resummon their hawk gliders at special spirit trees.
- At the end of the second night, the players travel to the Spirit Shelter to confront the Night Lord.
- Leveling up is much faster and less restricted. Players need only be within proximity of a Site of Grace to access its menus and benefits. Leveling up is a guided and beginner-friendly process.
- Players can respawn freely during the day but receive debuffs.
- It can be expected that Sites of Grace outside the Ring of Reign are deactivated.
- Spiritsprings are replaced with Spiritstreams. Players may jump to great heights by jumping near vertical purple fissures.

sections.text: The **Duchess**, initially known as the **Priestess** (巫女, *Miko*), is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign. She is one of the ten available Nightfarer classes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Duchess allied with the Nightfarers at the Roundtable Hold to address the looming Night's Tide that threatened the land of Limveld. She urged them to work together to defeat the Night Lord.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A noble by bearing and appearance, the Duchess is a virtuous thief. She wears a fine tunic and leather attire, wielding a decorative shortsword with precision in her white-gloved hands. A silver mask obscures her youthful face, and her long blonde hair is neatly tied back in a low ponytail, reflecting her composed demeanor.

sections.heading: How to Unlock the Duchess
sections.text:
1. Meet the Priestess at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold.
1. Face a Nightlord in battle.
  - If the Nightlord is defeated, the Old Pocketwatch is acquired automatically.
  - If the Nightfarers are defeated, the Old Pocketwatch may drop as a random reward.
1. Speak with the Priestess at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold and select **Show her the old pocketwatch**.
1. Select **Give it to her** to unlock the Duchess as a playable character.

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.text:
Duchess is a Dexterity class that specializes in stealth and burst damage. She has poor defenses, but is highly agile and can dodge attacks with ease.

- **Passive Ability**: Magnificent Pose — *"Attack and dodge optimally, dodging repeatedly when necessary. Reduces stamina reduction from attacks and evasive actions. Allows up to two consecutive evasive actions."*

- **Character Skill**: Restage — *"Stage reprisal of recent occurrences to damage nearby foes. Damage to phantoms affects original. This skill can be used at any time."*
  - Duchess can re-inflict the last 5 seconds of damage and static effects dealt to all enemies in front of her. It will not double the riposte damage. And you may activate this ability during all animations, including being hit, but not in the downed state.

- **Ultimate Art**: Finale — *"Obscure self and surrounding allies to hide from foes. Enemies lose track of the caster, wandering aimlessly or becoming prone to leaving themselves vulnerable."*
  - Gives an instant 3-second window of i-frames followed by 15 seconds of invisibility to her and nearby allies. However, enemies will still attack an invisible player from the last spot they dealt damage to that enemy.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Duchess is locked by default. However, she will be present near the Table of Lost Grace at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold. She is the Priestess in the white hooded robe.

sections.heading: Part 1:
sections.text:
After accepting the remembrance quest from your journal, you'll need to **talk to the Raider** in the Roundtable hold, who will inform you that you should **speak to Wylder**.

Wylder can be found in the room past the Journal room. **Head back to the Raider** afterwards.

Go on any expedition and an objective will appear on the **southwestern** part of the map opposite of where you spawn.

Approach the area and prepare to fight a few opponents. We recommend killing a few enemies on the way to raise your level to make the fight more manageable. Three Guardians of the Dew will spawn and prevent you from obtaining the Golden Dew.  After that you will get Golden Dew.

**Speak to Wylder** and show him the Golden Dew, who will thank you.

**Return to the Raider** afterwards and he will task you to **speak to the Revenant** on the western side of the Roundtable.

Head on over to the Revenant and **speak with her**, who will then **direct you towards the Iron Menial** in the Visual Codex room. A ghostly spring will appear next to the Iron Menial after speaking with him. Interact with it to **conclude the remembrance** and you'll receive the **Golden Dew** as a reward.

sections.heading: Part 2:
sections.text:
After the remembrance quest starts, you will need to **look for Wylder**. He can be found slumped against the left wall by the Roundtable Hold. **Proceed to the dining room, exit through the hole and take a right** to find Wylder.

Choose to **eat from Wylder's Pita Bread**, and he will speak to you afterwards.

**Locate the Iron Menial,** he will be next to the dresser and talk to him regarding Wylder's Pita Bread.

After completing this objective, a ghostly spring will appear for you to conclude this remembrance episode. This will grant you **Duchess' Chalice** as a reward.

sections.heading: Part 3:
sections.text:
The Raider will be located in the dining room. **Speak with him** and he will inform you of Weathervane after telling him that you shouldn't fight the Nightlord. After that you need to go on the southeastern beach and speak with Revenant. You must now **defeat Revenant in a duel**. This fight is similar to Revenant's unlock quest, and can be treated the same way. You can also repeat this fight as many times as needed if you die.

After go on any expedition with your Remembrance active and an objective will appear on the **northeastern** part of the map. Approach the area and three Fallen Mercenaries will spawn and prevent you from obtaining Weathervane's Words. Claim the item after defeating them.

**Speak to Raider** and show him Weathervane's Words, who will then give you the agency to choose your own path. A ghostly spring will appear next to the Raider. Interact with it to **conclude the remembrance** and you'll receive the **Crown Medal** as a reward.

sections.heading: Part 4:
sections.text:
When the Remembrance starts, it is time to bless the Iron Coin at the table of lost grace. Walk up and **interact with the table**.

Head on over to the Iron Menial and **give him the Blessed Iron Coin**. You can find him in the catacombs and can be accessed by going down the stairs from the Visual Codex room, then taking a u-turn left to another set of stairs.

**Speak to the Wylder** afterwards. He can be located by the fireplace near the outfit wardrobe.

**Return to the Iron Menial** to complete the Remembrance. A ghostly spring should appear next to the Iron Menial to conclude it after.

You will receive both **Duchess' Remembrance Outfit** and the **Blessed Iron Coin** as a reward.

sections.text: The **Eclipse** is a recurring event mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The sun in eclipse was a dreadful, mesmerizing sight. Drained of its color, it was a bulwark against Destined Death and held the power to imbue life into soulless bones. The symbol of Castle Sol and the Wandering Mausoleums, its image offered a star's protection to the slumbering soulless Demigods.

The knights of Sol fervently prayed for it to appear, hoping the dreadful event would call a spirit into the soulless demigod interred with their mausoleum. They planned to return the life of the demigod on behalf of Miquella the Kind. However, it never came to pass.

- The sun is typically depicted with eight, ten, or sixteen points.
- The Eclipse emblem is available as a tattoo. It shows the color dripping from the sun in a way that resembles a sunflower.
- Castle Sol holds a Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
- "Drained of color" is also used to describe Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones.
- The eclipsed sun is possibly synonymous with the polar star depicted on the Black Leather Shield.
- An eclipse likely occured in the past, possibly giving rise to the soulless king Ensha.
- The failure of the eclipse plan may have been a consequence of the Starscourge Conflict, when Starscourge Radahn halted the movement of the stars. It is also possible the revival was prevented by the Prince of Death setting the colorless eclipsed sun ablaze with his flames, spreading Death in the process.
  - Miquella finds a different way to summon the soul of Radahn into Mohg's body at the Gate of Divinity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fierce Demi-Humans** are enemies in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Demi-Humans are typically small in stature and bestial in appearance, often possessing fur, canine faces, and pointed ears. Although they are intelligent and capable of speech, as exemplified by Boc the Seamster, they are typically violent and brutish, particularly at night when their blood boils and they turn feral.

Demi-Humans wield a variety of weapons, such as falchions, daggers, and clubs. Those considered to be the toughest wield spiked clubs, which they believe to be a badge of honor.

Demi-Human society appears to be hierarchical, with the lesser Demi-Humans following much larger Demi-Human Chiefs. Demi-Humans lose hope if their leader dies, causing them to panic and stop attacking. At the top of the Demi-Human hierarchy are the Queens, who are capable of wielding rudimentary sorceries via their staves.

Despite their violent demeanour, Demi-Humans are capable of fostering diplomatic relations with humans, with Kenneth Haight building an alliance with a group of Demi-Humans in Fort Haight.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text: Larger, more bestial Demi-Humans that serve as leaders of their smaller brethren. Fierce Demi-Human walk on all four legs, and carry bloodstained daggers in each of their front paws. They strap large horns to their tattooed bodies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- If one is killed, any nearby demi-humans are demoralized and stop fighting.
- The duo boss variant encountered in the Coastal Cave are both called Demi-Human Chief.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Elden Throne** is a Site of Grace located within the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Elden Throne is the seat of the Elden Lord, the highest power in the Lands Between. It is a small court with a number of wood thrones on a platform connected to the Erdtree's entrance. These seats were once filled by the Demigods before their alliance crumbled in the wake of the Shattering. Only Morgott remains faithful to Queen Marika the Eternal.

The Elden Throne Site of Grace is unlocked after the boss has been defeated.

After Morgott is defeated, his curse if lifted and he reverts to an enfeebled human form. He reveals that the Erdtree's Impenetrable Thorns block the way inside, preventing even he from rising as Elden Lord.

Melina appears at the Site of Grace to offer a new quest: journey to the Forge of the Giants and use the Giants' Flame to ignite the Erdtree.

After the first cardinal sin has been committed, the area transforms into Leyndell, Ashen Capital. The Elden Throne Site of Grace is once again locked until Hoarah Loux, Warrior is defeated. The impenetrable thorns will be burned away, allowing access to the Stone Platform.
