sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: is a concept referring to one's immutable, predetermined **destiny** in the world of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Flashes of light portended the futures of those who dwelled in the Lands Between. Fate emitted by distant stars was glimpsed and studied by astrologers on the Mountaintops; pale-blue starlight determined the fate of common men while Amber Starlight commanded the fate of gods, or so it was believed. The spirits of those who died in battle followed red lamplight through the spirit world to the Helphen, while the blue light of Usher of Death, Rosus, guided Those Lost in Death to the catacombs.

During the age of the Erdtree, the Golden Order fettered and suppressed the fate cradled in the night sky.  Destiny was instead prescribed by the Guidance of Grace originated from Queen Marika, her Erdtree, and the Elden Ring. Grace manifested as golden rays of light, steering Marika's faithful toward their purpose. Later, Starscourge Radahn, mightiest hero of the Demigods, confronted the falling stars alone, and crushed them; the Starscourge Conflict sealed the very fate of the stars. His actions held his sister Ranni's Empyrean path in stasis, forestalling the meteor that shall strike near the Mistwood and open a path to lost Nokron, Eternal City.

sections.heading: Fates
sections.text:
- Destined Death is fated Death, particularly that of the Demigods.
- The Tarnished is destined to rise as the Elden Lord, as the one chosen by Torrent will break the Golden Order in search of the Elden Ring. Melina offers them this accord.
- Blaidd the Half-Wolf defied his fate by swearing an oath to Ranni the Witch, imbuing his sword with cold frost magic.
- The Cardinal Sin is the fated burning of the Erdtree. A Finger Maiden is destined to become the kindling maiden, sacrificed to awaken the dormant Giants' Flame.
- Malenia is fated to become a true Goddess of Scarlet Rot upon her third and final bloom.
- Melina is fated to become the kindling maiden or gain the Rune of Death to destroy the Lord of Frenzied Flame.
- Messmer the Impaler is fated to become the Base Serpent
- Millicent is fated to blossom into a scarlet valkyrie.
- Miquella the Kind's fate was St. Trina.
- Demi-Human Swordmaster Onze glimpsed the ruinous fate at the end of the Primeval Current.
- The blood-drenched Fingerslayer Blade only works in the hands of one who has been prescribed a special fate. It is proof of high treason committed by Eternal Cities against a vassal of the Greater Will, presumably Metyr, Mother of Fingers, long ago.
- Ranni the Witch slew her own Empyrean flesh to escape the path set by her Two Fingers, later wielding the Fingerslayer Blade against them beneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
- Sorceress Sellen cannot die while Starscourge Radahn holds the stars in stasis.
- According to Count Ymir, the stars will guide the fate of the one who rings the hanging bells found at Finger Ruins. The Hole-Laden Necklace is the same color as Starlight Shards.
- Pidia, Carian Servant references his poor lot in life by labeling himself "ill-starred." He sells the map which marks the Amber Starlight at St. Trina's Hideaway.
- Lightseeker Hyetta and other would-be Finger Maidens of the Three Fingers feel a distant light guiding them towards their duty at the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
- Traitorous Straghess's thirst for vengeance was such that it formed legs and stood of its own accord, becoming the Dreglord.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Bone-Like Stones of the outer god of Night hold the power to alter fate.
- Finger Reader Crones can foresee fate by studying fingers.
- After the followers of Sir Gideon Ofnir raided the Village of the Albinaurics, Elder Albinaurics prayed to the stars, night, and fate to punish every living thing.
- The would-be Finger Maidens of the Three Fingers feel a distant light guiding them towards their duty at the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
- The Eternal Cities used Starlight Shards to produce puppets.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Godfrey, First Elden Lord narrated a cut version of the opening sequence. He knew the Shattering would transpire and summon the Tarnished back to the Lands Between. He directed the Tarnished to cross the Sea of Fog and claim the Elden Ring, the arbiter of fate.
- The link between thread and destiny derives from the  (also known as the ), the goddesses of fate in Greek mythology. The Three Sisters subregion is a reference to this motif.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ensha**, also known as the **soulless king**, was a character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
King Ensha was a soulless champion with golden bones who claimed lordship over the Lands Between in ancient times. He was regarded as a hero to Those Lost in Death, who were always in desperate need of leadership. He held such masterful control over life energies that a single punch rendered his foes unconscious, stealing their vitality. His royal remains were likewise graced with potent restorative power, and so they were forged into armor.

The king's bones were later acquired by Ensha of the Royal Remains, the unspeaking associate of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Ensha's golden royal remains are set in bronze armor and decorated with crimson, cerulean, gold, and viridian gemstones, including a prominent red jewel on his forehead. His faded hair is worn in a ponytail and melted candlewax covers the besagew affixed to his right pauldron.

His golden bones are similar to Blessed Bone Shards, human bones imbued with the gold of the Scadutree—a blessing said to be the greatest honor that could be granted to the dead. Like the royal remains, these golden bones possessed healing properties similar to sunlight.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.text:
This list is conjectural based on common traits:

- Gold Skeleton Bandit
- Gold Skeleton Executioner
- Gold Skeleton Grave Warden
- Gold Skeleton Knight
- Gold Skeleton Militiamen

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Most information about Lord Ensha is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.
- Lord Ensha appears to be from an earlier batch of Those Who Live in Death, possibly granted life during an Eclipse.
- The Gold Skeletons that arise from graveyards on the Altus Plateau may have been followers of Ensha in the past.
  - Gold Skeletal Knights were Sun Realm warriors who wore red cloaks depicting a bright sun.
  - The Altus Bloom may also be related to Ensha.
- The crimson jewel on his forehead mirrors the red gem atop Helphen's Steeple, which is acquired from a Tibia Mariner outside Castle Sol.
- Ensha of the Royal Remains ambushes the player to obtain one half of the  Haligtree Secret Medallion, which is required to reach Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. Its counterpart lies in Castle Sol.
- He may be connected to the soulless Prince of Death, who can be reborn as the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince to usher in the age of the Duskborn.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Erdtree Burial** is part of the central religion in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Erdtree Burial is a process by which Death returns to the Erdtree, performed in catacombs throughout the Lands Between. It was an honor reserved for heroes, as a proper death meant returning to the Erdtree. The remains of such champions were laid to rest in Hero's Graves constructed around the Greattree roots, which were once linked to those of the Erdtree. Some heroes, abundantly blessed by the Erdtree, simply died upon receiving their honors. Statues of Rosus, Usher of Death guided lost souls on their journey back to the roots.

Many different measures were taken to protect the Erdtree burial. Various stone golems, including Imps and Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, were used to deter grave robbers. Following the banishment of Lord Godfrey and his Tarnished, champions were driven from the colosseums and assigned as Grave Warden Duelists.

On the Night of Black Knives, a stolen fragment of the Rune of Death was used to slay Godwyn the Golden, the first demigod to die. As a hero, Godwyn was buried in the Deeproot Depths beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital, overlooking the Nameless Eternal City. Although his soul perished, his body did not, and his Erdtree burial enabled the Rune of Death to spread through the great tree roots, manifesting as Deathroot across the Lands Between. Deathroot corrupted the catacombs and gave rise to Those Who Live in Death, who defied the Erdtree’s call to return. At some point, either before or after the Shattering, the connection between the Erdtree and the Greattree roots was severed.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Executor is a former Crucible Knight who originally came from the Land of Reeds.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Executor is a condemned Crucible warrior who wields a cursed katana. He is a Nightfarer tasked with defeating the Night Lord to avert an impending tragedy in the land of Limveld.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text: Stats displayed below are for character at level 15.

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.text: Executor has a deflection system reminiscent of the Deflecting Hardtear and *Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice*. Performing successful deflects will imbue the sword with gold, enabling a special attack.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.text: - Tenacity — "Receive boost while recovering from status ailments. Effects boosts attack and stamina recovery speed"

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.text: - Cursed Blade — "Draw a cursed sword that can deflect enemy attacks. Repeated deflections reveal blade, enabling powerful attacks with the living sword. Cannot run while at ready with enchanted blade."

sections.heading: Ultimate Art
sections.text: - Aspects of the Crucible: Beast — "Assume the form of the primordial beast. Use unique attacks in beast form that drain the Ultimate Art gauge. Activate again to quickly undo transformation."

sections.heading: Starting Equipment
sections.text:
- The Executor starts each run with Executor's Blade and may switch to the Suncatcher at any time.
- The Executor prefers Katanas.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Expeditions** are the core gameplay loop in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Expeditions are deadly, three-day missions into Limveld undertaken by the Nightfarers of the Shrouded Roundtable Hold. They brave the ruinous Night's Tide to grow in strength for two days before challenging the Nightlord boss on the final day.

Matchmaking for Expeditions is initiated by interacting with the Table of Lost Grace at the Roundtable Hold. Select at least one Expedition and hit confirm. Each Expedition features a different Nightlord and is randomly generated using an individualized pool of encounters. For example, the Nameless King boss never appears during the Tricephalos Expedition.

Shifting Earth and other Events like Catalysms affect the runs.

sections.heading: List of Expeditions
sections.text: There are **eight** standard Expeditions:

sections.heading: Expedition Flowchart
sections.text:
1. **Day One: Noontide** — Nightfarers enter Limveld via Spectral Hawk; Night's Tide later restricts safe space
1. **Day One: Night** — Nightfarers are confined to a small area, fight a wave of tough enemies, and face a Night boss
1. **Day Two: Noontide** — Night's Tide fully recedes and the Nightfarers resume farming; random events occur
1. **Day Two: Night** — Nightfarers battle a second round of Night enemies and bosses before entering the Spirit Shelter
1. **Final Day: Noontide** — Nightfarers prepare for the final battle, and enter the tree
1. **Final Day: Night** — Nightfarers confront the Nightlord

sections.heading: Leveling Up
sections.text:
Nightfarers start every Expedition at Level 1. They can grow up to Level 15 by spending  runes at Sites of Grace. Runes are earned by defeating enemies and bosses or by completing various objectives. Lower-level players cannot adequately wield higher rarity gear.

When a player dies, they are demoted a single Level and their Runes are dropped where they died. However, the deducted Level is not permanently lost; it is converted to Runes and added to the drop. If a player dies near a non-boss enemy, then that enemy will glow gold near its belly. It returns the Runes once it is defeated, even by other players or NPCs.

The Plague of Locusts raid event summons mobile insect swarms that temporarily steal Levels. The Sentient Pest is located somewhere in Limveld and can be tracked by observing where the insects fly after an explosion. The Sentient Pest is passive and doesn't attack. All stolen Levels are returned, and a boon that randomly adds  runes on hit is granted if the Pest is slain. However, the stolen Levels are permanently lost if the raid is not completed.

sections.heading: Deep of Night
sections.text: The **Deep of Night**, also known as the **Deep Night**, is a ranked game mode for Elden Ring Nightreign included in an update that launches on September 11, 2025. It offers a challenge to veteran Nightfarers who have braved the Night many times.

sections.heading: Key Features
sections.text:
- **Ranked, high-difficulty challenge mode**
- Progress through 'Depths' levels 1 through 5, each rank increasing difficulty
- 'Depths' 4 and 5 function as an "endless mode"
- Ratings fluctuate according to wins and losses; reaching a certain rank will increase your Depth
- Fully-randomized Nightlords
- Fully-randomized Shifting Earth events
- Stronger, tankier 'Red' Enemies and Bosses, identified by veiny red visual effects, that drop potent
- When the mode is unlocked, every Chalice for each Nightfarer gains three extra Relic slots (a total of six per vessel) dedicated to special Depths Relics.
- **Depths Relics**: powerful relics touched by the Deep of Night that only activate in the Deep of Night game mode. They provide both positive and negative effects.

sections.text:
An Empyrean's eye is a vessel of profound grace and proof of their divine lineage. Queen Marika sometimes sealed the eyes of her Demigod children.

<section begin="Everdark"/>Everdark Sovereigns are challenging versions of the standard Expeditions, available for a limited time on a weekly rotation. The Everdark Sovereigns in active weekly rotation are Tricephalos, Gaping Jaw, Sentient Pest, Augur, Equilibrious Beast, Darkdrift Knight, and Fissure in the Fog. Additional Everdark Sovereign Expeditions are scheduled to appear in future updates. This feature is not available in offline mode.

The Nightlord bosses of Everdark Sovereign missions are significantly more difficult, featuring upgraded strength and new movesets. They start at Phase 2 and advance to an empowered Phase 3. Defeating an Everdark Sovereign grants  Sovereign Sigils, with a bonus for first-time victories. Sigils can be exchanged for exclusive Relics and other rare items at the Collector Signboard.<section end="Everdark"/>

This page provides an overview of the **endings** to Elden Ring Nightreign. There are **four** ways to conclude the game: *The Dawn*, *The Endless Night*, *The New Night*, and *The Night of Love*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Just like in *Elden Ring*, the player decides the fate of the Lands Between upon completing the game. There are three secret endings tied to specific Nightfarers, unlocked after progressing their Remembrance Quests.

The endgame sequence plays every time the Nightfarers clear the Night Aspect Expedition by defeating Heolstor the Nightlord, claiming the Primordial Nightlord's Rune. The Night recedes, revealing a memory version of the Roundtable Hold where the Primordial Nightlord sits shriveled and inert.

sections.heading: The Dawn
sections.text:
This is the default ending, available to all Nightfarers. The player returns to the Roundtable Hold and offers the Primordial Nightlord's Rune to a shriveled corpse, causing the rune to disintegrate. Soon after, all Nightfarers dissolve into Grace and scatter to return to their true bodies.

The Night is undone, and the Lands Between are restored to their natural state, with the Erdtree reappearing. A colossal giant is also animated by the Grace of Gold. This entity resembles an enormous Heolstor formed of wood and covered in fingerprints. Upon rising, the giant surveys the Lands Between, refuses the call of Grace, and departs into the sea.

sections.heading: The Endless Night
sections.text:
This is the Ironeye’s secret ending. Upon completing all of his Remembrance quests and defeating Heolstor, Ironeye returns to the Roundtable Hold and confronts the shriveled corpse. Rather than offer the Primordial Nightlord's Rune to dispel the Night, he slays the corpse, thereby condemning the Lands Between to eternal darkness.

Following this act, cold ghostflame manifests within Ironeye’s right eye.

sections.heading: The New Night
sections.text: This is the Wylder’s secret ending. Upon completing all of his Remembrance quests and defeating Heolstor, Wylder uses the Silver Tear to rebirth into Heolstor’s body. He becomes the new Nightlord and perpetuates the Cycle of Night.

sections.heading: The Night of Love
sections.text:
This is Recluse’s ending. Upon completing all of her Remembrance quests and defeating Heolstor, Recluse returns to the Roundtable Hold. There she hears the cries of an infant. Rather than approach the shriveled corpse, she follows the sound to the bed quarters where she discovers the Infant. She takes the child into her arms as the game ends, leaving the final outcome uncertain.

After the end of Expedition summary, the Witch of the Wheel offers her thanks where the Infant was embraced.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The hidden Wylder ending requires the Silver Tear to be equipped to the active Chalice.
- The Witch of the Wheel post-game interaction cannot be repeated.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Unlike in Elden Ring, players have only four options (and not six) to conclude the game in *Elden Ring Nightreign*.

sections.text:
**FromSoftware **is a Japanese video game development company. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, founded in November 1986. It is best known for creating the Dark Souls series, Bloodborne, and Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are currently developing Elden Ring.

In April 2014, Kadokawa Corporation announced that it wanted to purchase the company from Transcosmos. The deal was finalized in May 2014. In December 2015, FromSoftware was nominated for developer of the year at The Game Awards 2015, but lost to CD Projekt Red.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **George Raymond Richard Martin **also known as **GRRM **is a American best-selling author and television producer. One of his most popular works is the book series "A Song of Ice and Fire", which has been adapted into television in the hit HBO series "Game of Thrones". Martin says that he always loved writing stories, and wrote many unfinished ones.

sections.heading: Elden Ring
sections.text:
Game director Hidetaka Miyazaki has explained how the collaboration with Martin came to be:
 "I loved *A Song of Ice and Fire* as well as the *Tuf Voyaging* series, however if I had to pick a favorite I would probably say *Fevre Dream*. I personally see *Fevre Dream* as a masterpiece among vampire fantasy and had even previously recommended it to all new employees. Me being such a known fan of Mr. Martin caused our executive business director Eiichi Nakajima to reach out to him with the expectation that we would get turned down."

As George Martin recants:
 A few years back, Hidetaka Miyazaki and his incredible team of game designers, the creators of the DARK SOULS videogame series, reached out from Japan to ask me to help them create the backstory and history for a new game they were working on. Now, video games are not really my thing [...] but this offer was too exciting to refuse. Miyazaki and his team from FromSoftware were doing groundbreaking stuff with gorgeous art...

Miyazaki:
 [...] we were then given the rare opportunity to talk one-on-one with Mr. Martin which was an incredibly fun and stimulating experience. It was then that I strongly felt that I wanted to work with Mr. Martin.
 I am still unable to put into words how grateful I am to Mr. Martin for agreeing to our offer.

 Mr. Martin respected the fact that we didn't want him to write the game's story or the in-game text. Because we felt that would actually limit his creative output, [...] and then it would limit the inspirations we could possibly get from him.

 So we established very early that he would be writing that foundation, that historical element to the game, something that took place long before the events of the game itself.

GMMR:
 What they wanted from me was just a bit of worldbuilding: a deep, dark, resonant world to serve as a foundation for the game they planned to create. And as it happens, I love creating worlds and writing imaginary history.

Miyazaki:
 The actual collaboration itself begun with Mr. Martin ever so politely confirming what sorts of themes, ideas as well as many game-related aspects I had envisioned for the game.

 We started off by giving him these very vague and broad themes and ideas for the mythos that I had swimming around in my head. [...] Then he would come back to us with a lot of ideas: how about this, this, and this?

 This allowed us to have many free and creative conversations regarding the game, in which Mr. Martin later used as a base to write the overarching mythos for the game world itself.

GMMR:
 So I did my bit, and handed off to my new friends in Japan, and they took it from there.

Miyazaki:
 [The mythos I received] was nothing visual - they were all text. Rather than being a short story, it was something that depicted the setting or set the scene for the game and for the world, detailing the flow of history and the figures who appeared throughout it.

 These dramatic and heroic characters weren't really in our previous titles, so this was something that was really appealing to me - how he would depict the mystique and heroic qualities of those characters.

 There was, of course a story that came with this as a sort of backbone, but it played as more of an introduction to that world and a natural course of events for these characters to follow. [...] And then we were able to interpret this in our own way and provide visual to go along with that.

In response to questions about the project, Martin said, “Building the world of Elden Ring with Miyazaki-san and his team was a treat! The graphics, mythos, and action-RPG gameplay will deliver an unforgettable experience. I can’t wait for people to see what Elden Ring has in store for them.”

After the game's release Martin blogged:
 " Take a look at a few of the reviews:
 [...]

 “Once in a generation… masterpiece… beautiful and brutal… a sumptuous open world… ”

 Music to the ears.

 Of course, almost all the credit should go to Hidetaka Miyazaki and his aston

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Fringefolk Hero's Grave** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This Hero's Grave is located in Limgrave, connected to the underground Stranded Graveyard. It is locked behind a fog gate, but is accessible after expending two Stonesword Keys to open the seal. This sprawling tomb houses the remains of fringefolk who fought valiantly for the Erdtree and earned the heroic honor of Erdtree burial. Though it is primarily guarded by the spirits of Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights, its main walkways are tracks for a Merciless Chariot. Additionally, a pair of Grafted Scions lurk near the Erdtree's Favor talisman. The Erdtree burial chamber contains the ashes of Banished Knight Oleg and is protected by an Ulcerated Tree Spirit.

sections.heading: Stranded Graveyard
sections.text: The Fringefolk Hero's Grave does not contain a dedicated site of grace. The nearest is the  **Stranded Graveyard** site of grace, which is found at the entrance to the dungeon. It is between the Stranded Graveyard and the lift to Limgrave.

sections.text: **Flask of Crimson Tears** is a refillable tool in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Obtained after reaching the Stranded Graveyard at the start of the game.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
- Restores between 250 (at +0) and 810 (at +12) HP when used.
- Maximum charges are replenished after resting at a Sites of Grace.
- A charge can be expended to revive Torrent if he is killed.
  - Torrent will be revived with half-health.
- Maximum charges can be increased using a Golden Seed at a Site of Grace. The number of seeds needed for each level increases as you progress.
- The potency of the flask can be permanently increased by expending Sacred Tears at a Site of Grace.
  - The potency of the flask can be temporarily increased even further by equipping the following items:
    - Crimson Tear Scarab (+10%)
    - Guardian Garb (Full Bloom) (+10%)
    - Crimson Seed Talisman/Crimson Seed Talisman +1 Shadow of the Erdtree (+20%/+30%)
- Charges can be allocated between this flask and the Flask of Cerulean Tears at a Site of Grace.

sections.text: **Fulgurbloom** is a crafting material in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Fulgurbloom grows abundantly in spots where lightning strikes regularly. These spots can be found in every major area.
  - The earliest accessible spot of 14 Fulgurbloom is in Limgrave, on the hill just north of the Agheel Lake North site of grace.
  - In Weeping Peninsula a group of 8 can be found east from the MInor Erdtree in a small ravine accessible via Tombstones embedded in the side of the cliff.
  - In Altus Plateau, the largest collection, with 3 groups, can be found near the Rampartside Path site of grace, east of the Sainted Hero's Grave. Head west from the Grace for the first group of 10 and then head south for the second group of 8. Go northeast to get up on the hill just south of the Grace itself for the third group of 10. Be aware that Ancient Dragon Lansseax spawns very close to the route.
  - In Liurnia of the Lakes, directly northeast from the Island Testu's Rise is located on a group of 14 can be found.
  - In Caelid, more specifically Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, a group of 10 can be found along the way between the Minor Erdtree and the Farum Greatbridge.
  - At Castle Sol in Mountaintops of the Giants, the largest collection of two groups can be found. Just west of the Castle Sol Main Gate site of grace first a group of 13 and the of 15 is located.
  - In Consecrated Snowfield, east from the Ordina, Liturgical Town site of grace up the hill in the most north-eastern part of the area a group of 27 can be found around a rock pillar formation.
- Also dropped by certain lightning-infused enemies found in Altus Plateau and Leyndell, Royal Capital. Specifically Lightning Sheep (20%), and lightning pot-throwing Imps (10%) and Leyndell Soldiers (5%).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Ellac Greatbridge** is a location within the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A massive stone bridge spans the Ellac River in northern Gravesite Plain. The Ellac Greatbridge lies southeast of Castle Ensis, beside the Run-Down Traveler's Rest. It can be reached from the  Three-Path Cross site of grace by traveling north toward the withered willow tree, then following the road northeast.

The bridge is reinforced with barricades and scattered rubble, but its layout is straightforward. Proceed across until you reach the central span, occupied by Messmer Soldiers and lined with impaled corpses. Two nearby bodies can be looted for Ballista Bolt and Lost Ashes of War. At the far end stands a stationary Heavy Ballista loaded with Explosive Greatbolts. Sprint directly toward the siege weapon, dodging its shots, and defeat the Messmer Foot Soldier operating it. Once the threat is neutralized, return to the midpoint to collect any remaining loot. Proceed across the bridge to reach the  Castle Front site of grace, where Messmer's army established a camp.

sections.text: ***Elphael Needle Statues***, also referred to as ***Veiled Needle Statues*** and other names in the community, are objects in Elden Ring. All information about the statues and the unseen character they depict is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Statues of a shrouded figure clinging to a great needle are prominently featured throughout Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, often flanked by Candletree candlestands.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The identity of the Elphael Needle Statue is unknown due to its heavy shroud, though it might be Miquella and St. Trina due to their shared attributes and context. However, the statues may represent someone older than the Empyrean.
- A mural of the Needle Statue aiding Those Lost in Death may link the shrouded figure to the Suppressing Pillar in the Gravesite Plain. It can also represent an end to the Shattering.
- The figure appears on various set dressings, like folding screens and coffins.
- Needle statues lay on stone caskets for those that were buried closer to the core of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Gatekeeper Gostoc** is an NPC and merchant in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Gostoc is a servant working in Stormveil Castle, in the role of gatekeeper. Gostoc detests his master, Godrick the Grafted, who always looked down on and mistreated him. Gostoc prowls the castle, looting from the corpses of the Tarnished who die in their hunt for Godrick. When he encounters the Tarnished, he offers to signal the gates to open for them, but also suggests a hidden path around the outer wall of the castle which will allow the Tarnished to get in undetected.

However, Gostoc secretly planned for the Tarnished to die, so that he could loot their corpse. He stalks the Tarnished through the castle, stealing their left behind Runes any time they die. He also locks them in a storeroom with a Banished Knight, seemingly intending for them to perish.

After the Tarnished slays Godrick, Gostoc can be found stomping on his corpse, cursing him for the abuse levelled at him. Later, when Nepheli Loux becomes lord of Limgrave, Gostoc quickly becomes her attendant, giving him free reign to continue looting as he pleases.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Stormveil Castle
  - Gostoc can be found in the gatehouse to the left of the main gate. He will offer you the choice of taking the main gate or using the side entrance. Choosing "No, I'll use the main entrance" will cause the main gate to open when you approach it. This will not prevent you from taking the side entrance, however.
1. Stormveil Castle
  - *(Optional)* Upon entering a dark room in the western section of the castle, Gostoc will close the door, locking you in with a Banished Knight enemy. To leave, grab the Rusty Key and return to the door to open it. If you die in this room, you can return to it and loot the item without being locked in again.
  - *(Optional)* Gostoc will now appear in several locations around the dungeon. Speaking to him in one of these locations for the first time will reward you with a Grace Mimic. The locations are as follows:
    - Stormveil Cliffside. He will appear on a ledge above the Site of Grace, only if you enter the castle via the wooden scaffold and head straight back.
    - Western Wall ground floor. He will appear here after you have gone up the ladder past the door unlocked with the Rusty Key.
    - Chapel roof. He will appear on the roof of the chapel where you meet Rogier, after visiting the roof with the Grafted Scion and returning.
    - Rampart Tower. He will appear in the elevator tower, on a wooden platform that needs to be jumped to.
  - While he is in any of these locations, he will take 30% of the Runes you drop if you die in the dungeon. In order to get him to stop, talk to him at any one of the first three listed locations, and then at the fourth location. Then, return to his location at the gatehouse and talk to him again. He will no longer steal any Runes.
  - Additionally, he will become available as a merchant if you return to him after he begins stalking you.
1. Stormveil Castle (Godrick's arena)
  - After defeating Godrick the Grafted, Gostoc will appear in the room. After exhausting his dialogue his shop will be open once again. He will also stop stealing your Runes if you skipped the previous part.
1. Stormveil Castle (Throne Room)
  - After completing Nepheli Loux's questline, Gostoc will appear in the back of the throne room. After exhausting his dialogue, his shop will become available again, now with an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone available to purchase.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Cut dialogue suggests Gostoc was to be revealed a son of Godrick and, by extension, the Golden Lineage.
- Much of his questline and content was cut from the game. He was able to compete with Nepheli Loux for lordship of Stormveil Castle after Godricks defeat. He would succumb to the process of grafting himself, however.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Flame Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  3,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Flame Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Fire damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  20 FP per cast.
- Costs  13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces fire damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *FlameFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
<math>TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {FireDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {FlameFortification}) )</math>
  - For example, if fire damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
<math>TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
<math>TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%</math>

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as fire damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple fire negation sources.
- Flame Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
- This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Fire damage in the game, especially against dragons, fire monks, and Radahn soldiers, as well as while exploring Mt. Gelmir.
- Flame Fortification offers greater fire protection than Fireproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
  - The Fireproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.
  - Fireproof Pickled Liver

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Fling a small ball of fire with Fire Attack Power equal to 202% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 255% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  11 points of FP to cast.
- Costs  22 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 29 points.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 5 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 9.25.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 26%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of 45%.
- Although this spell utilizes the Giants' Flame, its power is not boosted by the Giant's Seal.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- An easy to use spell with very early availability that'll provide very good damage throughout the game.
  - Doesn't hold up as well late game since more damaging spells such as Giantsflame Take Thee and Black Flame (especially the latter's maximum HP-based bonus burn damage) will be more useful when FP isn't as precious and kill speed becomes more important.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Like Catch Flame and Fire's Deadly Sin, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.
- 
- Flame Sling was formerly known as "**Feast Upon Flame**" during the Closed Network Test.
- Similar to the Fireball spell from the *Dark Souls* franchise.
- Patch 1.07: Increased attack power when charged.
  - The Attack Power of the charged version was increased from 240% of Incantation Scaling to 255% of the same.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Gestures ** are expressive animated player emotes in Elden Ring. There are 47 gestures in total, 12 of them are automatically received on the start of every new character and 35 are obtainable throughout the journey, however many of them are missable and can be left unobtainable until the next playthrough.

sections.heading: Gesture Types
sections.text:
There are overall three different kinds of gestures in Elden Ring, they are defined by how they influence the player's movement.
- Gestures that allow the player to walk while performing them.
- Gestures that lock the player in place until the animation is complete.
- Gestures that lock the player in place and can last for as long as they want until the player performs an action.

Some gestures my also hide the player's equipped weapons until the animation is complete while others won't.

sections.heading: Motion-Controlled Gesturing
sections.text:
On the Playstation versions of the game, players can perform gestures without opening up the menu through the use of motion controls, by simply holding the *Triangle* button and physically moving the controller in the designated directions. Which gestures are performed are dependent on which slot the players have put their gestures in.

This feature can be a double-edged sword though as players may accidentally trigger a gesture at inconvenient times due them trying to adjust their sitting position while at the same time trying to interact with the environment like doors and ladders, or if they want to use items equipped in their Pouch at potentially dire times like Flask of Crimson Tears. To avoid this problem players can simply unequip the gestures in the slots that are tied to the most common forms of movements.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The following Gestures are used to complete puzzles:
  - Erudition: As this gesture is used to clear the Converted Fringe Tower puzzle, missing it automatically makes the player lose out on it's reward of Gavel of Haima and Cannon of Haima. And while it is also used for the Converted Tower puzzle, that one can alternatively still be cleared with some platforming.
  - Extreme Repentance: Successfully performing the gesture mid-fight while physically close enough to Patches will make him forgive you and stop attacking. Failing to perform this gesture and dying to him will also automatically make him forgive you by the next time you talk to him.
  - O Mother: Use near the Marika statue in Shadow Keep to unlock the Hinterland section of Scaduview.
- Golden Order Totality cannot be substitute for Law of Regression to solve the statue puzzle at Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Many Gestures were carried over from *Dark Souls III*.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Game Version  **1.03** was released on March 17th, 2022 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This patch is notable for fixing several unfinished or broken NPC questlines.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.text:
We are distributing an update to improve the stability of gameplay and to adjust balance.

We apologize for the inconvenience, but please apply the latest update before you enjoy the game.

Targeted platforms:

- PlayStation 4
- PlayStation 5
- Xbox One
- Xbox Series X|S
- Steam

The version number of this update shown at the lower right corner of the Title Screen will be as follows:

- App Ver. 1.03
- Regulation Ver. 1.03.1

sections.heading: Changes
sections.text: Major Changes Included in the Latest Update

sections.heading: Additional Elements Added
sections.text:
- Added a function to record an icon and the name of an NPC on the map when you encounter that NPC.
- Added NPC Jar-Bairn.
- Added new quest phases for the following NPCs: Diallos / Nepheli Loux / Kenneth Haight / Gatekeeper Gostoc.
- Added some summonable NPCs in multiple situations
- Increased the number of patterns of objects player can imitate when using Mimic’s Veil.
- Added night background music for some open field area.

sections.heading: Balance Changes
sections.text:
- Increased the drop rate of Smithing Stone for some enemies.
- Added Smithing Stone to some early game shop line up.
- Increased shield’s effectiveness.
- Increased the damage for all offensive cracked pot items.
- Increased the damage for the following items: Spark Aromatic / Poison Spraymist.
- Increased the effect duration for the following items: Uplifting Aromatic / Ironjar Aromatic.
- Increased HP healing for Torrent when using the following items: Rowa Raisin / Sweet Raisin / Frozen Raisin
- Reduced FP consumption and increased the damage of the following sorceries: Glintstone Cometshard / Comet / Night Comet
- Increased the damage of the following sorceries: Gravity Well / Collapsing Stars / Crystal Barrage
- Decreased FP consumption of the following sorceries: Star Shower / Rock Blaster / Gavel of Haima / Founding Rain of Stars / Stars of Ruin / Greatblade Phalanx / Magic Downpour / Loretta’s Greatbow / Loretta’s Mastery / Carian Greatsword / Carian Piercer / Shard Spiral
- Raised projectile speed and range of Great Glintstone Shard
- Decreased Ash of War: Hoarfrost Stomp's damage and increase cast time.
- Increased Ash of War: Bloody Slash's self-inflict damage while slightly lowering the damage and increasing the cast time.
- Decreased weapon skill, Sword of Night and Flame’s damage.
- Increased FP consumption and lower duration of Ash of War: Barricade Shield.
- Changed FP consumption timing of Ash of War: Prelate’s Charge.
- Decreased the damage of spirit summoned when using the item Mimic Tear Ash and changed the spirit’s behavior pattern.
- Other enemy and weapon balance changes

sections.heading: Bug Fixed
sections.text:
- Fixed a bug that prevented summoned NPCs from taking damage in some boss battles.
- Fixed a bug that sometime prevented the player from obtaining item after boss battle.
- Fixed a bug that causes dialogue to be skipped when talking to NPCs and using custom key configurations.
- Fixed a bug that causes the player to freeze when riding.
- Fixed a bug that causes arcane to scale incorrectly for some weapons.
- In situation where the player cannot obtain more than 2 talisman pouches, added talisman pouch to Twin Maiden Husks shop line up.
- Fixed a bug that prevented the user from warping to sites of grace from the map at the end of the game.
- Fixed a bug that prevented the player from moving to the next area after the battle with the Fire Giant.
- Fixed a bug which causes some weapons to have incorrect scaling after strengthening.
- Fixed a bug which causes some weapons to not use stat scaling.
- Fixed hang-ups in certain occasions.
- Fixed a bug which incorrectly displays multiplayer area boundary when playing online.
- Fixed a bug that allows player to activate Erdtree Greatshield’s weapon skill without absorbing an attack using a special combination of item and incantation.
- Fixed a bug which causes Fire’s Deadly Sin incantation to have different effect.
- Fixed a bug with the Ash of War: Determination and Royal Knight's Resolve, where the damage buff will also apply to other weapons without that skill.
- Adjusted the visual effect of Unseen Form spell.
- Deleted the Ragged armor set from the game which was mistakenly obtainable in previous patch.
- Fixed a bug that causes some hostile NPCs to drop Furlcalling Finger Remedy.
- Fixed a bug that causes incorrect sound effect to play in some situations.
- Fixed a bug which causes visual animation and hitboxes to not be displayed correctly on some maps.
- Fixed bugs which causes incorrect visual and behavior for some enemies.
- Fixed a bug that causes incorrect stat parameter for some armor.
- Text fixes.
- Other performance improvement and bug fixes.

sections.heading: Closing Paragraph
sections.text:
The version number of this update shown at the lower right corner of the Title Screen will be as follows:

- App Ver. 1.03
- Regulation Ver. 1.03.1

**Online play requires the player to apply this update.**

We will continue to provide improvement update in the future so you can enjoy "ELDEN RING" more comfortably. Please stay tune for more news.

sections.text: **Flame of the Fell God** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Giants' Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

**Guaranteed Drop**: Liurnia of the Lakes
- Received upon defeating Adan, Thief of Fire, the boss trapped in the Malefactor's Evergaol.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Summons a raging fireball that deals Fire Attack Power equal to 415% of Incantation Scaling and explodes upon impact with a 3.5 meter radius, leaving lingering fire spots for 7 seconds that appear to be able to hit about once per second with Fire Attack Power equal to 35% of Incantation Scaling and a 1 meter effect radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  34 FP per cast.
- Costs  42 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 2 Memory Slots to equip.
- The projectile is quite large but travels slowly.
- Upon detonation, the spell applies a knockback effect to targets.
- The explosion deals 16 Stance damage, while each tick from the fire spots deals 1 Stance damage.
- Only one Flame of the Fell God can be active per player at a time. Casting a new one will remove the previous fireball, but lingering hazard spots will persist even after a new flame is cast.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- This spell is highly effective against Erdtree Avatars, as they are weak to Fire and rarely reposition during combat.
- The damage of the lingering fire spots is usually reduced to insignificance by an enemy's flat defense. However, their consistent Stance damage can prevent an enemy's Stance from regenerating for up to 7 seconds.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Update 1.07:
  - The FP cost was reduced from 42 to 34.
  - Increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - The stamina attack power of the explosion was increased from 190 to 360 (450 against players).
  - The stamina attack power of the residual flame hazard was increased from 20 to 40 (50 against players). Additionally, their hit frequency was increased to approximately once per second.
- Update 1.04:
  - The FP cost was reduced from 50 to 42.
  - The explosion damage of the fireball was increased from 352% to 415% of Incantation Scaling.

- The fell god was said to have been defeated by Queen Marika the Eternal before the Age of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Alleviates buildup of the Poison and Scarlet Rot status effects and cures Frostbite, Poison, and Scarlet Rot.

Deals 15 HP damage to the caster.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  14 FP per cast.
- Costs  10 Stamina per cast.

sections.heading: Strategies

- This incantation is considered vital for navigating swamp areas filled with Poison and Scarlet Rot.
  - This is especially true for Scarlet Rot areas as other means of removing it is either in limited supply (Preserving Boluses) or only get one use without resting at a Site of Grace again (Speckled Hardtear).
  - While technically only the Prophet and Confessor origins have enough Faith to use this incantation by default, it can still be used by any starting Origin's at base Faith by using the Two Fingers Heirloom (a Prisoner will need another point in Faith, easiest gained with either Marika's Scarseal or a Commoner's Garb or Commoner's Simple Garb).
  - All Origins also start with enough FP to cast this incantation at least 3 times without using a Flask of Cerulean Tears, provided they haven't used any FP for anything too expensive.

  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Flings 12 balls of fire each with Fire Attack Power equal to 115% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 140% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  16 FP per cast.
- Costs  40 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 52 points.
  - Technically the Stamina cost is 10 points for the uncharged version and 13 for the charged version, but the cost is taken 4 times.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 4 Stance damage per hit (12 at most). Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 6 (18 at most).
- The initial fireball will split into 12 after traveling a short distance.
- At most 3 of the small fireballs can damage a single target. This limits the effective maximum Attack Power of this spell towards a singlet target to roughtly 345% of Incantation Scaling, or 420% of the same when charged.
- When charged, the fireballs will explode on impact to deal area-of-effect (AoE) damage.
- Inflicts additional Stamina damage to blocking targets.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- Godfrey Icon increases the Attack Power of charged attacks by 15%.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 22%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of ??%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Each fireball deals individual damage, and hitting with multiple fireballs can greatly increase damage output.
- This spell is highly effective against large targets, as most or all fireballs can hit, and works well for groups due to its solid AoE damage, low FP cost, and quick casting.
- At close range, only the initial fireball may hit before splitting, so midrange is ideal for landing multiple hits.
- The wide spread and AoE of the fireballs can catch evasive enemies, making it useful against invaders or invisible Teardrop Scarabs.

sections.heading: Trivia

    - Against players the Stamina Attack Power was increased from 25 to 42 per hit for the uncharged version and from 34 to 52 per hit for the charged version.
- Update 1.04: Decreased the damage of single cast and improved the performance so that it hits the enemy multiple times. Decreased FP cost.
  - The Attack Power of the uncharged version was reduced from 245% of Incantation Scaling to 115% of the same, and the Attack Power of the charged version from 286% of Incantation Scaling to 140% of the same.

sections.text: **Flame, Protect Me** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Fire Monk incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot**: Mountaintops of the Giants
- Flame, Protect Me can be found in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave in the Mountaintops of the Giants. It is located behind an imp statue fog wall right next to the dungeon's grace. One Stonesword Key is required to access it.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Flame, Protect Me applies a Body Buff that increases Fire Damage Negation by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  30 FP per cast.
- Costs  20 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.

- This incantation reduces damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total Fire damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *FlameProtect* represents the PvE/PvP effect multiplier:
- : <math>TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {FireDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {FlameProtect}) )</math>
  - For example, if Fire damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 70%:
  - : <math>TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.60) ) = 70%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 40%:
  - : <math>TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.20) ) = 40%</math>

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text: - Old Lord's Talisman extends the duration from 70 to 91 seconds.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Acquired very late, most often after every significant Fire-heavy area and boss except for Mountaintops of the Giants itself and the Fire Giant, and perhaps Dragonlord Placidusax.
  - If doing the Volcano Manor questline to access Praetor Rykard, then he can be fought after acquiring this incantation since the last assassination also takes place in Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave
- This is the only improved elemental defense buff that doesn't also apply to nearby allies.
  - The only way to also buff nearby allies with Fire Damage Negation is Protection of the Erdtree, which also increases Holy, Lightning, and Magic Damage Negation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - This incantation is one of the oldest known techniques among the Fire Monks.

sections.text: **Fortissax's Lightning Spear** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Trade the Remembrance of the Lichdragon, gained by defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, with Finger Reader Enia.
- Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Calls on two red, crackling spears from above that is then slammed into the ground, hitting with Lightning Attack Power equal to 367% of Incantation Scaling in a small 0.2 meter radius, and creating a shockwave with a 3 meter radius that hits with Lightning Attack Power equal to 288% of Incantation Scaling.

From the point of impact, waves of red lightning are sent out directly ahead and behind, and to the left and right of the caster with Lightning Attack Power equal to 122% of Incantation Scaling in a 2 meter radius from the center of each wave.

The second spear is slammed down as the first spear's waves are spreading, repeating the process but with the power of the direct hit increasing to 374% of Incantation Scaling, the shockwave hit to 292% of the same, and the wave hit to 123% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 42 points of Stamina.
- Deals 16.8 Stance damage on a direct or shockwave hit and 5 Stance damage on a wave hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- The "direct" hit and the initial area attack cannot hit the same target, though the smaller, weakest waves can hit an enemy that has already been hit if they are either quick or large enough to also be where those are.
- The "spears" are actually flung downwards, meaning they can be used to hit the ground beneath a cliff if the caster is standing on its edge.
- Has a much longer casting time than Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear due to having two spears, but each hit is stronger.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - FP cost was reduced from 45 to 35.
  - Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 100 to 140 on the direct hit with the first spear and from 120 to 160 with the second spear.
    - Separate Stamina Attack Power values for guarding players: for the first spear the direct hit was increased from 140 to 175, the shockwave hit was increased from 100 to 125, and the wave hit was increased from 60 to 75, while for the second spear the direct hit was increased from 160 to 200, the shockwave hit was increased from 120 to 150, and the wave hit was increased from 60 to 75.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost, increased cast speed and decreased recovery time, and allows caster to withstand enemy attack while casting more easily.
  - FP cost was reduced from 65 to 45.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Giantsflame Take Thee** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Giants' Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  13,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Giant's Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Hurls a massive ball of fire with Fire Attack Power equal to 325% of Incantation Scaling and that explodes on impact, hurting enemies within a 2.5 meter radius.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 389% of Incantation Scaling and the explosion radius to 3.5 meters.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  3 FP per cast.
- Costs  34 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 44 points.
- Requires 2 Memory Slots.
- Deals 13.635 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 15.
- Applies a substantial knockback against medium-sized enemies.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
- Very strong thanks to its raw damage and large explosion radius.
- Has a somewhat inefficient FP-to-damage ratio, meaning that something weaker but more efficient such as Black Flame or Flame Sling might be more useful against durable lone targets such as Bosses. Especially if the caster has a more moderate FP bar.
  - Black Flame's maximum HP-based damage can especially make it more efficient.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07: Decreased FP consumption.
  - FP consumption was reduced from 32 to 30.
- Patch 1.04: Decreased Stamina Cost.

sections.heading: See also

- Flame of the Fell God
- Flame Sling
- O, Flame!

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The swords hover around you until something hostile approaches close to melee range, at which point they shoot forward to each do a single hit. Rather inefficient for general PvE, but can be very dangerous in an Invasion; a melee invader would be at great risk approaching you to attack while this is in effect.

- Duration of the blades appears indefinite including through Grace site rests (but not site warps), until the blades fire at an enemy or you accidentally run them into a wall or ceiling.

- Cannot be used simultaneously with Carian Phalanx, Greatblade Phalanx, or Ash of War: Glintblade Phalanx.

- It is one of the Carian Blade Sorceries, a subset of the Carian Sorceries.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Glintstone Breath** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Caelid
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of blue flames, dealing Magic damage equal to 159% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e. 477% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast, and another 40 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Smarag's Glintstone Breath.
- Compared to Smarag's Glintstone Breath, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 30% less FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 104 FP: 2*28 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 53 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the strongest "default" dragon breath attack, though as it only does 10% more damage than Dragonfire, if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation is lower than its Magic Damage Negation that will change.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

- Dragonice, a weaker version of this spell that also inflicts Frostbite
- Rotten Breath, a weaker Standard damage of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot
- Smarag's Glintstone Breath, a stronger but more expensive version of this spell

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Glintstone Kris** is a Dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- Cannot be buffed.

sections.heading: Skill
sections.text:
- Unique Skill: Glintstone Dart

  - Compared to Skill: Glintstone Pebble, an uncharged Glintstone Dart has 13% higher base damage on the projectile and the charged version has 39% more base damage. This is on top of the Dart having roughly 6% stronger scaling for the bullet.
  - The follow-up attack is a bit closer: the Dart's has a higher damage multiplier and goes further, but the Pebble's has somewhat better tracking and adds some base Magic damage to the hit.
- The follow-up thrust deals 30 Stance damage, which outperforms a standard dagger charged heavy attack (18 Stance damage).
- The skill is chargeable and thus benefits from the Godfrey Icon.
  - Note that this is only the projectile part. The follow-up thrust is not chargeable.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Raya Lucaria Grand Library
- Received if siding with Sorceress Sellen against Castellan Jerren in Academy of Raya Lucaria near the end of her questline.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The ancient ritual referenced by the design of the kris might be that involving the Primal Glintstone Blade, used by ancient sorcerers to slice open their hearts and imbue a primal glintstone with their soul.
- Embedded with blue glintstone and blue-green glintstone.
- Uses a variant dagger moveset with a special thrusting heavy attack, shared with the Main-gauche, the Miséricorde, and the Scorpion's Stinger.
- Essentially a Dagger with Magic affinity and a chargeable variant of the Glintstone Pebble skill, though it had a much lower critical multiplier.
- Receives the greatest Attack Power (AP) on a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence build with an even split.
  - A pure Intelligence build could also be used to gain about 10% more damage on the projectile part of the skill at the cost of a 5% decrease in AP and of damage on the follow-up stab. This also focuses the dagger's regular damage more on Magic damage.

sections.text: The **Formless Mother** (姿なき母, *Sugata-naki Haha*), also known as **Mother of Truth** (真実の母, *Shinjitsu no Haha*), is an Outer God in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Formless Mother was encountered by Mohg deep underground. She is known to crave wounds, and to bestow power upon accursed blood. Her body can be pierced using Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear, causing the weapon to become coated in Bloodflame, or an arm can be thrust into her body in order to scatter Bloodflame on the ground, using the incantation Bloodboon.

The mother of truth offered the residents of Prospect Town salvation and transformed them into bloodfiends.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Formless Mother is omnipresent and can be stabbed from anywhere in the Lands Between by using a ritual spear.
- Although never directly stated, many details point to the Land of Reeds being under the influence of the Formless Mother. Descriptions of Reedlanders as having "succumbed to a blood-soaked madness" and their clear favoritism for weapons that cause Blood Loss all point towards the work of the Outer God. The magical enhancement granded by the forbidden Reedlander combat technique, Seppuku, may very well be a blessing from the Formless Mother, with the technique acting as a form of offering. Additionally, both Okina and Eleonora join Mohg's Bloody Fingers.
- The entity responsible for the Thorn Sorceries, Briars of Punishment and Briars of Sin, referred to as the blood star, the may have some connection to the Formless Mother. It is entirely possible due to their perceived values of spilling blood and inflicting wounds, that the Formless Mother and "the blood star", could be one in the same.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The Mother's designation as "Formless" resembles the title of a Great One (conceptually similar to an Outer God) that is indirectly featured in the FromSoftware game *Bloodborne*, called "Formless Oedon" (姿なきオドン, *Sugata-naki Odon*). In fact, both entities are strongly associated with blood.

sections.text: **Giant Land Octopuses** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Giant Land Octopuses are bloodless creatures commonly found near bodies of water throughout the Lands Between. Their elastic bodies resemble writhing masses of tentacles, with two primary limbs used for combat. A beak protrudes from their central mass, nestled between these appendages. These creatures consume humans to nourish their otherwise pale ovaries. Their Land Octopus offspring are enlivened by a lingering warmth reminiscent of human skin.

Despite their sluggish nature, they react aggressively when approached, striking with unpredictable, sweeping attacks. Their primary method of attack involves flailing their tentacles in a wild barrage, making them dangerous at close range. Attacking their beak can stagger them, creating an opening for a critical strike.

These creatures are capable of regenerating tentacles, which can be severed with well-aimed attacks. They may consume their tentacles mid-combat to restore a portion of their health.

These creatures exhibit high durability and resist most forms of damage, except for direct attacks to their beak. However, they are especially vulnerable to  Frostbite, making weapons that inflict it particularly effective.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Takes reduced damage everywhere except the beak.
- If staggered, a critical attack can be performed on its beak.
- Tentacles can be severed, reducing its attack range. However, it can regenerate them by consuming one of its remaining limbs.
- Can be interrupted while healing if staggered before the animation completes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Internal name: **GroundTaco**, a humorous romanization of the Japanese word for octopus, 蛸 (*Tako*).

sections.text: , also known as , is a cold-burning flame in Elden Ring. Characterized by its blue and white hue, it deals  Magic damage and inflicts  Frostbite buildup.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Ghostflame was an ancient death hex produced by burning the bones of the dead. It was kept in kilns by Deathbirds—progeny of the Twinbird—who used it to unbind and release vengeful spirits, raked from the ashes with Death's Poker. Ancient death hexes like Rancorcall and Ancient Death Rancor were created or discovered and used as sorceries by the servants of Death long ago.

The Company of the Fallen Hawk was sent deep underground to explore the buried ruins of the Eternal Cities, but when their resources were exhausted, they burned the bodies of their companions for light. They acquired the cold ghostflame, but condemned themselves to inhabit the underground for eternity.

sections.text: , also known as **First-Generation Albinaurics**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The bearded Elder Albinaurics were gaunt, lanky men born from a drop of silver dew, artificially created by human hands. The immovable first generation Albinaurics had dysfunctional shins and could only crawl, their legs fading as death approached. When their legs vanished completely, so too did their lives. To compensate for their immobility, many became glintstone sorcerers, casting spells using blue glintstone and their innate arcane power, while others took to acting through puppets.

Due to the circumstances surrounding their occult origin, they were deemed impure and shunned by many inhabitants of the Lands Between. The Albinaurics were spurned from the Erdtree's grace, and suffered heavy persecution at the hands of the brutal Cuckoo Knights of Raya Lucaria. After the Shattering, the agents of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing attacked the Village of the Albinaurics and massacred its residents in search of the Haligree Secret Medallion. And so, the Albinaurics of old pleaded to the stars, night, and fate for to punish the world that condemned them.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: An Albinauric villager living in the Village of the Albinaurics. They move by dragging themselves with their hands and attack by lunging at foes or shoving them back. Sometimes, they will feign death before ambushing their foes in groups.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: An Albinauric sorcerer that uses their arcane nature and an Albinauric Staff to cast Glintstone Pebble. Albinauric sorcerers in Caria Manor and Volcano Manor can cast Magic Downpour.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: A sickly Albinauric consumed by poison. They can be found in the swamp surrounding the Village of the Albinaurics, periodically coughing up poisonous mist.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: An Albinauric prisoner locked in a pillory, at times suspended from the ceilings of Volcano Manor and Castle Sol to act the part of sentries. When an intruder approaches, they will scream to alert nearby allies. In Castle Sol, the screams of these sentries are capable of manifesting the spirits of Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: An Albinauric prisoner forced to wear a Black Dumpling. Driven to insanity, they will lunge and tear at their foe. They have a unique grab attack where they hold down the foe and rip their throat with their teeth.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Old Albus is a friendly Elder Albinauric character at the Village of the Albinaurics. He is initially disguised as a pot.
- Pidia, Carian Servant is an Elder Albinauric Sorcerer at Caria Manor. He acts as a merchant and maintains the puppets.
- First-Generation Albinauric are the male counterparts to Albinauric Archers, who appear younger and ride Wolves.
- First-Generation Albinaurics seek Miquella's Haligtree and Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

- The  also known as the shinbone or shankbone, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee. The first generation of Albinaurics lost the use of their tibias, and are unable to walk on their own.
- Elder Albinaurics wear Headbands of the Golden Ones.

sections.text:

- There are no subtitles for the ambient dialogue spoken by First-Generation Albinaurics.
  - It may foreshadow Elden Ring Nightreign.
- *Albinauric* is a constructed term derived from Latin roots *albus* (pale, white) and ** (gold), suggesting an approximation of silver made from gold.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fire Prelates** are Enemies in Elden Ring and Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Fire Prelates were commanders of the Fire Monks who once aided the champions of the Erdtree during the War Against the Giants and later became guardians of the Flame of Ruin. Their weighty frames symbolized the onus of the vows they took as guardians of the Flame. Their helmets were topped with cauldrons that once contained embers that would surge into flame when their faith reached its zenith. The most hallowed Prelate, Birac, once severed his own head to teach humility to his kin. His head was later made into the Cranial Vessel Candlestand.

Most wielded heavy hammers, croziers symbolizing their guardianship, while others carry whips fashioned in the image of the Briars of Sin.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: - Fire Prelates spawn in the Crater in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wears Fire Prelate Helm, Fire Prelate Gauntlets, Fire Prelate Greaves, and either Fire Prelate Armor or Fire Prelate Armor (Altered)
- Wields Prelate's Inferno Crozier or Thorned Whip
- The helm depicts Birac with an awakened third eye on his forehead.
- The chest emblem depicts two hands grasping the stem of a sunflower engulfed in flame. It resembles the burning Staff of the Guilty held by Guilty.
- Some Golem Smiths also bear similar bowl-like heads.
- The striking face of their hammer resembles a blazing red sun or a Torrent of Life.

sections.text: **Flame Chariots** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A Flame Chariot is a highly-mobile, armored war machine cast in bronze and modeled on the face of a Fire Giant, its braided beard reimagined as sharpened metal tusks. Constructed and operated by Fire Monks, it ignites oil stored in its head to produce makeshift Giants' Flame incantations, expelled from molten, tongue-like cannons. Designed to charge through enemy ranks, this tank then spins rapidly while scorching the area in steady streams of fire. A protective layer of verdigris coats its chassis, and its front bumpers proudly displays the crest of a golden hawk. Its eyes carefully track its targets, and a spiked corona adorns its scalp.

Flame Chariots are manned by teams of three Foot Soldiers, including one pilot, who sits in a cabin at the rear of the vehicle, and two unseen wheel operators. They are near-impenetrable, but can be destroyed instantly by killing the driver, whose backside is exposed, or with a plunging Critical Attack by dropping down onto their chimneys from above, rigging them to explode.

- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to a Critical Attack after a Stance break
- Vulnerable to backstabbing Critical Attacks
- Five-Tongued Fire Chariots produce five streams of flame on all attacks.
- According to concept art, there are two additional operators inside the Flame Chariot.
- Flame Chariots appear in Elden Ring Nightreign.
  - Three Flame Chariots are the Boss of  Fire-affinity Main Encampments.
  - Enemy variants patrol a ruined roadway deep within the Crater.
- Marika's Rune forms at the center of its wrinkled brow.
- A ring of eight bolts encircle the cap to each wooden wheel.
