sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Forge of the Giants** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: An enormous black cauldron atop a pedestal of octagonal black stone columns and solid rock, the Forge of the Giants overlooks the easternmost summit of the Mountaintops of the Giants. It is connected to Flame Peak by a hefty iron chain, held taut as if tethering the Lands Between in place. Two broken chains hang loosely at its side; a fourth once attached to the Forge's missing section. The inextinguishable Giants' Flame smolders quietly within the bowl, and colossal skeletal remains lie in the crevasse below.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
An ancient artifact of the Rauh civilization, the Great Forge contained the ever-burning power of the nameless fell god. The Fire Giants later claimed the forge when they invaded the Mountaintop, driving the Ice Dragons from their icy, windswept home. Sparks from the Forge of the Giants showered the frozen mountaintops, fertilizing the land with Fire Blossoms.

Long ago, Queen Marika ordered Lord Godfrey and his warriors to wage a war against the Giants, whose flame of ruin threatened her burgeoning age of the Erdtree. Marika's forces defeated the giants and confined the Flame, but it could not be fully extinguished. Marika cursed the last Fire Giant to tend it for all eternity.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text: Melina instructs the Tarnished awaken the flame of ruin and commit the first Cardinal Sin. After either she or the Tarnished burns the Erdtree, the Tarnished is transported to Crumbling Farum Azula, where the Rune of Death is hidden.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Forge of the Giants is accessible via Flame Peak after defeating the Fire Giant. The player teleports to Crumbling Farum Azula following a one-time cutscene at this location.

sections.heading: Forge of the Giants
sections.text: The  Forge of the Giants Site of Grace is found on the eastern lip of the forge. If Melina has not left the player, the option to burn the Erdtree will be present. The **"Listen to the flames"** option will be present if not. Both options will cause the Erdtree to burn and transport the player to Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Alexander, Warrior Jar believes the flame of ruin can repair the crack he sustained in his duel with Starscourge Radahn.
- The Forge shares architecture motifs with the Divine Towers and Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
- The decoupled chains suggest the Lands Between was once part of a larger island. Whatever missing landmasses they connected to may be sealed or have drifted away.
  - Statues from the Ancient Dynasty show a bearded man holding half of an engraved tablet, with the other half at his feet. The tablet texture was sourced from the , the earliest known world map.
  - Alternatively, the Forge may have once been a portable smithery, suspended by chains like a hanging cauldron.
- The titan skeletons here are smaller than those in Caelid.
- Forge of the Giants is visible from the First Step in Limgrave.

**Furled Finger** is a player role in Elden Ring's multiplayer.

Also called Cooperators, a Furled Finger is an ally or allies deliberately summoned to face and defeat an area boss alongside the summoner: a Host of Fingers. A summon makes themselves available by leaving a golden sign on the ground, which appears in other worlds for someone to touch and activate to bring the Furled Finger to their world. When they do so, they soon emerge in a swirling golden light and exhibit a soft, golden hue.

Players can make themselves available to be summoned using the Tarnished's Furled Finger while online. If a Host wishes to, they can use the Finger Severer to remove a Furled Finger from the session and send them back to their world.

sections.heading: NPC Summons
sections.text: While players can be summoned as Furled Fingers, even offline many in-game NPCs can be summoned from their golden sign on the ground. Most times, they are just outside the boss's arena before the fog gate, allowing time for the ally to appear and for the summoner apply buffs or change their equipment. In the case of a field boss like the Draconic Tree Sentinel, the signs are a short but safe distance away. Some summon signs are inside a boss arena, as is the case with Starscourge Radahn or Bayle the Dread.

App Ver. 1.02 Regulation Ver. 1.02.1

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Focus** is an resistance stat in Elden Ring.

Focus governs the Tarnished's ability to resist the build-up of Sleep and Madness. It will not decrease the amount of damage taken once afflicted by Madness.

The Tarnished's base Focus is the sum total of two different parts, with each part determined by their Level and Mind attribute. The first part is calculated based on the Tarnished's level. Their Focus will increase as they level up, with soft caps at level 71, 111 and 161. The second part is calculated based off of the Tarnishe's Mind stat, which will begin directly increasing the Tarnished's Focus from 31 Endurance and up. The total of these two parts is what is displayed on the status screen.

Raising Mind to increase Robustness has soft caps at 40 and 60 Mind.
- From 31-40 Mind: +3 Focus each level
- From 41-60 Mind: +0.5 Focus each level
- From 61-99 Mind: +0.25 Focus each level

Focus is further increased by equipping armor, which will display in the righthand column of the Status screen.

Focus can be temporarily increased by consuming Dappled Cured Meat.

sections.heading: Items that increase Focus
sections.text:
;Directly
- Rift Shield, a small shield that increases Focus while equipped.
- Shield of the Guilty, a small shield that increases Focus while equipped.
- Spiralhorn Shield, a small shield that increases Immunity, Robustness and Focus while equipped.
- Eclipse Crest Greatshield, a greatshield that increases Immunity, Robustness and Focus while equipped.

It is notable for it's inclusion of the *"Near/Far"* option when sending Summoning Signs or attempting to Invade another world, significantly improving player connectivity and overall multiplayer activity.

sections.heading: 1.05 (NG+-Transfered Bell Bearings Update)
sections.text: - 1.05 was released on June 13th, 2022 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This patch is notable for making non-NPC related Bell Bearings transfer over to NG+, multitudes of bug fixes and it's inclusion of several PC-only, quality-of-life improvements.

- 1.04 was released on April 19th, 2022 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This patch is notable for completing the primary task 1.03 set out to do by finishing Patches questline, making his store not permanently lost at the end of it while also allowing players to obtain the gesture, Patches' Crouch which had up until now been inaccessible. It also made a significant number of balance changes.

sections.heading: Shadow of the Erdtreee Review Update
sections.text: - 1.11 was an update that never released publicly. It is the patch that was distributed to game journalists and internet content creators so that they could make reviews for Shadow of the Erdtree in time for its public launch.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Review Update
sections.text: - 1.01 was an update that never released publicly. It is the patch that was distributed to game journalists and internet content creators so that they could make reviews for Elden Ring in preparation for the public launch of the game.

sections.heading: Demos
sections.text: - Closed Network Test was a Demo intended to stress test Elden Ring's online matchmaking servers. This version of the game is also known to have some slightly different assets and code, which have been used by fans to show differences between planned content and the final release of the game.

- 1.00 was released February 25th, 2022 alongside the game itself, Game Version **1.00**  was the initial version of Elden Ring made only available on physical media. It is known for it's many differences in comparison to later versions of the game, sporting many alternate icons, textures item descriptions, items/enemy placements and much much more.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Game Version **1.04**  was released on April 19th, 2022 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . sections.text:
We are distributing an update to improve the stability of gameplay and to adjust balance.
We apologize for the inconvenience, but please apply the latest update before you enjoy the game.

Targeted Platform
PlayStation 4 / PlayStation 5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / Steam

sections.text:

- Added some event phases for the NPC “Patches”

sections.heading: Balance adjustments
sections.text:
- Increased Colossal Swords/Colossal weapons attack speed and lowered their recovery time. Jump attack not included.
- Increased the two-handed attack damage of Colossal Swords/Colossal Weapons. Jump attack not included.
- Increased physical block rate and guard boost of the Colossal Sword, Colossal Weapons, Great Sword, Great Hammer, Great Axe, Great Spear, and Halberd weapon classes.
- Increased the damage of Grafted Blade Greatsword.
- Increased the damage of Devourer’s Scepter.
- Decreased the scaling of status effect build-up from spells and incantations of Albinauric Staff and Dragon Communion Seal.
- Decreased the effect of Greatshield Talisman for weapons with high block rate.
- Shortened the length of the madness afflicted animation.
- Lowered the speed of madness buildup recovery.
- Slightly increased FP and Stamina growth rate at lower levels*

Players will need to perform any of the following actions for the changes to be reflected. This is required only once. New characters created after this update will not require this action.
- Level up
- Activate Godrick’s Great Rune
- Re-equipping any equipment (armor, talisman) which grants bonus stat to either Strength, Dexterity, Vigor, Endurance, Intelligence, Faith or Arcane

・Other enemy and weapon balance changes

sections.heading: Bug Fixes
sections.text:
- Fixed a bug where the damage of Inescapable Frenzy was affected by right hand weapon.

- Fixed a bug that prevented a dialog from appearing when executing "Leave" on some items.
- Fixed a bug that allowed unauthorized items to be passed to other players.
- Fixed a bug in multiplayer that prevented grace to be registered on the map if it was found just before the player is summoned.
- Fixed a bug that sometime prevented the mechanic of Rennala Queen Of The Full Moon fight from working properly during cooperative multiplayer.
- Fixed a bug that sometime prevented the player from entering the boss area after defeating Morgott, the Omen King.
- Fixed a bug that prevented "Edgar the Revenger" and "Festering Fingerprint Vyke" from invading after defeating all the bosses in Liurnia of the Lake.
- The item Tonic of Forgetfulness can now be obtained at the Volcano Manor if the player wasn’t able to obtain it due to quest progression.
- Fixed a bug that caused the reduction of runes due to NPC "Gostoc" when player died in "Stormveil Castle" to occur at an unintended timing.
- Added a protective barrier to Millicent after helping her at Miquella’s Haligtree so she cannot be unintentionally killed.
- Fixed a bug that sometime prevented the player from obtaining the reward after defeating the Dung Eater.
- Fixed a bug that sometime prevented the player from progress Diallos’ questline.
- Fixed a bug that sometime prevented player from duplicating remembrance at the Walking Mausoleum.
- Fixed a bug that prevented player from inputting consecutive attacks when dual wielding thrusting sword.
- Fixed a bug that causes scythe to lose blood loss effect if poison affinity is applied to the weapon.
- Fixed a bug where the damage of the Iron Greatsword was lower than expected when an affinity is applied.
- Fixed a bug that caused FP consumption to increase when the player cast Night Comet with charge.
- Fixed a bug that causes he default key setting on keyboard for weapon skill (Left Ctrl) to not be set (on PC only).
- Fixed a bug in the Steam version where the history of players who played multiplayer was not displayed correctly under certain circumstances.
- Increased online multiplayer stability.
- Fixed a bug that caused incorrect sounds to be played under certain circumstances.
- Fixed a bug that caused some places on the map to have incorrect visual and hitbox.
- Fixed a bug that causes some enemies to have incorrect visual and behavior.
- Fixed a bug that causes some armor to have incorrect stats.
- Text fix.
- Other performance improvements and bug fixes.

sections.heading: Closing Paragraph
sections.text:
The version number of this update shown at the lower right corner of the Title Screen will be as follows:
App Ver. 1.04 - Regulation Ver. 1.04.1

We will continue to provide improvement update in the future so you can enjoy "ELDEN RING" more comfortably. You may also join the Official Discord server for additional updates and to connect with the ELDEN RING community. Please stay tuned for more news.

sections.text:
Game Version **1.07**  was released on October 13th, 2022 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This patch is notable for it's addition of PvP-exclusive damage-scaling, allowing FromSoftware to balance weapons for PvP while not altering their effectiveness in PvE. Player-damage in PvP was reduced across the board, making the average battles between them last longer.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.text:
This new update brings balance adjustments to **improve the stability of gameplay.**

Many changes were brought to **spells**, **skills**, **incantations** and **weapons** to encourage more versatility in terms of gameplay.

**Please note that online play requires the player to apply this update.**

Targeted Platforms

PlayStation 4 / PlayStation 5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / Steam

sections.heading: **Summary**
sections.text:
1. Additional features

2. PvP Exclusive balance adjustments

3. General balance adjustments

4. Balance adjustments for Magic and Incantations

5. Balance adjustment of Skills

6. Bug Fixes

sections.heading: Additional features
sections.text:
- Added separate damage scaling for PvP.

This feature allows separate damage scaling for Weapons, Skills, Spells, and Incantations when playing against other players.

In the future, this feature may be used to balance weapons, Art, Spell, and Incantation in invading/PvP mode.

Balance adjustments made within this feature will not impact single-player and cooperative play.

sections.heading: PvP Exclusive balance adjustments
sections.text:
**The adjustments in this section do not affect single-player or cooperative play.**

- Increased stamina attack power in PvP for all attacks against guarded foes, except for long-ranged weapons.
- Improved poise damage in PvP for every weapon’s normal attack, except for Skills and long-ranged weapons.
- With a few exceptions, the power of Ashes of War in PvP has been lowered across the board.
- The power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased:
  - Dragonfire / Agheel's Flame / Glintstone Breath / Smarag's Glintstone Breath / Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay / Dragonice / Borealis's Mist / Unendurable Frenzy

sections.heading: General balance adjustments
sections.text:
**The adjustments in this section affect both PvE and PvP aspects of the game.**

- Increased poise damage when using two-handed normal attacks.
- Increased the speed of some Colossal Sword attacks.
- The speed and hit detection of Colossal Sword crouching and rolling attacks have been decreased.
- Increased the speed of some Colossal Weapon attacks.
- Decreased recovery time for Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons, except for jump attacks, dual wielded attacks, and attacks while riding.
- Increased poise damage of Hammers, Great Hammers and some Colossal Weapons.
- Increased guard penetration for the following weapons:
  - Celebrant's Sickle / Nox Flowing Sword / Shotel / Eclipse Shotel / Vulgar Militia Shotel / Scythe / Grave Scythe / Halo Scythe / Winged Scythe

- The poise rating of some attacks has been increased for the following weapons:
  - Greatswords / Colossal Swords / Curved Greatswords / Greataxes / Great Hammers / Great Spears / Halberds

- With some exceptions, poise of all armor has been increased.
- The effects of the Greatshield Talisman and Hammer Talisman have been increased.
- Some effects of the spell Scholar's Shield, the Barricade Shield skill and the Shield Grease item have been adjusted as follows.
  - The effects on shields with low guard boost have been adjusted upward.
  - The effects on shields with high guard boost have been adjusted downward.

- The guard strength of the Fingerprint Stone Shield has been decreased.
- Decreased the status buildup done by dual wielded weapons.

sections.heading: Bug Fixes
sections.text:
- Added a process to remove the Ash of War from weapons that cannot normally be combined with certain Ashes of War.
- Fixed a bug that prevented users from obtaining items such as Great Runes, Crystal Tears, Cracked Pots, and Ritual Pots when the number of items in the inventory and the storage had reached the maximum limit.
- Fixed a bug that prevented users from obtaining Crystal Tear. If you fail to obtain a Crystal Tear, the item will be added to your inventory when moving within the vicinity of the place where you should have obtained it.
- Adjusted player character control when under certain damage animations.
- Fixed a bug that prevented charging some Incantations while casting them with a left-handed Sacred Seal in mid-air.
- Fixed a bug that prevented performing a normal attack from a dash immediately after landing from a jump when the weapon is two-handed.
- Fixed a bug where various action inputs were ignored when changing weapons while moving.
- Corrected the description of the Colossal Sword’s physical attack attribute.
- Fixed a bug where the timing to change the attack direction was narrower than expected for some attacks with Greataxes.
- Fixed a bug where the attack direction could not be changed when performing a charged attack with the Ruins Greatsword weapon.
- Fixed a bug where the Highland Axe’s effect was not applied to the skill Shriek of Milos.
- Fixed a bug where the effects of the Warrior Jar Shard and the Shard of Alexander were not applied to the skill Sorcery of the Crozier.
- Fixed a bug where the effect of the Roar Medallion was not applied to the Regal Roar Ash of War.
- Fixed a bug where the skill Viper Bite could inflict poison instead of deadly poison.
- Fixed a bug where the range of one of the three rocks was longer than expected when casting the Spell Rock Sling with a left-hand staff.
- Fixed a bug where recovery time after casting Beast Claw could not be shortened by magic or incantations.
- Fixed a bug where when attacking an enemy who cannot be grabbed by the incantation Inescapable Frenzy, the attack will be repelled if the enemy is holding a shield.
- Fixed a bug where HP or FP could be recovered when changing equipment to certain types of armor under certain circumstances.
- Fixed a bug that could cause death and result in the player becoming stuck in some locations.
- Fixed some terrain bugs that allowed users to reach unexpected locations with certain procedures.
- Fixed a bug where the rendering and collision detection of some maps were different from expected.
- Fixed a bug where bolts fired with the Hand Ballista weapon missed the lock-on target when the game was running at a frame rate below a certain level.
- Fixed a bug that could prevent online multiplayer from working properly on the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 versions.
- Several other performance improvements and bug fixes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Game Version **1.08**  was released on December 7th, 2022 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This update is notable for adding Arnea Duels, unlocking the Colosseums throughout the Lands Between that have remained vacant until now.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.text:
The Colosseum awaits.

In this new update, a brand-new multiplayer feature in the form of the Colosseum arenas have been added, as well as new hairstyles for you to enjoy. Additionally, new balance adjustments have been made to improve the stability of gameplay.

Please note that online play requires the player to apply this update.

Targeted platforms

PlayStation 4 / PlayStation 5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / Steam

Major Changes Included in the Latest Upgrade

sections.heading: **Major new features**
sections.text:
- The Colosseums of Limgrave, Caelid and Leyndell are now open.

In these arenas, players can engage in a variety of combat trials: one-on-one duels, free-for-alls & team battles up to six players, and special fights with spirit summoning enabled.

Learn more about the Colosseums by visiting our dedicated article.

- New hairstyles for character creation have been added. These are also available during character edition by using the Round Table Hold Clouded Mirror Stand.

sections.heading: **PvP-exclusive balance adjustments**
sections.text:
**The adjustments in this section do not affect single-player or cooperative play.**

- Reduced thrusting weapons counterattack damage.
- Reduced guard efficiency when attacking with your shield up for some weapon types.
- The poise damage of the following weapons have been reduced (Weapon Arts poise damage remains unchanged):
  - Straight Swords / Thrusting Swords / Heavy Thrusting Swords / Curved Swords / Axes / Spears / Twinblade Swords / Katanas
- Reduced the poise damage of the Incantation Bestial Sling.
- Reduced the power of the Spell Carian Slicer.

sections.heading: **General balance adjustments**
sections.text:
- Increased the speed and distance of some attacks and reduced the recovery time for the following weapons:
  - Daggers / Axes / Hammers / Flails (dual wielded)
- Increased the speed of some attacks and reduced the recovery time for the following weapons:
  - Twinblade (two-handed) / Reaper / Fist / Claw
- Slightly increased the speed of crouching and rolling attacks of Colossal Swords.
- Increased the stagger damage of Axes’ guard counters.
- Increased poise when attacking with two-handed Hammers.
- Increased poise damage of Claws. Weapon Arts remain unchanged.
- Increased poise value during the active part of the Stamp (Upward Cut / Sweep) Weapon Art.
- Increased poise damage of the weapon slash part of the Transient Moonlight Weapon Art, and reduced the poise damage of the magic wave.
- Reduced the speed Thrusting Swords and Heavy Thrusting Swords crouching attacks.
- Reduced the stagger caused by double-handed Heavy Thrusting Swords jumping attacks.
- Reduced poise damage of Hammers, Great Hammers, and some Colossal Weapons. Weapon Arts remain unchanged.
- Reduced the poise damage of the Cragblade Weapon Art.
- Reduced hitbox duration of the flame portion of the Flaming Strike Weapon Art.
- Reduced poise damage of the Flame of the Redmanes Weapon Art.
- Increased the time it takes to activate the guard part of the Shield Bash Weapon Art.
- Reduced the poise damage of the Gravity Bolt Weapon Art.

sections.heading: **Bug Fixes**
sections.text:
- Fixed a bug that sometimes prevented consumable items from being replenished when teleporting to a grace from the map.
- Fixed a bug where stamina would replenish when switching to a crouching position while running.
- Fixed a bug where Spell, Incantation, and item input actions were ignored while guarding against attacks.
- Fixed incorrect physical attack values of some attacks of the Serpent-Hunter weapon.
- Fixed a bug that prevented the follow-up attack from occurring when the Black Sword (sic) Incantation was activated with a Sacred Seal in the left hand.
- Fixed a bug where the attack power of the right hand weapon was sometimes applied when casting the Inescapable Frenzy Incantation with a two-handed Sacred Seal in the left hand.
- Fixed a bug that could cause multiple damage instances when certain Spells and Incantations were casted while jumping.
- Fixed a bug that caused Weapon Arts to be incorrectly used with specific combinations of weapon and Weapon Arts.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Game Version **1.09**  was released on March 23rd, 2023 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This patch is notable for it's inclusion of allowing ray tracing on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series X.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.text:
Targeted Platforms

PlayStation 4 / PlayStation 5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / Steam

sections.heading: **New feature**
sections.text:
Ray Tracing support has been added for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and PC versions.

Ray Tracing can be activated in the settings menu:

- PS5 / XSX: Game Options > Ray Tracing
- PC: Graphics > Ray Tracing Quality

Please note that performance - such as frame rate and resolution - may be impacted while playing with Ray Tracing on.

The minimum and recommended technical specifications to use Ray Tracing can be found at the end of the patch notes.

sections.heading: **PvP-exclusive balance adjustments**
sections.text:
The adjustments in this section do not affect single-player or cooperative play.

- The *Inescapable Frenzy* incantation power and grab angle have been increased.
- The *Lifesteal Fist* skill power, range and grab angle have been increased.
- Decreased the power of dual-wielded jumping attacks.
- Decreased the poise damage of heavy attacks and heavy running attacks of *Fist* and *Claw* weapon types.
- Decreased the power of the *Founding Rain of Stars* spell.
- Decreased the spell enhancement effect of the *Terra Magica* spell.
- Decreased the damage and poise damage of the *Wave of Gold* skill when hitting an opponent over a certain distance.
- Decreased the effectiveness of the *Determination* and *Royal Knight's Resolve* skills.
- Decreased the effects of the *Contagious Fury skill of the Jellyfish Shield*.
- Decreased the effectiveness of the *Claw Talisman*.
- Decreased the effectiveness of the *Lord of Blood’s Exultation* Talisman.
- Decreased the attack power buff granted by the *White Mask* head armor.
- Decreased the jumping attack damage buff granted by the *Raptor's Black Feathers* armor.
- Decreased the damage buff granted by *Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear, Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear, Lightning-Shrouding Cracked Tear, and Holy-Shrouding Cracked Tear* when activated with the *Flask of Wondrous Physick*.

sections.heading: **Bug Fixes**
sections.text:
- Fixed a bug where the Scarlet rot status buildup was not properly reflected when giving the *Antspur Rapier* a Cold affinity.
- Fixed a bug where the Scarlet rot status buildup was not properly reflected when giving the *Rotten Greataxe* a Blood affinity.
- Fixed a bug where some attacks of the *Partisan*, *Death Ritual Spear*, and *Lucerne* had unexpected Physical attack scaling.
- Fixed a bug where the *Nightrider Glaive* did not increase the damage of horseback attacks.
- Fixed a bug where the *Duelist Greataxe* and *Rotten Greataxe* did not increase the damage of charged attacks.
- Fixed a bug where the *Roar Medallion* Talisman effect didn’t increase the power of some incantations.

- Fixed a bug where the power and special effects of a left-handed weapon could be added to a skill cast with a right-handed weapon.
- Fixed a bug that caused an equipped Sacrificial Twig to be consumed when a player died in the Colosseum.

- Fixed a bug where a player could receive credit for a kill in the Colosseum when dying due to the Death status effect, instead of the player who inflicted that status effect.
- Improved stability in Colosseum matchmaking.
- Fixed a bug related to level correction when an invader used the *Phantom Bloody Finger*.
- Fixed a bug that could cause disconnections with other players in certain locations during multiplayer.
- Improved online multiplayer stability.
- [PS4] Fixed a bug that occurred when using the *Finger Severer* on summoned NPCs while offline that could cause the game to crash.
- Fixed a bug related to some enemies not rendering or behaving as expected.
- Several performance improvements and other bug fixes.

sections.heading: **Ray Tracing Technical Specifications**
sections.text:
Minimum

- OPERATING SYSTEM: WINDOWS 10
- PROCESSOR: Intel Core i5-10600K or AMD Ryzen 5 3600XT
- MEMORY: 16 GB RAM
- GRAPHIC CARD: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti, 8 GB or AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT, 12 GB
- RECOMMENDED GRAPHICS SETTING: 1080p - Low quality – Low Ray Tracing

Recommended

- OPERATING SYSTEM: WINDOWS 11
- PROCESSOR: Intel Core i7-10700K or AMD Ryzen 7 3800XT
- MEMORY: 16 GB RAM
- GRAPHIC CARD: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti, 8 GB or AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT, 16 GB
- RECOMMENDED GRAPHICS SETTING: 1080p - High quality – High Ray Tracing

sections.heading: About PC Ray Tracing settings
sections.text:
Under certain circumstances, ray tracing has been enabled by default after updating the game to **version 1.09**.

- If Ray Tracing has been unintentionally enabled and is impacting your game, you can disable it from the title menu or in-game by going to **System →** **Graphics → Set Ray Tracing Quality** to ***OFF***.

- If your game does not start properly or becomes unstable when Ray Tracing Quality is set to Low/Medium/High/Maximum, please consider the following options:
  - Check the minimum/recommended operating environment of your PC when using Ray Tracing.
  - Ensure that your graphics card drivers are updated to the latest version.

Game Version **1.10**  was released on July 26th, 2023 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC . This patch is notable for significantly overhauling poise values in PvP.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.text:
Targeted Platforms

PlayStation 4 / PlayStation 5 / Xbox One / Xbox Series X|S / Steam

sections.heading: **PvP-exclusive balance adjustments**
sections.text:
**The adjustments in this section do not affect single-player or cooperative play.**

- Increased poise damage of all weapons and some spells and incantations.

- Increased poise when attacking with some skills, spells, incantations and some types of weapon attacks that generates poise.

- Added damage reduction when performing attacks with some skills, spells and incantations and some types of weapon attacks that generates poise.

- Critical hit angles have been extended.

- Decreased the invulnerability window of the *Quick Step* and *Hound's Step* skills.

- Decreased the damage reduction granted by some skills, incantations and items.

sections.heading: **General balance adjustments**
sections.text:
- Increased critical hit damage.

- Decreased recovery time after a missed critical hit.

- Increased poise damage of attacks that occur after missing a critical hit.

sections.heading: **Bug Fixes and other changes**
sections.text:
- Adjusted the player damage animation so that the attack direction is not unintentionally shifted when getting hit while attacking with some types of weapons that generates poise.

- Fixed a bug that prevented some spells and incantations from causing damage while under the effect of some skills and items.

- Fixed a bug that caused the effects of the *Sacred Order* skill to continue after switching weapons.

- Corrected some text in certain languages.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Version 1.00** was a Game Version of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Released on February 25, 2022, alongside the game itself, Version 1.00 was the initial retail build of *Elden Ring* and was only distributed on physical media. It is accessible exclusively by installing and playing the disc version of the game without an internet connection.

This version is notable for its many differences compared to later updates. It contains alternate icons, textures, dialogue, item descriptions, unused items, and different enemy placements. Several unseen characters were removed entirely, while others—such as the Gloam-Eyed Queen—were expanded upon in subsequent updates.

While much of the removed content supplements the final story without contradiction, some elements diverge significantly and may no longer be considered canonical.

sections.heading: Enemies
sections.text:
- Scarlet Rot variants for Ancestral Follower Warrior and Ancestral Follower Shaman were at the Grand Cloister. They were covered in sores and spew scarlet rot from their mouths. They were removed and replaced with regular Ancestral Followers at the Lake of Rot and Consecrated Snowfield
- Oracle Envoys had a different name and used blue Claymen Sorceries.
- Maliketh used unique purple particles for Destined Death attacks.
- Blackflame Monks used unique particles that resemble a mixture of Giants' Flame and Destined Death for their fire attacks.
- Deathbirds had a golden glow.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Leyndell, Royal Capital lacked Oracle Envoys and Leyndell Knights, and was populated by Imps and Banished Knights, respectively. There were more Valiant Gargoyles.
- Deeproot Depths had bright golden lighting.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Flames** are a common theme in the world of Elden Ring. Not limited to standard fire attacks, they come in a variety of colors with unique properties.

sections.heading: Black Flame
sections.text:
Black and white-colored flames used by the Godskins and Blackflame Monks, Blackflame is a weakened variant of Destined Death.
Deals  Fire damage and gradually drains  HP for a short duration.

sections.heading: Blasphemous Flame
sections.text:
Blasphemous flames, also known as **Taker's Flames**, are the power of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy and his Blasphemous Blade.
Deals  Fire damage and steals  HP.

sections.heading: Bloodflame
sections.text:
Dark-red flame of the Formless Mother. Used by Mohg, Lord of Blood, his knights and reluctantly by Morgott, the Omen King.
Deals  Fire damage and applies a build-up of  Blood Loss.

sections.heading: Destined Death
sections.text:
Black and red-colored flame used by Maliketh and the Black Knife Assassins.
Deals  Holy damage, reduces maximum  HP and gradually drains  HP for a short duration.

sections.heading: Fires of Slumber
sections.text:
Violet flames of St. Trina, found only on St. Trina's Torch.
Deals  Fire damage and applies a build-up of  Sleep.

sections.heading: Flame Lightning
sections.text:
A lightning-infused flame wielded by Bayle the Dread.
Deals  Fire and  Lightning damage.

sections.heading: Frenzied Flame
sections.text:
Yellow and orange flame of the Three Fingers. Seen by tormented souls.
Deals  Fire damage and applies a build-up of  Madness.

sections.heading: Ghostflame
sections.text:
Ghostflame, also known as Spiritflame, is black-and-blue flames produced by burning the bones of the dead. Used by the Death Rite Birds.
Deals  Magic damage and applies a build-up of  Frostbite.

sections.heading: Giants' Flame
sections.text:
Giants' Flame, also known as the Flame of Ruin or simply the Flame, is a red-orange-colored flame associated with the ancient Fell God of Fire. Used by the Fire Giants, derived by the Fire Monks, and seen by Erdtree Prophets through visions.
Deals  Fire damage.

sections.heading: Glintstone Breath
sections.text:
The glintstone-infused flames spewed by the Glintstone Dragons.
Deals  Magic damage.

sections.heading: Golden Flames
sections.text:
Golden flame used by Ulcerated Tree Spirits, Dragonlord Placidusax, and the Elden Beast. A variant with shadow inside the golden flame is used by Scorched Tree Spirits.
Deals  Holy damage.

sections.heading: Magma
sections.text:
Molten lava used by Magma Wyrms, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and Bayle the Dread.
Deals  Fire damage.

sections.heading: Messmerfire
sections.text:
Dark red, serpentine flames wielded by Messmer and his followers during the Crusade.
Deals  Fire damage.

sections.heading: Nightflame
sections.text: Azure flames that burn beneath the Night's Tide, Nightflame is a power unleashed by the Nightlord in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Prince of Death's Flames
sections.text:
The Prince of Death's Flame, also known as Death, is a black-and-gold fire tied to the soulless body of Godwyn the Golden that deals  Holy damage and inflicts  Death Blight buildup. It is wielded by Mausoleum Knights and their leader, Lhutel the Headless, and channeled by the legendary Eclipse Shotel of Castle Sol.

A flame with similar properties burns within Fia's Mist, a Death Sorcery conceived by Fia, Deathbed Companion. Prince of Death-Serving Omen and Commoners cast the spell at the Minor Erdtree in the Capital Outskirts, positioned above the Prince of Death's Throne in the Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: Rotten Breath
sections.text:
Rotten Breath is red-orange flames spewed by Putrid Tree Spirits and Decaying Ekzykes.
Applies a build-up of  Scarlet Rot.

sections.text: The **Formless Serpents** are an unseen faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Formless Serpents were a company of assassins known for their expertise in archery and poison. Their bows were imbued with pagan magic, which amplified the lethality of their venomous arrows.

The Formless Serpents wielded equipment designed with elaborate serpentine motifs. Their enchanted bows were adorned with two serpents,  intricately carved and poised to strike. Their arrows resembled flying snakes, with spiraling tails and fangs that dripped with venom.

sections.text:
- The Serpent Bow is found in an Abandoned Cave tainted by the Scarlet Rot. It is located in proximity to Rot disciples, putrid Miranda blossoms, and broken down Abductor Virgins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Fire Monks**, also known as the **guardians of the Flame**, are a faction in Elden Ring. They include the Fire Monks, Fire Prelates, the Guilty, and the Fire Giant.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Fire Monks emerged during the War Against the Giants when they sided with young Marika against the Fire Giants. They used the Giants' Flame to protect her champions, allowing them to purge the Giants from Flame Peak. Afterwards, they were appointed guardians of the inextinguishable flame of ruin. They were sworn to protect the Golden Order and its Erdtree from the sealed Flame that once belonged to the Fire Giants.

The Monks were tasked with halting the surges and safeguarding the Giants' Flame secrets. Their work guaranteed that the Flame would never pose a threat to the Erdtree again.

sections.text:
- The Fire Monks have pale skin and red hair. Like the Northerners and other groups from the Mountaintops, the Flame Monks are likely descended from Giants.
- The Grand Lift of Rold features large statues of bearded Fire Monks with branch spears and the aprons of Erdtree priests, which also appear on the Rold Medallion. Their headbands the Fire Monk Hood without the metal hood.

sections.text: **Glintstone** is a type of mineral in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
activates Glintstone Scrap]]

Sorceries draw from the power imbued in glintstone. It is said that glintstone is the amber of the cosmos, and that it contains the vitality of the stars. Glintstones have a wide variety of applications: they can be embedded in staves used to cast sorceries, and the stone crowns worn by scholars of the Academy of Raya Lucaria Conspectuses; used as ornamentation in various weapons; or used as a receptacle for a sorcerer's soul after removal with a Primal Glintstone Blade. In addition, many glintstone sorceries conjure projectiles made of glintstone, which can be launched at enemies.

Glintstone has a crystalline appearance, and many varieties exist. The glintstone embedded in the staffs of the Raya Lucarian sorcerers is a turquoise color, a hue shared by many of the fundamental glintstone sorceries, while glintstone used by the Carian Royal Family is typically lapis lazuli blue.

sections.heading: Blue Glintstone
sections.text: Bright **blue glintstone** is associated with comets. It was worn on the stone crowns of the Karolos Sorcerers. It boosts Intelligence but limits Stamina. This color is associated with Primeval Sorcerer Lusat and Albinaurics.

**Blue-green glintstone** is associated with Primeval Sorcerer Azur.

sections.heading: Carian Blue Glintstone

**Carian blue glintstone** is a deep blue crystal linked to the moon, enhancing the power of Carian Sword Sorceries, Glintblade Sorceries, or Full Moon Sorceries, depending on the variant. The crowns worn by Lazuli Sorcerers are set with **lapis-lazuli** or blue-purple crystals.

sections.heading: Crystal Glintstone

The Crystalian Sorcery of the enigmatic Crystalians utilizes **crystal**, the purest form of glintstone. Although imbued with powerful magic, glintstone of this purity is impossible is susceptible to the stagnation of Scarlet Rot and cannot crafted by human hands.

sections.heading: Dulled Glintstone

**Dulled glintstones** are shiny, black-and-white crystals. They are associated with the nomadic Hierodas Conspectus and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, who made contact with the primeval current.

sections.heading: Green Glintstone
sections.text:
]]
**Green glintstone** appears in the crown worn by Sorceress Sellen, the Graven Witch, who seeks to uncover the forbidden secrets of the primeval current. Her crown increases Intelligence and Arcane.

sections.heading: Red Glintstone
sections.text:
The two variants of **red glintstone** are associated with Thorn Sorcery and Lava Sorcery, respectively. Both are viewed with disdain or disgust by the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Blind Thorn Sorcerers who glimpsed the Blood Star practiced heretical rites to transmute sacrificial blood to red glintstone. Red glintstone scales with Faith and enhances the power of thorn sorceries. This reviled glintstone catalyzes bloodthorns, and may be connected to the Briars of Sin.

The second variety of red glintstone empowers staves wielded by Gelmir Man-Serpents, amplifying their lava sorceries. These glintstones scale with both Intelligence and Faith.

sections.heading: Purple Glintstone

The **turquoise glintstones** crowned the staves of recognized sorcerers. It was worn by Olivinus Sorcerers increase Intelligence but reduce maximum HP. Sorcerers in this conspectus study meteors.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Frenzied Flame** (狂い火, *Kurui Hi*), also called **Yellow Flame of Frenzy** (黄色い狂い火, *Kiiroi Kurui Hi*) and **Yellow Flame of Chaos** (混沌の黄色い火, *Konton no Kiiroi Hi*), is a force that manifests in the eyes of those stricken by maddening grief and suffering. It is feared by many for its uncanny ability to destroy individuality, capable of melting away even eternal spirits. Those deeply stricken by its folly develop an insatiable need to spread its influence further, willingly seeking to infect others with it. These afflicted, known by some as Chaos Followers, yearn for the arrival of their lord so that they may incinerate all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
One of the unique properties of the flame, destroying individuality, manifests mainly in its ability to seemingly brainwash those it has afflicted. Many afflicted repeat the same cries and phrases despite never having interacted with one another (the most notable of these phrases being *"Melt it all away..."* and *"May chaos take the world!"* repeated ad nauseam). Seemingly blending their minds into a single, hivemind-like state.

A chosen few of those afflicted are capable of transforming into the Lord of Frenzied Flame after an apparent death, or some sort of transformation or rebirth process, it's not clearly stated and left to speculation. The strength of a lord can seemingly vary depending on who its original host was, with several individuals having proven capable of becoming one. However many of the afflicted were either too non-committal or physically feeble to accomplish anything, causing them to be considered frauds and failures in the eyes of their followers. Once a Lord of Frenzied Flame manifests, the head of the original host is replaced by a black hole with yellow flames spewing out of its core, completely erasing any trace of the original host's identity. However, if the Tarnished manages to inherit the flame, it's unclear whether his identity is truly erased. Given his ability to subdue demigods and gods like the Elden Beast, it is plausible that he did not succumb to the Flame, but instead mastered it—fusing with it rather than being consumed.

The origins of the flame are unclear, as the flame itself is said to have made its first appearance in the empty eye sockets of Shabriri, after his eyes were gouged out in punishment for slander. However, its incantations, the most powerful means that the flame manifests itself through, are also said to have come from the Three Fingers. It is also the clasp of Three Fingers that appoints a specific subject to become a Lord of Frenzied Flame.

Even without direct influence of the Three Fingers, the flame is capable of appearing on its own in sites of great suffering, such as the ninth campsite of Mt. Gelmir, where it has appeared in the eyes of Leyndell Soldiers suffering from the trauma of a particularly appalling battle. It has also appeared in the eyes of the surface-dwelling Nomadic Merchants, and while they are unable to settle and are forced to move around the lands constantly, their relative freedom gives them enough comfort to endure only minor symptoms, allowing some of them to have fairly normal conversations with passersby. They utter the mantras of the Chaos Followers only when attacked or dying.

Some have willingly pursued the Frenzied Flame in an attempt to use it as a powerful weapon, however every attempt to control the flame has ended in failure and left those who pursued it irreparably psychologically damaged. That said, even if the Tarnished chooses to purge himself from the Flame, he can still use the frenzy incantations in the pure form of a weapon, yet still susceptible to madness, however.

In a cruel twist of fate, the fear the world has for the flame has only supported its growth, as any attempt to quell it through the punishment and subjugation of its subjects has only intensified and worsened their symptoms, allowing the flame to fester more deeply into its hosts, becoming more powerful and widespread as their suffering increases. Primary example of this being the Golden Order's punishment of the Great Caravan, after they were accused of heretical beliefs, and the Hornsent's damnation of Midra and his entourage, after their attempt of studying of the flame. Both events would eventually lead to the near-or-complete successful manifestation of the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The flame's ability to blend minds together may have been more apparent in an earlier version of Elden Ring. As the brotherhood of Nomadic Merchants that can be encountered throughout the world would mention that they fear going to sleep, as while asleep, they would feel as if their minds would rapidly drift and switch between each other, leaving all of them bewildered and confused on who they really are when they wake up.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: are Enemies in Elden Ring, included in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. They act like unmarked bosses, and do not respawn.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Furnace Golems are animate metal cages of titanic proportions that contain a raging inferno of Messmer's Flame and the scattered sap from the Scadutree. Their thorny, iron bodies contain countless charred corpses locked in desperate, agonizing poses. They use their massive arms to catch enemies and dump them into their torsos. They reignite their kindling and burn brightly to incinerate their victims, which include animals and even dragons. Their kneecaps are adorned with Fire Giant hair and faces, and their "face" is a burning sun of horns in the image of the Fell God of fire, took from the hornsent's legends. Their faces are animated to show different expressions in reaction to taking damage.

Furnace Golems deal  Standard,  Strike, and  Fire damage. They are weakest to  Standard,  Strike, and  Magic damage. They are immune to all status ailments. They are especially vulnerable to Critical Attacks to their faces and Hefty Furnace Pots thrown into their bowls. Armored Furnace Golems are found at Charo's Hidden Grave and on the eastern Scadu Altus, north of the Bonny Village. Their legs are covered in highly durable metal armor, which protects them from physical attacks.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A furnace hex powers the deadly and destructive Furnace Golems. The Messmer the Impaler used them as powerful weapons of war in his genocidal Crusade, where they aided his army in purging the Realm of Shadow of anyone who are impure and didn't bear the light of Grace and destroyed everything in their paths. The majority of Furnace Golems throughout the Realm of Shadow are now inactive, and though some are still operational.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Some Furnace Golems are unlit, requiring a Hefty Furnace Pot to be awakened.
- The Furnace Visage is placed high above the Fire Giant faces, implying the Fell God towered over them.
- Furnace Golems use a different Poise system than other enemies that ignores the Stance damage of individual weapons. However, their posture can still be broken.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **Wickerman** (ID: 5170)
- Furnace Golems are a nod to , real-life wickerwork statues built to resemble giant men. They were used for human and animal sacrifices, as druids would burn the wicker man while the sacrifices were trapped within the statue.
- There are eight Furnace Golems.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Gate of Divinity** is a Site of Grace in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Gate of Divinity is a mysterious place that can be used to elevate Empyreans into godhood under the correct circumstances. It has existed since ancient times, and is an incredibly holy site and artifact to the Hornsent, and is found at the pinnacle of their civilization: atop the tower of Enir-Ilim, crowning the settlement of Belurat. It is even necessary to pass through a ceremonial cleansing room in order to reach the Gate.

Despite these ties to the divine, the Gate itself is a ghastly construct. It is composed of countless corpses roughly pressed and fused together into two massive, misshapen columns and the base they sit upon. Bodies and viscera are also messily scattered about the large plaza directly in front of the Gate. At one time in the ancient past, the corpses comprising the Gate looked much 'fresher', and the Gate appeared red and slick with fresh blood. In the present, however, the Gate appears grey, faded, and calcified, and much of the viscera in the plaza is partly buried beneath encroaching sand dunes.

Before the Age of the Erdtree, an Empyrean and Numen woman hailing from the Shaman Village named Marika travelled to the Gate and ascended to godhood, becoming the vessel of the Elden Ring. Little is known of her ascension, though it occurred during the era when the Gate was still slick and red with blood, and involved her holding a mysterious golden strand aloft in the golden light at the Gate's centre. Her ascension led to the creation of the Erdtree and the Scadutree and ushered in a new era, with Marika becoming sovereign of the Lands Between and Godfrey becoming her spouse and the first Elden Lord.

Much later, following the death of Mohg, Lord of Blood, his corpse was stolen and transported to the Land of Shadow, where Miquella would require it for an ancient ritual. At the Gate of Divinity, Miquella ascended to godhood and resurrected Radahn, using the body of Mogh as a vessel. Miquella then blessed Radahn and made him his consort. The Tarnished then defeats Radahn and Miquella, preventing the latter's "Age of Compassion".

sections.heading: Secret Rite
sections.text: The Secret Rite Scroll details the workings of the Gate of Divinity's ascension ritual. An Empyrean can reach godhood by passing through the gate. However, they cannot return until the Gate summons the soul of a champion worthy of becoming Elden Lord and binds it to the body of another Lord candidate.  Although the exact events that occur at these moments of ascension are unclear, those who meet the criteria return from the Gate in golden light, empowered as a true god.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Gate of Divinity is located at the top of Enir-Ilim. The  Gate of Divinity site of grace is unlocked by defeating Radahn, Consort of Miquella.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ghostflame Breath** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 3 Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of deathly mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 168% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 55 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. 504% of Incantation Scaling and 165 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonice.
- Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Dragonice, and Borealis's Mist), this is the most cost-effective for Magic damage, but causes considerably less Frostbite build-up.
  - Compared to Dragonice, this spell deals 25% more damage but also consumes 20% more FP and causes 50% less Frostbite build-up.
  - Compared to Borealis's Mist, this spell deals 5% more damage and consumes 15% less FP but causes 50% less Frostbite build-up.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Despite not being a named dragon breath, it behaves like one. This means that the caster floats in midair and that it cannot be cast when riding Torrent.
- This is effectively the second strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 11% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath and only 0.6% less damage than Agheel's Flame (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals 8% more damage than Rotten Breath.
  - However, the, admittedly low, Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks.
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Agheel's Flame, a stronger Fire damage version of this spell
- Borealis's Mist, a slightly weaker Magic damage version of this spell that inflicts more Frostbite
- Dragonice, a weaker but cheaper version of this spell that inflicts more Frostbite

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Giant Skeletons** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Giant Skeletons are towering spirits that lack lower limbs. They can crawl along the ground and produce a sustained stream of ghostflame from their left eyes. These enormous skeletons are summoned with oar horns by Tibia Mariners and Sanguine Albinaurics, and they vanish when their summoner is defeated.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Mohgwyn Palace - summoned by Large Sanguine Second-Generation Albinaurics
- Mountaintops of the Giants - passively summoned by Tibia Mariner
- Wyndham Ruins - summoned by Tibia Mariner

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: - Giant Skeletons do not drop items or runes upon death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- These enemies do not spawn on their own. They are summoned by other foes.
- Giant Skeletons are missing their legs like Serosh and First-Generation Albinaurics. The right side of its skull also has a massive, jagged hole.
- The sustained stream of energy is a ghostflame variant of Comet Azur, fired similar to Frenzied Burst.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Oversized social insects that fiercely defend their underground tunnels, where they feast upon gathered human remains. Red and hairy, Giant Ants grapple their prey with powerful jaws to pierce them with abdominal stingers. They can expel highly-acidic venom in viscous clumps, which solidifies into Formic Rock deposits. Their acid spray has surprising range and bypasses a shield's guard.

Giants Ants can cling to walls and even ceilings in their lairs, dropping down to swarm and ambush intruders. Others march up and down the boughs of Great Trees, foraging for resources to support their colonies.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.text:
Giant ants come in a variety of different forms:
- Giant Ant
- Giant Ant (Medium)
- Giant Ant (Saddle)
- Giant Hardhead Ant
- Giant Honeypot Ant
- Giant Winged Ant

sections.heading: Saddle
sections.text: **Saddled Giant Ants** are the reluctant mounts of Nox Swordstress, held in a trance placed by the Nox, indicated by glowing purple eyes. However, lulling the Ants to  Sleep dispels the enchantment, freeing them to turn on their former masters.

sections.heading: Winged
sections.text: **Giant Winged Ants** move faster and hover out of reach of melee attacks. Although they utilize exclusive airborne attacks, they are otherwise identical to their worker counterparts, using their moveset when grounded.

sections.heading: Hardhead
sections.text:
**Giant Hardhead Ants**, also known as **Shield-Headed Ants**, possess enlarged, heavily-armored heads that act as nigh-impenetrable shields, making them resistant to damage and tough to stagger. Their bites can inflict  Poison status, and they can spit globules of formic acid. If given the opportunity, they ram and knock enemies prone with a headbutt.

Their only weakness is their unarmored legs and abdomens, though they protect their bodies well in favorable positions.

sections.heading: Honeypot
sections.text:
**Giant Honeypot Ants**, also known as **Large Giant Ants** and **Bloated Ants**, are a voracious, highly-specialized caste rendered immobile by their enormously plump, honey-filled abdomens. Frail and utterly defenseless, they gorge themselves in heavily fortified chambers at Ainsel River and Deeproot Depths, protected by their colonies.

This variant boasts a different set of Resistances than other Giant Ants; it is not as vulnerable to  Fire damage, but is often slain with a single strike to its ballooned abdomen, which functions as a weak spot.

Honeypot Ants drop valuable items, such as Rune Arcs and Numen's Runes, but will not respawn once defeated.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Ainsel River
- Ainsel River Main
- Deeproot Depths
- Miquella's Haligtree
- Nokstella, Eternal City
- Rotted Woods

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Ants are quite susceptible to  Sleep status.
- Giant Ants have low  Poise.
- Weakness:  Fire damage

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
Giant Ant, Giant Ant (Medium), Giant Ant (Saddle), :
- Single Bite (avoided by backstepping)
- Triple Bite (avoided by double backstepping or rolling)
- Acid Spray (avoided by moving sideways)
- Grab (don't stand still in front of giant ant)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Winged Ants can die from fall damage.
- Like most non-respawning foes, Giant Honeypot Ants respawn in .
- A number of items have been fashioned out of ant body parts: Maleigh Marais created the Antspur Rapier, the spur of a giant ant which has been fashioned into a rapier, whose blade drips with scarlet rot.
- The huge head of one of the giant ants which inhabit the two underground rivers, was used without modification as a shield, excelling at repelling enemy attacks.  it also grants a boost to Immunity when wielding the shield
- Using the acidic rock dropped by the ants, a forbidden art of Depraved Perfumers releases an Acid Spraymist from user's mouth, damaging armaments and temporarily lowering Attack Power.
- Romina, Saint of the Bud, conceals an Ant's stinger.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Giant Ants are largely based on real-world ; each variant represents a different caste:
  - Giant Honeypot Ants are repletes, which store honey and sugar in their bloated abdomens for the colony to use. "**Honey**" is the filename for the Giant Honeypot Ant's abdomen.
  - Hardhead Ants are  ants, likely based on  soldiers, as they use their large, flat heads to seal colony tunnels and entrances.
  - Winged Ants are , mature ants that sprout wings and fly off to find mates and start new colonies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: Game Version **1.11** was an update that never released publicly. It is the patch that was distributed to game journalists and internet content creators so that they could make reviews for Shadow of the Erdtree in time for its public launch.

sections.heading: Differences from later versions
sections.text: This update never got any officially released patch notes from neither FromSoftware or Bandai Namco. However many reviewers made note of the Final Boss being significantly more difficult compared to the publicly released version, due to it having higher damage across the board along with one of its attack strings having such long hit-stun on each hit that once one attack in the string connected with the player then the entire rest of the string was guaranteed to land as well.

sections.heading: Map Changes
sections.text: It is also notable for having a different map design compared to the publicly released version. Sporting a different Scadutree design at the top of the map, the clouds that frame the edges being more akin to the in-game map of the Lands Between, along with the Jagged Peak not being obscured by fog.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Furious Blade of Ansbach** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Blood Oath Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Enir-Ilim
- Complete Sir Ansbach's questline while siding with him against Needle Knight Leda and defeat Promised Consort Radahn and then this Incantation (as well as Ansbach's Set and the Obsidian Lamina) can be found on his body, just to the right after entering the boss arena again.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
User dashes forward slightly before slashing twice in wide arcs with a bloodflame dagger to deal Fire damage equal to 97% of Incantation Scaling twice, before a wave of fire follows the path of the last slash to deal another burst of Fire damage equal to 154% of Incantation Scaling.

For the charged version, there are now three dagger slashes that deal damage equal to 98% of Incantation Scaling and the final burst deals damage equal to 163% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 37 points of Stamina to cast, whether charged or uncharged.
- Inflicts Blood Loss build-up, 180 for the uncharged version and 250 for the charged version.
  - Since all of the Blood Loss comes from bloodflame effects the build-up doesn't scale with Arcane, even if the Dragon Communion Seal is used.
  - For context, most enemies have a default resistance to Blood Loss of roughly 400 to 500, meaning the uncharged spell will most likely cause the Status Effect in 2-3 casts and the charged version will usually cause it within 2 casts, provided they are cast somewhat quickly after the other.
- Damage is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon when charged.
  - Since the damage of the dagger slashes already are increase by 1% the total increase is 16% for them, while the final burst has its damage increase by 6% and thus gets a total increase of 22%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.13 increased attack power, fixed a bug where the “Furious Blade of Ansbach” Incantation did not apply Hemorrhage status build up.
  - For the uncharged spell the dagger slashes had their damage increased from 90% of Incantation Scaling to 97% of the same, and the final burst had its damage increase from 145% of Incantation Scaling to 154% of the same. The charged spell's dagger slashes had their damage increased from 90% of Incantation Scaling to 98% of the same, and its final burst had its damage increase from 145% of Incantation Scaling to 163% of the same.
- Patch 1.14 cancelling this incantation into rolls will now take less time, increased poise damage, increased enemy knockback distance.
  - For the dagger hits the poise damage was increased from 4 (68 against other players) to 5 (85 against other players) and for the wave of fire the poise damage was increased from 2 (34 against other players) to 3 (51 against other players).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ghostflame Dragons** are optional bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree. They are weak to both Holy damage and anti-dragon effects.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Ghostflame Dragons are undead drakes with the innate ability to wield Ghostflame, a trait they share with the Deathbirds.

Their skeletal frames are cloaked in tattered funerary cloth, their wings sparsely feathered, and scraps of decaying flesh cling loosely to their bones. These dragons are the remains of fallen drakes that drifted into the Realm of Shadow. They possessed such vivacity that they could not fully die, becoming Those Who Live in Death.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
There are three Ghostflame Dragons in the Realm of Shadow:

- **Gravesite Plain**
  - Location: Near the  Greatbridge, North Site of Grace.
  - Details: Found asleep in the center of a swamp upon first encounter. During phase 2, it gains the ability to summon Skeletons to assist it in battle.

- **Scadu Altus**
  - Location: In a clearing near the  Moorth Highway Site of Grace.
  - Details: This Ghostflame Dragon is engaged in a skirmish with a battalion of Messmer Soldiers, Messmer Foot Soldiers, and Black Knights.

- **Cerulean Coast**
  - Location: South of the  Cerulean Coast Site of Grace.
  - Details: This dragon dramatically swoops down from the sky during its initial encounter. It summons several Skeletons each time it uses its *Ghostflame Bellow* attack.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: All Ghostflame Dragons drop a Dragon Heart and a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Ghostflame Dragons utilize a modified version of the standard Dragon movepool. Compared to other Dragons, they prefer to fight within melee range. Their Ghostflame breath attacks deal magic damage and apply Frostbite buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Ghostflame Dragons count as both Dragon and Undead enemies.
  - Ghostflame dragons are weak to both Holy damage and anti-dragon effects.
- Defeating a Ghostflame Dragon will unlock Ghostflame Breath when performing Dragon Communion.
- Multiplayer and Spirit Ashes are allowed in all Ghostflame Dragon encounters.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: These Kindred of Rot are like kin to Sir Moore. They find things and will share them with you.

sections.text: **Fire Serpent** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It's one of the Messmer's Flame Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Shadow Keep
- From the Storehouse, Back Section Site of Grace, head west to find a ladder on a banister and head up it. Head right at the top of the ladder and take the stairs to another floor and continue forwards until you reach a small balcony with a body holding this Incantation.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Creates a mote of flame that floats up in front of the caster before turning and flying towards a target, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 168% of Incantation Scaling.

If charged, Attack Power increases to 210% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 21%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total 39%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Fire Knight Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 3% when the Messmer's Helm is worn.
- Attack Power is boosted by 4% when the Fire Knight Armor is worn.
- Excellent tracking before it begins to move, able to launch even at targets that have managed to get between the caster and the flame. The tracking remains fairly good after launching.
- Has roughly 17% less Attack Power than Flame Sling with a similar casting time and the exact same FP cost. However, Flame Sling has no specific equipment that boosts only it, while Fire Serpent has several and stacking all of those means it will do roughly 1-3% more damage.
- The range is fairly mediocre. This, in combinations with the strong tracking, makes this more of a short to medium range spell.

- Magic Glintblade, another spell with good tracking that also has a delay before launching

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Glintstone Nail** is a sorcery spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Finger sorceries.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchased**: Cathedral of Manus Metyr
- Glintstone Nail may be purchased from Count Ymir for  12,000 Runes after ringing the bell in the Finger Ruins of Rhia.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
The caster releases a nail of white glintstone, dealing Magic damage with an Attack Power equal to 216% of Sorcery Scaling and 3 Stance damage.

Charging the spell increases its potency to 269% Sorcery Scaling and 5 Stance damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  10 FP per cast.
- Costs  21 Stamina per cast (27 when charged).
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- The projectile fired by this spell travels slowly but has excellent tracking.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- Finger Robe boosts attack power by 8%.
- Maternal Staff boosts attack power by 15%.
- Godfrey Icon boosts the attack power of charged attacks by 15%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Glintstone Nail is effective against distant or agile targets due to its strong tracking ability.
- The slow speed of this spell makes it easier to combo with other spells, timing it to catch targets after they dodge roll.
- Glinting Nail is a cheaper, tool version of this spell.
- Glintstone Nails is more expensive to cast but produces 6 projectiles.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is used by Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers.
- The Catacombs Sorcerers cast an unobtainable variant of this spell as a Death Sorcery. It fires a projectile in a straight line that periodically splits into glintstone nails. The main projectile can also ricochet.
- Update 1.13 increased the damage and improved the tracking of this spell.

- Since the incantation actually works by having a single "bullet" at the center that sends out the rest of the golden arc, it actually usually fares pretty well in tight tunnels and other restrictive areas.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Game Version **1.14** was released on September 11th, 2024 for Elden Ring on PlayStation, Xbox and PC. This patch is notable for adding even further adjustments many different tings that were added in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, making particularly numerous adjustments to the Final Boss of the DLC.
