sections.heading: **Final Boss balance adjustments**
sections.text:
The following adjustments have been made to the final boss of “**SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE**”

- Changed the action pattern when the battle starts.
- Adjusted some attack moves.
- Decreased the damage of some attacks.
- Decreased stamina damage of some attacks.
- Decreased the attack range of some non-weapon-based attacks.
- Improved the visibility of some attack effects.

sections.heading: **Equipment**
sections.text:
- Decreased the damage of Backhand Blades against other players. (The Smithscript Cirque's throwing attacks are not affected by this change)
- Decreased the damage of Spears’ dual wield attacks against other players.
- Decreased the damage of the Pata weapon against other players.
- The “Spread Crossbow” weapon will no longer cause the headshot damage motion when hitting another player.

sections.heading: **Skill**
sections.text:
**Scattershot Throw**

- Decreased damage against other players.
- This skill will no longer cause the headshot damage motion when hitting another player.

sections.heading: **Discus Hurl**
sections.text: - Decreased the damage animation value generated by this skill when hitting another player.

sections.heading: **Weed Cutter**
sections.text: - Decreased the poise value of follow-up attacks when using this skill against other players.

sections.heading: **Equipment**
sections.text:
- Increased the attack speed of the uncharged version of the first heavy attack for the following weapon types:

Dagger / Throwing Blade / Straight Sword / Great Sword / Colossal Sword / Heavy Thrusting Sword / Curved Sword / Twinblade Sword / Katana / Great Katana / Axe / Flail / Great Spear(Except Serpent-Hunter) / Halberd / Reaper / Whip (Except Urumi) / Hand-to-Hand Arts / Beast Claw.

- **After performing left handed attacks with weapons of the Great Katana category, cancelling into subsequent attacks using the right handed weapon will now take longer.**
- **Hand-to-Hand Arts weapon type**
  - Increased damage.
  - Shortened the recovery time between some normal attacks and follow-up attacks.
- **Colossal Sword weapon type**
  - Increased the move distance when attacking.
  - Increased the speed of the first normal attack.
- **Backhand Blade weapon type**
  - Decreased the attack speed of normal attacks from a crouching position.
- **Small Shield and Medium Shield weapon types**
  - Increased the damage negation of some shields when blocking physical attacks.
  - Increased the guard strength of some shields.
- **It will now take longer to be able to cancel into most actions after performing one-handed normal attacks with the Swift Spear.**
- **Extended the Smithscript Dagger’s throwing attacks range.**
- **Increased the attribute scaling of Rellana's Twinblade for lower Intelligence and Faith attributes.**
- **Rellana’s Cameo Talisman**
  - Reduced the delay before the damage enhancement activates.
  - Increased damage enhancement.

sections.heading: **Weapon Arts**
sections.text:
**Light**

- Increased attack speed

**Darkness**

- Increased attack speed

**Dynastic Sickleplay**

- Reduced stamina consumption
- Increased poise damage of follow-up heavy attacks.
- Increased the movement distance of the first follow-up heavy attack.
- Adjusted the damage animation recovery time when the second follow-up heavy attack hits another player.

**Shield Strike**

- Cancelling other actions to perform this weapon art will now take longer.

**Moon-and-Fire Stance**

- Increased the light wave range, poise damage, and attack speed of the stance’s normal attack.
- Increased the poise damage from the stance’s heavy attack.
- Adjusted the damage animation recovery time when a stance’s heavy attack hits another player.

**Devonia's Vortex**

- Increased attack power.
- Extended the attack range of the Great Hammer’s spin.
- Increased poise value and poise generation speed.
- Adjusted the damage animation recovery time when a charged attack hits another player.

sections.heading: **Spell**
sections.text:
**Rellana's Twin Moons**

- Increased attack range for the first and second attacks.
- Reduced the knockback distance of the second attack.

sections.heading: **Incantation**
sections.text:
**Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns**

- Increased attack power.
- Increased attack power, stamina attack power against guarding enemies.
- The close-range hitbox now follows the movement of the player

**Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom**

- Increased attack speed, increased size of the hitbox.
- Shortened recovery time between using this incantation and follow-up actions.

**Divine Bird Feathers**

- Decreased the minimum delay between consecutive hits.
- Increased range.

**Furious Blade of Ansbach**

- Cancelling this incantation into rolls will now take less time.
- Increased poise damage.
- Increased enemy knockback distance.

**Midra's Flame of Frenzy**

- Increased attack speed.
- Increased Frenzy status buildup range against enemies.
- Decreased Frenzy status buildup when using this skill.

**Bayle's Flame Lightning**

- Increased attack power.

sections.heading: **Bug Fixes**
sections.text:
- Black Pyreflies items will now correctly reappear when resting at a site of grace.
- Fixed a bug where performing a Light Greatsword heavy attack while jumping did not consume stamina.
- Fixed a bug where unintended Weapon Skills could be used when equipping the Ballista in the left hand.
- Fixed a bug that caused critical hit damage dealt to Taylew the Golem Smith when using certain weapons the be lower than intended.
- Fixed a bug that prevented the player from acquiring runes when an enemy was killed while holding a shield.
- Fixed a bug where casting the Inescapable Frenzy Incantation using the Staff of the Great Beyond would cause its hitbox to be generated incorrectly.
- Fixed a bug where whiffed backstabs with the Pata weapon had a smaller fist hitbox that intended.
- Fixed a bug where some attacks of the Lizard Greatsword weren’t registered as strike attacks.
- Fixed a bug where Euporia could increase the attack power of other weapons when its luster is restored.
- Fixed a bug where the restored luster effect of Euporia was sometimes displayed on different weapons.
- Fixed a bug where the power of some Weapon Skills of a right-handed Falx changed depending on the level of the weapon equipped in the left hand.
- Fixed a bug where the enchantment effects of certain skills were being applied to some attacks that did not use weapons.
- Fixed a bug that could cause incorrect player motions to be performed when using lock-on for the following Skills.
- Wild Strikes / Spinning Strikes / Unending Dance
- Fixed a bug that caused the Rolling Sparks Skill to go through some terrain.
- Fixed a bug where the Blades of Stone Spell did not hit targets at a different height level correctly.
- Fixed a bug where some attacks of the Bayle’s Tyranny Incantation did not hit multiple enemies.
- Fixed a bug that caused the attack of the Bayle’s Tyranny Incantation to go through certain terrain.
- Fixed a bug where Godfrey’s Icon Talisman did not apply to some Skills, Spells, and Incantations.
- Fixed a bug that prevented the player from becoming translucent when the Crepus’ Vial Talisman is equipped and the Unseen Form Spell is used.
- Fixed a bug where the hitboxes of some attacks of Rellana, Twin Moon Knight were different than intended.
- Fixed a bug where the “Leave” option could not be selected in the inventory menu for some equipment.
- Fixed a bug that made some Site of Graces difficult to touch under certain circumstances.
- Fixed a bug in some areas where the invasion spawn-in position was different than intended.
- Fixed a bug where the displayed name of certain areas was different than intended.
- Fixed a bug in which, under certain circumstances, the combat state was not released after defeating an invading NPC.
- Fixed a bug that prevented some effects from being displayed correctly.
- Fixed a bug where the Watchful Spirit Incantation’s attacks were sometimes invisible to other players in multiplayer.
- Fixed a bug where the effects of some tools and incantations were not correctly applied when trying to deflect or cancel.
- Several performance improvements and other bug fixes
- Corrected a descriptive error in the game’s credit that was incorrectly added in patch  1.12;

sections.heading: **Possible unstable performance fixes**
sections.text:
- For the PS5 version of the game, unstable framerate may be improved by using the "Rebuild Database" option from the device’s safe mode.

- In some PC versions, Ray Tracing may be unintentionally enabled and cause unstable performance. Please check the Ray Tracing setting in the "System" > "Graphics " > "Ray Tracing Quality" from the title screen or in-game menu.

- In the PC version, the message "Inappropriate activity detected" may appear without cheating. **To fix this issue, please verify the integrity of the game's files before restarting the game.**

- In the PC version, unstable framerate may be caused by third party applications that control mouse behavior.  Deactivating these third party applications may improve performance.

The version number of this update shown at the lower right corner of the Title Screen will be as follows:

**App Ver. 1.14**

**Regulation Ver. 1.14.1**

- In PS4, PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S versions, Regulation files can be downloaded by logging in to the server.
- If the Regulation Ver. listed in the lower right corner of the title screen is not1.14.1, please select LOGIN and apply the latest regulation before enjoying the game.

**Online play requires the player to apply this update.**

Further updates will be distributed in the future for you to continue to enjoy **ELDEN RING** more comfortably.

Please stay tuned for more news by following our social channels or joining us on the official **ELDEN RING Discord server here**.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Giant Dogs** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Giant Dogs are massive, monstrous hounds with oversized hind legs and underdeveloped forelegs. They are aggressive, fast enough to outrun mounted players, and lunge to bite with reckless abandon. They are exceedingly dangerous creatures with huge appetites.

sections.heading: Razor-Toothed
sections.text: These Giant Dogs have spikey white fur and razor-sharp teeth. The variants with red eyes howl upon detecting the player. This unique move alerts the other dogs to attack, much like the Foot Soldiers and Wandering Nobles with trumpets.

sections.heading: Snow
sections.text: Giant Dogs inhabiting the Mountaintops of the Giants are covered in snow and unafraid of the Beast-Repellent Torch.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Giant Dogs are found throughout Caelid.
  - A unique variant wearing a spiked collar keeps watch outside of Gowry's Shack. This guard dog has a unique move where it sprays a cloud of Scarlet Rot.
  - A pair monitors a herd of hostile Sheep near the Shack of the Rotting.
  - A pack of Giant Dogs attack the Redmanes near Redmane Castle
- A small group has gathered on the incline leading to the Hermit Merchant's Shack in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.
- Giant Dogs are found on the Mountaintops of the Giants, past the First Church of Marika.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Giant Dogs are vulnerable to many types of damage including  Standard,  Strike, and  Fire.
  - They are highly susceptible to  Sleep. A single Sleep Pot at Faith 22, Int 15 is enough to proc the status ailment.
- Giants Dogs have very low Poise and are easily Stance-broken, enabling a Critical Attack to the face.
  - Their stance can be broken with a single guard counter.
- Their attacks are easy to block or sidestep, despite their size and damage.
- Their attacks deal damage to other enemies, including other Giant Dogs.
- The standard variants are held at bay by the Beast-Repellent Torch; however, the red-eyed variants in Caelid and all snow variants on the Mountaintops of the Giants attack the player, regardless of the torch.

sections.text: **Giant crows** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The giant crows were easily recognized by their long legs, toothy beak, and black plumage. Though its wings were diminished, they enabled brief bursts of flight, making it an agile and formidable opponent. These crows were notorious for feigning vulnerability, often staggering as if injured, only to lure enemies into range for a swift and deadly grab attack with their beak.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
The **Giants' Flame** (巨人の火, *Kyojin no Hi*), also referred to as the **Flame of Ruin** (滅びの火, *Horobi no Hi*) and the **Flame of the Fell God** (悪神の火, *Akujin no Hi*), is a divine element in Elden Ring.

The flame of ruin is an ancient and inextinguishable fire capable of burning even the Erdtree itself. This power of the fell god is wielded as Giants' Flame incantations by Fire Giants and Fire Monks.

sections.heading: Background
Age of the Erdtree
sections.text:
The fell god's Flame was a forbidden subject during Queen Marika's reign. Although its presence was a native part of the Golden Order, it was anathema to Erdtree Worship. The Fire Monks were appointed to guard the Flame, and the path to the Mountaintops became Forbidden Lands. However, the Erdtree was fated to catch flame, and prophets who foresaw the cardinal sin were branded heretics and banished. The Fire Monks eventually succumbed to the Flame's allure, and worshipped it out of reverence and fear. The secrets of the Giants' Flame were documented in a Giant's Prayerbook and kept hidden by the Prelates. The Flame's ability to consume the Erdtree was later suppressed when Maliketh sealed the Rune of Death.

After the Shattering, Adan stole the Flame of the Fell God from Chief Guardian Arghanthy, and Fire Monks crusaded as far as Liurnia to reclaim it.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text: The flame of ruin continues to smolder within the forge on the northern mountaintops. It can be rekindled to burn the Erdtree and its impenetrable thorns. This unlocks the road to Crumbling Farum Azula and Destined Death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Some Fire Monks were captivated by the Black Flame, becoming Blackflame Monks.
- Only Melina or a Lord of Frenzied Flame may awaken the Giants' Flame.
- The fell god is said to inhabit the Giants' Flame.
- The champions of the Erdtree used Flame, Protect Me to bolster themselves during the War Against the Giants.
- A Flame within strengthens the body and cleanses poison and scarlet rot.
- Flame grants life to Burning Corpses.
- Giants' Flame is emulated by the Flame Chariots.
- The Furnace Golems use a variant of Flame.
- Messmerfire is closely related to the Giants' Flame.
  - Both resurrect Putrid Corpses
  - Messmer's Orb is nearly identical to the Flame of the Fell God.
  - Messmer's Kindling burns the Sealing Tree that shrouds Enir-Ilim.
  - Flare, O Serpent! follows the naming schema.
- Black Flame is closely related to the Giants' Flame.
- In the Chinese and Korean 1.0 version of the Sword and Night of Flame, Radagon is symbolized by Giants' Flame."

These incantations are used by the Chaos Followers of the Three Fingers to spread madness and destruction through the Frenzied Flame. The Frenzied Flame Seal increases the effectiveness of Frenzied Flame incantations by 20%.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Giants' Flame incantations**, also known as **Flame incantations**, are a type of Incantation spell in Elden Ring. These Fire-based incantations draw their power from the flame of ruin wielded by the Fire Giants of Flame Peak. They focus primarily on devastating attacks that can incinerate foes, unleash torrents of fire, or invoke protective flames to bolster the defenses and might of the caster. Many of these incantations demonstrate the raw, chaotic nature of fire, allowing for both area-of-effect damage and targeted assaults.

The Giant's Seal increases the effectiveness of offensive Giants' Flame incantations, except for Catch Flame, Fire's Deadly Sin, and Flame Sling.

sections.heading: Boosting Giants' Flame Incantations
sections.text:
<section begin="Giant Boost"/><section begin="Fire Boost"/>* Fire Scorpion Charm increases Fire Attack Power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Flame, Grant Me Strength increases Fire Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 30 seconds as a Body Buff.
- Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear increases Fire Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes.<section end="Fire Boost"/>
- Giant's Seal increases Attack Power by 20% when held in an active hand, and by 44% when wielded in each hand.<section end="Giant Boost"/>
  - The Giant's Seal bonus does not apply to Catch Flame, Fire's Deadly Sin, or Flame Sling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Catch Flame, Fire's Deadly Sin, and Flame Sling do not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating they are not true Giants' Flame incantations. Instead, these spells are associated with prophecies involving the Cardinal Sin.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Gladius, Beast of Night**, also known as **Tricephalos**, is a Night Lord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Gladius is a massive, demonic wolf with three heads and an extra set of forelimbs. It swings around a greatsword on a long chain and launches massive fireballs. It can split its body into three one-headed, quadrupedal versions of itself, but only the original shadow retains the flail sword. The form change is signaled by a howling roar.

Gladius may be challenged by selecting "**Tricephalos**" as the expedition target at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold. It is confronted on the third day after traveling beyond the tree door at the Spirit Shelter. Tricephalos is the first Night Lord expedition and is unlocked by default. It deals  Fire damage and is vulnerable to  Holy damage.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Damage Types
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (  ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Tricephalos Expedition.
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **NocturnalCerberus**.
- Gladius was first revealed in the initial trailer and was the only Nightlord featured in the network test.
- Among the Nightlords, Gladius is:
  - The first to be fought.
  - The last Everdark Sovereign to debut.
- The name *Gladius* derives from the Latin word for "sword," referring to the short, double-edged blades used by Roman soldiers from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD.
- Its design draws heavily from , the three-headed hound of  that guards the gates of the  to prevent the dead from leaving. This makes Gladius a fitting choice as the first Nightlord to be fought.
- In Maliketh, the Black Blade's boss area at Crumbling Farum Azula, there is a statue of a young girl surrounded by three wolves below a prehistoric depiction of the Elden Ring.
- Gladius' story is similar to that of the spirits of the Lone Wolf Ashes summon. This item, alongside the Spirit Calling Bell, were delivered to the Tarnished by Ranni the Witch, who was entrusted to do so by Torrent's former master.
- Curiously, the Tricephalos' expedition's description compares Gladius to shadows, a term similar to the Shadowbound Beasts.
- One of Everdark Gladius' attacks is the exact same used by Heolstor the Nightlord, hinting that the latter was the swordsman in Gladius' backstory.
- Gladius is reminiscent of Sif from the *Dark Souls* series:
  - Both are massive wolves who wield great swords for their boss fights.
  - They each have a bond with a swordsman, whose sword they utilize.
  - Their names may have ties with the word "sword", with Gladius' being of Latin origin and Sif's arguably sounding similar to saif of Arabic origin.
- Gladius might also hold ties to the Red Wolves. Interestingly, Gladius is weakest to Holy, which instead deals the least damage to the red wolves.

sections.text: The **Foot of the Jagged Peak** is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree. This area of the map is revealed by Map: Southern Shore.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Foot of the Jagged Peak lies on the Southern Shore, connecting the Gravesite Plain to the Jagged Peak. This craggy region is characterized by brown grass, sparse trees with few branches, and a vibrant orange sky. Fierce winds whistle around massive stones that thrust upward from the rugged earth at sharp angles. This land has felt the Ancient Dragons' red lightning, and the lifeless remains of numerous lesser dragons litter the landscape.

To reach the Foot of the Jagged Peak, start from the  Castle Front Site of Grace in front of Castle Ensis and head south to the Dragon's Pit. After defeating the Ancient Dragon-Man, exit via  Dragon's Pit Terminus and travel southeast. The path diverges at a clearing where a Jagged Peak Drake lies sleeping:

- The wooded trail heading south is patrolled by Lightning Rams and Azula Beastmen. This route leads to the  Grand Altar of Dragon Communion, where the colossal dragon's body rests. Beyond the dragon, Charo's Hidden Grave and the Cerulean Coast lie to the west.

- The northern trail passes beneath a molten rock archway. Following the mountain path, the route loops counterclockwise around the Finger Ruins of Rhia. Use the Spiritspring to ascend to the  Foot of the Jagged Peak Site of Grace, located across the bridge. The winds intensify, carrying glowing embers through the air. Climb the steep ramp past Igon and the dueling Jagged Peak Drakes to reach the Jagged Peak.

sections.text: The **First Defense of Leyndell** was an event that occurred during the The Shattering in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: At some point while the alliance of the Shardbearers still ruled over Leyndell, Royal Capital, Godefroy the Grafted, an influential member of the Golden Lineage plotted to seize control of the capital. The demigod apparently managed to recruit an army that assumed strong enough for the attack. Godefroy also made use of the special characteristic of his Shaman flesh, grafting into his body parts of corpses in an attempt to gain more strength.

sections.heading: Battle
sections.text: Godefroy and his soldiers apparently moved in the direction of Leyndell but ended up fighting around the Second Church of Marika, in the middle of Altus and well distant from even the outer walls of the capital.. The demigod and his soldiers would suffer a complete defeat at the hands of soldiers of Leyndell with their leader captured by Knight Kristoff, a member of the Ancient Dragon Cult of the capital.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text:
Godefroy was imprisoned in the Golden Lineage Evergaol with only his axe in a secluded area close to the Grand Lift of Dectus and guarded by Vulgar Militia men.
Knight Kristoff became an hero for his deed and earned the honor of Erdtree Burial. He chose to be laid to rest in the Sainted Hero's Grave, the catacomb for the warriors that took part in the War of the Ancient Dragons of whom he was a devout worshipper.

Though the capital was successfully defended, the event precipitated the deterioration of the sovereign alliance between the Shardbearers caused by the traces of the Night of Black Knives still lingering.
This would eventually lead to the demigods clashing against each other and the following wars of the Shattering.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Godefroy possessed the Godfrey Icon, a legendary talisman depicting Godfrey and Serosh, the patriarch and guide the Golden Lineage even during his imprisonment.
- It is possible that the soldiers and knights involved in the battle were buried in the richly decorated graveyard behind the Second Church of Marika and in a separate side graveyard close to it, as both these cemeteries and the sword monument in memory of the battle share the same pink flowers.
- The faction of the attackers is not explicitly confirmed, but Godefroy's involvement suggests that soldiers affiliated with the Golden Lineage and aligned with the rebel demigod were the main force.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Great Runes are mighty shards of the Elden Ring which were inherited by some of the demigods. The great strength they granted tainted the demigods, compelling them to war over control of the Lands Between.

The known Great Runes are as follows:

- *Ranni's Great Rune* (mentioned only)

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Great Runes are the shards of the Elden Ring, currently making up the Golden Order, and represent the concepts of order and discipline that the demigods enforced on the physical world. They were inherited by some of the demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal following the shattering of the Elden Ring. The mad taint of the newfound strength granted by the Great Runes precipitated the Shattering, wherein the demigods fought for control of the Lands Between. The demigods who inherited Great Runes were known as Shardbearers.

The Tarnished, upon returning to the Lands Between, were compelled by the Two Fingers to seek out demigods to relieve them of their Great Runes in order to become Elden Lord.  The Tarnished required one Great Rune to be granted audience with the Two Fingers in the inner chamber of the Roundtable Hold. They also required enough Great Runes to repair the Elden Ring before the Two Fingers would permit them to enter Leyndell, Royal Capital to have an audience with Queen Marika to become Elden Lord. During the course of the game, this is two Great Runes, however since the Shardbearer Morgott, the Omen King guards the entrance to the Erdtree and must be killed to access it, they will have at least three when granted audience. Finger Reader Enia has only ever seen two Great Runes together once before this.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- When initially obtained by the player, a Great Rune (except the Great Rune of the Unborn) would be devoid of any benediction, and had to be taken to the Divine Tower mentioned in its description, whereupon it would be restored by interacting with the image of the Great Rune above the inert Two Fingers at the summit of the tower. Further, a Rune Arc was required for The Tarnished (Protagonist) to be granted the blessing of a Great Rune after restoring it.

- The Great Runes acquired by The Tarnished were used to repair the Elden Ring in at least one ending.

- It is unknown if the Rune of Death is considered a Great Rune or an Elden Rune.

- The Great Runes reflect the demigods that inherited them. For example, Morgott's Great Rune was proof that he was born of the Golden Lineage, and the rightful Lord of Leyndell. Mohg, Lord of Blood's Great Rune was soaked with accursed blood from his devout love for the wretched mire he was born into. Morgott's and Mohg's Great Runes were naturally similar due to their bearers being twins. Malenia, Blade of Miquella's Great Rune was half-rotted but infused with Malenia's spirit of resistance.

- Miquella of the Haligtree and Ranni the Witch are the only Shardbearers known to have discarded their Great Runes. The whereabouts of Ranni's Great Rune remain unknown. Miquella relinquishes and breaks his Great Rune after the Tarnished crosses into one of three areas of the Land of Shadow: the eastern half of Scadu Altus, the Rauh Base region, or Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- "Great Rune" (GR) was the developmental codename for *Elden Ring*.
  - *Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice* contained Project "GR" assets.
- Proper names for various Great Runes were cut before release.
  - Rune of Life - In the Chinese and Korean 1.0 text Helphen's Steeple, the Golden Order Greatsword, and Icon Shield make reference to the Rune of Life, which provides the Erdtree's power and places a curse upon heroes of the Lands Between. It is presumably Marika's own Great Rune.
  - Rune of Abundance — The cut Abundance Twinblade and Abundance and Decay Twinblade, weapons make reference to "the Rune of Abundance" and the "the Rune of Decay" in their descriptions belonging to Miquella and Malenia respectively.
  - Rune of Decay
  - Rune of Grafting — In the Chinese 1.0 text, the Grafted Blade Greatsword refers to "the Rune of Grafting" (“接肢”的卢恩, *“Jiē Zhī” de Lú'ēn*), presumably Godrick's Great Rune.
  - Rune of Mind — In the Korean 1.0 text, the Dark Moon Greatsword refers to "the Rune of Mind" ("정신의 룬, *jeongsin-ui lun*), presumably Ranni's Great Rune.
- In English, Enia calls the player a Shardbearer after they acquire a Great Rune, while in Japanese she calls them .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Greater Will** is an unseen character in Elden Ring. It is a mysterious entity hailing from the lightless void and serving as the dominant force in *Elden Ring* and the history of the Lands Between. Its vassals and envoys are central to the Golden Order. Its image boosted Intelligence and Arcane.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Long ago, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, creating births and souls. The adherents of the Three Fingers consider this action to be a mistake, because it resulted in torment, despair, affliction, sins, and curses.

The Greater Will sent a star bearing its gleaming daughter to the Lands Between. It communicated with Metyr, Mother of Fingers, through the microcosm held between her tail fingers. Soon, a second, golden star containing an Elden Beast arrived in the Lands Between. This Elden Beast was the Greater Will's vision for Order, and it would later become the Elden Ring. This beast was its vassal, and the living incarnation of the concept of Order. The Greater Will has other vassals and envoys known as the Two Fingers, who speak in a cipher sign language of light.

sections.heading: Eternal Cities
sections.text: Before the age of the Erdtree, the denizens of the Eternal Cities rebelled against the Greater Will. To shield themselves from its influence, the Nox donned ritual mirrorhelms to block its intervention and that of its vassals. In an act of blasphemy, they drew the ire of the Greater Will by wielding the Fingerslayer Blade against one of its vassals. In response to this transgression, the Greater Will unleashed Astel, whose destruction of the Eternal Cities condemned them to an existence underground.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.text:
During the age of the Erdtree begun by Queen Marika the Eternal and at least the era immediately preceding it, the Greater Will's envoy Two Fingers selected Empyreans as candidates to become the God of the coming age. Queen Marika was one such candidate, and created the Golden Order by confining the Rune of Death. However, Marika would eventually shatter the Elden Ring, leading to her demigod offspring inheriting the Great Runes which in turn would trigger a war known as the Shattering. The Greater Will abandoned the demigods following the Shattering, as none managed to claim title of Elden Lord.

According to the Two Fingers, the Greater Will has not abandoned the realm, nor the life that inhabits it, proclaiming this is why the Tarnished have been extended the Guidance of Grace. After the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between following the Shattering, the Two Fingers, at the behest of the Greater Will, bade them kill the demigods in order to claim their Great Runes to become Elden Lord by becoming Marika's consort, as the Greater Will had long since renounced the demigods.

In the time of The Tarnished (Protagonist), it was discovered that the entrance to the Erdtree was blocked by impenetrable thorns, preventing anyone from becoming the Elden Lord. This caused the Two Fingers to commune with the Greater Will in search of answers, which may take thousands or tens of thousands of moons. When The Tarnished (Protagonist) suggested burning the Erdtree, which would unbind Destined Death and slay the world itself, Finger Reader Enia exclaimed that the Fingers and the Greater Will would never allow it.

After The Tarnished (Protagonist) caused the Volcano Manor's recusants to disband following the defeat of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, the recusant known as Knight Bernahl declared himself the inheritor of his comrade recusant's will. He declared their refusal to become the Greater Will's pawns and swore it would fall by his blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Greater Will is never directly referred to as an Outer God in the game. Instead the Two Fingers selected both Ranni and her Dark Moon and Malenia and her Rot as potential candidates for godhood and to forge a new Order through the Elden Ring
- The Nox Mirrorhelms presumably worked by reflecting the Greater Will and the Two Fingers' language of light.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Godwyn the Golden**, also known as the **Prince of Death,** and **First of the Dead**, is a character in Elden Ring. He was a Demigod who suffered a spiritual death on the Night of Black Knives. In the absence of a soul, his body transformed into the Prince of Death. His Erdtree Burial contaminated the Greattree roots with Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The golden-haired Prince of Death has grown to immense size, developing a scaly fish tail and webbed forearms reminiscent of basilisks. His face has warped into a grotesque, fungal-like disk, and his eyes are drained of color. Death Blight erupts from his body, drawing swarms of buzzing flies. He remains locked in the posture of his death, as if still propped up by his assassins. He wears bracelets and a tattered blue robe adorned with red and gold floral patterns.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Godwyn was born during the Age of the Erdtree to Queen Marika the Eternal and her first consort, Godfrey, making him a scion of the Golden Lineage. He emerged as a hero of the Erdtree after the end of Age of Plenty when the Ancient Dragon Gransax breached the walls of Leyndell, triggering the War of the Ancient Dragons. Godwyn played a pivotal role during the final battle with Fortissax outside Leyndell. He prevailed, but spared the dread dragon, forging a friendship that ended the war and founded the Ancient Dragon Cult.

The dragon cult worshiped the ancient dragons and studied their lightning incantations. These practices were sanctioned by the Golden Order, as lightning and Gravel Stones were imbued with gold. Godwyn learned to channel Fortissax's power to summon a storm of golden lightning. His inner circle of elite ancient dragon knights formed his personal guard, who received the largest amber medallions ever bestowed.

sections.heading: Death
sections.text: Godwyn was the first Demigod to die in recorded history, perishing on the Night of Black Knives. His stepsister, Lunar Princess Ranni, orchestrated the plot by stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and produced godslaying daggers imbued with Destined Death. The Black Knife Assassins infiltrated the royal capital and struck Godwyn, carving the half-wheel centipede into his flesh while a matching mark was etched into Ranni. The ritual caused both to suffer an incomplete death: Ranni's soul endured while her flesh destroyed; Godwyn's body remained, but his soul was gone.

sections.heading: Prince of Death
sections.text:
The soulless body of Godwyn the Golden was buried below Leyndell at the base of the Erdtree's roots, located in the Deeproot Depths. However, his spirit could not return to the Erdtree because he did not experience a true death.  Godwyn's soulless body then grew and transformed into an unrecognizable, piscine aberration known as the Prince of Death. Ancient Dragon Fortissax entered Godwyn's Deathbed Dream to fight against the Death within him, but was ultimately corrupted by the Death Blight.

Through Godwyn, the Rune of Death seeped into the Greattree roots and spread throughout the Lands Between. Soon after, the Death-Prince's distorted visage manifested itself across the realm. His eyes peered out of tendrils and vines, and even his distorted face materialized in places of Erdtree burial. This corruption sprouted Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death. Later, the roots of the Erdtree were disconnected from those below.

Wandering Mausoleums prowled the lands to recall the spirits of the soulless Demigod. Many lordsworn warriors protected these great Spirit Calling Bells, and willingly beheaded themselves in a Death rite to guard them eternally as Mausoleum Knights. Though the earth shook when the Mausoleums tolled, the spirit of Godwyn never returned. In contrast, Godwyn's innermost circle embraced his death and became the Death Knights, who quested for a cadaver surrogate to bring about the Age of the Duskborn.

Godwyn's downfall catalyzed the shattering of the Elden Ring and the subsequent Shattering War of the Demigods.  Later, the knights of Castle Sol and Miquella worked toward achieving an eclipse they believed would restore Godwyn's soul to his body. Despite their efforts, the failure of the plan contributed to the doom of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text: Fia, Deathbed Companion was the guardian of Those Who Live in Death. After recovering the half-wheel centipede taken from Godwyn's body, she makes her way to the Prince of Death's Throne.  If Fia acquires the cursemark from Ranni's body, she sleeps with Godwyn to transfer to him the strength of countless heroes and grant him a second life as the Prince of Death. If Lichdragon Fortissax is defeated within the Deathbed Dream, Fia is free to transfer the spiritual warmth and vigor of her champions to the Prince of Death. As a result of their union, she conceives the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince. She requests it be used to mend the shattered Elden Ring, integrating the principle of Life within Death into the Golden Order and ushering in an Age of the Duskborn.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Godwyn's transfigured main body rests at the  Prince of Death's Throne, located in a shallow pool of purple water at the base of a tainted root in the Deeproot Depths. It also appears within the Deathbed Dream version of the area.
- Lesser versions of Godwyn can be found at Fog Rift Catacombs, Scorpion River Catacombs, and beneath Stormveil Castle.
- Godwyn's eyes seem to appear on Death Crabs and clumps of deathroot in tainted areas across the Lands Between, such as Summonwater Village, Tombsward Catacombs, and Wyndham Ruins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Although the Prince of Death is the source of the  Death Blight, he and the  Prince of Death's Throne game area are harmless to the player.
- Godwyn was protected by a personal entourage in addition to the royal palace guard.
- After Godwyn's death, his closest allies did not agree on how to continue serving him. Godwyn's inner circle of golden knights embraced the Prince of Death and became his Death Knights, while Fortissax fought to stop the Death within his body.
- Godwyn's larger manifestations found at Fog Rift Catacombs, Scorpion River Catacombs, and Stormveil Castle are presumably the cadaver surrogates sought and protected by Death Knights.
- The Prince of Death's Pustule and Prince of Death's Cyst depict the duplication of his facial features. His cystic visage grows on the backs of Death Crabs and Giant Death Crabs living in tainted waters.
- Corpses clump together to form certain Prince of Death objects. They are likely a participating in a form of regression, similar to the gravestone accretions.
- Like his mother Marika, Godwyn is strung up and called a martyr.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Godwyn has a compound name with the suffix *wyn*, a Welsh word meaning "fair," "white," "pure," or "blessed." *Wyn* is widely used in Welsh culture as a standalone given name, a surname, or as a suffix/prefix in compound names.
- The Prince of Death's grotesque, semi-circular face is reminiscent of  (also known as bracket or shelf fungi) that grow on dead and dying trees.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Garden of Deep Purple lies at the bottom of the Stone Coffin Fissure beneath the Cerulean Coast. This is where Miquella the Kind abandoned his other half, St. Trina. When the Congealed Putrescence of the stone coffins imbibed Trina's nectar, it gained eternal rest and became her knight.

This area is reached by jumping from the bullhead of an oversized stone coffin near the  Fissure Depths Site of Grace. After falling a great distance, the player lands safely in pool of putrescent liquor in an expansive cavern filled with a deep purple haze. Patches of violet water lilies bloom radiantly admist the putrescence, alongside white flowers. Nectarblood Burgeon grows in spots where St. Trina's nectar-like blood has soaked the earth.

The  Garden of Deep Purple Site of Grace is unlocked after the Putrescent Knight is defeated. It is found outside a small tunnel leading to St. Trina's quiet inner sanctum.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Frenzied Flame Proscription** is a Site of Grace located within the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Frenzied Flame Proscription lies at the bottom of a catacombs in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, deep below Leyndell, Royal Capital. This area can only be accessed after defeating Mohg, the Omen at the Cathedral of the Forsaken. The path is concealed by an illusory wall at the altar, leading downward. However, the route is sealed off by Morgott, the Omen King, accessible only after his defeat at the Elden Throne.

The area is filled with countless mummified Nomads who play a haunting melody on their stringed instruments. The Great Caravan were immured here by Queen Marika after they were accused of harboring the Frenzied Flame. In their despair, they summoned the Three Fingers.

After navigating down the beams, jump to the bottom; the floor will collapse, delivering the Tarnished to the eponymous Site of Grace. An illusory wall opposite the Grace conceals a treasure chest containing a Rune Arc. A second illusory wall reveals a hidden path to the Deeproot Depths near the  Root-Facing Cliffs Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Lord of Frenzied Flame
sections.text:
**Warning**: Meeting the Three Fingers locks the player into the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending, an action that may only be reversed by using Miquella's Needle.

The smoldering stone door can be opened after the player unequips all Armor, initiating a cutscene in which the Three Fingers bestow the power of Frenzied Flame. Interacting with the Three Fingers causes Melina to leave permanently, vowing to kill the player Tarnished. However, the player can bypass her sacrifice by using the Fingers' flame as kindling to awaken the Flame of Ruin at the Forge of the Giants and commit the Cardinal Sin. The player can still meet the Three Fingers if they have already used Melina to burn the Erdtree. The Three Fingers do not clasp the player again if they cheat fate by inserting Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time.

If her questline has been advanced, Finger Maiden Hyetta will wait patiently on the side of the hall opposite the Site of Grace. She urges the Tarnished to seek an audience with the Three Fingers, whose sanctum lies beyond a large stone door that was partially melted by searing fingerprints. The door may only be opened once and only after unequipping all armor. After receiving the Flame of Frenzy, speak with Hyetta, who can then interpret the words of the Fingers to their chosen Lord of Frenzied Flame.

There are three ruined forge dungeons in the Realm of Shadow, each accessible from the overworld. These locations do not have bosses. Instead, an important item is looted from a large forge located at the end of the area.

The forges are filled with finished weapons and smoldering anvils. They were constructed many ages ago, when smithing was considered an act of divine significance. These sweltering workshops are home to Molten Tears, and are still operated by tireless Golem Smiths, who imbue smithscript weapons with souls.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow**, also known as the **Darkdrift Knight** and the **Night Centaur**, is a Nightlord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Fulghor was a gallant and pious centaur who, in ancient times, undertook an arduous quest in service of radiant gods that cloaked themselves in thunder. When his left arm was severed from behind, he realized his comrades had betrayed him and the gods they served.

Fulghor later encountered and embraced the Night, but his holy zeal did not falter. He channeled a sacred form of the Night's power and was consumed by battle, becoming a Nightlord and the champion of Nightglow.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow is the Nightlord fought on the final night of the Darkdrift Knight Expedition. The Darkdrift Knight is a masked, one-armed centaur with a massive sword. He is a swift, heavy-hitting boss with high mobility. During the second phase, he grows a new left arm.

- Fulghor deals  Standard and  Holy damage.
- Fulghor's greatest weakness is  Lightning damage. If he takes  Lightning damage during his power-up move, a lightning bolt strikes him from the sky. This staggers him and prevents him from casting the spell that creates golden spears beneath the players.
- Fulghor is resistant to  Holy damage and is fully immune to  Madness buildup. He is vulnerable to all other Status Ailments equally:  Poison,  Rot,  Blood Loss,  Frostbite, and  Sleep.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- Night of the Champion (first victory)
- Random Relics
- Murk
- Sovereign Sigils (Everdark Sovereign)

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text:
- HP (solo): 14,273
- HP (trio): 42,820
- HP (Everdark Sovereign): +25%
- Defense: 100
- Stance: 155
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- Cannot be parried
- Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow is scripted to stagger when hit with sufficient  Lightning damage during his powerup move. If staggered, he will not cast the spell that summons golden spears from below.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Damage Types
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (  ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.text:

- Phase 2: Amorphous Night left arm

sections.heading: Everdark Sovereign
sections.text:
- Phase 2: Amorphous Night left arm
- Phase 3: Restored left arm; gains a bow and twinblade. Hair turns from red to gold.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This Nightlord must be defeated during Ironeye's Remembrance quest.
- Fulghor appears to be blind.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: - Update 1.01.2: Defeating Fulghor will not advance the Revenant's remembrance quest, despite being listed as a possible choice.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **Centaurus**.
- Fulghor was the second Everdark Sovereign to debut.
- Among the Nightlords, Fulghor is the only one whose title is not simply just "of Night", rather "of Nightglow".
- During the Everdark fight, Fulghor's glowing cross bears some resemblance to Miquella's Cross.
- Also in his Everdark form, Fulghor is able to air-walk, not unlike Spirits such as Torrent and the Ancestor Spirit.
- Fulghor shares some characteristics with Gundyr from the *Dark Souls* series:
  - Their heavy build, armor, and helmet design.
  - Their transformation with an oversized, left arm of darkness.
  - Their alternate encounter, with both as their non-afflicted selves.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Glintstone Crowns** are a group of Headwear in Elden Ring. They are granted to Glintstone Sorcerers whose pursuits at the Academy of Raya Lucaria were deemed worthy, indicating the conspectus to which they belong. The nine stone masks each resemble the founder of their associated field of study and are set with glintstones of varying color.

Performing the "Erudition" gesture while wearing certain glintstone crowns causes the crystals to shine brightly and unlocks the puzzle at Converted Fringe Tower.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Witch's Glintstone Crown variant worn by Sorceress Sellen's second body, which features a larger crystal, is unobtainable.
- Four additional variants are also unobtainable: a Karolos crown with light blue crystals, a Lazuli crown with red crystals, an Olivinus crown with yellow crystals, and a Twinsage crown with purple and magenta crystals.
- Graven Masses are formed from the glintstone crowns of sacrificed scholars.
- Alberich's Pointed Hat and Alberich's Pointed Hat (Altered) feature red glintstones but aren't true glintstone crowns, as Thorn Sorceries are disdained by the Academy.
- Although Sorcerer Thops's pursuits warranted a new conspectus and crown in his image, his contemporaries deemed them unworthy. Consequently, he never received a glintstone crown.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Hoarah Loux, Warrior**, also known as **Godfrey, First Elden Lord** and the **Lord of the Battlefield**, is a mandatory boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Godfrey is a former consort of Queen Marika the Eternal and the first Elden Lord of the Golden Order. Although his actions directly shaped much of the history of the Lands Between, Queen Marika stole his grace and banished him to the badlands.

Both encounters with Godfrey are mandatory boss fights:
1. The first encounter, **Godfrey, First Elden Lord**, is a golden phantom from the past that ambushes the player at Leyndell, Royal Capital. Defeating this Great Enemy boss unlocks the  Erdtree Sanctuary Site of Grace and grants a Talisman Pouch and access to Marika's Bedchamber.
1. The second battle is at the Elden Throne in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. The real **Godfrey, First Elden Lord** transforms into **Hoarah Loux, Warrior** during the fight. Defeating this Legend boss grants the Remembrance of Hoarah Loux and access to the Stone Platform inside the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Lord Godfrey was once known as Hoarah Loux, a simple, yet ferocious warrior with a ceaseless lust for battle. He was an unmatched champion who earned his right to Lordship through sheer strength. Later, he took the name Godfrey when he took the spirit of Serosh upon his back. The Lord of Beasts suppressed his rage,allowing him to conduct himself in a manner befitting Marika's first Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.text:
Before it came to be an embodiment of Order, everything was in opposition to the Erdtree. Godfrey led Marika's golden armies in the War Against the Giants, a decisive conflict thay ended with the Giants' defeat and the confinement of the Fell God's Flame of Ruin. This war heralded the birth of the Erdtree, and the beginning of an age of Order ruled over by Marika and her Elden Lord.

The age of the Erdtree began amidst conflict, and Godfrey was regarded as the "Lord of the Battlefield." He fought the Storm Lord alone and emerged the new lord of Stormveil. Later, during the siege of Castle Morne, Godfrey bested a lone hero who wielded a grafted blade and fought for vengeance. Godfrey was commander of the Crucible Knights, and Ordovis and his men honored their master by wearing the crest of the axe, a symbol of Godfrey's.

Godfrey and his offspring with Queen Marika were the first Demigods, known as the Golden Lineage. His bond with Serosh became an emblem of this lineage, guiding them as they conquered the Lands Between. Godfrey's double-headed axe symbolized his warrior's vow of conduct and would later become a symbol of the Golden Lineage.

sections.heading: The Long March
sections.text:
At the end of his campaign, Lord Godfrey's golden armies remained unvanquished and unbowed. When his last enemy fell, it was said that the golden hue of Godfrey's eyes faded. He found his Grace lost, tattered, and faded.

Godfrey and his warriors were then informed by Queen Marika that she had divested them of their Grace. She drove them from the Lands Between to wage war in a distant land, where they would live and die. Marika promised Godfrey and his men that after their deaths, they would regain what she had taken from them. They would return to the Lands Between with the strength required to brandish the Elden Ring.

Thus, Godfrey and his kinfolk became the Tarnished. They left the Lands Between together on a pilgrimage known as the Long March, at the end of which Godfrey divested himself of kingship and became a simple warrior once more.

Godfrey became a chieftain of the Badlands under the name of Hoarah Loux. The head of his axe had been broken in a battle fought during the Long March. His loyal warriors honored him by wielding axes of their own, and they became the weapon of choice for Badlands chieftains.

sections.heading: Return to the Lands Between
sections.text: At some point, Hoarah Loux died. However, when the Elden Ring was shattered following the death of his son Godwyn the Golden, the Tarnished that died outside the Lands Between were returned to life by the call of their long-lost Grace. The Tarnished, who had grown strong in the face of death, crossed the fog and returned to the Lands Between, to stand before the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. Godfrey was among those who made their way back to the Lands Between.

sections.heading: The Ashen Capital
sections.text:
After the Tarnished champion has claimed the Great Runes, burned the Erdtree, and unbound the Rune of Death, they return to the city of Leyndell and approach the Erdtree. At the Elden Throne, they find Godfrey, Serosh on his back, mourning the death of his son Morgott, whom the Tarnished had previously slain.

Godfrey rises to his feet and addresses the Tarnished. He acknowledges their effort; however, he declares his intention to seek an audience once again. The two Tarnished do battle, and Godfrey finds himself overpowered. The former Elden Lord grabs the head of Serosh, thanks him for his service, and then tears him from his back. Drenched in the blood of his loyal regent, Godfrey resumes the fight, now as the savage Hoarah Loux. Nevertheless, the Tarnished defeats Hoarah Loux, who declares that their strength befits a crown.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: This is a boss fight against a golden, spectral version of Godfrey. He is fought within the Erdtree Sanctuary, accessed by climbing up a large root south of the West Capital Rampart Site of Grace. This battle is **not** optional as he must be defeated to progress Leyndell further and continue the story. Compared to the later encounter, this version of Godfrey has a greatly reduced moveset, mainly consisting of close-range axe swings. He can create areas of effect by stomping or smashing his axe into the ground, and he may also throw his axe at the player from a distance.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: Godfrey is fought in a long, fairly spacious room. There is a narrower, lower section to the left of the entrance, as well as various pillars which may restrict movement or allow one to gain distance from the boss.

sections.heading: Leyndell, Ashen Capital
sections.text: Nepheli Loux, Warrior and Shabriri are both available as summons for this fight, provided their questlines have been completed. Like the first battle, this fight is **not** optional and must be defeated to reach the final bosses of the game.

sections.heading: Phase 1 - Godfrey, First Elden Lord
sections.text:
Godfrey will usually initiate the fight by throwing his axe at the player and then dashing after it.

Godfrey has a stomp attack similar to that of the Crucible Knights, causing spikes to come out of the ground that are easier to dodge by jumping than to i-frame with a roll. He will generally follow up on the spike stomp with a series of axe swings, but can do a second stomp at any time, even repeatedly.

Godfrey's primary offense will be axe swing combos. They can be dodge rolled safely and involve enough delays for the player to sneak in a hit before having to dodge again.

He retains his moves from the earlier fight, with the addition of more close-range axe attacks and some abilities that generate earthquakes.

sections.heading: Phase 2 - Hoarah Loux, Warrior
sections.text:
After his health drops below 50%, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Godfrey no longer has Serosh or his axe, and has an almost entirely new, grappling-based fighting style.

Phase 2 always starts with him rushing towards the player with a delayed command grab. He will always briefly go into slow-motion mid-jump, which can roll-catch. He will attempt to grab the player like this multiple times over the course of phase 2. Properly rolling out of the way of it gives you one of the largest time windows to attack him out of his entire phase 2.

He will do many other grab attacks, ground-slams, leap attacks, delayed kicks and delayed stomp attacks. Panic-rolling and blocking is not recommended.

When he begins to crack the ground after a leap attack by smashing his hands into the ground, the player must run away from him as far as they can, otherwise they will get blown up by an explosion that is very difficult to roll through. He often announces this attack by knocking the player away from him with a roar.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles. It is the same arena where Morgott, the Omen King was fought previously.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating the golden **Godfrey, First Elden Lord** at Leyndell, Royal Capital for the first time unlocks the "Godfrey, First Elden Lord" achievement.
- Defeating **Hoarah Loux, Warrior** at Leyndell, Ashen Capital for the first time unlocks the "Hoarah Loux, Warrior" achievement.
- Godfrey wears the Elden Lord Set (Elden Lord Crown, Elden Lord Armor, Elden Lord Bracers, Elden Lord Greaves).
- Godfrey's lordly posture is maintained by Serosh, whose teeth sink into his left shoulder for the fight. These actions help suppress Godfrey's bloodlust.
  - How Serosh is anchored to Godfrey is similar to how Miquella attaches himself to Promised Consort Radahn. Their entwinement also parallels twin stalks of the Scadutree.
  - Serosh's crown bears an uncanny resemblance to the Elden Lord crown.
- The Axe of Godfrey was unbroken when he gained Serosh and vowed to become a Lord.
  - The axe wielded by the golden phantom version of Godfrey is unbroken and features twin blades, suggesting it represents Godfrey before the Long March.
  - Statues of Godfrey with Serosh and an undamaged axe are found at the Roundtable Hold and in the Stormveil Castle throne room.
  - There is a portrait of Godfrey with a broken axe in Stormveil Castle's main hall, which is guarded by a Grafted Scion. This was likely painted after Godfrey returned to the Lands Between.
  - The Axe of Godfrey strongly resembles the Beastman's Cleavers made by Azula Beastmen.
- Hoarah Loux, Warrior is a highlander.
  - Highlanders are mighty warriors capable of subduing beasts with sheer strength. While most wore blue, only the greatest bear hunters were permitted to wear red. Lord Godfrey is draped in blue, while Hoarah Loux is soaked in red beast blood.
  - The Highland Axe is found directly beneath a large portrait of Godfrey in the main hall of Stormveil. Godfrey’s kinfolk wielded these axes during the Long March.
  - Both Hoarah Loux and the highlanders begin battle by shouting their names.
  - Hoarah Loux roars like a Runebear and Ash of War: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker is used by Great Red Bears.
  - Just as Godfrey discards the golden lion to become Hoarah Loux, a nameless Redmane forsook the red lion to become Red Bear. Both cover themselves in red after besting savage beasts with their bare hands.
  - The  Brave's Battlewear, once the traditional garb of Godfrey's kin, was later repurposed into the Gloried Attire.
- Nepheli Loux, Warrior shares the surname "Loux" with Hoarah Loux, implying a familial or clan relationship.
  - If her questline is completed in her favor, Nepheli may be summoned as a cooperator against Godfrey and Serosh.
  - Although her exact relation is unclear, her age and warrior culture likely make her Godfrey's daughter or a close descendant born after he reverted to Hoarah Loux. Her relationship with Sir Gideon Ofnir may indicate that Godfrey was recalled to the Lands Between when she was young.
  - Godfrey became the lord of Stormveil Castle after defeating the Storm Lord in single combat, establishing the Golden Lineage as the rightful rulers of Limgrave. After the Stormhawk King bonds with Nepheli,  Kenneth Haight recognizes her as part of Hoarah Loux’s bloodline, and declares Nepheli the rightful heir to Limgrave.
  - Nepheli Loux claims she swore an oath when she became a warrior. Godfrey also made a vow upon becoming Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Godfrey has a wide range of dialogue lines that cut from the game. At one point, he would have directed the player to cross the Sea of Fog to reclaim the Elden Ring.
- Godfrey had a few differences in .
  - He had two health bars.
  - He delivered an extra line upon defeating the player in phase one: *"Tarnished Warrior. 'Twas nobly fought. Thy rest is well deserved."*
  - Upon death, Hoarah Loux laughed heartily after saying, *"Brave Tarnished. Thy strength befits a crown."*
- Much of Godfrey's character shares ties with the mythical Greek hero, Heracles. Godfrey possesses earthshattering strength, endured harsh trials to earn his godhood, slew the mightiest of the Giants, has a connection with lions through Serosh, and he even enters a berserker state.
- There are also parallels between Godfrey and Arthur, the legendary King of Britain, with both being great warriors once presiding over a lost golden age, and with Arthur himself being away - but prophesied to one day return, reclaim his rule and save his people. Other parallels include the round table seen at the Roundtable Hold, and his chief Crucible Knights, Ordovis and Siluria, being named for ancient Celtic tribes in Pre-Roman Britain.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: is a Boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer encountered in Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Godrick is a descendant of the Golden Lineage, the bloodline that began with Queen Marika the Eternal and her first consort Godfrey. Only a distant relation of Marika's line, his divine blood was sorely diluted, and he was viewed as the runt of the litter. Godrick idolized the first Elden Lord, desiring his ancestor to witness his feats. He wielded an axe emblazoned with a lion, a symbol of Godfrey, and furnished his army with the Erdtree and Serosh emblems of the Golden Lineage. Though he styled himself “lord of all that is golden,” he commanded far less respect than his forebear and was despised by many of his own servants.

After the Elden Ring was shattered, Godrick inherited the Great Rune from the center of the Elden Ring, referred to as the anchor ring. During The Shattering, he was hounded from Leyndell, Royal Capital. He claimed a multitude of treasures, including the Mimic's Veil, and hid among the womenfolk to flee the city. Godrick made his way south, settling in Limgrave with an army of soldiers who had fled Leyndell. He took up residence in Stormveil Castle, using it as a refuge to hide from General Radahn. When Malenia marched southward, Godrick insulted her, leading to a confrontation that left him beaten and humiliated, forced to beg for mercy.

Godrick again retreated to Stormveil Castle to practice grafting, the forbidden art of attaching the parts of other beings to oneself to gain power. When the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between, Godrick sent his soldiers on Tarnished hunts, seeking new subjects to graft. He also produced Grafted Scions; abhorrent beings comprised of many different limbs, seemingly grafted onto children.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
The Tarnished journeys to Stormveil Castle in search of Godrick's Great Rune, on the advice of White Mask Varré and Melina. The castle shows many examples of his grafting: severed limbs hanging in the dining hall, a dismembered Troll over a courtyard, and piles of corpses, including the companions of Roderika. Eventually the Tarnished finds Godrick in a graveyard, addressing a dead dragon impaled on a statue. He grafts the dragon's head to his own arm mid-fight, but is defeated, and his Great Rune is claimed.

Later, Nepheli Loux can become the lord of Limgrave at the appointment of Kenneth Haight.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text: The fight begins after a cutscene. Godrick primarily uses his axe and enlarged left arm, generating cyclones and quakes for area-of-effect damage. He rolls to reposition and uses a homing wind projectile.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: At roughly 60% HP, a cutscene plays, and he grafts the dragon's head to his arm. He gains ranged and area fire attacks layered onto his Phase 1 kit.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The arena is a narrow, paved approach flanked by graveyards, with a wider entrance near the steps. Movement through gravestones is possible, but it can hinder dodging.

sections.heading: Boss Fight

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **HUD** (heads-up display) in Elden Ring displays several pieces of information, listed below. When the HUD display setting is set to Auto, the HUD will automatically be hidden, except for the compass. Press the [△/Y] button to temporarily display and check the HUD.

sections.heading: HP Gauge
sections.text:
Current HP (life force). It decreases as you take damage, and you die when it reaches 0.

HP can regenerate by resting at a Site of Grace, using the Flask of Crimson Tears, or reading incantations.

sections.heading: FP Gauge
sections.text:
The power to stay focused in order to use skills and sorcery. It decreases as you use skills and sorcery, and it becomes ineffective when it reaches zero.

FP can regenerate by resting at a Site of Grace or using the Flask of Cerulean Tears.

sections.heading: Stamina Gauge
sections.text: This is your current stamina. When it reaches zero, you won’t be able to perform any further actions that consume stamina. Stamina automatically regenerates as time passes. Stamina is not consumed while in a non-combat state.

sections.heading: Status Icons
sections.text: When a special effect is active, such as an ability boost, the corresponding status icon will be displayed.

sections.heading: Compass
sections.text: Displays the direction. The location of runes that are dropped when you die and landmarks will also be displayed.

sections.heading: Lock-on Marker
sections.text: Press the [R3/R] button to lock onto a nearby enemy as a target. You can change targets using the right stick.

sections.heading: Currently Available Skills
sections.text: This displays the currently available skills.

sections.heading: Equipment Slot
sections.text: The icon of the currently equipped weapon, sorcery, or item will be displayed.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Sorcery
sections.text: This is the currently selected sorcery. It cannot be used unless a catalyst has been equipped.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Left-Hand Weapon
sections.text: This is the weapon that is currently equipped in the left hand.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Item
sections.text: This is the currently selected item and the next item to be displayed.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Right-Hand Weapon
sections.text: This is the weapon that is currently equipped in the right hand.

sections.heading: Action Dialog
sections.text:
The corresponding action will be displayed here.

It indicates how long it will take for you to change to and from an abnormal state. A list of abnormal states can be found below

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Forms the roaring skull of Greyoll upon casting, inflicting Physical damage and knockback to nearby enemies while also reducing the defense and attack of all hit by 10% and 15% respectively.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

This includes the two moon sorceries Rennala's Full Moon and Ranni's Dark Moon, the Shriek of Milos of the Sword of Milos, Acid Spraymist, and the Soul Stifler skill of the Winged Greathorn.
- Knocks down human-sized foes.
- Deals 17 Stance damage, about on par with an uncharged heavy attack from Great Hammers.

sections.text: **Grave Warden Duelists**, **Frenzied Duelists**, and **Putrid Grave Warden Duelists** are recurring enemies and bosses in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Duelists are muscular warriors lightly accoutered in bronze armor adorned with serpent effigies, which represent a traitor to the Erdtree. Whether armed with a Duelist Greataxe and iron ball or twin Battle Hammers, they are unrelenting fighters blessed with boundless stamina.

During the time of Lord Godfrey, these champions honored the Erdtree by participating in gladiatorial combat at colosseums. Their excited spectators were delighted to see the serpents on their armor get battered and broken. However, the gladiators were banished when the colosseums closed during the age of Lord Radagon. While many of them served as Erdtree Burial grave wardens in the catacombs, others became rampaging Mad Pumpkin Heads. Some Grave Warden Duelists now fester with the baleful scarlet rot.

sections.heading: Grave Warden Duelist (Greataxe)
sections.text:
These Grave Warden Duelists wield colossal Duelist Greataxes. A chain dangles from the greataxe’s pommel, terminating in a solid iron sphere.

The shadowy Grave Warden Duelist in the Sainted Hero's Grave is immune to damage until it is lured into a circle of holy light, marked by an Erdtree Burial spell sigil.

sections.heading: Grave Warden Duelist (Battle Hammer)
sections.text: These Grave Warden Duelists fight with a pair of heavy Battle Hammers tethered together by an iron chain.

sections.heading: Putrid Grave Warden Duelist (Greataxe)
sections.text: These axe-wielding Duelists have been corrupted by Scarlet Rot, which has stained their armor red. Their helms are crowned with many snakes, and when they grab a foe the bronze snake coiled around their arms will come alive and bite them, inflicting  Scarlet Rot. One can be found in the Consecrated Snowfield to the north of Ordina, Liturgical Town.

sections.heading: Putrid Grave Warden Duelist (Battle Hammer)
sections.text: These hammer-wielding Duelists have been corrupted by Scarlet Rot, which has stained their armor red. Their helms are crowned with many snakes, and when they grab a foe, the bronze snake coiled around their arms will come alive and bite them, inflicting  Scarlet Rot. One can be found in the Consecrated Snowfield, west of the  Consecrated Snowfield Site of Grace.

- The fighting lion motif associated with the Golden Lineage appears on the guard, though this detail is difficult to see in-game.
- While the Dexterity scaling is a good bit stronger than expected it will only exceed the benefits of the Strength scaling when the final softcap of 80 (54 if using both hands) Strength is reached.

sections.heading: Trivia

- The Chinese and Korean  release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "*A special greatsword created by joining together the swords of warriors who once served Godfrey. It is imbued with the power of the Rune of Grafting.*"

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Great Knife** is a Dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Starting equipment for the Bandit class.
- 2% drop chance from Small Demi-Humans.
  - The earliest farming spot is just inside Lakeside Crystal Cave, where once can be found hiding inside of a bush next to another, regular Demi-Human.
  - The most efficient farming spot is just north of the Craftsman's Shack Site of Grace on Mt. Gelmir, where four of them are hiding amongst a flock of Sheep.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Leans more towards the various Dexterity- and Arcane-scaling affinities.
  - Pairs well with the similarly Dex/Arc-leaning Reduvia as an off-hand weapon for dual wielding.
  - Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
  - Its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
  - While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.
- Curiously, the Strength-scaling of the Keen affinity is actually stronger than that of the Standard affinity, despite the Keen affinity usually greatly decreasing the Strength-scaling of the weapon.
- On the shorter side of daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Golden Order Seal** is a Sacred Seal and catalyst in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found inside the Minor Erdtree Church, located between the two ramparts of Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- Enhances Golden Order Fundamentalist incantations by 10%.
- Scales equally well with Intelligence and Faith for the purpose of casting Incantations, and boosts the effect of directly damaging Golden Order Incantations if held in an active hand (does not need to be used for casting the spell).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Only the Faith portion of its scaling applies to Healing and Weapon Buff incantations, most notably making it rather unsuitable for casting Order's Blade.
  - The strongest faith scaling of the hybrid seals at 159%, though that is barely over half of the faith only seals (averaging 250%).
- Incantations boosted by 10% when this seal is held in an active hand (not necessarily cast through) is Discus of Light, Triple Rings of Light, and Radagon's Rings of Light. Most notably, Law of Causality and Order's Blade is not boosted.
- Like most of the weightless seals, it lacks a Strength scaling for its Physical damage.
- Scales best with an equal split of Intelligence and Faith.
  - A 17/17 split (minimum requirements) gives 150 Incantation Scaling.
  - A 45/17 or 17/45 split (reaching one middle softcap) gives 244 Incantation Scaling.
  - A 80/17 or 17/80 split (reaching one of the highest softcaps) gives 270 Incantation Scaling.
  - A 45/45 split (reaching both middle softcaps) gives 338 Incantation Scaling, comparable to an Erdtree Seal gaining 353 Incantation Scaling at 80 Faith.
- For casting Incantations with a faith requirement below 17, the Frenzied Flame Seal is potentially better due to much lower Attribute requirements (none at all) but is attainable only later, and requires completing Lightseeker Hyetta's questline and at least partially committing to her Ending.
