sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Godskin Apostles** are Bosses in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Lanky humanoids clad in robes sewn together from patches of smooth skin. The Godskin Apostles were led by the Gloam-Eyed Queen, who cradled them as newborns in a swaddling cloth made from skin much like their robes. They served Destined Death, and wielded god-slaying black flame. However, when Maliketh, the Black Blade, sealed away the Rune of Death, the flame's true power was lost.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Dominula, Windmill Village
- Spiritcaller Cave
- Divine Tower of Caelid

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Godskin Apostle at the highest point of Dominula, Windmill Village oversees the Dominula Dancer's Dominula Festival. Torrent may be used during this fight. Millicent is available as a summon for this fight, provided she has been given the Valkyrie's Prosthesis.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Godskin Apostle is found at the bottom of the Divine Tower of Caelid, guarding a chest containing the Godslayer's Greatsword. To reach this boss, the player must complete a platforming section through the inside of the tower, which includes encounters with Redmane Knights and Blackflame Monks.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The spirit of a Godskin Apostle, along with that of a Godskin Noble, is summoned by the Spiritcaller Snail at the end of Spiritcaller Cave in the Mountaintops of the Giants. The Apostle must be defeated first, followed by the Noble, before the snail appears and can be killed to end the fight.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A duo consisting of a Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble, encountered in the  Dragon Temple within Crumbling Farum Azula. They share a health bar and have their own individual health. If one is killed, the other will resurrect them shortly. If both are killed before the shared health bar reaches 0, the Noble will respawn and summon the Apostle shortly.

 Sleep is highly effective against both enemies and temporarily incapacitates them when inflicted. Recusant Bernahl is available as a summon for this boss.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Godskin Nobles** are a reoccurring enemy and boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Godskin Nobles are stout humanoids who wear robes sewn together from patches of soft skin, featuring seven-faced aprons. They are the most ancient of the apostles who once served the Gloam-Eyed Queen, incorporating inhuman physiology, not unlike the primordial crucible.They wield elegant thrusting swords with skill unmatched by lowborns, and wield black flame like the Godskin Apostles.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Godskin Noble fought in the Temple of Eiglay in Volcano Manor, in front of a serpentine altar bearing the Serpent's Amnion. This boss drops the Godskin Stitcher and the Noble Presence incantation.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Godskin Noble who leads on the bridge from the Carian Study Hall to the Divine Tower of Liurnia. This encounter does not have a boss health bar, and spirit ashes cannot be used for the fight, however the enemy does not respawn when killed.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The spirit of a Godskin Noble, along with that of a Godskin Noble, is summoned by the Spiritcaller Snail at the end of Spiritcaller Cave in the Mountaintops of the Giants. The Apostle must be defeated first, followed by the Noble, before the snail appears and can be killed to end the fight.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A duo consisting of a Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble, encountered in the Dragon Temple within Crumbling Farum Azula. They share a health bar, as well as having their own individual health. If one is killed, the other will resurrect them after a short amount of time. If both are killed before the shared health bar reaches 0, the Noble will respawn and summon the Apostle after a short amount of time.

Sleep is highly effective against both enemies, and will temporarily incapacitate them when inflicted. Recusant Bernahl is available as a summon for this boss.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wears Godskin Noble Bracelets, Godskin Noble Hood, Godskin Noble Robe, and Godskin Noble Trousers
- Wields Godskin Stitcher and Godslayer Incantations
- The embroidered shape at the bottom of the robe completes a ring of eight surrounding a central design, both of which appear on the Blue Festive Garb, worn by Celebrants given a key role in the Dominula Festival. The gold embroidery resembles undulating horns or flames.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **God-Devouring Serpent**, also known as the **elder serpent**, **great serpent**, and **Serpent King**, is an optional Demigod boss in Elden Ring. The God-Devouring Serpent is the first phase of the fight against Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. Defeating this boss triggers a cutscene that initiates the battle with Rykard. It must be defeated to advance Tanith's questline.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The great serpent is an enormous blue snake with arms and an affinity for both lava sorceries and poison. This boss is weak to the Serpent-Hunter's Great-Serpent Hunt, the true power of which activates during this encounter.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Hated for its tremendous and insatiable gluttony, the elder serpent of Mt. Gelmir is an immortal terror that seeks to one day consume the entire world. It has been repelled by the white light of the Serpent-Hunter since ancient times. A cult on Mt. Gelmir practiced hexes and performed human sacrifices in reverence to a heretical serpent god. Over time, these practices ceased, and their Gelmir Sorcery was lost.

During the reign of Queen Marika, it was rediscovered by the Demigod Rykard. During the Shattering, Praetor Rykard willingly allowed the great serpent to devour him. Although his Gelmir Knights obtained the legendary Serpent-Hunter weapon, they failed to defeat their former lord. Now, the great serpent and Rykard share a single body as the Lord of Blasphemy, engaging in an appalling birthing ritual that spawned the Man-Serpents. They devour countless champions with the ultimate goal of consuming the gods and the world itself.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The God-Devouring Serpent can be found at the Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir, near the  Audience Pathway site of grace.

sections.text:
- HP: **30,739**
- Defense: **?**
- Stance: **?**
- Deals  Standard and  Fire damage, and inflicts  Poison buildup.
- Weakness: Serpent-Hunter
- Vulnerable to  Frostbite.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Godskin Duo** is a boss battle where you have to battle against a Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble at the same time. They can be found in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is **not** an optional boss as they must be defeated to advance further in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
The Godskin Duo share one health bar of around 24000 HP (NG), but also still have their own HP. If one is killed, it will either respawn automatically after ~15 seconds or the other Godskin will reanimate them. They will also still enter phase 2 if dropping close to 50% in individual HP.

The pillars within the arena are an effective way to separate them, although their phase 2 attacks will demolish the upper portion of them. In addition, both of them can be parried.

Sleep Pots can serve as a way to buy time as both bosses can be rendered temporarily paralyzed by sleep status.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Golden Order Greatsword** is a Greatsword, a melee armament in Elden Ring. It is one of the Legendary Armaments.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Received upon defeating the Misbegotten Crusader in Cave of the Forlorn, located in the Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
While a pure Faith build would be expected to be strongest investment in terms of pure Attack Rating (AR) for this weapon, after Faith reaches 50 Dexterity will grant roughly equal AR until it also reaches 50. The first option will grant stronger casting, more damage from the skill and potentially also higher melee damage if an enemy has lower or equal Holy defence to its Physical defence. The second option grants slightly quicker casting and potentially slightly better damage if an enemy has higher Holy defence than Physical defence.

This is one of the few weapons that deal 20% bonus damage to Undead enemies such as Skeletons and Death Rite Birds and will also prevent the former from resurrecting without needing an extra hit to finish them off.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Despite its description saying it is made of pure light it is actually of average weight among the Greatswords and is not one of the game's two weightless weapons, the Coded Sword and the Cipher Pata.
- The Chinese and Korean  release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "*A greatsword guided by the one and only Rune of Life. The overflowing golden light became a blade without substance. The embodiment of the power of the Erdtree itself.*"  The role of Carian matrimonial sword was instead filled by the Sword of Night and Flame.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Guardian Golems** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
<onlyinclude><section begin="bg" />Golems are giant stone warriors said to have been made with an impure crystal by a golem crafter long ago. They were built to defend a civilization now gone to ruin. Though many are long broken, some golems still protect the ancient ruins.

Their hard, stone bodies are very resistant to physical damage, and Fire and lava can be seen through the plates on their chests. They can eject streams of fire through their helmet. Many golems carry massive Golem's Halberds with surprising reach that can tear the earth asunder. Others fire Golem Greatbows with great precision.<section end="bg" /></onlyinclude>

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Halberd)
sections.text: A golem carrying massive Golem's Halberd with surprising reach that can tear the earth asunder. It can eject streams of fire through its helmet.

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Greatbow)
sections.text:
A golem carrying a massive greatbow. It pulls back the hardy string with its immense strength to shoot great arrows infused with the storm.

Almost defenseless at melee range since they can't point their bow further down at that point. The actual danger lies mostly in approaching them, after that the stomps should be of minimal difficulty.

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Magic Halberd)
sections.text: Be wary of the instance of this enemy on the cliffs just east of the Minor Erdtree in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow that wields a magically infused halberd, as it is extremely powerful and capable of using the halberd to summon three orbs that shoot a very destructive magical beam.

sections.heading: Guardian Golem (Magic Greatbow)
sections.text: Be wary of the Golems that guard the approach to the Great Jar of Caelid, as their arrows unleash a magical explosion upon landing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Cannot be Parried.
- Immune to all Status Effects.
- They topple and collapse to the ground when their Stance is broken, exposing a Critical Attack spot on their chests.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Guardian Golem, a boss variant found in Highroad Cave

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Golden Lightning Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Guaranteed Drop:** Crumbling Farum Azula
- Drops from a Scarab south of the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, near an Ancient Dragon.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Lightning damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for caster and allies within a 6 meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Overall a very strong defensive incantation, and one that comes just before the final Lightning-heavy area in the game, Crumbling Farum Azula, and the Dragonlord, one of the more Lightning-focused bosses in the game.
- Since it doesn't actually apply a flat increase to damage negation, just the damage taken, the actual effective new damage negation (the one shown on the character screen) can be calculated with the following formula: 1 - (1 - (current Lightning damage negation)/100) * (1 - 0.60).
  - As an example, if Lightning damage negation before casting the incantation is 25.000 the result becomes this: 1 - (1 - 25.000/100) * (1 - 0.60) = 0.7, or 70.0% Lightning damage negation.
  - Against other players, simply replace the 0.60 with 0.20 for a new end result of 40.0% Lightning damage negation.
- Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher Lightning damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell the less effective it may appear to be in the statistics.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Barrier of Gold
- Boltdrake Talismans, a talisman granting Lightning damage negation
- Lightning Fortification, a weaker, personal version of this incantation
- Lightningproof Dried Liver, a consumable item granting much weaker damage negation
- Protection of the Erdtree

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Golden Vow** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Mt. Gelmir
- Located inside the Corpse-Stench Shack east of the broken stone bridge on the Road of Iniquity. Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater will also invade at this same spot.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Grants an Aura Buff to the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius that increases all damage dealt by 15% (7.5% in PvP) and decreases all damage taken by 10% (5% in PvP) for 80 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 50 points of Stamina to cast.
- Can be held indefinitely if the caster wants to wait for their allies to step into range of the buff.
- Generally considered the strongest of all Aura Buffs due to having the second strongest universal attack and defense bonuses (highest against other players) after the unique skill Rallying Standard while also having the longest.
  - The only real disadvantage is that the cost is relatively high (though low for the very good duration) and the moderate Faith requirement.
  - The Rallying Standard skill does have the advantage of higher bonuses (though not in PvP), while the Shared Order skill at the cost of having no defense bonus, a lower attack bonus, and a slightly shorter duration of 60 seconds has no requirement beyond being able to wield an infusible weapon such as the Dagger and a lower FP cost of 20.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- While most things in-game only gained different values against other players after Patch 1.07, this incantation seems to have gained its PvP values with or prior to Patch 1.03.
- Patch 1.09.1 fixed a bug where the effects of some Skills, Incantations, Items, and Weapons that increased attack power were not applied to Spells and Incantations.
  - After this patch, the effect of Golden Vow applied to Spells again.
- Patch 1.09 fixed a bug that reduced the power of some skills while under the Golden Vow effect.
  - This update also introduced a bug where Golden Vow's effect was not applied to Spells.
  - The bug that was fixed appears to be the same one as the one that was fixed with Patch 1.05, below, which was apparently reintroduced with Patch 1.07.
- Patch 1.05 fixed a bug that caused the attack power of some skills to be reduced when using the "Golden Vow" skill.
  - The bug would cause some skills, such as Storm Blade, to deal no damage, while others, like Waterfowl Dance, would deal heavily reduced damage.
  - This bug appears to have been introduced with one of the 4 updates from Patch 1.03 to Patch 1.03.3.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Greatshield Talisman** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Obtained from a chest, within a black carriage, east of Erdtree-Gazing Hill Site of Grace, in western Altus Plateau.
  - The location is more precisely east southeast of Lux Ruins and almost straight north from the Grand Lift of Dectus.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Decreases Stamina damage taken from attacks when Guarding by 20%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Since the decrease to Stamina damage when guarding is a percentage of the Stamina damage otherwise taken it sees diminishing returns when paired with equipment with high Guard Boost, such as Greatshields.
  - This means it overall pairs better with equipment that has Guard Boost in the 40 to 60 range, such as Greatswords, Colossal Weapons, and Medium Shields.
  - Effectively increases Guard Boost by an amount equal to 100 subtracted by the equipment's actual boost and then divided by 5 (i.e. (100-(Guard Boost))/5).
    - For a piece of equipment with 40 Guard Boost wearing this talisman would effectively give it 40 + (100-40)/5 = 40 + 12 = 52 Guard Boost. For comparison, something with 60 Guard Boost would effectively get 60 + (100-60)/5 = 68 Guard Boost and something with 80 Guard Boost would effectively get 80 + (100-80)/5 = 84 Guard Boost.
- Before Patch 1.04 this talisman could bring the then-not-yet-nerfed Fingerprint Stone Shield to 100 Guard Boost, decreasing Stamina damage taken to 0 and making it near impossible to deal with unless using anti-block weapons such as Reapers or the Shotel, skills such as Piercing Fang and Impaling Thrust, or by managing to circle around the shield-wielder for a Backstab.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The icon is that of a Leyndell Knight and a Golden Greatshield.
- Patch 1.07 the effects of the Greatshield Talisman and Hammer Talisman have been increased.
  - The effect was actually changed, from a 10% increase to Guard Boost to a 20% decrease to Stamina damage taken while guarding.
- Patch 1.04 decreased the effect of Greatshield Talisman for weapons with high block rate.
  - While all other pieces of equipment received a 10% increase to Guard Boost this update made it so that Greatshields received a lesser increase to Guard Boost.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Goldmask is a Tarnished scholar and staunch Golden Order fundamentalist. He predicted the guidance of Grace, and upon being beckoned by it he came to the Lands Between to contemplate the Golden Order.

Although a Golden Order fundamentalist himself, Goldmask was critical of the hunters of Those Who Live in Death, lamenting that their learnedness had been reduced to fanatical raving and an obsession with finding a great evil to contend with, a concept which he did not believe existed within the Golden Order.

While contemplating the Erdtree in the Altus Plateau Goldmask is approached by Brother Corhyn, a man of the cloth who wished to travel alongside him as a scholar. In Leyndell, Goldmask becomes perplexed by the identity of Radagon, whose existence calls into question the principle that Queen Marika the Eternal is the one true god. With the help of the The Tarnished, Goldmask learns that Radagon is Marika.

Goldmask and Corhyn then travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, where Corhyn becomes aware of Goldmask's suspicions regarding the holism of the Golden Order. Corhyn begins to doubt Goldmask's faith, questioning his decision to travel to the Mountaintops.

Goldmask had come to the revelation that the imperfection of the Golden Order and the instability of ideology was due to the fickleness of the gods.  After the Erdtree burns, Goldmask returns to Leyndell and dies on the hill near the Erdtree Sanctuary, leaving behind the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which would allow the Golden Order to be perfected.

sections.heading: Basic Info
sections.text: Goldmask cannot be made hostile, and will disappear if attacked, giving no Runes or item drops. He will reappear in his last location after resting at a Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:

1. Altus Plateau (near Altus Highway Junction)

1. Altus Plateau (Forest-Spanning Greatbridge)

1. Leyndell, Royal Capital
  - Goldmask and Corhyn can be found near the colosseum. Corhyn will express frustration at Goldmask's current obsession with Radagon.
  - After using Law of Regression in front of the Radagon statue past the lift near Erdtree Sanctuary, talk to Goldmask to reveal Radagon's secret and then talk to Corhyn.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
  - Goldmask and Corhyn will move to the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins.
1. Leyndell, Ashen Capital
  - After defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, Goldmask's corpse can be found on a slope near the colosseum. Loot his corpse to receive the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which will unlock the option to complete the Age of Order ending.
  - After reloading the area, return to Goldmask's corpse to retrieve Goldmask's Rags, Gold Bracelets, and Gold Waistwrap.

sections.text: **Godefroy the Grafted** is an optional mini-boss in Elden Ring found in the Altus Plateau at the Golden Lineage Evergaol.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
A member of the Golden Lineage, he is a descendant of Godfrey, First Elden Lord, and Queen Marika the Eternal. Much like his kinsman Godrick the Grafted, Godefroy has practised the grotesque act of grafting.

At some point while the alliance of the Shardbearers still ruled over Leyndell, Royal Capital, Godefroy plotted to seize control of the capital. The demigod apparently managed to recruit an army that assumed strong enough for the attack. Godefroy also made use of the special characteristic of his Shaman flesh, grafting into his body parts of corpses in an attempt to gain more strength.

Godefroy would lead his men into what would become known as the First Defense of Leyndell, but ended up fighting around the Second Church of Marika, in the middle of Altus and well distant from even the outer walls of the capital.. The demigod and his soldiers would suffer a complete defeat at the hands of soldiers of Leyndell with their leader captured by Knight Kristoff, a member of the Ancient Dragon Cult of the capital.

Godefroy was imprisoned in the Golden Lineage Evergaol with only his axe in a secluded area close to the Grand Lift of Dectus and guarded by Vulgar Militia men. Though he was defeated, the demigod's attack would precipitate the deterioration of the sovereign alliance between the Shardbearers caused by the traces of the Night of Black Knives still lingering. This would eventually lead to the demigods clashing against each other and the following wars of the Shattering.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Godefroy possessed the Godfrey Icon, a legendary talisman depicting Godfrey and Serosh, the patriarch and guide the Golden Lineage even during his imprisonment.
- Godefroy had access to the corpses of Trolls and Banished Knights with the power of the storm to graft to his body.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.text:
Players who encounter Godefroy have most likely already defeated his relative, Godrick the Grafted. The same strategies used to defeat Godrick can be used here, since Godefroy uses the same moveset as Godrick's first phase, but without the second phase.

Be aware that he is considerably tankier, having twice as much HP as Godrick (12.5k vs 6k) and not being able to summon anything or anyone in his arena. He will also deal much more damage, even for his location.

Upon defeating Godefroy, he drops the Godfrey Icon.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Gloam-Eyed Queen** is a unseen character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by the Two Fingers long ago. She had a special eye and an affinity for god-slaying Rune of Death, manipulating its black flames in her palm and into her Godslayer's Greatsword. She embraced the highborn Godskin Nobles, needle-bearing servants of Destined Death, and cradled newborn Godskin Apostles in a swaddling cloth sewn from supple skin. Like their predecessors, the apostles assimilated serpentine physiology in a manner akin to the Crucible, and grew to bring death to the gods. Several Fire Monks abandoned their posts to swear fealty as Blackflame Monks.

The Gloam-Eyed Queen led the Godskin Apostles during a victorious god-hunt, however, she was defeated by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast of Queen Marika. Afterward, Marika removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it away within his Black Blade, creating the Golden Order and suppressing the true power of the Godslayer incantations. The Gloam-Eyed Queen's sword was locked away at the bottom of the Divine Tower of Caelid and her Godskin Swaddling Cloth is in Spiritcaller's Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants, guarded by a Spiritcaller Snail that summons the spirits of Godskin Apostles.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.text:
The Godskin Apostles were the followers of the Gloam-Eyed Queen:
- Blackflame Monk
- Blackflame Monk Amon
- Blackflame Sorcerer
- Godskin Apostle

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

- Her fate remains unclear.
  - She may be connected to Melina, an amnesiatic daughter of Marika with a special sealed eye and an association with Destined Death. Melina's quest to burn the golden Erdtree enables the defeat of Maliketh and upends the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

- "GloamEyedKnight" and 宵眼の女王の騎士 (*Yoime no Joi no Kishi*, lit. Gloam Eyed Queen Knight/Horseman) are internal names for the Putrescent Knight, which gained eternal rest by imbibing St. Trina's nectar in the Garden of Deep Purple.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Golden Order** (黄金律, *Ōgonritsu*) is a philosophical and theological movement in Elden Ring. It refers to the removal of the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and the historic reign of Queen Marika the Eternal. Its greatest symbols are the Erdtree and the Grace of Gold. It is the dominant set of beliefs in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Prior to the Golden Order, the Rune of Death was part of the Elden Ring. Its power was wielded as the god-slaying black flame by the Empyrean known as the Gloam-Eyed Queen, who led the Godskin Apostles on their god hunt. The apostles' purge ended in defeat when Maliketh, Marika's half-brother and Shadowbound Beast, triumphed over the Gloam-Eyed Queen. Destined Death was subsequently removed from the Elden Ring and sealed away by Maliketh inside his Black Blade, and he became known as the "Death of the Demigods."

sections.heading: Golden Order
sections.text:
The confinement of the Rune of Death marked the beginning of the Golden Order. With its establishment, Marika suppressed the power of her rival and granted immortality to herself and her demigod offspring, the Golden Lineage.

The Golden Order was a governing principle, a religion, and a philosophy. It was founded on the principle that Marika was the one true god, and was propagated by the Two Fingers. It replaced the concept of Destined Death with that of Erdtree Burial.

The Golden Order was capable of integrating conflicting ideologies and practices. The dragon cult of the royal capital was compatible because the ancient dragons' lightning was imbued with gold. Later, the Erdtree faith absorbed the practice of glintstone sorcery. Concepts that threatened to shatter the Order entirely, such as life in death, were labeled as heresy and violently persecuted by the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Golden Order Fundamentalism
sections.text:
Golden Order Fundamentalism was a scholarly pursuit that combined both intelligence and faith. It attempted to interpret the fundamentals of the Golden Order. Fundamentalism was based on two concepts: the Law of Regression, the pull of meaning and the yearning to converge; and the Law of Causality, the pull between meanings which links all things in a chain of relation.

Among the Golden Order Fundamentalists were the hunters of Those Who Live in Death, who abandoned learning in search of an absolute evil to contend with. Miquella, who once created Fundamentalist incantations to give to his father Radagon, abandoned Fundamentalism as it could not treat Malenia's rot. Other notable followers of Golden Order Fundamentalism included Brother Corhyn, Goldmask, and the twins D. Hunter of the Dead and D, Beholder of Death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The Japanese term *ōgonritsu* (黄金律, lit. "golden law") refers to the Golden Rule, the maxim of reciprocity whereby one should treat others as one would want to be treated by them ("Do unto others as you would have them do unto you").

sections.text: **Golden Epitaph** is a straight sword and melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found at the entrance of Auriza Hero's Grave. Requires a Stonesword Key to access and is guarded by a Basilisk.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The skill, Last Rites, functions as an Aura Buff and adds 25 Holy damage and a universal 10% (5% for PvP) damage bonus, as well as a 100% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death. While being an Aura Buff does mean it will stack with a lot of other buffs, it also places it in competition with Golden Vow (especially the spell version), which also adds a strong boost to damage negation on top of its damage boost, and the Golden Epitaph being Faith-leaning means meetings its requirements are easy.
  - However, Last Rites is generally quicker to use and doesn't require a Sacred Seal to use, making it possibly more convenient in combat.
- This weapon has an innate 30% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death (Skeletons, Deathbirds and such), on top of dealing the Holy damage that they are usually vulnerable to.
- Has the most Attack Power (AP) on a hybrid Strength/Faith build or a hybrid Dexterity/Faith build, with a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build being a bit weaker, and a pure Faith build being weaker still.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:

- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- An epitaph is "a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone" (Cambridge Dictionary), which in this case would be the phrase "O brother, lord brother, please die a true death." in the description.
- This weapons resembles the Rune Sword from Demon's Souls.
- Patch 1.12 fixed a bug that caused damage to the player and friendly summons when using the "Last Rites" Skill under specific circumstances.
  - Prior to the fix, Last Rites would be applied to non-damaging, persistent effects such as Terra Magica, making them deal the flat 25 Holy damage to any friendly players standing on it.
- Patch 1.07 increased effect duration, increased attack power, effect against Those Who Live in Death has been revised upward.
  - The skill's duration was increased from 45 seconds to 60 seconds, the universal 10% damage buff was added (limited to 5% in PvP), and the damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death was increased from 50% to 100%.
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed.
  - For the skill, that is.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Gurranq, Beast Clergyman**, also known as **Beast Clergyman** and **Maliketh, the Black Blade**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Gurranq is a hulking, bestial high clergyman from Farum Azula who resides in the Bestial Sanctum in north-eastern Caelid. Long ago, his terrifying ferocity earned him the name "Death of the Demigods. Presently, he seeks Deathroot, a product of the Rune of Death which spread through the Lands Between following the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. Gurranq consumes Deathroot, although it does not appear to sate him.

Gurranq was assisted in his eradication of the Deathroot by D, Hunter of the Dead, a hunter of Those Who Live in Death. However, D passes this duty onto a Tarnished after noticing their prowess for weeding Deathroot. The Tarnished brings the Deathroot they find throughout the world to Gurranq, and is given access to bestial incantations in exchange. Once they have fed Gurranq all the Deathroot they can find, Gurranq leaves the sanctum. Although still not sated, he realises that he can do no more, and that his appetite will be his sole companion.

When the Tarnished travels to Crumbling Farum Azula to claim the Rune of Death, they encounter Gurranq once more. If the Tarnished had given Gurranq all the Deathroots, he is saddened by his friend's betrayal, but nonetheless attacks the Tarnished to protect the Rune of Death from them. Gurranq is overwhelmed, forcing him to use the Rune of Death to empower himself and reveal his true form as Maliketh, the Black Blade, shadowbound beast of Queen Marika the Eternal. The Tarnished defeats Maliketh, and unleashes the Rune of Death.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. *(Optional)* Speak to D, Hunter of the Dead, after obtaining a Deathroot and he will advise you to visit Gurranq. This can either be done at the start of D's questline in Limgrave, or in Roundtable Hold.
1. Travel to the Bestial Sanctum at the north-eastern point of Caelid. The sending gate marked on your map by D if you showed him a Deathroot will lead you straight there. Speak to Gurranq. If you have at least one Deathroot, Gurranq will give you a Clawmark Seal and Beast Eye. The Beast Eye will notify you whenever you are close to another Deathroot.
1. Hand over each Deathroot you find to Gurranq in exchange for rewards. After you have given him four Deathroot, reload the area and Gurranq will attack you. After depleting 30% of Gurranq's health, he will be subdued- speak to him and reload the area so that he returns to his original position.
1. After giving him the ninth Deathroot, he will give you an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone before disappearing.
1. Gurranq will reappear at the end of Crumbling Farum Azula, under the name Beast Clergyman. After reducing his health to 50% he will enter phase 2, under the name Maliketh, the Black Blade.
  - Maliketh can be fought before completing Gurranq's questline. Doing so will not affect the questline, and Gurranq will remain in the Bestail Sanctum even after Maliketh has been defeated. Likewise, killing Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum will not affect the fight against Maliketh.
  - Maliketh will have unique dialogue if you complete Gurranq's questline before fighting him in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The weapon Gurranq uses is a Cinquedea.
- Gurranq can occasionally be found outside the Bestial Sanctum at night, howling in the direction of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Haligtree** (聖樹, *Seiju*) is a great tree in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Haligtree is a massive, withering tree covered in fungi, extending from a stump in the northern Lands Between. It lies far north of Leyndell, Royal Capital, and off the coast of the Consecrated Snowfield. Pilgrims must present a secret medallion at the Grand Lift of Rold to access the Consecrated Snowfield. From there, they follow a trail of lights, cross the river to Ordina, Liturgical Town, and use a Sending Gate to reach the Haligtree.

The Haligtree is divided into two areas: Miquella's Haligtree and Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. The upper area, Miquella's Haligtree, is a sparse canopy populated by Giant Ants and Oracle Envoys. This section contains Haligtree Town, an open and organic treehouse refuge for the unwanted that features statues of the twin Demigods. The lower section, Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, is a robust stone fortress occupied by Haligtree Knights and Cleanrot Knights who serve Miquella and Malenia. Both areas are made from different materials and for different purposes, though Haligtree Town appears far newer and cleaner than the brace. Its design features more complex curved surfaces, and it has more of the intricate knotwork patterns associated with Miquella's Haligtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Long ago, the Empyrean Miquella abandoned Golden Order Fundamentalism upon realizing it could not cure his twin sister Malenia's scarlet rot. Seeking to create a new order of Unalloyed Gold, he settled on the Haligtree as his sanctuary.

After the Battle of Aeonia, Miquella watered the sapling with his own Empyrean blood. He later embedded himself within a cocoon in the tree's roots to nurture it, attempting to grow it into an Erdtree. However, his efforts were interrupted when Mohg, the Lord of Blood, abducted him from the Haligtree. Under Miquella's charm, Mohg zealously sought to elevate the Empyrean to godhood and establish the Mohgwyn Dynasty as Miquella's consort. Without Miquella, the Haligtree began to wither.

Afterward, Cleanrot Knight Finlay carried Malenia's slumbering body to the Haligtree, placing her at its roots. There, Malenia awaited her brother's return while slowly corrupting the tree with the scarlet rot.

Nevertheless, the Haligtree became a refuge for societal outcasts, including the Misbegotten and Kindred of Rot. Loretta, a former Knight of Caria, established a sanctuary for the Albinaurics within its boughs, turning the area into a sacred haven for their kind.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The form of a young person with a hole in their torso can still be seen in the roots of the Haligtree where Miquella's cocoon once rested within it.
- The current Haligtree appears to have grown from the stump of the older tree originating from Miquella's cocoon.
- Haligtree game area has two sets of roots that often appear alongside one another. The larger, wider, and darker ones are older than Miquella's.

- The master of Castle Sol holding half of the Medallion required to access the Haligtree would have been allowed to enter it depending on the success of the Eclipse in reviving a soulless Demigod.
- Gideon Ofnir sought the path to the Haligtree, sending his shadow, Ensha, to retrieve the secret medallion from the Village of the Albinaurics. In the process, Ensha killed Lattena's wolf companion, Lobo, but ultimately failed in his mission.
- The Haligtree Secret Medallion depicts it with green or viridian amber.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Haligtree is a combination of the Old English word *hālig* (holy, sacred; healthy, sound) and *tree*. A literal translation would be "holy tree".
- In cut dialogue lines, Old Albus referenced a chalk city of Miquella called *"Eburion"*. This area may have been reworked into Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Grace** (祝福, *Shukufuku*), also referred to as the **Grace of Gold** (黄金の祝福, *Ōgon no Shukufuku*), is a blessing given to people throughout the Lands Between by the Elden Ring and the Erdtree that symbolizes its presence. This blessing is represented by a golden light in the eyes of the inhabitants of the Lands Between. Those who had grace bestowed on them, but later lost it, are known as Tarnished.

sections.heading: Grace
sections.text:
The Lands Between are blessed by the presence of the Elden Ring and by the Erdtree, which symbolizes its presence, and this has given grace or blessing to the people throughout the land, great and small.

At some point, Queen Marika the Eternal took away Grace from Godfrey, First Elden Lord and his kinfolk, turning them into Tarnished. They then left the  Lands Between in an event called the Long March of the Tarnished.  Long afterwards, Grace would be returned to them, or their descendants, and they would be called back to the Lands Between.

At the time of the game, when given back, Grace itself is what gives the Tarnished their life.

sections.heading: The Guidance of Grace
sections.text:
Sometimes, the Tarnished can see golden rays of Grace that point in a particular direction, called the Guidance of Grace. It exists to guide the Tarnished and lead them along the proper path. It was also said that the guidance of grace would ensure that a Finger Maiden be brought to her chosen Tarnished. Or at least, such was the promise long ago.

Even now, some sites of grace retain that power, and their golden rays can guide the Tarnished along the way.

It is said that true guidance awaits those with iron wills and unwavering faith, although it can be lost.  In fact, most Tarnished don't even see it nowadays.

Those in distant lands who saw the guidance of grace were usually seen as undesirables, and were usually expatriated, after which they set to journey to the Lands Between. Similarly, the churches outside the Lands Between, dedicated to the teachings of the Two Fingers, sent confessors out to follow the guidance of grace.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Localisation Notes
  - Grace is called 祝福 (*Shukufuku*), meaning "blessing" or "celebration." It can also refer specifically to "blessing (from God)" in a Christian sense.

sections.text: Glintstone Sorcerers are scholars who study glintstone sorcery at the Academy of Raya Lucaria in Liurnia of the Lakes. Each is an accomplished glintstone sorcerer worthy of wearing a heavy stone mask embedded with colored glintstone. These crowns represents one of the academy's conspectuses, or philosophies, associated with the various branches of glintstone sorcery.

sections.text:
Members of the Karolos Conspectus, established by the sorcerer Azur. They dedicate themselves to the study of comets.

Only capable of casting Glintstone Pebble.

Only capable of casting Carian Greatsword.

This form is found on the roofs of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, and in spectral form in Sellia, Town of Sorcery. They are capable of casting Shard Spiral and Swift Glintstone Shard

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Guardians**, also known as **Tree Guardians**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The masked guardians entered an ancient death pact with the Erdtree to be renewed with eternal life. Armed with swordspears whittled from the hard wood of old trees, they were dextrous, expert protectors of Minor Erdtrees and the Erdtree itself at Leyndell, Royal Capital. Budding branches grew from their backs, ready to release perfume and poisonous pollen. The blooming of their blood-red flowers was said to signal the impending end of their tenure, and the beginning of their transformation into trees.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.text: There are three variants: **Guardians**, **Putrid Guardians**, **Full Bloom Guardians**.

sections.heading: Guardian
sections.text: Masked guardians commonly found around Minor Erdtrees. They fight using swordspears, and have a charging attack which releases a cloud of poison.

sections.heading: Guardian (Full Bloom)
sections.text: Guardians with blood-red flowers blooming on their backs, said to mark the senescence of their ancient pact. They can grow additional flowers on their backs to restore their health, and can reinforce their weapons with large roots, granting them much heavier attacks.

sections.heading: Putrid Tree Guardian
sections.text: Guardians found in areas contaminated with Scarlet Rot, with withered roots on their backs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Internal name: **BugsEater**
- The Guardians' blades are embellished with a spiral motif.
- The gold medallion around their neck depicts a smiling, eight-pointed sun with swirling flames.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Guardian Golem** is an optional boss in Elden Ring. It is located in Highroad Cave.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Guardian Golem found at the end of Highroad Cave, having most likely fallen down from the bridge to the Divine Tower of Limgrave.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
Damage types: mainly Standard damage, with some Pierce damage from its thrusts and Fire damage from its flame breaths.

It's immune to all Status Effects and has 40% negation to all non-Physical damage types except for Magic, where it has only 20% resistance. It is somewhat weak to Strike damage, having 0% negation towards it, and a mild 10% negation against all other Physical damage types.

Since it starts out lying on the ground and will take a few seconds to get up once alerted, it's easy to get in some opening hits on its ankles. It has the range advantage and can hit most of the cave thanks to the length of its weapon.

The simplest strategy is to do the same as with a regular, non-boss halberd golem by sticking behind its ankles and backing away when its starts hitting the ground with the butt of its weapon or if it breathes fire.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Graven Masses**, also known as **Graven Schools** or **Schools of Graven Mages**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The primeval sorcerers who founded the Academy of Raya Lucaria adhered to the teachings of the primeval current, collecting lesser scholars and fusing them into spherical accretions known as the seeds of stars. The Graven Masses were large orbs of glintstone crowns created through forbidden glintstone sorcery—a practice that came to haunt the academy.

Upon gaining control of the academy, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon banned all inquiry into the primeval current. The primeval sorcerers Lusat and Azur were subsequently exiled. Later, the academy’s prodigy, Sorceress Sellen, revived the practice, transforming her peers into Graven Schools. Her actions earned her the title of "Graven Witch" and led to her expulsion and imprisonment.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Graven Masses take the form of large spheres composed of human faces wearing Olivinus Glintstone Crowns and Lazuli Glintstone Crowns. These Schools of Graven Mages are strange constructs animated by sorcery. In combat, they either release a purple mist that deals magic damage, or fire magic projectiles high into the air, which then rain down on their foes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Graven Masses do not drop items.
- Sorceress Sellen's sobriquet, the "Graven Witch", implies that she may have been one of the sorcerers responsible for the creation of Graven Masses.
  - Sellen becomes a Graven Mass herself at the end of her questline, provided the player sides with her against Castellan Jerren and reports the locations of Primeval Sorcerer Azur and Primeval Sorcerer Lusat.
  - Sellen's Graven Mass includes her Witch's Glintstone Crown.
- An inanimate Graven Mass can be found in a small room adjoining the Church of the Cuckoo in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, surrounded by crystals. Floating particles resembling a starry sky can be seen around it. Azur's Glintstone Staff can be picked up just in front of it.
  - Another can be found in Albinauric Rise in the Consecrated Snowfield, from which the Graven-Mass Talisman can be obtained.

sections.text: **HP** is one of the stats in Elden Ring. It represents the player's total hit points. If the HP bar is fully depleted, the Tarnished will die, dropping all Runes and respawning at the last Site of Grace rested at or the nearest Stake of Marika. It is represented by a red square ().

sections.heading: Increasing HP
sections.text: The total HP can be increased by leveling the Vigor attribute. The game applies soft caps beginning at levels 40 and 60, modifying the amount of HP gained per attribute level up.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Guard Boost** is a stat in Elden Ring.

It decreases the damage to Stamina received when guarding by an equivalent percentage, i.e. a +0 Dagger with its 15 Guard Boost would reduce 100 Stamina damage to 100*(1-0.15)=85 Stamina damage when guarding while a +0 Brass Shield with its 61 Guard Boost would reduce 100 Stamina damage to 100*(1-0.61)=39 Stamina damage when guarding. For 200 base Stamina damage the equivalent numbers would be 200*(1-0.15)=170 Stamina damage for the Dagger and 200*(1-0.61)=78 Stamina damage for the Brass Shield.

sections.text: The **Grand Lift of Rold** is a Location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A Grand Lift that links the Forbidden Lands east of Leyndell to the frigid Mountaintops of the Giants. It can only be activated using the Rold Medallion granted by Melina after defeating Morgott, the Omen King.

The Grand Lift of Rold also has another purpose: granting access to the Consecrated Snowfield, the land of Miquella's Haligtree. This region can only be accessed by uniting the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right), obtained in the Village of the Albinaurics, and the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left), found in Castle Sol. By using this route, the lift will stop at the Hidden Path to the Haligtree, a catacomb which opens onto the Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Guilty**, also known as **thorn sorcerers**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
These maidens were accused of a grave misdeed at the dawn of the Erdtree era, and the Briars of Sin crushed their eyes. Clad in the red garb of exiled criminals, the Guilty abandoned prayer when blind faith brought only despair. They dwelled in darkness until they discovered the blood star, embracing heretical thorn sorcery. They fashioned smoldering saplings into staves and transmuted sacrificial blood into red glintstone, a practice reviled by sorcerers at the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

The Guilty congregated with the Fire Monks, keepers of the Giants' Flame, and came to venerate a maiden who was reborn in the Lands Between after the Briars of Sin destroyed her eyes.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
A pale figure wearing a deep crimsom hood and bloodstained robes clutches a burning branch. Sharp briars coil around her gaunt frame, and a golden crown of thorns rests atop her head, twisting into a long trailing braid. Her nose and lips are cut off, and she screeches in agony.

These blind hexers wield faith-based sorceries that deal  Fire damage and inflict  Blood Loss buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Elden Ring Nightreign adds Blackflame Sorcerers, which are retextured Guilty Sorcerers that use Godslayer Incantations.
- The Guilty drop Smoldering Butterflies, which are associated with Melina.
- Blindness was a prerequisite for the Guilty to perceive the Blood Star.
- Queen Marika and Dominula Dancers also have long, single braids.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The internal names for Guilty are **DestructionsIntoFire** and **DestructionsIntoFire_Weak** (ID: 4381).
- The record for Blackflame Guilty in Elden Ring Nightreign (ID: 4386) was dummied out in the *Elden Ring* code.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: This page lists a number of glitches and bugs that have been recorded throughout Elden Ring's history.

sections.heading: Two-Minute Disconnect
sections.text:
The biggest issue that has been plaguing the multiplayer on the PC platform is the awfully frequent “two-minute disconnections”. Consoles don’t have this issue, so players have been left to believe it has to do with the “Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC)” software that was added to *Elden Ring*. Two minutes after establishing a multiplayer connection, players appear to be disconnected for failing to be validated by Easy Anti-Cheat’s services. However, this is obviously not working correctly as it happens at random for everyone who’s playing the game, the only consistent factor is that it happens at the two-minute mark.

The video goes into further technical detail.

sections.heading: Input Drops
sections.text: There are various animation interactions within *Elden Ring* which have been found to have clearly unintended behavior, such as consistently not taking player inputs at points which are intended. This results in combat feeling clunky and unfair, as players doubt and question if the game is even responding to their inputs when it’s supposed to. These are similar to exploits and passive glitches, which tend to affect the game as a whole negatively for all players, but in a way that is difficult for most to pin down. The following are input drop issues that players have been able to identify:

sections.heading: Block-Sprint Input Drop
sections.text:
When stopping a sprint and lowering your guard around the same time, any action the player inputs will be dropped (e.g. rolling, attacking).
          ► 0:29 ­ ­ ­ Block-sprint input drop
­

sections.heading: Two-Hand-Jumping-Input-Drop
sections.text:
When continuing to sprint after a jump, the player cannot queue a light attack action for a significant amount of time after landing, while any other input works including guarding. This does not occur when 1-handing weapons.
At the below  timestamp, you can see the keyboard “Light Attack” input being repeatedly dropped, only while 2-handing and after landing from a sprinting jump.
          ► 2:38 ­ ­ ­ Two-hand jumping input drop
­

sections.heading: Damage Occurrence Input Drop
sections.text: When the player receives damage that does not stun them, certain actions seem to be cleared from the input queue such as roll dodging, which causes players to be hit again as they expected the game to not clear their input. This has been confirmed to be a result of the damage occurrence and not any misconceptions with queue timing.

sections.heading: Moving Toggle Input Drop
sections.text:
While moving during a toggle (weapon swap/2-handing) animation, it is impossible to buffer another action out of the animation until it finishes. Despite this, you are still able to buffer actions when toggling while standing still.
At the timestamp below, you can see the keyboard “Heavy Attack” input being dropped only while doing a moving toggle.
          ► 1:59 ­ ­ ­ Moving toggle input drop

  Explanation video by Amir

sections.heading: Aim Punch
sections.text:
When a character in the middle of an attack animation is hit by an attack and is not interrupted out of it (either due to poise, or the attack not having any hitstun), the character still animates a bit in reaction to the damage. This animation is so strong, that it can frequently cause attacks to miss even if they would have certainly hit normally.

- At the below timestamp for example. The weapon would have hit the enemy directly in front of the player normally, but due to aim punch, the swing is redirected to the left and misses. Some of these examples in this video are so silly, that the weapon can even be seen swinging 360 degrees on a random axis.
- The same video at the following timestamp suggests a good solution for this issue implemented in one of Elden Ring’s predecessors.

sections.heading: Perpetual Casting
sections.text:
By generating an absurd amount of bullets, players can glitch their character to fire them off indefinitely.
The following video showcases this exploit and explains its mechanics and cause in detail:

sections.heading: Crouch Run Stamina Exploit
sections.text:
Entering or exiting crouch while running does not restrict stamina regeneration, nor consume stamina during those animations. This is clearly unintentional, as the regular running animation does consume stamina. The consequence of this glitch is that it allows players to continue running while in combat without breaks for stamina regeneration, as they lose minimal speed from entering and exiting crouch.

The following video showcases and explains additional details on the impact of this exploit:

sections.heading: Blessed Dew Talisman Regen Glitch
sections.text:
Rapidly equipping and unequipping the Blessed Dew Talisman allows the user to restore HP far faster than intended.

The following video showcases this glitch:

sections.heading: Infinite Health Helmet Swap Glitch
sections.text: By swapping between the Karolos Glintstone Crown and some other Glintstone Crowns, players can restore their entire health bar in a matter of seconds at no cost. This allows players to regenerate hundreds of health points per second, due to an issue with the status and attribute altering effects of the crowns.

sections.heading: Glitched Chain Casting
sections.text:
We are not certain how much of chaining casts between spells is intentional, but there are certain chain cast interactions that are clearly not intended. When queuing a spell out of a different spell that can chain cast such as Bestial Sling, it may attempt to play the third cast animation of the queued spell. However, not all spells that have the ability to chain cast also have a third casting animation. If the spell is prompted to play the third casting animation and does not have one, it appears to default to the Glintstone Pebble spell’s third cast animation. This causes many strange interactions.

- This video showcases the difference between possibly intentional inter-spell chain casting and clearly unintentionally glitched casting:

*Update: As of patch 1.05, several forms of chain casting including ones that play a clearly incorrect animation have been patched out. However, there are still methods of chain casting in the game. Cross-spell chain casting can still be achieved by queuing the spell out of a jump cast of another spell. Additionally, spells that utilize the same animation set can chain cast between each other as they would with themselves.*

sections.heading: Bolus Swap
sections.text:
Similar to the patched sprint pivot swap glitch, this glitch allows you to use a weapon skill on any other weapon, by way of a very tightly timed inventory unequip at the end of a quick consumable animation (such as Preserving Boluses). The capabilities of this glitch include putting any skill buffs on weapons that cannot be buffed using spells or consumables, or the use of weapon skills on unintended armaments such as the Bloodboon Ritual skill on Vyke’s War Spear.

The steps to execute this glitch are as follows:
- 1. Equip the armament with the skill you wish to use in your off-hand.
- 2. Equip the armament that you want to transfer the skill animation to in your right hand.
- 3. Two-hand the armament in your off-hand.
- 4. Use a quick eating consumable such as a Preserving Bolus.
- 5. Queue the skill use action (L2 on a PlayStation Controller).
- 6. Near the end of the animation, enter your inventory and press the unequip button on your left hand armament slot, removing the weapon you currently have two-handed.
- 7. If timed correctly, your character should be doing the skill of the armament you just removed.
Here is a video showcasing the glitch and how to execute it:

sections.heading: Off-Hand Stance Swap
sections.text: This bug allows the player to use weapon skills with a glitched lower-body state, which allows them to walk or run during skills that would normally prevent player-controlled movement.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Great Jar** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He offers a trial that, if completed, rewards the player with the Great-Jar's Arsenal talisman.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Great-Jar is located in front of a Colosseum structure at Caelid, but can only be accessed late in the game from an elevator located in Siofra River.

After speaking to it for the first time, three red summon signs will appear nearby, each allowing to summon a Knight of the Great Jar. After defeating all three summons without dying, the player will be rewarded.

sections.heading: Knights of the Great Jar
sections.text:
The Knights of the Great Jar are copies of other players who have already completed the challenge. In case of playing offline, the game provides three default options:

One wields a Magic affinity Estoc and an Albinauric Staff with which it casts Carian Phalanx and Magic Glintblade, and wears the Marionette Soldier Birdhelm, Lusat's Robe, and unknown hand and leg piece.

Another wields a Miséricorde with the Poison Moth Flight skill and a Buckler to parry with, and wears the Prophet Blindfold, Raptor's Black Feathers, an unknown hand piece, and Leather Boots.

The third combatant wields a Great Mace with the Prayerful Strike skill and a Banished Knight's Shield, and wears the Banished Knight Helm, Ronin's Armor, an unknown hand piece, and Raging Wolf Greaves.

sections.text: **Haligtree Soldiers** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Haligtree Soldiers are frontline infantrymen loyal to Miquella the Kind, one of the Demigods who participated in the Shattering. Numerous Haligtree Soldiers are stationed throughout Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, the ancient city below the canopy of Miquella's Haligtree. They support the Haligtree Knights and Haligtree Foot Soldiers in continued defense of the rotting Haligtree, despite their Empyrean's absence.

A braided crown of unalloyed gold adorns their helmets. They wear bloodstained, rusted iron armor beneath a white surcoat depicting the Haligtree, a symbol of Miquella. In this rendition, fresh buds emerge from a Haligtree sapling supported by a trellis.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- They do not drop their Torches or trumpets.
- The cross-hatch stitching on the Haligtree Crest Surcoat likely represents Lord Radagon's early influence on Miquella as well as Elphael's functional purpose.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Golden Lineage** is a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Golden Lineage is the royal bloodline descended from the union of Lord Godfrey and Queen Marika. A two-headed war axe and a golden lion serves as the emblem of their family, the former representing the favorite weapon of their founding patriarch and the latter being the likeness of his loyal advisor Serosh, Lord of Beasts.

sections.heading: **Founders**
sections.text:
After their victory against the giants and the Sealing of Destined Death, the fate of the Erdtree and the Golden Order was considered secured and thus the Elden Lord, Godfrey and God-Queen, Marika established a royal lineage with their first demigod children together, with Beast Regent, Serosh and his counseling serving as a guide for the generations to come.

Before long, Godfrey continued on his campaign to expand the Golden Order's influence and rule and strengthening his reputation as the Lord of the Battlefield, a reputation that would be quickly followed up in modest by their immediate children, but became a suffocating shadow that would progressively tower higher and higher over his later descendants.

sections.heading: **First Descendants**
sections.text:
The immediate descendants of their family's founders, these children would be the first to carry the unified blood of both Godfrey and Marika.

Many of these individuals would go on to make their names known, forging their own stories and pursue their own goals, fueled by their own convictions. Indeed these apples did truly not fall far from their tree.

sections.heading: **Later Descendants**
sections.text:
Unlike the first generation after Godfrey, many of the later descendants would become obsessed with their pedigree and status as a reputable, important bloodline. Continuously riding the glory of their founding father's accomplishments while progressively becoming less and less comparable to his greatness with each passing generation.

The current-day dregs of the golden lineage would go desperately searching for power and purpose in the past. Excavating for ancient relics and surrounding themselves with artifacts of a golden era, an era they played no part in and had long since passed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Before the Tarnished battles him, Godrick refers to a fallen dragon as "trueborn heir" and a "kindred". While it's unlikely that he is actually related to the dragon by blood, he is likely evoking the fraternal relationship established between Godwyn the Golden and Ancient Dragon Fortissax, and thus the Golden Lineage and dragonkind. They are also related on a thematic level, as the specific species of dragon Godrick is speaking to is in a similar existential situation as he is, a lesser descendant of greater ancestors. Even in the moment where he grafts the dragon's head onto himself, Godrick continues to reafirm the dragon's value, reffering to it as "the truest of dragons". As by reafirming it's value, he is by extention attempting to affirm his own value as well.
- Cut content suggests that Gatekeeper Gostoc is actually a son of Godrick the Grafted. Should this still be true in the final game, then this would make Gostoc a member of the Golden Lineage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Golems** are a type of autonomous constructs found throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Typically made of stone by ancient civilizations now gone to ruin, golems are generally resistant to all common status ailments.  Today, they are frequently positioned as guards of tombs and other sacred sites.

Long ago, it is said that a golem crafter employed a crystal tool that heavily resembles what would become the chiseled Crystal Darts that can be crafted and discovered across the world today. If enough of these darts penetrate a single golem in quick enough succession, that golem will malfunction and begin indiscriminately attacking everything in its vicinity (including its own allies) for a short period of time. This applies only to imps, Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, Guardian Golems, and Golem Smiths Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Haligtree Foot Soldiers** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A foot soldier blessed by Miquella. They can be found grouped together, often in the vicinity of a Haligtree Soldier or Haligtree Knight. They are nimble when wielding a Dagger or a Short Sword, but those that carry a Spear or Torchpole are less so. Some provide ranged support to their allies by throwing Poison Pots, whilst others employ the usage of heavier artillery such as Ballistae.

Once they reach half health they will ignite the sacred spark inside of them and try to rush their enemies and explode: if killed before they can explode, they simply die without doing so. This was the bitter insight they reached, hoping its light would guide their lord back to the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Haligtree Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Knights who have vowed to serve Miquella's Haligtree, they carry metal greatshields depicting the Haligtree with unalloyed gold, possessing high holy damage negation. Their armor is of such quality that time has yet to dull their luster; their left breast is emblazoned with the crest of the Haligtree, and they wear helms graced with crowns of unalloyed gold that increase faith. They also carry a flower signifying faith in the Haligtree, thought to be beloved by the Empyrean Miquella in his youth.

Haligtree Knights are strong and skilled warriors. Largely armed with greatswords, some also wield a shield while others switch to a greatbow for powerful long-ranged attacks. A select few carry Partisan spears instead of a sword. No matter their armament, these knights are blessed with access to a number of magical skills that can aid them in battle, such as Glintstone Pebble and Sacred Order, the latter of which allows them to regenerate health. Curiously, they even possess a Flask of Wondrous Physick which fully heals them when consumed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: Knights do not drop their Haligtree Knight Helm; instead it can be picked up once you climb a ladder near the Elphael Inner Wall site of grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
<noinclude>
**Glintstone** are a family of Sorceries in Elden Ring. The practice of this type of magic is said to have begun with an Ancient Astrologer's discovery of the Primeval Current and since then has served as a main focus of study amongst many sorcerers.

The Academy of Raya Lucaria in particular was founded with the sole purpose of studying this form of magic and thus many of the spells of this category find their origins at the academy, their varitiy of complexities making for excellent material of study for sorceres at different skill levels. Glintstone has become so integral to the sorcerous arts that many of its spells have become elementary knowledge among spell casters of all kinds.

All glintstone sorceries deal pure Magic Damage and have Intelligence requirements.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
<noinclude>
**Gravity Sorceries** are a school of magic in Elden Ring. The power of gravity is frequently seen used by beings from beyond the stars. The knowledge of these arts were introduced to mankind by the enigmatic Alabaster Lords and Onyx Lords.

Gravity sorceries either deal pure Magic Damage or a mixture of Physical and Magic damage and have Intelligence requirements. They are known for their ability to either forcibly pull targets closer to oneself or inflict heavy Stance damage against enemies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Godskin Apostles** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Godskin Apostles were servants of Destined Death, and the followers of the Gloam-Eyed Queen, an Empyrean who cradled them from infancy. They wore hoods and robes stitched together from patches of smooth, pale skin and wielded the god-slaying power of the blackflame,  and assimilated inhuman physiology, such as the ability to stretch like Gelmir Man-Serpents, not unlike the Crucible. Though they stand in opposition to the Erdtree, they have golden eyes. Additionally, the faces on their clothes bear the Grace of Gold in their eyes.

The Godskin Nobles were the first of these god-killers, who claimed Noble Presence during their god hunt. Their crusade came to an end when the Gloam-Eyed Queen was defeated by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast of Marika. With the Rune of Death sealed away by Maliketh within his Black Blade, the true power of the Godslayer Incantations was lost.

sections.heading: List of Godskin Apostles
sections.text:
There are two groups of Godskin Apostles:
- Godskin Apostle
- Godskin Noble

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:

- A pair of Godskins are summoned by a Spiritcaller Snail at Spiritcaller Cave. They guard the Godskin Swaddling Cloth.
- A Godskin Noble appear on the bridge leading to the Divine Tower of Liurnia, where Ranni the Witch slew her flesh on the Night of Black Knives.
- A Godskin Noble attends the  Temple of Eiglay at the Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir.
- The Godskin Duo guards the  Dragon Temple Altar at Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Marika's Golden Order was created when she removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring.
- The god-slaying black flames wielded by the Godskin Apostles were channeled through their queen's Godslayer's Greatsword.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Godslayer Incantations**, also known as **Blackflame Incantations**, are a group of six Incantations in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign. They deal damage over time and offer protection or enhancements.

All offensive Godslayer Incantations deal  Fire damage and inflict a Blackflame effect that deals additional damage equal to 2% of the target's maximum HP + 20 over the course of 2 seconds per hit (note that this doesn't stack, with another hit merely refreshing the duration).  All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to this percentage-based damage, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Godslayer's Seal increases the effectiveness of offensive black flame incantations (except for Black Flame Blade and Noble Presence) by 10%.
- The Godslayer incantation spell sigil represents a palm of blackflame.
- Godslayer Incantations channel the power imbued in the Gloam-Eyed Queen's Godslayer's Greatsword. They are practiced by Godskin Apostles to harness the power of the black flame.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Gods** are among the most powerful characters in the world of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Queen Marika the Eternal
sections.text: Queen Marika the Eternal is the divine sovereign of the Lands Between. She was a Numen woman hailing from a Shaman Village in the Hinterland. As an Empyrean, Marika traveled to the Gate of Divinity atop Enir-Ilim where she ascended to godhood and became the vessel of the Elden Ring. Marika is further known as the mother or step-mother of the demigods, grower of the Erdtree, founder of the Golden Order, slayer of the Fell God as well as the spouse of the Elden Lords Godfrey and Radagon. Although she vanished after the Shattering, Marika influences the Tarnished and her chosen through the golden Guidance of Grace.

sections.heading: Miquella the Kind
sections.text: After Godfrey was Tarnished, the demigod Miquella the Kind was born to Queen Marika and Lord Radagon. Despite his eternal youth, he was selected as an Empyrean like his twin sister, Malenia. He was the master inventer of Unalloyed Gold, the grower of the sacred Haligtree, and a coercive charmer. After divesting himself of his flesh, his eye, his fears, his vacillation, and St. Trina—his love and fate—Miquella, like Marika, ascended to godhood at the Gate of Divinity. He used the body of Mohg to resurrect his promised consort, Radahn, in a failed attempt to succeed his mother as sovereign and usher in an Age of Compassion.

sections.heading: Malenia, Goddess of Rot
sections.text: Malenia, the undefeated Blade and twin sister of Miquella the Kind, was born afflicted with baleful Scarlet Rot. However, she managed to suppress it with the help of the Blind Swordsman and Miquella's Unalloyed Gold Needle. During her legendary duel with Radahn at the end of the Shattering, she reluctantly unleashed the Scarlet Aeonia. Following this bloom, the Swamp of Aeonia manifested in Caelid, producing the Kindred of Rot. If the Empyrean Malenia is confronted and defeated at the Haligtree, she will blossom for a second time. Her third and final bloom is prophesied to complete her transformation into a true Goddess of Rot. Unlike her twin, Malenia has no interest in establishing her own Order.

sections.heading: Fell God
sections.text: The red-haired, one-eyed Fell God of fire is an ancient deity worshipped by the Fire Giants. It is regarded as an malevolent entity that opposes and threatens the Erdtree and the Golden Order. Queen Marika allegedly slew the Fell God during the War Against the Giants, and cursed the last survivor of their race to eternally tend the Flame.. However, the Fell God's still lingers within the giants.

sections.heading: Ancient Dragon God
sections.text: Dragonlord Placidusax waited for his fled god to return.

sections.heading: Old Gods
sections.text: The old gods ((古い神々, *Furui Kamigami*) were colossal giants who wielded ancient meteoric ore that contained explosive white light. An excavated shard of one of their arrowheads was the treasure of a ruined forge that came after them.

sections.heading: Radiant Gods
sections.text: Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow worshipped radiant gods (光を放つ神々, *Hikariohanatsu Kamigami*, lit. Light-Emitting Gods) cloaked in the roar of thunder. It is possible that they are one and the same with the Old Gods, as both are referred to as *kamigami* in the Japanese script, both produce light (their radiance is written with the same kanji as the Old Gods white light, 光), and the legends of them concealing themselves in thunder are reminscent of the thunderstone folklore which provided the real-world inspiration for the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword.

sections.heading: Serpent-God
sections.text: The ancient inhabitants of Mt. Gelmir made sacrifices in the name of a Serpent-God. It is likely connected to one of the god-like snakes, such as the Abyssal Serpent and God-Devouring Serpent.

sections.heading: Demigods
sections.text: Demigods are powerful beings with the divine blood or power but without possessing true godhood. In the Lands Between most demigods are children or step-children of Queen Marika and the Elden Lords. After Marika shattered the Elden Ring, many demigods acquired Great Runes and became Shardbearers. The Tarnished are guided by Grace to challenge the demigods and claim their Great Runes.

sections.heading: Empyreans
sections.text: Empyreans are beings capable of becoming gods. During the Age of the Erdtree, Empyreans were chosen by the Two Fingers. Examples of Empyreans are Marika, Miquella, Ranni, Malenia and the Gloam-Eyed Queen.

sections.heading: Greater Will
sections.text: The Greater Will is a mysterious entity or force known for fracturing the One Great, thus creating life and souls in the Lands Between. It once sent the Elden Beast to the Lands Between, which would eventually become the Elden Ring itself. The Greater Will also had other vassals like Metyr and her children, the Two Fingers, who selected Empyreans to become gods. The Greater Will is speculated to have imprisoned Queen Marika after she shattered the Elden Ring. Due to the Greater Will's power to rupture the One Great, create and imprison gods, it can effectively be seen as the supreme being of the *Elden Ring* universe.

sections.heading: Outer Gods
sections.text: Outer Gods are extremely powerful entities that exist outside of the Lands Between, the current Order of the Elden Ring or on an higher plane. Examples of outer gods are the Formless Mother, the God of Rot, the Twinbird's God, and the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Tutelary Deities
sections.text:
A tutelary deity is a god or spirit regarded as the guardian, patron, or protector of a specific location, natural feature, individual, lineage, nation, cultural group, or profession. The term "tutelary" derives from roots associated with safety and thus of guardianship.

Hornsent aspired to ascend as tutelary deities by engaging in severe ascetic training. Some became Curseblades or Divine Beast Warriors. Withered corpses of successful tutelary deities, enshrined across the Realm of Shadow, quietly gather Revered Spirit Ash in their palms.
