sections.heading: Ancient Dynasty
sections.text: A nameless bearded man with a bald head and one eye may have been the god of the Ancient Dynasty, which existed long before the age of the Erdtree. Once served by the claymen in Underground Ruins, he is now revered at the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum and Grand Cloister.

sections.heading: Nox Gods
sections.text: The Nox once revered mummified giants seated upon Chair-Crypt thrones, often honored them with Great Ghost Glovewort and other treasures.

sections.heading: Rauh
sections.text: The Ancient Ruins of Rauh feature large statues of a woman wearing an octagonal hat. She is associated with the Verdigris Discus and Bondstone. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to the "Rauh goddess" figure. The Golden Crucible originated in Rauh.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **The Grandmother** (大母, *Taibo*) was an unseen character in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Grandmother is a petrified maiden encased within the trunk of a large tree at the Shaman Village in the Hinterland of Scaduview. Roots or branches extend from her body, forming the tree itself. She kneels barefoot, arms outstretched, palms up in open embrace. A dark dress clings to her stone frame, and her eyes are veiled by long silver hair tied in two braids.

She was revered by the oppressed shamans, supposed denizens of another world.  After rising to power, Queen Marika severed a braid of her golden hair and left it as an offering to the matriarch of her people. She blessed the village with golden light and left—never to return.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- While her Japanese name, 大母, is rarely used to refer to the mother of ones parents, it can be more literally read as "Great Mother;" the same term is used to refer to Greyoll.
- Her features strongly resemble those of the tortured Jar Dwellers found in Bonny Gaol and elsewhere.
- The headless statue found outside Bonny Village resembles the Grandmother.
- The Grandmother may have embedded herself into the tree to water it with her blood in the way Miquella did his Haligtree.
- The Grandmother may have been a Numen.
- Fractured Marika is found in a statuesque form at the Stone Platform within the Erdtree.
- Her eyes are obscured, which implies blindness.
  - One of her eyes is open while the other is closed, though this cannot be seen under normal gameplay.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Golden Vow may be found in the Realm of Shadow on the Scadu Altus.
- Shadow Keep: x3 are found in the area with the large golden tree, guarded by a Black Knight.
- Shadow Keep: x1 is looted from a corpse.

sections.heading: Crafting
sections.text:
Golden Vow may be crafted after obtaining the Battlefield Priest's Cookbook (3). It requires the following Crafting Materials:
- Blessed Bone Shard (x1)
- Shadow Sunflower (x2)

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Golden Vow casts an Erdtree incantation that applies an Aura Buff to self and nearby allies.
- Golden Vow uses 30 FP to increase Attack Power by 12.5% and all Defenses by 8.8% for 45 seconds.
- The item is consumed upon use.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Golden Vow is weaker than Golden Vow (spell) but stronger than Ash of War: Golden Vow.
- The damage boosting effect stacks multiplicatively with Flame, Grant Me Strength and Howl of Shabriri.
- The defense boosting effect stacks multiplicatively with Boiled Crab and other food buffs.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Glintstone Nails** is a sorcery spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Finger sorceries.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchased**: Cathedral of Manus Metyr
- Glintstone Nails may be purchased from Count Ymir for  12,000 Runes after ringing the bell in the Finger Ruins of Rhia.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
The caster summons six magic nails that each deal Magic damage with an Attack Power equal to 66% of Sorcery Scaling and 2 Stance damage (396% and 12 Stance in total).

Charging the spell increases its potency to 75% Sorcery Scaling and 4 Stance damage (450% and 24 Stance in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  23 FP per cast.
- Costs  26 Stamina per cast (27 when charged).
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- The projectiles travel slower than other magic but have superior tracking and medium range.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- Finger Robe boosts attack power by 8%.
- Maternal Staff boosts attack power by 15%.
- Godfrey Icon boosts the attack power of charged attacks by 15%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The projectiles track enemies extremely well and can hit distant or agile targets effectively.
- It pairs well with other crowd control or zoning spells, offering consistent multi-target damage at medium range.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is used by Count Ymir, Mother of Fingers.
- The Catacombs Sorcerers cast an unobtainable variant of this spell as a Death Sorcery.
- Update 1.13 increased attack power by approximately 6% and improved enemy tracking.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Golden Arcs** is a spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It's one of the Spiral Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Scadu Altus
- Found in an already opened chest within the pit in Moorth Ruins in a shrine guarded by three Inquisitors.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Send out 3 swift, small golden arcs with a sweep of the arm, each having Holy Attack Power equal to 80% of Incantation Scaling (equal to 240% of Incantation Scaling in total).

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power per arc to 95% of Incantation Scaling (285% of the same in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. Charging increases the cost to 26 points.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit (15 in total).
- Attack Power is boosted by 20% per Spiraltree Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 19%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 37%.
- Since the Attack Power per arc is somewhat mediocre, the damage may be somewhat lower than expected.
- Surprisingly great Stance damage, especially if using the quicker uncharged casting.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.13: Fixed a bug that caused the "Golden Arcs" Incantation to generate attacks slower when cast with the left hand.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Golden Order Incantations**, also known as **Golden Order fundamentalist incantations**, are a type of incantation spell in Elden Ring.

The incantations of the fundamentalists of the Golden Order focused on holy damage, protection, and the eradication of Those Who Live in Death. The Golden Order Seal and the Radiant Gold Mask increase the effectiveness of Golden Order incantations by 10%. The Dryleaf Seal increases the effectiveness by 15%, barring Litany of Proper Death.

They each require a moderate amount of both Intelligence and Faith to cast, with the exception of Law of Causality and Law of Regression, both of which only require Intelligence.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Guardian** is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign. He is one of the ten playable Nightfarer classes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Guardian is charged with vanquishing the Nightlord to prevent a looming tragedy in Limveld. He lost his old flock during a tragic war long ago.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A proud Pinionfolk, he bears brown feathered wings, taloned legs, and a fierce, hawkish presence. Clad in ornate, heavy armor, he carries a tower shield and wields a great halberd. Though one wing is malformed, he takes to the skies, descending upon his foes with swift and tempestuous might.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text: Stats displayed below are for character at level 15.

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.text: Guardian is a tank class with high defenses and powerful crowd-control abilities.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.text: - Steel Guard - Guardian can enter into a more defensive stance by pressing dash whilst guarding with a shield. Improves guarding ability at the cost of gradual stamina drain.

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.text: - Whirlwind – Guardian sends foes flying by producing a strong gust of wind. While gust is active it can deflect projectiles.

sections.heading: Ultimate Art
sections.text: - Wings of Salvation – Guardian takes flight to swoop at enemies in a devastating divebomb attack. Hold to deploy a white aura that makes nearby allies invincible.

sections.heading: Starting Equipment
sections.text:
- Guardian starts each run with Guardian's Halberd and Guardian's Greatshield.
- Guardian prefers Halberds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Greattree** is an unseen location in Elden Ring. It is mentioned only in a few item descriptions.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The vast network of Greattree roots spreads throughout the Lands Between. The various catacombs and hero's graves of the region were built specifically around these roots. The Greattree roots begin where those of the Erdtree end: the Deeproot Depths—the source of the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers. The two root systems were once connected, which enabled Erdtree Burial.

After Godwyn the Golden received Erdtree Burial at the base of the Erdtree's roots, his soulless body transformed into the Prince of Death. Over time, fragments of the Rune of Death leaked from his body and spread through the roots of the Greattree, giving rise to Deathroot and, ultimately, Those Who Live in Death. Sometime after the Shattering, the two root systems ended up disconnected through the Deathroot corruption, impeding the Erdtree ability to recover bodies and souls through Erdtree Burial.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The roots of the Greattree secrete a special Root Resin used for making various greases.
- Elden Stars, the most ancient of all Erdtree Incantations, is placed near the  Great Waterfall Basin Site of Grace at the Deeproot Depths.
  - The Elden Beast's tail resembles golden roots.

- Oak leaves litter the area around the large hollowed-out tree protected by Crucible Knight Siluria.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Several references to the Greattree were not present in the English version 1.00 of Elden Ring. The relevant items instead used placeholder descriptions until a subsequent update.
- The "Greattree roots" are referred to as 大樹根 (*taijune*) in the Japanese version of *Elden Ring*. The term can be translated literally as "big/great tree roots", "great treeroots", or "Great Roots".
- The Japanese version of *Elden Ring* does not appear to use a distinct proper noun corresponding to "Greattree". Instead, it uses the descriptive term *taijune* ("great tree roots"). Compound names such as *Erdtree* and *lampwood* follow a naming convention often associated with  literature (e.g., **) and modern fantasy works inspired by it.
- The Finger Reader Crone in the Capital Outskirts refers to the Erdtree as a great tree in her dialogue; "Surely you see it, too? The gold that enshrouds the heavens. The great tree which begets the pillars of light. O Tarnished, hasten to the foot of the tree. And whatever you might face... The Fingers will surely guide you...". The Erdtree is also referred to as a great tree various more times in the Japanese text, such as with the name of the Tree-and-Beast Surcoat. 大樹と獣のサーコート translating to Great Tree and Beast Surcoat.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Gloveworts** are a type of flower in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Gloveworts are a type of flowering plant with hanging, bell-shaped white blooms borne in sprays in catacombs throughout the Lands Between. Spirits are drawn to the soundless tolling of these glowing, pendent flowers, making them essential to the art of spirit tuning. Certain specimens radiate profound spirituality, becoming semi-corporeal. Spirits often nestle closely to these ethereal buds.

Since ancient times, large gloveworts have served as tributes to heroic spirits who perish gloriously, ensuring their tales become legends.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Grave Gloveworts and Ghost Gloveworts are Bolstering Material used by Spirit Tuners to strengthen the power of Ashen Remains.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - "Glovewort" is an archaic name once used in England to describe the .

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Grand Altar of Dragon Communion burns within a large dish beside the corpse of a colossal dragon that had its heart devoured in Dragon Communion. This is where the Heart of Bayle may be devoured.

The Grand Altar of Dragon Communion lies in the unmarked Southern Shore area at the Foot of the Jagged Peak. It is accessed from the Gravesite Plain via the Dragon's Pit and heading south at the slumbering Jagged Peak Drake. Charo's Hidden Grave can be reached by dropping down near the dragon's feet.

sections.text: The **Grand Lifts** are landmarks in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Grand Lifts of the Lands Between provide passage between certain regions. The Grand Lift of Dectus carries champions between the Altus Plateau and Liurnia of the Lakes. The Grand Lift of Rold grants access between the Forbidden Lands, Consecrated Snowfield, and Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.text: The **Guard Counter**, also known as the **counterattack**, is a gameplay mechanic in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Guard Counters are special melee attacks that deal bonus Stance damage to enemies. They are heavy attacks performed immediately after blocking an attack, indicated by a sound effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Guard Counters quickly deplete a target's Stance, triggering a stagger proc. When timed correctly, they can be used to interrupt certain channeled attacks.
- Weapons that deal  Pierce damage can perform Thrusting Counterattacks.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **God Hunt** was an event mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The god hunt was a campaign launched by the Gloam-Eyed Queen to bring death to the gods of her time. It ended with her defeat and the sealing of the Rune of Death and thus the true power of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Rune of Death, also known as Destined Death, was once part of the Elden Ring until it was removed by Queen Marika to give shape to her Golden Order.

The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by her own Two Fingers, and individual with the potential to succeed Marika as vessel of the Elden Ring. At some point between the War Against the Giants, after the order Fire Monks was established to watch over the Flame of Ruin and the end of the Age of Plenty, when the Erdtree's blessed sap was still abundant she managed to get her hands on the Rune of Death, wielding it to empower the black flame she channeled from her spiral greatsword

sections.heading: Battles
sections.text:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen raised her Apostles, childrens with serpentine tails that had assimilated inhuman physiology like the Crucible that had created the Erdtree and cradled the newborns in swaddling cloths made of skin. The Queen taught them incantations of the black flame and they used Godslayer's Seals made with obsidian and representing the manipulation of her power.. She raised her children to became the servants of Destined Death and the death of the gods. The Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles thus started their hunts against the gods. Dozens of "gods" would be killed and flayed, and their divine hides were stitched into clothing for their hunters, thus giving them the title of "Godskin" Apostles

The Godskin Apostles wielded twinblade peelers that featured a sickle on one end and a spike for flesh piercing in the other, requiring high skill while the Godskin Nobles, the most ancient apostles, possessed incredible skill with the stitcher swords and wore aprons with seven faces They also stole a power that once represented the gods' wrath, and wielded it as a trophy in the form of a shockwave manifested from their bellies.

At some point during the conflict, some Fire Monks deserted their eternal duty of guardians of the Forge of the Giants and the Giants' Flame contained therein, their long watch having eroded their resolve as they started to succumb to the allure of the Flame's taboo. The first to abandon his post as guardian was Amon, who swore allegiance to the black flames of the gods' hunts and became the first Blackflame Monk. Many more would become traitors of their order, letting themselves be seduced by the black flames of the Gloam Eyed Queen and its apostles.

The God Hunt ended when the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles were defeated by Marika's shadowbound beast, Maliketh.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text:
After the defeat of the Gloam Eyed Queen, Marika's only need for her shadow was to serve as a vessel. On her orders, Maliketh sealed away the Rune of Death, binding it within his Black Blade. Marika's offspring thus obtained a form of immortality owing to the removal of their fated deaths from the Elden Ring, however Maliketh continued to instill fear in the demigods thanks to his blade containing the only power that could still kill them.

As a result of the Rune of Death being sealed, the true power of the black flame of the Godskins was also lost but, despite their Queen's defeat, her surviving Apostles and Nobles continued to remain hidden along with some Blackflame Monks. One Apostle and some Monks managed to flee to the fringes and continued to protect the Godslayer's Greatsword of their Queen deep inside the Divine Tower of Caelid. A Noble and an Apostle would die in the Spiritcaller Cave, still holding onto the swaddling cloth of their Queen.

Following the Shattering, many agents of the Gloam-Eyed Queen would reappear in the Lands Between with the apparent goal of continuing to seek the power of Death or to act against the gods. One Noble would try to infiltrate the Divine Tower of Liurnia where the Cursemark of Death left on Ranni's corpse is found. One Apostle would lead the skinning festivities of Dominula, Windmill Village. One Noble and a Blackflame Monk would protect the Temple of Eiglay, seemingly in serving of the God-Devouring Serpent. A Noble and an Apostle would manage to find their way into Crumbling Farum Azula, where Maliketh continued to protect the Rune of Death sealed inside his flesh.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The God Hunts could be the conflict in which the God-Devouring Serpent and serpents in general were branded as "traitors" by the Erdtree, implying a previous alliance.
  - A Godskin Apostle and Blackflame Monk can be found defending in the Temple of Eiglay where the shed skin of the deity can be found.
  - The Godskin Apostles have serpentine tails and share the ability to stretch their torso with Gelmir Man-Serpents, the children of the God-Devouring Serpent.
  - The robes of the Godskin Apostles were decorated with obsidian, also inlaid in their Godslayer's Seals, a natural product of volcanos, with Mt. Gelmir thus implied to be the main lair of the Godskin.
  - The Gelmir Hero's Grave implies a major conflict in the location that involved the forces of the Erdtree.
- The Two Fingers may have sanctioned the god hunt.
- Like the Godskin's emphasis on skinning their divine victims, flaying was the hallmark of the delightful festival of Dominula, Windmill Village, an old tradition tacitly tolerated by Queen Marika.
  - The design embroidered on the Blue Festive Garbs' cape used by the maidens selected to play a key role in the festivities of the Dominula Dancers matches the symbol on the Godskin Noble Robe.
  - One Godskin Apostle is found leading the skinning festivities of Dominula, Windmill Village.

sections.text: **Golem Smiths** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The stone Golem Smiths are rock constructs from ancient times. These golems labor away in the various ruined underground forges scattered throughout the Realm of Shadow. They imbue Molten Tears with souls to create smithscript weapons.

Golem Smiths are imposing, sluggish figures clad in brown aprons with white whisps of hair protruding from various parts of their bodies. They attack with their fists or with a variety of makeshift equipment, such as stone clubs and lava-filled crucibles. Others have inscribed a smithscript onto their fists, allowing them to be launched as fracturing projectiles.

They are powered by red glintstones housed at the base of their spines. These exposed gems are the Stone Golems' weak points.

sections.text: The **Golden Order Fundamentalists** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Fundamentalists directly worship the Golden Order through scholarly pursuits to the exclusion of all else. Their main core tenets were the Law of Causality and the Law of Regression. They believed all dead spirits should follow grace and return to the Erdtree after their deaths. They naturally vilified Those Who Live in Death and actively suppressed the spread of Deathroot. Some fundamentalists abandoned academia entirely to hunt an ultimate evil.

Their movement began when faith in the Erdtree waned and Queen Marika declared her theological inquiry into her Elden Ring. Fundamentalism was at its height during the Age of the Elden Ring, when Radagon of the Golden Order was Elden Lord.

sections.text: **Great Red Bears** are Bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Carnivorous feral beasts touched by the Crucible's influence, the Great Red Bears naturally sprouted horns suffused with spirituality. These red-haired Runebears prowled the Land of Shadow and took special pleasure in hunting and devouring other horned creatures.

They often clashed with local Highlanders, whose warriors also sought glory by subduing savage beasts and proving their own strength in battle. The fiercest Highlanders fixated on the bears' primal power, believing that hard-earned victory against such dangerous creatures revealed an inner, self-made divinity. A former Redmane warrior who slew a Great Red Bear in a blood-soaked duel became consumed by its unadorned power, wielding its claw without alteration and abandoning all desire except to be a Red Bear himself.

sections.text: The **Sentient Pest**, including **Animus, Ascendant Light**, **Gnoster, Wisdom of Night**, and **Faurtis Stoneshield**, is a Nightlord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
This Nightlord is two giant insects fought on the final Night of the Sentient Pest Expedition. The hardy scorpion shakes the earth when it stomps, and the white moth casts  Magic and  Poison spells. The sandy desert arena is covered in viridian leaves during the second phase, when the pests fight together as one. During the Everdark Sovereign version of the encounter, the bosses are revived after death by Animus, Ascendant Light, a red spectral moth.

If the moth grabs a player, it infects them with a parasite. If left unchecked, it develops into a worm that deals continuous damage. Allies can destroy both the worm and its larval form by attacking the infected player.

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.text: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, the Hero is the best choice for essentially any build which focuses mainly on Strength. Note that these builds are not necessarily "good", they are just what this origin is better at than any other.

sections.heading: Pure Strength
sections.text:
The Hero is by far and away the best origin for a build that increases strength while forsaking all other damage stats, saving 6 entire levels when compared to Wretch. This makes it the best choice for weapons such as the Greatsword or Giant-Crusher, which demand high strength but little of anything else. If a weapon requires 13 or more dexterity to wield, Vagabond will tie with Hero in point efficiency but hero will still outmatch every other origin considerably.

The Hero origin is also either the most efficient or tied for most efficient option for any hybrid class which is focused on raising the strength stat, with the exception of strength/dexterity/intelligence focuses and strength/dexterity/faith focuses, for which prisoner and vagabond are the best options respectively. This makes Hero the best option for essentially any strength hybrid weapon that does not demand high dexterity, such as:

- Ruins Greatsword
- Gargoyle's Black Axe
- Cranial Vessel Candlestand
- Staff of the Avatar
- Troll's Hammer

Note that Astrologer and Prophet both beat out Hero for strength/intelligence and strength/faith builds respectively if the dexterity requirement is 10 or higher, meaning that Hero is not optimal for weapons such as Starscourge Greatsword

sections.heading: Pure Arcane
sections.text: Surprisingly, Hero is also the best origin for a build which focuses on ignoring the leveling of other damage stats in favor of only increasing Arcane - although only being 1 level more efficient than both Wretch and Bandit - making it potentially the best option for bleed, poison and occult infusions. However, if the build also requires at least 11 dexterity or 9 intelligence, Bandit then becomes the most optimal origin.

sections.text: **Heal** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Equipped:**
- Heal is a starting spell for the Prophet origin.

**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
The caster kneels in prayer, healing HP equal to 230% of their Faith-based Incantation Scaling, and heals nearby allies for 115% of the same.

<section begin="RevEffect"/>Nearby Revenants and Revenant Followers take damage equal to 50% of their maximum HP plus an additional 300 HP. This attack also breaks their Stance, causing them to become staggered.<section end="RevEffect"/>

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  32 FP per cast.
- Costs  35 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Restores HP equal to 7.19% of Incantation Scaling for each FP spent.
- <section begin="Delay"/>The healing effect can be delayed indefinitely by holding the casting button, which is helpful if an ally is not yet within range.<section end="Delay"/>

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Heal is generally outclassed by the more efficient Great Heal and the significantly stronger Erdtree Heal.
- <section begin="Scaling"/>The healing amount is based on the Faith scaling of an equipped sacred seal. Seals that scale with other attributes will result in reduced healing effectiveness compared to those that focus solely on Faith.<section end="Scaling"/>
- <section begin="RevStrat"/>This spell breaks the stance of Revenants and Revenant followers, allowing you to quickly cast it again for a potential quick kill.<section end="RevStrat"/> This is the most FP-efficient way to quickly kill Revenants.
  - While technically only the Prophet and Confessor origins have enough Faith to use this incantation by default, it can still be used to kill a Revenant with any starting Origin's base Faith by using the Two Fingers Heirloom (a Prisoner will need another point in Faith, easiest gained with either Marika's Scarseal or a Commoner's Garb or Commoner's Simple Garb).
- All Origins have enough FP to cast this incantation at least 3 times without using a Flask of Cerulean Tears, provided they haven't used FP for anything too expensive.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is tied with Urgent Heal for the lowest healing effectiveness per FP spent.
- This incantation was included among the starting equipment for the Prophet class during the Closed Network Test.

- The requirement for an empty Cracked Pot is not listed directly in the crafting menu, instead having a row for it just above. The Pot is returned after the consumable is thrown.
- The seal created upon throwing this item is the same as the one used for Golden Order Incantations.
- Does somewhat mediocre damage against normal enemies but incredible amounts against Those Who Live in Death.
- Compared to the Sacred Order Pot:
  - Deals about 60-70% of the damage that a Sacred Pot deals against non-undead enemies.
  - Deals about 20% more damage against undead enemies.
  - Requires common ingredients, whereas the Sacred Pot requires farming Guardians for Golden Centipedes.

- (Empty) Cracked Pot x1

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Godrick the Grafted** is a Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The structure containing Stormveil Castle's throne room features an attached courtyard that serves as Godrick the Grafted's boss arena. It is a narrow, paved approach through a densely-filled graveyard. A slain dragon limply hangs from a pole, and Godrick seeks to graft its power.

If Godrick is defeated, Gatekeeper Gostoc moves here to stomp his face in the dirt. If Nepheli Loux, Warrior receives the ashes of the Stormhawk King, Kenneth Haight, Limgrave Heir identifies and can install her as the rightful Lord of Limgrave. Lord Godfrey—or Hoarah Loux, Warrior—earned the crown when he defeated the Stormhawk King in single combat long ago. Statues of Godfrey and Serosh still decorate the throne room.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
The  Godrick the Grafted site of grace is located in Stormveil Castle. It can be reached from the  Secluded Cell site of grace and passing through the boss fog gate. The site of grace appears inside the at the center of the graveyard after defeating Godrick the Grafted.

By passing through Stormveil's throne room and unlocking a door, the player can reach Liurnia of the Lakes.

sections.text:
- Redeemer Guilbert and Roundtable Knight Vyke appeared at this location in an early, prerelease version of the game. They would have been cooperators for the Godrick fight, but both questlines were cut.
- Gatekeeper Gostoc has cut quest stages in which he claims to be a son of Godrick and stakes his claim to the throne. He turned to grafting when attacked.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Grafting** is a concept in Elden Ring involving the attachment of severed body parts onto another living being.

It is a blending, melding, or merging of life. It is a way to gain another's power through the attachment of severed limbs. Even the body parts of trolls and dragons could be grafted.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Grafting was an accursed, grotesque, and shameful act practiced by certain members of the Golden Lineage, scions of Queen Marika the Eternal, most notably Godefroy and Godrick the Grafted. Godrick's grafting of Tarnished reflected his desperate attempt to compensate for his diluted divine blood through the accumulation of stronger limbs. The spirits of those he grafted became chrysalids.

sections.heading: Users
sections.text:
- Grafted Monarch
- Grafted Scion
- Godefroy the Grafted
- Godrick the Grafted

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Spirit tuning can ease the suffering of those who were grafted. Grafting inflicts less suffering than the way in which the Dung Eater ensnares souls.
- Warhawks had their talons "grafted", or forcibly replaced with lightweight swords.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Gatekeeper Gostoc has cut voicelines about how being the son of Godrick qualified him to graft.
- The Revenger merged many blades together to forge the Grafted Blade Greatsword, which appears to reflect the same principle of accumulated strength through amalgamation.

sections.text: The **Highland Axe** is an Axe, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Stormveil Castle
- The Highland Axe is found directly beneath a large painting of Elden Lord Godfrey and Serosh at Stormveil Castle.
- This area contains a Grafted Scion and may be reached by from the  Rampart Tower Site of Grace by descending the nearby elevator.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Boosts the strength of roar attacks (such as the enhanced heavy attacks of Barbaric Roar, or the projectile from Beast's Roar) by 10%. Do note that while this effect is very similar to the boost granted by the Roar Medallion, unlike that Talisman this Axe does not boost the damage of the breath and roar Incantations such as those found among the Dragon Communion Incantations.
  - Similar to how the damage boosts to spells from certain casting implements work, the Highland Axe only grants this boost while held in one of the active hands (left or right, the currently "shown" equipment). The other active piece of equipment can still be two-handed, as the other hand slot will still count as active in the meantime (so having a Highland Axe in the active left hand slot while two-handing a Greatsword in the right hand slot will still grant a damage boost to the Greatsword's War Cry skill.
  - Unlike many other such boosts, wielding two Highland Axes will not stack the boost and it will instead remain at 10%.
- This item is depicted on the Axe Talisman.
- This item's proximity to the painting and the description of the Axe Talisman posits Godfrey (Hoarah Loux) and the Tarnished as highlanders.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ivory Sickle** is a dagger found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Village of the Albinaurics
- The Ivory Sickle is looted from a stone coffin atop a hill at the Village of the Albinaurics, located beneath the Moonlight Altar in southwestern Liurnia of the Lakes. The item is near Old Albus and the  Village of the Albinaurics site of grace. Beware the Depraved Perfumer.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- While the skill, Quickstep, is rather generic for an innate, locked skill, it's still very useful for quicker traversal on surfaces that slow you down, like deep muck or water, and for getting around in combat aggressively.
  - Due to this weapon's mild Intelligence requirement and light weight, it allows for exploiting the fact that Quickstep costs 0 FP if the weapon's requirements aren't met and 8 out of 10 Origins won't do so by default (only the Astrologer and Prisoner meet them). While this heavily limits the skill's in-combat usage (decreases amount of i-frames from 15 to 5) it does make it ideal for traveling over slowing surfaces.
- Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed.
- Though its Dexterity-scaling is slightly stronger than its Intelligence-scaling it gains the most Attack Power from a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence approach.
  - Though the description may give the impression that this is a Faith-scaling weapon, it has not association with that stat.
- Overall a somewhat awkward weapon when it comes to how to best use it. A pure Intelligence build would do better with any other dagger with a Magic affinity while a hybrid Dex/Int build would probably prefer the Glintstone Kris.
  - It does admittedly serve as a decent stand-in for the aforementioned Glintstone Kris before getting it since it requires defeating two specific bosses holding Great Runes while the Ivory Sickle can be gained without defeating any boss at all if Stormveil Castle is bypassed and is available a bit earlier than most Cold or Magic affinity Skills. It's also a decent off-hand weapon but is somewhat hampered by requiring the somewhat hard-to-get-enough-of regular Smithing Stones.
- All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low original Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
  - This applies to both the Physical damage and the Magic damage.
  - As a dagger it will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Knight Bernahl** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Residing in the Warmaster's Shack of Limgrave, **Knight Bernahl** (騎士ベルナール) is a tarnished merchant who sells a number of Ashes of War. Bernahl was once a Tarnished champion worthy of becoming a lord, until his Finger Maiden cast herself into the flames.

Should the Tarnished join the Volcano Manor, they'll meet again with Bernahl, but this time he'll introduce himself as "Recusant Bernahl" (背律者ベルナール). After assassinating the first targets commissioned by Tanith, Bernahl will invite the Tarnished to join him in his hunt of Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm at the Fortified Manor of Leyndell, Royal Capital.

He will become as a summon against the Godskin Duo in Crumbling Farum Azula.

The Tarnished will come face to face with Bernahl one last time to the north of the Great Bridge in Crumbling Farum Azula, where the recusant will invade his former comrade.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave (Warmaster's Shack)
  - *(Optional)* Speaking to Bernahl unlocks the option to purchase Ashes of War from him, regardless of the answer to his question.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - Speaking with Tanith and selecting "**Join Volcano Manor**" to receive the Drawing-Room Key, Bernahl will relocate to the eastern quarter of the manor, where Rya the Scout is also found.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - After assassinating Old Knight Istvan, as commissioned in the first Letter from Volcano Manor, speaking to Bernahl unlocks the option to purchase the Ashes of War he used to sell in Limgrave and two new additions, Eruption and Assassin's Gambit.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - After assassinating Rileigh the Idle, as commissioned in the second Letter from Volcano Manor, speaking to Bernahl prompts him to give the Letter to Bernahl to the Tarnished, inviting him to join forces against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm at the Fortified Manor of Leyndell, Royal Capital.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Fortified Manor, First Floor)
  - Interacting with the invasion sign before the corpse holding Alberich's Set allows the Tarnished to fight alongside Bernahl against Vargram and Wilhelm. This assassination will reward the Tarnished with Vargram's Raging Wolf Set.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - With the task fulfilled, returning to Bernahl prompts him to give Gelmir's Fury to the Tarnished. This will also unlock his summon sign in Crumbling Farum Azula.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - After defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, exhausting Bernahl's dialogue triggers his departure from Volcano Manor. His shop will still be accessible via the "Sword of Bernahl" left on his chair.
1. Crumbling Farum Azula (Dragon Temple Transept)
  - *(Optional)* If the Tarnished and Bernahl hunted down Vargram and Wilhelm in Leyndell, the recusant's summon sign will appear outside the Dragon Temple, to aid his brother in arms against the Godskin Duo.
1. Crumbling Farum Azula (Besides the Great Bridge)
  - Following the path to the north from the Great Bridge, Bernhal will invade the Tarnished before the tower with the chest containing the Old Lord's Talisman. When defeated, he drops the Blasphemous Claw.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- If Rykard is killed by reaching him through the Abductor Virgin of Raya Lucaria before Bernhal moves to Volcano Manor, his regular drops will be found in the Warmaster's Shack.
- Bernahl's Bell Bearing will automatically upgrade its stock if its given to the Twin Maiden Husks after receiving the Drawing-Room Key, instead of beforehand.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Irina of Morne** is an NPC character in Elden Ring. She is found on the Weeping Peninsula, south of the Bridge of Sacrifice.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Irina is the daughter of Edgar, castellan of Castle Morne. Her eyesight has been weak since birth, and she wears a blindfold around her eyes.

Irina lived in Castle Morne with her father, until the Misbegotten servants rebelled and overran the castle. Edgar secreted Irina out of the castle, however the Misbegotten pursued her and killed her companions.

Irina encounters a Tarnished at the Bridge of Sacrifice on the Weeping Peninsula, and petitions them to rescue her father from Castle Morne, handing them a letter to deliver to him.

The Tarnished travels to Castle Morne and passes the letter onto Edgar. Once the Leonine Misbegotten has been defeated, Edgar leaves the castle to reunite with his daughter, vowing to devote his remaining days to her. However, by the time he reaches her location, Irina is already dead. Edgar swears vengeance on those responsible for her death, setting him on a path that eventually leads to his corruption by the Flame of Frenzy.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Weeping Peninsula (near Bridge of Sacrifice)
  - Irina can be found sitting on a rock near the Bridge of Sacrifice. Talk to her and accept her request to receive Irina's Letter.
1. Castle Morne
  - Find Castellan Edgar in Castle Morne and hand him Irina's Letter, before defeating the Leonine Misbegotten.
1. Weeping Peninsula (near Bridge of Sacrifice)
  - Return to Irina after delivering the letter to find her corpse. If you defeated the Leonine Misbegotten, Edgar will also be here.
  - If you rested at a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes after receiving Irina's Letter, Irina will die even if you have not done the Castle Morne segment of the questline.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Irina can be killed; however, this will prematurely end her questline and prevent Lightseeker Hyetta from appearing.
- If Irina dies, her blood can be used to soak the Lord of Blood's Favor for White Mask Varré.
- Lightseeker Hyetta shares the same appearance and voice actor as Irina of Morne. She will only appear if Irina's questline has ended with her death at the hands of the Misbegotten. This suggests Hyetta is Irina, possibly after undergoing a resurrection or rebirth ritual similar to Shabriri.
- Irina attacks by casting a weak spell resembling Rejection.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Voice actor: 
- Lightseeker Hyetta had an additional quest stage at Bellum Church in the , but the dialogue and key item she gave were both cut from the game by the  release. The context it provided offered insight into her transition from Irina of Morne and into the characters of Irina and Edgar. Hyetta gave Irina's Necklace after receiving the Fingerprint Grape, abandoning her long search for its owner. Irina carried the locket with her everywhere, a precious farewell gift from someone dear.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Jar-Bairn is a young Living Jar who lives in the secluded village of Jarburg in Liurnia of the Lakes. Like his uncle Alexander, he is a warrior jar, and strives to become a champion just like Alexander.

Presently, however, he is on the lookout for a new Potentate for the village. He meets the Tarnished when they pay a visit to Jarburg, but determines that they are not suited to be the new Potentate due to their rough hands. Nevertheless, he welcomes them to the village and invites them to come back and pick the flowers growing in the village whenever they want. He also warns the Tarnished of poachers who hunt and destroy other living jars.

Eventually, Jar-Bairn finds a new Potentate in Diallos Hoslow, a former Recusant who abandoned Volcano Manor after giving up on his path of revenge. Despite his disappointment that Diallos is not as strong as the Tarnished, he admires his smooth hands.

Not long after Diallos becomes Potentate, Jarburg is beset by poachers. Diallos defends the village and fights off the attackers, but many of the jars are broken and Diallos himself succumbs to his wounds. Jar-Bairn vows to become a warrior like Diallos, so that he can protect everybody. The Tarnished, having fought and defeated Alexander, offers the young jar his innards, which he uses to become even stronger, deciding to leave the village in search of glory, like his uncle.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Jarburg
  - Jar-Bairn can be found sitting in front of a house north-west of the Site of Grace. Exhaust his dialogue and decide whether or not to accept his request- the decision does not affect the rest of the questline. After resting at a Site of Grace, speak to him again to exhaust his new dialogue.
1. Jarburg
  - If you have met Alexander, Warrior Jar, Jar-Bairn will have new dialogue after you rest at a Site of Grace again.
1. Jarburg
  - After reloading the area, speak to him again to receive dialogue about poachers. This dialogue becomes available after Knight Diallos has arrived at Volcano Manor.
1. Jarburg
  - After Knight Diallos has left Volcano Manor, return to Jarburg and speak to Jar-Bairn again.
1. Jarburg
  - Reload the area six times and speak to Jar-Bairn near the middle of the village. Speak to Diallos and then reload the area and speak to Jar-Bairn once more.
1. Jarburg
  - After defeating Alexander, Warrior Jar in Crumbling Farum Azula, return to Jarburg and give Jar-Bairn Alexander's Innards. Reload the area, and speak to Jar-Bairn again to receive his final dialogue.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Jar-Bairn was added to the game as part of Update 1.03. Prior to this, Diallos's questline did not have a conclusion and Alexander's Innards served no purpose.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Said to hail from a settlement of horse-riding folk in the wintry mountaintops of the north, the brawny Kaiden Sellswords were fearless mercenaries who proved their prowess on countless battlefields.  They were renowned for their skill on horseback, dismounting other riders with hefty curved greatswords. They favored light, fur-lined scale armor and enhanced their considerable strength with fierce war cries, shouting the name of their home settlement.

- Their home settlement is not present in-game.
- Their helms are similar to the Leather Helms worn by highlanders, whose home settlement was also omitted.
- The Two-Handed Sword Talisman depicts a Horned Warriors brandishing a Dismounter, indicating cultural overlap with the hornsent.
- Kaiden Sellswords in Elden Ring Nightreign always spawn on horseback.

sections.heading: Trivia

- Kaiden Sellswords are voiced by , who also voiced Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, Shabriri, and the Fire Giant.
- In  and the , Kaiden Sellswords were known as **Northern Mercenaries** and were rumored to be descendants of giants.

sections.text: **Imps** are Enemies in Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree, and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Commonly found in Catacombs across the Lands Between, Imps are small, green stone Golems crafted with glintstone implements by an ancient golem-maker. They served as enduring attendants to the Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, guarding the tombs of the honored dead. Imps wield forked weapons known as "imp's tongues," whose undulating blades inflict Blood Loss. Each Imp wears a distinctive stone mask bearing the visage of a beast, demon, or elder.

They cling to walls and ceilings, waiting to ambush the unwary, and often fight in groups where their small size and agility make them dangerous opponents. However, attacking an Imp with Crystal Darts disrupts its programming, causing it to turn on allies and attack indiscriminately.

Attacking them during this animation can knock them to the ground, leaving them vulnerable. Hatchet Lion Imps can use their dragon-shaped hatchet to shoot streams of fire. sections.text: **Honed Bolt** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 7,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Hit with a bolt from above with Lightning Attack Power equal to 205% of Incantation Scaling.

Follow-up casts are quicker than the initial one.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
  - Also deals 2 Stance damage.
- Actually works by sending out an invisible bullet, which then creates the lightning bolt from above when it hits an opponent. This is also why Honed Bolt very often seems to hit far behind the target when it misses, as the bullet has hit its maximum range and automatically performs the attack.
- Combines well with other incantations due to its quick casting speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.04 increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Kenneth Haight** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He claims to be the next ruler of Limgrave but is in need of assistance as his fort has fallen.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
**Kenneth Haight** is a nobleman and claims to be next in line as the rightful ruler of Limgrave. He resided in a fort known as Fort Haight, and is known for his considerable largesse, at least by his own account. Godrick the Grafted assumed control of Limgrave following the Shattering, and at some point sent a knight commander to seize Fort Haight.

Driven out of his home, Kenneth began searching for adventurers who might help him restore control of his fort. He was stumbled upon by a Tarnished champion, and despite some reticence in accepting the help of a Tarnished, bid them to retake his fort in exchange for a handsome reward, while also sharing with them his exceedingly low opinion of Godrick.

Upon the Tarnished's success, a joyous Kenneth Haight grants them a reward and thanks them profusely. In addition, he offers them the opportunity to be knighted and enter into his service. He tells them to meet him as his fort, where the ceremony shall be held.

However, upon seeing the sorry state of his fort, Kenneth becomes maudlin. Believing that Limgrave cannot remain without a proper ruler, he dedicates himself to finding a true and stalwart Lord of the proper lineage as soon as possible. He apologizes to the Tarnished, telling them he now lacks the authority to lift them to knighthood.

After the death of Godrick, Kenneth eventually encounters a worthy lord; Nepheli Loux. Kenneth joins her in the throne room of Stormveil Castle to aid her in assuming the reins of the castle. When the Tarnished who had once aided him comes to visit, Kenneth tells him he intends to eventually return to his fort, where he can fulfill his old promise and raise them to knighthood at last.

He may or may not be a reference to the real-life role-playing game designer Kenneth Hite.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave (near Third Church of Marika)
  - Speak to Kenneth atop the ruin near the Third Church of Marika and agree to clear his fort.
1. Fort Haight
  - Kill the Godrick Knight in Fort Haight.
1. Limgrave (near Third Church of Marika)
  - Return to Kenneth and receive an Erdsteel Dagger. Accept his offer to make you a knight.
1. Fort Haight
  - Speak to Kenneth in Fort Haight.
1. Complete Nepheli Loux's questline.
1. Stormveil Castle
  - Speak to Kenneth in Stormveil Castle, in the throne room beyond the Godrick the Grafted Site of Grace.

sections.text: **Intelligence-knot Crystal Tear** is a key item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Found in a bowl at the bottom of a cliff south of the Caria Manor in Liurnia of the Lakes, guarded by several small Fingercreepers and one large one.

From the Sorcerer's Isle Site of Grace, right next to Testu's Rise, head north along the coast until a low-lying and forested area is found and then continue north. Be careful with approaching, as the large Fingercreeper is hiding in the ground right next to the bowl.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Diallos Hoslow** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Diallos Hoslow is a scion of House Hoslow and the younger brother of Juno Hoslow. From a young age, Diallos was all talk and no trousers, with an inability to commit to action. As a result, Juno inherited the Hoslow legacy without resistance. Juno loved his brother dearly and showered him with adoration. Diallos, in turn, admired his brother, a mighty warrior who lived up to the bloody legacy of House Hoslow. Diallos aspired to be like his older brother, knowing that pursuing the bloody legacy of their house would break his brother's heart.

Diallos had a servant by the name of Lanya and the two were companions since childhood. At some point, the two set out on a journey in the Lands Between, but Diallos lost track of the fickle Lanya, and the two became separated. He made his way to Roundtable Hold where he implored the Hold's visitors to keep an eye out for Lanya.

Diallos eventually managed to track Lanya down to Liurnia of the Lakes, where he found her dead. He deduced that the recusants of the Volcano Manor were behind her death and swore vengeance upon them. He tracked them down to their hideout on Mt. Gelmir, but when the proprietor of the manor, Lady Tanith, offered him a place among them, flattering him by telling him he had the stuff of champions, Diallos abandoned his vengeance and decided to join the manor as a recusant.

Diallos pursued the path of a recusant, dirtying his hands time and again, but soon came to realize his folly. Having achieved nothing, he declared himself a complete fool, just as his brother had said, for abandoning the path of revenge and sullying the name of his house.

Diallos left the Volcano Manor and travelled to Jarburg, a settlement for Living Jars. Diallos became Jarburg's new "Potentate" and devoted himself to caring for the jars. Diallos was at peace with his new calling, feeling for the first time in his life that he was on the straight and narrow. The jars enjoyed his soft, silky hands, but they were disappointed by his apparent lack of strength and courage.

When Jarburg was invaded by jar-poachers, Diallos took up arms to defend his charges. He was mortally wounded in the battle, but managed to drive off the poachers and saved most of the jars. Diallos died at peace, having finally proven his worth to his dear jars and to himself.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Roundtable Hold
  - (Optional) Diallos can be found in Roundtable Hold upon the player's first visit. He will ask you to look out for his servant, Lanya, who has gone missing.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Academy Gate Town)
  - Diallos will appear in Liurnia of the Lakes, northwest of the Academy Gate Town Site of Grace. Talk to him and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Diallos will return to Roundtable Hold. Speak to him to learn the location of Volcano Manor.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor}
  - After joining the Recusants, Diallos will appear in the drawing room in Volcano Manor.
  - After defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy or completing one of Tanith's requests, speak to Diallos again and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Jarburg)
  - After progressing the Jar-Bairn's questline, Diallos will relocate to Jarburg in Liurnia of the Lakes.
  - After resting at a Site of Grace five times, return to Jarburg to find Diallos dying. Speak to him and then reload the area to obtain Diallos's Mask and Hoslow's Petal Whip.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood** is a hostile NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Juno Hoslow is Diallos' older brother and the head of their illustrious house.

A successful, stern and self-possessed man of a few words, Juno inherited the legacy of the Hoslow family to protect his inept brother, whom he loved dearly.

Despite drenching himself in blood time and time again, he refused the invitation to the Volcano Manor. Later, he became their target.

His sign can be found in the Mountaintops of the Giants, outside the Shack of the Lofty.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - After joining the Volcano Manor and eliminating Old Knight Istvan and Rileigh the Idle under Tanith's request, retrieve the Red Letter to unlock Juno Hoslow's invasion sign in the Mountaintops of the Giants.
  - With Rileigh dead, you can also talk to Recusant Bernahl to receive the Letter to Bernahl, offering you to join him in his hunt against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm in Leyndell, Royal Capital.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - Once Juno is disposed of, return to Tanith to receive the Taker's Cameo: she'll now offer to transport you to the Audience Pathway Site of Grace by selecting **See the Lord**.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - With the Red Letter in inventory, even if Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is defeated prior to the invasion, abruptly concluding Tanith's questline, not only will the invasion sign still be available, but the reward will also be relocated in the spot where the Red Letter was retrieved.

sections.text: **Jarburg** is a Location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A peaceful village populated by Living Jars, secluded on the eastern coast of Liurnia of the Lakes. Jarburg is the home of Alexander, Warrior Jar, though he left to pursue his fate some time ago, vowing to never return. The villagers are in need of a Potentate to protect them from poachers.

Jarburg is difficult and dangerous to access. Located on a lower level south of Carian Study Hall, it can be reached by descending massive gravestones jutting from the side of eastern the cliff.

It contains a multitude of respawning flowers in gardens scattered around the area.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Imbued Sword Key** is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- Unlocks the disabled Sending Gates of The Four Belfries.
- Each key is consumed upon use.

sections.heading: Sending Gates
sections.text:
- **Crumbling Lands**: Leads to an isolated section of Crumbling Farum Azula, where the Pearldrake Talisman is found.
- **Night Sky Unceasing**: Leads to an isolated section of Nokron, Eternal City, where the Mottled Necklace is found.
- **Precipice of Anticipation**: Leads back to the game's starting area, allowing a rematch with the Grafted Scion. Also contains Stormhawk Deenh, The Stormhawk King, and the corpse of the Tarnished's former Finger Maiden for progressing White Mask Varré's questline.
A fourth Sending Gate is found at the Fifth Belfry in the Realm of Shadow, located behind Castle Ensis, on a small island north of the  Castle Ensis Checkpoint Site of Grace. This area is part of the Scadu Altus.
- This gate leads to a body of water in the southern Ancient Ruins of Rauh, where the Verdigris Discus is found.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
A total of **four** Imbued Sword Keys can be found per playthrough.

1. The Four Belfries: Found in a chest near the  The Four Belfries Site of Grace.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria: Located on the rooftop section of Raya Lucaria, northwest of the  Debate Parlor Site of Grace.
1. Caelid: Found in a chest guarded by a Twinsage Scholar outside Sellia, Town of Sorcery, nearest the  Sellia Under-Stair Site of Grace.
1. Castle Ensis: Found in a chest in a tower southwest of the  Castle-Lord's Chamber Site of Grace. Take the lower western opening from the grace and use the elevator to reach it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Required for parts of Nepheli Loux and White Mask Varré's questlines.
- Unused keys will be lost upon entering .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Kindred of Rot**, also known as **pests**, are enemies in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Anthropomorphic, insectoid beings that emerged from the Swamp of Aeonia, they are forsaken servants and unwanted children of the new Goddess of Rot. They are commonly found in places blighted by Scarlet Rot, such as Caelid and the Grand Cloister.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Fully grown pests found in Rot-infested areas. They wield glaives made from hard, sharpened shell, and can fire web-like threads from a distance. If Scarlet Rot or Poison is utilised near them, they receive a buff.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Fully-grown pests found in Rot-infested areas around the ancient Rauh Ruins and the Church of the Bud. They are colored pink to signify they have been embraced by Romina, Saint of the Bud. They wield glaives made from hard, sharpened shell, and can fire Pest Threads and Pest-Thread Spears from a distance. If Scarlet Rot or Poison is utilised near them, they receive a buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The pests at the Sellia Crystal Tunnel pray toward a statue of a woman.
- The pests at the Grand Cloister in the Lake of Rot pray toward the Scorpion's Stinger.
- The scarlet pests at the Rauh Ruins pray before a large, ancient statue of a woman.
- The pests loyal to Romina in Realm of Shadow are red, while those abandoned by Malenia are pale.

**Heavy Thrusting Swords** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
They have moderately quick attack speed and reasonable range as well as more damage against health, poise and have a relatively subtle telegraphs at the start of most of their attack animations.  However they are overall slower and have a higher stamina cost compared to smaller Thrusting Swords

Similar to Curved Swords and Thrusting Swords, their heavy attack charges can be canceled in favor of a quick feint-attack should the player press the Roll button while charging. They can also attack while guarding at the same time similar to smaller to their smaller brethren and Spears. Their two-handed moveset is generally very similar to their one-handed one, increasing overall damage to health and poise.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Holyproof Dried Liver** is a craftable, consumable tool in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Increases Holy damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP) upon consumption. This counts as a Body Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
Unlike the other Liver items, the Holyproof Dried Liver has a much stronger effect that is on par with the associated elemental fortification Incantation instead of weaker than it.

This means that it is almost strictly superior to Divine Fortification in both PvE and PvP due to having the same effectiveness, greater duration (120 seconds vs 90 seconds), much lower FP cost (0 FP vs 20 FP). The only downside is that Divine Fortification can be used infinitely after acquiring it as long as you have a Sacred Seal and 10 Faith while the Liver has to be repeatedly crafted for that, which may require you to run out of the way to grab crafting materials.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be crafted after acquiring the Missionary's Cookbook 6 from a cell in the bottom of dark tower in Volcano Manor. The tower is found beside the lava lake after the Temple of Eiglay Site of Grace, and is entered through an open window before descending further down through ladders and stairs.
- 2 are found on the rafters of the Inverted Carian Study Hall.
- Found in a dark sewer room under the wing of the great dragon Gransax's corpse in Leyndell, Royal Capital. The area is guarded by a Broken Gargoyle Statue in an opening and also contains one Erdsteel Dagger.

sections.heading: Required items
sections.text:

- Beast Liver x1
- Golden Sunflower x3

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Fireproof Dried Liver, the same item but for Fire damage negation and a weaker (15% (10% in PvP)) effect.
- Lightningproof Dried Liver, the same item but for Lightning damage negation and a weaker (15% (10% in PvP)) effect.
- Spellproof Dried Liver, the same item but for Magic damage negation and a weaker (15% (10% in PvP)) effect.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Hero's Graves** are Landmarks in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Hero's Graves housed the remains of fallen champions whose heroism and valor earned them the privilege of Erdtree Burial. Followers of Queen Marika constructed or repurposed these catacombs during the age of the Erdtree, selected for their proximity to Greattree roots. The process facilitated and prioritized the heroes' spiritual return to the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The surface entrances to Hero’s Graves are multi-tiered stone mausoleums with precise ornamentation. Each is crowned by a statue of a headless undertaker draped in a heavy shroud, cradling a pale, limp form as it proceeds toward the Erdtree. The dying figure reaches weakly for the golden tree in rigid, almost supplicant surrender—depicting the moment of death before the spirit’s return to the Erdtree.

Inside, the catacombs contain statues and shrines honoring a handless maiden, and banners corresponding to the factions the interred heroes served. The remains are typically guarded by imps and Merciless Chariots.

sections.heading: List of Hero's Graves
sections.text: There are **five** Hero's Graves in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The statues are orientated to directly face the Erdtree.
- The anonymous, faceless undertaker likely represents solemn impartiality toward the dead it receives.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Holy** is a Damage Type in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Fighting Against Holy
sections.text:
- Divine Fortification/Lord's Divine Fortification, increases Holy damage negation by 35%/60% (10%/20% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user, lasting for 90 seconds/70 seconds. Lord's Divine Fortification additionally grants the buff to nearby allies. Requires 10 and 27 Faith to cast.
- Protection of the Erdtree, increases Holy damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user and nearby allies for 70 seconds. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Magic damage negation by the same amount. Requires 35 Faith to cast.
- Haligdrake Talisman/Haligdrake Talisman +1/Haligdrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Holy damage negation by 13%/17%/20% (4%/5%/6% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time.
- Pearldrake Talisman/Pearldrake Talisman +1/Pearldrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Holy damage negation by 5%/7%/9% (2%/3%/4% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Magic damage negation by the same amount.
- Holyproof Dried Liver, a consumable and Body Buff that increases Holy damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP). Lasts for 120 seconds.
- Pest's Glaive, a Halberd that increases Holy damage negation by 2%. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Magic damage negation by the same amount. Only works if held in an active hand and does not stack with another Pest's Glaive.

sections.heading: Fighting With Holy
sections.text:
- Holy-Shrouding Cracked Tear, increases Holy damage dealt by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes when used with the Flask of Wondrous Physick.
- Sacred Scorpion Charm, a Talisman that increases Holy damage dealt by 12% (8% in PvP) while increasing Physical damage taken by 10% (15% in PvP).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Intelligence** (知力, *Chiryoku*) is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Intelligence stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Intelligence scaling. Increasing Intelligence will also increase their resistance to magic.

The Tarnished can level Intelligence by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Magic Defense gained through leveling Intelligence has soft caps at 20, 35, and 60 Intelligence.

sections.heading: Items that increase Intelligence
sections.text:
;Semi-permanent
- Haima Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 2. Also increases Strength by 2 but decreases FP by 10%.
- Hierodas Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 2. Also increases Endurance by 2 but decreases FP by 10%.
- Imp Head (Cat): Head armor that increases Intelligence by 2.
- Karolos Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 3. Also decreases Stamina by 9%.
- Lazuli Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 3. Also increases Dexterity by 3 but decreases HP by 18%.
- Marika's Scarseal/Soreseal: Talisman that increases Intelligence by 3/5. Also increases Mind, Faith, and Arcane by 3/5 while increasing damage taken by 10%/15%. Cannot both be worn at the same time.
- Olivinus Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 3. Also decreases HP by 10%.
- Salza's HoodShadow of the Erdtree: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 2.
- Stargazer Heirloom: Talisman that increases Intelligence by 5.
- Twinsage Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 6. Also decreases HP and Stamina by 9% each.
- Queen's Crescent Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 3.
- Witch's Glintstone Crown: Head armor that increases Intelligence by 3. Also increases Arcane by 3 but decreases Stamina by 18%.

;Temporary
- Fingerprint NostrumShadow of the Erdtree: Increases Intelligence by 6 for 90 seconds. Also increases Mind, Faith, and Arcane by 6 and drains 3 HP per second (270 HP total) for the same duration. Counts as a Body Buff.
- Godrick's Great Rune: Great Rune that increases Strength by 5 upon activation with a Rune Arc. Lasts until death or until the Great Rune is switched out, and also increases Vigor, Mind, Endurance, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith, and Arcane by 5 until death or the Great Rune is switched out.
- Intelligence-knot Crystal Tear: Crystal Tear that increases Intelligence by 10 for 3 minutes when the Flask of Wondrous Physick is used if it's equipped. Only two Crystal Tears can be equipped at the same time.
- Oath of Vengeance: Unique skill of the Grafted Blade Greatsword that increases Intelligence by 5 for 60 second upon activation. Costs 20 FP and also increases Vigor, Mind, Endurance, Strength, Dexterity, Faith, and Arcane by 5 for 60 seconds and greatly increases Poise for 5 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Hiding his festering face under tightly-wound bandages, Ghiza carries out his duties of surveillance, execution and gruesome rituals wielding a flesh-flaying iron wheel that would later inspire the Abductor Virgins' weapons.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
- Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)

Invades within the room upstairs near the Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Incantations** (祈祷, *Kitō*; lit. "Prayers") are a type of spell in Elden Ring.

All incantations require FP to cast, with most necessitating a high investment in the Faith stat. However, some incantations are based on Intelligence or Arcane. The Incantation Scaling varies depending on their stat requirements and the player's own stats.

Incantations can only be cast using sacred seals, which act as the required catalyst.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Info Items** is an inventory category in Elden Ring which cover a variety of purposes, including hints, clues, and other guiding information.

The tutorials are typically acquired after the player is introduced to a new game mechanic, while notes and simple maps are obtained from Nomadic Merchants or found scattered throughout the Lands Between. sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Host of Fingers** is a multiplayer role in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Host of Fingers is the host of the multiplayer session. Other players are being summoned to or invading the world of the host player. The Host of Fingers has one objective: Defeat the area boss without dying.

There are several ways to become a Host of Fingers. They are as follows:

- Use a Furlcalling Finger Remedy and summon a Furled Finger from a gold summon sign.
- Use a Furlcalling Finger Remedy and summon a Duelist from a red summon sign.
- Use the Taunter's Tongue in an area with a living boss to be Invaded by another player.

The connection will end if the host uses the Finger Severer, defeats a boss, or is killed in any way. The Finger Severer cannot be used to dismiss an Adversary.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Summoning Furled Fingers is mostly the same as summoning NPC Cooperators.
- Gold Ally summon signs are hidden after the area's boss has been defeated.
- The Host of Fingers has no color overlay (e.g., red).
  - The Host's Trick-Mirror can give the player a golden overlay, regardless of role.
  - The Furled Finger's Trick-Mirror has no effect when equipped to the Host of Fingers.
- The Finger Severer cannot be used to dismiss red players.
- The Host of Fingers retains their full Sacred Flask charges; however, they cannot rest at Sites of Grace while the Furlcalling Finger Remedy or Taunter's Tongue is active.
- If the host has activated the White Cipher Ring, blue Hunters may be summoned automatically to repel the Invading players.
