sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Incantation Scaling**, or **Incant Scaling**, is an attack power stat in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Incantation Scaling is a stat unique to Sacred Seals, and increases the amount of damage caused by Incantations cast by the seal used. The Tarnished must meet the required attribute stats to wield the weapon, or the Incant Scaling will be reduced. On the other hand, exceeding the Faith requirement will increase the Incant Scaling of the seal used. Incant Scaling can also be increased by upgrading the sacred seals.

Incant Scaling only affects the damage or healing of the incantations cast by the seal, and has no effect on the duration of buffs or other incantations. Incantations which heal over time do not benefit from Incant Scaling. The Incantation Scaling of the seal used to cast is the only Incant Scaling used to determine the effectiveness of the incantation. Having a second seal equipped will not affect the incantations being cast by the other seal.

For Healing and Weapon Buff incantations only the portion of the Scaling that comes from Faith will count, meaning hybrid seals (Clawmark Seal, Dragon Communion Seal, Golden Order Seal) will be much weaker for casting these spells.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Immunity** is an resistance stat in Elden Ring.

Immunity governs the Tarnished's ability to resist the build-up of Poison and Scarlet Rot. It will not decrease the amount of damage taken once afflicted by Poison or Scarlet Rot.

The Tarnished's base Immunity is two parts, with each part determined by their Level and Vigor attribute. The sum of the two parts is what is displayed on the Status screen. The Tarnished's Immunity will increase as they level up, with soft caps at level 71, 111 and 161, which will see dimishing returns based on level as the level increases. Vigor does not begin to directly affect Immunity until Level 31, at which point the resulting increase from Vigor will be added to the total base Immunity displayed.

- From 31-40 Vigor: +3 Immunity each level
- From 41-60 Vigor: +0.5 Immunity each level
- From 61-99 Vigor: +0.25 Immunity each level

Immunity is further increases by equipping armor, which will display in the righthand column of the Status screen.

Immunity can be temporarily be increased by consuming Immunizing Cured Meat, Immunizing White Cured Meat and Dappled Cured Meat.

sections.heading: Items that increase Immunity
sections.text:
;Directly
- Spiralhorn Shield, a small shield that increases Immunity, Robustness and Focus while equipped.
- Eclipse Crest Greatshield, a greatshield that increases Immunity, Robustness and Focus while equipped.

;Indirectly
- Crimson Hood, head armor that increases Vigor by 1, giving a slight boost to Immunity as a result.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
There are various animation interactions within *Elden Ring* which have been found to have clearly unintended behavior, such as consistently not taking player inputs at points which are intended. This results in combat feeling clunky and unfair, as players doubt and question if the game is even responding to their inputs when it’s supposed to. These are similar to exploits and passive glitches, which tend to affect the game as a whole negatively for all players, but in a way that is difficult for most to pin down.

The following are input drop issues that players have been able to identify:

sections.heading: Sprint-Guarding Input-Drop
sections.text:
When stopping a sprint and lowering your guard around the same time, any action the player inputs will be dropped (e.g. rolling, attacking).
­

sections.heading: Two-Hand-Jumping Input-Drop
sections.text:
When continuing to sprint after a jump, the player cannot queue a light attack action for a significant amount of time after landing, while any other input works including guarding. This does not occur when 1-handing weapons.
At the below  timestamp, you can see the keyboard “Light Attack” input being repeatedly dropped, only while 2-handing and after landing from a sprinting jump.
­

sections.heading: Damage Occurrence Input-Drop
sections.text: When the player receives damage that does not stun them, certain actions seem to be cleared from the input queue such as roll dodging, which causes players to be hit again as they expected the game to not clear their input. This has been confirmed to be a result of the damage occurrence and not any misconceptions with queue timing.

sections.heading: Moving Toggle Input-Drop
sections.text:
While moving during a toggle (weapon swap/2-handing) animation, it is impossible to buffer another action out of the animation until it finishes. Despite this, you are still able to buffer actions when toggling while standing still.
At the timestamp below, you can see the keyboard “Heavy Attack” input being dropped only while doing a moving toggle.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Kaiden** is a mentioned location in Elden Ring. It is said to be located at the mountaintops of the wintry north and serves as the home settlement for a clan of hulking, fearless mercenaries who are adept at fighting on horseback.

They primarily make use of a type of curved greatsword whose versatile design combines the blade of a scimitar with the heft of a hatchet. The mercenaries cover themselves in navy-blue cloth, chain-mail and scaly gray armor while insulating themselves from the blistering cold with the pelt of snow-wolves. They all take great care in maintaining their horses, carrying various types of Rowa Raisins to feed their animal companions.

__TOC__

While a decent amount of the Kaiden Sellswords can be unsurprisingly encountered in the snowfields of the Giant's Mountaintops, they are generally well traveled and can be encountered in more regions around the Lands Between, particularly in Limgrave where they have seemingly been hired to guard campsites, patrol shorelines or escort Wandering Nobles in the middle of transporting their excavated relics.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- It is unclear if Kaiden is or was once located on the Mountaintops of the Giants, as there is no explorable, in-game location that actually bears its name.
  - It could be possible that it is located even further north than the mountaintops, beyond the watery borders of the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**House Hoslow** is an illustrious family of nobles, its most notable members (as seen in-game) being two brothers; Diallos, the Younger Brother and Juno the Older Brother. It is implied that the house is based outside the Lands Between.

Their uniforms are distinguished by its black cloth, decorated with red embellishments and garish silver armor, the apparel being passed down through the generations of the family. The head of the family is distinguished by their twin-tailed silver helm decorated with flowery adornments.

__TOC__

The house follows the rare tradition of ultimogeniture, where the right of succession belongs to the youngest child. However due to Diallos, the last-born's inability to commit to action, Juno, the first-born was allowed to inherit the Hoslow legacy in his stead. A decision that was met with little resistance.

sections.heading: The Hoslow proverb
sections.text:
- *"The tale of House Hoslow is told in blood."*
While it is unknown who was the first member to utter the phrase, it was certainly not Diallos, as it is always written in quotation-marks within the game's subtitles whenever he utters it.
  - Diallos frequently interprets this proverb grimly, as the tale of the Hoslow family being defined by the spilt of blood from friends and foes alike. A tale of tragedy and revenge.
  - Judging from Diallos's admiration of Juno and his desire to emulate his older brother. It is possible the proverb was first spoken by Juno himself. However, considering Juno's adoration of his gentle, younger brother, along with his low opinion of himself and his blood-stained path. It is possible that to him the blood referenced in the proverb is the blood running within their own veins. That indeed, the tale of House Hoslow is a tale of family.

sections.heading: Etymology
sections.text:
- The name "Juno" may have roots in the Roman word "uno" meaning the number "one", while "Diallos" may be based on "duo" meaning the number "two", likely referencing their order of birth.
- "Juno" may also be a reference to the Roman goddess of love, Juno. Which would befit his affection for his younger brother.
- It is also notable that the name "Diallos" may be based on "ja-loh" a word with origins in the African language Fula, meaning "bold", while "Juno" may come from the French word "jeune", meaning "young". Which would be ironic, as by this logic their names would be referring to the opposite brother instead of themselves.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Marais** are a house of magisterial officials in Elden Ring. They are based by the northern cliffs of Altus Plateau and serve as castellans of the Shaded Castle, as well as being a major local operator of grim, unsavory tasks such as surveillance and execution. Indeed, they perform some of the darkest duties that drive the wheels of mankind. The most famous relic of the House of Marais is their legendary executioner sword, which has beheaded countless sinners.
__TOC__
The only image of the first representative of this house remains in the form of a mask of a young nobleman with long white hair, which is worn by all heads of the house. The heads of the house also wear a robe with a black cape on their shoulders, their family crest emblazoned on their chest.

While it has not prevented them from performing their executions, the sons of House Marais are all sickly born. Many protecting their fragile skin beneath layers upon layers of bloodsoaked bandages along with a variety of masks obscuring their festering faces beneath.

The current head of the family is Maleigh Marais who had become besotted by Malenia the Severed. So much so that he would hang up a large portrait of her in the castle's great hall, as well as develop a collection of prostheses akin to what Malenia herself uses.

One day, Elemer, the assassin of merchants and teachers alike, was brought to the Shaded Castle for execution. He was supposed to be beheaded with the family sword, however, Elemer stole the sword from the site of his looming execution, furnished it with battle skills from his homeland and laid siege to the castle. Now Elemer has taken up residence at the Castellan's Hall, and while Maleigh managed to escape the stronghold alive, he now spends most of his time wallowing in a graveyard of broken statues west of his childhood home.

Some argue that all the misfortunes of House Marais are just punishments for its veneration of Malenia, whom Maleigh in particular idolized. However, it shouldn't be much of a surprise that a child from family with a history of lifelong disease could become so captivated, when the figure of obsession would be a fierce and beautiful goddess, who despite having been rotting alive since birth, managed to persevere.

sections.text: - Maleigh Marais, Shaded Castle Castellan

sections.text:
- It's possible that the family's history of sickness from birth stems from their close proximity to toxic substances, as their castle itself is literally sinking into a poison swamp.
- It's possible that Chief Guardian Arghanthy is a member of House Marais, as he wears everything that Maleigh wears with the exception of a different mask.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Jagged Peak** is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree. Collecting Map: Southern Shore will reveal the Jagged Peak on the Shadow Realm map.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Dominating the eastern Southern Shore, the Jagged Peak is a towering mountain visible from many elevated points in the Realm of Shadow. At its base, the  Grand Altar of Dragon Communion is tended by an ancient Dragon Communion Priestess, who reveals the occult history and purpose of Dragon Communion. The mountain is populated by powerful dragons and drakes, as well as the lifeless remnants of drake warriors scattered along the perilous ascent. The weather grows violent near the peak, with red lightning striking the treacherous slopes and jagged stones. At the summit awaits Bayle the Dread, an indominable dragon whose burning enmity toward the Dragonlord is legendary.

sections.heading: Access
sections.text:
To reach the Jagged Peak:
1. Start at the  Castle Front Site of Grace near Castle Ensis and proceed south to the Dragon's Pit.
1. Defeat the Ancient Dragon-Man and exit through  Dragon's Pit Terminus to the Foot of the Jagged Peak.
1. At the clearing where a Jagged Peak Drake sleeps, take the northern trail beneath a molten rock archway.
1. Follow the mountain path looping partially around the Finger Ruins of Rhia and use the Spiritspring to ascend to the bridge.
1. Cross the bridge near the  Foot of the Jagged Peak Site of Grace, where embers dance on the strong winds.
1. Climb the steep ramp, passing Igon and the dueling Jagged Peak Drakes, to reach the summit of the Jagged Peak.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Igon** is an NPC character in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Igon was once a poor scavenger of battlefields but found honor in the ancient art of Dragon Communion, whereby hunters of dragons could consume their hearts to gain their strength.

Igon soon became a fearless drake warrior and set his eyes on the greatest prey of all: Bayle the Dread, progenitor of the drakes, and the very reason that Dragon Communion had been created. Driven by bottomless hunger and fiery ambition, Igon journeyed to Bayle's roost at the top of the Jagged Peak to challenge the dragon. However, Igon found himself outmatched. Bayle shattered both Igon's body and mind, leaving him broken and terrified.

Despite this, Igon willed himself to climb back towards the Jagged Peak. Here he encountered a Tarnished champion also hunting for Bayle. Igon begged the Tarnished to summon his soul when facing Bayle so that he might have his revenge. Together, the two drake warriors slay Bayle, allowing Igon to die in peace.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.text:
1. Gravesite Plain
  - Find Igon by following his screams; he is on the floor near the  Pillar Path Waypoint Site of Grace outside the Dragon's Pit. Talk to him until you exhaust his dialogue.
1. Foot of the Jagged Peak
  - After climbing the Jagged Peak and defeating the Jagged Peak Drake he starts screaming again, he is in the middle of the road that advances to the next area. Exhaust his dialogue until he gives you Igon's Furled Finger and asks you to summon him.
1. Jagged Peak
  - After Bayle the Dread appears in his arena, Igon can be summoned to fight him. His summon sign is right in front of the fog wall (on your very first fight against Bayle, the summon sign won't appear until the boss spawns).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Igon is missing his left leg. This is the reason he can't walk.
  - Both Igon's legs are functional when his soul is summoned against Bayle the Dread.
- Dragon Communion Harpoons may be purchased for  1,000 runes each from the Twin Maiden Husks after donating Igon's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Igon is a reference to Captain Ahab, who hunted the great white whale Moby Dick in the novel of the same name: both lose their leg in the process and use it as motivation to continue, both use harpoons as weapons against their respective quarry, and both are utterly and insanely dedicated to their hunt.
  - Igon is referred to in some internal files as "Dragon Communion Ahab" showing that this was an intentional comparison.
  - Another, perhaps intentional or perhaps not, link between the two is that "Bayle" and "whale" rhyme.
- Igon's character model is the only one that is missing a leg.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Hornsent** (角人, *Tsunobito*, lit. "Horned People") are a faction in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Hornsent were a polytheistic, deeply ascetic people who associated the spiral, the Crucible, and their tangled horns with the divine. They have lived in Belurat and the Land of the Tower since times of old, and constructed the spiral tower, Enir-Ilim.

The Hornsent held a great knowledge about multiple Outer Gods and seemingly integrated different divine powers into their culture. They were aware of the Formless Mother and Shadow Undead at the Abandoned Ailing Village cast Swarm of Flies, an incantation associated with the Formless Mother. They used Rot for purification rituals through Romina, Saint of the Bud and kept Gravebirds inside Belurat and Enir-Ilim, golems crafted as kindreds to the Deathbirds. They were also aware of the Fell God of fire that was part of their legends.
The hornsent butchered undesirables and stuffed them into jars. They conducted a divine ritual to rebirth the jar contents as better people.

sections.heading: Downfall
sections.text: Queen Marika betrayed hornsent.. Their tower and its Divine Gate was sealed by shadow and their lands hidden in the Realm of Shadow. The hornsent were later attacked by forces of the Erdtree led by Messmer, son of Marika. His flame burned their armies and settlements. Those who survived bore a deep grudge or swore vengeance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Knight's Lightning Spear** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Loot:** Scorpion River Catacombs
- After arriving in the room with a spiked falling roof, keep to the right to find a ladder in one of the small safe spots around the corner (in the second half of the room) and climb up it. Cross the bridge to the right and then, after waiting for the Death Blight build-up to subside, use a thin ledge to the left to cross to the side with the Death Blight inflicting statue to find a short tunnel with the Incantation at the end, guarded by two Imps wielding Greatswords.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Creates a spear of Lightning to hurl, with Attack Power equal to 138% of Incantation Scaling, accompanied by four sigils that create additional follow-up spear to hit twice with Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling per hit.

Charging the spell creates two more sigils that each launch a new spear, and increases the first spear's Attack Power to 164% of Incantation Scaling, though there's still only two hits total from the follow-up spears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Though the initial Attack Power is boosted by 19% (37% with the talisman above) when charged, the additional spears do not do any extra Attack Power (though the two actual damaging hits do gain a 15% Attack Power boost with the talisman), making the overall boost 11% (28% with the talisman) when charged.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- Deals 27 Stance damage if it's charged and all projectiles hit, about on par with a Straight Sword's charged heavy attack but at range, making it very strong at opening enemies for Critical Attacks.
  - A full uncharged hit deals 15 Stance damage.
- Enemies will not react to the casting of either the charged or uncharged version. This is unlike Lightning Spear, where only the uncharged version is not noticed by enemies.
- The sigils will always launch additional spears if created, even if the caster is interrupted before they can throw the first spear.
- Slightly stronger than Lightning Spear when it comes to the FP-to-damage ratio and deals considerably more damage per hit, but the uncharged version takes 0.3 seconds, or 55% more time, to cast.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
  - Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Knight's Lightning Spear was charged or not.
  - This effect can be triggered up to 2 times per cast, once from the initial spear and then a second time from the follow-up spears hitting.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This spell is used by the Death Knights.
- Patch 1.13 PvP-only adjustments: increased attack power of the initial lightning spear, decreased attack power of the spears launched after the first one, decreased Poise damage of all spears generated by this spell.
  - This increased the Attack Power of the first spear by 40% and decreased the Attack Power of the follow-up spears by 20% against other players, increasing overall Attack Power by 2% in PvP.
  - The patch actually increased damage to Poise done by this spell, doubling it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Heal from Afar** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

**Loot:** Scadu Altus
- North of Moorth Ruins there are two small bodies of water. At the northern edge of the southern body of water is a small cave tunnel with a Miranda Blossom and three Perfumers, with the incantation lying under a glowing tree at the end.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Throws out a golden orb that detonates on impact with a surface or character.

If the caster is caught in the blast, they are healed for 420% of their Seal's Faith-based Incantation Scaling, while any allies affected are healed for 336% of the Faith-based Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Effectively heals the user as much as Lord's Heal while costing 10 less FP, healing allies for 60% more, and having far greater range.
  - Heals roughly as much HP per FP as Erdtree Heal.
- Like all Incantations that can heal others, if this spell hits a Revenant or Revenant Follower, they will take damage equal to 300 + 50% of their maximum HP, and their Stance will break immediately.
  - Unlike all other incantations that can do this, Heal from Afar has far greater range and thus can be used for this purpose much more safely (other healing incantations require the user to stand almost adjacent to the Revenant for this to work).
- Since it also detonates on impact with an object, aiming it into the ground or a nearby wall makes it usable as a personal heal.
  - Combined with either high Dexterity or moderate Dexterity and Radagon Icon, it can be easily used for self-healing mid-combat.
- Has a fairly large area of effect that makes firing it into a large foe such as a boss a good method for healing Cooperators or Spirit Ashes.
- Can't be cast when riding Torrent, unlike most healing spells.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Though the description calls this an Erdtree Incantation, the sigil created on the ground when casting (two rings, one smaller and one larger, with script-like decorations on them) is that of a Two Fingers Incantation.
  - This has no mechanical effect as neither Incantation category has their spells strengthened by wielding a specific Sacred Seal.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Helphen**, also known as the **lampwood**, is an unseen location mentioned in Elden Ring, believed to be a great tree in another world.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The legendary lampwood tree was the  source of the **lamplight** that beckoned the dead of the spirit world. Just as the Grace of Gold guided the Tarnished to the Erdtree, the Helphen's rays of light appeared only to those slain in battle, ushering them toward its black steeple. It was connected to the Deathbirds' cold-burning ghostflame and the Tibia Mariners, who led Those Lost in Death from spectral vessels.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The Helphen's Steeple renders the lampwood as a black  tree with needles and excurrent, tapered branches. A prominent crimson gem inlaid at the apex of the black steeple design implies the Helphen's sap and lamplight are red in appearance. Lamplight is presumed to shine in the eyes of those it graces.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Most information about the Helphen is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.
- The game uses present-tense to describe the Helphen, implying it is still operational.
- Its name suggests a connection to the great tree stump at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.
- The Tibia Mariners, also psychopomps, likely produce lamplight when they emit red light from a sacred seal held in their left palm, conferring glowing red light to the eyes nearby Those Who Live in Death, who once fell in battle.
- The discordant red lights seen in the Forbidden Lands are speculated to be rays of lamplight.
- The Shadow Keep, Church District may have a connection to the Helphen due to the presence of Tibia Mariner boats and the appearance of its many spires. Two Scorched Tree Spirits in the flooded courtyard protect an unusual tree whose branches appear to grow downward like roots. This area contains the only path to the Scadutree Base.
- Usher of Death, Rosus fulfills a similar role by lighting the path to catacombs.
- While coniferous trees are found throughout the Lands Between, spirit conifers only appear on the Mountaintops of the Giants.
- The Spirit Shelter, known in the Japanese script as the 霊樹 (*Reiju*, lit. Spirit Tree) is another tree with a strong connection to spirits. It is possible that the Helphen's black steeple served a similar purpose to the Divine Tower which supports the Spirit Shelter; an artificial structure for their respective spirit trees to grow around.

sections.text: **Jar Innards**, also known as **Jar Dwellers**, **Jar Saints**, and **Shamans**, are Enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The jar innards were once undesirables ritualistically butchered and sealed within greatjars by the hornsent. They were stored deep underground in gaols where Greater Potentates prayed for their rebirth into sainthood. The innards were emulsified by the tortured flesh of shaman maidens, which was prized for its affinity for melding with that of others.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The jar innards are massive balls of pinkish-red meat inside great jars. The tormented spirits of the dead are bound to the meat, and can be seen struggling to break free on some individuals. The innards appear as a large tumor erupting from the backside of a trembling shaman maiden. She has silver hair and is blinded. A divine symbol is carved into her forehead and she is in dire agony.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- There are varieties of jar innards.
- Frozen Maggots develop inside the flesh of great jars.
- The jar lids have a Crucible Knot seal.
- The jars will jump and shatter, revealing the meat innards.
- Their grab attack can be broken out of within 1.5 seconds with enough button-mashing, making it possible to avoid the damage that otherwise would have followed in its entirety
- The Jar Innards are a blending of life, not unlike the Crucible.
- Unlike Living Jars, Jar Innards do not merge with the jar.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Heolstor the Nightlord** (夜の王、ナメレス, *Yoru no Ō, Nameresu*, lit. Lord of Night, Nameless) also known as the **Night Aspect** (夜を象る者, *Yoru o Katadorumono*), the **Primordial Nightlord** (原初の夜の王, *Gensho no Yoru no Ō*), and **The Shape of Night** (夜の輪郭, *Yoru no Rinkaku*), is the primary antagonist and final boss of Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
This Nightlord has two primary phases of its fight. The initial phase is against **The Shape of Night**. A thick black miasma escapes from its body when it is slain. The Nightfarers are transported to another space to fight **Heolstor the Nightlord**. Defeating the second phase triggers a special event during certain quests.

Heolstor holds a unique Moonlight Sword that wields the power of Night. He is a patchwork of champions, but his original self's undying hatred for all things is what drives him, nothing else.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
According to its Relic, Heolstor was once a man and a knight who was beaten by some nameless hero, along with countless other warriors. The country they fought for was destroyed, and they were left in a massive mound of corpses. He was the only one whose willpower allowed him to cheat death and rise from the pile, only to curse the world forever.

The Night Lord became the ruler of the Lands Between after the Shattering. It wields the power to summon monsters and champions from other worlds, and is responsible for the Night's Tide. The Nightfarers of the Roundtable Hold work together to overthrow the Nightlord and save Limveld. Its realm is accessible by entering a petrified tree in the Spirit Shelter at the end of the second day.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Damage Types
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (  ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
Heolstor can be fought on the Third day or the Final Day during the Night Aspect expedition. Like all the other Nightlords, its boss fight can be accessed through the Spirit Shelter.

Its arena is the same as with all Nightlords.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text:

- Stance: **130**
- It is vulnerable to Critical Attacks after it is Parried or its Stance is broken.
- Multiplayer is enabled.

sections.heading: Stats

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Night Aspect Expedition.
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- This boss has Parriable attacks.
- This boss is vulnerable to Holy damage, with which it gets crippled and debuffed by in both phases.
- Heolstor cleaves open rifts in the sky to draw power from other realms. Each rift reveals the skybox of a different Nightlord's arena and grants a corresponding elemental Affinity.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **Nameless**.
- The identity of the Nightlord was leaked early when the Nightreign Achievements were published.
- The Nightlord may be connected to the Lord of Night awaited by the Nox of the Eternal Cities.
  - The Wylder can be reborn into a new Nightlord using a Silver Tear.
- He wields what appears to be the next iteration of Fromsoftware's iconic Moonlight Greatsword. Lore clues indicate that this was his original sword, and is not a Carian blade like other Moonlight Swords in Elden Ring's lore, as it does not channel the freezing power of the Moon. It instead channels the abyssal power of Heolstor's Night.
- Heolstor's story shares some similarities with that of the Revenger of Castle Morne, slayed by Godfrey.
  - They both lost their life to a "hero".
  - It said that "[...] from the sky poured down a great rain", matching the constant rain of the castle's location, Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
- His Japanese name, ナメレス or *Nameresu* (pronounced nah-may-ray-su) is a somewhat unusual transcription of the word Nameless, which would normally be written ネームレス or *Nēmuresu*; seemingly prioritizing similarity between a romaji transcription of the name to the English word over phonetic matching.
- The word Heolstor is Old English for "darkness, veil".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Knights of the Cuckoo** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Knights of the Cuckoo are a mercenary group loyal to the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Though they could not cast Sorceries, they threw Glintstone Scrap as an alternative. They chose the Cuckoo as their emblem, and presumably fought alongside Marionette Soldiers and Carian Knights against Radagon's golden armies during the Liurnian Wars.

After Radagon left Rennala to become Elden Lord, the heartbroken Queen of the Full Moon was left indisposed, leading the Carian Knights to fall into disarray and her influence inside the Academy to decrease. At some point the Academy, through the Cuckoo Knights, would seize this opportunity to rebel against the Carian royal family, triggering a Liurnian civil war. They trapped Bols, Carian Knight in the Cuckoo's Evergaol, and razed Kingsrealm Ruins before marching upon Caria Manor. However, the grounds were protected by a potent magic trap. Many of the Cuckoo Knights that survived the Siege of Caria Manor were captured, becoming Pidia's puppets.

Although they failed to claim the manor, Lunar Princess Ranni abdicated her claim to Caria, the Academy, and Liurnia of the Lakes. The Knights of the Cuckoo remained active throughout the reign of Radagon and the later Shattering as the armed wing of the Academy. They maintain key checkpoints through the region even in the present day, particularly in the Academy Gate Town and before the Grand Lift of Dectus leading to Altus.

sections.text: They wear red and blue surcoats depicting twin cuckoo birds gazing into a mass of glintstone.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Queen Rennala's nascent, fleeting children studied the many books of the Raya Lucaria Grand Library, born and reborn by her beloved amber egg. Each frail, imperfect, and unable to stand, Juvenile Scholars grew dependent on their heartbroken mother's forbidden rite for endless reincarnation. On Rennala's command, they ascended in beams of light and entered a dreamlike trance, becoming spiritgraves as they rose to the cradles suspended from the ceiling, where they reawakened with faded memories.

They had innate spellcasting abilities and access to unique magic. A variation of Gravity Sorcery, Juvenile Scholars effortlessly moved distant objects by manifesting flame-like purple starlight in their raised palms. By singing a lullaby, their adoring voices conjured the golden, moon-like bubble that shielded their dissociative mother from harm.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
A tall girl with a soft and pale complexion, the Juvenile Scholar is a youthful, crawling clone of Queen Rennala. She wears a white undershirt and a red or blue tunic with puffed sleeves beneath a deep blue, floor-length mantle lined with yellow trim and white cords. A structured, round cap with soft pleating and a decorative medallion rests atop her cropped black hair. Her collar matches the cross-hatch pattern of her mother's crescent crown.

Her gravestone portrays a half-length figure framed by fluted columns, their arms folded across their chest, identity veiled by a curtain-like shroud. Adorned with flowers, the Briars of Sin obscure their eyes.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.text:
- There are three Juvenile Scholar variants, each with a different singing voice.
- **Candlestick**: A Juvenile Scholar in a short cap and robes with red trim. They carry a lit candlestick, which they blow into to produce flames that deal  Fire damage.
- **Quill**: A Juvenile Scholar in a short cap and robes with red trim, carrying a feather quill.
- **Tall Cap**: A distinguished Juvenile Scholar in a tall cap and robes with blue trim, carrying a feather quill. Her voice has the highest pitch.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: The Juvenile Scholars do not drop any items or runes upon death.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: The Juvenile Scholars are encountered only in the Raya Lucaria Grand Library of the Academy of Raya Lucaria during the first phase of the Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon boss fight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Some variants wear the Juvenile Scholar Cap and Juvenile Scholar Robe.
- Their song becomes desynchronized and discordant when Rennala's golden moon shatters. Some scholars respond by giggling.
- The Juvenile Scholars are born without the ability to walk, similar to Elder Albinaurics, Albinauric Archers, Commander Gaius, Giant Skeletons, and the Putrescent Knight.
- Complete the "Resurrection" Painting puzzle to acquire the red Juvenile Scholar Set. The Painter Spirit solution is found in the cemetery behind Caria Manor, near the Royal Grave Evergaol.
  - This context reaffirms the Juvenile Scholars' connection to the Carian royal family.
  - A troop of Young Albinaurics patrol the graveyard.
- When considering Rennala's dialogue and the Academy's choice to lock her in the Grand Library, the Juvenile Scholars may be transformed Glintstone Sorcerers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **RenalaChildren** (ID: 2040)
- Juvenile Scholars share animations with Rot Larva. Both enemies undergo a cycle of rebirth.
- A number of voiced dialogue lines were cut, including male voices.
- The Juvenile Scholars' candlesticks, quills, tall caps, and blue robes are unplayable.

The Hinterland is a lush and fertile eastern section of the Scaduview. Multicolored flowers grow in abundance here, untouched by Messmerfire. The deserted Shaman Village found here was once the home of Queen Marika the Eternal.

This secret area is accessible after solving the puzzle at the  Shadow Keep, Back Gate. Obtain the O Mother gesture from the headless statue north of the Bonny Village and perform it in front of the statue of Marika.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: ***Irina's Necklace***, officially **Rya's Necklace (#8130)** and **Azure Insignia**, is a Key Item that was cut from Elden Ring by .

sections.heading: Use
sections.text:
- The intended functional purpose of *Irina's Necklace* in the  is unknown. Given its item description and the woman's resemblance to Irina of Morne, the locket almost certainly portrays her mother, Castellan Edgar's wife.  Like Irina's Letter, *Irina's Necklace* may have been delivered to Edgar at Castle Morne, or Edgar the Revenger at the Revenger's Shack—provided he was somehow spared—though no such quest stages exist. The item most likely had no purpose once received.
- In , this item was **Azure Insignia**, and may have been connected to the Red Insignia that was replaced with the Volcano Manor Invitation in subsequent patches.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: *Irina's Necklace* is an **unobtainable** item; however, Lightseeker Hyetta would have given this item to the player at the Bellum Church after receiving the Fingerprint Grape.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The inclusion of *Irina's Necklace* would have given extra insight into Irina's transition to Hyetta, as Hyetta states she has searched for its owner for a long time.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The quest stage for *Irina's Necklace* was active during the , though it was disabled by the  release. Although it was unobtainable, this item was retitled "Azure Insignia" in *Elden Ring* version 1.00, but its description remained the same. It was renamed "Rya's Necklace" in subsequent builds of the game.
- *Irina's Necklace* and Irina's Letter are key items #8130 and #8131, respectively. Their records are sandwiched between items related to Volcano Manor and Rya the Scout; Rya's Necklace is key item #8136.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Highlanders** are an unseen faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The highlanders were a clan of simple warriors who revered the raw strength of savage beasts. They lived in the highlands, but wore white cloths tied to their headbands to symbolize their original lands. These brave warriors carried axes that amplified their roars in battle, and initiated combat by crying out their names. They wore leathers and animal pelts, and were reknowned bear-hunters—especially of Great Red Bears. Those who triumphed over such creatures earned the right to wear red-patterned cloth over their traditional blue garb. These elites could command a wild power unique to themself through divine invocation.

The highland warriors were fiercely loyal to their chieftain, Hoarah Loux—the unadorned, primal identity of Lord Godfrey. During the age of the Erdtree, they fought alongside the Lord of the Battlefield against Queen Marika's many enemies. When he was stripped of grace and exiled, they, too, became Tarnished. They followed him on the Long March and waged war in the Badlands outside the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Members
sections.text:
- Hoarah Loux, Warrior
- Logur, the Beast Claw
- Magnus the Beast Claw
- Red Bear

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Axe Talisman which depicts a Highlander is looted from a chest in a cellar at the Mistwood Ruins. The passage is blocked by a sleeping Runebear. A nearby Candletree leads to this area. Many Bears and Runebears, and their Golden Dung, are found along the path.
- Red Bear left the Redmanes in pursuit of the untamed strength of bears, adopting the cultural practices of highland warriors.
- Hoarah Loux, Warrior, the champion who became Lord Godfrey, was a Highlander.
  - The Highland Axe is found below his painting at Stormveil Castle.
  - The Axe Talisman depicts one of Godfrey's loyal followers wearing the Leather Crown and carrying a Highland Axe.
  - Godfrey reverts to Hoarah Loux after slaying a beast with his bare hands and drenching himself—and his blue armor—in red Beast Blood.
  - Hoarah Loux initiates combat by yelling his name.
  - Hoarah Loux's roar attack uses Runebear sound and visual effects.
  - Ralva the Great Red Bear and Rugalea the Great Red Bear use Ash of War: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker.
  - The Elden Lord Set is similar to the Highlander Set.
  - The Champion Pauldron worn by Nepheli Loux, Warrior features a strip of red fabric. Hoarah Loux wears this outfit in his slide in the intro cinematic.
- Kaiden Sellswords are likely an offshoot of the Highlanders.
  - The Kaiden Helm is a metal version of the Leather Crown.
  - The Leather Headband hints at the fact that the original land of the Highlanders could be the Consecrated Snowfield.
  - The mercenaries also start battle by shouting, though it is the name of their unseen settlement, Kaiden, in the northern mountaintops.
  - They were presumably hired by Godrick the Grafted, who idolized Godfrey.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The internal name for Kaiden Sellswords is **WarKingWarrior**, further aligning them with Hoarah Loux and the Highlanders.
- This faction was initially cut from *Elden Ring*.
  - Brave's Battlewear (the cut version of the Gloried Attire) was explicitly linked to Hoarah Loux. The red cloth represented participation in the Long March rather than conquering a bear. The highlands were referred to as the "frigid uplands."
  - Brave's Set: Brave's Battlewear, Brave's Battlewear (Altered), Brave's Bracer, Brave's Cord Circlet, Brave's Leather Helm, Brave's Legwraps

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Horns are an aspect of the Crucible and were once seen as the mark of divinity. Creatures suffused with the Crucible's energy sprout new horns, including the Omen, Misbegotten, Divine Beast Dancing Lions, Elder Lions and Great Red Bears.

sections.heading: Budding Horns
sections.text:
]]

Budding Horns are horns that continuously grow new protrusions, eventually branching out like antlers. These grow on herbivorous beasts that typically bear no horns. The Ancestral Followers use budding horns in their worship of Ancestor Spirits, from whose antler-like horns new life continues to sprout long after death.

sections.heading: Curled Horns
sections.text:
]]

Curled horns grow in a coiled, spiral pattern, though they may be synonymous with spiralhorns. The Furnace Golems used by Messmer's Army during the crusade depicted the fell god of fire as a stone face surrounded by eight curled horns and sixteen tanglehorns. This horned visage is required component of the furnace hex.

sections.heading: Spiral Horns
sections.text:
]]

Spiralhorns grow in a swirling, eddy-like pattern. The spiral is a sacred symbol of the Crucible. The hornsent dipped spiral horns in gold and silver and traded them as currencies. The Ancestral Followers gifted a Spiralhorn Shield to a Tarnished who learned their customs. Due to visual similarities, spiral horns may be synonymous with curled horns.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Iron Menial** is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Iron Menial aids the Nightfarers of the Shrouded Roundtable Hold. This puppet was once a Marionette Soldier, but was reprogrammed to be a helpful manservant. He is keen, inquisitive, and posseses considerable knowledge of the Lands Between. He is dedicated to restoring the Nightfarers' memories, and drives many of the Remembrance Quests.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Iron Menial is found in the Roundtable Hold, though his exact whereabouts shift between each Expedition. You may find him in the east hallway, by the fireplace in the waiting room, or near the Roundtable. His location may differ based on the active Remembrance Quest.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This NPC cannot be made hostile or killed.
- He does not trust the Recluse at first.
- The Iron Menial later exhibits strange behaviors during the Recluse's Remembrance questline. This reclusive menial is revealed to be the Witch of the Wheel, an imposter who locked the true puppet in the Crypt.
  - While unconscious, the Iron Menial dreamed of an encounter with an aspect of the Nightlord, from whom he received the essence of an outer god. When he awakens, he discovers the Bone-Like Stone on the crypt floor. He bestows it to the Recluse, insisting she decide how to use it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ictarus** is an unseen object mentioned in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Ictarus was initially created by the Recluse as a means to quell storms and save lives. However, it was twisted into a cursed weapon, capable of inflicting wounds that can never heal. A kingdom used the vicious weapon in the far west to clip the wings of the Pinionfolk.

The magic that powered Ictarus was anchored in the Witch's Brooch, which the Recluse entrusted to the Guardian after he uncovered her role in the plight of his people.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The name is likely a reference to , a character from Greek mythology known for losing his wings.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Journal** is an object in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The lost memories of the Nightfarers are recorded in the Journal at the Roundtable Hold. The first chapters for each hero are unlocked by default, and additional ones are available after defeating Nightlords or completing specific personal objectives.

Specific chapters contain Remembrance Quests, which allow them to "relive" events of the past in the Realm of Remembrance. These quests are managed and tracked in the Journal. Completing a Remembrance unlocks new chapters. Remembrance quests can be postponed at any time by changing characters or by selecting **Postpone remembrance** on the appropriate page in the Journal.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **horned giants** are characters in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The horned giants bore haloed crowns of tangled horns, an aspect of the primordial Crucible that originated in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The presence of such horns was regarded as a mark of divinity and an irrefutable sign of primacy. Hornsent scholars who studied the ancient ruins collected and archived the giants' remains at the Shadow Keep's Specimen Storehouse.

After Queen Marika's rise to power and the end of the Age of Plenty, however, aspects of the Crucible and horns on humans were deemed impurities. During the Crusade, Fire Knights Hilde and Salza refused to burn down the ruins, urging instead for the preservation of the horned specimens, even at the risk of their own lives. They succeeded in convincing Messmer, ensuring the specimens survived the cleansing fire. Messmer's Army continued this work, safeguarding both the Storehouse and its mission.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The "Horned Giant" name is conjectural.
- They are most likely the remains of the ancient inhabitants of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.Alternatively they could be ancient tutelary deities of the hornsent, or may have inspired the practice in hornsent culture.
- According to the hornsent, the "mother of all Crucibles" grew on the giants of Rauh in ancient times.
- They are strung up in a rigid crucifixion pose, similar to Queen Marika and the Prince of Death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Horned Giant are similar in stature to the giant mummies seated in the Chair-Crypts.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Knights are distinguished by affiliation, rank, equipment, and social status. They can be broadly described as well-equipped, high-ranking warriors, in service to a lord or faction. Many knights devote themselves and swear allegiance, but some fulfill obligations only on a contractual basis.

They wear extensive armor that covers the entirety or majority of their bodies. They wield various melee armaments and bows, and some can use skills, spells, tools, and steeds. Many can perform guard counters using shields. Most of their equipment is wrought from metal.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The  is the name given to the setting of Elden Ring. It is a vast realm formerly ruled by Queen Marika the Eternal.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Lands Between is an insular landmass featuring diverse biomes, including lush southern grasslands, a temperate central region, and a frozen, mountainous north. The Erdtree dominates the skyline, its golden presence visible across most of the realm. Two great underground rivers and an enormous root system span the continent's length.

sections.heading: Regions
sections.text:
The Lands Between consists of several contrasting regions, each with its own distinct environments. They are:

- Limgrave: Verdant plains, misty forests, and Stormveil Castle.
- Liurnia: A scholarly hub dominated by the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
- Caelid: War-ravaged lands plagued by the scarlet rot.
- Altus Plateau: The golden land of Leyndell, graced by the Erdtree's presence.
- Mountaintops of the Giants: A frigid and forbidden region tied to ancient Fire Giants.
- Siofra River: A starry, underground realm of the Nox and Ancestral Followers.
- Ainsel River: A series of underground tunnels leading to the vast and putrid Lake of Rot.
- Deeproot Depths: The burial ground of an Eternal City and Godwyn, the Prince of Death.
- Realm of Shadow Shadow of the Erdtree: The land of the Scadutree, hidden by Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
It is said that long ago, the Greater Will triggered a great rupture across the heavens, and the vitality of the stars rained down upon the Lands Between. The first star to arrive contained the daughter of the Greater Will: Metyr, Mother of Fingers. Later came a golden star bearing an Elden Beast, which later became the Elden Ring.

The Lands Between witnessed the rise and fall of many civilizations and their gods. In the prehistoric era, Dragonlord Placidusax served as the Elden Lord of the Ancient Dragons. During the Age of the Erdtree, Queen Marika, vessel of the Elden Ring, and her consort, the Elden Lord, ruled from Leyndell, Royal Capital, atop the Altus Plateau. Evidence of ancient cultures such as the Nox, Giants, Astrologers, Ancient Dynasty, and Hornsent remains scattered and buried throughout the realm.

The Lands Between was also home to the Primordial Crucible, where all life was once blended together. Under the guidance of the Two Fingers, Marika transformed the Crucible into the Erdtree during her rise to power. She later excised the heart of the Lands Between, creating a Realm of Shadow to conceal her secrets.

After Marika shattered the Elden Ring, the Lands Between became the site of The Shattering: a war between her Demigod offspring. Despite the power gained through their Great Runes, none of them succeeded in becoming Elden Lord. Grace was then extended to the Tarnished, who were called back to the Lands Between to seek the shards of the Elden Ring, so that one may become Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Nightreign
sections.text: Elden Ring Nightreign is set in a parallel timeline where the Shattering War had a different outcome, featuring Limveld, a volatile and ever-changing region.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Sections of the Lands Between have been displaced, buried, or sealed away over the ages.
- All manner of Death washes up on the Lands Between.
- The Suppressing Pillar stands at the center of the Lands Between.
- The various outer gods contest the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- George R. R. Martin invented the name "Lands Between" for the setting.
- The Lands Between were once referred to as "The Riftlands" through an unnamed character's monologue from a leaked internal trailer initially meant for European shareholders.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Malenia, Blade of Miquella**, later known as **Malenia, Goddess of Rot**, is an optional remembrance Boss in Elden Ring. She is a Demigod Shardbearer who is encountered in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A Demigod daughter of Queen Marika the Eternal and her second Elden Lord, King Consort Radagon, Malenia was born during the age of the Elden Ring. Like her elder twin brother, Miquella, a dreadful curse afflicted her from birth. The Scarlet Rot, an incurable, radiating sickness, ravaged Malenia, threatening to consume her from within. Although her condition eventually claimed her eyes and several limbs, the Two Fingers identified her as an Empyrean, a candidate to replace her mother as the god of a new age.

Miquella worked to undo the curses they had both inherited. While unable to find a cure for his sister within the Golden Order, Miquella designed a needle of unalloyed gold to keep the rot at bay. He also crafted the prostheses that enabled her to continue fighting. At some point, Malenia encountered the legendary blind swordsman of the Flowing Curved Sword, who had long ago sealed away an Outer God of Rot. The swordsman became her master, enabling her to gain wings of unparalleled strength. Malenia eventually became a peerless warrior and her brother's sworn blade and protector.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text:
]]
After the Elden Ring was shattered, Malenia claimed a shard of the fractured Elden Ring. She attracted loyal Cleanrot Knights, who vowed to fight next to her, despite the inevitable, gradual putrefaction of their flesh. During the Shattering, Malenia led an army that marched south from the Haligtree down the Bellum Highway. She won many battles against the other Demigods, even humbling fellow Shardbearer, Godrick the Grafted, who groveled at her feet for mercy after first insulting her and then suffering defeat.

sections.heading: Battle of Aeonia
sections.text:
Malenia and her half-brother Radahn would eventually be the last two demigods left standing in the conflict. Their forces clashed in the Caelid Wilds, and the two fought the Battle of Aeonia, a bitter duel to fulfill an unhonored vow. In the midst of the combat with Radahn, Malenia unleashes Scarlet Rot, resulting in her first Scarlet Aeonia.

The rot did not kill Radahn but robbed him of his wits, turning him feral. Malenia herself was left slumbering in a coma. She was rescued by one of her Cleanrot Knights, Finlay, who carried her across the Lands Between. When Malenia and Finlay took refuge at the Shaded Castle, Maleigh Marais, the sickly-born head of House Marais, was naturally drawn to the unconscious Demigod. He saw in her his personal goddess. Finlay carried Malenia back to the Haligtree, far north of the Erdtree.

The unleashed scarlet rot devastated Caelid, leaving it a rotting wasteland, and created the Swamp of Aeonia. Malenia inadvertently brought forth the Scarlet Butterflies and Kindred of Rot. The pests, including Sage Gowry, who worshipped her as a goddess and hoped to cause her to bloom once again, believing that she would usher in a new age of rot.  However, Malenia rejected her fate and never embraced the Servants of Rot.

Miquella had encased himself within the Haligtree in an effort to create a new Erdtree of his very own, hopefully granting him the power to cure both his and his sister’s curses. However, during Malenia's absence, Miquella was ripped from the womb of the tree and taken away by Mohg, Lord of Blood before he could emerge from his cocoon. Malenia dreamt while awaiting Miquella's return, and the scarlet rot seeped out from her and began infecting the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text: Malenia's slumber is eventually disturbed by a Tarnished, who found their way to the roots of the Haligtree. The two fight, and Malenia finally meets her match, but she suffers her first true defeat. However, in the end, Malenia succumbs to the Scarlet Rot and blossoms yet again, reborn as a nascent goddess. She unleashes her full fury against the invader, but falls short yet again, her dying words an apology to her vanished brother. Having bloomed twice, Malenia withdraws within her scarlet blossom.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
Malenia is fought at the end of Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, in a large chamber beyond the Haligtree Roots Site of Grace.

Her arena is an open cavern with a shallow pool of water at its center. There are no obstacles, so there is plenty of space to gain distance during some of Malenia's more devastating attacks.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text:
- HP: **33,251** (total)
- Defense: **123**
- Stance: **80**
- She must be parried three times to trigger a stance break, enabling a Critical Hit.
- Multiplayer is enabled
- Spirit Ashes are enabled
- She regains lost HP with every successful attack, even if they are blocked.
- She gains +10  Fire negation (0 → 10) and -10  Lightning negation (20 → 10) while standing in water.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- 480,000 runes
- Malenia's Great Rune
- Remembrance of the Rot Goddess

sections.heading: Phase 1 - Malenia, Blade of Miquella
sections.text:
- HP: **18,473**
- Deals  Standard,  Slash, and  Pierce damage
In phase 1, Malenia will primarily make use of melee attacks using her sword. Her quick attacks, combined with her HP regeneration on hit, mean that she can rapidly recover from any damage dealt. However, she staggers easily, and her attacks can be cancelled by attacking during her wind-up animations. Frostbite and Blood Loss are especially good for staggering her.

sections.heading: Phase 2 - Malenia, Goddess of Rot
sections.text:
- HP: **14,778**
- Deals  Standard,  Slash,  Pierce, and  Holy damage; and inflicts  Scarlet Rot buildup.
Once Malenia's health reaches 0, a transformation cutscene will play, wherein she embraces the rot, releasing a swarm of butterflies and initiating phase 2. **Malenia, Goddess of Rot** starts the second phase with 80% of her maximum health, but can recover it with her HP regeneration.

The phase always begins with a scripted Scarlet Aeonia attack, which can immediately end the fight if the player does not immediately get some distance. She flies on wings made from her hair and butterflies, and many of her regular attacks can now inflict  Scarlet Rot buildup. She gains a variety of rot-based attacks and can also create phantom projections of herself, which vanish after attacking. The most dangerous attack in her arsenal is her signature Waterfowl Dance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating this boss for the first time unlocks the Shardbearer Malenia achievement.
- The "Demigod Slain" flyout is displayed upon defeating Malenia, Goddess of Rot.
- Malenia has a prosthetic right arm, left leg, and right foot. These were added due to the infection of the scarlet rot. The rot has also visibly spread over her eyes, so she is presumably also blind. However, her disabilities do not handicap her battle prowess in the slightest.
- According to the Scarlet Aeonia Incantation description, Malenia will become a true Goddess if her scarlet flower blooms three times. She first used this spell during the Battle of Aeonia. Malenia blooms a second time during her duel against the Tarnished.
- Once defeated, she will leave behind a large, solid Scarlet Aeonia in her arena. If the player has the Unalloyed Gold Needle after completing Millicent's questline, it can be given to the Aeonia to receive Miquella's Needle and a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.
- Millicent and her four sisters are descended from Malenia in some way, but more as offshoots, or buds, of her Scarlet Bloom rather than actual daughters. Millicent seeks to return Malenia's sense of dignity.
  - They will be reborn as Malenia's Scarlet Valkyries if their deaths coincide with a great betrayal.
- Malenia and Miquella are together known as the "twin prodigies" (天賦の双子, *Tenpu no Futago*).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In , this character was also known as **Arbitress Malenia** and **Malenia, the Red Queen**.
- Malenia has unused dialogue.
- Malenia, Blade of Miquella delivered a different line upon killing the player in .
- Malenia has an alternative intro cutscene that was cut before release. Miquella was present in the tree, and Malenia calls the player her companion, indicating a cut third ending to Millicent's questline in which Malenia's pride is restored.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Mad Pumpkin Head** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Gigantic humanoids with brawny physiques, known for their distinct oval helmets. They are former gladiators, broken and driven mad. Their helmets are pitch black inside, intended to keep the warriors from panicking, and to alleviate feelings of pressure and claustrophobia.

They typically wield hammers with crude, stone heads, or spiky Chainlink Flails. Sometimes they can be seen carrying standards, which they will drive into the ground or throw at foes when initiating combat.

Their heads heavily reduce the damage of any attack that hits it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Margit the Fell Omen** is a boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Margit is an Omen who gained notoriety during The Shattering, in which he slaughtered countless champions who harbored ambitions for Lordship, stacking high their corpses during the Second Defense of Leyndell.

He is encountered by the Tarnished at the gates of Stormveil Castle, where he makes clear his disdain towards the Tarnished, and attempts to put an end to their quest for Lordship. Although he is defeated, Margit's voice is heard as he disappears.

Later, he appears once more outside Leyndell, Royal Capital, initially in the guise of a Commoner. After being defeated by the Tarnished once more, he vanishes, leaving the corpse of the commoner behind.

After the Tarnished has made their way through Leyndell and reached the Elden Throne, Margit stands between them and the Erdtree. He repudiates the other Demigods, calling them all traitors, before revealing himself to be Morgott, the Omen King, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage, who took up the responsibility of protecting the Erdtree, despite receiving no love in return. He fights the Tarnished once more and, upon his defeat, he warns them that the Erdtree will reject them, as it did him.

sections.heading: Encounters
sections.text:
- Limgrave | (Castleward Tunnel)

As the Tarnished approaches the gates of Stormveil Castle, Margit will materialize on a nearby tower and jump down the courtyard to confront his opponent. This encounter will not take place if Morgott, the Omen King is defeated beforehand.

- Altus Plateau | (Outer Wall Battleground)

As the Tarnished treks through the Capital Outskirts, Margit will possess the body of a nearby Commoner to once again hunt down his enemy. This encounter does not count as a boss fight, and it is possible to run away when he appears.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text: Sorcerer Rogier is available as a summon for this fight.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Margit is quick and relentless, his powerful combos and rapid follow-ups make it hard to find a window to punish him, but there are two types of attacks that leave him open amply: overhead strikes and ground stabs.

Since both can be easily evaded by running to the right, the key to victory is learning how to bait out these moves, which is generally done by dodging away from the first part of a combo, while remaining just in range for him to keep going through with it fully.

His jumping stab can also be exploited, as he always tells this move by tossing his holy dagger twice, while the player is far way: as he finishes throwing his weapons, walk towards him and dodge through the jump attack.

Without being particularly weak to anything, he still takes some additional damage from slashing and fire attacks, and he can also be poisoned and bled, which makes the Uchigatana a particularly favorable choice against this boss.

While standard light attacks won't impact him much, an aggressive playstyle made of jump attacks, charged attacks and Ash of War will see Margit repeatedly falling on his knees, leaving him open to a critical strike.

Margit's Shackle can be used during this phase to temporarily stun him, opening him to attacks. This will not work in phase 2.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
As his health drops to 60% or below, he will enter Phase 2 always executing the same hammer sweep plus jumping strike.

Even with the addition of some new moves, the bait-and-punish strategy of Phase 1 is still applicable.

While the moves made with his holy weapons cannot be parried, the majority of his regular weapon attacks are susceptible to interruption.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text:
Margit's arena is a narrow and long pathway with chasms on each side. While the boss himself cannot fall to his death, the player must constantly reposition himself to avoid having their back against the wall or the brink.

The area is also filled with obstacles and while the weapons scattered through out can be broken by dodging into them, the wooden barricades might just get in the way of a safety roll.

One must also not overestimate the length of the arena, as Margit's gap-closing attacks are fast and cover a long distance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Longsword** is a straight sword in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Starting armament of the Vagabond origin.
- Purchased from Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold for 1,000 Runes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
- Consistently the second strongest of all regular Straight Swords, outmatched only by the Broadsword, almost matching it on a Keen affinity and outclassing it on a Quality affinity.
  - This may be somewhat surprising since the Longsword's scaling values leans towards Strength more so than Dexterity, but it's primarily because the Broadsword scales rather less well on Keen.
  - Quality affinity requires high stats to use properly, making this somewhat difficult to exploit before New Game Plus/Journey 2 and later.
- While not quite to the level of the Short Sword's unique heavy attack chain, since the first heavy attack in a chain is a Pierce damage attack as well as the heavy variant of its default skill and as such can hit for heavy counter damage with the Spear Talisman.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Litany of Proper Death** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Sold by D, Hunter of the Dead for 2500 runes.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Causes the user to cross their arms before performing a T-like pose to unleash a medium-ranged wave of crossing lights on the ground with Holy Attack Power equal to 56% of Incantation Scaling.

Has a massive 900% Attack Power bonus against Those Who Live in Death, effectively making it have Holy Attack Power equal to 560% of Incantation Scaling against them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast.
- Attack Power is increased by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%.
- Deals low damage overall against non-weak enemies, with only the massive Attack Power bonus against undead making it deal enough damage to actually be somewhat usable.
- The damage vector is very groundbound and can be stopped by changes in elevation.
- Skeletons defeated by this spell are immediately killed and cannot resurrect themselves.
- The reach is somewhat hard to judge visually, with the clear golden sheen ending after about one-third to one-half of the range.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Magic Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  3,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Magic Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Magic damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  20 FP per cast.
- Costs  13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces magic damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *MagicFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
<math>TotalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {MagicDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {MagicFortification}) )</math>
  - For example, if magic damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
<math>TotalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
<math>TotalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%</math>

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as magic damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple magic negation sources.
- Magic Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
- This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Magic damage in the game, particularly against sorcerers, Deathbirds, and Glintstone Dragons, especially in regions like Liurnia of the Lakes.
- Magic Fortification offers greater magic protection than Spellproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Maliketh, the Black Blade** is a boss in Elden Ring, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is **not** an optional boss as Maliketh must be defeated to unlock Leyndell, Ashen Capital and reach the endgame of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Maliketh is the loyal Shadowbound Beast and half-brother of Queen Marika the Eternal, an Empyrean of Numen descent, who would become the vessel of the Elden Ring.

Maliketh fought and defeated the Gloam-Eyed Queen, the leader of the Godskin Apostles. On Marika's orders, Maliketh sealed away the Rune of Death, binding it within his blade, causing the true power of the god-slaying black flame to be lost.

When the Rune of Death was plucked from the Elden Ring, and confined, the Golden Order was created, with Queen Marika as its one true god. Marika's offspring were granted a form of immortality owing to the removal of their fated deaths from the Elden Ring, however there was not one Demigod who did not fear Maliketh and his blade imbued with death. He was a beast of such terrifying ferocity that his name came to mean "Death of the Demigods". He also led the Black Blade Kindred, living gargoyles who wielded weapons held together by blackened corpse wax.

During the Golden Age of the Erdtree, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen from Maliketh. The perpetrator was Ranni the Witch, who used it to forge godslaying black knives, which were wielded by the Black Knife Assassins during the assassination of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. Maliketh responded by binding his blade- and the Rune of Death sealed within- into his own flesh, to prevent death from ever being stolen again. Later, the Rune of Death sprouted from Godwyn's corpse and began to spread through the Lands Between in the form of Deathroot.  Maliketh, under the name Gurranq, resolved to track down and devour the Deathroot, eventually gaining an insatiable hunger for it.

Maliketh, now Gurranq, eventually came into contact with D, Hunter of the Dead. D entered Gurranq's service and assisted him in weeding Deathroot, the source of Those Who Live in Death. D would later find a Tarnished, who agreed to take his place in weeding Deathroot.

The Tarnished encounters Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum in Caelid. The beast, dressed in the robes of a clergyman, gives them an eye which trembles in the presence of Deathroot, and instructs them to bring him any Deathroot they find in return for bestial incantations. Despite consuming all the Deathroot the Tarnished could bring him, Gurranq is not sated. Despondent, he realises that he has done all he can for the land and departs, with his hunger as his only companion.

When the Tarnished arrives at the foot of the Erdtree, they find the entrance obstructed by thorns. To remove the thorns, the Tarnished and their companion, Melina, set the Erdtree ablaze at the Giant's Forge. After doing so, the Tarnished finds themselves in Crumbling Farum Azula, an ancient city in the sky, where they seek the Rune of Death. The Tarnished finally comes upon Gurranq, who attempts to stop them from stealing the Rune of Death from him. Despite his best efforts, Gurranq struggles to overcome the Tarnished. As a last resort, he unbinds his death-imbued blade from his flesh and reveals his true identity to the Tarnished. Nevertheless, Maliketh falls to the Tarnished, and with his dying breath cries out to Marika for forgiveness. The Rune of Death is unbound, and enshrouds the Lands Between. However, this allows the impenetrable thorns to finally burn away, allowing the Tarnished to finally gain access to the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Phase 1 - Beast Clergyman
sections.text: Phase 1 is much like combat against Gurranq. During this phase, the Beast Clergyman will make use of his Cinquedea as well as a variety of bestial incantations. His attacks are very fast, leaving few obvious spaces for the player to attack. He may use an earthquake attack, causing area of effect damage in a small circle around him.

sections.heading: Phase 2 - Maliketh, the Black Blade
sections.text:
At half health, a cutscene will play and phase 2 will begin. Maliketh now wields his Black Blade, and all of his attacks will cause rapid health loss overtime as well as temporary reduction of maximum health. Maliketh is a fast and acrobatic fighter, relying on quick slashes, spins and leaps. He will sometimes jump up and cling to the pillars around the arena, before either jumping at the player or jumping away and firing a ranged attack.

During this phase, the Blasphemous Claw can be used to deflect Maliketh's Black Blade attack, as well as the spin attack he performs after plunging his sword into the ground. Deflecting his attacks will stun him for a few seconds, creating a window during which to attack.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The arena is a wide, circular room. It is possible to fall off the edges all around the perimeter of the room. There are several pillars around the centre of the room, which Maliketh may jump onto to perform certain attacks. These pillars can also be used to create distance between oneself and Maliketh, or to avoid his ranged attacks.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **BlackSwordMariques**
- Maliketh's most powerful Destined Death attacks used purple visual effects in .

When the maltreated Misbegotten servants of Castle Morne overthrew their masters and seized the fortress, the Leonine Misbegotten sought to claim the Grafted Blade Greatsword at the Morne Moangrave. Castellan Edgar, commander of the castle, remained behind, sworn to prevent the storied blade from falling into Misbegotten hands: His Summon Sign appears beside the boss gate if he receives Irina's Letter.
