sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lichdragon Fortissax** is a boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Fortissax is an Ancient Dragon who was once known as the "mightiest boulderstone", known for its use of twin red lightning stakes, and the sibling of Ancient Dragon Lansseax.

During the Age of the Erdtree, the Ancient Dragons warred against the forces of Leyndell, after an assault on the royal capital by the great Ancient Dragon Gransax. Fortissax was challenged by Godwyn the Golden, who fought to the last. Godwyn defeated Fortissax, but he befriended his fallen foe, and their bond gave rise to the Ancient Dragon Cult of the Royal Capital. Through this friendship, Godwyn gained the ability to wield golden lightning, while the dragons gained acceptance as part of the Golden Order.

On the Night of Black Knives, Godwyn was slain by assassins. Godwyn would die in soul alone, with his body condemned to undeath, as it mutated beyond recognition. Fortissax fought long and hard against the death within its companion, becoming corrupted by death in the process. The Lichdragon is encountered within the Deathbed Dream after securing the Cursemark of Death and giving it to Fia, another companion of Godwyn's. Following Fortissax's defeat, Fia gestates the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince, which may usher in an age of death restored.

As well as being able to breathe fire like other Ancient Dragons, Fortissax possesses the ability to summon a storm of gold and black lightning bolts which cover a wide area and inflict Death Blight. It can also summon a bolt of red lightning, which it slams into the ground, releasing waves of red lightning in multiple directions. After its health has been reduced to 60%, it gains the ability to summon two lightning spears at once, as well as a divebomb ability which is followed by a spinning attack using a lightning glaive.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lightning Strike** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- **Guaranteed Drop:** Weeping Peninsula
- Lightning Strike is received upon defeating the Scarab at the bottom of the ravine splitting the Weeping Peninsula region in half. The stone platforms on either side of this can be used to descend safely. Note that it's surrounded by large bats and that lightning strikes constantly hit around this area.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Creates an uneven line of lightning strikes with Lightning Attack Power equal to 246% of Incantation Scaling per hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
  - Also deals 2 Stance damage.
- Can hit multiple times per cast.
- Targeting may seem somewhat random due to the line that is being struck not being quite straight. However, the lightning bolts will always strike on the same intervals which means getting a feel for this and keeping a consistent distance will help with hitting greatly.
- This incantation does not work under low roofs.
  - This is because the targeting is done by sending a projectile straight above the caster's head that then travels forward while sending down lightning bolts periodically. This projectile is destroyed if it hits a solid object.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lansseax's Glaive** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Lansseax's Glaive is obtained by defeating Ancient Dragon Lansseax on the Altus Plateau, south of the Rampartside Path site of grace outside of the wall to the Capital Outskirts.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Call down a glaive made of red lightning that is then swept horizontally, hitting for Lightning Attack Power equal to 325% of Incantation Scaling, and sending out a wave of red lightning with Attack Power equal to 167% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 45 points of Stamina.
- Deals 12 Stance damage on a direct hit. The wave deals 5 Stance damage.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- A bit too slow to be used against tough foes but very effective against crowds.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption.
  - FP cost was reduced from 28 to 22.
- Patch 1.04 included an undocumented change that reduced the FP cost.
  - FP cost was reduced from 35 to 28.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Law of Causality** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Given by Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing after defeating Mohg, Lord of Blood and choosing to talk "About the Lord of Blood's Cocoon".

Can also be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks for 5,000 Runes after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Grants a unique Buff that lasts for 120 seconds. If the buffed target is damaged 5 times within 7 seconds, they explode, hitting for 487 Holy Attack Power against all enemies within a 4-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Deals 7 Stance damage.
- Since the buff caster has to take damaging hits to trigger the effect, shields with 100% Guarded Damage Negation can prevent the effect from activating. Shields with almost but not quite 100% Guarded Damage Negation (such as the Lordsworn's Shield and its 94% Guarded Damage Negation against Physical damage) can minimize the damage needed.
- The final hit for the buffed can be triggered during a roll or another effect that reduces damage taken to 0. If this happens, the explosion's damage is also reduced to 0.
- Does not scale at all with Incantation Scaling, meaning its damage can only be increased with effects that can buff general damage, incantation damage, and Holy damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 extended effect time.
  - Duration was extended from 60 seconds to 120 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Law of Regression** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 10,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character for the rest of that Journey.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Removes the Status Effects, Buffs, and debuffs from the caster and allies and enemies within a radius of 15 meters and also dispels all active spells within that effect radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 50 points of Stamina to cast.
- The requirements of the Sacred Seal don't need to be met to cast this spell, making it usable with no Faith investment.
- Surprisingly useful for crossing the Lake of Rot. While it's slower to cast than other spells and items, it's still somewhat useful for characters with high medium to high Intelligence but without the Faith needed for Flame, Cleanse Me or the materials for Preserving Boluses.
- Be careful when using it near allies so it doesn't remove their beneficial effects.
- Needed for Goldmask's quest: Reveals a secret referenced by Miriel when used while standing on top of the unknown artist's Wizened Finger message in front of the Radagon statue in Leyndell, Royal Capital, just outside of the Erdtree Sanctuary. Once you have revealed the secret message, you will be able to tell Goldmask about it to progress Brother Corhyn's quest.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lightning Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Altus Plateau.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> If the player lights the Forge of the Giants before this incantation appears in Corhyn's inventory, it will become unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Lightning Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Lightning damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  20 FP per cast.
- Costs  13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces lightning damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *LightningFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
<math>TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {LightningDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {LightningFortification}) )</math>
  - For example, if lightning damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
<math>TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
<math>TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%</math>

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as lightning damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple lightning negation sources.
- Lightning Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
- This incantation is especially valuable against Leyndell Knights, Silver Tears, and Spark Orbs, particularly in Crumbling Farum Azula, where lightning damage is prevalent.
- Lightning Fortification offers greater lightning protection than Lightningproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
  - The Lightningproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:

- Divine Fortification
- Flame Fortification
- Golden Lightning Fortification, a stronger, area version of this incantation
- Magic Fortification

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Creates a small, golden spear in hand to throw, with Lightning Attack Power equal to 234% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the incantation increases the Attack Power to 293% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Casting the spell costs 28 points of Stamina. Charging it increases the cost to 36 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 9.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 44%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- Charging this incantation more than doubles the casting time. In fact, though Knight's Lightning Spear is a good bit slower when both are cast uncharged, if they are charged they take the same amount of time to cast.
- Non-player characters will not actively try to dodge the uncharged version of this incantation. This is especially useful when fighting against evasive foes such as Tarnished-type enemies, since they are otherwise near-perfect at dodging projectile attacks.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
  - Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Lightning Spear was charged or not.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 increased attack power when charged.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lord's Aid** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Lord's Aid is sold for  2,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Two Fingers' Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: The caster kneels in prayer to remove Poison, Blood Loss, and Sleep and their buildup from themselves and nearby allies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  9 FP per cast.
- Costs  10 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- The healing effect can be delayed indefinitely by holding the casting button, which is useful if an ally is not yet within range.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Lord's Aid is an effective utility spell for removing status effects during general gameplay.
- As the Status Effect removal niche is generally better covered by more specialized alternatives such as Flame, Cleanse Me or Bestial Constitution, this incantation instead serves much better as a way to cure some common Status Effects from partners in Co-Op, whether as a summoned Furled Finger or as a summoning Host of Fingers.
- Lord's Aid is preferable to Law of Regression for helping allies in PvE encounters, as the latter also removes positive Buffs.
- The caster crouches while casting this incantation, which may cause some attacks to miss due to the reduced height.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - This is one of only two spells in the entire game that removes Status Effects from nearby allies. The other is Law of Regression, an incantation with a high Intelligence requirement.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Bestial Constitution – Cures Blood Loss and Frostbite
- Cure Poison  – A niche incantation focused solely on removing Poison
- Flame, Cleanse Me – A versatile variant for cleansing status effects
- Lucidity – A sorcery that removes Sleep and Madness
- Neutralizing / Staunching / Clarifying Boluses – Consumable tools that alleviate status buildup

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lord's Divine Fortification** is a incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Quest Item / Purchase:** Roundtable Hold
- Received from Gideon after discussing the haligtree roots, once Malenia, Blade of Miquella has been defeated.
- Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 3,500 Runes if the player does not talk to Gideon about the roots before unleashing the Rune of Death.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Grants a Body Buff that decreases holy damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  30 FP per cast.
- Costs  20 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces holy damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total holy damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *Lord'sDivineFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
<math>TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {HolyDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {Lord'sDivineFortification}) )</math>
  - For example, if holy damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
<math>TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.60) ) = 51.25%</math>
  - Against other players, the total reduction would be 40%:
<math>TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.20) ) = 40%</math>
- Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher holy damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell, the less effective it may appear in the statistics.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as holy damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple holy negation sources.
- Lord's Divine Fortification is a very strong defensive spell that can significantly protect against the ranged attacks of many of the more difficult bosses, such as Maliketh, the Black Blade; Radahn, Consort of Miquella; and Radagon of the Golden Order.
- This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Holy damage in the game, particularly when facing enemies like Cleanrot Knights, Erdtree Avatars, Miranda Blossoms, and Oracle Envoys, especially while exploring Miquella's Haligtree.
- Lord's Divine Fortification offers greater holy protection than Divine Fortification (60% vs. 35%) but with a shorter duration (70 vs. 90 seconds). This spell requires 27 Faith, 1 Memory Slot, and 30 FP to cast, while Divine Fortification requires only 10 Faith and 20 FP.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - This is the only upgraded Fortification spell that is a Two Fingers Incantation.

sections.text:

- Magic Fortification
- Flame Fortification

**Magic Downpour** is a spell in Elden Ring. Creates a magical orb slightly above your head which then randomly fires weak bolts down in a cone pattern. The bolts are not guided to nearby enemies, so the accuracy of the attacks (and therefore efficiency of the damage output) is extremely limited against all but the largest enemies that may be hit by a large number of the bolts.

It is one of the Carian Blade Sorceries, a subset of the Carian Sorceries.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Creates a wyrm head to spit a ball of magma that remains on the ground. Can be cast again to immediately spit a second ball.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Attack Power is boosted by the Roar Medallion and by holding a Dragon Communion Seal in an active hand.
- Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Theodorix's Magma.
- Compared to Theodorix's Magma, this spell deals about 30% less damage but also consumes 33% less FP.
- The leftover magma pools last for roughly 6 seconds and deal about 5% of the damage of a direct hit, less early on due to enemy flat defenses.
  - Pools are useful as traps against agile enemies such as Strays and Fingercreepers by forcing them to stagger a bit.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Land Squirt Ashes** is a spirit ash in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes, at the foot of the cliffs east of Academy Gate Town.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Grave Gloveworts.
- Summons three Land Squirts that spread a heavy, poisonous mist.
- Their mist both deals Standard damage and causes Poison build-up.
- This is the only Spirit Ash that is vulnerable to Poison and Scarlet Rot, and like their enemy counterpart they will explode into a cloud of Poison that affects enemies and allies if either Status Effect is fully applied to them.
- Spawn at the Summoning Monument when summoned, instead of at the player's side.
  - Not completely immobile, just very, very slow.
  - Since they most likely won't move far from their spawn point and the monument has a tendency to be somewhat out of the way it's important to know where it is, especially for when summoning in the open world rather than a boss arena.
- Very tanky and potentially capable of inflicting heavy damage if an enemy gets stuck or held up between them, even if they are immune to Poison. However, this can be somewhat complicated by their often out-of-the-way spawn position and though they have quite a bit of health they are a bit too lacking in Poise to fully withstand the resulting assaults on them.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Liurnia of the Lakes**, also known as **Liurnia**, is a region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Liurnia is the westernmost region of the Lands Between. Characterized by its vast forests, sheer cliffs, and ever-present fog, the majority of the region is sinking into a lake. On the eastern side, the Bellum Highway runs north to south, connecting the area to the regions of Altus Plateau and Limgrave. The western coast is closely associated with the Carian royal family, and this is where their Manor stands. The Academy of Raya Lucaria rises above the lake in the center of the region, at a junction between two highroads, with the Academy Gate Town spreading around it, slowly disappearing into the waters.

The Moonlight Altar, a high plateau at the southern point, obscures the Village of the Albinaurics and its surrounding poisonous lake on the overworld map. It can only be accessed via an elevator located past the Grand Cloister deep underground, guarded by Astel, Naturalborn of the Void.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Leyndell, Royal Capital** is a legacy dungeon on the Altus Plateau in Elden Ring. This area is revealed on the map by collecting Map: Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Leyndell, Royal Capital sits at the foot of the Erdtree on Altus Plateau. It is connected to the Capital Outskirts, Forbidden Lands, and Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. The city is enclosed by double ramparts, with the city proper contained within the inner wall. The current lord of Leyndell is Morgott the Grace-Given, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage, who took it upon himself to become the Erdtree's protector, despite being born a graceless Omen.

Long ago, the city was assaulted by the colossal Ancient Dragon Gransax- the only time in recorded history that Leyndell's walls have fallen. This marked the dawn of the War of the Ancient Dragons. The bloody conflict came to an end when Godwyn the Golden befriended the dread Fortissax, an event which gave rise to the capital's Ancient Dragon Cult. Gransax's corpse can still be found towering over much of the city.

The Fortified Manor, in the southwestern portion of the city, is a perfect likeness of the Roundtable Hold. In its heyday, the manor was the headquarters of the Two Fingers and the warriors of Elden Lord Godfrey. Unlike the Table of Lost Grace, where Tarnished champions gather, the Fortified Manor is completely abandoned.

Far below the city is the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, a network of sewers and waterways inhabited by the Omen. The Leyndell Catacombs also branch off from this underground realm. Even further below lies the Cathedral of the Forsaken, where the Great Caravan of nomadic merchants were entombed so as to bury the Madness that followed them. In their underground prison they chanted a curse of despair, summoning the Frenzied Flame.

The Elden Throne sits beneath the Erdtree, in the south-eastern area of the city. It is here that Morgott stands guard, determined to protect the Erdtree from would-be champions.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Lake of Rot is a large cavernous area beneath Liurnia of the Lakes filled with rotting waters. The lake itself is littered with the crumbling remnants of an ancient dynasty. Within the center of the Lake of Rot are obelisks with stone pressure plates that when activated, raise platforms from beneath the lake, creating a pathway. In the southern part of this area, the Grand Cloister is found; a large walkway infested with rotted-flora and fauna.

The divine essence of an Outer God is sealed away in this lake, after it was defeated by a blind swordsman with a flowing sword. The Servants of Rot have a presence here, as a Mushroom Crown is found in the lake and the Kindred of Rot populate the Grand Cloiser.

Instead, the Grand Cloister featured a group of approximately six Rot Worshippers (rot-infused Ancestral Follower Warriors), and one rotten Ancestral Follower Shaman. The primary differences were that the Warriors had a stun-locking rot-breath ability, while the Shaman’s melee attacks inflicted Scarlet Rot. Additionally, the Putrid Tree Spirit at the far end of the area was always visible.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lightseeker Hyetta**, later known as **Finger Maiden Hyetta**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Hyetta is a blind woman who travels the Lands Between in pursuit of a distant light that she believes to lead her to her duty as a Finger Maiden. To this end, she begs for donations of Shabriri Grapes, which allow her to see the distant light in the back of her eyes. Hyetta requests grapes from The Tarnished at various points across Liurnia of the Lakes, eventually learning that the grapes she has been eating are human eyeballs, vomiting in repulsion. However, her resolve returns, and she becomes more determined than ever to become a Finger Maiden, realizing that with everyone's eyes together, the distant light is clearer. With the light seeming closer than ever, Hyetta asks the Tarnished for a Fingerprint Grape, the eye of one who has been clasped by the burned Fingers. The Tarnished fights and defeats Festering Fingerprint Vyke, a Tarnished who was scorched by the Flame of Frenzy, and offers his eyeball to Hyetta, who eats it.

If her questline has been advanced, the light guides Hyetta to the Frenzied Flame Proscription, far below the capital, where it is revealed that all along she had been guided by Three Fingers. She waits patiently on the side of the hall opposite the Site of Grace, urging the Tarnished to seek an audience with the Three Fingers, whose sanctum lies beyond a large stone door that was partially melted by searing fingerprints. Should the Tarnished allow themselves to be burned by the Flame of Frenzy and touch Hyetta's forehead, she becomes a Finger Maiden and relay the words of the Three Fingers. She reveals that all that there is came from the One Great, and that every sin and every curse was born of a mistake of the Greater Will. She states the purpose of the Flame of Frenzy: to melt everything away until all is One again. Her body then becomes engulfed in Frenzied Flames, and she burns away, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
For Lightseeker Hyetta to appear, you must have completed Irina of Morne's questline, meaning Irina must be dead.

1. Lake-Facing Cliffs (Liurnia of the Lakes)
  - Hyetta first appears near the  Lake-Facing Cliffs Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes. Exhaust her dialogue, and she shall request a Shabriri Grape.
  - Give her a Shabriri Grape, the nearest of which is south of Hyetta, found within the rear entrance to Stormveil Castle. However, the door is locked from the other side, accessible from the Stormveil Castle throne room.
1. Purified Ruins (Liurnia of the Lakes)
  - Hyetta moves to a spot close to the Purified Ruins. She again asks for a Shabriri Grape, the closest of which is east of Hyetta's location, within the Purified Ruins. It is in a secret cellar, hidden beneath some wooden planks.
  - Give her the Shabriri Grape and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Gate Town Bridge (Liurnia of the Lakes)
  - Hyetta will now appear just north of the  Gate Town Bridge site of grace. She will ask for yet another Shabriri Grape. The final grape is dropped by Edgar the Revenger, who ambushes the player at the Revenger's Shack, found north of the Minor Erdtree in western Liurnia.
  - After giving her the third grape, you will have the option to tell her that the grapes are human eyes. After hearing her dialogue following this revelation, reload the area and speak to her again in the same spot.
1. Bellum Church (Bellum Highway)
  - Hyetta is next found within the ruined Bellum Church, found along the Bellum Highway. After talking to her, she will ask you to bring her a special Fingerprint Grape. This item can be obtained by defeating Festering Fingerprint Vyke, who invades the player at the Church of Inhibition in eastern Liurnia.
  - Bring Hyetta the grape and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Frenzied Flame Proscription (Subterranean Shunning-Grounds)
  - Hyetta's final location is in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, deep below Leyndell, Royal Capital, at the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription. A seal at the Cathedral of the Forsaken restricts access to this location, available only after defeating Morgott, the Omen King. Exhaust her dialogue until she instructs you to unequip all Armor and interact with the burnt door at the end of the hall, past where she stands.
  - Remove all Armor and interact with the door to initiate a cutscene wherein the player meets the Three Fingers and inherits the Flame of Frenzy. (**WARNING**: this action permanently removes Melina as a companion and sets you on the path to the "Lord of the Frenzied Flame" ending, the latter of which can only be undone by using Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time to cheat fate.)
  - After the cutscene, return to Hyetta and exhaust her dialogue. After speaking to her twice, the Frenzied Flame burns her away, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal and five Frenzyflame Stones.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Hyetta will not appear if the player kills Irina of Morne early.
- Hyetta can be killed and her blood can be used to soak the Lord of Blood's Favor for White Mask Varré.
- Hyetta has the same facial appearance and voice as Irina of Morne, and she will only appear if Irina's questline has ended and she has died. Hyetta is Irina, having experienced some form of resurrection or rebirth similar to Shabriri.
- The player can meet the Three Fingers and commit the Cardinal Sin without meeting Lightseeker Hyetta, and her questline proceeds as usual if started after.

- Lightseeker Hyetta had an additional quest stage at Bellum Church in the , but the dialogue and key item she gave were both cut from the game by the  release. The context it provided offered insight into her transition from Irina of Morne and into the characters of Irina and Edgar. Hyetta gave Irina's Necklace after receiving the Fingerprint Grape, abandoning her long search for its owner.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The locked, innate skill, while not unique and reliant on its weaker Intelligence-scaling, is very strong for both the projectile bullet part and the weapon stab part.
- Gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Intelligence build (600 AP from having 45 Strength, 9 Dexterity, and 45 Intelligence), a bit less from a pure Strength build (579 AP from 80 Strength, 9 Dexterity, and 13 Intelligence), and even less from a pure Intelligence build (561 AP from 8 Strength, 12 Dexterity, and 80 Intelligence).
  - Note that since the projectile part of the skill is a bullet-type it scales with associated stat, in this case Intelligence, meaning that the pure Intelligence build will deal the most damage with that part of the skill, and that the pure Strength build will most likely end up dealing somewhat less damage overall with the skill.
- Has a unique blocking heavy attack, shared with the Carian Knight's Sword. While this can make attacking into an attacking foe a bit less punishing, the resulting Stamina damage that will be taken if hit can prevent the user from attacking or rolling away.
  - While the brief hit-stun taken by shields isn't suffered when hit, the low Stability means that using the unique heavy attack is highly likely to result in a stun from being guardbroken.
  - Stability can be increased by 10% via two-handing and then further by the Greatshield Talisman.
  - While the uncharged unique heavy attack deals the same amount of Stance damage as a normal uncharged heavy attack, but the charged version only deals 1.5 times more Stance damage, instead of the regular charged version which deals 3 times more Stance damage.

sections.text: **Maleigh Marais, Shaded Castle Castellan** is a hostile NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Maleigh Marais is the Lord of the Shaded Castle, a location that has been overseen by executioners for generations. He was once a private worshipper of scarlet rot, and would later become obsessed with Malenia. This is partly due to his own sickly bloodline, fueling an admiration of Malenia for remaining strong despite her own affliction.

The state of the Shaded Castle reflects this shift in fixation, as the Castellan's Hall is filled with prostheses, Cleanrot armor, and a large portrait of Malenia. This worship seems to have been blamed as part of the reason for the Shaded Castle's downfall, as Malenia is viewed as a "severed harpy" by other residents.

With the Shaded Castle sacked by Elemer of the Briar, Marais seems to have escaped as one of the few survivors, located to the west of the Castle with a Guardian Golem in his company.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Leyndell Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A knight of Leyndell, distinguished by the golden canopy on their helms that marks them as one of the tree's defenders. Their armor's left breast is emblazoned with a symbol of Erdtree Worship, rumored to have been imbued with an incantation of protection. They carry with them an oval greatshield made of gold, earning the knights a reputation for their sturdiness.

All Leyndell Knights carry a Golden Greatshield. Those that wield Knight's Greatsword are capable of imbuing their armament with lightning by using Ash of War: Lightning Slash. Those that wield a Partisan are capable of calling down lightning, using Ash of War: Thunderbolt, as well as casting Rejection. They are highly skilled combatants, able to Guard Counter if an attack lands on their shields. Some Leyndell Knights wield a Greatbow, but will switch to their melee armaments upon approach. Like other knight enemies, they can also appear on horseback. There are also Frenzied Leyndell Knights on Mt. Gelmir that are capable of casting The Flame of Frenzy and Howl of Shabriri incantations.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Leyndell Foot Soldier** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A foot soldier tasked with the protection of Leyndell. They can be found grouped together, often in the vicinity of a Leyndell Soldier or Leyndell Knight. They are nimble when wielding a Dagger or a Short Sword, but those that carry a Spear or Torchpole are less so. Some provide ranged support to their allies with a Soldier's Crossbow or by throwing Lightning Pots, whilst others employ the usage of heavier artillery such as Ballistae or Trebuchet. There are also Frenzied Leyndell Foot Soldiers on Mt. Gelmir that are capable of casting The Flame of Frenzy incantation.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Leyndell Soldiers** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A soldier sworn to defend Leyndell. They wear a surcoat bearing the majestic likeness of the Erdtree, its golden backing an honor not bestowed upon any other soldier.  They fight their battles defensively and during the Shattering they were the ramparts that fortified the royal capital.

They wield either Lordsworn's Straight Sword or Warpick and can carry either a Torch or Brass Shield in their offhand. Those with a shield can perform a Guard Counter if an attack lands on their shield. They can also employ the use of a Spark Aromatic. Some of them will also carry a trumpet on their person. Upon spotting the player, they will use it and attract nearby enemies towards their position.

Some of them wield a Heavy Crossbow for ranged combat, while others are able to employ the use of Spark Aromatic. Those that wield a Partisan also carry a Lordsworn's Shield, while those that use the Lordsworn's Greatsword carry no shield but are capable of performing the Ash of War: Determination. There are also Frenzied Leyndell Soldiers on Mt. Gelmir that can cast The Flame of Frenzy incantation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The spear used by the Soldiers is a modified Partisan, missing the red cloth that is on the version given to the player.
- Two Leyndell Soldier allies can be summoned by using Leyndell Soldier Ashes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The narratives of Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign are built bit by bit and told mainly through context and environmental storytelling techniques. This page summarizes the main story and lists the major factions, characters, and events that define the Lands Between and broader *Elden Ring* setting. This page allows users to easily locate parts of the text that offer insight into each topic. Please refer to the Lore category for a complete list of articles.

sections.heading: Story
sections.text: In the beginning, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, which led to divisions, births, and souls. It sent its daughter, Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and its golden vassal Elden Beast through the Primeval Current to the Lands Between, the place to which all Death inevitably drifts. The Elden Beast held the power of runes and was the living embodiment of Order, and it was later forged into the great Elden Ring. The Lands Between became the arena of champions vying to become the Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Prologue
sections.text:
Long ago, in the Lands Between, the Two Fingers directed the Empyrean Marika to claim godhood at the Gate of Divinity and become the next vessel for the Elden Ring. Marika then waged a violent War Against the Giants to upend the Fell God and suppress the Flame of Ruin, using a Golden Seed to transform the primordial Crucible of life into the Erdtree. This act ushered in an age of Plenty. Empowered by soaring Grace of Gold, Godfrey, her first Elden Lord, and his warriors set out to conquer the entirety of the continent in her name. However, this age of abundance soon came to a swift, unforeseen end. Marika later removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and commanded her loyal shadow, Maliketh, to seal it away. Thus, she, her Demigod offspring, and those blessed by her Grace of Gold would live forever, earning her the title of Queen Marika the Eternal.

Godfrey, by then known as the Lord of the Battlefield, fought until Marika's reign was absolute. When the last worthy enemy fell to his axe, the very same Grace that blessed him and his army was taken away by Marika, who instructed them to wage another war and die abroad, with the promise that life and Grace would be returned to them after death. All those who were stripped of their Grace, as well as their descendants, were Tarnished, and forced onto boats and across the Sea of Fog to carry out their Long March into the Badlands, though one vessel failed to leave. Queen Marika also sent her son Messmer and an army of outcasts on a crusade to destroy the hornsent, the old folk who dwelled in the Land of the Tower. She trapped them in the Realm of Shadow to protect herself from the Base Serpent and to conceal her shrouded origins. She later claimed Radagon of the Golden Order as her second Elden Lord, who was, in truth, her other self and a very part of her being.

After a time, Marika later instructed her children to rise as Lords or gods, or become sacrifices. She then shattered the Elden Ring, fracturing her Golden Order and releasing its Great Runes into the Lands for her children to claim. After that, Queen Marika was nowhere to be found—punished by the Elden Beast and imprisoned within the Erdtree. The Demigods were each corrupted by the power of their Great Runes, triggering the appalling Shattering, a war from which no victor arose, leading to their abandonment by the Greater Will. True to Marika's promise, it was then that the Grace of Gold returned to the Tarnished, and beckoning them back to the Lands Between so that one might repair the shattered Elden Ring and become the Elden Lord.

sections.heading: *Nightreign*
sections.text: Elden Ring Nightreign shares the same world and backstory as *Elden Ring*, but takes place on a parallel timeline that diverged after Marika shattered the Elden Ring. A Shattering War also took place between the Demigods; however, it had a different outcome: Heolstor the Nightlord, empowered by the Primordial Nightlord's Rune, ushered in the Night. An azure Night's Tide created the Nightlords and threatened to wash away the Lands Between. The Dreglord, a comparable threat, emerged soon after, driven by vengeance to smash the Night.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Latenna the Albinauric** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Latenna is an Albinauric woman and a deft archer. She and her wolf companion, Lobo, began their journey in the lands of the Haligtree, a sanctuary for Albinaurics. She journeyed to the far south, eventually coming to Liurnia of the Lakes.

Here, Latenna was accosted by the servants of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, a Tarnished wishing to gain access to the hidden lands of the Haligtree. Believing Latenna had a secret medallion that opened the way to the Haligtree, Ofnir's servants attacked her and killed her wolf, leaving her crippled, but Latenna still refused to divulge the location of the medallion, feigning ignorance.

After the Tarnished receives a half of the secret medallion from the elderly Albinauric Albus, Latenna tells them the location of the other half, and asks them to bring her along to the lands of the Haligtree, where she might fulfill her duty. The Tarnished agrees, and Latenna voluntarily becomes Spirit Ash, so they might carry her with them.

In the Mountaintops of the Giants, Latenna alerts the Tarnished that the medallion is near when they approach Castle Sol. With the second half retrieved, the path to the Haligtree is opened. She urges them to bring her to the liturgical town of Ordina. Here, a towering young Albinauric known as Phillia slumbers. Latenna grants her the birthing droplet, allowing her to create new life for all the Albinaurics. She thanks the Tarnished for their aid, promising to fight alongside them until the bitter end, requesting that they lay her to rest by Lobo once the fighting is done.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Slumbering Wolf's Shack)
  - Latenna can be found at the Slumbering Wolf's Shack, accessible by clearing the Lakeside Crystal Cave. If you have the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right), obtained from Old Albus in the Village of the Albinaurics, she will die and you will be able to pick up Latenna the Albinauric (Spirit Ashes).
  - If you have already obtained Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left) from Castle Sol, Latenna will already be dead, and you can pick up her Spirit Ashes.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants (Castle Sol)
  - After defeating Commander Niall, continue past his arena and pick up the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
1. Consecrated Snowfields (Apostate Derelict)
  - Travel to the Apostate Derelict in the northernmost part of the Consecrated Snowfields and approach the giant Albinauric woman to summon Latenna. Exhaust Latenna's dialogue to obtain a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Man-Bats**, also known as **Giant Bats**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Man-Bats are nocturnal predators found across the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow. They commonly dwell near ancient black stone ruins but also populate caves, mines, and forts. By day, they often sit idly or hang from ruins; by night, they become far more active and aggressive. Man-Bats are frequently encountered in groups alongside matriarchal Operatic Bats, whose mournful Latin arias blame Marika for their vile circumstances.

Dark, leathery skin wraps these emaciated winged creatures, from whose backs sprout tufts of silvery hair. Their enormous ears aid in echolocation, and the undersides of their membraned wings bear a layer of striking patterned fur. While Man-Bats may crawl around using their forelimbs, they prefer to fly during combat. They attack using their sharp hind claws and, if they get close enough, by sinking long, dagger-like fangs into their prey. They are capable of emitting a concussive sonar screech that can strike from range.

Two distinct varieties of Man-Bat exist, each identified by the color and pattern of fur growing on the front of their wing. The common Man-Bat is distinguished by vivid bright red fur with yellow markings. The Elite variant, exclusive to the Mountaintops of the Giants, has duller wings that fiercely display eyespot mimicry. Additionally, it possesses significantly greater HP, and yield more runes upon defeat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In the , Man-Bats possessed a cut animation in which they stood upright and sang "Herutun Rutun" by Umeko Ando a cappella. The song is performed in Ainu, a critically endangered language indigenous to Japan.
  - , an oral storytelling tradition practiced by the Ainu, is told in first-person and often describes the world from the perspectives of animals.
  - This animation may have been a placeholder for the "Song of Lament" sung by Operatic Bats.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Latenna the Albinauric** is a Spirit Ash in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Obtained after talking to Latenna the Albinauric (NPC) at Slumbering Wolf's Shack and accepting her request.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.
- Summons a dismounted Albinauric Archer.
  - She can actually mount Albinauric Archer Wolf wherever they are found, though it's unknown if this is an intended interaction.
- Mostly immobile, only able to shuffle around very slightly. Make sure to place her carefully, preferably on a high, hard to reach spot.
  - Railings and big rocks are good positions, as are weapons with good mix of decent reach and good speed, such as Straight Swords and Spears, to keep hostile attention on the summoner.
- Fires 3 arrows at once at a steady rate. While these don't deal that much damage individually, the steady fire gives her good damage if enemy attention can be kept away from her.

sections.text: The **Lord of Blood's Favor** is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
- The Lord of Blood's Favor must be soaked in a Finger Maiden's blood to become Lord of Blood's Favor (Soaked). This can be done through the following options:
1. Interact with the corpse of the Tarnished's own Finger Maiden at the Chapel of Anticipation (requires an Imbued Sword Key to access the Sending Gate at the Four Belfries).
1. Interact with the corpse of Vyke's Finger Maiden at the Church of Inhibition near the  Frenzied Flame Village Outskirts.

1. Invade and defeat Magnus the Beast Claw three times at the Writheblood Ruins in the Altus Plateau.
1. Use Festering Bloody Fingers to Invade actual players three times (online only).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Madness** is one of the status effects in Elden Ring.

Madness causes a heavy stagger while draining a significant amount of the player's HP and FP, making it a more dangerous version of Sleep. However, it is ineffective against most enemies except for Tarnished. The player's resistance to this status is determined by their Focus stat, which is increased by the Mind stat.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.text: Madness builds up over time, inflicting minor damage as the effect accumulates. Once the Madness bar is fully filled, the player suffers a significant amount of damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Mad Tongue Alberich** is an NPC invader in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Alberich was an aloof yet disturbed heretical sorcerer, his attire adorned by red glintstone born from the blood of sacrifices. It is said he was driven mad by jeering tongues during his service to the Roundtable Hold long ago.

He wields a scythe imbued with cold, and a combination of frost and thorn-based sorceries. He invades in the hall of Roundtable Hold, accessed by dropping down from the balcony.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - A corpse holding Alberich's Set can be found on the first floor of the Fortified Manor―in the same hall where Alberich invades at the Roundtable Hold.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Mad Tongue Alberich was named **Frenzy-Tongue Alberich** in .

sections.text: **Marionette Soldier** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Four-armed automatons created and controlled by the sorcerers of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, they are mostly found patrolling the academy and the nearby area. They use their four arms to wield a greater number of weapons than the average soldier, overwhelming targets with attacks rather than skill. When damaged, Marionettes will lash out erratically in all directions so it is best to stay back until the flurry ends.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Living Jars** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Sentient, animated jars found throughout the Lands Between. They are brought to life by human flesh and blood, and are considered a kindly folk, however they will protect themselves from perceived threats. They contain human innards within them, from which they inherit the dregs of those who came before. Fragments of their bodies are sought after due to the magical power locked within, making them targets of poachers.

An enclave of peaceful Living Jars reside in Jarburg, on the cliffs of Liurnia of the Lakes.

Little=

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Small, childlike Living Jars, often found under the protection of Warrior Jars. They are often passive unless provoked.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Living Jars with distinct yellow lids. Their primary tactic is to rush at their enemies and then explode, killing themselves and dealing damage to friends and foes alike. They will also explode if they come into contact with fire.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Larger Living Jars that contain the remnants of warriors. They pass these warrior's innards from jar to jar, carrying their dreams of greatness with them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Companion Jar talisman mentions that perhaps they were made to be better than their innards. In Shadow of the Erdtree, it is revealed that undesirable people were stuffed into jars so that they could be reborn into good people. Shamans then perform their worship at gaols where they offer their prayers to the innards of the greatjars, such that they might be reborn one day into sainthood, or good people. This is the cycle of death and rebirth, taken into the hands of mortal men.
  - Living Jars drop Raw Meat Dumplings that contain teeth and inflict  Poison, not unlike the  Poison-inflicting Tooth Whips used by Greater Potentates to tenderize Shamans.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In the context of Living Jars, "saint" and "sainthood" refer to "a very virtuous, kind, or patient person" and "a person acknowledged as holy or virtuous and typically regarded as being in heaven after death." The Japanese version uses 善き人 (lit. "good/righteous person"), rather than terms specific to Catholic and Orthodox saints. This applies to the following texts:
    - "*I swear**—a living saint** I'll surely be!*" Stranded Souls -> 天に誓う。**善き人**になる
    - "***Nigh-sainthood** itself awaits you within.*" Stranded Souls -> そして、**善き人**になりなさい
    - "*This is what becomes of the condemned, who get sliced up and stuffed into jars to become **saints** instead.*" Innard Meat -> **善き人**になるために 切り刻まれ、大壺に詰め込まれた罪人どもの なれの果てである
    - "*They offer their prayers to the innards of the greatjars, such that they might be reborn one day into **sainthood.***" Greatjar -> その祈りは大壺の中身に捧げられる いつか、**善き人**として生まれ変わるように それは、人の手による輪廻である

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Land Squirts** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Land Squirts are stationary creatures that release poisonous gas when threatened. Their fleshy, tube-like bodies remain rooted in place, continuously spraying poison into their surroundings when approached.

Land Squirts are vulnerable on their soft undersides and to their own element. Inflicting Poisoned status on a poison Land Squirt will cause it to explode, potentially creating a chain reaction among nearby Land Squirts.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Land Squirts can be staggered and riposted.
- They fall over when staggered, exposing their soft underbellies.
- When poisoned, they explode, creating a chain reaction among nearby Land Squirts.
- Found primarily near water sources.
- The spirit of three Land Squirts can be summoned using Land Squirt Ashes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Magic** is a Damage Type in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Fighting Against Magic
sections.text:
- Magic Fortification/Barrier of Gold, increases Magic damage negation by 35%/60% (10%/20% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user, lasting for 90 seconds/70 seconds. Barrier of Gold additionally grants the buff to nearby allies. Requires 10 and 24 Faith to cast.
- Protection of the Erdtree, increases Magic damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP) as a Body Buff for the user and nearby allies for 70 seconds. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount. Requires 35 Faith to cast.
- Spelldrake Talisman/Spelldrake Talisman +1/Spelldrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Magic damage negation by 13%/17%/20% (4%/5%/6% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time.
- Pearldrake Talisman/Pearldrake Talisman +1/Pearldrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Magic damage negation by 5%/7%/9% (2%/3%/4% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount.
- Spellproof Dried Liver, a consumable and Body Buff that increases Magic damage negation by 15% (10% in PvP). Lasts for 120 seconds.
- Pest's Glaive, a Halberd that increases Magic damage negation by 2%. Also increases Fire damage negation, Lightning damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount. Only works if held in an active hand and does not stack with another Pest's Glaive.

sections.heading: Fighting With Magic
sections.text:
- Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear, increases Magic damage dealt by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes when used with the Flask of Wondrous Physick.
- Magic Scorpion Charm, a Talisman that increases Magic damage dealt by 12% (8% in PvP) while increasing Physical damage taken by 10% (15% in PvP).
- Terra Magicus, a Sorcery that creates a groundbound, stationary sigil that increases Magic damage dealt while standing inside of it by 35% (20% in PvP). Requires 20 Intelligence to cast.
- Spellblade's Pointed Hat/Spellblade's Traveling Attire (or Spellblade's Traveling Attire (Altered))/Spellblade's Gloves/Spellblade's Trousers, increases Magic damage dealt by 2% per piece for Skills that deal magic damage (and any Skill used by the Horn Bow). Effect stacks if wearing several pieces at the same time (though the two Chest armor pieces cannot be worn at the same time) for a maximum damage increase of 8%.

- Pearldrake Talisman/Pearldrake Talisman +1/Pearldrake Talisman +2, talismans that increases Lightning damage negation by 5%/7%/9% (2%/3%/4% in PvP). Only one can be worn at a time. Also increases Fire damage negation, Magic damage negation, and Holy damage negation by the same amount.

sections.text:
<noinclude>

Maps are a type of Key Item found in Elden Ring. They are found in fragmented pieces across the Lands Between, and each piece displays an artistic rendition of their local region's geography. Once a map fragment has been acquired, it will become a permanent addition to the player's inventory, staying even when transitioning into .

They are typically found near large, stone Guide Stele inscribed with glowing yellow text that fades once that tablet's map has been acquired. These tablets are typically found near roads and are even marked on the obscured map before the current region's map fragment has been acquired.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The complete map has sometimes had its art changed over the course of several patches.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Royal Knight Loretta**, also known as **Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree**, is a recurring, optional Great Enemy boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Loretta is the boss of two locations: Caria Manor and Miquella's Haligtree. Her oath-sworn spectral form—Royal Knight Loretta—is found at the former, while her corporeal body defends the latter. Loretta is mechanically similar to the Tree Sentinels and Draconic Tree Sentinels and cannot be separated from her steed.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Loretta was once a royal Carian knight, and served as a personal guard for Carian royalty. Loretta's favored weapon was said to be the bow, and she developed sorceries imitating the power of a greatbow.

Loretta eventually became concerned with the plight of the Albinaurics and embarked on a long and bloody journey searching for a haven for the Albinauric people. She determined that the Haligtree was their best chance for eventual salvation. It was rumored she was actually an Albinauric herself, due to the shape and symbolism associated with her Silver Mirrorshield.  She would eventually find it at the Haligtree, in service to demigod Miquella, where she now remains.

Loretta appears to have entered into Miquella's service, replacing the blue glintstone that once adorned her war sickle with unalloyed gold. Now she stands guard within the Haligtree, refusing to abandon her post although Miquella himself is long gone. Her lapis-lazuli blue cape is the emblem of the knightly pride that continues to guide her.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
**Royal Knight Loretta** is a boss in Elden Ring. She can be found at Caria Manor in the Royal Moongazing Grounds.

She appears to be an apparition of Loretta summoned to guard Caria Manor, just as the real Loretta presumably used to do before leaving her duty to help find sanctuary for the mistreated Albinaurics.

Defeating her disables the magical spell of warding that complicates the approach to the Manor.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
**Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree** is a mini-boss in Elden Ring found in Miquella's Haligtree and is required to progress to Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. This boss is a stronger version of Royal Knight Loretta, found in Caria Manor.

It is possible to parry Loretta's halberd swings.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating Royal Knight Loretta for the first time unlocks the "Royal Knight Loretta" achievement. Similarly, defeating Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree for the first time unlocks the "Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree" achievement.
- Loretta is presumed to be an Albinauric Archer in disguise.
  - Rumored to be an Albinauric, she cares deeply for them, abandoning her duty to travel to the Haligtree.
  - This female character appears only on horseback and demonstrates unmatched skill with the bow.
  - Her naming scheme aligns with Latenna.
  - Loretta's War Sickle, Royal Knight Armor, and Silver Mirrorshield were crafted from silver.
  - The Carians were known to employ Albinaurics as servants.
  - Although she bleeds red when struck, so does Commander Gaius, a known First-Generation Albinauric. The red blood may be attributed to the mount and rider being coded as a single enemy, with red chosen over white because players are more likely to hit the horse or boar.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Magma Wyrm** is a reoccurring boss and non-respawning enemy in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

Magma Wyrms are quadrupedal draconic beings with torn, vestigial wings and broad heads. They were once human heroes who partook in Dragon Communion, for which they were cursed to crawl the earth as flightless imitations of Dragons, losing their humanity in the process. They wield scaly greatswords that resemble the jawbones of dragons, and can spew magma from their mouths.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: There are two non-boss Magma Wyrms that can be encountered. One is found in the lower part of Volcano Manor, accessible via an elevator near the  Temple of Eiglay Site of Grace. The second is found in the Dragon's Pit minor dungeon in Gravesite Plain, found by progressing normally through the dungeon, and going up the stairs through a cave opening.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
**Magma Wyrm Makar** resides in ancient ruins at the top of the Ruin-Strewn Precipice, blocking the secret path from Liurnia of the Lakes to Altus Plateau. Makar was likely a human hero who became a wyrm after partaking in Dragon Communion.

In its second phase, it will spew magma onto its sword, coating it in fire.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A Magma Wyrm is encountered in a lava pool near Fort Laiedd, southwest of the  Seethewater Terminus Site of Grace. It can be lured out of the lava for an easier fight.

After defeating this boss, Magma Breath can be obtained at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for  1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Magma Wyrm is encountered at the end of Gael Tunnel in Caelid.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
**Great Wyrm Theodorix** is encountered at the eastern end of the frozen river in the Consecrated Snowfield, northeast of the  Inner Consecrated Snowfield Site of Grace. He was once an ancient troll warrior and hero of the war against the Giants, who became a Magma Wyrm after partaking in Dragon Communion.

His attacks can inflict damage on the Crabs and Land Octopus nearby, which will cause them to aggro against it.

After defeating this boss, Theodorix's Magma can be obtained at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for  2 Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
The **Land of Reeds** (葦の地, *Ashi no Chi*) is a mentioned location in Elden Ring.

It is located outside the borders of the Lands Between and is said to be a place locked in a long and miserable civil war, which, over time, has caused its alienation from neighboring nations and left the entire land succumbed to a blood-soaked madness.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Land of Reeds is home to a caste of warriors known as Samurai, who wield katanas designed to inflict blood loss. Cone-shaped hats woven from straw are also worn in the Land of Reeds.

The warrior, Okina, was a swordsman from the Land of Reeds. It is said that through repeated combat, his mind was sharpened. From his perspective, he began to see the absurdities of the world in stark relief. As a result, he chose to renounce everything, ascending to a plane where it only himself, his katana, and his mastery. Before long, Okina had become a demon of a swordsman. For unknown reasons; perhaps seeking stronger opponents, Okina travelled to the Lands Between. There, he met Mohg, Lord of Blood, in battle. Upon feeling OkIna's blade strike his flesh, Mohg realised the extent of the Reedlander's maddness, and was captivated. In that moment, he made the swordsman an offer: a life in which his thirst for blood would never be sated. Okina agreed, joining the ranks of Mohg's Bloody Fingers. In return, Mohg coated his katana in cursed blood, so that Okina could better pursue his bloodlust.

During Okina's time in the Land of Reeds, his talents had earned a loyal following of fellow warriors known as the Inaba, who became his disciples. The Inaba, and potentially Okina himself, practiced Seppuku, a forbidden combat technique developed in the Land of Reeds. It involves the user impaling themselves with their own weapon, briefly enchanting it to improve damage output and its abilty to inflict blood loss on others. Having been abandoned by Okina when he left for the Lands Between, the Inaba soon pursued their former master, seeking revenge and death in battle, as was their ultimate goal.

sections.heading: People
sections.text: The peoples hailing from this land are referred to as "Reedlanders" and are select-able as a base template for the player character's appearance.

sections.heading: Known Reedlanders
sections.text:
- The Samurai Origin
- Yura, Hunter of Bloody Fingers
- Okina, the Bloody Finger
- Inaba Clansmen

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Its history, weapons and mentioned customs are extremely reminiscent of the Sengoku (warring states) period of Japan, during the the 15th and 16th centuries.
  - One of the legendary names of ancient Japan was 葦原の中つ国 (*Ashihara-no-Nakatsu-Kuni)*, which translates literally to "The Land Amongst the Reeds." (More idiomatically, it might be read "the land of abundant rice.")
- Although never directly stated, many details suggest the Land of Reeds is under the influence of the Formless Mother. These include descriptions of Reedlanders as having "succumbed to a blood-soaked madness" and their clear favoritism for weapons that cause Blood Loss. The Outer God delights in the inflicting of wounds and the spilling of blood in all forms. The magical enhancement granded by Seppuku may very well be a blessing from the Outer God, with the technique acting as a form of offering. If the Formless Mother does preside over the Land of Reeds, it remains unclear if Reedlanders are willing to serve it, or if they are even aware of it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lightningproof Dried Liver** is a craftable, consumable tool in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Increases Lightning damage negation by 15% (10% in PvP) for 120 seconds upon consumption. This counts as a Body Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Compared to Lightning Fortification:
  - In PvE there is a tradeoff, the Liver has greater duration (120 seconds vs 90 seconds) and much lower FP cost (0 FP versus 20 FP) while the Fortification has greater Magic damage negation (35% versus 15%).
    - Unlike the other Liver items this item's cookbook is acquired far later in the game, making it unavailable for Leyndell, Royal Capital, one of the game's major Lightning-focused area.
  - In PvP the Liver is stronger, since these effects have the same strength but the Liver has a greater duration and no FP cost.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be crafted after acquiring the Ancient Dragon Apostle's Cookbook [4] from a round building atop floating stone walls making a bridge upwards in Crumbling Farum Azula. It is found past the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, straight across the courtyard and jumping atop two buildings on the right to get across a gap. Following across the ascending pseudo-bridge, it is guarded by 2 Giant Skeleton Beastmen.
- 2 found in Leyndell, Royal Capital, on the stairs leading to the Fortified Manor. From the Avenue Balcony Site of Grace, head up the stairs and head right to see the stairs, which are guarded by 2 Leyndell Soldiers and 1 spear-wielding Leyndell Knight.
- 1 found in Crumbling Farum Azula, near the Crumbling Beast Grave Site of Grace. Head right and look to the left at a hole in the wall as soon as the next room is entered to find it.
- 1 found in Lake of Rot, to the side of an island near the place where the Dragonkin Soldier is fought in the eastern part of the fetid lake.
- 1 found in Altus Plateau, on a high rock just south of Lux Ruins.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A network of catacombs beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital, accessed via the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. The layout of the catacombs is disorienting, as many of the chambers and hallways are identical to one another, including a room that has the same appearance as the boss rooms in many other catacombs. Omen have made their home here, likely wandering in from the Shunning-Grounds. A blood priest of Mohg also resides here, accompanied by two bloodthirsty hounds.

The entrance to the dungeon is in a large room containing Giant Crayfish, south of the  Underground Roadside Site of Grace.

sections.text: **Leyndell, Ashen Capital** is a legacy dungeon located in Altus Plateau. It is an altered form of Leyndell, Royal Capital which can be accessed after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
With the defeat of Maliketh, the Black Blade, the Rune of Death is unbound, and the Flame of Ruin burns away the impenetrable thorns blocking the entrance to the Erdtree. The city of Leyndell is blanketed in thick ash, burying all but the tallest buildings. The Tarnished returns to the city after releasing the Rune of Death, finally able to approach the Erdtree and gain entry.

This area is connected to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and the Stone Platform. It is still possible to access the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds from this version of Leyndell. A manhole cover that was previously closed is now open, allowing for one to drop down into the sewers below.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Lionel is a dauntless knight who adopted Fia after her exile from her homeland. Known as a chivalrous fighter having earned the title "The Lionhearted," he is a skilled fencer and battle mage.

He is first encountered during the Radahn Festival at Redmane Castle, available as a spirit summon against Starscourge Radahn. He can be met again later as one of the champion spirits that Fia summons to defend herself in Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Redmane Castle (Caelid) - attends the Radahn Festival in phantom form, waiting in the Redmane Castle Plaza.
- Wailing Dunes (Caelid) - his summon sign appears during the Starscourge Radahn Boss Fight
- Prince of Death's Throne (Deeproot Depths) - his blue spirit essence appears during the final wave of Fia's Champions.
- Lower Capital Church (Leyndell, Royal Capital) - his presumed, charred remains hold his armor set.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: - Fia's Mist (as part of Fia's Champions)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- He has unique character data in Zullie the Witch's video "Elden Ring - Hidden Faces of Enemy NPCs" he is an older man, with somewhat unkempt and heavily greyed hair, beard, moustache, and bushy eyebrows, bright silver eyes and a heavily wrinkled face.
- Wears the Lionel's Set, a very heavy armor set that provides exceptional protection particularly against slashing damage.
- Wields a Great Épée with Ash of War: Repeating Thrust and a Prince of Death's Staff that is used to cast Fia's Mist and Rancorcall.
  - Lionel the Lionhearted uses a Carian Glintstone Staff when summoned as a Coooperator against Starscourge Radahn.
- A corpse that can be presumed to be his, what with his armor being lootable from it, can be found in the Lower Capital Church inside of Leyndell, next to the Deathbed Dress.
- Given his inclination for Death Sorceries, Lionel presumably relayed information regarding Black Knifeprints to Fia, specifically the Knifeprint Clue.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- His distinctive rounded armor set and chivalrous personality (inferred by his apparent attitude towards Fia) is likely a reference to the Knights of Catarina from the Dark Souls series, who are jovial people clad in onion-like rounded suits of armor. Unlike these knights, however, he cannot be interacted with or spoken to.
- Based on other Fia's Champions being Tarnished such as other players when online and Sorcerer Rogier, it could be the case that Lionel is also a Tarnished.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Magnus the Beast Claw** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Magnus the Beast Claw is an NPC that can be invaded. To invade him, one must go to the Writheblood Ruins and find an invading summon sign, which costs one Festering Bloody Finger each try to activate. Once the sign is activated, the player will invade Magnus' world with the objective of killing him. The main point of this NPC is  to have another option to advance in White Mask Varré's questline, where the Tarnished is tasked to try invasions 3 times, of either him or other players (though defeating him also counts as all 3 invasions).

Though there are few, if any, hints as to his place in the world, under his mask his face has vertical red markings similar to those borne by the Ancestral Follower Warriors.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
- Both Beast Claw and Gurranq's Beast Claw can be jumped over.
  - This means they serve as good openings for jumping attacks, should you be ready to approach as he starts them up.
- Bestial Sling can simply be dodged through straight forwards and he's unlikely to spam it, limiting its power.
- Having both a Great Hammer (one with Lion's Claw as its skill at that) makes it rather unsafe to block him, especially with anything that isn't at least a decent Greatshield.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Added with Patch 1.06.
- The summon sign used for the invasion only disappears once he is killed, even if White Mask Varré's quest line progresses past this point.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Leonard is the withered horse of Starscourge Radahn during his boss fight at the Radahn Festival in the Wailing Dunes of the Caelid Wilds. Leonard does not attack during the battle and disappears after Radahn's defeat.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Despite Leonard's small and scrawny stature, Radahn continued to ride him even as he grew to an enormous size. Unwilling to abandon his beloved steed, Radahn studied gravitational magic in Sellia under a master who was an Alabaster Lord.

Leonard served the Red Lion General in many battles during the Shattering. After Radahn's duel with Malenia at the Battle of Aeonia, Leonard remained by his lord's side as he was consumed by the baleful scarlet rot.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Leonard is referenced in the description of the Remembrance of the Starscourge.
- Unlike the steed of the Putrescent Knight, Leonard has no attacks of his own.

sections.text:
- Starscourge Radahn's model is internally labeled as "RadahnAndLeonard."
- Leonard is hidden underground directly below the player when Radahn uses his meteorite attack. Leonard remains below the player to ensure Radahn does not miss. He phases through the ground during the explosion and Radahn rides him once more.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Lanya** is a character in Elden Ring. She is a servant of House Hoslow and childhood companion of Diallos Hoslow.

Described by Diallos as being "fickle as the wind," she has a habit of running off to unknown places, frequently requiring him to search for her whereabouts.

She would eventually meet her fate in the middle of one of her disappearances, having been murdered by an unspecified Recusant of Volcano Manor, and her body was left in a pool of blood at the northern edge of Academy Gate Town. This act that would put Diallos on a path of revenge; however, true to his nature, he was unable to commit to the act in the end, instead joining the Recusants himself as a prospective champion. He would still feel pain and sadness over Lanya's death, calling it cruel and unfortunate, but believed they were both simply laid hard roads by fate.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text:
Lanya has a slender figure and mild orange skin with faintly visible freckles covering her cheeks. Her eyes are light blue. She has messy, orange-blonde hair that reaches down to her shoulders, with some covering her left eye and some tied into a small ponytail at the top of her head.

She wears the Chain Armor, Chain Gauntlets and Chain Leggings.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

sections.text:
The Land of the Tower consists much of the northeastern Realm of Shadow. It was once the center of population for the Hornsent culture, though after Marika's crusade and Messmer's burning, much of the land was abandoned. The divine tower of Enir-Ilim is shrouded in shadow, and the tower settlement of Belurat rests on its southern base near the Gravesite Plain. Beyond the canyon carved from the Ellac River, the Ancient Ruins of Rauh stand overgrown with greenery and nature unbound.

The land of the tower is the home of the Crucible. The spiral is an oft-discussed topic in this region.
