sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Lord of Frenzied Flame** (狂い火の王, *Kurui Hi no Ō*), also known as the **Lord of Chaos** (混沌の王, *Konton no Ō*), is a status and title in the world of Elden Ring. It refers to the prophesied, messiah-like figure of the Frenzied Flame and its ailing followers. Promising them salvation from their torment, despair, their affliction, every sin, and every curse by melting it all away.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A chosen few of those afflicted with the flame of frenzy are capable of transforming into the Lord after an apparent death, or a process of rebirth, it's not clear and it's left to speculation. The strength of its form can seemingly vary depending on its original host, with several having proven capable of becoming one. However, many of them were either too weak-willed or physically feeble to accomplish anything, causing them to be considered frauds and failures in the eyes of their followers.

Similar to the power of its namesake, it has an uncanny ability to erase the original identity of its vessel. However, in the case of the Tarnished, it's unclear whether his identity is truly erased. Given his ability to subdue demigods and gods like the Elden Beast, it is plausible that he did not succumb to the Flame, but instead mastered it—fusing with it rather than being consumed. It can apparently emerge from its host even if they don't want it to and could even prompt them to abruptly die at a moment's notice to force their transformation into itself. Either way, the constraints of the transformation are left open to interpretation within the lore.

Once a Lord of Frenzied Flame manifests, the head of the original host is replaced by a black hole with yellow flames spewing out of its core, apparently erasing any visible trace of the original host's identity. In the case of Midra, it moves his body around with mannerisms completely alien to not only the original host but even other chaos followers as well. Making gestures that suggest complete delight and overwhelming euphoria at the sight of its flames consuming everything in its path. An ironic contrast for something supposedly being born from unspeakable torment and despair. However, since Midra is regarded as a failed Lord, that might not fully apply to the Tarnished, or it may manifest differently—yet still in a similar way to Midra or other candidates, should they possess a stronger will.

While it is seen as a savior from the perspective of those stricken by madness, it is a harbinger of insanity and death to everyone else. A menace to all life and the joys of living.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Though this is a dagger it counts as a Thrusting Sword when dual-wielding, meaning that except for another copy of itself it cannot be dual-wielded with another dagger.
  - Uses the Thrusting Sword dual-wielding moveset if paired with itself.
  - Keep in mind that the second dual wield attack will only use the right-hand weapon, and hits 3 times.
  - Does more than a dagger usually would when dual-wielded, but not enough to truly compete with an actual Thrusting Sword.

- Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Miséricorde, and the Scorpion's Stinger.
- Compared to a Thrusting Sword with Parry equipped, this dagger will have the same amount of start-up frames and takes the same amount of time to complete but with twice as many active parry frames, with a slightly shorter recovery time to compensate.
  - Since only the Rapier and Rogier's Rapier have increased Critical Attack damage (130 and 110 respectively), having this weapon in the off-hand to another Thrusting Sword to then two-hand upon making an enemy vulnerable to a such an attack might increase such damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Lord of Frenzied Flame** is one of the possible endings in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending is the legacy of Shabriri, Finger Maiden Hyetta, and the Three Fingers. As the Lord of Frenzied Flame, the player shall burn away all that divides and distinguishes, allowing chaos to take the world.

**Warning**: Progressing the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending locks the player out of other endings and causes Melina to cut ties with the player, vowing to kill them. The player can change to a different ending by inserting Miquella's Needle at storm beyond time; however, this action cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.text:
The "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending is achieved by inheriting the Frenzied Flame from the Three Fingers at the Frenzied Flame Proscription and finishing the game at Fractured Marika without using Miquella's Needle at Crumbling Farum Azula.

The smoldering stone door at the Frenzied Flame Proscription can be opened after the player unequips all Armor. Opening it initiates a cutscene in which the Three Fingers bestow the power of Frenzied Flame. Interacting with the Three Fingers causes Melina to leave permanently, vowing to kill the player Tarnished. However, the player can bypass her sacrifice by using the Fingers' flame as kindling to awaken the Flame of Ruin at the Forge of the Giants and commit the Cardinal Sin. The player can still meet the Three Fingers if they have already used Melina to burn the Erdtree. The Three Fingers do not clasp the player again if they cheat fate by inserting Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time.

If her questline has been advanced, Finger Maiden Hyetta will wait patiently on the side of the hall opposite the Site of Grace. She urges the Tarnished to seek an audience with the Three Fingers, whose sanctum lies beyond a large stone door that was partially melted by searing fingerprints. The door may only be opened once and only after unequipping all armor. After receiving the Flame of Frenzy, speak with Hyetta, who can then interpret the words of the Fingers to their chosen Lord of Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The "Lord of the Frenzied Flame" ending will unlock the Lord of Frenzied Flame achievement.
- Meeting Lightseeker Hyetta and completing her questline are optional steps for getting the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending. Her questline can still be started after interacting with the Three Fingers, though it proceeds as if the player has not yet received the Frenzied Flame. Choosing to "**Touch Hyetta**" on the forehead enables her to touch the words of the Fingers, incinerating her eyes. She relays them to the player and is then burned away by Frenzied Flame, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal.
- If the player spares Melina and selects the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending, Melina's left eye unseals and she gains power over Destined Death, vowing to stop the player in a secret cutscene. If the player sacrifices Melina before meeting the Three Fingers, however, they shall melt away all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Lampreys** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The lampreys are eel-like humanoids distinguished by their eight eyes, circular jaws, and diminutive legs. They hunt using Glinting Nails and are the progenitors of the Finger Sorceries practiced by the finger-weavers. These enigmatic creatures can slip into white wormholes, enabling them to quickly teleport around the Finger Ruins they safeguard. Pearlescent Scales, a key component of Fingerprint Nostrum, grow inward deep within their skin. Some use this dubious form of esoteric medicine to transform their bodies into fingers, becoming lampreys instead.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.text:
Lampreys are either black or pale in appearance. All variants are gaunt, elongated figures with smooth, slippery skin. Dorsal and caudal fins line their long tails, which they use to prop themselves upright in a curved posture. Their drooped faces bear four sets of forward-facing, human-like eyes. They have five fingers on their large hands, but three digits on their vestigial feet. Strips of what appear to be shed skin or textile loosely cling to their lower body.

There are three variants of this enemy: Black Lamprey, White Lamprey, and Giant Lamprey.

; Black Lamprey

The black lampreys are the standard variant of this enemy type.

; White Lamprey
The pinkish-white lampreys dwell in the foggy Finger Ruins of Dheo. These individuals have additional attacks that deal Poison damage. They appear to vomit a mixture of blood, bile, and worms when fighting at short range.

; Giant Lamprey
The largest lampreys are vigilant sentries that cast binding magic from afar. These creatures act as stationary turrets, maintaining their position and refusing to pursue distant targets that move out of their line of site. However, they are more active when fighting nearby targets.

Giant lampreys conjure explosive purple spheres and hurl them at their targets. Upon detonation, the blast stuns the victim with concentric purple rings for a few seconds. If their target is stunned by their Finger Snare attack, one nearby lamprey will teleport in to perform a grab attack.

sections.text: **Merchant Kalé** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Kalé is a member of a tribe of Nomadic Merchants, scions of the Great Caravan who were spurned by Grace long ago. His ancestors were immured beneath the royal capital. Kalé is acquainted with Blaidd the Half-Wolf, considering him to be a good person despite being boorish.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Merchant Kalé is a nomadic merchant who has set up shop at the Church of Elleh in Limgrave, located north of the  The First Step site of grace. He is the first merchant many players are likely to encounter, and is the only merchant who sells the Crafting Kit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

- May mount his Mule during combat
- Merchant Kalé and his Mule fall asleep when Renna the Witch visits the Church of Elleh.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **RedEyeGypsy**
- Merchant Kalé was among the earliest characters added to the game and has a substantial amount of cut content. Although he underwent multiple iterations before release, his personality, mannerisms, and association with Frenzied Flame were established from the start.

sections.heading: Great Caravan
sections.text:
- Merchant Kalé had a full questline in which he actively searched for the lost Great Caravan. After acquiring the Burial Crow's Letter, his journey would have brought him to the Frenzied Flame Proscription, where he expressed tremendous anger toward the people of the Erdtree for what they did to his ancestors. Kalé then attempted to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame, but failed and was burned by the Three Fingers.
  - This questline may have been replaced or cut to avoid conflict with Lightseeker Hyetta's questline, as both arrived at the Frenzied Flame Proscription after directing the player to seek the Three Fingers.

sections.heading: Cursed Red Eyes
sections.text:
- In his earliest known draft, Kalé and the Nomadic Merchants were conceived as a single being divided into many bodies. They bore the cursed red eyes, an early version of the Frenzied Flame that threatened to blend them back together.
  - This version of Kalé and his brothers actively rode their mules and roamed the map, much like the Great Coffins pulled by Trolls.
  - The brothers were telepathically linked and dreamed together, but yearned to extinguish the flame and separate.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Melina** is a deuteragonist character in Elden Ring. She is a mysterious, spectral woman who offers an alliance with the Tarnished to help them on their journey to become Elden Lord. She may only be encountered when resting at specific Sites of Grace, though she may be summoned to help fight Morgott, the Omen King at the Elden Throne.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Melina has long observed the Lands Between. She was born at the foot of the Erdtree. She is a secret child of Queen Marika. Unlike Messmer or Morgott, Melina does not recall Marika with fondness.

At some point long ago, Melina bore a vision of fire. She was burned, leaving her bodiless; a drifting spirit bound to Grace.. Like her brother Messmer, she was assigned a purpose by Marika. However, she was unable to remember it. And so, Melina traveled with the spectral steed Torrent in search of the Tarnished who would lead her back to the foot of the Erdtree. There, she may ascertain her given purpose.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
Torrent identifies and selects a maidenless Tarnished, who recently washed up in the Stranded Graveyard, as one capable of brandishing the Elden Ring. Melina descends the spectral steed to grant the fallen champion a set of Sacred Flasks, choosing to aid them in violation of the Golden Order.

Sometime later, Melina approaches the Tarnished to offer them an accord: She could play the role of the missing Finger Maiden in return for a ride to the foot of the Erdtree. If the player desires the strength of runes, and, if they accept the accord, Melina entrusts them with the Spectral Steed Whistle and, therefore, Torrent. Melina advises them to follow the guidance of Grace and seek the shardbearer at Stormveil Castle.

Once the Tarnished defeats the demigod, Melina confesses that she was testing the Tarnished to see if they truly possessed the guidance of grace and if they were fit for the challenges to come. Satisfied with her new companion, Melina offers to take them to Roundtable Hold, a gathering place for Tarnished champions.

Throughout their journey, Melina also provides specks of guidance at certain sites of grace and, at churches dedicated to Queen Marika, she offers to reveal words spoken by Marika herself in the distant past.

sections.heading: Leyndell, Royal Capital
sections.text:
Upon arriving at their destination, the Royal Capital at the foot of the Erdtree, Melina thanks the Tarnished for escorting her and leaves to ascertain her purpose, claiming that she can govern her movement more freely there. She entrusts the power of runes and Torrent to the Tarnished. She will also offer her aid should the Tarnished challenge Morgott, the Omen King, ruler of Leyndell and guardian of the Erdtree.

After defeating Morgott, the Tarnished finds the path into the Erdtree barred by impenetrable thorns refusing entrance to all. Melina, having ascertained her purpose and seeing the Tarnished stuck, rejoins the Tarnished to say that she can burn the Erdtree to gain entrance inside, provided that she can get ahold of the Giants' Flame. And hence, she asks to go on a new journey, this time to the flame of ruin, far above the clouds, upon the snowy Mountaintops of the Giants. and tells them she will take care of the "kindling" required to set the tree alight.

Defeating Morgott also unseals a path to the Three Fingers. If the Tarnished rests at the nearest grace from their entombment, Melina will warn against meeting them and insist against inheriting the Frenzied Flame, for it would end all lives and births, which she cherishes. If the Tarnished heeds her warning, Melina and the protagonist will continue their journey for the flame of ruin.

sections.heading: Cardinal Sin
sections.text: When making their way to the Forge of the Giants, Melina clarifies that she is now acting of her own volition, regardless of the purpose that her mother gave her. After defeating the guardian of the flame, Melina puts her plan into action. She takes the Tarnished's hand, narcotizing them by doing so, and proceeds to sacrifice herself to channel the flame of ruin, setting the Erdtree aflame. The Tarnished, maidenless once more, wakes up at Crumbling Farum Azula. There, they must confront the Black Blade Maliketh and recover the Rune of Death. In this, Melina fulfills her purpose: *"The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death."*

sections.heading: Destined Death
sections.text:
If the player ignores her warnings at the  Frenzied Flame Proscription, or just inherits the Frenzied Flame without speaking with her, she will say that The Tarnished is no longer fit, ending her accord, and forever leaving their side but threatening to kill them should they become the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

If Melina did not fulfil her purpose as Kindling Maiden, an additional cutscene will play after the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending. At the Stone Platform, a chorus of whistling guides a transformed Melina to the Spectral Steed Whistle. She retrieves the smoldering ring from a pile of ash and holds it in her open palm. As Torrent's final remnants are consumed by the Frenzied Flame, Melina reveals her unsealed left eye and vows vengeance upon the player in the form of Destined Death.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.text:
Melina's questline runs parallel to the main story and is required to complete the game. It has two possible outcomes.
1. Stranded Graveyard
  - After fighting the Grafted Scion at the Chapel of Anticipation, Melina and Torrent appear during a cutscene. Melina grants the Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears before departing.
1. Sites of Grace (Limgrave)
  - After leaving the Stranded Graveyard, activate and rest at either the  Agheel Lake North or  Gatefront Ruins Sites of Grace. A cutscene will play and Melina will offer an accord.
    - Alternatively, activate at any two Sites of Grace in the overworld and then rest at one of the following eight Sites of Grace:  Agheel Lake North, Agheel Lake South, Bridge of Sacrifice, Church of Elleh, Gatefront Ruins, Seaside Ruins, Stormhill Shack, or Third Church of Marika.
  - *(Optional)* If you refuse her accord, you cannot enter Leyndell, Royal Capital, even with two Great Runes. You can reconsider at any time by selecting "Talk to Melina" at any Site of Grace.
  - Accepting grants the Spectral Steed Whistle, allowing you to summon Torrent.
1. *(Optional)* Sites of Grace
  - Melina may appear when you rest at any Site of Grace, offering the dialogue options "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal".
    - **Note**: these options will no longer be available once you progress to the next step.
  - Melina offers to share the words of Queen Marika when the player rests at one of the following Sites of Grace:  Church of Pilgrimage, First Church of Marika, Grand Lift of Dectus, Minor Erdtree Church, Outer Wall Battleground, Queen's Bedchamber, and Third Church of Marika. Select "Talk to Melina" and accept to hear them.
1. Sites of Grace
  - Rest at any Site of Grace outside Limgrave or fight Margit, the Fell Omen at least once to trigger another conversation in which Melina extends an invitation to the Roundtable Hold. Accepting this invite is mandatory for accessing Leyndell, Royal Capital later in the game.
1. *(Optional)* Sites of Grace
  - After progressing Boc the Seamster's questline, Melina may appear to discuss him.
    - If Boc moves to the  East Raya Lucaria Gate, Melina will appear there to ask about him.
    - If Boc moves to the  Altus Highway Junction, Melina will appear there to ask about him again.
1. *(Optional)* Sites of Grace (Altus Plateau or Capital Outskirts)
  - Speak to Melina at any Site of Grace on the Altus Plateau or in the Capital Outskirts. This step is missed if the player enters Leyndell, Royal Capital.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital
  - Resting at a Site of Grace in Leyndell will trigger another interaction with Melina, after which she will leave you. Her dialogue options at various Sites of Grace will be temporarily unavailable.
  - Defeat Morgott, the Omen King.
    - *(Optional)* Melina may be summoned as a cooperator by activating her summon sign outside Morgott's boss room.
  - Approach the entrance to the Erdtree, turn back, and rest at the  Elden Throne Site of Grace. Melina will appear and, after some dialogue, give you the Rold Medallion.
1. *(Ending A)* Mountaintops of the Giants
  - After defeating the Fire Giant and resting at the  Forge of the Giants, you may talk to Melina. Speak to her and respond "I'm Ready" to commit the cardinal sin. Melina awakens the Giants' Flame, becomes its kindling, and burns the Erdtree. The player collapses and awakens in Crumbling Farum Azula.
    - **Note**: this ends Melina's questline, as her spirit . You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.
1. *(Ending B)* Frenzied Flame Proscription
  - Visit the Frenzied Flame Proscription and interact with the Three Fingers. Melina will appear at the next Site of Grace you rest at and will leave you permanently.
    - **Note**: this action cannot be reversed by using Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows or inserting Miquella's Needle at  Dragonlord Placidusax. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Melina uses the Black Knife Assassin animation set.
- Attacks that produce lingering hazards can hit Melina when she sits at a Site of Grace, even applying Status Effects.
- Melina is a child of Marika and has access to her most secret incantation.
  - This incantation will also be automatically cast when she dies, even as a cooperator, the only way to see this in-game without modding.
- Melina can be summoned to help fight against Morgott.
  - Melina wields the Blade of Calling, which is golden flame counterpart to the Black Knife. Additionally, she uses two unplayable incantations that resemble the effects of Minor Erdtree and Miranda's Prayer.
- Melina is not a Finger Maiden.
- Melina is aware her agency will be restored if the Erdtree is destroyed.
- If the player spares Melina and chooses the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending, she will be transformed after Marika and the Erdtree are destroyed.
  - Melina's purpose remains the same, but its context becomes flipped: *"The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death."*

sections.heading: Speculation
sections.text:
- It is implied that Melina is another child of Radagon and Marika:
  - **Naming Convention**: Most siblings in the Lands Between share the first letter of their name. Messmer/Melina/Miquella/Malenia would be no exception to this rule.
  - **Hair Color**: Melina's hair color seems to be a combination of Radagon and Marika's hair colors.
  - **Butterflies**: There are four butterfly items in-game, each representing a cursed demigod: Nascent Butterfly (Miquella), Aeonian Butterfly (Malenia), Black Pyrefly (Messmer), Smoldering Butterfly (Melina).
  - Messmer had a younger sister who also bore a vision of fire and, like Melina, he possessed the kindling to burn the Erdtree It is unknown when in the timeline Melina was born exactly, but she knew Marika's secret incantation and Messmer was the older brother of Radahn.
  - The soundtrack for Messmer's boss fight shares a leitmotif with Radagon's boss theme.
- Melina has an implied connection to the Gloam-Eyed Queen as she reveals her eye with a violet iris and inherits the power of Destined Death should the player spare her by using the Frenzied Flame as kindling.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Melina is internally named "**MaricaOfDaughter**" (ID: 2180).
- There are several lines of Melina's dialogue that can be heard in pre-launch game trailers that end up not being used in the main game. Whether they were envisioned as Melina's own words or spoken echoes of Queen Marika is not known.
  1. *The Tarnished will soon return ... guided by grace once lost.*
  1. *The Golden Order is broken to its core.*
  1. *They will fight. And they will die. In an unending curse.*
  1. *For how else is champion, or a lord, to be born?*
  1. *Brandish the Elden Ring ... for all of us.*

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: Within the lands of Elden Ring are scattered various important elements the player should make themselves aware of.

sections.heading: Runes
sections.text: Runes can be obtained by defeating enemies or using items. Runes are used to level up your character's Stats and Attributes, buy items, and strengthen weapons and armor.

sections.heading: Site of Grace
sections.text:
There are rest points called Sites of Grace.

Resting at a Site of Grace will restore your HP, FP, and heal any status ailments. It will also refill all of your Sacred Flasks. Most of the enemies you have defeated will be revived when you rest at a Site of Grace.

sections.heading: How to use a Site of Grace
sections.text:
Approach the Site of Grace and press the [△/Y] button to activate it.
From here, pressing the [△/Y] button will bring up the menu and let you rest.
Sites of Grace that you have not reached yet emit rays of light.

sections.heading: Site of Grace menu
sections.text:
The Site of Grace menu is available while resting.
The selections available will change as the story progresses.
:{| class="article-table"
|Pass Time||Move time forward in the game.
|-
|Level Up||Enhance your character’s stats.
|-
|Add Charge to Flask||Increase the number of times you can use the flask.
|-
|Increase Amount Replenished by Flasks||Enhance the flask’s restorative effect.
|-
|Distribute Flask Charges||Allocate the number of charges for your sacred flasks.
|-
| Memorize Spell||Equip magic you have learned in the memory slots to use it in the game. The number of slots available depends on your character’s status.
|-
|Mix Wondrous Physick||Mix acquired Crystal Tears to customize the effects of Flask of Wondrous Physick.
|-
|Sort Chest||Store items in or remove items from the chest.
|}

Sites of Grace that you already discovered will be saved on the map. Select the Site of Grace you want to travel to on the map, and you will move to that location. You cannot travel while in some dungeons.

sections.heading: Guidance of Grace
sections.text:
The light emanating from some Sites of Grace gives a hint as to where you may want to go next.

The Guidance of Grace can also be found in the map menu.

sections.heading: Summoning
sections.text:
When a rebirth monument is nearby and a monument icon is shown on the left side of the screen, you can use ashes to summon a spirit.

The summoned spirit will leave when its HP reaches zero, when a boss is defeated, when the spirit moves a certain distance away from the monument, or when the same ashes are used again.

Only one type of spirit can be summoned at a time, and spirits cannot be summoned during multiplayer.

sections.heading: Stakes of Marika
sections.text:
Upon dying, you will be revived at the last Site of Grace at which you rested. However, if you died near a Stake of Marika, you can choose to be revived there instead.

You can confirm if you are in the area of effect of a Stake of Marika by checking if the status icon (bow and arrow icon) appears.

sections.heading: Spectral Steed
sections.text:
Use the Spectral Steed Whistle to summon a Spectral Steed to ride.

If the Spectral Steed dies it can be summoned again, but it will consume a Flask of Crimson Tears.

sections.heading: Map
sections.text:
You can see your current location, terrain, buildings, and other information. Markers and landmarks can be placed on the map.

You can also go to a Site of Grace that you have discovered from the map menu.

You cannot open the map when you are engaged in battle.

sections.heading: Birdseye Telescope
sections.text: Use the Birdseye Telescopes in each area to see into the distance like a bird and get a better view of your destination.

sections.heading: Death
sections.text:
A character dies when their HP reaches zero.

When you die, all the runes you are carrying will be dropped. You can retrieve them by going back to the location of your death. If you die again before retrieving them, they will be lost.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Madding Hand was branded a heretic by the Hornsent and hunted by their Inquisitors for his belief in the Frenzied Flame. His unyielding desire for revenge drove him to craft his signature Madding Hand from flayed skin. He wears the Prophet Blindfold, Gravebird's Blackquill Armor, Gravebird Bracelets, and Gravebird Anklets.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Lord of Night**, also known as the **Nightlord** and **Night Lord**, is a title in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Long ago, the Nox people of the Eternal Cities committed a grave sin against the Greater Will and were subsequently banished underground. They awaited the coming of a Lord of Night who would usher in an Age of the Stars. The Tarnished becomes the Lord of Night if they choose to facilitate the ascension of Ranni the Witch and her Dark Moon in the Age of the Stars ending.

sections.heading: Nightreign
sections.text: - In Elden Ring Nightreign, Heolstor the Nightlord became a Lord of Night, and threatens Limveld.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - "Lord of Night" and "Nightlord" are spelled the same way in Japanese.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Limveld** is a region in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Limveld exists within the same universe as the Lands Between and shares a Roundtable Hold. It is the setting for *Elden Ring Nightreign*, which occurs in parallel to the events of Elden Ring after diverging during or after the Shattering.

Limveld is influenced by the power of Runes and is home to colossal shadow giants and various Sites of Grace. It is currently under the rule of the Night Lord and threatened by the encroaching Night's Tide. A maiden enlists the Nightfarers to save the land from its impending doom.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Liurnian Civil War** was a event mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A civil war between the Carian royal family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria broke out across Liurnia of the Lakes. It was the third and final major conflict in Liurnia, long after the First and Second Liurnian Wars with the people of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Prelude
sections.text:
After Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon left his wife Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon to become the second husband and King Consort of Queen Marika the Eternal. When Radagon departed and became second Elden Lord, Rennala's heart went with him, leaving her a grieving wreck. After Rennala's breakdown, the Academy realized that their queen did not have the unwavering strength of a true champion. With the Carian matriarch no longer in a state to oppose them, the Academy seized the opportunity to rebel against the Carian Royal Family and locked Rennala away in their Grand Library.

Rennala's weakened leadership was not the cause of the Academy's rebellion, merely the opportunity to do so. Their actual motive was a long-held resentment for the restriction of Primeval Current study enforced when Rennala became governor of the Academy.  The Primeval Current is the origin of glintstone and the power behind all glintstone sorcey derived from the material. Exposing one's mind too deep into the Primeval Current's depths was a highly dangerous practice that had claimed the sanity of all sorcerers that did so. Rennala believed it was too risky and took steps to limit the practice during her appointment. However, the prevailing sentiment within the ambitious Academy did not agree. By overthrowing the Carians, they hoped to restore their once unabated research.

To aid in their insurrection, the Academy called upon their private army, the Knights of the Cuckoo. The Cuckoo were a group of mercenaries who had served a lucrative, longstanding contract defending the Academy's interests. Their symbol is a Cuckoo bird, its shrewd gaze representing their refusal to be mere servants of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. As part of their contract with the Academy, they were given free rein to wage war as they pleased, gaining an infamous reputation for their rapacious ways as a result. Another clause within their contract allowed them access to "faux sorceries", lesser, martial-focused, spells taught by the Academy. They loathed Albinaurics and found ways to weaponize their silver blood.

Meanwhile the Carians had long anticipated the Academy's eventual betrayal, and secretly prepared their forces for when the time would come. Firstly, they developed sorceries and battle arts that could absorb incoming spells, and reform their energy into glintblades to then be used against the caster. Secondly, the shields of the Carian Knights were specially made for defense against magical attacks.

sections.heading: Civil War
sections.text:
A major battle took place along the road north of the Liurnia Highway North Site of Grace, with the destroyed remains of Cuckoo Flame Chariots littering the roadside.

By some means, the Carian Knight, Moongrum, was able to take a defensive position at the lift that led to the Library, stopping any further harm coming to his queen.

sections.heading: The Siege of Caria Manor
sections.text:
The Siege of Caria Manor marked the end of the Cuckoos' offense into Caria. A magic snare resulted in a total Carian victory. Captured Cuckoos consumed Seluvis's Potion, and were enthralled as living puppets.

The Cuckoos withdrew, but the Carians never recovered. Though Ranni the Witch returned to the Manor following the conflict, her house was already ousted.

sections.text: **Man-Flies** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Man-Flies are insectoid humans, blindfolded and wrapped in soiled linens. These gregarious creatures thrive among filth, commonly inhabiting the squalid cisterns and sewers of the Realm of Shadow. Their backs bear large, veined insect wings while their lower bodies have transformed into elongated abdomens, protected by a hardened tergum. They often crawl on all six limbs, but can hover just above the ground by buzzing their translucent wings.

Man-Flies deal  Standard damage and are weakest to  Fire damage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Man-flies were once hornsent who were afflicted with the dreadful fly sickness. Many sick were tossed from the wooden platform at the Abandoned Ailing Village into the depths. Their bodies have accumulated into a large mound in the Ellac River down below. It is said they were freed from their suffering as the metamorphosis took hold, and that those who cared for them were unaffected.

A hornsent moldmonger cultivated the flesh and blood of man-flies into a Fly Mold that could be used for making Jar Dwellers.

sections.text:

sections.heading: Notes

- Man-Flies cannot attack while in flight.
- Man-Fly Spitters lack melee attacks.
- Man-Fly Ashes is a Spirit Ash that summons two Man-Flies and one Man-Fly Spitter.
- Man-Flies shed their exoskeletons as they grow larger. Many of these discarded shells litter areas where Man-Flies are common.
  - Large shed exoskeletons can be found but no Man-Fly in the game is big enough to have left them.
- The Ailment Talisman is found at the Abandoned Ailing Village on the wooden platform from which bodies were dumped.
- A Man-Fly in a shack at the Abandoned Ailing Village prays to a pile of corpses containing the [[Greater Potentate's Cookbook 10|Greater Potentate's Cookbook [10]]], which unlocks Hefty Fly Pot.
- Shadow Undead at the Abandoned Ailing Village cast Swarm of Flies, an incantation associated with the Formless Mother.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Liurnian Wars** were a series of events mentioned in Elden Ring. There were two wars between Caria and the Academy and the Golden Order, culminating in the marriage of Rennala and Radagon.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: After the end of the Erdtree's Age of Plenty, the Carian royal family and their allies at the Academy of Raya Lucaria anticipated conflict with the Erdtree. The Carian Knights thus steeled themselves for eventual battle against Marika's holy golden forces.

sections.heading: First Liurnian War
sections.text: A mighty champion with flowing red locks, Radagon of the Golden Order joined the heroes' ranks when he invaded Liurnia at the head of a great golden host, and clashed against the enchanted forces of the Rennala, the Full Moon Witch. Although the Grace of Gold empowered his forces, the Knights of Caria were their equal match. Although both sides achieved glory, the war ended inconclusively; neither emerged as the victor.

sections.heading: Second Liurnian War
sections.text: Radagon returned to do battle with Rennala once more and was again evenly matched. He eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, and swore his love to Rennala. He became the husband of the Carian Queen, wedding her at the Church of Vows. Rennala bequeathed him a greatsword, bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse to honor long-standing tradition.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.text:
- Peace between Altus and Liurnia. Marriage between Rennala, Queen of Liurnia, and Radagon, Prince of the Erdtree. Houses of the Moon and the Erdtree conjoined.
- Liurnia assimilated into the Golden Order. Radagon accesses Raya Lucaria's knowledge.
- After joining the Carian line, he ordered the Carian magic preceptors to don masks of confidence, to make it clear that all of their matters were to be kept strictly private.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Libra, Creature of Night** (夜の魔、リブラ, *Yoru no Ma, Ribura*), also known as **Equilibrius Beast** (調律の魔物, *Chouritsu no Mamono*), is a Night Lord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Libra is a capricious, goat-headed demon obsessed with equality and fairness. He disguises himself as a Scale-Bearing Merchant and offers a deal before the fight. He offers three deals, pulled from a randomized pool. Each deal is a Monkey's Paw wish: it provides a powerful buff, but comes at a great cost. Players may decline to bargain or simply attack Libra outright.

- Libra deals  Physical and  Holy damage, and inflicts  Madness buildup.
- He uses the Crossed Legs gesture to inflict  Madness. He is shielded by a golden sphere when he meditates in this way. The barrier can be shattered through force or by destroying the nearby sigils.
  - If the orb is shattered, he loses control and rampages like a beast.
  - If he finishes channeling, he enters a more composed state.
- Its attacks sometimes generate tiny false-gold pieces. Collect them to reduce  Madness buildup.
- When it uses the chanting attack that makes a goat eye icon appear over the Nightfarers, prioritize collecting the yellow embers to avoid the incoming Frenzy proc.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Damage Types
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (  ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Equilibrious Beast Expedition.
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- When Libra starts pummeling the ground and summoning a Madness aura, run around and collect as many false-gold pieces around the arena as you can. Each one heals you a bit but most importantly, alleviates Madness buildup.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **Baphomet**.
- His connection to dubious alchemy and counterfeit gold are likely a play on the fact that the Japanese word for western alchemy, 錬金術 (*Renkinjutsu*, lit. the art of refining gold) refers in modern parlance to hucksters making money through unethical means and scams.
- He wields his staff in his left hand. Making him the next unique left-handed character that Fromsoft puts in their games. There’s always at least one in each installment. That is, Iron Golem in Dark Souls 1, Fume Knight and Throne Watcher in Dark Souls 2, Old Demon King and Dancer of the Boreal Valley in Dark Souls 3, Ludwig in Bloodborne, and Messmer in Elden Ring. Artorias was also rumored to be left-handed, before his arm was shattered.
- His name, Libra, is the same as a star sign in Astrology. Its unique symbol is that of a balance/scale, and its gemstone is an Opal. Its most prominent traits are that of Balance, Diplomacy, Charm, Intelligence, and Fairness.
- Libra is referred to as a *Demon* (悪魔, *Akuma*), making him the first of his kind in the Elden Ring universe.
  - The demons of the Demon's Souls and Dark Souls universes are known as デモン (*Demon*) in the Japanese script, a simple transcription of the English word Demon, while Libra uses 悪魔 (*Akuma*), a Japanese word which refers to demons such as the buddhist Mara and Christian devil, tying into its links to Baphomet, a medieval Christian garbling of the name of the Islamic prophet, which was later attached to Éliphas Lévi's Sabbatic Goat, an iconic depiction of a goat-headed figure which formed the basis for Libra's design.
  - Libra's title in Japanese (夜の魔) directly calls him "Demon of Night".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Maliketh, the Black Blade** is a Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The ruined sanctum atop Crumbling Farum Azula is the boss arena for the Beast Clergyman and Maliketh, the Black Blade—Queen Marika's feared shadowbound beast. An ancient shrine for Beastmen, it contains statues of a hallowed scene: three wolves attend to a young Empyrean, kneeling in prayer, beneath the glowing depiction of a primordial Elden Ring. Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is its caretaker.

Defeating Maliketh unbinds the Rune of Death, also known as Destined Death, and finalizes the Cardinal Sin, unsealing the Erdtree by burning away its impenetrable thorns with black flame.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
The  Maliketh, the Black Blade site of grace is located in Crumbling Farum Azula. It can be reached by traveling southeast from the  Beside the Great Bridge site of grace and climbing the ramp to the top, though the road is protected by a Draconic Tree Sentinel.

The site of grace appears inside the structure after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.

sections.text:
- The area features pillars with the mummies of immured lupine beastmen. Much of its crumbling architecture floats as if frozen in time.
- The young girl in the scene is presumed to be the first vessel for the Elden Ring and the God of Placidusax, confirming the old legends that claimed wolves were the first shadowbound Beasts. The statues have long muzzles like Red Wolves who serve Radagon, though they most resembled Azula Beastmen in their concept art.
- The old Elden Ring strongly resembles the root-like tail of the Elden Beast.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Miséricorde** is a dagger found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found behind a fog wall that requires 1 Stonesword Key to open, near the roaming Grafted Scion inside Stormveil Castle and the elevator shortcut back up to the Rampart Tower Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Has the highest critical multiplier in the game, at 140.
- Generally average or above average damage depending on the affinity used, but always the strongest dagger for Critical Attacks such as backstabbing or riposting. As such it's useful as a secondary weapon to be pulled out quickly, even when a build isn't focused on daggers.
  - Deals damage equivalent to a Colossal Weapon, for comparison.
  - This damage is strong enough that a riposte with a Fire affinity Miséricorde can oftentimes overwhelm the flat defences that often hold back split damage weapons, dealing strong damage (doesn't work as well on backstabs since the damage multiplier for them is lower).
- While it technically leans towards Dexterity it actually performs about as well on the Heavy affinity as the Keen affinity, technically better due to most daggers not working as well with Strength.
  - Actually the strongest pure Dexterity dagger with the Cold affinity and the strongest dagger period on the Occult affinity, but lacks the support of other Status Effects that other daggers such as the Bloodstained Dagger and Great Knife have.
  - Despite the general Dexterity tendency its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Main-gauche, and the Scorpion's Stinger.
- Somewhat stronger on lower stats than other daggers due to its higher base damage but lower scaling.
- The longest of all daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
  - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

Standard=

sections.text:
- The name of this dagger is French for "mercy", signifying its use for giving the death stroke to heavily wounded knights, an "act of mercy".
  - "Dagger of Mercy" is a literal translation of the Japanese name.
- This weapon was popular among speedrunners before the heavy nerf to the Stance damage of Flame of the Redmanes (from 40 to 10), due to the power of its critical hits.

It immediately assumes the form of the player as they enter the room, complete with their equipped weapons, armor, and spells. Its Stats and Attributes, such as HP, shall also reflect the player's.

The Mimic Tear is encountered at Nokron, Eternal City, in the ruins of a colossal temple built by the Ancient Dynasty. The nearest site of grace is  Nokron, Eternal City; however, this area can only be reached via the Starfall Crater in western Limgrave, which appears after defeating Starscourge Radahn in the Wailing Dunes.

The  Mimic Tear site of grace appears in the arena after the player defeats the Mimic Tear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Morgott, the Omen King,** is a remembrance boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Leyndell, Royal Capital. He is **not** an optional boss and must be defeated to unlock Mountaintops of the Giants and progress the story.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Morgott was a direct offspring of Lord Godfrey and Queen Marika, and the rightful heir to their Golden Lineage. Despite his royal pedigree, he and his twin brother, Mohg, were born with accursed blood that caused tangled horns to sprout from their infant bodies. Once revered as divine aspect of the Crucible, these growths branded them as Omen spurned by the Erdtree and excluded from its grace. Though spared the painful excision of their horns, they were nonetheless banished to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital. A Regal Omen Bairn was made in secret to honor Morgott in a long-standing tradition.

Unlike his twin, Morgott's devotion to the Erdtree never wavered. He renounced his omen blood, extracted a portion of it, and sealed it away. The blood that formed Morgott's Cursed Sword caused it to shimmer in shifting hues, and so he encased it in stone and wielded it like a cane. Several horns were removed from his brow line.

sections.heading: The Shattering
Game events
sections.text:
When the Tarnished returned, Morgott and his Night's Cavalry hunted them throughout the realm. Morgott first encounters the Tarnished at Stormgate, where he tests their mettle as Margit before allowing them to challenge Godrick for his Great Rune. Later, he ambushes the hero again by disguising a commoner as himself in the war-torn Capital Outskirts.

The Tarnished gains entrance to Leyndell, Royal Capital and challenges Morgott at the Elden Throne after claiming two shards of the Elden Ring. Denouncing the Tarnished and his siblings as willful traitors, Morgott launches his assault. As he falters during the battle, he unleashes his sealed curse to aid him, though he feels unbearable shame in doing so. Despite his efforts, he is ultimately defeated and stripped of his Great Rune.

Without his Rune, Morgott is freed from his curse, and transforms into an enfeebled old man. He warns the Tarnished the impenetrable thorns would bar them from becoming Elden Lord, just as they rejected him. After the Cardinal Sin and the release of the Rune of Death, Morgott was finally able to truly die. At the Ashen Capital, Godfrey returned just in time to find his son in his final moments, cradling him tenderly as Morgott's body crumbled into golden dust.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text: Melina and Dung Eater are both available as summons for this fight. For Dung Eater to be available, the player must have released him from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text: Morgott is a highly aggressive and fast-moving enemy, chaining together attacks in rapid succession while leaving few openings. His curved sword inflicts blood loss on impact, while the holy armaments he summons deal holy damage. He has ranged attacks, such as his throwing knives and spear, and utilises jumps, cartwheels, and dashes to close or create distance.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: Once his health drops to 50%, Morgott performs an area of effect attack in which his cursed blood erupts from the ground. His blade becomes infused with his cursed blood, and he gains a number of bloodflame-based attacks. He may also summon golden blades that rain down from the sky.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles, aside from the throne which will break if hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Though a common characteristic on Misbegotten, Morgott is the only Omen to display the tail Crucible aspect.
- Morgott likely seized power during or in the aftermath of the First Defense of Leyndell. As Margit the Fell, he actively participated in the Second Defense of Leyndell.
- Morgott was known as **the Grace-Given**, presumably awarded grace for his loyalty and dedication to the Erdtree, despite being an Omen born without it. Ironically, he dismisses the player as "graceless" before their battle.
- His other title is **the Veiled Monarch** of Leyndell, an alias adopted to conceal his Omen heritage from the public. All of his appearances—whether participating in battle or hunting champions—were conducted under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.
- Morgott can summon spectral weapons during his fights, including the Treespear, Giant-Crusher, Erdsteel Dagger, and Carian Knight's Sword.
  - While the first three weapons are associated with the Erdtree, its warriors, or its nobility, the Carian Knight's Sword originates with the Carian Royal Family, a curious choice given their shared ties to night. This may imply Morgott once observed Carian Knights—perhaps the guards of visiting diplomats—or that he mastered the sword sorceries during the Shattering.
- Though he fought on the battlefield for the majority of his time as Elden Lord, Godfrey reveals he knew Morgott before their banishment. He likely made the tanglehorn bairn in secret to memorialize his son, an ancient hornsent practice.
  - The precious bairn has a tail and Morgott's general horn pattern. It is wrapped in a small cloak identical to the one he wears in game. It is obtained using the Remembrance of the Omen King and is the only Remembrance reward made to memorialize its subject.
- Until his defeat, Morgott's seal at the Cathedral of the Forsaken prevents access to the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
- Like Godrick the Grafted and other Demigods, Morgott remains alive after his defeat. He becomes an NPC that can be spoken to.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Morgott, the Omen King was named **Morgott, Prince of the Omen** in .
- Morgott referred to himself as Elden Lord in a dialogue that was cut from the game.
- There was a cut questline involving Shanehaight, a nobleman of the capital, who discovers the truth about their Veiled Monarch, much to their horror.
- Morgott's name may be inspired by , the alias of Melkor, the main and very first antagonist of 's .

sections.text: The **Night's Cavalry**, also known as **Nightriders**, are recurring bosses in Elden Ring and end-of-night bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Night's Cavalrymen were once led by Margit, the Fell Omen, delivering death to great warriors, knights, and champions. Their fond remembrances inspired the Phantom Slash battle art, which manifests an apparition of their former teacher. Presently, they can be found across the Lands Between, appearing only at night.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Night's Cavalry are knights in black armor with flowing black hair that only appear at night, riding atop funeral steeds. They fight using flails, which can inflict  blood loss, or glaives, which allow them to perform wide, sweeping attacks.

The Night's Cavalry and its Funeral Steed have separate health bars. Defeating the horse dismounts the rider. The knight summons a new horse from a purple portal after a while, or after the player runs away.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
- Stance: 80
- Stance Damage Reduction: 80%
- Immune to Stance Damage while mounted
- Vulnerable to Critical Hits after being Stance-broken or dismounted from the horse

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Mohg, Lord of Blood** and **Mohg, the Omen** are Bosses in Elden Ring. **Luminary Mohg** is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and at the Mohgwyn Palace.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Mohg, also known as the Lord of Blood, was born of the Golden Lineage—the offspring of Queen Marika and Godfrey, First Elden Lord—and was the twin brother of Morgott. The twins were accursed Omen and, as a result, were confined and shackled to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell.

Unlike his brother, Mohg embraced his Omen blood. Deep underground, Mohg made contact with an Outer God known as the Formless Mother, who ignited his accursed blood with bloodflame, granting him powerful magic.

Mohg escaped confinement in the wake of the Shattering, claiming a Great Rune of the Elden Ring. He began establishing his domain from Mohgwyn Palace and recruiting followers, including his Sanguine Nobles and a murderous Tarnished known as the Bloody Fingers. Among these followers was Sir Ansbach, commander of the Pureblood Knights, and Varré, a war surgeon who was able to successfully tame Mohg's accursed blood.

Miquella the Unalloyed later embedded himself within his Haligtree in an attempt to shed his affliction. In this vulnerable and unguarded state, Mohg seized the opportunity to abduct him from the tree. Miquella was an Empyrean, thus having the potential of ascending to godhood; Mohg intended to raise Miquella to full godhood so that he may rule at his side as consort and take the role of Elden Lord. At some point during or after the abduction, Mohg was unknowingly enchanted by Miquella. The circumstances and timeline of this enchantment remain unclear.

After abducting Miquella, Mohg hibernated with him within the Cocoon of the Empyrean, and had his followers render offerings of blood, drenching its chamber in order to facilitate Miquella's awakening.  But no matter how much of Miquella's bloody bedchamber Mohg tried to share, he would receive no response from the young empyrean.

During this time, Mohg largely escaped the notice of the Roundtable Hold, who were searching for clues as to his whereabouts.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text:
Eventually, the Tarnished came to learn the location of Mohg's palace, where he had hidden alongside the stolen Miquella. When the Tarnished stumbles upon his chambers, Mohg emerges from a pool of blood, holds Miquella's hand and apologizes for leaving him, ready to confront their "guests". Despite unleashing the full power of his accursed blood, Mohg is unable to overcome the Tarnished, falling at their hands.

Following his death, Mohg's corpse was stolen and transported to the Land of Shadow, where Miquella utilized it for an ancient ritual at the Gate of Divinity. Mohg's body became a vessel to house the revived soul of Radahn, Miquella's promised consort.

sections.heading: Mohg, the Omen
sections.text:
**Mohg, the Omen** is projection encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, within the Cathedral of the Forsaken that lies beyond the  Forsaken Depths Site of Grace. The arena is a fairly small chapel, with pillars on the side that can be used to gain distance. The Dung Eater is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been released from his cell.

Mohg's trident attacks have long delays, and cover a wide range. He uses a number of bloodflame-based attacks, which deal  blood loss as well as  fire damage. Mohg's Shackle can be used to stun him for a few seconds, allowing for some additional hits.

Defeating **Mohg, the Omen** unlocks the  Cathedral of the Forsaken Site of Grace and grants Bloodflame Talons and  100,000 runes. He must be defeated in order to access the Frenzied Flame Proscription.

sections.heading: Mohg, Lord of Blood
sections.text:
**Mohg, Lord of Blood** is encountered at the top of the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum. The arena is reasonably wide and open, with some gravestones on each side that act as obstacles.

This fight plays out much like the **Mohg, the Omen** fight, until the second phase, when he performs a Bloodboon Ritual and subsequently sprouts enormous black wings. During phase 2, many of Mohg's moveset expands and his attacks will cover large areas in fire.

**Mohg, Lord of Blood** must be defeated to unlock the *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree* expansion, and enter the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text: Phase 1 is largely the same as the fight against **Mohg, the Omen**. The key difference is the introduction of a countdown. When his health drops to certain levels, he will thrust his spear into the air and chant, causing a red ring to appear around the player. He will do this three times, and once his health reaches 50% he will perform Bloodboon Ritual, dealing huge amounts of damage for each ring and inflicting  blood loss, while simultaneously recovering his own health. The Purifying Crystal Tear can be added to the Flask of Wondrous Physick to significantly decrease the amount of damage dealt by this move.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: After performing Bloodboon Ritual and recovering much of his health, Mohg will sprout wings and his spear will be imbued with bloodflame. The majority of his attacks will spray bloodflame on the ground, leaving patches of fire that last for a long time. He also now has abilities that utilize his wings to get out of range or to close distance easily.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Defeating **Mohg, the Omen** and **Mohg, Lord of Blood** for the first time unlocks the "Mohg, the Omen" and "Shardbearer Mohg" achievements, respectively.
- Mohg's has five fingers on his right hand wielding the trident, but his left hand appears to have six. The finger, the third on his left hand, is actually a stiff, solid claw that sticks out when he summons his Bloodflame Talons.
- Mohg's blood is possibly given to the Bloody Fingers invaders covenant. They have it injected into their finger after completing initiation, and it leads them to develop madness and bloodlust.
- His death pose is visually identical to the "Heart Stolen" death animation the player can suffer during the Promised Consort boss fight; hinting even prior to Shadow of the Erdtree that Mohg was under Miquella's charm all along.
- The specific timing of Mohg assuming the title of **Lord of Blood** and the exact sequence of his activities relative to the Shattering are not well-documented, making the precise timeline of these events unclear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Miquella the Kind**, also known as **Miquella of the Haligtree**, **Empyrean Miquella**, and **the Unalloyed**, is a Remembrance Boss in Shadow of the Erdtree. He is an Empyrean and a son of Queen Marika the Eternal and King Consort Radagon. He is the older twin brother of Malenia, and together they are known as the **Twin Prodigies** (天賦の双子, *Tenpu no Futago*). His other self is St. Trina, whom he divested and cast into the depths of the Stone Coffin Fissure. He is encountered at the Gate of Divinity atop Enir-Ilim in the Realm of Shadow, where he fights alongside Radahn, Consort of Miquella.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Miquella and his twin sister were born with incurable afflictions, with Miquella's curse being perpetual youth. Miquella made a promise to Malenia and experimented tirelessly in an attempt to undo their curses. The twins were very close, and Malenia became Miquella's sworn blade and protector. Miquella was loved by many people and had a remarkable ability to compel affection from others. For this reason, many regarded him as the most fearsome Empyrean.

Just as his parents were two halves of the same person, Miquella also had another half—St. Trina—who held the power of Sleep. St. Trina was Miquella's fate, and she was his "love".

Miquella was chosen by his Two Fingers to become an Empyrean, destined to succeed Queen Marika. He was an adherent of Golden Order Fundamentalism, and developed new incantations as gifts to his father Radagon. However, Miquella abandoned Fundamentalism when it failed to treat Malenia's rot. He then began creating Unalloyed Gold, which he used it to craft needles that could ward away the meddling of outer gods and forestall Malenia's incurable rot. These needles could even be used to subdue the power of the Frenzied Flame. He also unsuccessfully sought a solution for his half-brother Godwyn's state of incomplete death.

sections.heading: The Haligtree
sections.text:

At some point, Miquella started watering a sapling with his own blood in the hope that it would become a new Erdtree. The sapling was grown on top of the fortress of Elphael and became known as the Haligtree. Soldiers and Knights sworn to protect the Haligtree would use unalloyed gold to symbolize their loyalty and devotion to Miquella, wearing braided crowns made of the metal and creating shields embedded with it.

Miquella was also said to favor the low and meek, and his Haligtree was intended to be the eventual salvation for the many. It became a hidden haven for the persecuted and the unwanted of the Lands Between, such as the Misbegotten and Albinaurics.

As Miquella pursued godhood, he knew that he would have to take a consort, to which his eyes fell upon his half-brother General Radahn, for he was strong but remained kind. He approached Radahn with his naive offer, to which the General vowed that he would become as such, in return for unspecified terms on Miquella and Malenia's behalf.

Malenia journeyed with her armies to Caelid to confront Radahn. The resulting Battle of Aeonia ended with Malenia unleashing her Scarlet Aeonia, whispering beforehand in Radahn's ear that *"Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."* After using her last resort attack, Malenia entered a comatose state, and one of her knights took it upon herself to carry her leader's slumbering body back across the Lands Between to the Haligtree. Radahn had survived, albeit barely standing, and his mind was riddled by the Scarlet Rot. He was now little more than a howling beast aimlessly wandering the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike.

Following the Battle of Aeonia, Miquella embedded himself into the Haligtree to progress his ascension, but was kidnapped during his slumber. Another of Miquella's half-brothers was to blame: Mohg, who served an Outer God known as the Formless Mother. He took the sleeping Empyrean deep underground to the Mohgwyn Palace, where he aspired to raise Miquella to full godhood himself through blood offerings, and then to take on the role of Miquella's consort instead of Radahn, becoming the new monarch of a Mohgwyn Dynasty. Mohg urged his followers  to render offerings of blood and drench Miquella's cocoon in order to facilitate his awakening.

Despite all of Mohg's efforts, Miquella remained completely unresponsive. At some point, Miquella had covertly placed an enchantment on Mohg, wishing to use the Omen to gain access to the Realm of Shadow. Sir Ansbach, a Pureblood Knight in service to Mohg, attempted to free his lord by challenging Miquella, only to succumb to an enchantment of his own.

Without Miquella's blood offerings, and Malenia no longer protected by her Unalloyed Gold Needle once she was returned, the Haligtree became a misshapen husk. slowly succumbing to the unmitigated Scarlet Rot. Malenia and the Haligtree's soliders desperately awaited Miquella's return to save their rotting home.

sections.heading: The Realm of Shadow
sections.text:
Making use of Mohg, Miquella entered the Realm of Shadow, the location of the Gate of Divinity. As Miquella traveled through the Realm of Shadow, he abandoned parts of himself, including his flesh, his eye, his doubt and vacillation, his love, and his fears. Golden Miquella's Crosses resembling a Great Rune appeared at each location where he abandoned something, akin to Miquella's footprints. Miquella's followers, who pursued him into the Realm of Shadow, used these crosses to trace his path through the realm. Miquella also discarded his other half, St. Trina, in the Stone Coffin Fissure. St. Trina, whose love for Miquella was boundless despite her abandonment, recognized that godhood would be a prison for the Empyrean, and desired for him to be killed out of mercy.

Eventually, a Tarnished champion broke into Mohg's palace and slew the Lord of Blood for his great rune. Sir Gideon Ofnir suggested it might be safer to destroy the cocoon that Miquella remains asleep in. Instead, the Tarnished met Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella, who urged them to travel to the Realm of Shadow by touching Miquella's withered arm within the cocoon.

Within the Realm of Shadow, the Tarnished encounters several more of Miquella's followers, learns of his mission to ascend to godhood via the Gate of Divinity, and of the powerful charm that he had placed upon his disciples, which is broken when he discards his Great Rune. After gaining access to the tower of Enir-Ilim, the Tarnished is confronted by a resurrected Radahn, in a vessel made from the remains of Mohg. It is unclear whether Miquella always intended to use Mohg's body to resurrect Radahn. However, he needed a vessel, likely a hornsent or omen one due to their strong connection to the spiritual world, to bind to Radahn's soul. During the ensuing battle, Miquella steps out of the Gate of Divinity and embraces Radahn as his consort. The Tarnished triumphs over Radahn and Miquella, thus preventing Miquella's age of compassion.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Miquella's Lily is a delicate flower of Unalloyed gold, thought to be beloved by him in his youth. It signifies the faith in the Haligtree.
- The Albinaurics, beings artificially created by human hands, view Miquella's Haligtree area as the chosen land.
- The Haligtree is also inhabited by many unwanted and persecuted races, such as the Albinaurics, the Misbegotten, the Crystalians and the Kindred of Rot.
- The success of Miquella's Haligtree was dependent on the Eclipse.
- Even before *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree* released, there are hints in-game about the connection between Miquella and St. Trina:
  - They are associated with their respective lilies, Miquella's Lily and Trina's Lily. Either is a rare drop from the Cleanrot Knights, who serve Malenia, Miquella's sister.
  - Similarly, the Albinauric Archers guarding the waygate to the Haligtree have lily motif armor and can drop St. Trina's Arrows.
  - A cookbook dedicated to St. Trina allows the player to create the Bewitching Branch, blessed by Unnalloyed Gold incantations.
  - The duality of Marika and Radagon, Miquella's parents.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- To "quell" is to suppress, put an end to, or calm something, like an uprising, fear, or strong emotion, often by force or authority.
- Quella, a young boy whose emblem was a sacred tree,  was the god of dreams in *Dark Souls II*.

sections.heading: Cut Content
sections.text:
- In earlier versions of Elden Ring, Miquella was the shardbearer of the Rune of Abundance.
  - In one version, Miquella was associated with the Abundance Twinblade, an item which was later released as Euporia in *Shadow of the Erdtree*.
  - In another build of the game, Miquella's consciousness would have been within the world of his dream. In a cut quest, Miquella acted as *St. Trina of the Cradlesong*, the saint of slumber. He would have sung a lullaby to soothe the Red-Eyed Merchants of their Frenzied Flame affliction and helped them to retain their personhood and prevent them from becoming "one".
- A cutscene associated with Miquella was cut from the final version of Elden Ring., with associated materials including Leaf, Root, Root_Large, Soil_Blood_Stain, Seedling_Blood_vessel, Seedling_Blood_vessel_branch, and Seedling_Blood_vessel_MultColor_branch.
  - There is a cut dialogue most likely associated with this cutscene: *"Young seedling, young seedling. Return to the bosom of earth. But remember well, Thou'rt mine. So shall I give of myself. This is for thee. Mine abundance, my drop of dew. Quench thy thirst, throughout thy frame. Blossom and burgeon, time and and time again. Grow larger, stronger. Until the day cometh. When thou canst share in my dream. Elden Ring, O Elden Ring. Beget Order most elegant, from my tender reverie." *
  - There is a separate dialogue, possibly related to the use of Miquella's Needle: *"If thou covetest the throne, Impress my vision upon thine heart. In the new world of thy making, all things will flourish, whether graceful, or malign."*
- There is cut dialogue in which Miquella would have intervened in support of Malenia;
  - The phase one cutscene had her say: *"Sweet Tarnished.. Dearest companion... Did you not heed my warning? Your greed knows no end. You would steal the last drop of warmth from his empty frame? After all you've taken, you still want more? Then you will have to kill me. I am Malenia, Sword of Miquella. And I have never known defeat."*
  - During her second phase cutscene, Miquella would've said: *"My dear twin, accept this gift. A gift of abundance, my last drop of dew.  Let all things flourish, whether graceful, or malign."* Presumably, this drop of dew would allow Malenia to ascend to her second phase, and would've been a prerequisite of some kind for Miquella's cut cutscene.
- In Shadow of the Erdtree, there is an unused alternate set of dialogue for the Promised Consort Radahn cutscenes, sandwiched between the retail dialogue internally;
  - Radahn's phase 1 cutscene would have him say: *" I am Radahn. Born of red-maned Radagon, and Rennala of the Full Moon. A lion bred for battle."*
  - The phase 2 cutscene would have had Miquella say: *"I hereby swear. To every living being, and every living soul. Now comes the age of our eden. A thousand year voyage guided by compassion. Beginning here, love encompasses all. No living thing will be denied, no deed censured. I am ready. To embrace the whole of it. Let us go together. Radahn, my promised consort."*

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Noble Presence** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Godslayer incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Guaranteed Drop:** Volcano Manor
- Noble Presence is acquired by defeating the Godskin Noble found at the Temple of Eiglay on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Noble Presence creates a repelling shockwave that knocks back human-sized enemies within a 1.3-meter radius, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 239% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting a Blackflame effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds.

Charging the spell increases the radius to 2.3 meters and increases the Attack Power to 279% of Incantation Scaling, while also launching human-sized enemies into the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  20 FP per cast.
- Costs  28 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 36 points.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Deals 16.8 Stance damage. Increases to 21.84 Stance damage when charged.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- The Godskin Noble Robe boosts the effectiveness of this spell by 20%.
- This spell is not strengthened by the Godslayer's Seal.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Noble Presence is fairly effective against groups of enemies, as its large area-of-effect shockwave can push back or launch multiple foes at once.
- The knockback effect can be useful in controlling the battlefield by throwing enemies off cliffs or into hazardous areas.
- Can be used defensively to break the Stance of incoming attackers, giving the caster time to heal or reposition.
- Charging the spell for maximum potency is particularly effective against heavier foes and enemies with shields.
- The additional damage from the Blackflame effect is somewhat unreliable, as the invincibility given to launched foes will prevent it from being applied to human-sized foes. It is nonetheless
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07: Increased stamina consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies. Shortened recovery time.
  - Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 180 to 200 for the uncharged version, while the charged versions Stamina Attack Power wasn't changed.
    - The Stamina Attack Power against guarding players was increased from 180 to 250 for the uncharged version, while it was increased from 234 to 292 for the charged version.

sections.heading: Acquisition

  - The first location where she can be killed, and drop the talisman, is the Windmill Heights site of grace at Dominula, Windmill Village.
  - The only way to kill her and not have the talisman drop after giving her the prosthesis (as of update 1.03) is after choosing to assist her in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, as part of her questline.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Increases Dexterity by 5 and also increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 4%/6%/11%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point.

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hits towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive) also increasing the effect.
  - These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land.
  - For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive.
- For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count.
- Can be worn together with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia or the Winged Sword Insignia to stack the effect, but only the latter can be obtained in the same playthrough.
- Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy.
  - An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice.
  - This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.
