sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Misbegotten** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
According to the hornsent, Crucible aspects sprouted on a Giant in the distant past, and its influence would profoundly mark the life forms present in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh

At some point, a group of people would make contact with the Crucible, becoming the Misbegotten, malformed beings that exhibit characteristics of different types of animals, often possessing tails, horns, scales, and wings. They typically have red fur and golden hair. For this act, they would be punished and treated as slaves from birth under the rule of Marika, and their appearance would make them considered impure like Omens. They often wield weighty, iron weapons steeped in resentment.

Misbegotten appear in various regions of the Lands Between. Many found sanctuary in Haligtree Town, situated in the branches of Miquella's Haligtree. Others worship graves and a hooded warrior’s statue in Leyndell, Royal Capital, or guard ancient forges within the Realm of Shadow. A Misbegotten Crusader wields the marital sword forged by Radagon of the Golden Order and leads a group that found refuge in the Cave of the Forlorn. The only friendly Misbegotten is Smithing Master Hewg, a blacksmith cursed by Queen Marika to forge a weapon capable of killing a god. Bound to the Roundtable Hold, he labors endlessly for the Tarnished.

At some point, a population of Misbegotten were employed as slaves at Castle Morne; however, after the Shattering, they rebelled against Godrick's forces stationed there and took over the castle. Castellan Edgar remains behind to ensure the Grafted Blade Greatsword does not fall into the wrong hands. Later, if the Tarnished assists Edgar, a Misbegotten murders Edgar's daughter, Irina of Morne. This drives Edgar to embrace the Frenzied Flame and become a revenger, vowing to avenge his daughter by slaughtering all Misbegotten.

There are four Misbegotten enemy types: cleaver-wielding Misbegotten, bow-wielding Winged Misbegotten, axe-wielding Scaly Misbegotten, and sword-wielding Misbegotten Warriors.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Common Misbegotten that wield iron cleavers. They can be found throughout the Lands Between, and are seemingly used for slave labour. They possess vestigial wings, however they do not possess the ability to fly.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Misbegotten with large, feathery wings capable of prolonged flight. They fight using daggers and shortbows.

sections.heading: Variant Description

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Mt. Gelmir** is a subregion in Elden Ring, located on the Altus Plateau.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text:
A volcano in western Altus Plateau, which houses the Volcano Manor at its summit. It is characterized by sheer cliffs and ominous skies, qualities which grew more pronounced in the wake of The Shattering.

The dried-up Seethewater River runs along the base of the volcano, with geysers that spew jets of boiling water. The river terminates on the west side, near Fort Laiedd where the forces of Leyndell are locked in conflict with the Fire Monks. The Hermit Village, inhabited by Demi-Humans and Glintstone Sorcerers, sits on the southeastern edge of the volcano. Primeval Sorcerer Azur, one of the founding Glintstone Sorcerers, settled near the village after his banishment from the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Mt. Gelmir was the site of the most horrendous conflict of the Shattering, which has left scars that can still be found. Ruined campsites litter the cliffsides. Some Leyndell Soldiers remain, driven to frenzy by the horrors they saw.

The Volcano Manor, which sits atop the mountain, is the home of the Demigod Praetor Rykard, who once led a company of inquisitors. After the Elden Ring was broken, Rykard fed himself to the blasphemous serpent, Great Rune and all, in defiance of the gods. His knights abandoned him when his noble ambitions were reduced to gluttony and depravity, yet his consort, Tanith, remained by his side. Rykard is now served by the Recusants; a band of Tarnished who hunt their own kind.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Nepheli Loux, Warrior** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Nepheli Loux is a Tarnished warrior from the Badlands. In her infancy, Nepheli lived through murder and pillage unchecked. At some point, she lost the guidance of grace, and was taken in by Gideon Ofnir, who became her foster father. Gideon promised Nepheli that if he became Elden Lord he would never allow the downtrodden to be cheated again, earning her loyalty and aid in his pursuit of the title of Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text:
At the behest of Gideon, Nepheli infiltrates Stormveil Castle, the home of the demigod Godrick the Grafted. Here, she encounters a Tarnished, who aids her in defeating the decrepit demigod. With Godrick slain, she returns to Roundtable Hold, where she awards them with an Arsenal Charm she found in Stormveil, and encourages them to speak to her foster father.

Travelling to Liurnia of the Lakes, Nepheli comes upon the Village of the Albinaurics, where she witnesses the slaughter of the Albinauric inhabitants at the hands of her father's men. Reminded of the brutality she witnessed as a child, Nepheli vows to deliver justice to the oppressors, assisting the Tarnished in defeating the Omenkiller responsible for the slaughter.

For giving into her emotions and abandoning the mission, Nepheli is cast aside by Gideon. Without her estranged father's guidance, she becomes crestfallen, resigning to the lower levels of Roundtable Hold where she questions the faith she had in Gideon.

The Tarnished obtains the ashes of The Stormhawk King in the Chapel of Anticipation, which they may choose to give to Nepheli. She can smell the ancient storm within the ash, and is reminded of her first hawk. Despite her inability to sense spirits within ash, she gladly receives them.

After claiming the Stormhawk King's ashes, Nepheli encounters Kenneth Haight, who recognises her as a worthy heir of Limgrave. Nepheli accepts the role, having been reminded by Limgrave of her own home. As the new lord of Limgrave, Nepheli pledges to aid the Tarnished should they become Elden Lord, pledging to call upon the storm to drive away the foulness that has settled on the winds.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave (Stormhill Shack)
  - Talk with Roderika, receiving the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes, and give her the Chrysalids' Memento retrieved from Godrick's grafting grounds in Stormveil Castle to have her move to the Roundtable Hold. Otherwise, just entering Liurnia of the Lakes is enough to trigger this passage and, while the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes will be lost, the Golden Seed you'd have received at the Hold can instead be found in her spot at the shack.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Talk with Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing and exhaust his dialogues to have him move inside his study guarded by Ensha of the Royal Remains.
  - Talk with Hewg selecting **About Roderika**, then speak to her selecting **Tell her what the blacksmith said** and finally return to the smithing master selecting **About Roderika** -> **Would you watch over Roderika?** -> **It's what she wants**. Roderika becoming a Spirit Tuner under Hewg's wing is necessary to complete step #7.
1. Limgrave (Liftside Chamber)
  - Past the first two Stormhawks, Nepheli can be found in a small room on the path leading to the Secluded Cell Site of Grace. Exhaust her dialogue to unlock her summon sign outside the fog gate of Godrick the Grafted.
    - *(Optional)* Summoning her will unlock alternate dialogue in the next step of her questline.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Nepheli will be standing just outside Gideon's study. Talk to her to receive the Arsenal Charm.
    - If you defeated Godrick without speaking to her in the previous step, she will not give the Arsenal Charm.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Village of the Albinaurics)
  - Nepheli can be found on the slope leading up to the village. Exhaust her dialogue to unlock her summon sign past the bridge leading to the Omenkiller Mini-Boss.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (The Four Belfries)
  - Use an Imbued Sword Key (one is found in the chest near the Site of Grace) at the **Precipice of Anticipation**'s Sending Gate to return to the starting area of the game and, past the Grafted Scion, enter the previously closed door next to the Chapel of Anticipation to reach the rooftop where The Stormhawk King is found.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - With the Omenkiller defeated (regardless of whether you summoned her), she will return to the Roundtable Hold, relocating at the bottom of the stairs near Hewg. Talk to her, then speak with Gideon selecting **Nepheli's despair** and return to Nepheli to exhaust her dialogues. At this point, you'll have the following options available:
    - **Give Seluvis's Potion**: if you have initiated Ranni the Witch's questline at Caria Manor and talked with Preceptor Seluvis, you can administer this tonic to Nepheli, ending her questline prematurely, with Nepheli Loux Puppet becoming available for purchase from Pidia, Carian Servant.
    - **Give The Stormhawk King**: this Key Item will allow her questline to enter its final stage, once exhausted all of her dialogues.
1. Limgrave (Godrick the Grafted)
  - After defeating Morgott, the Omen King, return to the Godrick the Grafted Site of Grace and exhaust Gatekeeper Gostoc's dialogues, reloadig the area until he disappears from stomping on Godrick's corpse. Gostoc and Nepheli will now be found within the throne room of Stormveil Caste: exhaust her dialogues to receive Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone x1 and he too will now sell one for 20,000 Runes.
    - While this also concludes Kenneth Haight's questline, without the need to have proceeded through any of the other steps in his questline in order to unlock this step, he is completely optional for Nepheli and Gostoc's questline.
1. Leyndell, Ashen Capital (Queen's Bed Chamber)
  - *(Optional)* Nepheli's summon sign can be found outside the fog gate of Godfrey, First Elden Lord, alongside Shabriri's if the player has followed Hyetta and Yura's questlines.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Nepheli Loux's name implies that she is related to Godfrey, who's name following his banishment from the Lands Between is Hoarah Loux. This connection is also supported by Kenneth Haight's decision to appoint her as the new lord of Limgrave, following his proclamation to find someone of the "proper lineage".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Millicent** is an NPC cooperator in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Millicent is a red-haired woman afflicted by Scarlet Rot. She and her sisters were found in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid by Sage Gowry, who raised them as his daughters. Her four sisters travelled to Miquella's Haligtree under Gowry's guidance, however Millicent alone remained behind.

At Gowry's behest, the Tarnished obtains an Unalloyed Gold Needle and brings it to the Church of the Plague, where Millicent is slowly succumbing to the Rot. She inserts the needle to stall the Rot, regaining her strength. However, her memories appear to have been affected by her sickness, as when she struggles to remember Gowry upon returning to his shack to find it abandoned.

Millicent sets off on a journey across the Lands Between, retracing the route taken by Malenia, Blade of Miquella after the battle of Aeonia. She once again meets the Tarnished on the Altus Plateau, where they present her with a Valkyrie's Prosthesis to replace her missing sword arm.

Millicent's journey takes her to the Mountaintops of the Giants, in search of a fort containing a medallion which will allow her to access the Haligtree. After the Tarnished claims the medallion and travels to the Consecrated Snowfield, Millicent makes her way to the Haligtree, and to Elphael, the city at its base. Here, she reveals to the Tarnished that she is of Malenia's blood, although she is unsure whether she is a sister, daughter, or offshoot of the Demigod. Unbeknownst to Millicent, however, the Tarnished has been advised by Gowry to assist his remaining four daughters in killing Millicent, so that she can be reborn as a scarlet valkyrie when Malenia ascends to godhood.

The Tarnished may then make a choice: kill Millicent alongside her four sisters, or fight alongside her against the attackers. Should the Tarnished kill Millicent, she will become a scarlet aeonia flower, waiting for Malenia's ascension. If the player fights alongside her, she will remove the needle from her body, allowing her to succumb to the Rot.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Caelid (Swamp of Aeonia)
  - *(Optional)* Millicent can invade in the south-eastern part of the Swamp of Aeonia.
1. Caelid (Swamp of Aeonia and Gowry's Shack)
  - Defeat Commander O'Niel to obtain the Unalloyed Gold Needle and bring it to Gowry. Reload the area and speak to Gowry again to obtain the repaired Unalloyed Gold Needle.
1. Caelid (Church of the Plague)
  - Give Millicent the Unalloyed Gold Needle, then rest at the Site of Grace and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Caelid (Gowry's Shack)
  - Return to Gowry's Shack and exhaust Millicent's dialogue.
1. Altus Plateau (Erdtree-Gazing Hill Ruins)
  - Find Millicent on a hill north of the  Erdtree Gazing Hill Site of Grace.
  - Go to the Shaded Castle and find the Valkyrie's Prosthesis in a treasure chest.
  - Return to Millicent and give her the Valkyrie's Prosthesis.
  - Millicent will now be available as a summon for the following bosses: Godskin Apostle (Windmill Heights), Draconic Tree Sentinel (Capital Outskirts), Black Blade Kindred (Forbidden Lands).
1. Altus Plateau (Dominula, Windmill Village)
  - After defeating the Godskin Apostle, reload and speak to Millicent near the Site of Grace of the battle and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
  - Find Millicent beside the  Ancient Snow Valley Ruins Site of Grace and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree
  - Find Millicent next to the  Prayer Room Site of Grace and exhaust her dialogue.
  - *(Optional)* Speaking to Gowry at this point will cause him to provide new dialogue explaining the next part of the questline.
1. Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.
  - After defeating the Putrid Tree Spirit there will be two summon signs on the right ledge above the Scarlet Rot pool, both very close to each other.
  - **Selecting the gold summon sign** will send you into Millicent's world to help her fight off her four sisters: Mary, Eldest Sister; Maureen, Second Sister; Amy, Third Sister; Polyanna, Youngest Sister. Doing so will reward you with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia. After the fight, find Millicent lying beside the poison pool and speak to her to end her quest. Afterwards, after exhausting his dialogue, Gowry will drop the Flock's Canvas Talisman if killed. Only if Millicent was assisted, Malenia will drop Miquella's Needle when revisiting the area after defeated.
  - **Selecting the red summon sign** will send you into Millicent's world in order to kill her alongside the aforementioned NPCs. Doing so will reward you with Millicent's Prosthesis; an Aeonian Bloom will appear in your world, and Gowry will disappear but leave a Flock's Canvas Talisman.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Millicent's questline can still be started even after defeating Malenia.
- The Valkyrie's Prosthesis links Millicent and Malenia through the symbolic loss of the right arm. Statues of Malenia at Haligtree Town depict her in her youth without a right arm. None of Millicent's Sisters meet this criteria.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - In an unused cutscene, Malenia refers to the player as her companion. This implies a cut third ending to Millicent's questline in which she succeeds in returning Malenia's lost pride.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Mountaintops of the Giants** is a region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The northern Mountaintops were once the home of the Fire Giants, after they claimed them from the Ice Dragons. At the birth of the Erdtree, the forces of Queen Marika the Eternal and Godfrey, First Elden Lord marched up the mountain and put the Giants to the sword. With the Giants defeated, the Flame of Ruin was confined within the Giants' Forge atop the mount, and the Age of the Erdtree began.

The Fire Monks, who were left behind to watch over the Flame of Ruin, can be found patrolling the region. They are often accompanied by the Guilty: thorn sorcerers who were banished to the north. Their fortress, the Guardians' Garrison, sits on the eastern side of the mountain.

The Zamor Ruins in the southwest are the home of an ancient clan of Zamor Warriors. They were ancient enemies of the Fire Giants, and are regarded as heroes due to their actions in the War Against the Giants.

The Mountaintops were also home to the astrologers, neighbors of the Giants and predecessors to the modern Glintstone Sorcerers. The ruins of their civilization can be found in the central Mountaintops.

The northernmost section of the Mountaintops is dominated by Castle Sol, where the site of an eclipse once inspired dreadful awe. Half of a medallion that will grant access to Miquella's Haligtree can be found here, protected by Commander Niall.

The medallion can be used at the Grand Lift of Rold to gain access to the Consecrated Snowfield, which sprawls to the west of the Mountaintops. The Albinaurics, and others who revere Miquella, seek this sacred land in the hopes of earning the Empyrean's favour. Ordina, Liturgical Town is the final stop on the way to the Haligtree, and is home to several Albinauric Archers.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Nokron, Eternal City** is a subregion in Elden Ring, located along the Siofra River.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Nokron is one of the Eternal Cities of the Nox, who were banished underground after invoking the ire of the Greater Will. Nokron's chair-crypt houses the Fingerslayer Blade, a blood-drenched fetish made from a corpse that can harm the Greater Will and its vassals, and is proof of the treason of the Nox.

Nokron is notably difficult to access. Long ago, a band of slaves-turned-soldiers called the Fallen Hawks were ordered to explore the Eternal Cities. Although they managed to find their way into the subterranean realm, they became trapped after they discovered the Ghostflame. While the city is visible from the lower portion of Siofra River, the route to it is only opened after Starscourge Radahn is defeated, which causes a star to fall upon Limgrave, opening a deep crater near Fort Haight.

sections.text:
Nokstella is one of the Eternal Cities inhabited by the Nox, who were banished underground after invoking the ire of the Greater Will. It is located in the Ainsel River Main, on the west side of the underground river, and can only be accessed by using the Sending Gate in Renna's Rise and following the path through the northern Uhl Palace Ruins.

The lost Black Moon of Nokstella was once the guide to countless stars, and a talisman made in its image was regarded as the treasure of the city.

sections.text: The **Mohgwyn Palace** is a subregion in Elden Ring. It is located on an island in the Siofra River.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
An island in the underground Siofra River, far to the east of Nokron, Eternal City. The grave of an ancient dynasty civilization can be found here, and it is in these ruins that Mohg, Lord of Blood, has chosen to be the seat of his coming Mohgwyn Dynasty.

A large part of the area is taken up by a blood-red lake, which is the habitat of many abominations. The Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum juts out of the west side of the island, housing the Lord of Blood and his vassals.

There are two possible entrances to this area. The conventional route is via a sending gate on the western edge of Consecrated Snowfield, which leads to a cliff on the southeastern side of the palace. Alternately, by becoming a Pureblood Knight of the Mohgwyn Dynasty, one can obtain a Pureblood Knight's Medal from White Mask Varré, which will teleport the player to the mausoleum entrance at will.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Miquella's Needle** is a key item in Elden Ring. This item is part of Millicent's questline.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree
- Miquella's Needle is obtained by interacting with Malenia's Scarlet Aeonia flower near the  Malenia, Goddess of Rot Site of Grace in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. This interaction only occurs while holding the Unalloyed Gold Needle, which is acquired from Millicent after helping her defeat her sisters.
  - If Malenia's flower is absent, reload the area by resting at a Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Use
sections.text: This item can only be used within the arena of Dragonlord Placidusax in Crumbling Farum Azula: dispels the Flame of Frenzy inherited from the Three Fingers in the depths of Leyndell, allowing to attain a different ending from the Lord of Frenzied Flame finale.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: Once Miquella's Needle is used, the burn marks from the Three Fingers will remain. However, the Frenzied Flame eye variation will be removed. The burn marks may be removed by Renalla during character customization, and they may also be reapplied at any time.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The near-final Japanese 1.0 edition of the game has a different final line, roughly translating to "At the end of time, if you do not wish to become Lord of Frenzied Flame, use this needle to pierce your eye(s)."
  - Miquella has a cut dialogue most likely associated with the use of this item, swaying the Tarnished away from the despair of the Frenzied Flame: "*If thou covetest the throne, impress my vision upon thine heart. sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Miquella's Haligtree** (ミケラの聖樹, *Mikera no Seiju*) is a legacy dungeon located north of the Consecrated Snowfield. It is accessible after solving the puzzle in the Evergaol at Ordina, Liturgical Town and taking the Sending Gate.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Miquella's Haligtree is a vast, misshapen tree in the far north of the Lands Between. Built into the canopy is Haligtree Town, a sanctuary for the unwanted. At the base of the tree is Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, a city largely inhabited by the Haligtree Knights and Cleanrot Knights who serve Miquella and Malenia. Both areas contain statues of the twin Demigods.

Long ago, the Empyrean Miquella abandoned Golden Order Fundamentalism after realizing it could not treat Malenia's Scarlet Rot. He sought to establish an Unalloyed Gold order away from the Erdtree and settled on the Haligtree. Miquella watered the sapling with his own Empyrean blood, and later wove a cocoon and embedded himself within its trunk to nurture it directly. However, it would fail to grow into an Erdtree. Before he could finish, Miquella was cut and taken from the tree by Mohg, who was under his charm. The Lord of Blood zealously wished to raise the Empyrean to godhood and become his consort. After returning from her battle with Radahn, Malenia awaited her brother's return at the base of the tree, and over time infected the tree with her Scarlet Rot.

Nevertheless, the Haligtree and its city became a haven for those rejected by society, such as the Misbegotten and the Kindred of Rot. Loretta, a former Knight of Caria, founded a sanctuary for Albinaurics among the boughs of the Haligtree. Those who made the pilgrimage presented a secret medallion at the Grand Lift of Rold to gain access to the Consecrated Snowfield. They traveled north and crossed the river to Ordina, Liturgical Town, where they journeyed through a Sending Gate.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Miquellan Knight's Sword** is a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, near the  Prayer Room Site of Grace.

After exiting the Grace in it to continue forward there will be a parapet on the right that leads to a tower with a ladder on the other side. Climbing that ladder leads to the sword's location.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- While the skill, Sacred Blade, is excellent, at this point of the game most bosses and tough enemies are resistant to Holy damage, and most tough Those Who Live in Death will have been defeated, making it far less useful than the much earlier acquisition of Ash of War: Sacred Blade is.
- Has a unique heavy attack that causes the user to step forward. This attack has good forward reach, and since the first attack in the charged version makes a short dash forward it's useful to catch opponents out of their roll and for landing the Stance-breaking charged heavy attack while not having to stand too close to enemies.
- This weapon gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, as the Faith-scaling is mostly useful for increasing the damage of the Skill.
  - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 605 AP, 80 Strength or Dexterity grants 581 AP, 45 Strength (or Dexterity) and 45 Faith grants 566 AP, and 80 Faith grants 516 AP.
  - In other words, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity is best if looking to maximize AP while 45 Strength and 45 Faith (Strength is slightly preferable over Dexterity due to the bonus from two-handing) is better for a mix of attack damage and skill damage.
- Pairs surprisingly well with the Golden Epitaph, another Holy sword that scales similarly well on a hybrid Strength/Dexterity or Strength/Faith build.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary

sections.heading: Acquisition

  - Sword-and-torch-wielding nobles will not drop the sword.
  - The Carriage on the road that runs north from the Agheel Lake South Site of Grace has several of these Nobles in its caravan.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
- The longest of all Straight Swords, with very good scaling but bad base damage making it a mostly good weapon, not counting how hard it can be to farm.
- Performs best on the Keen affinity as it has the lowest damage deficit there and is usually only a dozen or fewer points behind in terms of pure Attack Power.
  - Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- As the description implies, this swords sells for 10 times as much as most other Straight Swords.

- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Moongrum, Carian Knight** is a hostile NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Moongrum is one of the few enchanted knights left. Anointed by the Lunar Queen, these heroes of the highest honors had power to match even the champions of gold in battle, but fell into disarray with the decline of the Carian royal family.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
- Liurnia of the Lakes (Debate Parlor)

Guards the elevator to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library, where Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon is found.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
Running past him to send the elevator up and then either baiting him to swing his sword or pushing him with strong attacks with heavy foward momentum down the shaft is a quick and effective tactic.

Be careful when he keeps his shield raised, as it means he's ready to parry any incoming attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Moongrum, Carian Knight was named **Carian Knight Moongrum** in .
- Moongrum's name in Japanese is ムーングラム (Mūnguramu), which can also be read as "Moonglum." Moonglum is a character in 's , which Hidetaka Miyazaki has cited as an inspiration for *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Miriel, Pastor of Vows** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Miriel, Pastor of Vows is the steward of the Church of Vows in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. A gigantic tortoise wearing a large white mitre, Miriel is a gentle soul who will happily assist the Tarnished on their journey.

Well-versed in both sorceries and incantations, Miriel can be given scrolls as well as prayerbooks, and will readily teach new spells to the player for an appropriate fee. Miriel's true passion is for the miracle of Absolution, which he believes will mend the world.

Miriel also serves as an excellent source of lore on Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and her former husband, Radagon of the Golden Order. Exhausting Miriel's dialogue can direct the player toward secrets that advance multiple questlines.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Miriel is the most reliable cleric NPC for prayerbooks, since he never moves away from the church, accepts all types of books and only becomes unavailable once during the Bell Bearing Hunter invasion.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Moonlight Altar** is a subregion of the Lands Between in Elden Ring. It is located above Liurnia of the Lakes and can only be accessed after advancing Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A plateau on the east side of Liurnia bathed in the light of the Dark Moon. It is accessible only by passing through Ainsel River and the Lake of Rot and defeating Astel, Naturalborn of the Void. The lift which leads to the Moonlight Altar is sealed, and can only be accessed by obtaining the Dark Moon Ring from the treasure chest in Rennala's library in the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

The plateau, which sits above the Village of the Albinaurics, is the site of the Cathedral of Manus Celes, a large, ruined church. The Ringleader's Evergaol, housing the ringleader of the Black Knife Assassins, can also be found here.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Night of Black Knives** (黒き刃の陰謀の夜, *Kuroki Yaiba no Inbō no Yoru*) was an event mentioned in Elden Ring. It involved the theft of Destined Death and the assassination of Godwyn the Golden, a son of Queen Marika the Eternal. It would serve as the catalyst of the conflict known as The Shattering.

sections.heading: Prelude
sections.text:
Although the conspirators behind it remained unknown to the wider world, it was in fact orchestrated by Lunar Princess Ranni as she was looking for a way to free herself from the control of the Two Fingers.
Ranni, who sought to change her fate, stole a piece of the Rune of Death from Maliketh, who served as the guardian of the rune. With the stolen fragment, Ranni proceeded to imbue the Black Knives of Numen Assassins, all of them being women from the Eternal Cities with ties to Marika, with the powers of Destined Death.

On the same night, Ranni gifted her brother, Praetor Rykard, with the Blasphemous Claw, a rock engraved with traces of the Rune of Death, as a reward for helping her in the plot and to make Rykard able to challenge Maliketh on the day of his blasphemy.

sections.heading: Assassination
sections.text:
Wishing to shed her Empyrean body but preserve her spirit, she knew that the spirit of someone else had to die as well. On the night of the plot, the assassins arrived in Leyndell, the Royal Capital, and slew Godwyn the Golden, carving the Cursemark of Death into his flesh. The Cursemark was supposed to form a circle; however, as Ranni perished in the same moment as Godwyn, the mark was split into two half-wheels. Godwyn's soul alone perished, while Ranni became the first Demigod to die in the flesh.

Immediately following the assassination, the Black Knives fled the capital. Tiche, the daughter of the Black Knife Ringleader Alecto, died protecting her mother during the escape.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text:
Godwyn's body was interred in the Deeproot Depths at the base of the Erdtree's roots, where he mutated and deformed into the being that would become known as the Prince of Death. Later, the traces of the Rune of Death used to slay him spread through the network of Greattree roots that span the Lands Between, taking the form of Deathroot, the source of Those Who Live in Death.

Ranni, whose Empyrean body perished upon the carving of the Cursemark, transferred her soul into a doll modeled after her mentor. She maintained a low profile following the Night of Black Knives, and it is unknown whether her death was widely known.

Following the Night of Black Knives, the Elden Ring was shattered by Queen Marika. As a result, the great war known as The Shattering ensued.

In the aftermath of the Shattering, a Tarnished known as Fia, the Deathbed Companion, came into contact with the soulless body of Godwyn. Fia sought the two half-wheels, wishing to reunite them and produce a Mending Rune, which could introduce Those Who Live in Death to the Elden Ring. During this time, another Tarnished named Rogier began to study the Night of Black Knives, bringing him into contact with Fia.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Noble Page** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Pages are servants to nobility. They came to serve by birth into obscurity, regardless of aptitude or volition. They wear fine clothes as to avoid any undue shame in their master's way, and sack-like hoods befitting their unremarkable servitude. High Pages are selected for special privileges by their master.

Pages are dexterous opponents, capable of weaving in and out of attacks before either lunging with their Estoc or firing a bolt from their off-hand Soldier's Crossbow. They rely on the element of surprise or ranged engagements, as their physical defenses are lacking. High Pages wield a Pulley Crossbow loaded with Perfumer's Bolts instead.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Misbegotten Warriors** are enemies in Elden Ring. They are a powerful variant of the Misbegotten enemy and often appear as bosses, including Leonine Misbegotten and Misbegotten Crusader.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Misbegotten Warriors are feral humanoids marked by bestial traits—claws, fangs, feathered wings, serpentine tails, and a thick red lion’s mane. Like other Misbegotten, their appearance is seen as punishment for ancient contact with the primordial Crucible. They are nimble and aggressive, wildly swinging weighty Iron Greatswords and leaping into the air.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Misbegotten Warriors deal  Standard damage. They are highly aggressive and mobile, and finding safe openings to counterattack can be difficult. They can enter a buffed state with glowing red eyes by using Barbaric Roar.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
*See also: Perfumer Tricia (Boss)*

A Misbegotten Warrior fought alongside Perfumer Tricia at the end of the Unsightly Catacombs. Tricia, a healer devoted to treating impure creatures, appears to have allied with the Misbegotten.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
*See also: Crucible Knight*

A Misbegotten Warrior fought in the plaza of Redmane Castle when the Radahn Festival is not active. When reduced to half health, a Crucible Knight joins the fight.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The pale spirit of a Misbegotten Warrior guards the secrets of Miquella the Kind deep within the Stone Coffin Fissure. This unmarked boss uses Multilayered Ring of Light and drops the incantation upon defeat. Like all unmarked Bosses, it will not respawn.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- **Internal name**: ラダゴン獅子 (*Radagon Shishi*, lit. Radagon Lion)
  - This name remained in usage even in the DLC.
- A Misbegotten Warrior at Leyndell, Royal Capital prays towards a statue of a hooded man holding an Iron Greatsword.

- Misbegotten Crusader
- Winged Misbegotten
- Crucible Knight

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Transforms the player into an object based on assets found in the player's current location, such as statues, small trees, or gravestones. This effect lasts until the player takes damage, rolls, jumps, attacks, or uses a consumable.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Miranda Sprouts** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Miranda Sprouts are small, mobile, flesh eating flowers that cause a variety of Status Effects with their pollen.

They are often found around the larger Miranda Blossoms, and are said to descend from Miranda, maiden of the Flower Crucible who are also their namesake.

They are very weak to Fire and since they are slow and short-ranged in their attacks they are easily handled with a ranged weapon or consumables.

Five of the pink Poison variant can be summoned via the Miranda Sprout Ashes.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: The standard, pink variant that inflicts  Poison by expelling spore clouds.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: A yellow variant that inflicts  Poison buildup.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: A blue variant that only differs from the standard pink one because of their increased Magic Resistance.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text:
A black variant that inflicts  Madness buildup. Explodes into frenzying spores when attacked with Fire.

Found between the Church of Inhibition and Frenzied Flame Village as well as within the Uhl Palace Ruins.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: A red variant that inflicts  Scarlet Rot. Found wherever the Rot can be found, such as the Swamp of Aeonia and Miquella's Haligtree.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: A Miranda Sprout blighted by purple splotches. Grows in the Perfumer's Grotto on the Altus Plateau and inflicts  Poison buildup.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - **RuneFlowerLittle** is the internal name for Miranda Sprouts.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Soldiers who guard the Wandering Mausoleums, where the soulless Demigods are lain to rest. The soldiers followed their masters into death by severing their own heads, persisting as spirits. Their surcoats depict the mausoleum bell, which rings in mourning for the soulless Demigods.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Miners are laborers with skin like cracked stone, found in mines and tunnels throughout the Lands Between. Their stonelike skin grants resistance to slashing attacks, but they are vulnerable to  Strike-based damage.

They wield mining tools such as Pickaxes and Explosive Stones, once used for rock blasting. Some carry lanterns that can spew fire, while others haul sacks of rocks, hurling them alongside Explosive Stones and Poisoned Stones. These stones were originally pest control tools, though the Miners have long forgotten how to craft them.

Some miners are failed scholars, working in crystal tunnels as sorcerer-miners. They wield Digger's Staffs that double as mining tools, enhancing Stonedigger sorceries like Shatter Earth. Others may hurl Glintstone Scraps during combat.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Miners typically found in caves and mining tunnels. Most wield pickaxes, while some carry lanterns that they can use to spew fire. Some have sacks of rocks on their backs, and will throw rocks as well as Explosive Stones and Poisoned Stones, which are employed as tools for pest extermination, although the Miners have long forgotten how to craft them.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Sorcerer-miners who work in crystal tunnels. They wield glintstone staves which serve as mining tools, enhancing the power of Stonedigger sorceries which mark these miners as failed scholars. Some may also throw Glintstone Scraps in combat.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Mausoleum Knights** is enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Mausoleum Knights of Castle Sol willingly beheaded themselves to serve their masters in Death, a self-inflicted curse that bound their souls to the land. In doing so, they became phantasmal guardians of the Wandering Mausoleums—enormous, tolling belfries interring the soulless cadavers of dead Demigods. Lhutel the Headless, leader of the Mausoleum Knights, sacrificed her life to continue serving a soulless Demigod until their revival, earning her the hero's honor of Erdtree Burial.

The Knights commanded the Mausoleum Soldiers and Mausoleum Foot Soldiers, and maintained a large presence in Tombsward, northern Liurnia, and around the Nameless Eternal City in the Deeproot Depths. A detachment at Noklateo, the Shrouded City included Headless Trolls, Headless Gladiators, and Headless Fallen Hawk Soldiers.

They wore wing-shaped ornaments on their backs to evoke the wicked Deathbirds of old—offspring of the Twinbird who burned death in cold ghostflame to release vengeful spirits. Their crested shields displayed the sun in eclipse, a star that protected the soulless by keeping Destined Death at bay. They bore weapons enrobed in the Prince of Death's black-and-gold flame, inflicting  Holy damage and  Death Blight buildup, and they hurled phantasmal spears.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Minor Erdtrees** are Landmarks in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Gargantuan deciduous trees with dense canopies of golden leaves, visible from great distances. The bark of young Minor Erdtrees gives off a golden glow that apparently fades as they reach maturity.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Erdtree's offspring sprouted from its fabled Golden Seeds, scattered across the Lands Between when it sensed the end of its life for the first time.

Queen Marika the Eternal would plant developing Minor Erdtrees at the Minor Erdtree Church, where she would deliver a speech, demanding to abandon blind faith and declaring her intent of inquiring the depths of her Golden Order in an attempt to strengthen its grace through understanding. The order of the Erdtree Guardians would be established to protect the Erdtree's offspring through a pact with it. Talismans depicting the Erdtree seed, once believed as something that could not exist, were crafted to increase the powers of its blessed sap. Perfumers developed wondrous physicks using the crystal tears that were slowly collected in basins at the feet of the Minor Erdtrees. Catacombs for Erdtree Burial would be built close to Minor Erdtrees as their roots were once linked together with those of the Erdtree.

Upon the shattering of the Elden Ring, fearing its coming end again, the Erdtree would release new seeds that would start growing into Illusory Trees and deploy Erdtree Avatars to protect its already grown but withering offspring.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Crystalized Tears for the Flask of Wondrous Physick are commonly acquired at Minor Erdtrees.
- Small collection basins are found at the base of most Minor Erdtrees. They collected hardened sap.
- Teardrop Scarabs often linger near Minor Erdtrees.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Nomadic Merchants** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Long ago, the ancestors of the Nomadic Merchants were spurned by Grace, condemned to a life of endless wandering with no place to settle. Once they had thrived as the Great Caravan, but a maddening disease had followed in their wake. In an effort to bury it, Queen Marika had their people sealed deep beneath the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. There in the dark, they chanted a curse of despair, calling forth the Frenzied Flame.

Those who remained roamed the Lands Between, bound by a code forbidding them to lament their solitude or seek sympathy, and vowing to show no mercy to any who dared to harm them. These wandering traders searched the realm for their ancestors, and the home that vanished with them.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: A scattered clan of Nomadic Merchants is found all over the Lands Between, often sitting at campfires, sometimes with their Mules nearby. Some can be seen playing a somber melody on stringed instruments. The wares they sell are frequently influenced by or representative of their current locations. Each merchant wears a unique recolor of the basic outfit. The notes of information they offer are marked by colored feathers matching the seller's outfit.

sections.heading: Notes

- The song played by the nomadic merchants is a simplified version of Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame's boss theme.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Mind** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Mind stat directly affects their FP totals. In addition, leveling Mind will also increase Focus, increasing the Tarnished's resistance to Sleep and Madness.

The Tarnished can level Mind by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Mind has a soft cap of 50 and 60 for increasing FP, and a soft cap of 40 and 60 for increasing Focus, with each derivative stat seeing diminishing returns after reaching these soft caps. Leveling Mind will not begin to see Focus returns until 31 and onwards.

A +0 Flask of Cerulean Tears replenishes 80 FP upon use, equivalent to 9/10 Mind, while a +12 Flask replenishes 220 FP, equivalent to 37/38 Mind.

sections.heading: Increasing Mind
sections.text:
- Fingerprint NostrumShadow of the Erdtree: Increases Intelligence by 6 for 90 seconds. Also increases Mind, Faith, and Arcane by 6 and drains 3 HP per second for the same duration.
- Marika's Scarseal/Soreseal grants +3/5 Mind, as well as Faith, Intelligence, and Arcane, but increases damage taken by 10%/15%. Cannot be worn at the same time.
- Navy Hood grants +1 Mind.
- Preceptor's Big Hat grant +3 Mind but decreases Stamina by roughly 9%.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Messages are an asymetric multiplayer mechanic, returning from many of FromSoftware's previous games, they allow players to potentially influence the gameplay experience of others through the sharing of cryptic, yet helpful hints, deceptive and unhelpful advice, jokes lightening the mood or sharing of one's rejoice of a glorious victory.
Messages are written through the use of the Tarnished's Wizened Finger.

sections.heading: Write Message
sections.text:
Players can place down messages in the hopes of them getting rated. Should a message be rated, whether they be applauded or disparaged the player who's message have been rated will get some of their HP restored.

Messages are constructed through the use of filling in two (to potentially six) different slots for preset phrases in the form of three different formats, Templates, Words and Conjunctions (players may also add a Gesture to the message in order to add some extra clarification in terms of directions or just to give the message more personality).

sections.heading: Message Compositions
sections.text:
There are four different message compositions the player can chose from each varying the amount of available options.
However the fourth composition is generally the most convenient since it'll still allow a message to be placed even if only the slots that are available in the first three compositions are filled.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.text: Templates usually include a section of "****"s, these will be filled in by whatever option the player has selected in the "Words" box.

sections.heading: Words
sections.text:
The "Words" box is used to fill in the "****"s of the "Template" section.
There are twelve different categories where the writer can get their words from.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text: Conjunctions become available should the first two "Templates" and "Word" boxes not be enough for the message's clarity and will serve as a transition between the first set of templates and words boxes into the newly revealed second set.

sections.heading: Gestures
sections.text:
Adding a Gesture will make a phantom version of the writer perform said gesture while other players are reading the message.
Any Gesture that the player has found on their journey will be available for selection.

sections.heading: Messages Written
sections.text: You can leave a total of 10 messages at a time. Once you've made an 11th message the game will automatically remove your oldest message no matter how highly rated it is.

sections.heading: Messages Discovered
sections.text: Any messages you've read recently will be stored in this section for later reference and rating. The game can only remember 10 messages at a time though, so the moment you've read your 11th message, the oldest discovered message will be removed.

sections.heading: Rating Score
sections.text: Messages will have their icons change over time depending on how many ratings it has received.

**Memory Slots** is a base stat in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished has two Memory Slots by default, and this amount can be increased through finding Memory Stones throughout the Lands Between. There is also a Talisman, Moon of Nokstella, which will increase the Tarnished's Memory Slots by 2. The Tarnished can have a maximum of 12 Memory Slots after finding all of the Memory Stones and equipping the Moon of Nokstella Talisman.

Memory Slots are used in order to equip Sorceries and Incantations at Sites of Grace, and must be set before magic can be used.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Misbegotten Crusader** is an optional Enemy boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Misbegotten Crusader is a Misbegotten Warrior—a feral humanoid marked with bestial traits: claws, feathered wings, serpentine tails, and a thick crimson mane. Like other Misbegotten, its form is viewed as punishment for ancient contact with the primordial Crucible. It wields the Golden Order Greatsword—the sacred sword forged by Elden Lord Radagon—and is capable of using its unique skill, Establish Order.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: - At the bottom of the Cave of the Forlorn, located in the eastern Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- 93,000 runes
- Golden Order Greatsword

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: The Misbegotten Crusader wields the Golden Order Greatsword and deals  Standard and  Holy damage attacks. It is highly aggressive and mobile, and it may be challenging to find openings to attack it. It can buff itself with Red Eyes when it uses its Barbaric Roar.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Golden Order Greatsword is one of the Legendary Armaments.
- After divesting himself of St. Trina in the Stone Coffin Fissure, Miquella the Kind left behind a golden Misbegotten Warrior to guard his discarded other half.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Nomads are withered, tormented musicians with gold and silver hair whose filthy white robes hang loosely to their frail frames. They play a somber melody on their stringed instruments using bows that terminate in a five-fingered hand. They are the ancestors of Merchant Kalé and the Nomadic Merchants.

They are found exclusively in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, between the  Cathedral of the Forsaken and the  Frenzied Flame Proscription Sites of Grace. A single Nomad can be found playing the nomadic merchant song on his instrument on the way down to the Frenzied Flame Proscription. He will remain non-hostile until the player provokes him by attacking.

Nomads wield the Frenzied Flame, which they release in deadly volleys in combat. They deal  Standard and  Fire damage and inflict  Madness buildup.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The nomads once comprised the Great Caravan, a once-thriving tribe of merchants and traders in the Lands Between. However, with the rise of Queen Marika, they found themselves spurned by the Grace of her Erdtree. Like many others, the members of the Great Caravan were left to struggle at the fringes of society. They did not mind their situation, but were deeply unforgiving toward those who would harm them.

A maddening sickness followed the nomads wherever they went, and they were accused of harboring the Flame of Frenzy. Soon, the entire clan was rounded up and confined to a claustrophobic catacombs in the suffocating depths below Leyndell, Royal Capital—buried beneath even the accursed Omen. Immured within the Frenzied Flame Proscription, the nomads chanted a curse of despair, summoning the heretical Three Fingers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Nomads are immune to  Sleep ailment buildup.
- They share several moves with the surface-dwelling Nomadic Merchants; however, their Frenzied Flame attacks are more potent and they can't cast buffs on themselves with their musical instruments.
- The nomads of the Great Caravan were adverse to settling down, predisposing them to chaos. Their confinement under the Golden Order took away their nomadic lifestyle.
- The Nomads' hand bow and robe cannot be acquired.
- Their attacks can demolish the tents in the area, allowing access to the items underneath.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Nomads use a highly detailed animation when playing their instruments. Their fingers accurately slide to the correct spots to produce the notes being played.
- Their immunity to Sleep may be a holdover from a cut iteration of the Nomadic Merchant story that involved St. Trina and Slumber Fog.
- A cut version of Merchant Kalé's questline allowed him to discover the fate of the Great Caravan.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Millicent's sisters** are adopted daughters of Sage Gowry and siblings of Millicent. These red haired girls once sprouted as buds from the Scarlet Aeonia found within the heart of Caelid. They all wear the Traveler's Set and use weapons and skills associated with either aspects of their inadvertent mother Malenia, both her role as the unalloyed blade of Miquella and her looming transformation into the goddess of rot. They all seek to aid their adoptive father in cultivating Millicent into a Scarlet Valkyrie.
__TOC__

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
All sisters can be found in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree towards the end of Millicent's questline.
To reach them the player needs to:
- 1. Retrieve the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle by defeating Commander O'Neil in the Heart of Aeonia.
  - Optional: Polyanna, Adopted Daughter can be summoned as a cooperator to assist in this fight.
- 2. Give the snapped needle to Sage Gowry at Gowry's Shack so that he may repair it.
- 3. Reload the area by either:
  - A. Resting at/teleporting to a Site of Grace
  - B. Exit to the Main Menu and then enter back into the game.
- 4. Retrieve the repaired needle from Gowry and then give it to Millicent at the Church of the Plague.
- 5. Reload the area by resting or teleporting to a grace then exhaust the dialogue of the now lucid Millicent.
- 6. Reload once more so Millicent moves to Gowry's Shack then exhaust her dialogue there.
  - Optional: The player may now summon Millicent to assist in the fight against Magma Wyrm Makar in Ruin-Strewn Precipice.
- 7. Defeat the Godskin Apostle at the peak of Dominula, Windmill Village.
  - Optional: Millicent can be summoned as a cooperator to assist in this fight.
- 8. Reload the area so Millicent may appear at the top of the Windmill Village and exhaust her dialogue.
  - Optional: The player may now summon Millicent to assist in the fight against the Draconic Tree Sentinel in Capital Outskirts.
  - Optional: The player may also summon Millicent to assist in the fight against the Black Blade Kindred in the Forbidden Lands.
- 9. Millicent will now appear by the Ancient Snow Valley Ruins Site of Grace at Mountaintops of the Giants. Exhaust her dialogue there.
- 10. Millicent will next appear by the Prayer Room site of grace in the beginning of Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. Exhaust her dialogue there.
- 11. Defeat the Putrid Tree Spirit found in the isolated pool of Scarlet Rot just before the Drainage Channel site of grace in Elphael.
  - Optional: Players may talk to Sage Gowry at this time to unlock another option for the next step in Millicent's Quest.
- 12. One/Two summon signs will appear on a hill next to the pool of rot. The player may chose one to influence the end of Millicent's questline.
  - A. Assist Millicent: Accepting the Gold Sign will summon the player to help defend Millicent against her sisters. Failing in this task by either the player or Millicent dying will send the player back to their own world but allows them to retry assisting her or change to the other side. Succeeding in this task will reward the player with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia and then the purified Unalloyed Gold Needle.
  - B. Challenge Millicent: Accepting the Red Sign will summon the player to help the sisters in killing Millicent. The player dying to Millicent will send them back to their own world but allows them to retry their attempt of killing her or change to the other option of assisting her. Succeeding in this task will reward the player with the Millicent's Prosthesis talisman.

sections.heading: Details
sections.text:
Unlike her sisters Polyanna can be encountered long before the confrontation at Elphael.

She can be summoned within the Swamp of Aeonia as a friendly cooperator against Commander O'Neil to help retrieving the snapped needle for Gowry.

Her Summon sign can be found directly south of the Inner Aeonia site of grace, en-caved among the tall roots of the Aeonia flower that are erupting directly up from the ground.

sections.heading: Polyanna's Appearance
sections.text:
Polyanna has a slender body, fair skin and the left half of her face is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

Her right eye is covered with a white eye-patch and her visible left eye reveal that they are slightly clouded with a golden-yellow iris and a darkened, near-black sclerae.

She has faded orange-red hair tied into a bun at the back of her head, her forehead is covered with bangs that have been cut horizontally at the height of her eyebrows, along with thinner bangs on the sides reaching down to the height her chin.

sections.heading: Amy's Appearance
sections.text:
Amy has a slender body, fair skin and the upper half of her face from the top of her cheeks to her forehead, is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

She has small pursed lips and both of her eyes are covered with a white blindfold. Despite not being visible, her eyes share the same features as Polyanna.

She has a faded orange-red, unkempt hair that reaches down to her shoulders, enveloping most of her whole head and even the right side of her face.

sections.heading: Maureen's Appearance
sections.text:
Maureen has a slender body, fair skin and the upper-left half of her face is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

Her left eye is covered with a white eye-patch and her visible right eye reveal that her sclerae is also darkened like her sisters however unlike them, her iris and pupils are almost completely clouded over.

She has chin-length, curvaceous, faded orange-red hair covering most of her head. An opening revealing her face beginning on the right side of her forehead before curtaining out to the sides. where they eventually begin flowing back in towards the cheeks to then finally curve back outwards to the sides.

sections.heading: Mary's Appearance
sections.text:
Mary has a slender body, fair skin and the upper half of her face, from the top of her right cheek to the left-side top of her forehead is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

She has both of her eyes are covered with a white blindfold. Despite not being visible, her eyes share the same features as Polyanna and Amy.

She has long faded orange-red hair that reaches down to her collar bone, an opening beginning on the upper left side of her face before curtaining outwards into large fluffy bangs framing her face.

sections.heading: Tactics
sections.text:
Successfully assisting Millicent can be accomplished with relative ease even with a character that hasn't leveled any of their attributes or weapons yet, as Millicent herself is significantly more powerful than any of the sisters individually. Her damage is high but her health is relatively low, so Millicent's safety is at the most risk only when she's greatly outnumbered and the majority of her sisters are attacking her at once.

Due to Millicent's high damage (particularly from her Waterfowl Dance), the player can equip the Shabriri's Woe Talisman and/or any pieces of the Duelist Set or Rotten Duelist Set to make the majority of the sisters more easily prone to chase them around the environment, leaving Millicent to deal with a single sister one at a time.

]]
Since Polyanna can cast Pest Threads, she's the only one who can harm the running player from a distance and so it's preferable to leave her with Millicent first so she can eliminate Polyanna before she becomes a problem for the player.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Maureen's Treespear is unique and impossible to replicate by the player as it has Charge Forth. Instead the version the player has access to cannot be infused with Ashes of War and it has Sacred Order as it's default skill.
- It's possible to infer that Millicent may be the fourth sister to sprout from the Heart of Aeonia due to the fact that Polyanna is still present in Caelid at the start of the questline while her older sisters are comparatively absent, due to them likely having a head start on their journey to the Haligtree as they would have been born earlier than both Millicent and Polyanna.
- Since Malenia and Millicent can both blossom into giant flowers on death, it brings into question the large flower found in a chamber near the Haligtree Roots site of grace. It is unclear whether this is an earlier bloom from Malenia herself, as a copy of the Traveler's Set that can be found next to it may imply it is from one of the four sisters. However considering how much higher Gowry seems to value what Millicent's potential flower is likely going to be compared to her sisters, it may be from a sister we haven't heard of before.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Millicent's Sisters had different nameplates in : **Amy, Third Daughter**, **Mary, Eldest Daughter**, **Maureen, Second Daughter**, and **Polyanna, Youngest Daughter**.

sections.heading: Etymology
sections.text:
- ***Polyanna*** is derived from a combination of the names *Polly* (which in of itself has roots from the name *Mary*) and can mean "sea" and *Anna* (Derived from the Hebrew name *Hannah*, meaning "grace").
  - "Polyanna" has also been historically used as noun to describe an excessively cheerful or optimistic person. Stemming from the name of a character created by US writer of children's stories, *Eleanor Hodgman Porter*.
- ***Amy*** stems from French and means "beloved" or "well-loved". It's derived from the Latin word "amare" which in of itself means "to love".
- ***Maureen*** and ***Mary's*** names both stem from the same Hebrew name *Miriam*. It can translate to "drop of the sea", "bitterness", "beloved" and "wish for a child".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Messmer the Impaler** (串刺し公、メスメル, *Kushizashi Kō, Mesumeru*), later known as **Base Serpent Messmer** (邪な蛇、メスメル, *Yokoshimana Hebi, Mesumeru*), is a mandatory remembrance boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Messmer is a Demigod who is encountered in the Shadow Keep. He is the source of Messmerfire and the Messmer's Flame incantations.

Messmer is **not** an optional boss as he must be defeated in order to acquire Messmer's Kindling that would allow the burning of the Sealing Tree at the Church of the Bud.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Messmer was born to Queen Marika the Eternal prior to the Second Liurnian War. His birth was cursed by a dark entity, an evil serpent coiled within that threatened to subsume him. Known to Messmer as the Abyssal Serpent, this force was restrained only through Marika's intervention—she removed her son's right eye and replaced it with a seal of her Grace. Ever since his accursed birth, Messmer was in constant company of the winged serpents, friends who suppressed the base serpent.

Much like his younger sister, Messmer bore a vision of fire. and he despised the flame inside himself, and time and time again hoped to rid himself of it, but found that it ever burned.

At some point, Messmer befriended Commander Gaius, an Albinauric who, like him, was cursed from birth and akin to an older brother to General Radahn, Gaius' fellow student in the art of gravitational sorcery. Gaius would go on to command Messmer's armies during the crusade.

sections.heading: The Crusade
sections.text:
Toward the end of the Age of Plenty, Messmer was charged by his mother with carrying out a purge of the tower-dwelling hornsent of the Land of Shadow, who did not bear the light of grace. At some point during his Crusade, Messmer was abandoned in the Land of Shadow, but continued to zealously enforce the purge even though Marika used him as a scapegoat and ceased all contact with him. Messmer came to reside in a fort known as the Shadow Keep.

Key in his army were the Black Knights, commanded by Black Knight Commander Andreas and his son and second-in-command Black Knight Captain Huw. Although they remained devoutly loyal to Messmer despite his abandonment by Marika, they ultimately rebelled upon learning of his serpentine nature. The pair were imprisoned in an underground tomb, and despite his betrayal, Messmer mourned the loss of Huw, whom he had considered a brother-in-arms. His Fire Knights would also refuse to follow the orders of burning the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and the destruction of the specimens in the Specimen Storehouse.

Eventually, an intruder invaded Messmer's stronghold, the Shadow Keep, and was noticed by the demigod's serpents, who identified them as a Tarnished Champion and a pretender to the title of Elden Lord. Though surprised that a Tarnished had come to the Land of Shadow, Messmer nonetheless attacked them to continue enforcing the purge. However, the serpentine demigod struggled overcome the Tarnished. Unwilling to accept "a Lord devoid of light" and desperate to regain the upper hand, Messmer ripped out Marika's seal and unleashed the power of the Abyssal Serpent, allowing him to frequently transform into a massive serpent. Nonetheless, the Tarnished was able to land a fatal blow upon Messmer. Realizing that his mother had indeed forsaken him, Messmer used his dying breath to curse Marika.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text: Hornsent can be summoned for this boss. His summon sign is found inside of the boss room, and will appear if the player decides to side with him against Leda or ignore this part of Leda's quest.

sections.heading: Phase One
sections.text:
The attacks of **Messmer the Impaler** are imbued with fire damage, making him a formidable opponent who relies heavily on his spear's reach and agility. To proceed in this boss fight, readiness for his swift movements is important. When fighting Messmer at a close range, you will have more chances of retaliating and chipping away at his health while he recovers. Engaging Messmer patiently is the best strategy to effectively take him down. When he finishes a string of attacks, focus on breaking his poise by pulling off heavy attacks for a chance to deal significant damage.

Because of his speed, Messmer can quickly transition between offense and defense by quickly disengaging with a leap after he finishes a move. Be aware that Messmer counters swiftly after sustaining damage, too. As his speed and precision in combat are his biggest asset, observation is required to avoid being overwhelmed. Once Messmer's health is half-depleted, a cutscene will trigger, which will start Messmer's second phase.

sections.heading: Phase Two
sections.text: During the second phase, **Base Serpent Messmer** remains at 50% HP and not only retains his original attacks, but also introduces a set of new and more lethal attacks with the help of the Abyssal Serpent. Among the fresh additions to his move set is the ability to transform into a large red serpent that rises up to the ground to throw a fireball or do bite attacks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Messmer was likely born earlier than the other Demigods. Exactly when he was born remains unknown, as all mention of him was erased by his mother after she abandoned him in the Land of Shadow.
  - He is older than Radahn, who was born before Miquella, Malenia, Trina, and Ranni.
- Although not explicitly stated, Messmer is strongly implied to be an Empyrean child of Marika and Radagon, born of a single god.
  - Messmer has the red hair of Radagon and his children.
  - Messmer was cursed at birth by a threat to Marika's power.
  - Radagon's motif in *The Final Battle* is echoed in the soundtrack for Messmer's boss fight, *Messmer the Impaler*.
  - Messmer is linked to Black Pyreflies, one of four butterflies found in-game, two of which are associated with Empyreans born from a single god. The Smoldering Butterflies correspond with Melina.
  - Seals are placed on his eyes.
- Messmer is the elder brother of Melina, as both she and his younger sister were daughters of Marika with visions of fire.
  - Melina serves as kindling to burn the Erdtree, and Messmer's Kindling can burn the Sealing Tree.
  - Melina, who has a corresponding butterfly and faded red hair, must also be an Empyrean child of Marika-Radagon because the game makes the distinction that Messmer and Radahn, his half-brother, are not brothers; Messmer acted like an elder brother to Radahn, but was not one.
- Upon his defeat, Messmer denounces Marika and curses her with his dying breath. This is the only time he refers to his mother by name.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Messmer's name may be a nod to German physician Franz Mesmer, who theorized about the existence of "animal magnetism" (a universal, invisible force or "magnetic fluid" that he supposed connected all living things and was capable of curing diseases, later referred to as *mesmerism*). Mesmerism would eventually come to be associated with hypnosis and is today considered a synonym for the former (with the term "mesmerizing" coined after it).
- Messmer's epithet is most likely inspired by Vlad III, commonly known as "Vlad the Impaler" (Romanian: *Vlad Țepeș*; rendered in Japanese as "串刺し公" (*Kushizashi Kō*)), who was one of the historical inspirations for Bram Stoker's novel **. Like Vlad III, Messmer has a notable draconic motif: while "Dracula" means "son of the dragon" (Vlad's father was called Vlad Dracul), Messmer for his part wears a helm shaped like a dragon's head, dons armor resembling the Drake Knight set, and has a snake with dragon wings.
- Messmer's visual design was likely inspired by the marble sculpture of Laocoön and His Sons, which depicts a pair of serpents winding circuitously around a priest and his sons, whose divine punishment for attempting to destroy the Trojan Horse and expose the trap is misinterpreted by the Trojans as proof that Laocoön was the real traitor and that the horse was trustworthy. This sculpture is famous for being one of the greatest examples of dynamic motion and emotion of its time.
- Messmer has an unused voice line that would have played during the cinematic for his boss fight. He would have told the Tarnished, *"Miquella spoke of thee..."*
