sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Poison** is a status effect in *Elden Ring*, inflicting damage over time to the player and serving as a less dangerous variant of the Scarlet Rot status effect. The player's resistance to this status ailment is determined by their Immunity stat, which is increased by the Vigor stat.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.text: Poison accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Immunity stat, the longer it will take for Poison to become effective. Immunity can be increased by increasing the Vigor stat. Once effective, the player will receive continual damage over time until the effect wears off.

sections.heading: Types of Poison
sections.text:
The damage received from poison can vary greatly depending on the source and the target inflicted. In general, poison is split up into two categories: Normal and Deadly.

**Normal**  poison is generally the most common and is automatically granted to any weapon that has it's affinity changed to Poison with one exception.

**Deadly**  poison is innate to the weapons that already come with it and damages it's targets at a faster rate than normal poison. However, it does not last as long and the total damage received from a single proc of Deadly Poison is ultimately lower than Normal Poison.

sections.heading: Skills
sections.text: Ash of War: Poison Moth Flight has a unique property that allows it to inflict burst-damage through an un-named Blood Loss-like status effect on targets that are already poisoned. Damage received is mostly based on a percentage of the Target's total HP pool. Triggering this effect will instantly cure the target's poison ailment making it most efficient when applied just before their affliction is about to wear off. This is a downside particularly in Online-PvP, as the effect can trigger while the target is in i-frames, allowing them to take no damage from the proc while at the same time be cured of their poison status. However this property can also be taken advantage of, as this allows the player to constantly re-trigger the Kindred of Rot's Exultation buff from continuously poisoning the same target multiple times in quick succession.

sections.heading: Buffs related to Poison
sections.text: There are certain equipment that gives the player buffs when poison has been inflicted in the general vicinity, they do not discriminate between what has been poisoned in order to activate, it can be friend, foe and even oneself and generally lasts for around 20 seconds since the last poison infliction.

sections.heading: Swamps
sections.text:
Poison swamps can be found in several locations throughout the Lands Between.
They generally comprise of bodies of filthy sludge that continuously build up Poison as the player is standing in them. Rolling around in said sludge will also cover the player-character's body with the fluids, which will slowly yet consistently build up poison even if the player is no longer directly standing in the liquid itself or even tries to cure their poison ailment with boluses. While these stains will gradually wear off over time, they can be removed immediately if it's raining, the player rolls around in clean water or uses Soap.

sections.heading: Traps
sections.text:
Poison traps are environmental hazards that are deployed by Vulgar Militia.
They come in the form of a cluster of small spiked balls on the floor. Coming into contact with these will make them explode, releasing a poisonous gas that obscures the players vision, while also making any Vulgar Militiamen hiding in the general vicinity spring forth and ambush the player in the ensuing smokescreen.

Poison traps can be found in a few areas of the game:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Poise** is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Poise allows them to resist being staggered or knocked down by enemy attacks. Poise is granted through equipping armor and talismans, as well as other effects.

Non-Tarnished enemies have two separate systems of Poise. The regular Poise system, same as the one used by player's where they are interrupted if dealt more Poise damage within a short time span, and the Stance system, where they are stunned and become vulnerable to a Critical Attack (except for horse-locked enemies such as Tree Sentinels and Night's Cavalry) if dealt enough Stance damage in a short time span (the Stance "health bar" resets after between 8 and 20 seconds depending on the enemy, unless at least 1 Stance damage has been dealt to the enemy in which case the timer is reset again and the health doesn't regenerate).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Primeval Sorcerer Azur** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Azur is one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and the originator of the Karolos Conspectus, considered to be the oldest and most venerable lineage of study at the Academy of Raya Lucaria, dedicated to pursuing the mysteries of comets. Azur was Sorceress Sellen's first teacher at the Academy, and she vieweed him as a stern judge of character. He glimpsed into the primeval current, where he saw darkness, leaving him both bewitched and fearful of the abyss.

Along with Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, another founding glintstone sorcerer, Azur was driven from the Academy. He settled on Mt. Gelmir, on the outskirts of a Hermit Village populated by Glintstone Sorcerers and Demi-Humans. His body became overrun by blue-green glintstone and he achieved a near-inorganic state, with his glintstone crown replacing his brain and skull.

The Tarnished discovers him on Mt. Gelmir, protected by a group of sorcerers and Demi-Human Queen Maggie. Azur reaches out to the Tarnished and grants them his legendary sorcery, Comet Azur. After revealing Azur's location to Sellen, and subsequently discovering the whereabouts of Lusat, Sellen has the bodies of the two sorcerers moved to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, planning to use them to hone the primeval current.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Azur's Glintstone Staff can be found in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, in a room above the Church of the Cuckoo Site of Grace, guarded by a Noble Page. The room also contains an inactive Graven Mass and a portrait of a woman resembling the Witch's Glintstone Crown.
- The Karolos Glintstone Crown resembles a portrait seen in several places in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. As the Karolos Conspectus began with Azur, it is possible that both the portrait and the headpiece are modelled after his original appearance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Primeval Sorcerer Lusat** is a character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Primeval Sorcerer Lusat hailed from Sellia, a town of magic-practicing assassins located in the eastern Caelid Wilds.

Lusat was one of the founding glintstone sorcerers of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. His inquiry into meteors at the academy formed the basis for his Olivinus Conspectus. When he glimpsed into the primeval current, he witnessed the final moments of a great star cluster—the sight of which broke him.

Lusat was exiled alongside Primeval Sorcerer Azur when the Carian Royals gained control of the academy. He returned to his home but at some point he was locked inside the Sellia Hideaway, thanks to a barrier which could only be broken using a Sellian Sealbreaker. In this cave his body became corroded by glintstone as he attained a near-inorganic state, his blue glintstone crown entirely replacing his brain and skull.

After the Tarnished discovers the similarly inorganic body of Azur on Mt. Gelmir and reports his whereabouts to Sorceress Sellen, she entrusts them with a Sellian Sealbreaker and tasks them with tracking down Lusat's body.  The Tarnished discovers Lusat, almost immobile and covered in blue crystals, and the sorcerer bestows upon them their legendary sorcery, Stars of Ruin. With both primeval sorcerers located, Sellen has their bodies moved to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, planning to use them to hone the primeval current.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Lusat's Glintstone Staff can be found in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, in a chest beneath a chair-crypt, accessible after defeating the Nox Nightmaiden and Nox Swordstress boss fight.
- The Olivinus Glintstone Crown resembles a portrait seen in several places in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. As the Olivinus Conspectus began with Lusat, it is possible that both the portrait and the headpiece are modelled after his original appearance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Omen** (忌み, *Imi,* or 忌み子, *Imigo*) are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Newborn children bearing horns were considered divine in ancient times. A potent spirituality suffused their oversized horns, a blessing of the primordial Crucible believed by the hornsent to mark them as a chosen people. These and other Crucible aspects were later deemed impurities during the reign of Queen Marika, who excluded those who bore them from her Grace of Gold.

The Omen's horns are imbued with wraiths and their blood is tainted. Without the Grace of Gold, they were shunned from society, their souls barred from returning to the Erdtree. Royal Omen, including the twins born to Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey, were secretly banished to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell, buried and shackled by golden magic for eternity. In contrast, the horns of commoners were severed, a brutal surgical procedure that few survived.

During times of war, conscripted Omen received curved cleavers that took advantage of their brute strength, though a worsening curse placed upon the blades ensured they would later be reclaimed. Additionally, wicked, horned elder spirits tormented Omen in their nightmares, and masked perfumers imitated these hideous spirits. Omenkillers mercilessly hunted and subdued Omen with blades decorated with amputated Omen horns. However, Perfumer Tricia and her partner instead provided aromatic treatments to the help Omen as they died.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Omen are hulking, blue-skinned brutes with small heads and silver hair. They have four fingers and toes, and twisted horns sprouting from their large bodies, though lowborn Omen bear bleeding stumps instead. Demigod Omen, such as Morgott, the Omen King and Mohg, Lord of Blood, have scales, tails, and even black-feathered wings.

Accursed Omen, born of royalty, possess some horn growth but are forced to live underground in secrecy. They harbor some amount of wraiths, which they can expel from their mouths at foes. The Strong Accursed Omen, capable of unleashing a barrage of wraiths in a fiery explosion, consequently imbuing their weapons with their power. In this empowered state, they can slam their weapons with explosive force to release more wraiths.

Omen wrapped in black cloaks aligned with Death-Serving Commoners in worship of the Prince of Death, who was once Godwyn the Golden.

sections.heading: Omen Cleaver
sections.text:
The Omen wields an Omen Cleaver, a heavy-bladed, curved sword etched with a pattern that is the remnant of a deteriorating malediction. The swords have a deceptively long reach, which the Omen take full advantage of with their fighting style.

A hooded Omen with an Omen Cleaver can be found praying in front of a Minor Erdtree in Altus Plateau alongside human Death-prince Followers. Another can also be found in Altus, hidden in the depths of Auriza Hero's Grave. Though their horns may be excised, they can summon Fia's Mist.

sections.heading: Warped Axe
sections.text: The Omen wields an oversized Warped Axe with an almost melted appearance. While lacking the more extended reach of the Omen Cleaver, they are capable of mixing their swings with slaps and kicks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Fell Twins duo boss encountered on the bridge leading to the Divine Tower of East Altus are both Omen. Other Omen bosses include Margit, the Fell Omen, Mohg, the Omen, Mohg, Lord of Blood, and Morgott, the Omen King.
- The Dung Eater has the heart of an Omen and wears red armor resembling an Omen with severed horns. He spreads the Seedbed Curse that produces more Omen, and his Mending Rune of the Fell Curse turns everyone into Omen.
- Perfumer Tricia and her associates dedicated their efforts to treating Omen and other impure beings. When her efforts failed, she instead became their companion when they died, ensuring they could pass peacefully.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal names: **ShunnedChildSword** (ID: 214000)  and **ShunnedChildAxa** (ID: 214010)
- Localization Notes
  - The Omen are called 忌み (*Imi*), which would mean "Abomination" in this context.
  - They are also occasionally referred to as 忌み子 (*Imigo*), which means "Abominable Child", "Unwanted Child", or "Shunned Child."
  - Margit's "Fell Omen" title is 忌み鬼 (*Imi Oni*), meaning "Abominable Demon."
  - The Mending Rune of the Fell Curse is called 忌み呪いの修復ルーン (*Imi Noroi no Shūfuku Rūn*) "Mending Rune of the Abomination Curse" or "Abominable Curse", where 忌み (Imi) is the same word localised as "Omen." Therefore, "Mending Rune of the Omen Curse" would be a localization in line with the rest of the text.
  - The Omen Bairn items are called 水子 (*Mizuko*), which can refer to a newborn baby, or an aborted, stillborn, or miscarried fetus.
    - 水子供養 (*Mizuko kuyō*) is a Japanese Buddhist memorial service for those who have had a miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion. The ceremony is meant to comfort parental grief, guilt, or the soul of the fetus, sometimes in fear of its vengeful spirit. Statues of Jizō, a Bodhisattva thought to protect children, are commonly offered by temples, which may be the inspiration for the Omen Bairns.
- Possibly inspired by the Shope papilloma virus that causes rabbits to form horn-like growths.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Nox** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
<section begin="lore"/>
The Nox are the inhabitants of the subterranean Eternal Cities of Nokron and Nokstella. They are a grey-skinned, cold-blooded race known for wielding flowing weapons forged from the liquid metal of Silver Tears.<section end="lore"/> They used the Fingerslayer Blade and are responsible for the creation the Mimic Tear and Dragonkin Soldiers.

The Monks, Swordstresses, and Nightmaidens of the Eternal Cities are highly skilled warriors and clerics, distinguished by their flowing silk garments and veiled crowns. They wield unique flowing weapons, capable of reforming to suit their needs. The high-ranking nightmaidens cast a life-sapping silver mist.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
<section begin="lore"/>
Long ago, the Nox committed treason against the Greater Will and its vassal Fingers, fashioning crystalline helmets out of glass to ward off their intervention. However, they invoked the ire of the Greater Will and were banished deep underground, forced to live under a false night sky in eternal anticipation of the coming Age of the Stars, and of their Lord of Night.<section end="lore"/>

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- In the Japanese script, rather than being "banished deep underground," the Greater Will's ire 触れ (*Fure*, lit. touches, proclaims) the Nox deep underground and 滅ぼされた (*Horobosareta,* lit. destroyed, overthrew) them, leaving open the possibility the Nox were already living underground at the time, as the Eternal Cities architecture suggests. The kanji for destruction used in this context, 滅, is also used to refer to the **ruin** that Eternal Darkness manifested, and when Astel "**destroyed** at Eternal City and took away its sky," implying Astel's attack and the Greater Will's destruction of the Nox deep underground were one and the same event. This destruction may be the cause of the strange masses of petrified humanoids at Nokron, Nokstella, and Noklateo, the Shrouded City.
  - Additionally, this is said to have occurred 大古 (*Dai Inishie*), the same timescale given for the Fire Giants chasing the Ice Dragons from the Mountaintops and coming into conflict with the Zamor, placing the destruction of the Nox sometime after Bayle's rebellion and the proliferation of drakes but before the War Against the Giants.
  - Notably, the Nox use Gravel Stones in their Silver Tear experiments to create lightning-generating Tears, and manufactured Dragonkin Soldiers in a failed attempt to emulate the Ancient Dragons, suggesting they sided against Dragonlord Placidusax in Bayle's rebellion. It is possible that such conflict against the Greater Will's vassal dragons lead to its ire and the Nox's destruction.
- Although the English script describes Noklateo being "desolated in a single night and sealed underground" as a single action, in the Japanese script there is a line break between "A lost city desolated in a single night" and "Once sealed underground, it has now appeared on the surface" with no reference to it **re**surfacing, preserving the Japanese base games ambiguity on whether the Nox were already underground when they faced the Greater Will's ire.
- The Black Moon once provided a magical boon for the Nox of Nokstella.
- The Nox are the oldest known users of puppets. Some willingly became dolls.
- The Eternal Darkness spell used by came to symbolize the downfall of the Eternal Cities.
- Astel was the punishment inflicted upon the Eternal Cities.
- Nox descendants later founded Sellia, Town of Sorcery, where glintstone sorcerers used invisible night sorceries to carry out assassinations.
  - The Black Knife Assassins were fellow descendants of the Nox. They had personal ties to Queen Marika the Eternal. In the Japanese script they are referred to with the same word for descendant as the Sellians, fellow surface-dwelling invisible Nox-descended assassins, implying their origin likely lies in Sellia, or perhaps Ordina, where the Black Knives are found in greatest concentration to this day.
- The Nox collected Celestial Dew.
- A statue of a swordstress pours Celestial Dew into the Basin of Atonement at the Church of Vows.
- Silver Tears around Nokstella are charged with yellow lightning.
- The Silver Tears may have been an attempt to replicate the process by which the Golem Smiths imbued souls into Magma Tears to create Smithscript weapons.
- The Albinaurics are likely another creation of the Nox.
- The Snow Witch may be associated with the Nox.
- It is implied the Nox and or War Counselor Iji used the Fingerslayer Blade to sever the Ringed Finger from Metyr, Mother of Fingers, ending her link to the Greater Will.
- Cut content reveals that the Nox were once intended to be descendants of Marika in earlier drafts of the script. Additionally, the Eternal Cities are internally labeled as マリカ遺跡 (*Marika Iseki*, or Marika Ruins) while Nox enemies and Silver Tears are internally labeled as MarikaLineageMan and MarikaLineageSlime, respectively.

sections.text: **Phantom Bloody Finger** and **Phantom Recusant Finger** are consumable tools in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Using this item will make the Invader kneel for a second before teleporting to a random spawn location in proximity to the Host of Fingers of a recently invaded world.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Varies
- Phantom Fingers are temporary items acquired automatically upon invading another world. The Phantom Finger obtained depends on the invasion item used to invade the world.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The game uses the Host's current X and Z-coordinates to determine multiplayer spawn points; it does not take the Y-coordinate into account. This can lead to Invaders being placed at the top or bottom of a cliff, demanding an inappropriately lengthy detour. This item is helpful when the spawn point is less than ideal.
- Phantom Fingers can be used to escape to another location when spotted or cornered.
- Phantom Fingers can also be used to ambush an isolated Host of Fingers after luring their Furled Fingers far away.
- The effectiveness of this item varies based on the platform and the drive the game is installed on, as the game enters a Loading Screen upon using this item. The quicker the Loading Screen, the faster the maneuver.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Despite the phantom fingers received from using the Bloody Finger and Festering Bloody Finger having the same name, they are technically different items with their own unique icons.
- Despite technically being considered different items, their function and item descriptions are completely the same, including the Recusant version.
- When there is an over-leveled Furled Finger in a world, the game will try to adjust their stats to improve balance; decreasing their survivability by lowering their HP, Stamina, and FP, while reducing their damage-output by increasing the defenses of everything else against them, specifically, this includes invaders. However, before version 1.09 was released, there was a consistent bug that completely removed the invader's defense bonus against these co-operators (always after one of the phantom fingers had been used in that session), effectively giving the over-leveled Furled Finger all of their original, unscaled damage-output back against the invader alone.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Online** is a gameplay mode in Elden Ring. Bringing in aspects of cooperative, casual competitive play along with Invasions.
Multiplayer mainly takes on two distinct forms, there is the standard variant, which is spontaneous and variable in intensity and complexity and then there is Arena Combat.

sections.heading: Matchmaking
sections.text: For the sake of balance the game will primarily search for guests that are within a certain radius of the Host's character level as well as and the highest upgraded weapon the players has ever obtained. It does not matter if said weapon has been stored or even discarded, even if the player has completely removed access to said upgraded weapon the game will still count that weapon's level to their matchmaking radius.

sections.heading: Flasks
sections.text:
For the sake of balancing, multiplayer alters how many flasks charges different players have and how these charges are replenished based on what role said player is currently in.
The Hosts of Fingers will keep their maximum flask count and guests will have their flasks charges cut by half of what it usually is in their own world. If a guest's flask-count is an odd number in their own world then it will be rounded down to an even number when visiting another host's world, so if a guest wants to maximize their flask-count they should try to allot both of their flasks into an even number whenever possible.

sections.heading: Replenishing Flasks
sections.text:
Allies can have their flasks replenished from vanquishing enemy groups, killing Crimson Tear Scarabs and defeating Invaders.
Meanwhile Adversaries will have their flasks replenished from the death of any other player, whether it be a Furled Finger, Hunter or even a fellow Invader. The death of the Host of Fingers does not replenish flasks however as it will end the session anyway.

sections.heading: Arena Combat
sections.text:
- Duel
- United Combat
- Combat Ordeal
- Combat with Spirit Ashes

sections.heading: Passwords
sections.text: Located in it's own designated Multiplayer menu. Passwords are used to isolate potential connections and make it easier for specific players to connect with each other.

sections.heading: *Multiplayer Password*
sections.text:
Hosts who have inserted a multiplayer password may only be able to see the Summon Signs of players who have the same password and likewise the Summon Signs of a Guest with a password can only be seen by Hosts carrying the same password.

This option also completely removes Player-Level and Weapon-Upgrade-based matchmaking, allowing vastly under-leveled or over-leveled guests to join a host's world. Over-leveled guests will have their stats reduced in an attempt of preserving game-balance, though the effectiveness of this down-scaling varies greatly based on the Host's level compared to the guest and what kind of build the guest is using. Under-leveled guests do not get their stats scaled upwards.

sections.heading: *Group Password*
sections.text: Players can have a total of five active group passwords at a time. They do not influence the matchmaking system in any way and only serve as a means of letting players know that a Player Phantom, Message, Bloodstain or Summon Sign came from someone carrying the same Group Password. Players accomplishing a significant feat of progression in their own game will also let everyone carrying the same group passwords as them know of this feat while at the same time distributing a rune-boosting buff to those same players.

sections.heading: Passive Features
sections.text: Online has a number of passive features that are present at all times and require no direct input from the player to appear. These features include:

sections.heading: *Player Phantoms*
sections.text:
Spectral afterimages of other players exploring and interacting with the world in their own game. The moments captured are mere recent short recordings of their journey and are not quite real-time.

Outside of being a reminder than in some way one is never truly alone in the adventure, these momentary glimpses into the lives of other players may directly assist the person witnessing them in revealing potential secrets such as a seeing a phantom appear just as it walks through an Illusory Wall that the witness wasn't initially aware of themselves.

sections.heading: *Messages*
sections.text:
Players may leave messages comprised of differing combinations of preset words and phrases to either assist, deceive or lighten the mood of any other player who may come across them and read them.

Should a message leave a strong enough impression for the reader to rate them Good or Poor, either option results in the writer (should they be playing at the moment of rating) receiving a decent chunk of their HP healed.

sections.heading: *Bloodstains*
sections.text: Bloodstains appear at the location of a player's death. They are five second recordings of their last moments before being forcibly sent back to a Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: *Shared Accomplishments*
sections.text: Should someone with a group password either defeat a Shardbearer or reach the Credits screen in their playthrough, every other player who shares the same group password as them will receive a buff that increases the amount of Runes received from fallen enemies by 5% for five minutes.

sections.heading: Options
sections.text:
; *Cross-Region Play*
- **Perform Matchmaking:**
Makes it possible to play with other players from across the world with no region-based restrictions.
- **No Matchmaking:**
Disables the user's ability to play with other players outside of the their own designated region. The size of these regions vary greatly, as some may contain several countries at once like America, Europe or Africa, yet the singular country of Japan gets their very own region.
This feature is greatly reduced on PC as it effectively only has two regions it can group players into; Japan and everywhere else.

; *Send Summon Signs*
- **Enable:**
Prevents one's own summon signs from appearing in worlds with an Adversary present.
- **Disable:**
Allows one's own summon signs to appear in worlds with Adversaries present.

; *Voice Chat*
This option is absent on the PC version of Elden Ring.
- **Allowed:**
Enables in-game voice chat.
- **Restricted:**
Disables in-game voice chat.

; *Display Player Names*
Controls what name will appear above the health bars of other players. This option absent on the PC version of Elden Ring.
- **Character name:**
Displays the name that player chose for their character on the in-game Character Creation screen.
- **Online ID:**
Displays the player's PSN or XBOX username/gamertag.
; *Launch Settings*
This setting controls whether the game automatically attempts to log-on to the official Elden Ring Online servers after crossing the "PRESS ANY BUTTON" prompt on the title screen.
- **Play Online:**
- **Play Offline:**
This option is automatically set to "Play Online" at the start of a new profile, meaning players who have a functioning connection but are adamant to play specifically in Offline mode need to manually set it to "Play Offline" then either make a character first then quit to return to the title screen or turn the game off then boot it back up again. Starting the game in Offline mode adds a "LOG IN" prompt amongst the "CONTINUE", "LOAD GAME" and "NEW GAME" options on the main menu.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Puppets**, including **dolls** and **marionettes**, are a type of being in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: There are two main categories of puppets in the Lands Between: those made from cloth, wood, and metal, and those who were human. Some puppets are playable Spirit Ash items, and may lend their aid when summoned by the player. These puppets are living people whose soul has been snatched by another person while keeping their body alive. This allows the user to manipulate the body against the will of its owner.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The stars of the night sky influenced fate long ago, and so it was that the Eternal City gathered Starlight Shards in preparation of a special draught. Members of the Nox clergy imbibed cloudy, bluish-black tonics, yielding their bodies and souls to fate, becoming puppets. However, the practice nearly vanished after the Greater Will banished the Nox deep underground.

Crude, handmade dolls, such as the Marionette Soldiers and Avionette Soldiers, were created to serve sorcerers during the age of the Erdtree. They were turned towards martial ends during the Liurnian Wars instigated by the Erdtree. The avionettes swooped through the air with scythes, raining Fire Pots.

Certain puppets become vessels for the souls of others, such as Ranni the Witch and Sorceress Sellen. After the Night of Black Knives, Ranni acquired the puppet of her secret mentor, the Snowy Crone of the deep forest. Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant considered to be the greatest puppet ever created.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Paired Weapons** in Elden Ring refer to particular weapons that naturally come in a set of two, without taking up another equipment slot. When inputting to wield these weapons two-handed, the Tarnished will instead equip a second, identical weapon in their off-hand. This is different from **Dual-Wielding**, AKA **Power Stance,** which involves equipping two of the same type of weapon in both hands (ex. two Daggers, two Greataxes, etc.).

sections.heading: Paired Weapons VS. Dual-Wielding
sections.text:
Paired weapons differ from dual-wielding in a few distinct ways:

- Light attacks strike with both weapons
- Strong attacks strike with both weapons when using Fists and Claws (the Starscourge Greatsword and Ornamental Straight Sword only strike using the right-hand weapon)
- Can still guard with both weapons in-hand, allowing for Guard Counters
- Occupies only a single armament slot, and reduces Equip Load
- Weapon buffs such as Greases are applied to both weapons at the same time

Although two-handing paired weapons have these advantages, dual-wielding can potentially inflict more damage with dual attacks (L1 on consoles), and can potentially apply more status effects by applying different affinities/buffs to either weapon.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Various paintings can be found scattered across the Lands Between. Once the Player has discovered and interacted with the artwork, they're then able to perceive the soul of that painting's creator and retrieve unique items from their location. The location is the point of perspective depicted by the artwork itself.

The Painter Spirits are initially invisible when viewed from a distance, but will eventually reveal themselves as the player gets physically closer to them. Successfully locating the artist's spirit will make it dissipate before leaving a unique item behind for the player to pick up, an item that is usually thematically related to the artwork itself.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
<noinclude></noinclude><noinclude>

The **Prophet** was one of the five playable characters . It, along with the Warrior, would reappear in the final release, but with a different weapon, offensive spell, and sacred seal, and with slightly altered stats (Faith remained the same but it gained 1 more Vigor and Dexterity, and 4 more Arcane, and 1 less Strength and Intelligence, 2 less Mind and Endurance).

sections.heading: Recreating
sections.text:
Though this beta origin is mostly available in the form of the release version of the Prophet, some equipment has been changed.

The weapons, shield, and seal are acquirable early on: The Club is dropped by Club-wielding Demi-Humans with a 2% drop rate (not to be confused with the Spiked Club-wielding Demi-Humans, which are similar), and can also be gained by starting with the Wretch Origin or by buying it for  600 Runes from the Nomadic Merchant (Western Limgrave). The Rickety Shield is dropped by any Shield-wielding Demi-Humans with a 2% drop rate or by starting as the Prophet Origin. The Clawmark Seal is gained by going to Bestial Sanctum and giving Gurranq, Beast Clergyman 1 Deathroot, most easily gained by killing the Tibia Mariner at Summonwater Village.

Ash of War: Holy Ground is gained by destroying the Merciless Chariots inside of Auriza Hero's Grave in Capital Outskirts.

For the Armor Set, the entire 3-piece Prophet Set can be bought from the Hermit Merchant (Capital Outskirts) at Hermit Merchant's Shack. However, the Closed Network Test's Prophet Robe uses the visuals of the Corhyn's Robe, which can only be gained when Brother Corhyn dies, either because he's killed or because his questline ends.

For the two spells, Heal gained by either starting as the Prophet Origin or by buying it from Brother Corhyn for  1,500 Runes, while Beast Claw is gained by giving 5 Deathroots to Gurranq at the Bestial Sanctum.

Note that the Clawmark Seal's scaling being split between Strength and Faith means it can only apply half it's Incantation Scaling towards Heal.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.text:
The Prophet Origin is the most suitable origin as it has suitable stats for the equipment and also starts with the shield, the armor set, and one of the spells needed.

The Confessor and Wretch Origins are also suitable, as the former has very similar stats to the Prophet even though it lacks the equipment while the latter starts with the Club and has close enough stats to what's required that it could be made into a fitting build.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The  is a Boss in *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Interred within stone coffins and buried at sea in an age long past, the stagnant, congealed remains of tainted heroes eventually drifted toward the Gravesite Plain of the Lands Between, where all Death converges. Though putrescence was once incinerated in ghostflame by Deathbirds, the contents of the vessels leaked and pooled at the bottom of the Stone Coffin Fissure, where they lingered in endless wait for true Death.

When St. Trina fell into the depths of the Fissure, her gentle sleep intensified into a deadly poison. Her nectar-like blood pooled, sprouting flowers, creating the Garden of Deep Purple. A mass of putrescence imbibed this nectar, finding salvation in her velvet, eternal sleep. From this, the putrescence reformed into a Putrescent Knight sworn to Trina.

The Knight is both rider and mount, each lacking functional legs. It wields a vast, crescent-shaped cleaver of human bone and hardened putrescence, its strength drawn from the Knight's arcane power. It conjures putrescence-born Death Sorceries, transmuting liquor into spiritual explosions of bruise-colored ghostflame.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text:
- HP: 20,612
- Defense: 123
- Stance: 100
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken
- Deals  Standard,  Slash, and  Magic damage, and inflicts  Frostbite buildup

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Putrescent Knight appears to be a form of proto-Albinauric.
  - Its body has a silver color and it lacks lower legs like Elder Albinaurics.
  - It has a frog-like face like Young Albinaurics.
  - Its crescent-shaped cleaver draws power from the wielder's arcane attribute like Albinauric Staves.

sections.text: **Palace Approach Ledge-Road** is a Site of Grace located within the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Palace Approach Ledge-Road is found beneath a set of ancient ruins at the Mohgwyn Palace on the Siofra River. It overlooks a bloody swamp across a bottomless gorge to its northwest. The road heading northeast is populated by many Young Albinaurics who wait idly and sleep on the ground, although several Sanguine Albinaurics actively patrol the area. The path leads to a sprawling lake of blood pooling around enormous, petrified trees.

It is the first Site of Grace the player will come across should they follow Mohg's trail through the sending gate located by the western cliffs of Consecrated Snowfield, northwest of the Yelough Anix Ruins. However, the portal remains inactive until a Sanguine Noble (Invader) is defeated. This teleporter delivers the Tarnished to a linear cave that leads to the Palace Approach Cliff-Road.

If the player instead uses Pureblood Knight's Medal, then they can still reach this location by traveling either on foot or on horseback from the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum.

The damage of the ammunition won't matter, as one hit is enough to make the crow run off the nearby cliffs to its death, in its attempt attack the player in retaliation.

Primordial gold is a red-tinged alloy of gold inhabited by an ancient holiness said to be close in nature to life itself. It was born when Queen Marika used a Golden Seed to transmute the Crucible's matter into the Erdtree at the direction of the Two Fingers.

It also became the material for the armor and weapons of the Crucible Knights who served Godfrey, the first Elden Lord. The primal energy that dwelled within empowered their ability to channel the various Aspects of the Crucible. During the Shattering, the Godrick Knights used the red in the metal to symbolize their homeward yearning for Leyndell, Royal Capital. These soldiers were loyal Godrick the Grafted, the last of Godfrey's Golden Lineage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In the beginning, everything was the One Great. At some point, it was fractured by the Greater Will, creating divisions, births, and souls. According to the findings of the Glintstone Sorcerers, life began as stardust, born of this great rupture. The Three Fingers believe that the Greater Will made a mistake in fracturing the One Great, as it also resulted in torment, despair, affliction, sin, and curses. They seek a Lord of Chaos to bestow upon the Frenzied Flame, the power with which to melt away life, spirits, and all that divides and distinguishes. In so doing, they believe that all in creation shall return to the One Great.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
The **Primeval Current**, also known as the **procession of stars**, is an unseen location in Elden Ring.
The primeval current of glintstone sorcery is intrinsically tied to the cosmic vitality of the stars, shaping both the land and fate of the Lands Between. It is described as a torrent of glintstone flowing from a distant star cluster, often likened to a celestial procession of stars. However, its cosmic mysteries bewitch those who gaze into the current, often driving them to the brink of despair.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
]]
Long ago, the Greater Will triggered a great rupture in the One Great, scattering the ancient life of the stars across the cosmos. This celestial event is seen as the primordial causality that led to fractures, births, and souls.

The first star to arrive on the Lands Between carried Metyr, Mother of Fingers, daughter of the Greater Will. Later, a golden star descended, bearing the Elden Beast, which would become the Elden Ring. Later, many more of these shooting stars would become meteors that struck the Lands Between, giving rise to the Alabaster and Onyx Lords and lifting Farum Azula into the sky. During an age when Fire Giants ruled Flame Peak, an ancient astrologer on the Mountaintops of the Giants perceived the primeval current. Soon, the stars' amber rained down upon the Lands Between. This meteorological phenomenon introduced glintstone and glintstone sorcery to the world.

The Black Moon once hung over Nokstella, guiding countless stars. However, it was lost long ago. The Nox of Nokron used the Fingerslayer Blade against Metyr, a blasphemous act that enraged the Greater Will. In response, the Greater Will sent a malformed star from its lightless abyss through a portal to assault the Eternal Cities. In a hail of meteorites, Astel leveled the Nameless Eternal City and banished the Eternal Cities deep underground, disconnecting the Nox from the true night sky.

The Academy of Raya Lucaria was later founded by two glintstone sorcerers, Azur and Lusat, who sought to uncover the secrets of glintstone and the enigmatic crystalians. Both peered beyond the "wisdom of stone" into the primeval current and were irrevocably changed by what they saw. Azur was left bewitched and haunted by the abyss, while Lusat was shattered after witnessing the dying light of a star cluster. When the Carians, followers of the Moon and allies of the crystalians, gained control of the academy, they suppressed the study of the primeval current. However, Sorceress Sellen defied this ban, obsessively pursuing its secrets. She even transformed fellow sorcerers into Graven Masses—the seeds of stars. For her treachery, the Graven Witch was expelled from the academy.

Shortly after Miquella's vow, Queen Rennala's son Radahn harnessed Gravity Sorceries in defense of Sellia. In the ensuing Starscourge Conflict, Radahn stood alone against the stars—and prevailed. His victory halted their movement, thereby forestalling the fate of his sister, Ranni.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
The **Pureblood Knights** were once the oath-sworn champions of Mohg, Lord of Blood. Esteemed noble servants defined by their extravagant clothing and elegant swordsmanship. These men, along with their master, swore a pact of blood to each other, to one day establish a new and glorious dynasty. The oldest known member of this entourage is the commander, Sir Ansbach, a scholarly gentleman of noble manners and frightfully deadly swordsmanship. When Mohg became ensnared by Miquella's enchantment, Ansbach sought to challenge the ever-youthful demigod in an attempt to free his master. And while he managed to grievously injure the empyrean, Ansbach was ultimately defeated in the confrontation by having his heart stolen, just like his master.

Ansbach's defeat would mark the beginning of a degradation in the values of the Pureblood Knights. Who, in the belief that it could eventually bring about their desired dynasty, would begin to hunt their fellow man in order to harvest their blood and offer it as sacrifice to slake the thirst of Miquella's cocoon. Steadily gaining infamy as nothing more than depraved, blood-crazed zealots that stalk their own. With most of the newer members inaugurated at this time, the Bloody Fingers, being Pureblood Knights in name only.

sections.text: **Powerstancing** is a gameplay mechanic in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Powerstancing is a special L1 attack that is performed when holding two melee weapons of the same weapon type (e.g., Dagger and Erdsteel Dagger). Powerstance attacks swing both weapons, hitting twice and dealing higher damage per second (DPS) overall when compared to One-Handed and Two-Handed attacks. Additionally, the chain attack for Powerstancing is a four-hit combo; it strikes the enemy up to eight times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Paired Weapons replace Two-Handed attacks with a variation of powerstancing that requires only one weapon.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Its skill, Reduvia Blood Blade, is essentially a version of the Blood Blade skill that costs twice as much FP and deals a little less Stance damage in exchange for not costing any HP to cast and having 50% more base Blood Loss (90 instead of 60).
  - Since this skill hits with both the projectile and the blade, it deals much more damage and inflicts more Blood Loss build-up when used within the dagger's range.
  - Ultimately, Blood Blade will do about 4% more damage at half cost with equivalent Arcane and an Occult affinity, making it the stronger alternative if the user is willing to stomach the self-damage and the relatively lower Blood Loss isn't a problem.
- Not counting the Wakizashi this is the strongest dagger for a hybrid Dexterity/Arcane build and the second strongest dagger for a hybrid Strength/Arcane or pure Arcane build, after the Bloodstained Dagger.
  - However, the Bloodstained's advantage is rather slight, only 8 AP (Attack Power) for the Str/Arc build and a mere 1 AP for the pure Arc build and the Reduvia will consistently have 10 more points of Blood Loss build-up.
- Since this weapon has innate Arcane-scaling its innate Blood Loss will scales with that stat.
- The Bandit starting Origin has enough stats to wield this quite strong weapon without any level ups or stat increases.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Rejection** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Rejection produces a shockwave, knocking back enemies within a 2-meter radius and inflicting heavy Stamina damage to guarding enemies—180 in PvE and 220 in PvP—while also dealing 10 Stance damage.

Charging the spell increases the radius to 4 meters, Stamina damage to 220 in PvE and 275 in PvP, and Stance damage to 14.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  9 FP per cast.
- Costs  24 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 31.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Rejection has 0 Attack Power and deals no damage.
- Knockback occurs in the direction the caster is facing.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The player model is just under 2 meters tall, making it a useful reference for measuring the spell's reach.
- Although this incantation deals no damage, it can instantly kill enemies or other players by knocking them off edges.
- This spell easily knocks down most flying or jumping foes and can be used to break the Stance of many enemies.
- The knockback effect applies to Crystalians even while armored, breaking their Stance in 7 hits, or 5 hits if charged.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Rejection is one of the few offensive spells that deal no damage.
- Although this spell is affected by the Godfrey Icon when charged, its 0 damage output makes the 15% damage boost irrelevant.
- Patch 1.07: Increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
  - This increased the Stamina damage against guarding enemies from 150 to 180 when uncharged and from 180 to 220 when charged.
  - Stamina damage against guarding players was instead increased to 220 when uncharged and 275 when charged.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ruptured Crystal Tear** is a Key Item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Causes concoction to explode in mixed physick.
- Immediately after drinking the mixed physic, a pulsing, orange aura begins to emit from the player for 3.2 seconds before they explode.
- Explosion deals Holy damage. This damage can be increased by holy-damage-boosting Incantations like Golden Vow and Talismans like the Sacred Scorpion Charm.
- Stacking two Ruptured Tears increases the potency of the explosion, widening its radius and significantly increasing its damage dealt to other foes.
- The explosion deals a flat amount self-damage that cannot be mitigated by damage-reducing statuses, with 300 self-damage with one tear and 700 with two.
- Should the user survive the explosion then their character will be launched high into the air from said explosion before falling down again. This animation has i-frames.

sections.text: **Rune Arc** is a consumable Tool in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Consuming a Rune Arc grants the following effects:
- Slightly raises  maximum HP.
- Enables the effects of an equipped Great Rune.
These bonuses last until death or when the equipped Great Rune is switched for another, but are temporarily disabled whenever the user invades or is summoned to the world of another player. Rune Arcs remain active and can still be used when the user becomes a Host of Fingers.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Rune Arcs can be earned by completing online objectives**:
- All summoned Furled Fingers gain one Rune Arc upon when the area Boss is defeated, regardless of contribution.
- All present Invaders (Bloody Fingers and Recusants) gain one Rune Arc when the Host of Fingers dies, regardless of circumstances.
- All present Hunters gain one Rune Arc whenever an Invader dies, regardless of circumstances.

**Enemy Drops**:
- Rats and Giant Rats have a 1.00% chance of dropping x1 Rune Arc. Earthbore Cave and the  Beside the Rampart Gaol Site of Grace in Castle Morne, both in the Weeping Peninsula, are suitable farming locations.
- Frenzied Rats and Giant Frenzied Rats have a 0.50% chance to drop x1 Rune Arc.
- x1 is dropped by each of the following Volcano Manor assassination targets: Old Knight Istvan, Rileigh the Idle, and Great Horned Tragoth.

**Locations**:

- x1 is found on a corpse on a ledge in Sellia Crystal Tunnel in Caelid.
- x1 is found found on a corpse near where the Golden Seed is in Siofra River. Follow the small path along the cliff's edges to the north to find a small cave with the corpse and a campfire.

**Purchase**:
- x5 are sold for  4,000 runes each by the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold.
- x3 are sold for  4,000 runes each by the Nomadic Merchant near the Bellum Church in Bellum Highway.
- x3 are sold for  4,000 runes each by the Hermit Merchant at the Hermit Merchant's Shack in the Capital Outskirts.
- x3 are sold for  8,000 runes each by the Hermit Merchant in eastern Mountaintops of the Giants.
- x3 are sold for  8,000 runes each by the Imprisoned Merchant in the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum at the Mohgwyn Palace.
- x3 are sold for  8,000 runes each by Moore near the  Main Gate Cross in Gravesite Plain.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy** is a boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Volcano Manor.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Rykard was born the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala, head of both the Carian Royal Family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He had two siblings, Radahn and Ranni.

At some point, the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, was robbed of grace and hounded from the Lands Between. Rykard's father, Radagon, left Rennala to become Queen Marika's new consort and the second Elden Lord. Rykard and his siblings were thus raised to demigods by their new stepmother, Marika.

Under the Golden Order, Rykard was a ruthless justiciar who commanded a company of inquisitors. His inquisitors persecuted and mercilessly tortured those considered heretics to the Golden Order, such as the Albinaurics. He spent time in the volcanic Mt. Gelmir, where he discovered the ancient magma hexes of a forgotten serpent-worshiping religion native to the region, which he brought back into practical use as new sorceries. Rykard also travelled to a foreign land where he encountered a dancer by the name of Tanith, who he would eventually take as his consort.

Rykard was also known for the construction of the Iron Virgins, automatons which were capable of both battlefield carnage and abducting victims to transport them to the Volcano Manor.

Rykard's budding blasphemous inclinations led him to assist his sister, Ranni, in orchestrating the Night of Black Knives. On the night of the plot, Ranni rewarded Rykard with a slab of rock engraved with the traces of the Rune of Death, which would allow him to challenge the black beast of Destined Death, should the coming trespass one day transpire.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text:
At some point following the the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, and her offspring acquired the Great Runes. The maddening taint of their newfound strength led to the Shattering, a war between Marika's demigod descendants, each seeking to become the new ruler of the Lands Between.

Rykard was indignant, and viewed the Erdtree and the gods demanding that the demigods fight over miserly scraps of power to be debasing. He launched a blasphemous campaign against the Erdtree and the Greater Will. When he turned to heresy, taking by force became the rule, the gods themselves being no different. Rykard's ambitions, though blasphemous, marked him a worthy sovereign, and drew many followers to his cause who admired his heroic aspirations. His rebels were known as the Recusants.

Based in the Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir, his forces battled the armies of the Leyndell in what would become the most appalling battle of the Shattering, a wretched, unending war with no glory. Acts of cannibalism became a sickening reality across the battlefields, and some forces from both sides became afflicted with the Frenzied Flame sickness.

sections.heading: Blasphemy
sections.text:
At some point during the Shattering, Rykard fed himself, Great Rune and all, to the blasphemous serpent that dwelled inside Mt. Gelmir, an ancient traitor to the Erdtree, merging with the creature. In the final moments before being devoured, he briefly had a vision of the future wherein he witnessed a serpent devouring the world.

Following this, his lofty ambition degraded into gluttonous depravity. He fed on his greatest champions, and in the bowels of the serpent, they became the lord's family. Disturbed by what had become of their master and by the costly battles waged in his name, Rykard's forces abandoned him. Some attempted to put him to rest by searching for a mighty weapon capable of killing their lord. Such a weapon was found in the Serpent-Hunter, an enchanted spear crafted to hunt an immortal serpent in the distant past. However, all attempts made to take his life failed. The spear would come to reside in Rykard's chambers, left by a former Recusant who hoped a worthy champion might one day appear to wield it and spare the once-noble Rykard from further dishonor.

When Rykard gave himself to the elder serpent, the birth of the man-serpents followed, the deformed offspring of a repellent birthing ritual. One such man-serpent, known as Zorayas, would go on to be adopted by Tanith, and learn to assume an illusory human form in which she went by Rya. She was unaware of the origins of her birth, as Tanith concealed the truth of the Volcano Manor from her and insisted she was born of the grace of a king. It is implied that the woman known as Daedicar was one such woman subjected to the ritual, the biological mother of Zorayas and other man-serpents.

At some point before giving himself to the serpent, Rykard offered Tanith the Tonic of Forgetfulness to purge her memories of him. However, she refused, claiming "My Lord, there could be no greater distress than to forget you." Tanith was the only human known to stand with Rykard after he merged with the serpent of blasphemy; as in that moment, she was truly charmed by him. The Crucible Knight bodyguard of Tanith may have also served the Volcano Manor before Rykard was devoured, and as such, would have been the second human known to remain loyal, but this remains unknown. Tanith would continue her lord's legacy by leading a new force of Recusants, recruiting unsuspecting Tarnished after their return to the Lands Between following the end of the Shattering. The worthiest of these Tarnished champions would be granted an audience with Rykard, which ended with them being devoured by the serpentine demigod to increase his power further.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text: Eventually, a Tarnished champion managed to reach Rykard's chambers, and defeated the serpentine demigod to claim his Great Rune. Rykard took notice of this and awoke to confront the Tarnished, then pulled out a massive sword from the serpent's mouth, while boasting that they would join the Serpent King as family. After a hard battle, Rykard was ultimately slain by the Tarnished. Upon his death, he claimed "A serpent never dies",  proven true when his initially vanished corpse began to regenerate. After Rykard is slain, Tanith suggested she planned to soon depart, having no reason to remain at Volcano Manor. However, afterwards she secretly journeyed to Rykard's chambers and attempted to eat his tremendous corpse, muttering her hopes that Rykard might live on within her, just as he had the serpent.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text:
The fight consists of two distinct phases, each with its own health bar. Phase 1 must be beaten each time to reach phase 2.

The Serpent-Hunter can be found sticking out of a pile of corpses near the entrance to the arena, and can be obtained without alerting the boss. This weapon makes the fight significantly easier, as it produces blades of light when swung that allow for long-distance attacks.

Defeating this boss will terminate Tanith's questline, regardless of how far one has progressed it. Any Volcano Manor targets not yet unlocked will also be missed.

sections.heading: Phase 1 - God-Devouring Serpent
sections.text: The God-Devouring Serpent is slow-moving, surrounded by a pool of magma. The magma makes it difficult to get close without taking damage, however the Serpent-Hunter allows for one to attack from a safer distance. It uses a combination of quick biting attacks and eruptions of magma, as well as a poison attack.

sections.heading: Phase 2 - Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
sections.text: After reducing the Serpent's health to 0, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Rykard, armed with a sword, moves around the arena similarly to the Serpent, however his moveset is almost entirely new.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: Rykard's arena is a spacious cavern, dotted with piles of corpses and tall corpse pillars, which can be broken by Rykard's attacks. The size of the arena is helpful for avoiding Rykard's Rancor and Rancor Rain, as one can run around the room until the attack ends.

sections.text:

- As seen in the opening cutscene and his paintings, Rykard appears to have light red hair or, arguably, blond hair, in contrast to his direct siblings.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: is a character in Elden Ring. She is a Shardbearer Boss encountered in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. While this encounter is not required to advance the story, Rennala must be defeated to unlock the ability to respec, Moonlight Altar, and "Age of the Stars" ending.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The young Lunar Princess was an astrologer who gazed at the night sky and chased the stars. In her youth, Rennala and her younger sister, Rellana, encountered moons that one day made them champions. Hers was an enchanting full moon. Later, she bewitched the Academy of Raya Lucaria with her lunar magic, becoming its master. She prohibited study of the primeval current at the academy, exiling its founders, Azur and Lusat. She established the house of Caria as royalty and anointed the enchanted Carian Knights, heroes of the highest honors.

When the sorceries of the Carians were still only the prototypes of the latter sword-phalanx sorceries., Rennala gifted a braid of her hair to Rellana, who disavowed her birthright to join Messmer the Impaler in his Crusade in the Realm of Shadow.

In the age of the Erdtree, a champion known as Radagon led Queen Marika's armies against Liurnia of the Lakes. Rennala and the academy rallied forces to repel the invasion. She led her Glintstones Knights and, despite numbering fewer then twenty, their magic made them a match for even the champions of gold in battle. Two Liurnian Wars were fought, both of which saw no clear victor.

Radagon ended the Second Liurnian War by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew. Repenting his territorial aggressions, he swore his love to Rennala. They married at the Church of Vows, uniting the houses of the Erdtree and the Moon. As a Carian Queen, Rennala bestowed Radagon a Moon greatsword in accordance with a long-standing tradition. They had three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni. Rennala led young Ranni by the hand to meet her Dark Moon.

Later, Radagon gifted an amber egg, the Great Rune of the Unborn, to Rennala, and left her side to become the second King Consort of Queen Marika, receiving the title of second Elden Lord. When Radagon left, Rennala's heart left with him.

Realizing their heartbroken queen was no champion at all, the Academy rebelled against the Carian Royal Family and Rennala was locked away in the grand library. Clutching the amber egg left to her by Radagon, she dissociated, devoting herself to the grim art of reincarnation. She would use it on Juvenile Scholars found around her, calling them her "sweetings", continuously rebirthing them in an imperfect process which would leave their memories fading into oblivion. The children born anew by Rennala were all frail and short-lived, imperfect beings, each and all.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
Rennala remained in the Grand Library throughout the reign of Lord Radagon and the ensuing Shattering war. She hovered idly in the air, clutching her egg, while her reborn Juvenile Scholars sang a lullaby that shielded her in a golden, moonlike bubble.

If the Great Rune separates from Rennala, a protective mechanism activates, releasing a dense black fog. The disembodied voice of Ranni the Witch warns intruders as an illusory image of Rennala emerges from the darkness to battle the player upon a moonlit sea. This apparition reflects Rennala as she once was, at the height of her power.

If the illusion is defeated, the present Rennala regains her egg and sits quietly in her bassinet at the center of the library, calling softly to her timid sweetings.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: A tall, barefooted woman with an immaculate, pale complexion and lustrous black hair. She is dressed in deep blue and red robes with gold trim and wears a large hat curved like the crescent moon.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
- HP: 3,493 (Phase 1)
- HP: 4,097 (Phase 2)
- Defense: 109
- Stance: 0
- Cannot be parried
- Vulnerable to Critical Attacks after her Stance is broken
- Deals  Standard and  Magic damage
- This boss summons Juvenile Scholars during Phase 1. She summons Wolves, Troll Knights, Flying Dragons, and Bloodhound Knights during Phase 2.
- Drops:  40,000 runes, Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen, and Great Rune of the Unborn

Throughout both phases, Rennala resists magic but is more vulnerable to physical attacks.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Phase 1: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.text:
Rennala's first phase occurs in a circular room with an open inner area and a more narrow outer area, divided by bookcases. Rennala floats around the room encased in a golden sphere that prevents her from taking damage. The majority of her Juvenile Scholars congregate in the inner arena, however a few can be found hiding behind the bookcases.

Rennala rarely attacks directly during this phase. Instead, the Juvenile Scholars lunge, breathe fire, and use telekinesis to assault the player with the books and globes. They also drop chandeliers from the ceiling if the player stands underneath them. However, Rennala periodically converts scholars to gravestones, which she sends flying towards the player. She also summons new Scholars to replace those the player has slain.

One of the Scholars sings, surrounded by a golden aura. The song grows louder as the player draws near. Hitting the singing Scholar at least once—without necessarily killing them—causes another to begin singing. Disrupt three singing Scholars to shatter Rennala’s sphere, dropping her to the ground and leaving her vulnerable. While she lies stunned, the Scholars cease their attacks, giving the player an opening to strike. After a few seconds, Rennala releases a golden explosion and rises again, her protective sphere restored. Repeating this process several times creates additional opportunities to damage her.

Defeating Rennala triggers a cutscene, and advances the fight to Phase Two. A spell placed by Ranni the Witch on the amber egg activates, releasing a dense fog of darkness.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Phase 2: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.text:
After the cutscene, the arena transforms into a vast, moonlit watery plane with no obstacles or clutter. Ranni's illusory Rennala engages the player directly with a full health bar. She relies primarily on ranged magical attacks but also swings her staff to strike if the player approaches too closely.

When her health drops below 60%, she begins summoning spirits for assistance. Each time she summons, a glowing circle expands around her, dealing damage to anything within it. She can call forth a Bloodhound Knight, three wolves, a Flying Dragon, or a Troll Knight, each lasting only a few seconds before vanishing. During this phase, Rennala moves more evasively, making it difficult for melee fighters to land consistent attack chains.

Moving away from Rennala's homing attacks is simple, as there is nothing to get stuck on or blocked in by. However, there is nothing to separate Rennala from her summoned allies.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (NPC)
sections.text:
After defeating her, Rennala becomes an NPC, remaining in the library where she was fought in phase 1. As an NPC she offers two services: **Rebirth** allows the player to reallocate levels to different stats at the cost of a Larval Tear, while **Cosmetics** allows the player to alter their character's appearance, which is the same function that the mirror in Roundtable Hold has.

When Sorceress Sellen moves to the Academy of Raya Lucaria during her questline, she will temporarily occupy Rennala's spot, while Rennala will move behind one of the bookshelves in the library. She will return to her usual place once Sellen's questline is completed.

sections.page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wears the Queen's Set and wields the Carian Regal Scepter as her Glintstone staff. It is one of the best staffs in the game and it enhances full moon sorceries.
- Rennala survives their fight and may interact with the player. She is always found in the Grand Library at the top of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
- After Rennala is defeated, she allows players to change their appearance or reallocate their stats using her Rebirth magic. The process requires Larval Tears.
- When Sellen takes over the Academy, Rennala can still be found in the Grand Library, hiding behind some bookshelves. When Sellen eventually turns into a Graven Mass, Rennala is back in her place while Sellen is moved to the side of the library where she remains for the rest of the game.
- The approach to the Grand Library which houses Rennala is guarded by Moongrum, one of the last Carian Knights who once served the Lunar Queen. A Mad Pumpkin Head and Giant Silver Tear also protect the route.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Ranni the Witch**, also known as **Lunar Princess Ranni** and **Renna the Witch**, is a character in Elden Ring. She is one of the Demigods, and the focus of one of the game's most elaborate questlines.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A child born of the union between Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon and red-haired Radagon during the age of the Erdtree, Ranni embodied an alliance between Raya Lucaria and Leyndell. She had two older brothers, Radahn and Rykard. As a daughter of the Carian Queen, she was a Lunar Princess, and first heir in the royal line. Led by the hand of her mother, young Ranni encountered her Dark Moon—cold, dark, and veiled in occult mystery.

The Two Fingers named Ranni as an Empyrean, one with the potential to one day succeed Queen Marika as the divine ruler of the Lands Between, and granted her a Shadowbound Beast named Blaidd to be her vassal. He was approved of by Rennala and was raised as her foster brother. Ranni grew up playing with Blaidd, and they were often accompanied by Iji, a troll blacksmith who served the Carian royals.

At some point, Ranni's father abandoned her mother to marry Queen Marika and assume the title of second Elden Lord. Although Ranni and her siblings were raised to Demigod status by their new stepmother, their heartbroken mother was left indisposed, cradling her Amber Egg in all-consuming grief.

Ranni later ventured deep in woods, where she encountered a snowy crone who became her secret mentor. She was an old witch well versed in cold-based sorceries, and she taught Ranni to fear the Dark Moon as she imparted her magic. The full Dark Moon, cold and leaden, would become Ranni's sigil and symbol of her power and authority.

sections.heading: The Night of Black Knives
sections.text:
Although the Two Fingers had chosen her as Marika's successor, Ranni did not wish to be a puppet for the Greater Will and resented her Empyrean fate. In order to escape it, Ranni stole a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh, the Black Blade and, through a fearsome rite, imbued it into the blades of Numen assassins, who were said to be close to Queen Marika herself. She also gave a fragment to her brother Rykard as a last resort, so he could kill Maliketh if necessary. Ranni plotted for the assassins to kill another individual while she simultaneously killed herself, slaying her own body while the other person died in spirit, thus freeing herself from being an Empyrean.

In what would become known as the Night of Black Knives, the assassins murdered Godwyn the Golden, killing him in spirit, while Ranni killed herself in body, transferring her spirit into a doll said to be modeled after the image of her mentor, the Snow Witch. This marked the step-siblings as the first demigod casualties in history. Ranni's fate and her involvement in the plot remained largely unknown by the denizens of the Lands Between.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text: At some point after the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring. Ranni claimed a Great Rune, but appears to have discarded it, and largely remained outside of the conflict that followed. As a consequence of her doll body, Ranni required extended periods of hibernation and withdrew from the world, hiding in the Carian Manor while her agents worked to bring about her plan of ridding the Lands Between of the influence of the Greater Will, allowing her to pursue her divine ascension on her own terms.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
After the Shattering, Ranni learned of a recently arrived Tarnished riding the spectral steed, Torrent. She approached them at the Church of Elleh, inquiring whether they possess the steed that once accompanied Melina. Upon confirming her suspicions, she bestowed upon them a Spirit Calling Bell and Lone Wolf Ashes, explaining that Torrent’s former master had entrusted her with delivering these items to its next owner.

Ranni later reunited with the Tarnished at her Rise in the Three Sisters, where she invited them into her service. She tasked the Tarnished with aiding Blaidd in uncovering a path into Nokron, Eternal City, to claim its treasure—a weapon capable of slaying the Two Fingers who had chosen her as an Empyrean. However, the path to Nokron would only reveal itself with the death of her brother, Starscourge Radahn, who had long held the stars—and thus Ranni's fate—in stasis with gravity magic.

After Radahn's defeat and the acquisition of the Fingerslayer Blade, Ranni descended to the Ainsel River Main, leading to Nokstella, Eternal City. There, she commanded her champion to rid her of the Baleful Shadows sent by the Two Fingers to assassinate her. Upon their victory, Ranni rewarded the Tarnished with a key to a Carian chest containing the Dark Moon Ring. Then, Ranni departed to fulfill her dark purpose. She traveled to the Cathedral of Manus Celes on the Moonlight Altar, where she slew the great Two Fingers beneath it and abandoned her doll body.

If the Tarnished retrieved the Dark Moon Ring and presented it to Ranni's doll, she accepted them as her consort, granting them the Dark Moon Greatsword as a symbol of their union. She revealed the full extent of her plan: to succeed Queen Marika as god and bring about the Age of the Stars. Ranni intends to remove the Elden Ring from the Lands Between and journey into the cosmos, freeing its inhabitants from the influence of the Greater Will and granting them true autonomy over their lives.

After defeating the Elden Beast, the Tarnished may summon Ranni, who ushers in the Dark Moon and her Age of the Stars, realizing her vision for a new Order.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Ranni's disembodied spirit inhabits the woven puppet of a four-armed maiden with pallid blue skin and long, flowing blue hair. Her left eye—the doll's right—is sealed shut by an azure sigil, while both open eyes glow cyan. She wears an elegant white gown beneath a voluminous fur cloak, lined with two long brown braids. A massive, floppy-brimmed witch’s hat rests atop her head, crowned with a delicate silver filigree. Luminious blue veinwork runs throughout the frozen brim's cold underside.

sections.heading: Ranni's Quest
sections.text:
- Completing Ranni's quest will result in the "Age of the Stars" ending.
- Her questline intersects with the following NPCs: Blaidd the Half-Wolf, Castellan Jerren, Fia, Deathbed Companion, Pidia, Carian Servant, Preceptor Seluvis, Smithing Master Iji, and Sorcerer Rogier.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.text:
1. *(Optional)* Church of Elleh
  - After meeting Melina and obtaining the Spectral Steed Whistle, use Torrent at least once. After that, rest on any Site of Grace. Then, fast travel to the  Church of Elleh Site of Grace and find Ranni (using the pseudonym "**Renna the Witch**") sitting on a broken wall. Exhaust her dialogue to receive the Spirit Calling Bell and Lone Wolf Ashes for free.
  - If you miss this step, these items will be available for purchase at the Twin Maiden Husks in Roundtable Hold— 200 runes for the Lone Wolf Ashes and  1,000 runes for the Spirit Calling Bell respectively.
1. Caria Manor
  - Traverse Caria Manor in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes.
  - Defeat the apparition of Royal Knight Loretta at the  Royal Moongazing Grounds, which unlocks the path to Three Sisters behind her.
1. Ranni's Rise
