    - **WARNING:** This will permanently end Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant's quests.
    - **WARNING:** Ranni's questline will no longer progress; however, this can be undone by using Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows.
1. Caelid
  - Defeat Starscourge Radahn to resume the movement of the stars.
1. Nokron, Eternal City
  - Nokron can only be accessed via the *Starfall Crater* in east Limgrave after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
  - Proceed through the area to obtain the Fingerslayer Blade, which is in a chest northeast of the  Night's Sacred Ground Site of Grace.
1. Three Sisters
  - Travel to Ranni's Rise and deliver the Fingerslayer Blade to Ranni, who will give you the Carian Inverted Statue.
    - This key item is required to progress Fia, Deathbed Companion's questline. However, it is *not* necessary to complete Ranni's quest.
    - **WARNING:** This will permanently end Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant's quest.
  - Travel to Renna's Rise, which unseals after Ranni departs with the Fingerslayer Blade. Enter and climb to the top, and go through the Sending Gate to the upper portion of Ainsel River.
1. Ainsel River Main
  - Pick up the Miniature Ranni near the spawn point and rest at the  Ainsel River Main Site of Grace. Use the "Talk to miniature Ranni" option three times to get her to speak.
1. Nokstella, Eternal City
  - *(Optional)* Ranni will also have dialogue at the  Nokstella, Eternal City and  Nokstella Waterfall Basin Sites of Grace. These are not required to continue her questline.
  - Defeat the Baleful Shadow invader just past the  Nokstella Waterfall Basin Site of Grace to obtain the Discarded Palace Key.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
  - Defeat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon at the Raya Lucaria Grand Library.
  - Unlock the chest behind Rennala and obtain the Dark Moon Ring.
1. Lake of Rot
  - Ride the Transportation Coffin at the Grand Cloister. Defeat Astel, Naturalborn of the Void and then travel up the lift. However, this lift remains locked until the player obtains the Dark Moon Ring.
1. Moonlight Altar
  - Travel to the Cathedral of Manus Celes and descend through the tunnel near the altar to find Ranni sitting on the corpse of her Two Fingers. Interact with her to trigger a cutscene. After the cutscene, speak to her again, and she will disappear, bequeathing the Dark Moon Greatsword.
1. Stone Platform
  - After defeating the final boss, there will be a blue summon sign beside  Fractured Ma

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Wears the Snow Witch Set: Snow Witch Hat, Snow Witch Robe, Snow Witch Skirt

- Ranni cannot be killed but will vanish if attacked. She will reappear if the player uses Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows.

- Ranni inhabits a doll body resembling the Snow Witch, her former master. She later inhabits miniature versions of it. It is unclear whether it was made by the Nox of the Eternal Cities, Ranni, or the snow witch herself.

- Ranni's original Empyrean body can be found atop the Divine Tower of Liurnia and still possesses one-half of the Cursemark of Death.
  - Examining the blackened remains closely reveals hints of red hair on her head, which is characteristic of a daughter of Radagon.
  - Ranni's original body has two arms, while her doll body has four. It is thus similar to Miquella the Kind and the Marionette soldiers utilized by Sorcerers throughout the game.
  - The Stargazer Heirloom can be found on her body as well, a memento of her mother Rennala.

- Certain stages of Ranni's questline trigger Seluvis to go inert and Pidia to die at the hands of puppets of Raya Lucaria Soldiers. This outcome occurs either if Ranni is offered the Amber Draught or after she receives the Fingerslayer Blade and departs from Caria Manor.

- If the player administers the Amber Draught to Ranni, she will awaken and express her disappointment in them for indulging Seluvis before banishing them from her sight. Should the player persist in attempting to speak with her, Ranni will instantly kill them. This transgression may also be forgiven through absolution at the Church of Vows.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Radagon of the Golden Order** is a boss in Elden Ring. He is encountered inside the Erdtree in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, and is the first half of the final boss fight, with the Elden Beast as the second half.

sections.heading: Liurnian Wars and Marriage to Queen Rennala
sections.text:
Radagon first rose to prominence during the Liurnian Wars, when he joined the heroes' ranks. A great champion with flowing red locks, he arrived in Liurnia at the head of a golden host, where he met Queen Rennala in battle. Although two wars would be fought between them, the First and Second Liurnian Wars,, no victor would emerge from either. Radagon eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, and swore his love to Rennala. He became husband to the Carian Queen, wedding her at the Church of Vows. Rennala bequeathed him a greatsword, bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse to honor long-standing tradition. After entering into marriage with Rennala and joining the Carian line, he ordered the Carian magic preceptors to don masks of confidence, to make it clear that all of their matters were to be kept strictly private.

Radagon and Rennala had three children: Radahn, Rykard and Ranni. While husband to Rennala, Radagon studied glintstone sorcery taught at the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

After Godfrey, the First Elden Lord was stripped of grace and hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon returned to the capital where he went on to marry Queen Marika and become her King Consort and second Elden Lord. Before leaving Rennala, Radagon gifted her an amber egg. His departure left her heartbroken, and eventually led to her being deposed by the academy and imprisoned in the Grand Library. His three children from the previous marriage would be raised to demigod status as stepchildren of Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Marriage to Queen Marika
sections.text:
A sculptor from Leyndell was commissioned to create a statue of Radagon. In doing so, he discovered a secret - that Radagon is Marika. This secret was hidden within the statue, and is revealed by casting Law of Regression in front of it, causing the statue's form to change from Radagon to Marika.

Radagon and Marika had a twin daughter and son: Malenia and Miquella. As they were born of a single god, they were both Empyreans, but were born afflicted: Malenia with a rotting sickness and Miquella with eternal childhood.

While married to Marika, Radagon studied incantations. He is heavily associated with Golden Order Fundamentalism, a branch of the Golden Order said to be scholarship in all but name, which incorporates incantations that rely on a combination of faith and intelligence. His son Miquella followed in his fundamentalist footsteps, and created several incantations as gifts for his father. Radagon would return the favor with his own gift of gratitude to young Miquella, however Miquella later abandoned Fundamentalism, realising that it could do nothing to treat Malenia's Rot.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text:
Following the Night of Black Knives, Marika shattered the Elden Ring, breaking the Golden Order. Radagon, on the other hand, remained loyal to the Golden Order, and attempted to repair the Elden Ring with the same hammer used to shatter it. As punishment, Marika was imprisoned inside the Erdtree. While Radagon had opposed Marika's treachery, he would share Marika's sentence, as the two were now bound in a single body.

When a Tarnished sets fire to the Erdtree in order to burn away the wall of thorns denying their entry, they encounter the imprisoned Marika. Suddenly released from her bonds, her hair immediately turns red as Radagon assumes control of their shared body and wields Marika's hammer to fight the Tarnished. However, Radagon is unable to defeat them and falls at their hands, with his body being subsumed by the Elden Beast to transform into a large sword, as it emerges to be the Tarnished champion's final challenge.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.text: Radagon is the first of two enemies that compose the final boss fight of Elden Ring, with the Elden Beast being the second. Players will have to fight Radagon again if they die to the Elden Beast.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Radagon relies on very fast hammer swings, and some of his attacks will generate shockwaves. These shockwaves will either be immediate, or will occur after a brief delay- for the latter, golden cracks will appear in the ground moments before the explosion.

At range, Radagon can throw golden spears at the player. He will either leap into the air and throw a single, giant spear, or quickly hurl five spears in a loose fan. These spears will remain in the ground for a second before exploding. He also has a grab attack which he may perform at close- or mid-range. During the grab, his left arm will glow gold and he will wind it back behind him before lunging. The shockwave generated by the grab may still cause damage even if the grab itself misses.

All of his gold attacks will inflict Holy damage.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: After his health has been lowered somewhat, he will leap into the air and perform a Gold Breaker attack, creating a large area of effect shockwave. During this phase, Radagon will sometimes teleport, generating an explosion when he reappears. In addition to the golden spear attacks used in the previous phase, he may now jump up and throw a volley of spears. His stomp will also now create a shockwave that deals Holy damage.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text: Once his health is below half, Radagon will teleport into the middle of the arena and perform three rapid hammer strikes on the ground, each producing a large shockwave. He will now teleport much more often, and can perform two shockwave-inducing hammer strikes in quick succession.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The arena is a featureless, oval platform with no obstacles. It is not possible to fall of the edges.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text: - This boss can be cheesed by running up to him as soon as possible and blocking his way. The AI doesn't become aggressive until it has made a certain number of steps, so you can take him down with ease as long as you have a way to deal damage without moving (bows, damage dealing auras, etc). This can also be done by running up to him as soon as possible, performing a jump attack (so landing too low for his line of sight), and quickly sidestepping behind him. You are then most likely free to make multiple strong attacks on him until his guard is broken, perform a critical hit, charge a strong attack again while he's standing up, and start the fight proper at that point onward with roughly half his health already gone.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Radagon needs to be parried multiple times to trigger a stagger.
- Radagon was said to have despised his own red hair, as it was perhaps the result of a curse by red-haired Fire Giants. Ironically, most of his children would inherit it, and some of them would even be proud of its heroic implications.
- Radagon's rune can be seen in Radagon's Scarseal, Radagon's Soreseal, and in the thorns blocking the Erdtree. It resembles the criss-cross pattern seen in his statues, and is reminiscent of a sewing pattern, as he was also associated with sewing needles, perhaps symbolizing his need to keep things held together.
- The Radagon Icon mentions how he studied sorcery as husband of Rennala, and incantations as husband of Marika, aspiring to be complete.
- When Marika's body changes into Radagon, her dress becomes his skirt.
  - Queen Marika and Lord Radagon wear the same black outfit with gold floral patterns in their side profile paintings at the Roundtable Hold, teasing their secret at an early point in the game's narrative.
- The Revenant's ghost stares at a Radagon painting at the Roundtable Hold in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal name: **MaricaOfDistorted** (ID: 2190)
- Radagon/Marika are reminiscent of the alchemical Red King and White Queen, who are often depicted as the two halves of the Rebis. In alchemy, the Rebis is a single being possessing both male and female qualities, also sometimes referred to as the divine hermaphrodite. It is said that the Rebis originated from a being that was divided into male and female halves, until it was unified again to form a transcendental being empowered by a dragon.
- Lord Radagon prophesied the Tarnisheds' return in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Putrescence** (泥濘, *Deinei*, lit. Muddy mud) is a material in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Congealed Putrescence was a bruise-colored ooze that formed from the tainted, impure remains of heroes housed within the stone coffin ships. Decorated with sculptures of bulls, beasts, and the bearded god of the Ancient Dynasty, they were sent off with Great Grave Glovewort for burial at sea. The colossal arks drifted to the Southern Shore of the Gravesite Plain since time immemorial, washing up on its Cerulean Coast.

Although the tainted flesh had putrified into a foul liquor by the time they washed ashore on the Lands Between's Cerulean Coast, it nonetheless received the cleansing Death rites of the time: incineration by cold ghostflame in the kilns of the Deathbirds. At some point, the ghostflame practices ended, and the coffins accumulated over time in the Stone Coffin Fissure, where their leaked contents formed stalactites and dripped down into the chasm.

After Shattering, Miquella the Kind embarked on a pilgrimage through the Realm of Shadow. When he visited the Stone Coffin Fissure, he abandoned his love and other self, casting St. Trina down into the depths. Though wounded, Trina survived, and soon her presence transformed the area into the Garden of Deep Purple. When the sludge imbibed her velvety nectar, it received its long sought-after eternal rest, and coalesced into her Putrescent Knight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Putrescence is tied to the Ancient Dynasty, Ancient Death, and Tibia Mariners.
  - Claymen Sorceries have an Arcane requirement, and the Japanese name of the  shares the exact same kanji for muddiness used for , strongly implying that Claymen are Putrescent.
- Putrescence is connected to Albinaurics and Night.
  - Both putrescence and Albinaurics are deemed impure beings.
  - Arcane, night-tinged dew formed by starlight produced the Albinaurics, and starlight can be seen in the head of the Putrescent Knight.
  - Like weapons wielded by male Albinaurics, the Putrescence Cleaver scales with Arcane.
  - The humanoid Putrescent Knight has silver skin and lacks feet and can hop around on his tibias, while the horse component lacks hind legs.
  - Like the fallen dew that caused the ripple that created the Albinaurics, Putrescence Knight was formed from drops of putrescence falling into the Garden of Deep Purple.
  - The Ancient Dynasty Man that appears on the Stone Coffins also appears at The Four Belfries, where Sending Gates powered by starlight transport the Tarnished across the Lands Between.
  - Both Albinauric Bloodclot and Congealed Putrescence are thick and coagulated. Both can be used to craft items which lure in humanoid enemies.
  - Putrescence and starlight are described as being alcoholic.
- Vigilant Sentry Stones and Soporific Gravebirds watch the putrescence of the Stone Coffin Fissure.
- The blade of the Putrescence Cleaver is visually similar to Rosus' Axe.
- Bruise-colored Ancestral Followers worship in the dynastic ruins depicting stone coffins.
- The Numen also arrived from outside the Lands Between.
- "GloamEyedKnight" is the internal name for the Putrescent Knight, suggesting it was tied to the Gloam-Eyed Queen in development or shares a common theme.

Tricia the perfumer worked alongside a nameless Traveling Perfumer, and dedicated her efforts to treating Misbegotten, Omen, and all those seen as impure. She remained with them as they died, ensuring that they passed peacefully and without pain, not unlike the origins of the Deathbed Companions.

Tricia fights alongside a Misbegotten Warrior, whom she supports with aromatics.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: ***Obelisk Beacons*** are Objects in Elden Ring. Most information about Obelisk Beacons is conjectural, based on its visual details and context.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Obelisk Beacons are artifacts left by the Ancient Dynasty that once flourished in the Lands Between. Lighting the beacon ignites a flame on a corresponding pillar at a nearby Hallowhorn Grounds. The power of Ancestor Spirits gathers in the Horned Remains when all Beacons are lit, indicated by bluish flame.

Obelisk Beacons are activated by approaching them and selecting "**Light flame**."

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
- Lighting x8 Obelisk Beacons in Worshipper's Woods (Siofra River) unlocks an encounter with an Ancestor Spirit at Hallowhorn Grounds (south).
- Lighting x6 Obelisk Beacons in Ancestral Woods (Nokron, Eternal City) unlocks an encounter with a Regal Ancestor Spirit at Hallowhorn Grounds (north).

sections.heading: Note
sections.text:
- You can check how many unlit Obelisk Beacons are left by checking the Hallowhorn Grounds staircase for unlit pillars.
- They are engraved with five sacred scenes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Original Sin** is an unknowable event mentioned in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The original sin was the first and gravest of the many blasphemous crimes committed by Queen Marika and her Erdtree, though its exact nature remains shrouded in mystery. Its evidence was sealed away in the Realm of Shadow by Marika when Messmer the Impaler launched the crusade.

Marika punished the Cutting-Gifted Tribe after they glimpsed the original sin.

Miquella the Kind sought to erase the original sin by abandoning everything and ascending to godhood at the Gate of Divinity. He discarded parts of his being along his pilgrimage through the Shadow Realm, a Miquella's Cross forming at each stop.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Giant bears found throughout the Lands Between. They are far larger than other Bears, and display strange markings on their chests.

They are tanky enemies with tremendous strength. These savage beasts were hunted by a tribe of highland warriors who sought their powers.

White Runebears are covered in snow. They roam the Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Regal Ancestor Spirit** is an optional Remembrance boss in Elden Ring. It is encountered at the northern Hallowhorn Grounds along the Siofra River after lighting six bonfires.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Deer-like spirits found in Siofra River. They exist beyond the purview of the Erdtree, and follow the principle that life sprouts from death as it does from birth. This process is reflected by their horns, which sprout new growths even after the ancestor's death. Shamans of the Ancestral Followers don headdresses fashioned from horns with buds, mirroring the appearance of the ancestor spirits.

Ancestor Spirits appear emaciated, with exposed ribs, matted fur, and cavities in their chests. They have large, antler-like horns which glow and sprout small buds.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: An Ancestor Spirit is found in the upper part of Siofra River at the northern Hallowhorn Grounds, north-east of Night's Sacred Ground and the Ancestral Woods Site of Grace. Much like the other Ancestor Spirit, this one can only be fought after lighting flames- in this case six- in the surrounding area and then touching the horned remains.

sections.heading: Boss fight
sections.text: Although it initially fights in much the same way as the standard Ancestor Spirit, once its health has been reduce to half it will start to heal itself by siphoning HP from the player, as well as from the spirit animals in the arena. It will also sometimes collapse and fade away, and then emerge from one of the other animals in the arena. It can also use abilities reminiscent of other animals- hopping like a springhare, charging like a boar, or curling into a ball and rolling like a goat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - In Norse mythology,   eat among the branches of the world tree . According to the , the stags crane their necks upward to chomp at the branches. The morning dew gathers in their horns and forms the rivers of the world.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Roped Holy Water Pot** is a craftable, consumable tool in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be crafted after purchasing the Missionary's Cookbook [1] from Merchant Kalé for 1000 runes at the Church of Elleh.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Creates a Golden Order seal before throwing the pot, causing Holy damage and inflicting 300% bonus damage towards Those Who Live in Death and preventing Skeletons from resurrecting.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The requirement for an empty Cracked Pot is not listed directly in the crafting menu, instead having a row for it just above. The Pot is returned after the consumable is thrown.
- Does somewhat mediocre damage against normal enemies but incredible amounts against Those Who Live in Death.
- Thrown much quicker than the non-roped pot, though only backwards which makes it harder to hit. It can still be used in normal combat if one quickly turns around when close to an enemy, before quickly turning back.

sections.heading: Required items
sections.text:
- Mushroom x1
- Tarnished Golden Sunflower x1
- String x1
- (Empty) Cracked Pot

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Radagon's Rings of Light** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Creates a halo of light above the caster's head, which is then thrown out as an expanding ring of light around them, with Holy Attack Power equal to 310% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 395% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 37 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 48 points of Stamina.
- Deals 10 Stance damage on a hit, increasing to 14 Stance damage if charged.
- Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
  - Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
- Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 27%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 46%.
- While its large hitbox would seem able to hit large targets multiple times, it can actually only hit a target once.
  - This makes it less able to hit weak spots on large foes, since the large hitbox can fairly easily hit another, non-weak body part beforehand.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Actually consists of 16 separate but overlapping projectiles.
- Patch 1.07 reduced FP consumption and recovery time.
  - FP cost was reduced from 25 to 21.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost, increased damage, and cast speed. Decreased recovery time.
  - FP cost was reduced from 29 to 25.
  - Attack Power was increased from 282% of Incantation Scaling to 310% of the same for the uncharged version and from 333% of Incantation Scaling to 395% of the same for the charged version.

sections.text: **Rotten Breath** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Dragon Communion:** Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a heavy, rotting mist, dealing Standard damage equal to 131% of Incantation Scaling and causing 65 Scarlet Rot build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 393% of the same and 195 build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 48 points of Stamina to cast, and another 48 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
  - Note that while the Dragon Communion Seal scales with Arcane, Scarlet Rot will not scale with that, so Rotten Breath gains no innate benefit except for the damage boost.
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Ekzykes's Decay.
- Compared to Ekzykes's Decay, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 29% less FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 120 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
  - Only 65 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the weakest "default" dragon breath attack, but it's also the only one that deals Physical damage.
  - Compatible with the Blue Dancer Charm, even more so since its two primary boosting items, the Dragon Communion Seal and Rock Heart, are weightless.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.
- The Scarlet Rot deals damage roughly equal to 1170 + 29.7% of the target's maximum health over the course of 90 seconds.
  - The total Scarlet Rot build-up is 390 if using both breaths, enough to afflict many vulnerable enemies and bosses with the Status Effect and most non-resistant ones within two full casts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the Scarlet Rot status effect buildup for Rotten Breath.
  - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.
  - The status build-up per hit was decreased from 130 to 65 (total build-up reduced from 780 to 390).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Roundtable Hold** is the main hub area in Elden Ring. Entry to Roundtable Hold is locked until the player receives an invitation from Melina, achieved by resting at a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes or Caelid, or by defeating Margit, the Fell Omen. Afterward, the Roundtable Hold can be accessed via fast travel from the map.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A pocket realm tied to the Erdtree's Grace, the Roundtable Hold exists to aid the Tarnished on their quest for the Elden Ring, with Smithing Master Hewg as its foundation. It is a copy of Leyndell's Fortified Manor, once a gathering place for great champions seeking the Two Fingers' divine wisdom. A bustling community of mighty Tarnished likewise convened in the Hold in the distant past; however, it is now a shadow of its former glory, with its present occupants lacking the venerable status and lofty aspirations of those past heroes, such as Vargram the Raging Wolf, Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, Mad Tongue Alberich, Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, and Roundtable Knight Vyke, who came closest to the title of Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Layout
sections.text: Roundtable Hold consists of a main floor and a cellar, each comprised of several rooms. Certain rooms are inaccessible until certain requirements are met.

sections.heading: Lobby
sections.text: The central chamber of the Hold, containing the circular Table of Lost Grace site of grace, from which it gets its name. The player shall appear in this chamber every time they visit Roundtable Hold. Brother Corhyn, Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, and Knight Diallos can all be found here initially, later joined by Roderika, Spirit Tuner and D, Hunter of the Dead. A Marika statue by the fireplace can be used to access the Colosseums, once unlocked.

sections.heading: Northern Wing
sections.text: The northern wing, ahead and to the left upon arriving in Roundtable Hold, consists of a corridor which branches into Gideon's study and the Twin Maiden Husks' room. Ensha of the Royal Remains stands guard outside Gideon's study, and Nepheli Loux, Warrior briefly appears here after Godrick the Grafted has been defeated.

sections.heading: Gideon's Study
sections.text: A spacious room which has been adapted into a study by Gideon Ofnir, who can usually be found behind his desk. It will be locked upon first visiting Roundtable Hold, but will open either after claiming a Great Rune or talking to Gideon and reloading.

sections.heading: Twin Maiden Husks
sections.text: The Twin Maiden Husks can be found in a room through a door in the northern wing. Here, the player can buy and sell various items. They receive Bell Bearings, which allows them to sell the goods of dead merchants. Some of these Bell Bearings carry over into .

sections.heading: Library
sections.text: A small library behind a door in the Twin Maiden Husks' room, which will only open after touching a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau. The back of the library is piled with decaying corpses, and is occupied by the spirit of the Dung Eater.

sections.heading: Eastern Wing
sections.text: The eastern wing is a corridor which connects to Fia's room, the armory, and the cellar. Smithing Master Hewg resides here, and is later joined by Roderika.

sections.heading: Fia's Room
sections.text: A large bedroom occupied by Fia, Deathbed Companion. The Clouded Mirror Stand to the right upon entering can be used to open the Character Creation menu and alter one's appearance.

sections.heading: Balcony
sections.text: Situated between the northern and eastern wings, a balcony overlooks the great hall. Sorcerer Rogier retreats here after leaving Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Hall
sections.text: A large hall lined with banners and statues, accessed by dropping down from the balcony. Mad Tongue Alberich will invade when the player approaches the far end of the hall. After he has been defeated, a wisp of light will appear which allows the player to return to the balcony above.

sections.heading: Living Quarters
sections.text: A series of rooms connected to the hall, to the left after dropping down from the balcony. The Cipher Pata can be found on a corpse lying on one of the beds.

sections.heading: Armory
sections.text: A locked room at the far end of the eastern wing. It will only open after giving D the Weathered Dagger, received from Fia.

sections.heading: Pantry
sections.text: A storage room on the lower level, at the bottom of a flight of stairs past Hewg in the eastern wing. It is initially empty, but Nepheli Loux will move here after the Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics has been defeated.

sections.heading: Dining Room
sections.text: A narrow room connected to the pantry, which requires a Stonesword Key to open. There is a treasure chest containing Crepus's Black-Key Crossbow and 20 Black-Key Bolts.

sections.heading: Kitchen
sections.text: A room connected to the dining room, requiring two Stonesword Keys to open. A treasure chest contains the Assassin's Prayerbook.

sections.heading: Audience Chamber
sections.text: A throne room connected to the lobby, wherein resides the Two Fingers and Finger Reader Enia. This chamber is locked until at least one Great Rune has been obtained. The player comes here to progress the main story and to trade in Remembrances for boss items.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Rotten Winged Sword Insignia** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Obtained from Millicent after choosing to assist her in defeating her sisters, as part of her questline.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 6%/8%/13%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point.

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hit towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive).
  - These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land.
  - For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive.
- For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count.
- Can be worn together with the Millicent's Prosthesis to stack the effect, but not with the Winged Sword Insignia.
  - However, this talisman and the Prosthesis can't be obtained in the same playthrough, instead requiring a new cycle of New Game+ to obtain.
- Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy.
  - An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice.
  - This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: - At some point between an unknown Patch and Patch 1.03.3, this talisman was apparently bugged, with the buff that is applied to attack power both increasing and decreasing with successive attacks. That is, in some scenarios, performing an additional attack within a sequence would cause attack power to decrease, rather than increase. This could be observed when using the Dagger and Short Sword weapons. This effect could be observed for the Winged Sword Insignia as well.

  - Boosts the damage of the follow-up heavy attack granted by the skills Barbaric Roar, Braggart's Roar, Shriek of Milos, Troll's Roar, and War Cry by 15%.
  - Boosts the following incantations (mostly Dragon Communion Incantations) by 10%: Agheel's Flame, Borealis's Mist, Dragonfire, Dragonice, Ekzykes's Decay, Ghostflame Breath, Glintstone Breath, Greyoll's Roar, Magma Breath, Rotten Breath, Smarag's Glintstone Breath, and Theodorix's Magma, as well as Placidusax's Ruin.
- Stacks with the 10% roar damage boost of a Highland Axe.
  - The Highland Axe only boosts skills, not incantations, and does not stack with itself (meaning two Highland Axes wielded together gives as much of a boost as one Highland Axe does).

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.

  - Wields a Greatbow for ranged combat and a Knight's Greatsword paired with a Redmane Greatshield in melee.
- Deals Standard damage with his greatsword and Pierce damage with the greatbow.
- Using any "roar" or "cry" type Skill, such as Regal Roar or War Cry will cause Ogha to use the Rain of Arrows skill on his target. This can only be done once per summoning.
- He is a "Red-eyed" spirit, meaning that, once summoned, he will patrol his spawning spot and attacks any enemy that wanders into his range.
  - Since he won't follow his summoner by default like most other ashes, Cursed-Blood Pots are the only way to make him move predictably.
- He prefers his Greatbow, and will only switch to the other set if an enemy wanders into his melee range.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Rotten Stray Ashes** is a spirit ash in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found in a building in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, north of the Sellia Under-Stair Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Grave Gloveworts.
- Summons the Rotten variant of the Stray.
- Deals Standard damage and inflicts Scarlet Rot build-up with its bite.
  - 50 Scarlet Rot build-up per bite.
- Scarlet rot effect stays for 3 minutes (twice the regular duration of 90 seconds), with the total amount of damage dealt being equal to 2700 + 32% of the target's maximum health.
- An excellent early summon if you are willing to go to Caelid early, due to the Scarlet Rot being capable of removing well over half of the health of early bosses.
  - Examples: Margit, the Fell Omen has 4,200 HP and thus takes roughly 4,000 damage over the duration (95% of his health), while Godrick the Grafted has 6,100 HP and takes roughly 4,700 damage over the duration (77% of his health, though all Status Effects are removed from him upon starting phase 2).
  - Falls of later on due to wider and stronger attacks as well as higher health pools reducing the effective damage.
- Upgraded with Grave Glovewort*.*

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Runes** () act as both the currency and experience points (XP) in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Runes are a main game mechanics behind runes is that they'll be lost on death, and the only way to get them back is to return to the area where they were lost to reclaim them. However, if one should die before they can retrieve the lost runes, they'll be lost permanently.

Runes are gained by defeating enemies, but also exist as Tools, which can be picked up and are sometimes dropped by enemies. These Golden Runes exist in various forms, which provide increasing numbers of runes when used or sold to merchants (for the same number of runes as when used).

sections.heading: Golden Runes
sections.text: The various forms of these rune objects, in increasing order of how many runes they provide, are: Golden Rune 1, Golden Rune 2, Golden Rune 3, Golden Rune 4, Golden Rune 5, Golden Rune 6, Golden Rune 7, Golden Rune 8, Lands Between Rune, Golden Rune 9, Golden Rune 10, Golden Rune 11, Golden Rune 12, Golden Rune 13, Numen's Rune, Hero's Rune 1, Hero's Rune 2, Hero's Rune 3, Hero's Rune 4, Hero's Rune 5, Lord's Rune

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Unlike dungeon boss fights, if one dies inside an evergaol, the runes will be retrievable on the surface/entrance area to the evergaol, so there's minimal risk in fighting bosses in evergaols.
- Golden Runes and any other item that grants runes are not lost on death, so it's best to keep them in their object state until ready to level up or buy something to minimize rune losses
- Sacrificial Twigs can be used in a talisman slot, so on the subsequent death, the twig is lost rather than one's runes.
- Remembrances grant runes upon use.
- Gold-Pickled Fowl Foot, Golden Horn Tender, and Gold Scarab boost rune acquisition.
- A Rune bonus multiplier applies anytime a player with the same multiplayer password defeats a Shardbearer or becomes Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Redmane Castle** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A fortress on an island to the south of Caelid, connected to the mainland by a heavily fortified greatbridge. The castle is the stronghold of General Radahn's army, beaten yet unbowed after their defeat at the hands of Malenia and her Cleanrot Knights.

Redmane Castle is also the site of the Radahn Festival; a contest in which great champions attempt to defeat the Rot-maddened Radahn and claim his Great Rune. This event is initiated either by activating a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau or by progressing Ranni the Witch's questline.

During the Radahn Festival, all of the enemies in the castle (except for the two Elder Lions) will disappear, and the boss (if not defeated already) will not show up in the plaza. Once Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, the enemies will return and the boss can be fought if not defeated already.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Roderika, Spirit Tuner**, also known as the **Heartbroken Maiden**, is a merchant character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A Tarnished noblewoman who, despite having never seen the guidance of grace, travelled to the Lands Between along with her companions. After arriving, those companions fell victim to Godrick, becoming subjects for his grafting. Roderika alone survived, taking refuge in Stormhill Shack. It is here that she meets the Tarnished. She beseeches the Tarnished to bring a message to her grafted companions, whom she refers to as chrysalids, assuring them that she loves them and will join them soon.

Roderika then heads to Roundtable Hold. Here, she becomes acquainted with Smithing Master Hewg, who takes notice of her gift for spirit tuning and is reminded of a spirit tuner he knew long ago, whose eyes were of the same hue as Roderika's. Reluctantly, Hewg agrees to teach Roderika everything he knows about spirit tuning.

Roderika remains at Roundtable Hold, where she hones her newfound talent and eventually becomes a fully-fledged spirit tuner. Her ability to sense spirits allows her to notice the Dung Eater's presence, which she warns the Tarnished about.

After the Erdtree burns, Roderika attempts to convince Hewg to leave Roundtable, but to no avail. She chooses to respect Hewg's decision, and remains behind with him even after he forgets her. As the hold burns, she begs the Tarnished to become Elden Lord, and to use the weapons Hewg forged to slay Queen Marika the Eternal.

sections.heading: Spirit Tuning
sections.text: Roderika can upgrade Spirit Ashes up to +10 using Grave Glovewort and Ghost Glovewort.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.text:
1. *(Optional)* Stormhill Shack
  - Roderika can be found in Stormhill Shack in Stormhill, provided you have not defeated Godrick the Grafted or touched a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes. Exhaust her dialogue to obtain both the "Sitting Sideways" Gesture and Spirit Jellyfish Ashes.
1. *(Optional)* Stormveil Castle
  - In an adjoining courtyard to the large hall containing a Grafted Scion in Stormveil Castle, pick up the Chrysalids' Memento.
1. *(Optional)* Stormhill Shack
  - Deliver the Crysalids' Memento to Roderika in Stormhill Shack and exhaust her dialogue to get her to move to Roundtable Hold.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Roderika can be found by the fireplace in the central room. Talk to her to obtain a Golden Seed once she arrives.
  - **Note**: if you defeated Godrick or rest at a Site of Grace in Liurnia without speaking to Roderika in Stormhill Shack, she will move to Roundtable Hold on her own, and will leave the Golden Seed on the ground in the shack.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Speak to Roderika, and then speak to Smithing Master Hewg and select "About Roderika".
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Return to Roderika and speak to her to tell her what Hewg said.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Return to Hewg and select "About Roderika" again, followed by "Would you watch over Roderika?" and finally "It's what she wants".
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Reload the area and Roderika will be sitting opposite Hewg. It is now possible to upgrade Spirit Ashes by speaking to her.
1. *(optional)* Roundtable Hold
  - Upgrade a Spirit Ash to at least +4 and talk to her to receive the "Curtsy" Gesture.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - After burning the Erdtree, return to the Roundtable Hold, speak to Hewg, and select "Let's talk a while". You may then select the dialogue option "Why are you still making weapons?" After talking to Roderika and selecting "About Hewg", return to Hewg and select "What happened to her?"
1. Roundtable Hold
  - After defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, speak to Hewg and select "About yourself", and then speak to Roderika.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- After becoming a Spirit Tuner, Roderika will no longer wear her hood. The Crimson Hood will be in Stormveil Castle, on top of the pile of corpses where the Chrysalids' Memento was.
- The Crimson Hood's description suggests that Roderika was royalty in her native land, sent to Lands Between without specific orders to get rid of her.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

- Roderika has cut dialogue.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Royal Greatsword** is a Colossal Sword, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Obtained from Blaidd, along with his armor set (except the Black Wolf Mask), when encountered at Ranni's Rise after Ranni the Witch's storyline has been completed. Killing him prior to this will award no items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Intelligence-scaling is actually slightly stronger than the Strength-scaling despite having the same letter grade.
  - This means that a pure Intelligence build is the strongest way to build this weapon. However, because scaling values become less effective after reaching 40-50 in a stat and because wielding this weapon already requires a fair investment in Strength, a hybrid Str/Int build has almost as much AR while requiring much fewer Attribute points to do.
- The weapon itself does not cause Frostbite but both parts of the skill, the stab-jump and the explosion, do cause some build-up (60 on the stab and 100 on the explosion).

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.text:
- The Royal Greatsword is upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- The Royal Greatsword cannot be buffed or have its affinities altered with Ashes of War or Whetblades.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This weapon's guard ratings were significantly increased with patch 1.04, from 55/63/44/44/44/42 to 71/63/44/44/44/52.
- Patch 1.04 increased the cast speed and decreased recovery time for the skill.
- Patch 1.07 increased the poise when casting the skill.
- Patch 1.09 increased the scaling values of the weapon.
- As the description implies, this resembles a much more ornate version of the standard Greatsword.
- Shares it name with a weapon from Dark Souls 2 (Royal Greatsword), which was a Greatsword-type weapon and Strength-based counterpart to that game's version of the Flamberge.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Rotten Crystal Sword** is a straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: In a treasure chest guarded by three Crystalians in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, behind some large tree roots right after the Ephael Inner Wall grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Effectively just the Crystal Sword but with slight Scarlet Rot build-up, much, much later acquisition, and lower damage from very slightly lower Strength-scaling and lower Physical and Magic base damage.
- The skill, Spinning Slash, is potentially quite damaging, especially if it catches another player offguard and with low Poise, though it's somewhat hampered by the lack of reach on Straight Swords.
- Does best as a pure Strength weapon, as Dexterity and Intelligence are somewhat hampered by having much lower scaling numbers and being based off the lower Magic base damage respectively.
  - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 625 Attack Power (AP), 45 Strength and 45 Intelligence grants 607 AP, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 599 AP, and 80 Intelligence grants 540 AP.
  - Has on average 25 less AP
- A good offhand weapon for those wishing to dual-wield Straight Swords on a Strength build with some Intelligence, due to the ease of upgrading weapons reliant on Somber Smithing Stones and its somewhat mediocre skill not mattering there.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Rune of Death** (死のルーン, *Shi no Rūn*), also known as **Destined Death** (運命の死, *Unmei no Shi*), is an unobtainable Great Rune in Elden Ring that controls the fated deaths of the Demigods. Once part of the Elden Ring, it was removed by Queen Marika and sealed away when she established her Golden Order. It appears during the cutscene that plays when the player defeats Maliketh, the Black Blade at Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Destined Death is a crimson, cross-shaped rune with tapered ends, resembling Marika's Rune with a downward arc. Smoke emanates from the rune as a jagged black fissure splits it vertically through its center. It manifests within a font of Darkness upon its unsealing.

sections.heading: Destined Death
sections.text:
The Rune of Death can grant Destined Death, or true and fated death. When used to carve the Cursemark of Death in a full ring, it kills the recipient in both body and soul; however, incomplete rings can apply partial effects under specific circumstances. Known as half-wheels of the centipede, the waxing crescent burns away the flesh while the waning crescent destroys only the soul.

The Rune also produces crimson flames with golden motes that inflicts the Destined Death status effect, which reduces maximum HP and deals damage over time. The power of Destined Death could be repelled by the Blasphemous Claw or a depiction of the eclipsed sun.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Rune of Death was once embedded within the Elden Ring, empowering the black flames to deliver Destined Death to even gods. It was venerated by the Godskin Apostles and wielded by the Gloam-Eyed Queen, whose sacred Godslayer's Greatsword channeled black flames. The Queen, an Empyrean chosen by the Fingers, led the Apostles on their god hunt; however, she was ultimately vanquished by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast and loyal vassal of Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Golden Order
sections.text: With the Gloam-Eyed Queen defeated, Marika extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it within his Black Blade. This act was the foundation of the Golden Order and established Marika as the one true god. It exempted the Demigods from dying true deaths, granting them immortality, and also conferred a form of unending life to the Erdtree people. With the true lethality of Godslayer incantations suppressed, only Maliketh held the power to destroy the Demigods, and there was not one among them who did not fear him.

sections.heading: Night of Black Knives
sections.text:
At a later point in history, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen from Maliketh by Ranni the Witch, who used it to create the godslaying Black Knives through a fearsome rite. On the Night of Black Knives, the Black Knife Assassins used these blades to murder Godwyn the Golden, the first Demigod to perish in all of recorded history. However, due to Ranni carving the Cursemark of Destined Death into her flesh at the same moment as Godwyn's death, he was unable to die a proper death and perished in soul alone. Meanwhile, Ranni's flesh perished and her soul continued to live, inhabiting a doll body. After the Night of Black Knives, Maliketh bound his sword within his own flesh in order to ensure that none would ever steal Death again.

Godwyn was given an Erdtree Burial at the Erdtree's roots in the Deeproot Depths beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital. However, his soulless body soon began a grotesque transformation into the blighted Prince of Death. Fragments of the Rune of Death began to spread through the underground Greattree roots connected to Godwyn's corpse, sprouting in the form of Deathroot, and leading to the rise of Those Who Live in Death.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text:

As Gurranq, Beast Clergyman, Maliketh attempts to reclaim the stolen shards by consuming Deathroot, an endeavor he believes will restore the Golden Order and end his hunger. After devouring all nine Deathroots, his hunger persists and he realizes that the Golden Order cannot be restored. He was, in truth, betrayed by Marika.

Marika's daughter, Melina, aids the Tarnished knowing their quest will ultimately violate the Golden Order. Her purpose as the Kindling Maiden is to commit the Cardinal Sin and unlock the path to Maliketh and Destined Death. Although Maliketh unbinds the Black Blade, he is defeated. The Tarnished interacts with the Rune, unleashing a burst of crimson flame. The Erdtree is engulfed in crimson flames, and its impenetrable thorns are burned away.

If the Tarnished rises as the Lord of Frenzied Flame after using the Frenzied Flame to spare Melina, she gains or unlocks the power of Destined Death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Rune of Death might be an Elden Rune due to its similarity to Marika's Rune and its significance to the setting and story.
- A power similar to Destined Death appears to be wielded by the Black Blade Kindred, certain Vulgar Militia, and the Baleful Shadow. However, it only inflicts damage over time, and does not reduce maximum HP like the effect of Maliketh's Black Blade, the Black Blade incantation, or the Black Knife.
- The Rune of Death's fissure motif also appears on Maliketh's Black Blade, the Blasphemous Claw, and the Black Knives.

- Destined Death may have been inspired by the "Death Rune" from **, which Miyazaki has cited as an inspiration for Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition

If it's currently active, it can be deactivated by defeating Starscourge Radahn and talking to Jerren once more in the chapel just before the lift down to Radahn and then reloading the area, preferably by teleporting to the Chamber Outside the Plaza Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Ruins Greatsword is one of eight Legendary Armaments required for completing the "Legendary Armaments" achievement.
- Charged heavy attacks cost more stamina than usual but also deal with above-average damage thanks to a secondary hit with some extra area of effect.

- While this weapon scales with both Strength and Intelligence, it is borderline useless to invest in the latter anywhere beyond meeting the Attribute requirements. This is because the damage are incredibly minimal to both normal attacks (maxing out at +32 Magic damage with 99 Intelligence if the weapon is upgraded to +10) and because unlike how these sort of weapons scale normally, where Intelligence provides minimal weapon damage bonuses but great skill damage bonuses, both weapon upgrade level and Strength provide far greater bonuses to the skill's damage.

- Despite the appearance of its effects, it does not cause bonus damage to gravity-type enemies (e.g., Fallingstar Beasts), presumably because it is not extraterrestrial in origin.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The ruin that the rubble used to make this sword originated from was most likely Crumbling Farum Azula, giving its dilapidated state and nearby location.
- While the weapon resembles the Fume Ultra Greatsword from *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*, it even more so resembles the King's Ultra Greatsword from *Dark Souls 2*, especially because it resembles a statue wielded on a hilt.
- This weapon's guard rating was increased in patch 1.04, from 65/56/50/50/50/45 to 82/56/50/50/50/56.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Regalia of Eochaid** is a straight sword in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: On a ledge at the beach bordering Caelid and Limgrave, to the east of the Third Church of Marika. It can be reached through the Gaol Cave or by using Torrent to perform some tricky jumps to ascend the cliff face onto its ledge.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The skill, Eochaid's Dancing Blade, is both chargeable (benefiting from the Godfrey Icon) and actually counts for repeated-hits boosters such as the Winged Sword Insignias and Thorny Cracked Tear, something many other repeated-hits skills such as the Ghiza's Wheel's skill Spinning Wheel or the Ornamental Straight Sword's skill Golden Tempering's special heavy attacks don't.
  - It's however somewhat outclassed by the Marais Executioner's Sword when it comes to dealing damage with the skill, as the latter is a Greatsword and thus has greater Attack Power for the skill to be based off.
  - Since the skill's damage is based entirely of off the weapon's base Attack Power, and about a third of the Regalia's damage is Magic damage, Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear and Terra Magica functionally give +7% damage and +12% damage respectively if they can be set up beforehand.
- Though both the Dexterity-scaling and the Arcane-scaling may appear equal, and technically are as both are valued at 0.66, the Arcane-scaling actually applies to BOTH the Physical damage and the Magic damage. This effectively places it as a mid-tier B-scaling (1.08 scaling instead of 0.66 scaling). However, due to scaling falling off around 54 points in a damage stat (see the Weapon Scaling page) a hybrid Dexterity/Arcane build holds up fairly well.
  - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Arcane grants 631 Attack Power (AP), 45 Dexterity and 45 Arcane grants 618 AP, and 80 Dexterity grants 561 AP.
  - With a pure Arcane build this weapon will outmatch Occult affinity Straight Swords by 90-100 AP. As this is largely due to the innate Magic damage, this can be somewhat misleading in its performance if enemies are resistant to that damage type.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

  - Applies to the skill.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Rya the Scout**, also known as **Zorayas the Scout**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A young woman who works as a scout for the Recusants of Volcano Manor, tasked with recruiting Tarnished to the cause. Rya is the adopted daughter of Tanith, although she believes her to be her true mother. In truth, Rya is a Man-Serpent of Mt. Gelmir, born of a repellent birthing ritual, and her true name is Zorayas.

Rya first encounters the Tarnished in Liurnia of the Lakes, where they assist her in retrieving her Necklace from Blackguard Big Boggart. In return, Rya invites the Tarnished to Volcano Manor, where they have the opportunity to join the Recusants and serve under Tanith. During their service, the Tarnished stumbles upon Rya in her true, serpentine form. Rya reports hearing slithering sounds beyond the walls of the Manor, and begins to question her origins when the Tarnished reveals to her the secrets of the Manor, having previously believed herself to have been born of a king's grace. When the Tarnished presents her with the Serpent's Amnion, which she surmises to have come from her birth mother, she ventures deeper into Volcano Manor to learn the truth behind her birth, hoping to one day be able to call Tanith her mother again.

Concerned about her daughter, Tanith requests that the Tarnished give Rya a Tonic of Forgetfulness, to prevent the distress caused by the truth of her birth.

The Tarnished finds Rya deep within the Manor, where she reveals that she has discovered her origins as the product of a hideous ritual. Distressed, she begs the Tarnished to kill her. Should the Tarnished agree, she will thank the Tarnished and her mother before passing. Should they instead give her the Tonic of Forgetfulness, she will fall asleep, and later return to the Manor's drawing room, with no memories of her journey, still believing Tanith to be her mother.

Should the Tarnished refuse to kill her or give her the tonic, she will leave Volcano Manor, leaving behind a letter declaring her intention to set out on a journey so that she can continue Tanith's work.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
Note: This questline locks after killing Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and all steps not yet completed will no longer be available.
1. *(Optional)* Liurnia of the Lakes
  - Rya can be found in a folly north of the Laskyar Ruins. Speak to her and exhaust her dialogue, then travel to Boilprawn Shack and purchase Rya's Necklace from Blackguard Big Boggart. Return to Rya and hand over the necklace to receive an Invitation to Volcano Manor.
  - It is not possible to kill her in this location, as she is protected by a barrier.
1. *(Optional)* Altus Plateau
  - If the previous step was completed, Rya will be waiting at Lux Ruins in Altus Plateau. Speak to her and she will offer to transport you to Volcano Manor.
  - It is not possible to kill her in this location, as she is protected by a barrier.
1. Volcano Manor
  - Rya can now be found in the Volcano Manor drawing room after joining the Recusants. After defeating Old Knight Istvan and receiving the reward from Tanith, talk to Rya in the drawing room, then reload the area and enter the previously locked room across the corridor from the drawing room to find Rya in serpent form. Exhaust her dialogue.
1. Volcano Manor
  - After defeating Rileigh the Idle and receiving the reward from Tanith, speak to Rya in the same room as the previous step. Go into the room next to this and pass through the illusory wall at the back, then follow the path to the prison Town Church Site of Grace. Rest at the Site of Grace, then return to Rya and speak to her once again.
1. Volcano Manor
  - After defeating the Godskin Noble boss in Volcano Manor, obtain the Serpent's Amnion and give it to Rya.
  - *(Optional)* Speak to Tanith to obtain the Tonic of Forgetfulness.
1. Volcano Manor
  - Rya can now be found in a small room above the Temple of Eiglay Site of Grace, past an Iron Virgin. You now have three options to resolve this questline.
  1. If you received the Tonic of Forgetfulness, you may offer it to her, causing her to fall asleep. After killing Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, return to the Volcano Manor drawing room and speak to her. Reload the area and return to where she was to obtain Daedicar's Woe.
  1. If you choose to kill her, you will obtain Daedicar's Woe.
  1. If you refuse to kill her and do not give her the Tonic of Forgetfulness, return to where she was after defeating Rykard to obtain Daesicar's Woe and Zorayas's Letter.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The reward for Rya's questline, regardless of the outcome, is Daedicar's Woe, said to represent a woman who gave birth to a myriad of grotesque children. This may imply that Daedicar is Rya's birth mother.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Her true name, Zorayas, appears in the 1978 novel, *Night's Master*, by British author *Tanith* Lee. The Zorayas of *Night's Master* is the disfigured child of a tyrant, raised by a hermit to be unaware of her origins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Raya Lucaria Grand Library** is a Site of Grace located within the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Situated at one of the Academy of Raya Lucaria's highest points, the Raya Lucaria Grand Library was the hub of knowledge in Liurnia of the Lakes during the age of the Erdtree. It was where Queen Rennala was sequestered following her abandonment by Radagon, and remained since the subsequent Liurnian Civil War that ignited when the Knights of the Cuckoo betrayed and invaded the Carians. Here, Rennala cradled an amber egg, the Great Rune of the Unborn Demigods—a final farewell present from Lord Radagon. She dedicated herself to the forbidden art of rebirth, producing countless Juvenile Scholars, her sweet children.

- Boc the Seamster (optional)
- Sorceress Sellen (optional)
- Witch-Hunter Jerren (optional)

- Dark Moon Ring - open the chest with the Discarded Palace Key
- Glintstone Kris - side with Sellen to defeat Jerren
- Great Rune of the Unborn - defeat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
- Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen - defeat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Rennala sits at the center of a star with eight points contained within concentric rings.
- There is a single chest in the library, which is locked by the Discarded Palace Key. Within is the Dark Moon Ring required to complete Ranni's questline at the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
- There is a statue of Radagon of the Golden Order performing his usual Golden Order Totality pose.
- Sellen and Witch-Hunter Jerren will have their final confrontation here, depending on who the Tarnished sides with; either Jerren will remain outside or Sellen will take her place inside, where she may continue to sell the Tarnished any glintstone sorceries.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Rebirth** (commonly known as *respeccing*) is a mechanic featured in Elden Ring. Allowing the player to allocate points into different Attributes points during the game.

It is unlocked after defeating Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and is located next to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Rebirthing requires one Larval Tear.

It is important to note that the players starting origin (I.E. Samurai, Vagabond, or Astrologer) serves as the starting basis in terms of stat allocation for Rebirthing. Meaning that a player who started as a Samurai will have 12 Vigor points invested already while an Astrologer will start with 6 Vigor points. All points earned up to the level the player is currently at must be allocated for rebirth.

If the player chooses to cancel their Rebirthing, they will not lose a Larval Tear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Regal Omen Bairn** is a reusable tool in *Elden Ring* and a stronger, more costly alternative to the Omen Bairn.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Trade the Remembrance of the Omen King, gained by defeating Morgott, the Omen King, and 5000 Runes with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Using this item will make the player-character brace themselves for a second before unleashing a close-ranged explosion that'll launch human-sized (or smaller) opponents away from them before sending out 10 long-ranged wraith projectiles that'll track any target that the user was locked on to as they were ejected from their body. These wraiths travel in three groups, the first two groups being comprised of 3 projectiles each and the final having 4, each group also have their own defined travel speed, leading to three distinct rolling windows whenever the player is fighting against this tool in PvP.

As it deals Holy Damage; any holy-boosting equipment or spell will further increase the damage from this item.
Each piece of the Omen Set will also increase the damage of this item by 5%, meaning wearing the full set will increase it by 20%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The doll depicts Morgott, the Omen King and was likely made in secret by his father, Godfrey, First Elden Lord.

- The Bewitching Branch is a

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A series of caves winding up the cliffs, joining Liurnia of the Lakes to the Altus Plateau. This dungeon can be used as an alternative route to the Grand Lift of Dectus in order to access Altus.

The lower levels of the dungeon consist of a series of mineshafts, illuminated by crystals, housing Glintstone Miners and Vulgar Militiamen. Higher up, the caves give way to an exposed portion of the cliff face, displaying ancient architecture.

A Magma Wyrm dwells in the highest cavern, which also contains a lift to Altus Plateau.

sections.text:

Rileigh the Idle, one of the confessors, became a target of the Recusants of Volcano Manor. His sign is found in Altus Plateau, in the ravine south of the Shaded Castle.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - After joining the Volcano Manor and eliminating Old Knight Istvan under Tanith's request, retrieve the second Letter from Volcano Manor to unlock Rileigh's invasion sign in Altus Plateau.
  - With Istvan dead, you can also talk to Patches the Untethered to receive Letter to Patches, tasking you with killing Great Horned Tragoth in Liurnia of the Lakes.
1. Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
  - Once Rileigh is disposed of, return to Tanith to receive the Serpentbone Blade: the Red Letter will now appear, targetting Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood in the Mountaintops of the Giants.
  - You can also visit Recusant Bernhal to receive the Letter to Bernahl, offering you to join him in his hunt against Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm in Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.text: **Rot Disciples**, also known as **Servants of Rot**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Rot Disciples are humanoid spellcasters whose bodies have been overtaken by Scarlet Rot and fungal growth. They act as priests of the Servants of Rot, worshipping and spreading Poison in noxious swamps and old caves.

Rot Disciples fight from a distance, casting toxic bolts and clouds that inflict  Poison or  Scarlet Rot. When the player becomes poisoned, they enter a fervent state that increases their offensive power. Despite their frailty, their persistence and range make them dangerous in confined caverns such as the Abandoned Cave and Stillwater Cave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Deals  Standard damage and  Pierce damage.
- Inflicts  Poison buildup.
- Gains a temporary attack buff while the player is poisoned.
- Weak to  Slash and  Fire damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Raya Lucaria Soldier** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Soldiers in the service of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, also known as the Cuckoos. They were given free rein by the academy to wage war as they pleased, and they are infamous for their rapacious ways.  They wear red-and-blue surcoats bearing a design of two cuckoos peering at a flourishing mass of glintstone, and each of their helms is adorned with a single cuckoo's feather. They are capable of using Cuckoo Glintstone in combat.

When the Academy turned against the Carian Royal Family, the Cuckoos launched an assault on Caria Manor, however they were caught in an enchanted snare. They were turned into spectral puppets, forced to defend the Manor against further invasions.

A detachment of Raya Lucaria Soldiers can be found in the Frenzied Flame Village, having apparently succumbed to Madness.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Royal Revenant** is an enemy and boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Pale, gaunt creatures resembling corpses with many limbs. They emerge from pools of shallow water, and attack with unnatural speed and the ability to inflict Poison.

They are weak to Holy damage, and take damage from and are stunned by healing incantations such as Heal, Great Heal, Lord's Heal and Erdtree Heal, losing half their health if hit. They also take damage from healing over time incantations, such as Blessing's Boon and Blessing of the Erdtree, losing 90% of their health over 30 seconds if affected by such as spell.

They are often accompanied by Revenant Followers.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Royal Revenant encountered in the hidden cellar of Kingsrealm Ruins in north-western Liurnia of the Lakes. It guards a chest containing the Frozen Needle.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
Encountered in a very small room and without having to go through their signature lengthy spawning animation, this Revenant will turn aggressive quickly.

If it leaps towards roll forwards to the left of it and get in a hit before backing away, being ready to roll. Should it start to use more short-ranged melee slams, back away to provoke more leaps. Sometimes it will start to chain these slams into one long combo, either try to keep as far away as possible from this or get behind it if already close.

Occasionally it will start to emit a green color around its head which signifies that it's about to spit out a thin cone of Poison sludge. Potentially dangerous if caught in the middle of an action such as drinking a Flask of Crimson Tears but otherwise easily rolled or jumped away from.

Sometimes it will slip through a portal underground to appear behind its target and spit poison before starting its attack routine again.

sections.heading: Healing incantations
sections.text:
One easy way to kill it is to find an opening to cast a cheap healing spell such as Heal and then cast it again immediately while it's stunned. Any class can do this as even a Prisoner has enough Faith with a Commoner's Garb/Commoner's Simple Garb and Two Fingers Heirloom.

Another way to do this is to summon the Finger Maiden Therolina Puppet, though she's more unreliable in casting her healing incantation.
|-|

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Revenant Followers** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: Cloaked, hunched humanoids with four elongated arms, Revenant Followers wield Wraith Calling Bells, which summon hostile wraiths that pursue their targets. They appear in damp or dark locations, commonly encountered near Royal Revenants. Some Revenant Followers ride pale, emaciated horses. Much like the Revenants, they are weak to Holy damage, and take damage from healing incantations such as Heal, Great Heal, Lord's Heal and Erdtree Heal.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Revenant** (復讐者, *Fukushuusha*, lit. Revenger), also known as the **Night Idol** (夜の偶像, *Yoru no Gūzō*), is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign. She is one of the ten available Nightfarer classes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Revenant is a living doll that joined the Nightfarers to take down the Nightlord.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Revenant is a summoner class that specializes in ranged magic damage.

Revenant is a blue-eyed maiden with porcelain skin and braided white hair. A white veil and a crown of assorted blue flowers rest upon her head. She wears a ghostly white gown, a blue cape, and an assortment of amulets depicting rings. She is often seen playing a lyre while barefoot, and uses a variation of Spirit Ashes system to summon the spirit of a Giant Skeleton.

sections.heading: How to unlock the Revenant
sections.text:
The Revenant is not present at the Roundtable Hold at the start of the game. She must be unlocked before she may be selected.

1. Face or defeat the first Nightlord.
1. Purchase Besmirched Frame () from the Small Jar Bazaar.
1. Locate the Revenant's phantom in the room adjacent to the Table of Lost Grace. She stares at a painting of Lord Radagon.
1. Interact with her and select **Yes** to **Touch the phantom**.
1. Player is transported to a Fort in Limveld, directly facing the same painting of Radagon.
1. Travel southeast to the nearby Ruins.
1. Face the Night Idol.
  - She casts Rejection and Triple Rings of Light.
  - Her summoned buddies will not respawn once defeated.
1. Defeating the Night Idol unlocks the Revenant as a playable character.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Revenant was the last of the eight heroes revealed on April 30, 2025.
- Among the Nightfarers, the Revenant stands as the shortest.
- Her name as a doll, Daphne, is Greek for "laurel".
- Although all Nightfarers have custom movesets with their preferred weapon types, the Revenant is the only one with a moveset unique to her weapon alone and not its type.
- A common internet meme surrounding the Revenant among the player base was using her to wield colossal weapons due to her stature. Notably, this might have been given an official nod in the form of one of the clones spawned during the Everdark Sovereign Libra fight being a Revenant wielding a great sword and great crusher.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
- Although her english name is shared with the Royal Revenant (王族の幽鬼) enemy, her Japanese name, 復讐者, is different and was consistently translated as Revenger in the base game, such as Dragon Communion Revenger Ekzykes, Revenger's Shack, and Edgar the Revenger.
  - Interestingly, she does fight a Royal Revenant by the end of her Remembrance.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Soldiers in the service of General Radahn, reputed to be masterful warriors and rumoured to know no weakness. Their surcoats display the crest of a red-maned lion raising a sword in the image of Radahn, and their visors are styled after a lion's fangs.

They can be found throughout Caelid, fighting off the Scarlet Rot using torches and Fire Pots.

Blue, spectral Radahn Soldiers, akin to puppets, can be found in Fort Faroth.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Redmane Knight** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Knights in the service of General Radahn's Redmane army. They wear the crest of a red-maned lion on their armour and greatshields, and the red plumes on their helms symbolise Radahn's pedigree as the son of Radagon.

When they were driven to defeat by Malenia's Scarlet Rot, the Redmane Knights burned the crest on the left breast of their armour to indicate their resolve, knowing that their duty in Caelid would prevent them from seeing their homes again. They remained in Caelid, staving off the Rot using fire-based techniques, employing Redmane Fire Pots and igniting their own weapons.

The longest-serving Redmane Knight, Ogha, studied gravity-manipulating techniques alongside Radahn.

Spectral Redmane Knights can be found engaged in combat with spectral Cleanrot Knights in the War-Dead Catacombs.
