sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux. Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord. To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

In the past, Gideon took in Nepheli Loux after she lost sight of the guidance of Grace, taking advantage of her youthful credulity.  He promised her that he would not allow the downtrodden to be cheated any longer if he became Elden Lord. He also became acquainted with Preceptor Seluvis and Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, although he and Seluvis would go their separate ways because of Dolores.

At some point, Gideon engaged in a long exchange with the Two Fingers, and in doing so learned that everything—including the Erdtree and the Two Fingers themselves—had been broken. He also glimpsed into the will of Queen Marika the Eternal, shuddering in fear at an end that should not be. He concluded from this that the queen wished for the Tarnished to struggle eternally.

When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable Hold, the first in a long time, Gideon is initially dismissive of them, welcoming them to the Hold but calling them a mere visitor. Gideon encourages the Tarnished to seek a Great Rune in order to gain audience with the Two Fingers and be welcomed as a proper member of the Roundtable Hold.

True to his word, Gideon inducts them as a true member of the Roundtable upon their meeting with the Two Fingers, and shares with them some of the information he has amassed on the Shardbearers.

Although Gideon had amassed knowledge on many of the shardbearers, he had not ascertained the whereabouts of four demigods: Ranni the Witch; Mohg, Lord of Blood; Malenia, Blade of Miquella; and Miquella of the Haligtree. In his search for the latter, he sends his men to ransack the Village of the Albinaurics in Liurnia of the Lakes, knowing that the Albinaurics possess half of a secret medallion that would open the path to the Haligtree. The slaughter of the Albinaurics causes Nepheli to lose faith in him, which causes him to abandon her. He also  sought Latenna, an Albinauric woman with knowledge of the location of the other half of the medallion. If the Tarnished claims one half of the medallion, Gideon's underling Ensha will ambush them in Roundtable Hold, apparently of his own volition. After Ensha is defeated, Gideon compensates the Tarnished by sharing the possible whereabouts of the medallion's other half.

When the Erdtree rejects the Tarnished, forcing them to contemplate journeying to the Forge of the Giants to burn the thorns barring entry into the Erdtree, Gideon encourages them to take no heed of the Fingers' warning that this would be a cardinal sin. He also offers to reward the Tarnished for any information they can deliver on the four great runes whose locations are unknown. If the Tarnished pursues this quest to its ending, finding the cocoon of Miquella within the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, Gideon thanks them, declaring that this is one of the last pieces he needs to put everything together.

After the Tarnished burns the Erdtree and unseals the Rune of Death, Gideon makes his way to Leyndell, Ashen Capital, where he confronts the Tarnished in the Erdtree Sanctuary. Upon his defeat, he warns them that a Tarnished could not become a Lord, and that a man cannot kill a god.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.text: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing is a boss encounter in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. He utilises both sorceries and incantations in combat, and learns new spells depending on whether you have defeated Rykard, Malenia, or Mohg. He only has seven memory slots, and knows six spells by default, meaning that the spells learned by defeating the aforementioned bosses can replace his default spells. If two of these bosses have been defeated, Gideon will lose Comet Azur. If all three have been defeated, he will lose Triple Rings of Light.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Roundtable Hold
  - *(Optional)* If you visit Roundtable Hold before defeating a shardbearer, Gideon can be found in the central chamber of Roundtable Hold. After exhausting his dialogue he will move to his study.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - After defeating a shardbearer and speaking to Finger Reader Enia, Gideon will welcome you as a member of Roundtable Hold, and will offer you information on Godrick the Grafted, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, Starscourge Radahn, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and Morgott, the Omen King. He can also discuss Nepheli Loux if you have spoken to her.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - *(Optional)* If you obtain either half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Ensha will ambush you the next time you return to Roundtable Hold. After defeating him, speak to Gideon to learn the location of the other half.
  - *(Optional)* If you have obtained Seluvis's Potion, you may give it to Gideon to dispose of it. This will remove it from your inventory, preventing you from obtaining Nepheli Loux Puppet or Dung Eater Puppet.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Resting at any Site of Grace in Leyndell, Royal Capital will cause Gideon to receive new dialogue about the unlocated Demigods.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Gideon will now offer rewards in exchange for meeting certain requirements:
    - Black Flame's Protection: activate a Site of Grace in Miquella's Haligtree.
    - Lord's Divine Fortification: defeat Malenia, Blade of Miquella.
    - Fevor's Cookbook 3: activate a Site of Grace in Mohgwyn Palace.
    - Law of Causality: defeat Mohg, Lord of Blood.
1. Leyndell, Ashen Capital
  - Gideon will be present in the Erdtree Sanctuary as a boss encounter after you have defeated Maliketh, the Black Blade. Any previous parts of his questline will now be locked, however the rewards from the previous step can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics is implied by Nepheli to be one of Gideon's agents. Due to the connection between Omenkillers and perfumers, the Depraved Perfumer in the village may be working with the Omenkiller.
- Recusant Henricus, an invader in Limgrave, wears the Eye Surcoat which is said to be worn by Gideon's "eyes and ears". The Eye Surcoat can be looted from a corpse in Rykard's boss arena, indicating another agent of Gideon.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Siofra River** is an underground region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Siofra is said to be the grave of civilizations that flourished before the Erdtree, and evidence of this can be found in the many ancient structures that litter the vast, subterranean space. The towering remains of an ancient dynasty are prominent throughout the area, inhabited by the Claymen who once served as the dynasty's priests.

The lower portion of Siofra River can be accessed via the Siofra River Well in Limgrave's Mistwood. This wooded area is home to spectral Ancestral Followers, who live alongside a diverse assortment of wildlife. The remains of a great, horned beast can be found in the Hallowhorn Grounds. Interacting with the remains after lighting the flames scattered throughout the area will facilitate an encounter with an Ancestor Spirit. This area also connects to Caelid via the Deep Siofra Well.

Towering over the woodland is Nokron, one of the Eternal Cities inhabited by the Nox. Nokron is initially inaccessible, however a route is opened when a star falls upon Limgrave, following the defeat of Starscourge Radahn. The Fingerslayer Blade, a treasure of Nokron said to be able to harm the Greater Will and its vassal Fingers, is found within Night's Sacred Ground, beneath a chair-crypt that holds a vast corpse. This upper region also houses another Hallowhorn Grounds, from which the Regal Ancestor Spirit can be encountered. Nearby, the aqueduct hides a coffin which can be used to access Deeproot Depths, guarded by a pair of Valiant Gargoyles.

To the east, on a separate island within the vast cavern, are the ruins of an ancient palace. It is here that Mohg, Lord of Blood has established the seat of his coming Mohgwyn Dynasty, and all the nightmares it may bring.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sage Gowry** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
**Gowry** is an elderly sage dwelling in the blighted Caelid Wilds. When the Empyrean Malenia unleashed the Scarlet Rot during her battle with General Radahn, she permanently blighted Caelid. Since that day, Gowry has dedicated himself to her and the Order of Rot he hopes she will usher in.

Gowry found Millicent and her sisters in the Swamp of Aeonia and raised them as his daughters. Seeing them as buds, he sent each of Millicent's sisters to the Haligtree in the hopes that they would bloom into scarlet valkyries.

Millicent became consumed by the Scarlet Rot, and was housed in a church, where she was worshipped by the Pests. Gowry sought the aid of a Tarnished, offering to reveal to them the secret of the magical town of Sellia in exchange for their aid. Gowry bids the Tarnished to journey deep into the Swamp of Aeonia to retrieve a needle of unalloyed gold, which could stem the effects of the Scarlet Rot. After the Tarnished retrieves the needle, Gowry shares the secret of the town, and asks them for another favor; to find Millicent and give her the needle.

Gowry avoids Millicent when she comes to visit his shack, later telling the Tarnished that she has no need of him anymore, and must embark on her fated journey. The Tarnished may aid Millicent on her journey, even giving her a prosthetic arm. Doing so will earn them Gowry's good will, who will offer to teach them a rot incantation, and reveal to them his allegiance to Malenia.

As Millicent travels to the Haligtree, where Malenia awaits, she draws ever closer to her "sisters", who made the same journey as her. Gowry bids the Tarnished to aid the sisters in murdering Millicent, believing that a betrayal by someone she trusts so dearly will cause her to blossom into a flower, which will be reborn as a scarlet valkyrie when Malenia ascends to godhood.

Should the Tarnished kill Millicent, they will return to Gowry's shack to find him seemingly dead. Should they instead aid Millicent against her sisters, she will prevail, but will remove the golden needle, willfully allowing herself to succumb to the Scarlet Rot. The Tarnished may then find Gowry lamenting Millicent's decision, questioning whether she and Malenia detests him and the other children of rot so utterly.

If the Tarnished attempts to kill Gowry, his body will transform into that of a Kindred of Rot. Upon returning to his shack, he will once again resume his human form, revealing that he can inhabit other pests to avoid death.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Caelid (Sellia, Town of Sorcery)
  - Gowry can be found in his shack near the entrance to Sellia. He will request that you find an Unalloyed Gold Needle in the swamp and bring it to him in exchange for a secret about Sellia.
1. Caelid (Swamp of Aeonia)
  - Travel to the Swamp of Aeonia and defeat Commander O'Neil to obtain the Unalloyed Gold Needle.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Smithing Master Hewg** is a character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Hewg is a blacksmith at the Roundtable Hold who improves armaments to maximum level and provides other services.

sections.heading: Services
sections.text:
- **Strengthen Armament**: Hewg incrementally strengthens weapons up to their maximum levels, but requires Smithing Stones (or Somber Smithing Stones) and  Runes to do so.
- **Ashes of War**: Hewg applies Ashes of War and Affinities to weapons.
- **Ash of War Duplication**: Hewg converts Lost Ashes of War into any known Ashes of War.
- **Sell**: Hewg purchases any unwanted items from the player.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A Scaly Misbegotten bearing aspects of the primordial Crucible, Hewg practiced the once-divine art of smithing. A spirit tuner with distinctive eyes helped him out in the distant past, though she died before he could repay her.

Long ago, Queen Marika cursed Hewg with an impossible task under her Golden Order: to create a weapon capable of slaying a god. Chained to the Roundtable Hold for eternity, he maintained the weapons of Tarnished seeking the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
When he meets Roderika,  he recognizes that her eyes share the same hue as those of his old acquaintance. Although reluctant at first, Hewg agrees to take Roderika under his wing at the insistence of the the Tarnished.

After the Tarnished sets fire to the Erdtree, the Roundtable Hold also begins to burn. Hewg's chains are broken, yet he insists on remaining in the hold, where he can continue to smith weapons to slay a god, despite Roderika's pleas for him to leave. As the Roundtable burns, Hewg's mental state deteriorates, causing him to slur his words and, eventually, to forget both Roderika and the Tarnished. Roderika decides to respect Hewg's decision to stay at the Roundtable, and resolves to remain with him. Her last request is for the Tarnished to use the weapons Hewg smithed to slay Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Hewg's Quest
sections.text: - Hewg and Roderika's questlines progress together.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.text:
Smithing Master Hewg remains in a fixed location at the Roundtable Hold throughout the entire game.

1. Speak to Hewg
1. Once Roderika arrives at the Roundtable Hold, speak to Hewg and select the **"About Roderika"** dialogue option.
  - Return to Roderika and tell her what Hewg said.
  - Return to Hewg and select **"About Roderika"** again, followed by **"Would you watch over Roderika?"** and finally **"It's what she wants"**.
  - Reload the area. Roderika moves, seated across from Hewg, now offers spirit tuning services.
1. Upon reaching the Forge of the Giants, return and talk for advice.
1. After burning the Erdtree, return to the Roundtable Hold and select **"Let's talk a while"**. You may then select the dialogue option **"Why are you still making weapons?"**
  - After talking to Roderika and selecting **"About Hewg"**, return to Hewg and select **"What happened to her?"**
1. After defeating the Godskin Duo, return to Roundtable Hold and speak to Hewg and select **"About the god-slaying weapon"**.
1. After defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, return to Hewg and select **"About yourself"**.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- He wears a brown smith's apron and wields a Hammer.
- Although Hewg shares a model with fellow Scaled Misbegotten, he lacks a tail and hair, but has a beard.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Hewg resembles Dark Souls' Andre of Astora. Both are bearded, older, do not leave, wield hammers, upgrade weapons, are always hammering, and can be interacted with for dialogue and lore. They also share a pariah status in their settings, Hewg being a Misbegotten and Andre being an undead.
- In an early prerelease version of *Elden Ring*, Hewg was found in Stormhill Shack, which at that time served as a character hub. Notably, this is now where Roderika is initially found.
  - Redeemer Guilbert advised the player to meet Hewg, wondering whether he held any unresolved grudges.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Serpent-Hunter** is a Great Spear, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Mt. Gelmir (Volcano Manor)
**Loot: **Can be picked up within the boss arena of Praetor Rykard, just after the fog gate.

This item does not re-spawn when the player has one in either their inventory or chest, even in NG+. However it will re-spawn (and thus can be picked up again) from the same location should the player discard it. This is to make sure that the player always have the means of fighting Rykard with it.

Because of this safeguard it is still possible to obtain duplicates of this weapon:
- **Requirements:**
  - The player needs to not have a copy it in their inventory.
  - Rykard needs to still be alive.
  - The game needs to be in online-mode.
- 1) Stand outside Rykard's arena and attempt to connect to another player's world through any means necessary.
(Tarnished's Furled Finger, Duelist's Furled Finger, Bloody Finger, Recusant Finger, Festering Bloody Finger or Blue Cipher Ring)
- 2) When the game has successfully found a world it can try to connect to, enter Rykard's arena and pick up the Serpent-Hunter before the Loading Screen appears.
- 3) Leave the multiplayer session either by completing your objective or using the Finger Severer.
- 4) When you re-spawn back in your own world, do not fast travel or rest at the Sites of Grace, instead enter Rykard's arena again and you'll see the Serpent Hunter is still there, available to be picked up again for a second time.
(Traveling or resting at the site of grace will make the game check if the Serpent-Hunter is in your inventory before it decides if it'll spawn in a new one for you to pick up)
- It's possible to obtain even more copies of this weapon if the player simply loops back to step 1 after finishing step 3.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The Serpent-Hunter's special effect only activates when fighting the God-Devouring Serpent and Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. It does not activate against Base Serpent Messmer or other serpents.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Shadowbound Beasts** (影従の獣, *Eijuu no Kemono*), also known as **Shadows** (影, *Kage*), are a concept in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Wolves are the undying vassals of Empyreans, shadowbound beasts granted by the Two Fingers. Often half-humanoid in appearance, they are tailor-made to reflect their Empyreans and execute their masters' will with unerring loyalty.  Should their Empyreans reject the path to godhood presented by the Two Fingers, a terrible curse causes the loyal blades to go mad, becoming dangerous Baleful Shadows.

sections.heading: Maliketh
sections.text: The first named Shadowbound Beast is Maliketh, the Black Blade, who became the loyal shadow and half-brother of Queen Marika the Eternal. However, her sole need of her shadow was a vessel to lock away Destined Death, which was harboured in his sword after the defeat of the Gloam-Eyed Queen. After a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen during the Night of Black Knives he sealed the rune within his own body so that none could steal Death again. When the stolen fragment sprouted in the form of Deathroot throughout the Lands Between, he would attempt to recover it under the alias Gurranq, Beast Clergyman by consuming the Deathroot.

sections.heading: Blaidd
sections.text: The other named Shadowbound Beast is Blaidd the Half-Wolf. Blaidd was approved by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon and given to her daughter, the Empyrean Ranni the Witch, at a young age. He became her stepbrother and they grew up together. In defiance of the fate he was born into, he swore to serve no other master but Ranni, assisting her in her rebellion against the Two Fingers. Against his own will, Blaidd would eventually succumb to becoming a Baleful Shadow, but in his final moments gave himself to Ranni.

sections.heading: Baleful Shadows
sections.text: Although all Shadows who turn on their Empyreans are considered Baleful Shadows, there are particular Baleful Shadows that are assassins of the Two Fingers. The last of the Baleful Shadows is killed by the Tarnished in the Ainsel River during Ranni the Witch's quest.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The wolf statues at Crumbling Farum Azula resemble Red Wolves, though they were Beastmen in the concept art.
- A Tarnished known as Vargram the Raging Wolf aspired to become a wolf and shadow of an Empyrean.
- It is unknown whether the Miquella the Kind, Malenia, Goddess of Rot, and the Gloam-Eyed Queen ever had Shadowbound Beasts, as they are not mentioned and never appear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Scarlet Rot** (朱い腐敗, *Akai Fuhai*) is a status effect in *Elden Ring*, inflicting damage over time to the player and serving as a more dangerous variant of the Poison status effect. The player's resistance to this status ailment is determined by their Immunity stat, which is increased by the Vigor stat.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Scarlet Rot is an old legend in the Lands Between, a dangerous sickness that eats away life like a vicious plague. It corrupts men and beasts who come into contact with it, deforming their bodies and eating away their wits, driving them to madness and causing them to act like wild animals. Those afflicted with the Scarlet Rot such as Millicent also suffer from nightmares due to the affliction. Areas afflicted with Scarlet Rot sprout fungal growths or flower buds. As such, Scarlet Rot is often fended off using fire.

The Empyrean and demigod, Malenia, Blade of Miquella harbored the affliction of Scarlet Rot within her body from birth, which has decayed her body and caused her to lose her limbs. Her will, pride, dignity, and sense of self, along with the help of her brother Miquella of the Haligtree's Unalloyed Gold Needle assisted with resisting the call of the Scarlet Rot. However, at the Battle of Aeonia, the final battle of the Shattering, she abandoned this pride to meet Starscourge Radahn's measure. This resulted in the blooming of the first flower of Aeonia causing both Caelid and Radahn to become blighted by the Scarlet Rot.  Upon Malenia's return to Miquella's Haligtree, it too was infected and malformed by the Scarlet Rot. The Swamp of Aeonia spawned by the flower in Caelid gave rise to Kindred of Rot, also known as "Pests." Some inorganic beings are capable of contracting and hosting the disease; a number of Crystalians, and their weapons, fester with Scarlet Rot.

Despite the horrific effects of the sickness, some worship the Scarlet Rot as a god. The sickly Maleigh Marais of the Shaded Castle was a private believer, and considered Malenia his personal goddess. To those enraptured by the Scarlet Rot, the mushrooms that spawn from it growing on their bodies are holy vestments that root them to the earth. Long ago, great lords served the Scarlet Rot, perhaps with such large fungal bodies serving as their crowns. Ever since the Battle of Aeonia, Sage Gowry has dedicated himself to the resplendence of the Order of Rot, the cycle of decay and rebirth, desiring Malenia to bloom into a goddess, and her daughters to join her as scarlet valkyries.

Long ago, Malenia's mentor, the Blind Swordsman, sealed away an ancient god that was Rot itself using a flowing sword bestowed upon him by a fairy in legend. The divine essence of this Outer God was sealed in the Lake of Rot in the Ainsel River deep below Liurnia of the Lakes.

The head confessor Crepus, an assassin of the Roundtable Hold serving the Two Fingers, used bolts imbued with Scarlet Rot with his Black-Key Crossbow.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.text: Scarlet Rot accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Immunity stat, the longer it will take for Scarlet Rot to become effective. Immunity can be increased by increasing the Vigor stat. Once effective, the player will receive continual damage over time until the effect wears off.

sections.heading: Skills
sections.text: There are currently no skills in the game that apply Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Buffs related to Scarlet Rot
sections.text: There are certain equipment that gives the player buffs when scarlet rot has been inflicted in the general vicinity, they do not discriminate between what has been poisoned in order to activate, it can be friend, foe and even oneself and generally lasts for around 20 seconds since the last rot infliction.

sections.heading: Swamps
sections.text:
Rot swamps can be found in several locations throughout the Lands Between.
They generally comprise of bodies of filthy sludge that continuously build up Scarlet Rot as the player is standing in them. Rolling around in said sludge will also cover the player-character's body with the fluids, which will slowly yet consistently build up Scarlet Rot even if the player is no longer directly standing in the liquid itself or even tries to cure their Rot ailment with boluses. While these stains will gradually wear off over time, they can be removed immediately if it's raining, the player rolls around in clean water or uses Soap.

sections.text:
Enemies capable of inflicting Scarlet Rot include:
- Giant Land Squirt (Swamp of Aeonia)

- Putrid Corpse (Scarlet Rot, Giant Scarlet Rot, and Mushroom Variants)

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Despite the Antspur Rapier indicating that the Giant Ants can inflict Scarlet Rot, they don't in actual gameplay. This is either because it was fashioned from an ant that was infected with the disease (such ants are not encountered by the player) or Marais somehow modified it.

- "朱い" in the Japanese "朱い腐敗" is a spelling of the word "赤い" (red) which indicates the color vermilion, rather than scarlet.  While both are bright, reddish colors, vermillion has a distinctly more orange hue than scarlet; an example of this is Malenia's flower.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sellia, Town of Sorcery** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A town in Caelid on the eastern bank of the Swamp of Aeonia.

The Eternal City of Nokron sleeps below Sellia, and it is said that the Sellians are descended from the city's inhabitants. Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, one of the founding Glintstone Sorcerers, came from Sellia. Other Sellian sorcerers followed in Lusat's footsteps, travelling to the Academy of Raya Lucaria to study the Olivinus Conspectus.

Sellian sorcerers are assassins who are said to hunt their fellow sorcerers, employing night sorceries that allowed them to turn their weapons, or their own bodies, invisible to deceive their enemies.

General Radahn studied gravity sorcery in Sellia in his youth, learning from an Alabaster Lord. The knowledge he gained allowed him to challenge the stars during the Starscourge Conflict, where he held the town of Sellia secure.

Presently, the town is inhabited by spectral Glintstone Sorcerers and mechanical marionettes, and many of the buildings have been ensnared by the roots that trail from the nearby Swamp of Aeonia. Several buildings are protected by seals, which can be broken by lighting the flames at the tops of the town's three towers. Lighting all three will break the seal that blocks the entrance to the chair-crypt, where two former Nox inhabitants of the Eternal Cities reside.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Shardbearers** (破片の君主, *Hahen no Kunshu*) are special bosses that are key to progression in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Defeating a shardbearer grants the player a Great Rune. To progress the story, at least one Great Rune is required to gain an audience with the Two Fingers at the Roundtable Hold, while two are needed to access Leyndell, Royal Capital. Defeating at least three Shardbearers is necessary to achieve an ending.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Shardbearers were the inheritors of the Great Runes, the fragments of the Elden Ring, and were primarily among the Demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal. Uniquely among the Shardbearers, Ranni the Witch cast aside her Great Rune. The mad taint of the power they acquired from their Great Runes precipitated the Shattering wherein most of them fought for control of the Lands Between. However, none succeeded in becoming Elden Lord, or the god of a new age.

Unlike the other Shardbearers, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, is not a Demigod. She received her Great Rune of the Unborn from Radagon of the Golden Order long before the Shattering. This Great Rune was removed from the Elden Ring long ago and stored within the amber egg that was left by her former husband.

The Tarnished, upon their return to the Lands Between, were tasked by the Two Fingers to defeat the Shardbearers in order to claim their Great Runes, and use them to repair the shattered Elden Ring. Several Tarnished, such as Roundtable Knight Vyke and Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, became shardbearers and earned a personal audience with the Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Facing the Shardbearers
sections.text:
Certain bosses or events must be completed before the shardbearers can be fought.
1. Godrick the Grafted (Stormveil Castle, Limgrave):
  - Defeat Margit, the Fell Omen and navigate Stormveil Castle
1. Mohg, Lord of Blood (Mohgwyn Palace, Siofra River):
  - Use the item given by Varre after completing his quest at Rose Church or take the waygate in the Consecrated Snowfield
1. Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (Academy of Raya Lucaria, Liurnia of the Lakes):
  - Defeat Red Wolf of Radagon and navigate the Academy of Raya Lucaria
1. Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy (Volcano Manor, Mt. Gelmir):
  - Speak to Tanith at the Volcano Manor after completing all three of her contracts, or take the waygate after defeating the Godskin Noble in the Volcano Manor
1. Starscourge Radahn (Redmane Castle, Caelid):
  - Speak to Jerren at Redmane Castle after reaching Altus Plateau or defeating the Crucible Knight & Misbegotten Warrior duo

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- There are several demigods who are not known to be shardbearers. Namely, Godwyn the Golden, Godefroy the Grafted, and the Soulless Demigods carried in the Wandering Mausoleums.
  - Messmer the Impaler is not a shardbearer. He was sent on his crusade and forlorned in the Realm of Shadow prior to Radagon leaving Rennala.
- Radagon was a shardbearer before he gave the amber egg to Rennala.
- The Scadutree Avatar technically becomes a shardbearer after Miquella discards his Great Rune.
- Both Patches and White Mask Varré allude to having gained an audience with the Two Fingers. Similar to other NPCs, they do not drop Great Runes upon defeat.
- Melina receives the Rune of Death in the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending if she did not sacrifice herself at the Forge of the Giants.
- Rennala also did not participate in the Shattering due to being locked inside Raya Lucaria Grand Library after the Academy's mages rebelled against the Carian Royals.
  - When the Tarnished confronts Rennala, their battle is interrupted by Ranni the Witch, who conjures a phantom of Rennala in her prime from the amber egg, which the Tarnished defeats instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Localisation Notes
  - In Japanese, the shardbearers are rather called "Monarchs of Fragments" or "Sovereigns of Shards" (破片の君主, *Hahen no Kunshu*.)
    - The Sword Monument that reads "The First Defense of Leyndell / A sovereign alliance rots from within / Traces yet remain of bloody conspiracy" also uses the same kanji 君主 (*Kunshu*) to refer to the "sovereign alliance." This may indicate an alliance between the shardbearers before the First Defense.
  - In English, Enia calls the player a shardbearer after they acquire a Great Rune, however, in Japanese she simply calls them "Master of the/a Great Rune" (大ルーンの主, *Dai Rūn no Omo*.)
  - In English, Tanith refers to the shardbearers vying for power, however, in Japanese she uniquely calls them "Great Rune Monarchs" / "Sovereigns of (the) Great Rune(s)" / (大ルーンの君主, *Dai Rūn no Kunshu*.)

sections.heading: Effects

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Young Albinaurics**, also known as **Second-Generation Albinaurics**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Young Albinaurics are pale, pot-bellied creatures with frog-like faces and large, vacuous, black eyes. Created by human hands, the arcane circumstances of their birth has led many to believe they live impure lives untouched by the Erdtree's grace. Unlike the first generation, the second generation retains the use of their legs at the cost of their ability to speak. Their improved physique allows them to wield a greater variety of weapons, which they use to fight back against the formidable sorcerers that seek to slay them. They revered the ripple and the Crescent Moon.

Some young Albinaurics traveled to the Consecrated Snowfield in search of Miquella's Haligtree. They were imbued with holy energy.

Others followed Miquella to the Mohgwyn Palace, sprouting tangled horns and turning crimson after receiving a boon from the Formless Mother via Mohg's accursed Omen blood. These Sanguine Albinaurics produce bloodthorns whenever they cartwheel, suggesting a link to the blood star. The larger Albinaurics blow into their Curved Great Clubs like alpine horns, summoning the legless Giant Skeletons like the Tibia Mariner in Wyndham Ruins.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Regular Albinaurics who freely roam Liurnia of the Lakes, often gathered around the ruins that dot the landscape.

sections.heading: Blessed
sections.text: Albinaurics blessed by grace, their once dim eyes now shining with a golden gift. They are capable of casting Discus of Light at foes, and are otherwise unremarkable from their regular variants.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Albinaurics tainted by Mohg, Lord of Blood's accursed blood. They roam the swamp surrounding Mohgwyn Palace, ready to defend their Lord from those who would seek to stop the birth of his Dynasty. Those that carry the Great Curved Clubs are able to beckon forth Giant Skeletons. Those that possess lighter weaponry are able to bristle sharpened Bloodthorns of accursed blood from their bodies. Either cart-wheeling into intruders and shredding them to pieces, or painfully expelling them onto their immediate vicinity.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Their frog faces are a reference to the leglessness of other Albinaurics (tadpoles).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - *Albinauric* is a constructed term derived from Latin roots *albus* (pale, white) and ** (gold), suggesting an approximation of silver made from gold.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sleep** is a status effect in *Elden Ring*, incapacitating most lesser enemies for an extended period of time or inflicting heavy stagger towards stronger enemies and players alike as well as draining a chunk of the player's FP, making it into a slightly less dangerous version of Madness. The player's resistance to this status ailment is determined by their Focus stat, which is increased by the Mind stat.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.text:
Inflicting Sleep on a player will briefly stagger them, even through a roll, and drains FP equal to 30 + 10% of max FP.
Inflicting on most generic enemies will briefly stagger them.

Sleep has special interactions with certain enemies: some, like the Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble, Vulgar Militia, and Mad Pumpkin Heads, will fall into a heavier sleep, making them vulnerable to a Critical Attack and potentially sleeping for up to a minute if not damaged. Others, enemies that ride other entities, will get knocked off their mount. This includes almost all enemies on horseback (such as Godrick Knights, Cuckoo Knights, Leyndell Knights, and Kaiden Sellswords) but also the Giant Ant-riding Nox Swordstresses but doesn't include Night's Cavalry (since they are immune to Sleep) or Tree Sentinels (since them and their horse are effectively one entity).

sections.heading: Eternal Sleep
sections.text: A special variant of Sleep introduced with Shadow of the Erdtree, Eternal Sleep has slightly different effects from regular Sleep. The FP drain to players is increased to 50 + 15% of max FP, weaker enemies such as Godrick Soldiers can potentially be slept permanently and never wake up, and bosses vulnerable to Sleep won't wake up the until 5 seconds after they were first attacked and aren't susceptible to Critical Attacks.

sections.heading: Spells
sections.text: There are no spells that inflict sleep in the game currently.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skeletons** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Skeletons are found all throughout the Lands Between and come in several different variants employing a myriad of different weapons.

They are vulnerable to Strike damage and most often vulnerable Holy damage. As they are part of Those Who Live in Death they are also very weak to certain holy based attacks such as the Golden Epitaph, Skill: Shared Order, and Holy Water Pot.

All skeletons also carry a trait unique to this enemy type where they do not die immediately upon having their health reduced to zero. Instead, after a few seconds, their remains begin to glow white and they can be finished off with any damage, or else they resurrect after another few seconds, now with full health.

This resurrection mechanics can be skipped by killing them with certain weapons more effective against Those Who Live in Death.

There is also a version of the regular Skeleton variant, found only in Black Knife Catacombs, who cannot be finished off when defeated. Instead, they can only be dealt with permanently by killing one of the nearby Necromancer variant Commoners that otherwise keep them "alive".

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Skeleton warriors found only on the surface (and within Sage's Cave) they carry a wide variety of weapons and clothes that help distinguish them from each other. They can be found in graveyards all across the Lands Between and many of them are linked to local Tibia Mariners, meaning should certain local Mariner's be felled, then the presence of these skeletons may fade from several nearby graveyards as a result.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: These enemies are often encountered in groups, with Grave Wardens and Crossbow Militiamen providing range support while Knights close in from the front while blocking attacks and Bandits use their jump attacks.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Heavily built skeletons wielding greataxes and halberds, they have much greater poise than normal skeletons and will attack sequentially as long a Tarnished remains near.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Skeletons with golden bones, they share most of their moveset with the normal counterparts however with the addition of an attack that involves them gliding around the air like a kite while spewing magic gas beneath them. They've also shed most of their frailty against holy damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: As these are so similar to the base variant of the skeleton, their sudden flight is likely to prove quite a scare when first encountered. Additionally, their existence is largely limited to one graveyard in Altus Plateau that is just east of Hermit Merchant (Capital Outskirts).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Scarabs**, also known as **Teardrop Scarabs**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Scarabs are beetles found throughout the Lands Between, typically rolling balls of various colors, which indicate the type of item they drop when killed. Scarabs are sources of valuable resources such as spells, ashes of war, smithing stones, and replenishments for the Sacred Flasks. They come in various colors and sizes, each bearing an eye on their thorax.

Scarabs are non-hostile wildlife that flee when approached. They roll their precious dung away from perceived threats before vanishing. Some scarabs are nearly invisible, leaving only tracks on the ground that follow a set pattern, making them predictable to hit. Certain scarabs can also fly, hovering in place until attacked. In rare cases, scarabs will explode when attacked, killing themselves and damaging nearby foes.

The laborious beetles abandoned their treasured balls and returned home when it was time for them to die.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Red Crimson Teardrop Scarabs that roll balls of golden twigs filled with crimson tears.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: When killed, they will restore charges to the Flask of Crimson Tears.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Blue Cerulean Teardrop Scarabs that roll balls of golden twigs filled with cerulean tears.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: When killed, they will restore charges to the Flask of Cerulean Tears.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Grey scarabs that roll clumps of ash. When killed, they drop Ashes of War which can be added to weapons to apply affinities and skills.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Blue-green scarabs that roll clumps of glintstone. When killed, they drop sorceries.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Golden scarabs that roll clumps of stone containing incantations, which they drop when killed.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.text: Grey scarabs that roll clumps of stone. They drop smithing stones when killed.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: Scarabs are found throughout the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text: Scarabs typically have no attacks and will flee. Some scarabs may detonate themselves, dealing area-of-effect damage. Other scarabs teleport instantaneously when attacked. These scarabs have simply moved to a predetermined location nearby.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- There are six different colors for scarabs.
- Nearby scarabs play a sound cue.
- Scarabs disappear after fleeing from the player. This is forewarned by a series of sound and visual cues and is interrupted when the scarab takes damage.
- Scarabs that have disappeared can be reencountered after resting at a Site of Grace.
- Those that drop unique loot, such as Ashes of War, will no longer respawn once defeated.
- Scarabs that refill the Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears will respawn.
- The Gold Scarab and Silver Scarab talismans provide bonuses to Runes earned and Item Discovery respectively.
- There are five headgear items based on scarabs: the Ash-of-War Scarab, Cerulean Tear Scarab, Crimson Tear Scarab, Glintstone Scarab, and Incantation Scarab.
- Scarabs drop Talismans in Elden Ring Nightreign. They respawn after disappearing.
- The scarab is the seal of the Everdark Sovereigns and appears on the Collector Signboard in *Nightreign*.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Scarabs are the only enemies that can despawn themselves.
- The symbol displayed on the Gold and Silver Scarab talismans also appears on the Crimson Teardrop Scarab depicted in the icon for About Teardrop Scarabs. A different icon appears on the bodies of Teardrop Scarabs in-game.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sanguine Noble** is an enemy and boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Nobles who serve Mohg, Lord of Blood. They serve as both assassins who emerge from pools of blood to strike down foes, and missionaries who share the gospel of the accursed blood. They bear elaborate designs on their shoulders to signify the noble rank they intend to claim once Mohg's dynasty has been established.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A Sanguine Noble encountered in the cellar of Writheblood Ruins in Altus Plateau. This enemy guards a chest containing a Bloody Helice, the same weapon wielded by all Sanguine Nobles.
|-|

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Sanguine Noble at the Second Church of Marika will only spawn before or after the encounter with Bloody Finger Hunter Yura and Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger. It will not spawn while they are present.
- Sanguine Nobles wield a Bloody Helices in their right hand and a Reduvia in their left hand.
  - If blood loss is inflicted near them, they receive a damage boost similar to Lord of Blood's Exultation; they are highly vulnerable to suffering a bleed.
- The Sanguine Noble Set is dropped by Sanguine Noble (Invader) in the Consecrated Snowfield. This is an NPC who does not have the same model or moveset as the Sanguine Noble enemy, and who dual wields Reduvias just like Nerijus.
- Sanguine Nobles have black horns resembling Mohg's protruding from their necks. They also have horns growing downwards out of the soles of their feet, serving like high heels, and they also have long claws on their fingers and toes.
  - The nobles may be a late stage of the "cessblood" affliction used among the Bloody Fingers, as this seems to use Mohg's own blood.
- Their internal name is "daemonbloodlaity."
  - Daemonblood, again, likely references them having been given the injection as per the initiation ritual.
  - A laity is non-ordained member of a religious organization; a layperson.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Shabriri** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He is a spirit that possesses the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, appearing after the player ascends the Grand Lift of Rold. Note that once Shabriri appears, Yura's questline will end regardless of how much progress has been made in it. It is not necessary to have started or completed Yura's questline for Shabriri to appear. If player visits the Three Fingers before reaching Shabriri, he will not appear. The Ronin's Set can be found on the ground where he would otherwise stand.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The most reviled man in all history, Shabriri was found guilty of slander long ago and sentenced to blindness. With his eyeballs completely gouged out, it is said that, in time, the Frenzied Flame came to dwell within his empty sockets. He believed that chaos should take the world and was regarded to be the origin of the sickness of Frenzied Flame. Following his death, Shabriri endured as a spirit capable of inhabiting the bodies of others.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.text: The Tarnished encounters Shabriri in the Mountaintops of the Giants, where he is inhabiting the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura. The Tarnished, at the behest of Melina, is bound for the Forge of the Giants so she may set the Erdtree aflame. However, Shabriri advises the Tarnished to seek out the Three Fingers in the depths below Leyndell, revealing that their ascendency to the throne of Elden Lord would otherwise require Melina's sacrifice. He proposes an alternative path: the Tarnished may spare the life of Melina by inheriting the flame of frenzy and using their own body as kindling. Shabriri bids the Tarnished become the Lord of Chaos, burning the Erdtree to the ground and incinerating all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Shabriri is found near the  Zamor Ruins Site of Grace on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Summon Sign
sections.text: Shabriri is a summonable cooperator for the Godfrey, First Elden Lord / Hoarah Loux, Warrior boss fight if the player has visited the Three Fingers and has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.text:
- Shabriri can be attacked and killed at the Mountaintops of the Giants ( 3,107 HP).
- Drops:  1,000, Iron Kasa, Ronin's Armor, Ronin's Gauntlets, and Ronin's Greaves.
- The version of Shabriri at the Mountaintops of the Giants can cast one extra spell: Inescapable Frenzy.

sections.heading: Shabriri's Quest
sections.text: - Shabriri's questline intersects with the following NPCs: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, Melina

sections.heading: Questline Steps
sections.text:
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
  - Shabriri can be found by the  Zamor Ruins Site of Grace near the beginning of the Mountaintops of the Giants area. Exhaust his dialogue to unlock new dialogue from Melina when resting at a Site of Grace.
1. Frenzied Flame Proscription
  - Travel to the Frenzied Flame Proscription through the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and Cathedral of the Forsaken. Remove all of your armor and interact with the door on the lowest floor for a cutscene in which the Three Fingers embrace you. This can be done regardless of whether you have met Shabriri already. Doing so will cause Shabriri to disappear from his previous location.
  - This will unlock the Lord of Frenzied Flame Ending. This will lock you out of achieving any of the other endings unless you obtain Miquella's Needle by completing Millicent's quest and defeating Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and using it in Dragonlord Placidusax's boss room.
1. *(Optional)* Leyndell, Ashen Capital
  - Shabriri will be available as a cooperator to assist with the fight against Godfrey, First Elden Lord at the Elden Throne if the player has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Shabriri and Bloody Finger Hunter Yura wear the same armor set and have the same face data and voice actor; however, Shabriri does not use Yura's Nagakiba or battle art, instead wielding an Uchigatana with Impaling Thrust.
- Shabriri performs a unique gesture: he covers his eyes with both hands.
- Shabriri was said to have gained the Flame of Frenzy from reading the message imprinted on the tomb of an ancient god by the Readerless Fingers.
- The eyeballs of those afflicted with madness were called Shabriri Grapes. Lightseeker Hyetta, a blind maiden, is guided to the Three Fingers after consuming enough of them.
- Shabriri most likely influenced Roundtable Knight Vyke to inherit the Frenzied Flame and  spare his Finger Maiden. Festering Fingerprint Vyke invades near the body of his maiden and drops a Fingerprint Grape, which is a Shabriri Grape touched by the Three Fingers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Shabriri is voiced by , who also voiced Yura, Kaiden Sellswords, and the Fire Giant.
- *"Shabriri"* (lit. "dazzling glare") is a demon associated with blindness in Jewish folklore and Talmudic demonology. It rests on uncovered water at night and blinds those who drink from it. In modern Hebrew, the literal translation for *shabriri* is "fragile".

They are viscous, silver droplets, and they can manifest spear-like appendages from their bodies. Some can generate electricity, while others sport hardened shields that protect them from damage.

A variation, known as the Mimic Tear, was created in the Eternal City in an attempt to forge a lord. They initially appear as standard Silver Tears, but they can morph into other forms.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Spinning Slash** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It comes in two different variants carrying the same name, one is generic, is available as an Ash of War and is native to many different weapons (particularly among Curved Swords, Curved Greatswords, Twinblades, Halberds and Reapers). While the other variant, despite sharing the exact same name, has unique, additional Ice Lightning properties and only exists on one weapon, the Dragon Halberd.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and halberds (except for Colossal Swords) with the Ash of War: Spinning Slash.
- Innate skill of many Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Curved Greatswords, Twinblades, Halberds, and Reapers.
  - Straight Swords: Crystal Sword, Rotten Crystal Sword, and Warhawk's Talon.
  - Curved Swords: Bandit's Curved Sword, Beastman's Curved Sword, Falchion, Flowing Curved Sword, Grossmesser, Mantis Blade, Scavenger's Curved Sword, Scimitar, Shamshir, and Shotel.
  - Curved Greatswords: Beastman's Cleaver, Dismounter, Freyja's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Omen Cleaver, and Monk's Flameblade.
  - Twinblades: Black Steel Twinblade Shadow of the Erdtree, Gargoyle's Twinblade, Gargoyle's Black Blades, Twinblade, and Twinned Knight Swords.
  - Halberds: Gargoyle's Black Halberd, Gargoyle's Halberd, Glaive, Guardian's Swordspear, Nightrider Glaive, Pest's Glaive, Ripple Crescent Halberd, Vulgar Militia Saw, and Vulgar Militia Shotel.
  - Reapers: Grave Scythe and Scythe.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Spin once, hitting for 110% (105% with larger weapons and Twinblades) of Attack Power.

Using the skill again afterwards makes the user spin twice again, hitting for 65% and 115% (60% and 110% on larger weapons and Twinblades) of Attack Power respectively.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The first spin costs 10 points (20 points for larger weapons) of Stamina to perform. The follow-up spin costs 25 points (35 points for larger weapons) of Stamina to perform, 10 points for the first hit and 15 points (25 points for larger weapons) respectively.
- Weapons that use the tight spin/small weapons are Daggers, Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Twinblades, and Axes, while weapons with the sweeping spin/larger weapons are Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Greataxes, Spears, Great Spears, Halberds, and Reapers.
- 
- Particularly effective on very long weapons like a Pike or Nagakiba, especially since the latter uses the quicker variant.
- For smaller weapons if the first hit lands an enemy player can be locked into the whole 3-hit combo without being able to roll out, making it deal devastating damage.
  - The Nagakiba and its great reach is a very strong combination with this skill.
- Stance damage multipliers varies by weapon size. Smaller weapons deal 290% Stance damage on the first and last hits while the second only deals 90% Stance damage (670% total), while large weapons hit for 230% on the first and last hit and 75% on the second hit (535% total).
  - Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree deal 13.4 Stance damage.
  - Daggers deal 20.1 Stance damage.
  - Spears, Halberds, and Reapers deal 26.75 Stance damage.
  - Straight Swords, Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Curved Swords, Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Katanas, Twinblades, and Axes deal 33.5 Stance damage.
  - Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Greataxes, and Great Spears deal 29.425 Stance damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.12 PvP-only adjustment: Decreased damage.
  - The damage multiplier against other players was lowered from 80% to 70%, an effective 12.5% decrease in damage against other players.
- Patch 1.12 Decreased the status buildup of your weapon when using this skill. Fixed a bug with Spinning Slash Skill that generated poise when used with Twinblades.
  - The Status Effect multiplier was decreased from 100% on each hit (300% build-up in total) to 65% on the first hit, 50% on the second hit, and 70% on the final slam (185% build-up in total).
- Patch 1.07 Increased poise damage against enemies when used with the following weapons: Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Twinblades, Greataxes, Spears, Great Spears, Halberds, and Reapers.
  - The Stance damage of the first and last hits was increased from 125% to 230%.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Call down a blue lightning bolt on the halberd, granting it a Weapon Buff that gives 160 Lightning Attack Power and 80 Frostbite build-up, then spin once, hitting for 105% of Attack Power.

Using the skill again afterwards makes the user spin again before slamming down with the weapon, hitting for 60% and 110% of Attack Power respectively, and sending down a bolt from above with 149 Lightning Attack Power where the head of the weapon hits.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The first spin costs 21 points of Stamina to perform, while the follow-up takes 36 points of Stamina to do (10 points from the small spin and 26 points from the final slam).
- The Attack Power of the Lightning bolt scales with upgrade level, increasing to 596 at +10.
- If the lightning bolt hits water or a water surface a small area attack with 69 Lightning Attack Power is sent out.
  - This shockwave-in-water scales with upgrade level, increasing to 276 Attack Power at +10.
- The skill can deal up to 26.75 Stance damage with the spins (11.5 for the first spin and final slam each, and 3.75 for the in-between spin) and another 10 Stance damage with the bolt for 36.75 Stance damage in total.
- This skill makes the Dragon Halberd extremely dangerous at low levels since the buff is always at full power and will provide a large amount of extra damage early on.
  - For comparison, a +0 Dragon Halberd at the minimum amount of stat required to wield it has 161 Attack Power while the buff grants another 160 Lightning Attack Power and more or less doubles it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The Attack Power of the Weapon Buff was increased from 130 to 160 at some point. The Frostbite build-up was also increased from 70 to 80 and the duration from 30 seconds to 45 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Stamp (Upward Cut)** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and hammers (except for swords smaller than Greatswords) with the Ash of War: Stamp (Upward Cut).
- Innate skill of many Greatswords: the Banished Knight's Greatsword, Bastard Sword, Fire Knight's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Flamberge, Forked Greatsword, Greatsword, Iron Greatsword, Knight's Greatsword, Lizard Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Lordsworn's Greatsword, Watchdog's Greatsword, and Zweihander.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Crouches down, ignoring the stagger from the next enemy attack to hit.

Using a heavy attack afterwards causes a slow uppercutting blow, launching human-sized foes, dealing heavy Stance damage, and inflicting damage equal to 215% of the weapon's Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The stomp costs no Stamina (though still requires at least 1 point of Stamina to use) and the heavy follow-up attack costs 50 points of Stamina.
- During the stamp incoming damage is reduced by half.
  - This effectively sets your damage negation to (Current damage negation) + (100 - Current damage negation)/2 or 50 + (Current damage negation)/2.
  - This disappears the same moment the Stagger resistance does, i.e. when the animation for the heavy attack follow-up begins.
- The heavy attack follow-up deals 600% Stance damage.
  - Axes deal 30 Stance damage.
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Greataxes deal 33 Stance damage.
  - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 36 Stance damage.
  - Hammers deal 39 Stance damage.
  - Great Hammers deal 42 Stance damage.
  - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deals 45 Stance damage.
- The Stance damage of the heavy attack follow-up is on par with a charged heavy attack for that weapon type.
- Using a light attack instead of a heavy attack immediately after the crouch will use the second attack of the light attack chain instead of the first one.
  - This attack doesn't cost any FP, unlike the heavy follow-up.
  - This attack is primarily useful for its speed, as it comes out quicker than the heavy attack. While this isn't very useful versus regular enemies, against other players it can be very useful for a mix-up, especially if only the uppercut has been used before.
- While the primary usage would seem to be using the uppercut to launch lesser foe and therefore control their movement, the fact that the initial crouch both resists the stagger of attacks and potentially can duck under high-centered attacks means it can sometimes more easily deliver Stance damage than a charged heavy attack.
  - Especially useful for trading hits with other players, and with special enemies that use the same moveset/skeleton as a player.
- Due to its vertical reach it's capable of catching jumping opponents when they are in mid-air, ignoring the partial invincibility of jumping attacks due to the range.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill, increased attack power, reduced the timing between the end of the skill and performing actions other than the strong attack.
  - Also applies to the Stamp (Sweep) skill.
  - Damage was increased from 200% of Attack Power to 215% of Attack Power.
- Patch 1.08 increased poise value during the active part of the Stamp (Upward Cut) Weapon Art.
  - Also applies to the Stamp (Sweep) skill.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Skill: Stamp (Sweep), the other Stamp skill, with an identical initial skill but different follow-up
- Skill: Endure, essentially first part of the skill but with an effect that lasts several seconds

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Stamp (Sweep)** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and hammers (except for swords smaller than Greatswords) with the Ash of War: Stamp (Sweep).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Crouches down, ignoring the stagger from the next enemy attack to hit.

Using a heavy attack afterwards causes a crouching spin that hits twice, dealing damage equal to 92% of weapon Attack Power on the first hit and damage equal to 112% of Attack Power on the second hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The stomp costs no Stamina (though still requires at least 1 point of Stamina to use) and the heavy follow-up attack costs 50 points of Stamina (15 Stamina for the first hit and 35 Stamina for the second one).
- During the stamp incoming damage is reduced by half.
  - This effectively sets your damage negation to (Current damage negation) + (100 - Current damage negation)/2 or 50 + (Current damage negation)/2.
  - This disappears the same moment the Stagger resistance does, i.e. when the animation for the heavy attack follow-up begins.
- The heavy attack follow-up deals 150% Stance damage on the first hit and 250% Stance damage on the second hit (400% Stance damage in total).
  - Axes deal 7.5 and 12.5 Stance damage (20 in total).
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Greataxes deal 8.25 and 13.75 Stance damage (22 in total).
  - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 9 and 15 Stance damage (24 in total).
  - Hammers deal 9.75 and 16.25 Stance damage (26 in total).
  - Great Hammers deal 10.5 and 17.5 Stance damage (28 in total).
  - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deal 11.25 and 18.75 Stance damage (30 in total).
- Of the two hits of the spin attack, the first will briefly stagger human-sized enemies while the second while fling them back.
  - Since this attack is a spin it can have a fair bit of horizontal reach, especially if used with a Colossal Sword, letting it hit several foes.
  - The second hit deals decent Stance damage, on par with a jumping heavy attack from that weapon type.
  - The first spin is slightly weaker than the second one, about 45% of the total damage, while the second spin deals the remaining 55% of the total damage.
- Using a light attack instead of a heavy attack immediately after the crouch will use the second attack of the light attack chain instead of the first one.
  - This attack doesn't cost any FP, unlike the heavy follow-up.
  - This attack is primarily useful for its speed, as it comes out quicker than the heavy attack. While this isn't very useful versus regular enemies, against other players it can be very useful for a mix-up, especially if only the uppercut has been used before.
- Do note that the spin can fairly easily be jumped over.
- Since the two-hits of the follow-up chain into each other, it's very useful for delivering the Status Effects build-up from a Blood affinity or Cold affinity weapon, especially the massive build-up on a Colossal Sword or Colossal Weapon.
- As the follow-up is considered to be a heavy attack, each hit counts as two points for the damage increase from the Winged Sword Insignias. This means that if both attacks hit the bonus will immediately increase one tier.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill, increased attack power, reduced the timing between the end of the skill and performing actions other than the strong attack.
  - Also applies to the Stamp (Upward Cut) skill.
- Damage was increased from 200% of Attack Power to 215% of Attack Power.
- Patch 1.08 increased poise value during the active part of the Stamp (Sweep) Weapon Art.
  - Also applies to the Stamp (Upward Cut) skill.

sections.heading: See also

- Skill: Endure, essentially first part of the skill but with an effect that lasts several seconds

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Wild Strikes** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable axes, hammers, curved swords, and greatswords (except for Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons) with the Ash of War: Wild Strikes.
- Innate skill of the Battle Axe, Celebrant's Cleaver, Iron Cleaver, Jawbone Axe, Ripple Blade, Sacrificial Axe, and Smithscript AxeShadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Holding the skill button will make the user swing the weapon at steady pace, alternating between 126% and 119% of weapon Attack Power for the hits (107% and 114% of Attack Power for "Great" weapon types).

Using a light attack when in this stance causes a light slash leading into wide blow to the front, with 52% and 183% of weapon Attack Power (44% and 154% of Attack Power for "Great" weapon types) respectively, while using a heavy attack when in the stance results in backhand slash and an overhead slam that has 52% and 253% weapon Attack Power (44% and 203% of Attack Power for "Great" weapon types) respectively.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 6 points of Stamina (9 for the "Great" weapon types) per swing when held and then 20 points of Stamina for the light attack follow-up and 30 points of Stamina for the heavy attack follow-up (respectively 30 and 40 for the "Great" weapon types).
- The regular FP cost of 2 happens for every swing in the basic "stance".
- The speed of the held version is roughly the same across all weapon types, even for Great Hammers.
  - Though the version of the skill used by "Great" weapons (Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Greataxes, and Great Hammers) has a lower damage multiplier, the higher Attack Power of those weapons means they still generally deal more damage.
- Due to the very stead attack speed it's fairly easy to parry.
- Deals surprisingly heavy Stance damage with the follow-up attacks, with the light attack version dealing between 20 and 26 Stance damage depending on weapon type (equivalent to a jumping heavy attack), and the heavy attack version dealing between 30 and 40 Stance damage depending on weapon type (equivalent to a charged heavy attack).
- Simply using the held version of the skill deals surprising amount of damage, as it both attacks much quicker than normal and consumes low amounts of Stamina per attack. User Poise will also constantly reset, making the user fairly difficult to stagger out of the skill.
  - Very useful against enemies with long staggers upon being Stance broken, such as Dragons, with the repeated strikes often dealing more damage than a Critical Attack. The follow-ups serve as strong endings to such combos, provided they can be timed correctly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 shortened the time between various actions and the activation of skills, slightly increased attack power.
  - The swings when the skill button is held had their damage multiplier increased from 120% and 114% (98% and 114% for "Great" weapon types) to 126% and 119% (107% and 114% for "Great" weapon types), damage for the light attack follow-up was increased from 50% and 175% (40% and 140% for "Great" weapon types) to 52% and 183% (44% and 154% for "Great" weapon types), and damage for the heavy attack follow-up was increased from 50% and 230% (40% and 185% for "Great" weapon types) to 52% and 253% (44% and 203% for "Great" weapon types)

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Skill: Spinning Strikes, essentially Wild Strikes but for polearms
- Skill: Spinning Chain, a very similar skill exclusive to Flails but lacking an Ash of War

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Lion's Claw** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and hammers (except for Daggers and any thrusting sword) with the Ash of War: Lion's Claw.
- Innate skill of the Claymore.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Quickly ducks down before leaping forwards with a vertical stuff ending in a slam with the weapon, dealing damage equal to 240% of weapon Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 45 points of Stamina to use.
- Damage is boosted by 10% when Freyja's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree is held in either active hand.
  - Note that Lion's Claw doesn't necessarily need to be equipped on that weapon to gain the damage bonus.
- Deals 600% Stance damage.
  - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, and Axes deal 30 Stance damage.
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Greataxes deal 33 Stance damage.
  - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 36 Stance damage.
  - Hammers deal 39 Stance damage.
  - Great Hammers deal 42 Stance damage.
  - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deals 45 Stance damage.
- Grants heavy hyperarmor when mid-air, effectively making the skill almost impossible to interrupt when leaping.
- Deals heavy Stance damage, on par with a charged heavy attack for that weapon type.
  - Just 2-4 uses is enough to break the Stance of most bosses.
- An excellent skill due to having a quick start-up time and good reach in combination with solid damage and Stance damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.04 increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: See also

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Cragblade** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type (except for Whips) with the Ash of War: Cragblade.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
User slams their weapon into the ground, dealing damage equal to 100% of weapon Attack Power, before pulling it out to deal damage equal to 80% of weapon Attack Power and granting a Weapon Buff.

The buff lasts for 60 seconds and increases Physical damage by 15%, damage to Poise and Stance by 10%, and Stamina damage against blocking opponents by 50%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to use, divided up as 20 points of Stamina for the slam and another 20 points for the pull.
- Since this is a Weapon Buff it means that it won't stack with other Weapon Buffs such as Fire Grease.
- The slam and the subsequent pull both count as attacks, if very short-ranged ones, and can be parried.
  - The slam deals damage equal to 100% of weapon Attack Power and the pull deals damage equal to 80% of weapon Attack Power.
- An easy-to-use and widely applicable skill for Physical-damage dependent attackers, since it's relatively easy to set-and-forget and only occasionally has to be re-used to re-apply the buff. It also just generally boosts combat performance, without the user having to think much about using it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 extended effect duration, increased attack power, poise damage and stamina attack power against guarding enemies.
  - Duration was increased from 30 seconds to 60 seconds, and attack power bonus was increased from 10% to 15%, Poise/Stance damage bonus was increased from 10% to 20%, and Stamina damage against blocking opponents was increased from 20% to 50%.
- Patch 1.08 reduced the poise damage of the Cragblade Weapon Art.
  - Poise/Stance damage bonus was reduced back down from 20% to 10%.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Kick** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type with the Ash of War: Kick
- Innate skill of the Arbalest, Crepus's Black-Key Crossbow, Full Moon Crossbow, Hammer, Hand Ballista, Heavy Crossbow, Hoslow's Petal Whip, Jar Cannon, Light Crossbow, Mace, Monk's Flamemace, Morning Star, Pulley Crossbow, Rabbath's CannonShadow of the Erdtree, Short Sword, Soldier's Crossbow, Spread CrossbowShadow of the Erdtree, Stone Club, Thorned Whip, Urumi, Warpick, and Whip.
- This is also the innate skill of The Tarnished's own empty fists.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Kicks with one foot, causing an attack with a low 30 base Strike Attack Power, staggering foes, and breaking their guard by dealing 999 damage to the Stamina of guarding opponents.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 16 points of Stamina to use.
- Does NOT appear to be boosted by the Shattered Stone Talisman.
- Actually a "bullet"-type Skill, meaning its (admittedly pretty poor) damage scales entirely from weapon upgrade level and Strength.
  - It's not really worth trying to make this skill deal damage, as even when used on a weapon with a Heavy affinity for increased scaling and 80 Strength will have at most 180 Attack Power or so, and this is before enemy flat defences are applied and reduce the damage even further.
- Can break the guard of pretty much any blocking enemy, even Crucible Knights.
  - Somewhat more limited effectiveness against player Greatshields as the short reach makes it harder to use.
- Deals light Stance damage, 6, about as much as a Hammers light attack.
- This skill's effect can mostly be replicated by either simply attacking with the Hammer Talisman equipped, which is simpler than equipping this skill on a weapon or leaving the right-hand and left-hand skill slots empty and can have a fair bit more range, but takes up a Talisman slot and isn't a guaranteed guard break.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 increased poise damage and stamina attack power against guarding enemies.
  - The damage to the Stamina of guarding opponents was increased from 350 to 999.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Hammer Talisman, a Talisman that also helps with breaking blocking enemies' guards

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Endure** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type with the Ash of War: Endure.
- Innate skill of the Blacksteel GreathammerShadow of the Erdtree, Bloodfiend's ArmShadow of the Erdtree, Caestus, Dragon Greatclaw, Duelist Greataxe, Giant-Crusher, Golem FistShadow of the Erdtree, Great Mace, Great Stars, Iron Ball (though it has Ash of War: Braggart's Roar equipped, overriding the skill), Pickaxe, Rotten Greataxe, Smithscript GreathammerShadow of the Erdtree, Spiked Caestus, and Star Fist,

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Briefly raises the weapon and hold still. For 3 seconds Poise is greatly increased, Damage Negation is increased by a flat 45%, and user has Tier 1 Deflection against weapons.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Since the boost to Poise that this Skill grants lasts an additional 2 seconds after the animation has ended, the player can tank damage to use healing flasks or trade hits without the risk of getting stunned.
  - Putting this on a light weapon such as a Dagger or Caestus gives a player a convenient tool for more easily using items and skills in tight situations.
  - This Poise boost doesn't prevent stagger from headshots and attacks that launch you into the air.
- Tier 1 Deflection means that certain one-handed attacks (mostly regular light attacks) from Daggers, Thrusting Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Spears, Reapers, Claws, and Torches causes the attacker hitstun.
  - This is most likely also true for Throwing BladesShadow of the Erdtree, Backhand BladesShadow of the Erdtree, and Beast ClawsShadow of the Erdtree weapon types, but this needs checking.
- Larger weapons (Greatswords, Colossal Swords, Greataxes, Great Hammers, and Colossal Weapons) have a slower version of the initial stance, taking roughly 1.5-2 seconds, making this skill harder to use for them.
  - This is most likely also shared with the Great KatanasShadow of the Erdtree weapon type, but this needs checking.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 extended effect duration, added an effect that prevents staggers caused by blood loss and frostbite status effects, reduced the time between skill activation and being able to perform actions other than attacking.
  - Duration increased from 3 seconds to 5 seconds.
- Patch 1.07.1 shortened effect duration. Adjustments made in patch 1.07 had a greater impact on the game balance than expected.
  - Duration was lowered back down again, from 5 seconds to 3 seconds.

sections.heading: See also
