sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Ground Slam** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type with the Ash of War: Ground Slam.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Slightly crouches down before jumping up into the air and then lands to with base 264 Strike Attack Power on a direct hit and cause shockwave for another 175 base Standard Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to perform.
- As a bullet-type skill the Attack Power scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
  - Strength-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult affinity.
  - Attack Power is always at least 1056 for a direct hit and 700 for the shockwave for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
    - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the direct hit 1291 Attack Power and the shockwave 856 Attack Power, while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively the direct hit either 1316 Attack Power or 1430 Attack Power and the shockwave either 872 Attack Power or 948 Attack Power, and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively the direct hit either 1403 Attack Power or 1555 Attack Power and the shockwave either 930 Attack Power or 1031 Attack Power.
- User gains hyperarmor when in mid-air, making it very difficult to knock them out of the skill.
  - Do note that it doesn't grant any invincibility frames, unlike a jump (which grants those from the waist down), meaning that if an attack isn't completely and physically avoided damage may still be taken more often than normal.
- Deals surprisingly heavy Stance damage, 15 on the landing hit and 30 on the following shockwave. For comparison, a Great Hammer's charged heavy attack deals 40 Stance damage and a hammer-type Colossal Weapon's charged heavy attack deals 42 Stance damage.
- Will flatten human-sized enemies if they are hit directly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the time between using the skill and being able to roll, increased attack power.
  - Base Attack Power for the direct hit was increased from 240 to 264 and base Attack Power for the shockwave was increased from 160 to 175.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Skill: Golden Slam, a Holy variant of this skill
- Unique Skill: Erdtree Slam, a stronger Holy variant of this skill

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Earthshaker** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to infusable axes, hammers, and spears of great-size and larger as well as Colossal Swords with the Ash of War: Earthshaker.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Slam weapon head first into the ground, dealing damage equal to 100% of weapon Attack Power, before causing a shockwave all around the user with 120 base Standard Attack Power.

Using a heavy attack afterwards causes the user spin around to lunge forward while sweeping the weapon in front of them, dealing damage equal to 140% of weapon Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The initial slam costs 25 points of Stamina to perform, the shockwave costs another 8 points of Stamina, and the follow-up attack costs 35 points of Stamina to do.
- Since the initial slam down into the ground is an attack it's capable of interrupting very close foes.
- The initial slam and the follow-up attack scales with the used weapon's Attack Power, while the shockwave is a bullet-type and as such scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
  - Strength-scaling for the shockwave is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult affinity.
  - Attack Power of the shockwave is always at least 480 for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
    - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the shockwave 587 Attack Power, while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 598 Attack Power or 650 Attack Power, and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 638 Attack Power or 707 Attack Power.
  - This skill is still fairly usable on those affinities, as while the shockwave will see a roughly 25% penalty to Attack Power on a low-Strength build with a weakening affinity compared to a high-Strength build with a Heavy affinity the direct weapon hits still work well.
- The follow-up can launch human-sized foes backwards.
- The follow-up can actually be delayed a fair bit, useful against other players when waiting out their rolls or simply using it after they would've expected you to be unable to use it.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Skill: Waves of Darkness, essentially a Magic-based variant of this skill with expanding shockwaves
- Skill: Golden Land, essentially a Holy-based variant of this skill with added projectiles

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to infusible melee weapons of any type with Ash of War: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker.

sections.heading: Effect

Let loose a staggering, 0 damage roar before slamming down to send out a shockwave with 220 Standard Attack Power.

Using the skill again causes another slam to send out a shockwave with 250 Standard Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes

- Costs 25 points of Stamina per slam (50 total if both are used).
- Deals 15 Stance damage with the first part of the roar and 1 Stance damage for the second and third parts of the roar, while each slam deals 20 Stance, for a total Stance damage of 57 if the entire skills is used and hits.
- The roar is actually 3 separate 0 damage hits.
  - Each hit of the roar still causes damage to the Stamina of guarding enemies, and also counts as a hit for the purpose of gaining the Attack Power buff from the Winged Sword Insignias. If all 3 hits land on a single target this means that 1 tier of said attack boost is gained and will be applied to the slam-shockwaves. If the roars hit more than 1 target the boost can potentially be even stronger.
- Since the shockwaves are ground-bound they can be jumped over.

  - Attack Power of the roar is always at least 880 for the first shockwave and 1000 for the second shockwave for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
    - A Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the shockwaves 1076 and 1223 Attack Power respectively, while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives 1097 respectively 1192 Attack Power for the first shockwave and 1246 respectively 1354 Attack Power on the second shockwave, and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives 1169 respectively 1296 Attack Power for the first shockwave and 1328 respectively 1473 Attack Power for the second shockwave.
- Deals 20% less damage against players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.05 fixed a bug in which a status effect was applied when using the "Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker" skill.
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed. Increased cast speed on follow up input, decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: Summary

sections.heading: Effect

Roar to gain a Weapon Buff that increases the weapon's Physical Attack Power by 7.5% and adds 0.05 to its Strength-scaling for 40 seconds.

If a charged heavy attack instead is performed, it's preceded by a charge that hits with 0 Attack Power twice to stagger and then the attack has is an overhead slam with 175% Attack Power (185% if two-handed), and a second charged heavy attack is preceded by a charge that hits with 0 Attack Power once and the attack is another overhead slam with 178% Attack Power (188% if two-handed). For Fists-sized weapons their two-handed charged heavy attacks become two slams with 125% Attack Power each for the first charged heavy attack and 130% Attack Power for the second one.

  - For Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 40 points of Stamina on the first attack and 45 points on the second attack (48 points on first and 54 points on second if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 55 points of Stamina (66 points if two-handed).
- The changed heavy attack is different between slashing weapons, spears, and fist-sized weapons. When the heavy attack is charged the attack will be preceded by a short, staggering charge.
  - For Straight Swords, Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Colossal Swords, Curved Swords, Curved Greatswords, Katanas, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Axes, Greataxes, Hammers, Flails, Great Hammers, Colossal Weapons, and Reapers the first attack is an overhead slam while the second attack is an upwards cut. Speed varies slightly by the size of the weapon type.
  - For Twinblades the first attack is a jumping forwards stab while the second attack is an upwards cut.
  - For Spears, Great Spears, and Halberds the first attack is a jumping forwards stab while the second attack is another thrust.
  - For Fists, Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree the first attack is an overhead slam while the second attack is a spinning uppercut.
- For all one-handed weapons the Stance damage multipliers are the same, with the regular heavy attack dealing 200% Stance damage and the charged heavy attack dealing 600% Stance damage. Two-handed fist-sized weapons, however, deal 120% Stance damage per hit (240% in total) with regular heavy attacks, while charged heavy attacks deal 360% Stance damage per hit (720% in total) with the first attack and 480% Stance damage (960% in total) with the second attack.
  - For all weapons that aren't fist-sized, two-handing the weapon increases the Stance damage by 20% for the regular heavy attacks by 20% and by 10% for the charged heavy attacks.
    - Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree deal 8 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (9.6 Stance damage in total if two-handed) and 24 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (28.8 Stance dam

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 Extended effect duration. Reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill. The power of strong attacks during the duration of the effect has been increased when using the following weapons: Straight Sword / Curved Sword / Katana / Axe / Hammer / Flail / Spear / Great Spear / Halberd / Reaper / Fist (one-handed) / Claw (one-handed).
  - The duration of the Weapon Buff was extended from 20 seconds to 40 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Barbaric Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to any infusable weapon through Ash of War: Barbaric Roar.
- Default skill on the Butchering Knife, Club, Curved Club, Curved Great Club, Rusted Anchor, and Spiked Club weapons.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Grants a Weapon Buff for 40 seconds upon use, increasing damage by roughly 10%.

As long as this buff remains active the regular heavy and charged heavy attacks are changed to a 3-hit combo, which can then be followed by either a single hit or a 2-hit combo depending on the weapon type.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Although this Skill functions similarly to War Cry, the new heavy attack animations are different.
- Though it is a Weapon Buff, its visual effect is more akin to a Body Buff, being red rising lines around the user's body.
- New attacks resemble the original moveset of the weapon used, meaning most weapons will perform heavy slashing or smashing attacks.
  - The exception to this is the various polearms (Spears, Halberds, and Great Spears) as well as the Twinblades final follow-up attack, which instead are thrusts.
- The Roar Medallion and the Highland Axe can be worn to further increase the damage of the two follow-up attack combos.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Braggart's Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Troll's Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can granted to infusable large and colossal swords, axes, and hammers with the Ash of War: Troll's Roar.
- Default skill on the Troll's Golden Sword, Troll's Hammer and Troll Knight's Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Slowly step forward and let loose a roar with 195 base Strike Attack Power (155 base Standard Attack Power for targets further out) to hit enemies around you.

Use a heavy attack to follow-up with a slow, overhead slam with Attack Power equal to 180% of the weapon's own.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The roar costs 30 points of Stamina while the follow-up heavy attack costs 40 points of Stamina.
- The Attack Power of both the roar and the follow-up heavy attack is boosted by 15% if the Roar Medallion is worn.
- The Attack Power of both the roar and the follow-up heavy attack is boosted by 10% if a Highland Axe is held in one of a character's active hand slots (this boost remains active even if the weapon with Troll's Roar is two-handed).
- The roar is a bullet-type skill so its Attack Power scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
  - Strength-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy Affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire Affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood Affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult Affinity.
    - Since the Troll's Hammer counts as a Standard affinity weapon despite its ample Strength-scaling and being unable to change the skill, making its roar deal substantially less damage than a Heavy affinity weapon at equivalent levels of Strength (15% less Attack Power at 80 Strength) while the Troll Knight's Sword has somewhat improved Strength-scaling due to being a Somber weapon with decent Strength-scaling at +0.
  - Attack Power of the roar is always at least 780 (620 for more distant targets) for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
    - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the roar 954 Attack Power (758 against distant targets), while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 972 Attack Power (773 against distant targets) or 1056 Attack Power (840 against distant targets), and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 1036 Attack Power (823 against distant targets) or 1149 Attack Power (913 against distant targets).
    - The Troll's Hammer's roar has 917 Attack Power (729 against distant targets) at 45 Strength and 977 Attack Power (777 against distant targets), while the Troll Knight's Sword's roar has 1076 Attack Power (855 against distant targets) at 45 Strength and 1206 Attack Power (959 against distant targets).
- The roar deals 40 Stance damage (only 9 Stance damage against more distant targets) and the follow-up deals either 33 Stance damage (Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Curved Greatswords, and Greataxes), 36 Stance damage (Colossal Swords and non-hammer Colossal Weapons), 42 Stance damage (Great Hammers), or 45 Stance damage (hammer Colossal Weapons).
- Only the roar costs FP to perform, with the follow-up heavy attack having no FP cost.
- The roar throws back enemies that are hit.
- The follow-up heavy attack has an unusually high modifier of 180% for Status Effects, whereas most Skills and weapon attacks has a modifier of 100% or lower.
- Hits quite hard but is very slow and as such hard to hit with, the follow-up even more so since it has a smaller hitbox.
  - Especially hard to use against other players since it's so slow, though that slowness can also bait them to roll early and get caught by either the roar or follow-up attack.
  - The roar has a tendency to throw smaller enemies out of reach for the follow-up, so it can be better to reserve said follow-up for when an enemy is knocked back into a closeby wall or obstacle, or for when an enemy's Stance is broken.
  - Consider using a light attack as a follow-up instead, as it will come out quicker and can be surprising if used only occasionally against other players.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 increased attack power, fixed the timing of the poise increase during activation.
  - This increased the Attack Power of the roar from 170 to 195, and from 135 to 155 for targets that are further away.
- Patch 1.05 fixed a bug where recovery time for some actions of the "Barbaric Roar", "War Cry", and "Troll's Roar" was longer than expected.
- Patch 1.04 decreased Stamina Cost, increased cast speed on follow up input and increased distance traveled.
  - Stamina cost was decreased from 50 to 30 for the roar, and from 60 to 40 for the follow-up attack.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Impaling Thrust** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable weapons capable of making thrusting attacks (except for Colossal Swords) with the Ash of War: Impaling Thrust.
  - Note that while two Fists has Impaling Thrust as their innate skill, they cannot equip the Ash of War and as such can only use the skill with a Standard affinity.
- Innate skill of many Thrusting Swords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Spears, and Fists.
  - Thrusting Swords: Antspur Rapier, Carian Sorcery Sword Shadow of the Erdtree, Cleanrot Knight's Sword, Estoc, Frozen Needle, Noble's Estoc, and Rapier.
  - Heavy Thrusting Swords: Godskin Stitcher, Great Épée, Queelign's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, and Sword Lance Shadow of the Erdtree.
  - Spears Clayman's Harpoon, Cross-Naginata, Crystal Spear, Partisan, Short Spear, Smithscript Spear Shadow of the Erdtree, Spear, Spiked Spear, and Swift Spear Shadow of the Erdtree.
  - Fists (not compatible with the Ash of War): Katar and Pata Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Lunge forward with a attack that always deals Pierce damage, hits for 187% Attack Power, and ignores 85% of Guarded Damage Negation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 40 point of Stamina to use.
  - The version found on the Carian Sorcery Sword Shadow of the Erdtree costs slightly less to perform, at 39 points of Stamina.
- The block-piercing effect effectively scales with how high the Guard Damage Negation of an opponent's blocking implement is. For a 100% Guard Damage Negation rate only 1-1*0.85=0.15=15% damage will be blocked while a 50% Guarded Damage Negation rate will let 0.5-0.5*0.85=0.075=7.5% damage will be blocked.
  - Effectively, if x is the blocking implement's Guarded Damage Negation then the formular x*(1-0.85)=0.15*x can be applied to know how much damage will be blocked when using Impaling Thrust (or 1-0.15*x for how large a fraction of the damage of Impaling Thrust will go through).
- The effective damage against a Guarding opponent can become slightly lower than 85% of the damage against a non-Guarding opponent if the decrease lowers the effective Attack Power compared to the opponent's defense.
- The Stance damage multiplier per hit is 600%, the same as with Lion's Claw. This is the same amount of Stance damage as a one-handed charged heavy attack for that weapon type (except for Throwing Blades, where the Stance damage is doubled compared to a one-handed charged heavy attack).
  - Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree deal 12 Stance damage.
  - Daggers and Claws deal 18 Stance damage.
  - Thrusting Swords deal 24 Stance damage.
  - Straight Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Spears, Halberds, and Fists deal 30 Stance damage.
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Great Spears deal 33 Stance damage.
- Compared with Piercing Fang: lower FP cost (9 vs 16), lower Attack Power modifier (187% vs 212%), lower Guard-piercing (85% vs 100%), shorter lunge distance, quicker cast, and same Stance damage multiplier (600%).
- Due to the fairly long delay this skill is fairly easy to recognize and parry for other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 increased motion speed and attack power, reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill, and reduced the timing between the end of the skill and being able to attack and to roll.
  - Increased the Attack Power from 170% to 187%.
  - The other changed increased the speed of the lunge, how early the skill can be used, and the aftercast duration of the skill where nothing else can be done.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Skill: Piercing Fang, a similar, slower skill with more damage and guard-piercing
- Skill: Giant Hunt, a thrusting skill that exchanges guard-piercing for launching foes into the air

sections.heading: Summary

sections.heading: Effect

  - Straight Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Spears, and Halberds deal 30 Stance damage.
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Great Spears deal 33 Stance damage.
- Compared with Impaling Thrust: higher FP cost (16 vs 9), higher Attack Power modifier (212% vs 187%), higher Guard-piercing (100% vs 85%), longer lunge distance, slower cast, and same Stance damage multiplier (600%).
- Due to the very long delay this skill is fairly easy to recognize and parry for other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07 increased motion speed, attack power and poise damage., reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill, and reduced the timing between the end of the skill and being able to attack and to roll.
  - Increased the Attack Power from 185% to 212% and the Stance damage multiplier from 200% to 600%.
  - The other changed increased the speed of the lunge, how early the skill can be used, and the aftercast duration of the skill where nothing else can be done.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Repeating Thrust** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be any infusable weapon capable of thrusting (except for Colossal Swords) with the Ash of War: Repeating Thrust.
- Innate skill of the Rogier's Rapier and Scorpion's Stinger.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Rotates around and stab forward with 99% Attack Power, then thrust twice more for 57% Attack Power on each hit, and finally inflict a piercing blow with 115% Attack Power.

Using a Dagger lowers the Attack Power of the first and final blows to 80% of Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 7 points of Stamina for each of the first three thrusts and 12 points for the final one (33 points in total).
  - The Daggers variant decreases the Stamina cost to 5 points for the first three and 10 points for the final one (25 points in total).
- Always deals Pierce damage.
- Compared to Skill: Blood Tax this skill costs less FP (7 vs 16), deals has more Attack Power in total (328% vs 286%), costs less Stamina (33 points vs 45 points), and has the same total amount of Status Effect build-up (200%), in exchange for Blood Tax also restoring HP on hit (10% of maximum HP + 120 in total).
- Works quite well with long weapons such as Halberds since it gives a good amount of reach and lets the user stagger human-sized foes, while also breaking Stance fairly well.
- Easily parried since all 4 separate hits can be parried.
- Deals 200% Stance damage with the first thrust, then 40% Stance damage on the two middle thrusts and 100% Stance damage on the final stab (80% Stance damage with the final stab for Daggers) for 380% Stance damage in total (360% in total for Daggers).
  - Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree deal 7.6 Stance damage in total.
  - Daggers deal 10.8 Stance damage in total.
  - Thrusting Swords deal 15.2 Stance damage in total.
  - Straight Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Spears, and Halberds deal 19 Stance damage in total.
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Great Spears deal 20.9 Stance damage in total.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.07: Increased motion speed. Reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Double Slash** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to any infusable sword or polearm capable of making slashing attacks (except for Colossal Swords) with Ash of War: Double Slash.
- Innate skill of the Serpentbone Blade.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Make two horisontal slashes with 92% and 105% Attack Power.

Using the skill again makes the user spin around before making another three horisontal slashes, hitting with 84%, 86%, and 115% Attack Power respectively.

Using the skill a third time leads to final, strong overhead slash with 145% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 6 FP on the first input and then 3 FP each for the other two inputs (12 FP in total).
- Each slash from the first two inputs cost 14 points of Stamina each while the final attack costs 20 points of Stamina (90 points in total for the whole skill).
  - For larger weapons the first five slash take 16 points each while the final one needs 24 points (104 points of Stamina in total for the whole skill).
  - While it's very Stamina-hungry overall, only 1 point of Stamina is needed to start each sequence. This means only 29 points of Stamina is needed to use the second input (33 points for larger weapons) and 71 points for the final input (81 points for larger weapons). Be wary that this will leave you without any Stamina for a few seconds.
- Larger weapons (Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas, Twinblades, Halberds, and Reapers) have a slower variant of this skill, with more of a delay between each input's attack sequence.
- Deals 75% Stance damage on the first, third, and fourth slash, 100% Stance damage on the second and fifth slash, and 200% Stance damage on the final, sixth attack (625% Stance damage in total).
  - Throwing Blades  deal 12.5 Stance damage in total.
  - Daggers deal 18.75 Stance damage in total.
  - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Katanas, and Twinblades deal 31.25 Stance damage in total.
  - Light Greatswords , Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas , Halberds, and Reapers deal 34.375 Stance damage in total.
- Deals 525% of the weapon's innate Status Effect build-up over the course of the entire skill (175% on the first input, 250% on the second input, and 100% on the third input).
- Very parriable, as each of the six separate hits are parriable.
- Very flexible in its usage. The first input is quite quick and easy to use, the second input is strong but very long, and the third input is by far the strongest per hit but requires using the other two parts beforehand.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The first part of this skill is used by sword-wielding Radahn Soldiers.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Sword Dance** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Can be granted to Swords, Axes, and Polearms capable of making slashing attacks (except for Colossal Swords) with the Ash of War: Sword Dance.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Lunge forward while making two spinning upward slashes, hitting with 120% Attack Power on each swing (130% on each swing for Larger non-Polearm Weapons).

Use the skill again to rear back with the weapon and then slam it down, hitting with 150% Attack Power (155% for Polearms)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 15 points of Stamina each for the first input's two slashes and 20 points for the second input's overhead slash (50 points in total).
  - For larger weapons the first input's first slash costs 20 points of Stamina and the final, overhead slash costs 25 points (60 points in total for larger weapons).
- Larger weapons (Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas, Halberds, and Reapers) have a slower variant of this skill, with more of a delay before and between each input's attack sequence. Twinblades also use the slower variant of the skill, despite having the same damage multipliers as smaller weapons.
- Polearms (Spears, Halberds, and Reapers) have slightly higher Attack Power for the follow-up slam.
- Stance damage multipliers are the same as for Attack Power of the weapon type used (390% for small, non-polearm weapons, 410% for large, non-polearm weapons, and 395% for polearms).
  - Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree deal 4.8 and 3 Stance damage per input respectively (7.8 Stance damage in total).
  - Daggers deal 7.2 and 4.5 Stance damage per input respectively (11.7 Stance damage in total).
  - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Katanas, Twinblades, and Axes deal 12 and 7.5 Stance damage per input respectively (19.5 Stance damage in total).
  - Spears, Halberds, and Reapers deal 12 and 7.75 Stance damage per input respectively (19.75 Stance damage in total).
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, and Great Katanas deal 14.3 and 8.25 Stance damage per input respectively (22.55 Stance damage in total).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.07: Reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Unsheathe** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable Katanas with the Ash of War: Unsheathe.
  - Since all infusable Katanas already have Unsheathe as their innate skill, the purpose of this is purely to change their Affinity.
- Innate skill of the Nagakiba and Uchigatana.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Using and holding the skill places the Katana in its sheath and the user in a stance, while the user's Stamina regeneration rate and movement speed is greatly decreased.

Using a light attack while in this Stance makes the user dash forward slightly and make a horizontal slash with 190% Attack Power.

Using a heavy attack while in this Stance makes the user step forward and perform a heavy overhead slash with 245% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Stance costs no points of Stamina. The light attack follow-up costs 24 points of Stamina while the heavy attack follow-up costs 40 points of Stamina.
  - The Stance costs no points of FP. The light attack follow-up costs 10 points of FP while the heavy attack follow-up costs 15 points of FP.
- The light attack follow-up deals 300% Stance damage while the heavy attack follow-up one deals 600% Stance damage.
  - This means the light attack follow-up deals 15 Stance damage while the heavy attack follow-up deals 30 Stance damage.
- The Rellana's Cameo grants a 45% boost to Attack Power to the follow-up attacks if the Stance is held for at least a second.
- This is an extremely strong skill in PvE, primarily due to how quick and damaging the heavy attack follow-up is and due to it dealing 30 Stance damage, on par with a charged heavy attack, and thus being able to break most enemies' Stance in 3-4 hits.
- The Stance can be cancelled without using a follow-up attack.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Unique Skill: Transient Moonlight, a unique version of this skill with added projectiles

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Quickstep** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon with the Ash of War: Quickstep.
- Innate skill of many Daggers and Claws, and a few Axes.
  - Daggers: Bloodstained Dagger, Celebrant's Sickle, Cinquedea, Crystal Knife, Dagger, Erdsteel Dagger, Fire Knight's Shortsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Great Knife, Ivory Sickle, Miséricorde, and Wakizashi.
  - Claws: Hookclaws, Raptor Talons, and Venomous Fang.
  - Axes: Forked Hatchet and Hand Axe.

sections.heading: Basics
sections.text:
The Player Character dashes quickly in any direction. This dash has invincibility frames (i-frames), the amount of said i-frames depends on the player's Equip Load. The distance and i-frame-count gradually decreases the more Quickstep is used repeatedly in quick succession.

While quickstep is omnidirectional, it mainly uses the four primary directions (left, right, forward, backward) as a base for it's movement and should the player follow up a step with a normal, non-strong attack, what attack-animation is used depends on which of these base-directions are used.
- Forward: triggers the Rolling Attack, with it's fast windup, but short reach.
- Left, Right and Backwards: triggers the Backstep Attack, with it's ability to quickly close distances.

Quickstep can also be used to quickly move through waist-deep waters and swamps.

sections.heading: Advanced
sections.text:
Inexperienced users may be thrown off from quickstep's base-directional nature during especially hectic fights, (particularly when implementing both locked-on and locked-off play) it is possible to take advantage of the different directional dashing animations by intentionally aiming them in unintended directions.

Such as the reverse-quickstep, with it's ability to quickly position the player directly behind the enemy or close even further distances, which can be performed with these inputs:

sections.heading: Advanced
sections.text: If the player can time and space their reverse-quickstep correctly they may even be able to put themselves in the perfect position for a backstab against humanoid opponents. This is one of the fastest, safest and most consistent ways a player can weave in backstabs against an aggressive opponent in PvP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 12 points of Stamina per use.
- If used without meeting the stat requirements of the weapon this skill costs no FP, which is useful for traveling in environments where you can't run.
- Compared to Skill: Bloodhound's Step this skill costs less FP (3 vs 5) in exchange for traveling a shorter distance and not becoming partially invisible during its use.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This is a returning skill from Dark Souls III.
- Patch 1.10: Decreased the invulnerability window of the Quick Step and Hound's Step skills.
  - Both Quickstep and Bloodhound's Step are referred to incorrectly in this update, as "Quick Step" and "Hound's Step" respectively.
- Patch 1.06: Shortened the activation interval when using “Quick Step” skill in succession, increasing its ability to circle around the enemy when locked-on and add the changes below: Reduced performance when used continuously, Increased travel distance when on light equip load.
  - Quickstep is incorrectly referred to as "Quick Step" in this update.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Bloodhound's Step** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon or thrusting shield with the Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step.
- Innate skill of the Bloodhound Claws.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Turn invisible while dashing in the character's current direction (forwards by default), granting 16 i-frames (0.53 seconds) (14 i-frames (0.47 seconds) on follow-up uses).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 12 points of Stamina.
- The dodging functions the same way as a roll, meaning that no damage is taken during the dodge but that build-up from Status Effects is still inflicted.
  - Note that the direct damage from Blood Loss or Frostbite won't be taken if they fully applied during a dash, but the user will still be staggered out of the dash.
  - The damage from Madness and the stun from Madness and Sleep will still be inflicted, as will the Damage Negation decrease from Frostbite and the passive damage from Poison and Scarlet Rot.
- This skill is very similar to the skill Quickstep, however it covers a longer distance and grants more i-frames (16 or 14 vs 15 or 13) at the cost of more FP (5 vs 3).
- Very usable as a movement skill for movement-restricting areas such as as deep water or swamps.
  - Still very usable for this when out of FP, though the amount of i-frames will be heavily decreased so that should preferable only be used outside of combat for this.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.06: Decreased the travel distance and invincibility frames of Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step while adding the changes below: Reduced performance when used continuously. Increased travel distance when on light equip load.
  - The "Reduced performance when used continously" means that the amount of i-frames granted on follow-up uses is decreased from 16 to 14 (effectively a 12.5% decrease in effectiveness for follow-up uses).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Skill: Quickstep, a generally weaker but cheaper variant
- Unique Skill: Bloodhound's Finesse, an offensive skill that incorporates Bloodhound's Steps into it

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Raptor of the Mists** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon or thrusting shield with the Ash of War: Raptor of the Mists.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Crouch down for a second, in readiness for an attack. If an attack would have hit during the crouch, the attack is dodged and the skill's user instead jumps up in a flash of feathers.

Any attack performed during the jump becomes a jumping attack.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- FP is only consumed if a hit was prevented by the crouch and thus triggers a jump. The crouch itself doesn't cost any FP.
- The crouch doesn't cost any points of Stamina, though it will stop any ongoing Stamina regeneration.
  - Any jumping light attack or jumping heavy attack used as a follow-up will consume the same amount of points of Stamina as they usually do.
- Since the user crouches down when the skill is activated, attacks that normally would have hit sometimes sail straight above their head and as such don't trigger the jump.
- The dodge from the crouch functions the same as a regular roll dodge, meaning that no damage is taken but the build-up from any Status Effects still takes effect.
  - As with a roll, the direct damage from Blood Loss and Frostbite is also avoided but the passive effects from Frostbite, Poison, and Scarlet Rot still take effect as do the effects of Sleep and Madness.
- As any attacks performed mid-air count as jumping attacks, their Attack Power is strengthened by the Claw Talisman and either Raptor's Black Feathers or Gravebird's Blackquill Armor.
- The user is briefly left vulnerable to attacks if they weren't hit during the crouch, as it takes a moment to stand up from the crouch during which the jump won't be triggered.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.07: Reduced FP consumption.
  - FP cost when the dodge is activated was reduced from 14 to 6.
- Associated with the Ravenmount Assassins faction.
- Given that the Ravenmount Assassins idolize Deathbirds, the raptor referred to in the name of this skill is most likely also a Deathbird.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Raptor's Black Feathers, an associated piece of Chest Armor

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Beast's Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to any melee weapon or thrusting shield with the Ash of War: Beast's Roar.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Stomp and roar to send out a small air-based projectile with 110 base Strike Attack Power. Upon hitting a enemy or an object, a shockwave with 80 base Strike Attack Power that cannot hit the main target is created.

A 0 base Strike Attack Power is also created by the stomp.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 30 points of Stamina.
- Deals 6 Stance damage if the roar hits. Deals another 6 Stance damage at melee range, for 12 Stance damage in total.
- The Attack Power of the roar is boosted by 15% if the Roar Medallion is worn.
- The Attack Power of the roar is boosted by 10% if a Highland Axe is held in one of a character's active hand slots (this boost remains active even if the weapon with Beast's Roar is two-handed).
  - This boost does not stack with multiple Highland Axes.
- Range is slightly increased by the Arrow's Reach Talisman, though only be a very small amount.
- This is a bullet-type skill so its damage scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Dexterity.
  - Dexterity-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Keen Affinity, slightly increased if it has a Lightning Affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood Affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Heavy, Fire, Magic, or Occult Affinity.
  - Attack Power of the roar is always at least 440 (320 for adjacent targets) for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
    - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood and 45 Dexterity gives the roar 538 Attack Power (391 for adjacent targets), while a Lightning Affinity and either 45 or 80 Dexterity gives respectively 548 Attack Power (399 for adjacent targets) or 596 Attack Power (433 for adjacent targets), and a Keen affinity and either 45 or 80 Dexterity gives respectively 584 Attack Power (425 for adjacent targets) or 648 Attack Power (471 for adjacent targets).
- Very similar animation to the initial roar of skills such as War Cry and Barbaric Roar, lending it some potential for surprise against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This is the only Keen Affinity Skill that does not scale off of the weapon's attack rating, but instead from the Dexterity stat and weapon upgrade level.
- Runebears can also use this skill.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable weapons of certain weapon types with the Ash of War: Glintstone Pebble.
- Default skill of the Lazuli Glintstone Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Launches a short-ranged Magic projectile.

Can use a heavy attack to launch follow-up lunging thrust.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- As a Magic-based skill it benefits from the Spellblade's Set damage boost.
- Gains a 10% damage boost if used with a weapon that has the Magic affinity.
- The projectile part of the skill counts as a bullet-type and as such it scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the wielder's Intelligence.
  - Gains increased Intelligence-scaling depending on how strong the weapon's own Intelligence-scaling is, whether that be innate, or from the Magic or Cold affinities.
- The follow-up stab depends only on the weapon's own damage for its damage.
- The range of the projectile is quite short, often only barely outranging the follow-up thrust.
- The pebble deals minimal Stance damage, but the stab deals twice as much as a regular heavy attack, which ends up being roughly 20 Stance damage for most compatible weapons (exceptions are Daggers at a mere 12 Stance damage, and Thrusting Swords at 16 Stance damage).

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable weapons of certain weapon types with the Ash of War: Carian Grandeur.
- Innate skill of the Carian Knight's Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Manifests a spectral greatsword from with 220 Magic base damage that is then used in an overhead slash.

Can be charged up to two more times for more damage, first to 315 base damage and then to 400 base damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 30 points of Stamina to use when not charged, 40 points of Stamina when charged once, and 60 points of Stamina when charged twice.
- As a Magic-based skill it benefits from the Spellblade's Set damage bonus.
- As a bullet-type skill it scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the wielder's Intelligence.
  - Gains increased Intelligence-scaling from the Magic and Cold affinities.
  - The Carian Knight's Sword has scaling on par with Magic affinity weapon, dealing only 0.5% less damage when fully upgraded and at 80 Intelligence.
- Damage is increased by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since the second and third levels already increase damage by 43% and by 82% of the uncharged base damage, this increases their damage increases to 65% and 109% respectively
- Compared to the Carian Greatsword skill this skill deals equal damage when uncharged but less damage when charged once (315 base damage compared to the Carian Greatsword's 340 base damage) but charges quicker and deals more than the Carian Greatsword at the highest charge level.
- Since the skill takes a bit to charge and requires the user to be stationary, this skill is best used in place of a Critical Attack or when ambushing an enemy.
  - It's also possible to time the charging so that it can be used just as an enemy steps into its reach, though this is considerably harder.
  - When fighting other players, consider varying which stage is used to surprise them, especially if they are about to perform an action such as attacking.
-

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

  - Increased the base damage when charged once from 280 to 315, and the base damage when charged twice from 350 to 400.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be applied to infusable weapons with Ash of War: Gravitas.
- Found as the innate skill on the Meteoric Ore Blade.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Stabs the weapon into the ground and draws nearby enemies in with a magical implosion.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 13 FP.
- Causes 26 Stance damage, on par with a jumping heavy attack for the heavier weapons (Greatswords, Colossal Swords, Curved Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Greataxes, Hammers, Great Hammers, Colossal Weapons, Great Spears) and on par with a charged heavy attack for the rest.
- Both the stab and the implosion are attacks. The former causes the same damage type as your weapon while the implosion causes Magic damage.
- The implosion scales with the user's Intelligence and the weapon's upgrade level, with a small (roughly 10%) additional damage boost if the weapon has the Magic affinity selected.
- The implosion actually consists of three overlapping waves with different ranges. This means that those standing furthest out only take damage from one wave, those standing in the middle take damage from two waves, and those standing furthest in take damage from all three waves.
  - This stacking of separate damage sources does unfortunately mean that the damage of the skill will be heavily blunted by enemies' flat defences early on.
- Fairly effective for farming items from weak animals, since it has a decently large area-of-effect and will bring their bodies closer to you.
- As stated by Note: Gravity's Advantage, this skill draws down flying enemies, such as the Warhawks that dot the rooftops of Stormveil Castle, onto the ground.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Sweeps the weapon forward, launching a wave of Holy light.

Grants a Weapon Buff giving 90 bonus Holy damage for 40 seconds.

All parts of this skill also causes 100% bonus damage against Those Who Live in Death and prevents Skeletons from resurrecting.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The wave and the swipe gain a 10% damage boost if used with a weapon that has the Sacred affinity.
- Since both the weapon and the wave causes damage, this skill causes much more damage up close.
- The wave's damage scales with weapon upgrade level and the user's Faith, and the swipe scales with the weapon's damage.
  - The wave gains increased Faith-scaling depending on how strong the weapon's own Faith-scaling is, whether that be innate or from the Sacred affinity.
- Causes incredible damage against undead foes such as Death Rite Bird, even with no investment in Faith as long as the weapon is upgraded well.
  - The 100% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death granted by the Weapon Buff applies to all of the weapon's damage, not just the bonus Holy damage from the buff itself.
- Besides the Sacred Order skill, this skill is the only way to increase the Holy damage of Sacred affinity weapons directly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

- Patch 1.07 increased motion speed and range of the (sacred) blade, added damage detection to the weapon part, and increased effect duration and attack power that gives the weapon holy power.
  - The second line means that the swing of the weapon itself also causes damage after the patch, and the third line means that the duration of the Weapon Buff was increased from 20 seconds to 40 seconds and that the additional damage was increased from 85 to 90.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Shared Order** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Raises the weapon to the user's face and then grants a buff to self and nearby allies that increases all damage by 10% (2.5% in PvP) and also increases damage by 50% against Those Who Live in Death while preventing Skeletons from resurrecting. Lasts for 60 seconds and counts as an Aura Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Mainly useful as an extra buff when fighting Those Who Live in Death due to being solidly outclassed by Golden Vow. It does however have something of a niche against Ash of War: Golden Vow as a general aura buff due to having slightly longer duration (60 seconds vs 40 seconds) and is much cheaper (20 FP vs 40 FP), in exchange for slightly less damage (10% vs 11.5%) and no defence increase (0% vs 7.5%).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: The user's readies the blade before lunging forward, slashing to deal 250 Poison build up and "detonates" any Poison inflicted on an enemy for damage equal to 250 plus 5% of that enemy's maximum health.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Cannot apply and detonate poison in the same usage, even if its own hit would apply Poison.
- The default status buildup scales somewhat with Arcane, with greater scaling on an Occult-affinity weapon.
- Since the damage is the same regardless of how much duration is left on the Poison, it is generally best to wait out the duration a bit, especially if the Poison is of the more powerful Deadly variant.
- Besides the obvious use of getting more damage on a Poisoned enemy, it can also be used to more easily keep up the damage buff from Kindred of Rot's Exultation and Mushroom Crown, especially so if using regular Poison.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed and decreased recovery time of this skill.
- Patch 1.07 increased poison status buildup and its power against poisoned enemies, increased the duration and damage of poison, and reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill.

sections.text: are enemies in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The stone sentries are bizarre, ominous creatures made from living rock. Their cylindrical, tube-like bodies are long chains of rounded stones bound together by gravitational energy. A crater in the topmost rock bears a single eye. They enjoy crawling around like earthworms, and are typically passive. At night, their eyes beam bright purple light as they keep active watch over the Evergaols in silence.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
Sentry stones are found across the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow.
- Deep Siofra Well
- Evergaols
- Stone Coffin Fissure

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
Although, visually, all sentry stones appear identical, there are a few variants.

- Sentry Stones found around Evergaols or in some cemeteries are passive, crawling about slowly like a inchworm or stand erect and motionless, staring at the sky. Even when attacked, they are sluggish: they slowly spin up like a propeller and move around wildly, striking with both ends of their "body" repeatedly, but eventually slow their rotation and come to a stop. They deal only moderate damage, but their attacks cannot be interrupted and deal high stamina damage if blocked.
- Sentry Stones in the deep canyon between the Deep Siofra Well grace and the Caelid Colosseum behind the Great-jar sit dormant in a small pile rather than elongated. When you come close, they begin to glow bright purple and emit a high-pitched whine before exploding after a short delay. Otherwise, they do not move or attack.
- The Sentry Stones in the Stone Coffin Fissure stand erect like their Evergaol counterparts but are able to detect you from long range and will automatically begin firing a high-velocity purple laser beam at regular intervals similar to Astel. This attack can be avoided using the terrain and timing the sounds of their charging, although they continue to fire

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- They are immune to all status effects.
- They are one of the few creatures not directly referenced or spoke about in the game, and internally they are labeled "AliveStones."
- The sentry stones drop Ruin Fragments, shards that fell from Crumbling Farum Azula. The city of the ancient dragons was lifted into the sky after being struck by a meteor in prehistoric times.
  - The stone sentries may fire lasers from their eyes in a manner similar to Metyr, Mother of Fingers, whose star was the first to fall upon the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Smithing Stones** are Bolstering Materials in Elden Ring, of which 9 variants exist.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Smithing Stones can be used by Smithing Master Hewg or War Counselor Iji to incrementally upgrade Weapons in exchange for runes, up to +25, consuming the stones in the process. Every "tier" of Smithing Stone can upgrade an armament up to 3 times before the next tier of Smithing Stone is needed; the first upgrade of a tier requires 2 stones, the second 4, and the third 6. Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones are the sole exception — only being used once to upgrade weapons from +24 to +25.

However, for certain special armaments, the rarer Somber Smithing Stones are needed instead; such armaments can only be upgraded to +10, and only require one somber stone per upgrade.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: They can be found scattered through both the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, sometimes looted from certain enemies when killed, or purchased from some Merchants in usually limited quantity. However, excepting Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones, they can be purchased in unlimited quantity from the Twin Maiden Husks after giving them Smithing-Stone Miner's Bell Bearings, of which 4 are scattered throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Smithing Stones may be harvested from certain caves, such as Morne Tunnel.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Serosh, Lord of Beasts**, also known as the **Golden Lion** and **Beast Regent**, is a character in Elden Ring. He indirectly fights the player during the Godfrey, First Elden Lord boss encounter at the Elden Throne in Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Serosh is a large lion with a dark gray coat and a silvery white mane, though it was once golden in his youth. The skin on his snout and lips are both colored black and his face is covered in scars, the most notable ones passing over his perpetually closed eyes—indicating his blindness. His largest wound was inflicted by the death blow that cleaved through the left side of his silver crown, before continuing across his forehead and over his right eye, ending at the bottom his right cheek.

Serosh wears silver platemail armor that covers his chest and shoulders, with matching, sharp-tipped gauntlets covering his paws. His broken crown resembles the Elden Lord Crown. While mounted on Godfrey's back, Serosh's body is translucent, with the lower half of his body not visible.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Serosh was a regal, golden lion regarded as the Lord of Beasts in ancient times. For the beastmen of Farum Azula, the presence of five fingers was celebrated as a symbol of the intelligence granted to their kind, with the five black nails of the Beastclaw Greathammer representative of Serosh.

The soul of Serosh was taken upon Hoarah Loux's back when the warrior vowed to become Godfrey, Marika's first Elden Lord, suppressing his ceaseless lust for battle. Serosh offered counsel and guidance to Godfrey and his Golden Lineage as their Beast Regent, his insignia becoming a longstanding symbol of their glory. General Radahn, captivated by Godfrey in his youth, wore armor depicting a golden lion, said to symbolize both Godfrey and Serosh.

Serosh remained with Godfrey even after he became Tarnished and was exiled from the Lands Between. After the Axe of Godfrey broke and the Long March came to an end, Godfrey divested his kingship, and became Hoarah Loux once more. Serosh and Hoarah Loux settled in the badlands, where they lived and died together as simple warriors. Following their deaths, the Guidance of Grace returned, restoring them to life and ushering them home. They reclaimed the axe and became Godfrey once more, crossing the Sea of Fog to claim the Elden Ring.

The pair arrive at the foot of the burning Erdtree after the player Tarnished commits the Cardinal Sin and defeats Maliketh, the Black Blade. They mourn the passing of Morgott, and Grace directs them to confront the player. When pushed to their limit, Serosh transitions from a spirit to a tangible, corporeal form, preparing to play an active role in the duel. However, Godfrey interrupts the process; he thanks Serosh for his service and violently kills him, drenching himself in the blood of his Beast Regent. He discards his axe to fight as Hoarah Loux, Warrior.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Serosh and Hoarah Loux's pairing most likely occured at the Gate of Divinity, as per the requirements for Marika returning from the other side. The Divine Beast Warriors who protect the Gate each wears a lion's head and allows a Divine Beast to control their actions, paralleling Godfrey and Serosh.
- Serosh is often shown with his teeth sinking into Godfrey's arm or torso. This may be a means of keeping Godfrey's lust for battle in check.
- Serosh and Elder Lions are the same color, but Serosh lacks horns.
- Although the Talisman of Lord's Bestowal omits Serosh, his presence is indicated by Godfrey's stoic demeanor and Elden Lord Crown.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Serpents**, also known as **Snakes**, are types of reptilian creature in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
]]
There was once an ancient religion based at Mt. Gelmir that worshiped a Serpent-God, offering sacrifices to it through a creature known as the God-Devouring Serpent, also refered to as the Great Serpent. The Serpent-Hunter was a weapon crafted and used in the distant past to kill a incarnation of the God-Devouring Serpent; but the Great Serpent is immortal, and has since been reborn by some means.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.text:
The eldest child of Queen Marika, Messmer the Impaler, was born entangled by serpents. He was inhabited by the Base Serpent, a malevolent creature without light. However, two benevolent Winged Serpents were also present from birth. They served as his constant advisors during the Crusade and, more importantly, suppressed the abyssal serpent's influence.

The Erdtree regarded serpents as traitors. Even displaying their image was considered a curse. In Godfrey's age, Duelists adorned with bronze serpents fought in the Colosseums. Audiences took pleasure in seeing their effigies struck down.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text:
Disillusioned with the Golden Order and the state of the world the Shattering brought, Praetor Rykard, son of Rennala, swore to oppose the Erdtree. From his residence at the Volcano Manor atop Mt. Gelmir, Rykard spent time studying the ancient religion once based there. He discovered hexes the serpent worshipers had used and by applying his extensive knowledge of sorcery, natural to Carian Royal like himself, Rykard brought these hexes back into practical use, creating the Magma Sorceries.

After waging a bloody, undending war against the Erdtree, Rykard had since seemingly become obsesed with a young reincarnation of the Great Serpent. In an appalling act, Rykard fed himself, Great Rune and all, to the God-Devouring Serpent, and the birth of the unnatural Man-Serpents followed. With the power of Rykard's rune, and the sacrifices of many Recusant champions it has been fed, the Great Serpent has grown to an enormous size.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Servants of Rot** are a faction in Elden Ring. They are an ancient sect dedicated to the Goddess of Rot, and an outer god embodying death, decay, and rebirth through the power of Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
In ancient times, great lords dwelled within poison and served the Scarlet Rot, a divine element of an outer god of Rot. They regarded the mushrooms that colonized their bodies as holy vestments, connecting them to the earth. They believed that death brought new life, offering the possibility of rebirth. They called this cycle of decay the Order of Rot.

The old servants worshipped a deity with a Scorpion's Stinger. However, their outer god of rot was defeated and sealed away beneath the Lake of Rot by the blind swordsman. Its relic was stored in the Grand Cloister of an ancient dynasty.

Later, Malenia rejected and abandoned the loyal servants of Rot. After she bloomed in the Swamp of Aeonia, sage Gowry nurtured her offshoots, guiding them along the path of the scarlet valkyrie. While some servants chose new masters, others found a new mother when a divine element was discovered in the Rauh Ruins and weaved into the scarlet rot.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**The Scadutree** (影樹, *Eiju*; lit. "Shadow Tree") is a colossal tree in Elden Ring, included in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

It is the shadow of the Erdtree which looms over the Land of Shadow, born of dark notions that bear no sense of Order, that twist and bend its stock, rendering it misshapen and brittle.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Scadutree is holy but its gold is veiled in shadow and covered in impenetrable thorns.

Like the Erdtree, the Scadutree can manifest avatars to defend itself and its offspring. Scadutree Avatars take the form of giant Shadow Sunflowers.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Scadutree is located at the northernmost point in the Realm of Shadow, found at the Scadutree Base.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
]]

The blessed sap of the Scadutree once fell like tears into the Scadutree Chalice, but it has since scattered, pooling deeply within the Furnace Golems.

Its splinters were collected, displayed, and prayed to in some Churches of Marika by the people of the Erdtree. Scadutree Fragments bestowed a Scadutree blessing of great power, although it has no influence outside of the Realm of Shadow. The remains of the warriors who perished in the realm of shadow were touched by the gold of the Scadutree, a blessing said to be the highest honor that can be afforded to the dead.

For those who abandoned the practice of incantations after devout faith rewarded them with only despair, the image of the misshapen Scadutree is an edict: *“Spurn all that exists. Wound all that exists. For we have been abandoned. Denounce their ways. Do them harm. For they have abandoned us.”*

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Director Hidetaka Miyazaki mentioned the title "Shadow of the Erdtree" contains a secret: the Scadutree is the shadow of the Erdtree, and the shadow of its former self.
- The Scadutree Grail holds six Red Relics, complimenting the Sacred Erdtree Grail's six yellow slots. When considering the nature of primordial gold, these Chalices indicate that the Scadutree is still imbued with the red power of life, containing the primordial form of the Erdtree.
- The straight, leaning Scadutree trunk oozes a vast quantity of pitch (i.e., a sticky, protective resin secreted by conifers—pines, firs, spruces, cedars—when sick or wounded, different from the tree's internal sap), supporting textual evidence of the Scadutree's deterioration.
- The Sealing Tree resembles one of the Scadutree's trunks.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - "Scadutree" (*pronounced Schadutree*) derives from *"scadu"* ([https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/sceadu#Old_English *sċeadu*), an Old English word for "shadow" or "shade"—meaning the Scadutree is literally named "Shadowtree".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sir Ansbach**, also known as **Pureblood Knight Ansbach**, is a character in Shadow of the Erdtree

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Formerly the feared commander of the Pureblood Knights in service of Lord Mohg, Ansbach is one of the compatriots of Needle Knight Leda who followed Miquella into the Realm of Shadow. A wise old man, Ansbach has dedicated himself to investigating Miquella's purpose by following the trail of crosses he left behind.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text:
As with the rest who followed Miquella into the Shadow Realm, Ansbach was under the influence of a charm, which breaks when the Empyrean abandons his Miquella's Great Rune. With his mind free of the charm, Ansbach recalls that he once challenged Miquella in an attempt to free Mohg of his enchantment, which resulted in him falling under the enchantment himself.

With his faculties restored, Ansbach makes his way to the Specimen Storehouse within the Shadow Keep. There, he learns that Mohg's body has been taken to Miquella, and with the assistance of the Tarnished, discovers that Miquella intends to use Mohg's corpse as a vessel for his king consort.

Ansbach becomes one of Needle Knight Leda's possible targets, resulting in a duel in which the Tarnished may intervene on either side. Should Ansbach survive Leda's attack, he will aid the Tarnished against Leda, Dryleaf Dane, and their allies in Enir-Ilim. Ansbach will then be available to assist the Tarnished in their battle against Promised Consort Radahn, before which he admits that he knows the Tarnished was responsible for killing Mohg, but bears no grudge against them, viewing Mohg's death as an honorable one. After defeating Miquella and his consort, Ansbach dies before the Gate of Divinity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **servants of Death** were a faction mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
In an age long past, the servants of Death worshipped an outer god. They venerated the Deathbirds as evil deities, symbolically invoking them during sacrificial rituals. They valued meaningful death; those who faced death with valor were granted a glorious end. Other worshippers preserved their lives in hopes of making a greater sacrifice in the future.

Over time, the influence of the Deathbirds waned. Some priests pledged their spears to protect the birds, entering the rite of Death in exchange for a promised, distant resurrection. Later, Gravebird golems were created in the Deathbirds' likeness to guard the spiritgraves on the Gravesite Plain. Although a few hexes continued to be practiced in the tower of Enir-Ilim, the importance of the ghostflame diminished, and the secrets of Death sorcery were eventually forgotten.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- A number of other characters surrender their own lives to continue serving their masters as spirits.
  - Lhutel the Headless entered a rite of Death to protect a soulless demigod, and her Ashes were promised Erdtree Burial at the Tombsward Catacombs. Following her example, the Mausoleum Knights beheaded themselves to protect the Wandering Mausoleums as spirits.
  - Spirits of Banished Knights and Exile Soldiers fight for Commander Niall and Commander O'Neil, respectively. Commander Niall of Castle Sol commanded these spirits in defense of his deceased lord.
  - Troll Knights beheaded themselves to protect the Four Belfries as spirits.
  - Latenna the Albinauric willingly becomes a Spirit Ash.
- Similarly to the Servants of Death forming the wings of Death Rite Birds, Aeonian Butterflies came together to form the Goddess of Rot's wings.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Siege of Caria Manor** refers to the failed siege of Caria Manor, the home of the Carian Royal Family, by the Knights of the Cuckoo, the private army of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. It was the final battle in the Liurnian Civil War.

sections.heading: Prelude
sections.text:
*Main article: Liurnian Civil War*

The Siege of Caria Manor was the decisive battle that occured towards the end of Liurnian civil war.

The head of the Carian Royal Family, Rennala, was left a grieving wreck after being abandoned by her husband, Radagon. The Academy of Raya Lucaria realised she was a champion no longer, and in her weakened state, they took the opportunity to attempt a restoration the long-restricted study of the Primeval Current that had been in place before Rennala became their governor. The Academy imprisoned Rennala in their Grand Library and, alongside their mercantile allies, the Knights of the Cuckoo, began a rebellion against the Carain royalist forces. This marked the beginning the Liurnian civil war.

Some members of the Academy who followed the Lazuli Conspectus chose to defend the Carians. Permitted, yet deemed heretical and shunned within the Acadamy itself, their study believed in equality between the moon and stars.

sections.heading: Siege
sections.text:
The Knights of the Cuckoo launched a surprise attack against the Caria Manor. The Cuckoo leveled the family's forward defense at what became the Kingsrealm Ruins, swiftly moving on towards the Manor itself. From the design of their shields, specially made for magical defense, it is no secret that the Carians believed the Academy's treachery would one day come. Although they were caught off guard, the Carian's preparations meant their forces were scarcely weakened. The Carians also created an enchanted snare over the Manor as the fighting raged, which in turn ultimately ended the Cuckoo's advance. The Cuckoos caught in the snare had  their souls trapped, being redeployed against their comrades as puppet soliders.

The Siege of Caria Manor was somewhat of a pyrrhic victory for the Carians, as they themselves had suffered a great number of casualties. While the battle was won, Rennala was still held captive by the Academy, With Rennala imprisoned, and her successors absent, the Carians fell into disarray. Despite the Cuckoo's defeat, the Academy had regained its independence.
