sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Spinning Gravity Thrust** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable large and colossal swords with the Ash of War: Spinning Gravity Thrust Shadow of the Erdtree.
- Default skill on the Sword Lance Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Hang in the air before rotating and charging forward with your weapon, hitting 4 times with 33% of weapon Attack Power on each hit and finishing with an upwards thrust with 115% Attack Power.

Using the skill again causes another spinning gravity thrust, that hits 3 times with 33% Attack Power each time before crashing to the ground to hit with 125% Attack Power and knock back enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The first input costs 27 points of Stamina to perform (3 from each weak hit and 15 from the final one) while the second input takes another 29 points of Stamina (3 from each weak hit and 20 from the final hit).
  - Though the entire skill with the follow-up costs 56 points of Stamina, technically only 28 points are needed to perform it fully.
- This Skill works with multi-hit buffs such as the Winged Sword Insignias.
- The Status Effects build-up of each hit is generally reduced much less than usual, as each hit has 65% build-up. This means that the first part of the skill has 295% Status Effect build-up and the follow-up has 230% build-up, totaling 525% Status Effect build-up while the total Attack Power is only roughly 471%.
- Each weak hit has a 70% Stance damage multiplier, while the while the finale of the first and second part has a 100% and 240% multiplier respectively. This means the first input has a 380% Stance damage multiplier while the second one as a 450% Stance damage multiplier (830% multiplier in total).
  - Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Curved Greatswords, and Great Katanas deal 20.9 Stance damage on the first input and 24.75 on the second one (45.65 Stance damage in total).
  - Colossal Swords deal 22.8 Stance damage on the first input and 27 Stance damage on the second one (49.8 Stance damage in total).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Savage Lion's Claw** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and hammers (except for Daggers, Thrusting Swords, or Heavy Thrusting Swords) with the Ash of War: Savage Lion's Claw Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Using the skill performs a quick, jumping forward spin that has 195% Attack Power compared to the weapon's own.

Using the skill again makes them jump again and flip mid-air to hit with 68% Attack Power before landing with a final slam for 155% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The first spin costs 37 points of Stamina to perform. The follow-up spin costs 20 points of Stamina to make the mid-air flip and then another 30 points of Stamina for the final slam.
  - Costs 87 points of Stamina to use both the first and second part of the skill. This is a very heavy cost, so consider carefully if you want to use the follow-up after the first one.
  - Technically only 38 points of Stamina is needed to perform the entire skill.
- The first spin only has about 81% of the Attack Power of the Lion's Claw skill, but the entire skill has roughly 74% more Attack Power.
- Using the follow-up can more than double the damage of the skill compared to only using the first somersault.
- Attack Power is increased by 10% if Freyja's Greatsword is in one of the user's two active hand-slots, even if the other weapon is being two-handed.
- The first part has a 250% Stance damage multiplier, while the follow-up has 200% on the first hit and 400% on the second hit for a total multiplier of 850% if all hits land. For comparison, Lion's Claw has a 600% Stance damage multiplier.
  - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, and Axes deal 42.5 Stance damage.
  - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Greataxes deal 46.75 Stance damage.
  - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 51 Stance damage.
  - Hammers deal 55.25 Stance damage.
  - Great Hammers deal 59.5 Stance damage.
  - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deals 63.75 Stance damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.13 PvP-exclusive: The second hit of the follow-up attack is now easier to land. Decreased damage animation of the first attack against other players.
  - Hitting the mid-air flip of the follow-up now guarantees that the final slam hits if the hit target is still inside of the weapon's reach.
- Patch 1.13 increased attack power and poise damage of the first attack.
  - Attack Power for the first spin was increased from 185% to 195%.
  - Poise (and Stance) damage of the first spin was increased from 200% of the weapon's base value to 250% of it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Overhead Stance** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to infusable Great Katanas with the Ash of War: Overhead Stance.
  - Since the only infusable Great Katana already has Overhead Stance as its innate skill, the purpose of this is purely to change its Affinity.
- Innate skill of the Great Katana.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Using and holding the skill holds the Great Katana above and places the user in a stance, while the user's Stamina regeneration rate and movement speed is greatly decreased.

Using a light attack while in this Stance makes the user step forward slightly and make an overhead vertical slash with 147% Attack Power.

Using a heavy attack while in this Stance makes the user continuously step forward and perform 3 overhead slashes with 87%, 97%, and 103% Attack Power respectively (287% Attack Power in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Stance costs no points of Stamina. The light attack follow-up costs 20 points of Stamina while the heavy attack follow-up costs 20 points of Stamina per attack (60 points in total for all 3 slashes).
  - The Stance costs no points of FP. The light attack follow-up costs 8 points of FP while the heavy attack follow-up costs 10 points of FP.
- The light attack follow-up deals 200% Stance damage while the heavy attack follow-up one deals 400% Stance damage (100% each from the first two attacks and then 200% from the final one).
  - This means the light attack follow-up deals 11 Stance damage while the heavy attack follow-up deals 22 Stance damage.
- The Rellana's Cameo grants a 45% boost to Attack Power to the follow-up attacks if the Stance is held for at least a second.
- A rather unimpressive skill, especially when compared with Unsheathe's 15 and 30 Stance damage and quicker speed, with the primary use being the heavy attack follow-up's 230% Status Effect build-up.
- The Stance can be cancelled without using a follow-up attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.13: Increased attack power against enemies (other than players).
  - This increased the Attack Power of the light attack follow-up from 130% to 147% while heavy attack follow-ups slashes had their Attack Power increased from 77%, 83%, and 93% to 87%, 97%, and 103% respectively.
  - The Attack Power multiplier against other players was decreased from 0.8 to 0.7. This actually made all strikes except for the second one from the heavy attack follow-up (which became slightly stronger) slightly weaker against other players, though only by about a percentage each.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Swift Slash** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree with the Ash of War: Swift Slash Shadow of the Erdtree.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Encountering Messmer the Impaler before getting this item prevents that character from acquiring it until their next Journey.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Dash forwards while slicing with both blades, hitting with 92% Attack Power while dodging all attacks. After the dash ends, shearing winds expand to hit with 120% Attack Power.

Charging the skill extends the range of the dash and increases the Attack Power of the dashing slices to 104% and that of the shearing winds to 160%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 30 points of Stamina. Charging the skill increases the cost to 50 points.
- The Godfrey Icon seems to only apply it's Attack Power boost to the dashing slices but not the shearing winds. This results in an overall 6% increase in Attack Power instead of the regular 15% increase.
- Deals 100% Stance damage on the initial dash and another 100% Stance damage with the shearing winds (200% in total). Charging the skill increases the Stance damage multiplier of the dash to 300% (400% in total).
  - In effect, this means that the skill deals 10 Stance damage, or 20 Stance damage if charged.
- Very strong against other players due to it being able to move past them while effectively being invulnerable to their attacks and also attacking them at the same time.
- Mildly useful for moving when on slowing surfaces such as knee-deep waters or swamps, since the user will still dash forward when they have 0 FP.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.13: Reduced movement distance when using this skill. Extended recovery time.
- Patch 1.12.3: (PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustment) Decreased the damage and damage animation of the shearing vacuum effect of the “Swift Slash” Skill.
  - This reduced the damage multiplier against other players from 0.8 to 0.65, effectively reducing damage in PvP by 18.75% (not accounting for flat defences).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Blind Spot** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree with the Ash of War: Blind Spot Shadow of the Erdtree.
  - Since the only infusable Backhand Blade already has Blind Spot as its innate skill, the purpose of this is purely to change its Affinity.
- Innate skill of the Backhand Blade Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Dash forwards and to the side while dodging, then stab in towards the target with 145% Attack Power while slipping past the opponent's Guard.

By default the user will dash to the right initially, but holding left or right as the skill starts let's the user control the direction of this initial dash.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 30 points of Stamina.
- Deals 200% Stance damage.
  - In effect, this means that the skill deals 10 Stance damage.
- Always deals Pierce damage.
- Unlike Skill: Impaling Thrust or Skill: Piercing Fang, this skill doesn't technically pierce through Guarded Damage Negation. Instead, the bypass effect comes from attacking at an angle that the blocking doesn't cover.
  - This means that the skill should be blockable, though it is difficult.
- The dash grants 6 i-frames upon activation, meaning the first 0.2 seconds of the skill functions as a roll.
  - While no damage will be taken during this time, Status Effects will still build up.
  - It's unclear how Patch 1.13 has affected the performance of this dodge against other players.
- Very strong against other players due to effectively combining a roll and an attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.13: (PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustment) Decreased invulnerability window against other players' attacks.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Savage Claws** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree with the Ash of War: Savage Claws Shadow of the Erdtree.
  - Since the only infusable Beast Claw already has Savage Claws as its innate skill, the purpose of this is purely to change its Affinity.
- Innate skill of the Beast Claw Shadow of the Erdtree weapon.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Continuously dash forwards while attacking 5 times, before dealing a final, heavy blow.

Has 80%, 81%, 73%, 74%, and 75% Attack Power for the first 5 attacks, and 102% Attack Power on the final blow.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 10 points of Stamina per attack (60 points in total).
- Deals 100% Stance damage on the first two attacks, then 50% Stance damage on the next three attacks, and 200% Stance damage on the final blow (550% Stance damage in total).
  - Deals 22 Stance damage in total if all hits lands.
- Has 485% Attack Power for the entire skill, not accounting for flat defences.
- Deals 60% Status Effect build-up per hit (360% build-up in total).
- Pairs very well with Bloodflame Blade due to the many hits, providing an additional 240 Blood Loss build-up.
  - This is on top of a non-Status Affinity Beast Claw dealing 162 Blood Loss build-up.
  - Also works with Blood Grease or Drawstring Blood Grease, though they will only provide an additional 108 or 137 Blood Loss build-up respectively due to Weapon Buffs only having 60% effect for each hit. Bloodflame Blade, meanwhile, will always deal its full effect 40 Blood Loss build-up per hit.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Raging Beast** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Can be granted to Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree with the Ash of War: Raging Beast Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Dash forwards with 6 i-frames (0.20 seconds) and then hop and slash with 145% Attack Power.

Using a heavy attack leads to a follow-up attack with a jump where a mid-air spin with 70% Attack Power followed by a slam for 160% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 15 points of Stamina for the initial input. Using the heavy attack follow-up costs 10 points of Stamina for the spin and then 20 points for the slam (30 points of Stamina in total for the follow-up, or 45 points for the entire skill).
- Deals 150% Stance damage with the initial attack, then 60% Stance damage on the spin and 200% Stance damage on the final blow (410% Stance damage in total).
  - Deals 16.4 Stance damage in total if all hits lands.
- Has 375% Attack Power for the entire skill, not accounting for flat defences.
- The direction of the initial dash can be controlled, while the heavy attack follow-up always attacks in the character's direction.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.13: (PvP-Exclusive Balande Adjustment) Decreased invulnerability window against other players' attacks.
  - This made the initial dash have fewer i-frames when being attacked by a player.
- Patch 1.13: (Bug Fix) Fixed a bug where a different Rage Art was sometimes performed when following up with a strong attack after using the “Raging Beast” and “Dynasty Sickleplay” Skills.
  - Before this bug was fixed, using the heavy attack follow-up for Raging Beast would instead use the heavy attack follow-up of the most recently used non-Raging Beast skill that has a heavy attack follow-up.
  - The name of the Unique Skill: Dynastic Sickleplay was misspelled for this update.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Scattershot Throw** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree with the Ash of War: Scattershot Throw Shadow of the Erdtree.
- Innate skill of the Claws of Night Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Create a fan of weapons in each hand before making a melee attack with each hand and throwing the weapons. The throw can hit up to four times and the melee attack hits twice.

Use the skill again to throw again.

Effective Attack Power varies per weapon type:
- For Throwing Blades the projectiles have 25% Attack Power per hit while the melee attacks have 88% Attack Power each.verification needed
- For the Claws of Night the projectiles have 20% Attack Power per hit while the melee attacks have 70% Attack Power each.verification needed

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 32 points of Stamina per throw.
  - Technically this is an 8 points cost applied 4 times.
- The FP cost of 11 is per throw.
- Stance damage per hit varies per weapon type.
  - For Throwing Blades it is 120% Stance damage per hit (up to 480% if all thrown projectiles hit and up to 720% with all hits). verification needed
    - This equals 9.6 Stance damage if all projectiles land, or 14.4 Stance damage with all hits.
  - For the Claws of Night it is 70% Stance damage per hit (up to 280% if all thrown projectiles hit and up to 420% with all hits). verification needed
    - This equals 11.2 Stance damage if all projectiles land, or 16.8 Stance damage with all hits.
- The Throwing Blades version effectively has 276% Attack Power for the entire skill while the Claws of Night version has 220% effect Attack Power. Neither calculation takes into account for flat defences, which may reduce effective damage below these numbers.
- Deals 70% Status Effect build-up per throwing hit and 100% per melee hit (up to 480% build-up in total).
- Although only up to 4 projectiles can damage a single target, each throw involves 28 projectiles.
- Always deals Pierce damage, meaning it benefits from the Spear Talisman and counterhits if it can land during an enemy's attack.
  - For the Claws of Night this is somewhat less relevant, as only 61% of its Attack Power is Physical.
- Generally much more effective on the Claws of Night as they usually have twice as much Attack Power as the Smithscript Dagger and has innate Blood Loss without having to sacrifice Attack Power to an Affinity.
  - For comparison: when both weapons are fully upgraded and the character is at minimum stats with 80 Dexterity the Claws of Night has 684 Attack Power while a Keen Affinity Smithscript Dagger has 331 Attack Power.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.14: (PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments) Decreased damage against other players. This skill will no longer cause the headshot damage motion when hitting another player.
  - For both version of the skill the damage multiplier against other players was lowered from the default 0.8 to 0.7, providing an effective 12.5% reduction in damage against them.
  - The removal of the ability to headshot other players removed the ability to stun them occasionally and also provided an additional reduction in damage and Poise damage against players.
- Patch 1.13: (Bug Fix) Fixed a bug where the physical attack attribute of the “Scattershot Throw” Skill of the “Claws of Night” weapon was different than expected.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Skill: Piercing Throw** is a Skill in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Can be granted to Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree with the Ash of War: Piercing Throw Shadow of the Erdtree.
- Innate skill of the Smithscript Dagger Shadow of the Erdtree weapon.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: Rear back and then throw a blade with 175% Attack Power that penetrates through enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs 15 points of Stamina.
- Deals 150% Stance damage.
  - Deals 3 Stance damage.
- Though it goes through all enemies it will not ignore the damage reduction from an enemy that is keeping its guard up if they are guarding in the direction it's flying from.
- Fairly spammable due to a short casting time.
- Compared to a one-handed charged heavy attack with the Smithscript Dagger, Piercing Throw costs FP, has roughly 50% greater range, and is considerably faster, and also has greater Attack Power (175% vs 150%) but worse Stance damage (3 vs 6).
  - Compared to a one-handed regular heavy attack the disparity in Attack Power is greater (175% vs 120%) while Stance damage is closer (2 vs 4) in exchanged for being more similar in speed.
  - Two-handed charged heavy attacks are harder to compare with, as their total Attack Power is technically higher (175% vs 196%) but divided over two attacks with 98% Attack Power each (meaning they may suffer greater damage reduction from flat defence) and even higher Stance damage (3 vs 6.4).
- Always deals Pierce damage, meaning it benefits from the Spear Talisman and counterhits if it can land during an enemy's attack.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Second Defense of Leyndell** was an event that occurred during the The Shattering in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
At some point after the collapse of the alliance of the Shardbearers
, Starscourge Radahn and Godrick the Golden, the last still living inside the city, plotted to conquer Leyndell, Royal Capital.
Alongside soldiers of Stormveil Castle and those affiliated with Godrick, Radahn and his Redmanes also took part in the battle..

sections.heading: Battle
sections.text:
After entering the Altus Plateau from the Grand Lift of Dectus, the forces of Stormveil did not move toward the capital along the main highway. Instead, they took the long route, marching on the rampartside path in the direction of Dominula, Windmill Village.

Once on the paved road that led to the secondary entrance in the outer walls of Leyndell, the clashes against the capital's forces began from under the Highway Lookout Tower. The attacking forces fought their way to the first ring of walls, bringing siege engines behind them, eventually managing to force the defenders to retreat from the ramparts.

Once they entered the capital area, the besiegers continued to fight along the secondary paved road, expanding into the surrounding hills. However, Stormveil forces failed to force the city's main gate during their initial push. At some point the battles slowed, giving the attackers time to build camps inside Leyndell's outer walls and deploy siege engines to hit the second layer of ramparts. Perfumers of the city would devise biological weapons that the defenders threw on the enemy's camps to release poisonous clouds.

During the siege of Leyndell, Morgott, the Omen King, would enter the battlefield himself under the guise of "Margit the Fell Omen". The Omen managed to hurt Starscourge Radahn and slaughter many heroes in the defense of the Erdtree.

Radahn survived Morgott's attack but the Redmanes and Stormveil soldiers were unable to force the walls of the capital. Leyndell forces started repelling the invaders and pushing them outside their camps inside the walls. The collapsing army was unable to retreat in organized way, leaving their equipment and a trail of corpses. Fearing for his life, Godrick abandoned Leyndell, hiding among the women escaping from the capital and stealing many treasures.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text:
The forces aligned with the Golden Lineage attackers became a defeated army and together with their lord they fled back to Limgrave. Here Godrick would hide inside Stormveil Castle in fear of Radahn and his army marching back to Caelid.

Despite their defeat in the battle for Leyndell, forces of Stormveil would continue to linger on the Altus plateau. One group set up a camp between the Altus Highway Junction and the Grand Lift of Dectus. However they would end up being overrun by Misbegotten, either their own rebellious slaves or those aligned with Leyndell's army. Another group would retreat to the hills between the Lux Ruins and Wyndham Ruins. However Leyndell forces set up a great camp there, defended with Ballistas, thus blocking the path to the Grand Lift of Dectus and defeating the invaders.

The capital's army would also deploy its forces to protect the path to the side gate of the outer walls and the highway lookout tower, installing siege engines to bombard any intruder attempting to follow the same road of the invaders.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Misbegotten and Omen can be found close to the sites of battles on the Altus plateau. The Misbegotten occupying a camp of defeated knights from Stromveil while the Omen set up their own camp close to the greater base of Leyndell's forces. This could either indicate that the capital mobilized those treated as slaves to reinforce its army or that the impure creatures rebelled against Stormveil's army and were tolerated by the Leyndell's forces.
- The first Leyndell camp facing the the Lux Ruins and Wyndham Ruins is empty and two Great Coffins containing the Greatshield Talisman and the Troll's Golden Sword can be found inside it, possibly indicating that a knight and troll fighting for the capital recently died in the battle.
- A camp without banners or clear affiliation can be found between the Minor Erdtree Church and the Outer Wall main gate. The camp is occupied by three Leyndell Foot Soldiers and a Great Coffin inside it contains the Giant-Crusher, a weapon used by the forces of Leyndell in the War Against the Giants.
- The soldiers affiliated with Godrick used armor and weapons of the Banished Knights, as seen in the corpses still left on the battlefield, and raised standards with the old symbol of the Stormhawk King. This was possibly done to disguise themselves and hide the demigod involvement in the siege, as he was still living inside Leyndell before he escaped hiding among the womenfolk.

sections.text:

After the water has been drained, descend an elevator found behind a door in the large central church north of the  Sunken Chapel Site of Grace. Travel north across the bridge in the cavernous  Tree Worship Sanctum to reach the Scadutree Base.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Shaman Village** is a location within the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Shaman Village is a tranquil hamlet hidden in the Scaduview, nestled among lush vegetation and vibrant, multicolored flowers. A few cobblestone homes rest on a hill warmed by the gentle golden light of an Erdtree sapling. At the village's highest point, an old tree contains a statue of a silver-haired maiden.

This village was once populated by persecuted shamans before the Age of the Erdtree. It was the home of Marika before her ascension to godhood. By the time Marika returned, her kinfolk had vanished. In their memory, she planted a minor Erdtree and offered her Golden Braid to the Grandmother entombed within the tree.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
The Shaman Village is situated in the eastern Hinterland of Scaduview, a secret area unlocked by solving a puzzle at the Shadow Keep. To access it, perform the O Mother gesture before a statue of Marika near the  Shadow Keep, Back Gate Site of Grace and head southeast.

The road to the village is guarded by two Tree Sentinels in possession of a Blessing of Marika. The nearest Sites of Grace are  Hinterland and  Hinterland Bridge, though the village itself lacks a dedicated Site of Grace. The village is entered from the west, with a one-way path connecting to Scadu Altus in the southeast, where a cliffside descent reveals a secret area within Rabbath's Rise.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- There are no bosses or enemies at the Shaman Village; however, two Tree Sentinels guard the surrounding surrounding Hinterland area.
- The shamans were spirited away or kidnapped by the hornsent Greater Potentates of the Bonny Village.
- Many of the former residents were tortured and turned into Jar Dwellers.
- The music for this location is *Shaman Village*.
- Godrick the Grafted may be referring to the Shaman Village when he says, *"And one day, we'll return together. To our home, bathed in rays of gold."*

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The church district of the Shadow Keep is connected to the upper section of the Specimen Storehouse and the northern Scaduview. It is accessible from the road running north from Bonny Village, near the  Church District Highroad site of grace and is the only path to the Scadutree Base.

This holy quarter was flooded by Messmer's army to prevent access to the Scadutree. However, the lever to open the sluices can be reached by navigating the rooftops. Pushing the lever triggers a cutscene, drains the water, and reveals the lower half of the area.

An important and unique tree with root-like branches dominants the central square. An elevator in the large church descends to the  Tree-Worship Sanctum and  Scadutree Base sites of grace in Scaduview.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Shanehaight** is an unused NPC. He is a noble from Leyndell, Royal Capital and has a small quest tied to him.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Shanehaight is an elderly human viscount born of House Shanehaight, with long blonde hair and facial hair, who dons a luxurious robe, its fine blue mantle serving to prove its wearer's status. His face is hidden behind a mask in the image of a wizened sage. He heavily espouses the virtues and strength of Leyndell, Royal Capital, gatekeeping it against those deemed unfit to live there. He longed to be part of higher society among the Erdbishops and, one day, be granted an audience with King Morgott himself, unaware of the monarch's secret.

One day, Shanehaight happens across a Tarnished within the Capital; not immediately noticing their status, he greeted them warmly, but once he realized he urged them to leave at once. However, if the Tarnished shows them proof that they hunt Omens, he takes an interest, offering a job to hunt and kill the vile creatures whose tortured howling in the sewers affronted his ears. With the task completed, Shanehaight was elated, rewarding the Tarnished with a family heirloom and giddily setting about preparing to meet the King.

When the Tarnished happened upon Shanehaight some time after, the viscount, having met Morgott and discovering the monarch's true nature, was horrified, begging the Tarnished to kill the "kingly imposter".

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- He looks and dresses distinctly like Kenneth Haight, although older, with a similar last name and some shared mannerisms. While his quest was cut, he likely was reworked into the nobler, well-intentioned Kenneth.
- In the official release, his robe and mask are found in a carriage at the Abandoned Coffin site, alongside a large group of omens. This indicates that, having made an enemy of Morgott, he attempted to flee the city only to be ambushed and killed by the Omens, avenging their fallen who died by his order. While his quest was cut, its events are thus hinted to have already taken place by the time the player arrives.
- He was likely cut to make meeting Margit, the Fell Omen at the Erdtree more of a surprise.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Shamans** were a faction mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Supposed denizens of another world, the shamans were a tribe of silver-haired Numen women who followed the Grandmother, a matriarch who grafted her body into a tree. Seldom born, they possessed long lifespans and a physical and spiritual affinity for trees. They settled in the Hinterland of the Lands Between, near the Finger Ruins of Dheo, and filled their Shaman Village with many-colored flowers.

After the hornsent discovered that their flesh was special for its power to meld harmoniously with that of others., they condemned the shamans to a ritual of rebirth, through which their unwanted were supposed to be remade into well-behaving people. The shamans were systematically captured, tortured, butchered, and stuffed into pots with many others at the Bonny Village. Rancorous spirits clung to their pinkish-red, twitching meat, which coalesced into Jar Dwellers.

In time, Marika was born in the Shaman Village. She was later recognized as an Empyrean by the Two Fingers, who gifted a Shadowbound Beast: her half-brother Maliketh. Marika left her home to fulfill her fate. However, after her acquisition of the Elden Ring and ascension to godhood, she returned to find her village abandoned and empty. She cut off one of her braids in offering to the Grandmother, and bathed her home in healing gold, though she knew that none remained to be healed. She never returned again.

sections.text:

- Jar Dwellers

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Marika's descendants, the demigods of the Golden Lineage or the progeny she had with her other self, share her affinity for grafting.
  - Godefroy the Grafted and Godrick the Grafted pursued strength by grafting others onto their bodies.
  - Miquella of the Haligtree was able to graft his body inside his Haligtree like the Shaman's Grandmother.
- The Shamans may have a cultural connection with the Dominula Dancers, who skin others and harvest their runes with ceremonial bone weapons.
  - The many-colored flower fields around the Shaman Village are reminiscent of those near Dominula, Windmill Village.
  - Blessed Bone Shards are found in a wood outside the Shaman Village.
  - The pagan Dominula Festival was old enough for Queen Marika to tacitly tolerate. Warrior priests who fought in the Crusade spread the recipe for Festive Grease: tree resin mixed with human bones.
- Through their cultural connection with Dominula, Shamans may be connected to serpent deities.
  - Marika wore golden snake bracelets.
  - A shed skin resembling that of the God-Devouring Serpent is also found in Bonny Village, close to a headless corpse resembling that of the Grandmother of the Shaman Village.
  - Women with the same traditional clothes of the women of Dominula Village are found in the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir, where an old religion once offered sacrifices to the God Devouring Serpent.

sections.text: **Shifting Earth** is a gameplay feature in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
<section begin="Shifting Earth"/>Shifting Earth events are semi-random Expedition modifiers that drastically alter the landscape of Limveld. Each one replaces part of the map with a sprawling new location filled with enemies, bosses, and valuable treasures. These changes are static and remain consistent across Expeditions.

Shifting Earth events are unlocked by defeating the Nightlords or by advancing select Remembrance quests. Once unlocked, they are cycled by defeating the Nightlords. Events persist for several runs before fading on their own, though they can also be skipped early by resting in the bed at the Roundtable Hold and choosing to pass time. The active event is displayed when launching an Expedition.

The **four** possible Shifting Earth events spawn the following locations:
- Shifting Earth: The Crater
- Shifting Earth: Mountaintop
- Shifting Earth: Rotted Woods
- Shifting Earth: Noklateo, the Shrouded City
- Shifting Earth: The Great Hollow (upcoming DLC content)<section end="Shifting Earth"/>

sections.text: **Sap**, also known as **amber**, **dew**, **tears**, and **resin**, is a material in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The blessed golden sap of the Erdtree and Scadutree fell like tears from its boughs, and were used to spread the faith. Sap hardened into Crystal Tears or amber,which was regarded as the most precious of jewels during the age of Plenty. Godfrey accepted the sap stoically, without any sign of wavering, when he became Queen Marika's first Elden Lord.

The Stars produced arcane dew, which accumulated in basins or upon flora. The ancient Rauh civilization used it in sprite medicine. The Eternal Cities used a primordial drop of this silver dew to create the synthetic Albinaurics.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Sea of Fog** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Sea of Fog is a vast body of water separating the Lands Between from other lands. Lord Godfrey and his Tarnished warriors crossed the sea by ship following their banishment on the Long March. They sailed to the Badlands and other unseen realms to wage war and die. The call of long-lost grace beckoned them to return for the Elden Ring after the Shattering war concluded without a clear victor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The proper name **Sea of Fog** comes from Cut Content.
- The Sea of Fog also surrounds Limveld and the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Lord Radagon foretold the Tarnisheds' return across the Sea of Fog in .

sections.text:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Smithing** is a concept in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Blacksmithing was said to have originated among the Giants in ancient times, who saw in the anvil the shape of an altar. Miners bored out Tunnels in search of Smithing Stones to strengthen armaments. Gas Stones were once used as fuel for the smithing process at old forges, where smiths read the script they perceived in the wrinkles of molten steel to imbue weapons with souls.

Taylew the Golem Smith became the guardian deity of smithing.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Tarnished** (褪せ人, *Asebito*; lit. "Faded Ones/People") are a faction in Elden Ring. The player character, the Tarnished, is a member of this group.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Tarnished are individuals who lost the grace of the Erdtree and were consequently banished from the Lands Between by Queen Marika the Eternal. Following the breaking of the Elden Ring, the Tarnished were beckoned by lost grace, fragmentary divine light from the Erdtree, to return.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In the early age of the Erdtree, Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, fought many battles throughout the Lands Between. He led the War Against the Giants, and defeated the Storm Lord. When his last enemy fell, it is said that the hue of his eyes faded. Queen Marika addressed Godfrey and his warriors as she divested them of their Grace, commanding them to leave the Lands Between and travel to a faraway land, where they would wage war and die. She promised them that, after their deaths, their Grace would be given back, and that they would return to the Lands Between once again, to wage war and brandish the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: The Long March
sections.text:
Godfrey and his kinfolk  were banished from the Lands Between, beginning an exodus referred to as the Long March. They left their home on boats, although one was said to have been left behind. The warriors who accompanied Godfrey honored him by wielding axes, although Godfrey's own axe was broken in battle during the course of the march. When the Long March came to an end, Godfrey divested himself of kingship and became a simple warrior once more. As Hoarah Loux, he became a chieftain of the Badlands, revered by its bravest warriors.

The Tarnished settled in lands outside the Lands Between, and bore descendants who were also Tarnished. As Queen Marika had commanded them, the Tarnished lived and died in these distant lands.

sections.heading: Return to the Lands Between
sections.text:
A long time after the Tarnished left the Lands Between, the Elden Ring was shattered and Queen Marika disappeared. Marika's offspring, the Demigods, claimed shards of the Elden Ring. Tainted by their newfound strength, the Demigods warred in the Shattering, causing the Greater Will to abandon them. With the war yielding no victor, the Guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who returned from the dead and went back to the Lands Between, guided by Grace. Upon setting foot in the Lands Between once more, the Tarnished received the aid of the Two Fingers, who bid them to seek the Great Runes possessed by the Demigods so as to restore the Golden Order and become Elden Lord. The Tarnished, given life by Grace, gained a form of immortality,, allowing them to return from the dead over and over on their quest to become Elden Lord.

The Guidance of Grace brought together the Tarnished and their Finger Maidens, women in the service of the Two Fingers who were tasked with serving their appointed Tarnished. The Finger Maidens would offer guidance and aid to the Tarnished, as well as turning the Runes they gathered into strength.

sections.heading: Table of Lost Grace
Game events
sections.text:
This would change when a Tarnished of no renown crossed the fog and entered the Lands Between. Unlike others, this Tarnished did not meet a Finger Maiden to guide them, but was instead chosen by Torrent, the spectral steed, and Melina, a mysterious woman bound to Grace. Melina provided them with the Sacred Flasks and offered to serve as their maiden, aiding them by turning their Runes into strength. She extended an invitation to the Table of Lost Grace and bestowed the Spectral Steed Whistle to summon Torrent.

This Tarnished gained an audience with the Two Fingers, claimed the Great Runes, and journeyed to the Erdtree to brandish the Elden Ring and become the Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Stormveil Castle** is a legacy dungeon located in Limgrave.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Stormveil Castle perches atop a cliff overlooking Limgrave. Currently, it is the stronghold of the Demigod Godrick the Grafted, but long ago it was ruled over by an old king, back when the true storm raged. The castle is heavily guarded and patrolled by Banished Knights, Exile Soldiers, and warhawks with blades grafted to their talons. The exterior of the castle is mottled with craters lined with thorns, which have also spread to the soldiers within. It is said that the source may be hidden deep within the castle.

sections.heading: Stormveil Main Gate
sections.text: Found after Margit, the Fell Omen, in front of the main gate.

sections.heading: Gateside Chamber
sections.text: Found on the other side of the main gate. From the gate, go up the path, and then turn left and double back. The Site of Grace is through the door.

sections.heading: Stormveil Cliffside
sections.text: On the cliffs on the south-western side of the castle. Found by taking the secret passage past Gatekeeper Gostoc's room.

sections.heading: Rampart Tower
sections.text: Found after re-entering the castle from the secret passage and going up the lift from the room with the Banished Knight. The Site of Grace is in a room to the north after stepping off the lift.

sections.heading: Liftside Chamber
sections.text: In a small room found after climbing the steps past the Omen in the central courtyard.

sections.heading: Secluded Cell
sections.text: In a small room just before Godrick's boss room.

sections.heading: Godrick the Grafted
sections.text: Found in the boss room. Appears after Godrick the Grafted has been defeated.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Smoldering Butterfly** is a Crafting Material in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Smoldering Butterflies are harvested in abundance throughout the Lands Between:
- They are almost always found at campfires and bonfires.
  - Near Bloody Finger Hunter Yura
  - Near Nomadic Merchants
  - On the burning pile of bodies in Castle Morne's courtyard
- They swarm wildfires and Fire Slugs.
  - North of Warmaster's Shack is a swarm around 2 Slugs.
  - Southwest of the  Eastern Tableland Site of Grace in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes is a Fire Monk camp that contains the gesture "Fire Spur Me". In the nearby area are 3 swarms of Butterflies.

Dropped by various enemies:
- Exile Soldiers
- Fire Slugs
- Guilty Sorcerer
- Enemies that carry Torchpoles or throw Fire Pots

They are a common minor loot item in Limgrave, Stormhill, and Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: , also known as **General Radahn**, the **Red Lion General**, and later as **Promised Consort Radahn** and **Radahn, Consort of Miquella**, is an optional Demigod boss in Elden Ring and a mandatory God boss in Elden Ring:;Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: General Radahn was feared as the strongest Demigod during the Shattering. This Shardbearer must be defeated to access the Realm of Shadow and achieve the "Age of the Stars" ending.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Red-maned Radahn was the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala of the Full Moon, head of both the Carian royal family and Academy of Raya Lucaria, born after the Second Liurnian War. He had two siblings, Rykard and Ranni. Radahn inherited his father's flaming red hair and was fond of its heroic implications. From a young age, he was enamored with the Elden Lord Godfrey. Attempting to emulate his idol, Radahn adorned his armor with lions, the symbol of Godfrey and Serosh.

At some point, the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, was robbed of grace and hounded from the Lands Between. Radahn's father, Radagon, left Rennala to become Queen Marika's new consort and the second Elden Lord. Radahn and his siblings were thus raised to demigod status by their new step-mother, Marika.

In their youth, Radahn's Empyrean half-brother Miquella deeply admired him for his kindness and strength, seeing in him the qualities of a lord. When he decided to pursue godhood, he made a vow with Radahn that, upon his deific return, he would take Radahn as his consort. In return, Miquella would uphold some unspecified part of the vow.

Not wanting to abandon his scrawny but beloved steed, Leonard, Radahn studied gravitational magic in Sellia under a master who was an Alabaster Lord. Radahn befriended the Albinauric Gaius, a senior disciple of his teacher, and the two formed a competitive yet friendly rivalry. Radahn's step-brother Messmer the Impaler was also friends with Gaius, and the two became as elder brothers to Radahn.

Mastering gravitational magic allowed Radahn to manipulate the forces of gravity and challenge the stars themselves. During the Starscourge Conflict, Radahn saved Sellia by conquering the stars and arrested their cycles, delaying fate. Having earned himself the moniker "Starscourge," he engraved the gravity crest upon his blades.

Radahn's soldiers were known as the Redmanes for the red-maned lion raising a sword in the image of Radahn on their surcoats. The longest serving of the Redmane Knights was Ogha, who studied gravitational techniques alongside Radahn in Sellia. It was popularly said that the Redmanes knew no weakness. At an unknown period in time, Jerren, a guest of the Carian royals, became a guest commander for Radahn's armies, and they swore a mutual oath of honorable death. During his youth, Radahn witnessed the valor of a gladiator called Freyja, who he asked to become another member of his knights; an offer Freyja accepted.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.text:
At some point following the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, and her offspring acquired the Great Runes. The maddening taint of their newfound strength led to the Shattering, a war between Marika's demigod descendants, each seeking to become the new ruler of the Lands Between.

From his stronghold of Redmane Castle in the Caelid Wilds, Radahn led his armies against the forces of the other demigods. Radahn tried to challenge Godrick the Grafted in Limgrave, but the latter hid in Stormveil Castle.

By the end of the Shattering, only Radahn and his half-sister Malenia, Blade of Miquella were left standing. The two fought to a stalemate in the Battle of Aeonia, their duel ending inconclusively when Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot. As the Scarlet Aeonia flower blossomed, Malenia whispered in Radahn's ear, *"Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."*

The Scarlet Rot ravaged Caelid and consumed Radahn from the inside, eating away at his psyche but failing to kill him. Following the Battle of Aeonia, Radahn roams the Wailing Dunes as a mindless beast who devours the flesh of friend and foe alike, howling at the sky. Without their commander, the Redmane Knights burned the crest on the left breast of their armor to indicate their resolve not to return home, and to serve as a bulwark against the spread of the rot in Caelid using fire.

Despite his madness, Radahn continues to ride his scrawny steed, as well as halt the motions of the stars. The Radahn Festival has been organized by his men in Castle Redmane to celebrate his last battle. It is a gathering of mighty warriors who might finally put the General out of his misery and claim his Great Rune for themselves. The festival serves as Jerren's way of fulfilling his oath of honorable death to Radahn.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.text: Upon the participation of a Tarnished Champion, the Radahn Festival is a success, and Radahn is freed from his tortured existence. His death causes the stars to resume their cycles, some of which come crashing down upon the Lands Between. One such falling star lands in Limgrave, opening the path to Nokron, Eternal City, and allowing the fate of Ranni the Witch to progress.

sections.heading: Shadow of the Erdtree
sections.text: Following Radahn's defeat, his soul met its end. However, Miquella sought to revive it, still desiring for Radahn to be his lord consort. Miquella successfully revived Radahn, placing his soul into a vessel made from the remains of Mohg, Lord of Blood, another Demigod slain by the same Tarnished who had defeated Radahn. The Tarnished encounters the newly-resurrected Radahn at the Gate of Divinity at the top of Enir-Ilim. Radahn stands guard as Miquella completes his ascension to godhood and battles the Tarnished once more. During the ensuing battle, Miquella steps out of the Gate of Divinity and embraces Radahn as his consort and fights the Tarnished with Radahn. The Tarnished triumphs over Radahn and Miquella, thus preventing Miquella's age of compassion.

sections.heading: First Encounter (Starscourge Radahn)
sections.text:
The fight against Starscourge Radahn only becomes available when the Radahn Festival commences. This requires the player to either activate a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, talk to Blaidd the Half-Wolf about Radahn in Siofra River, or talk to War Counselor Iji about Jerren.

Torrent can be called during this fight and is useful for closing distance and evading Radahn's ranged attacks.

Multiple NPCs are available to be summoned during the fight, and their summons can be located throughout the arena. Six can be summoned at a time, and once a summon sign is used it will vanish, however each NPC has multiple summon signs that can be used.

The following nine champions are available:

- Alexander, Warrior Jar
- Blaidd the Half-Wolf
- Castellan Jerren (phase 2 only)
- Finger Maiden Therolina
- Great Horned Tragoth
- Knight Leontiel (Tarnished Pack)
- Lionel the Lionhearted
- Okina
- Patches (disconnects after arrival)

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The player will spawn some distance away from Radahn, with the boss visible at the top of a dune in the distance. Immediately, Radahn will begin firing volleys of arrows which rain down from above, homing in on the player, as well as gravity arrows. The latter can be avoided by hiding behind the clusters of weapons dug into the ground, however the weapons will break when struck. Riding Torrent will make it easier to avoid the volleys. Summon signs can be found in clusters all around the arena, and can be used to summon NPCs to assist in the fight.

Once the player is close enough, Radahn will begin attacking using his swords. He is very mobile, using his horse to cover distance easily. He also uses a number of gravity-based attacks, such as Cragblade, gravity waves, and Collapsing Stars.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: Once his health is below 50%, Radahn will launch himself into the sky, disappearing for several seconds. He will then come crashing down in a ball of fire, dealing devastating damage to anyone caught in the impact. Radahn now gains the ability to raise four floating rocks, which will hover beside him and then launch at the player or their summons. He also gains the ability to float into the air and spin rapidly while charging.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The Wailing Dunes is a very large arena consisting of many tall dunes, with Radahn initially standing at the top of the largest dune close to the centre of the area. Clusters of weapons can be found stuck in the sand, and can be used to hide from Radahn's arrows. Summon signs can be found throughout the arena, often in clusters of two or three.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: - During the first encounter, Radahn can be defeated by luring him to the cliffs in the far north, causing him to fall to his death. Alternatively, players can position themselves at the southern shore during his phase transition, leading Radahn to crash into the ocean upon descent.

sections.heading: Second Encounter (Promised Consort Radahn)
sections.text: The second encounter with Radahn serves as the final boss of the *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree* expansion. The first phase is **Promised Consort Radahn** and the second is **Radahn, Consort of Miquella**.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Just like in the base game, players will spawn a distance away from Radahn. While retaining his gravity magic, and as his soul now possessed Mohg's remains, Radahn now employs Bloodflame, and seamlessly switches between the two elemental magics while in combat. To defeat him, it is always important to time your attacks in between Radahn's string of attacks or pull off counters at the very end of a combo. Because of his recovery time, this makes his boss battle complicated, as he can launch other attacks almost instantly after finishing a heavy attack. As a result, it is important to note that patience and appropriate timing are the keys to defeating Radahn. The optimal moment to attack is when he finished his basic sword combos, and would take a brief pause to recover.

At the start of his boss battle, he will nearly always use a gravity attack to prevent players from summoning or buffs upon entry into the boss battle. Because of this, players are recommended to use buffs before accessing the boss and cast summons right after dodging the initial attack. During his first phase, Radahn will use a flurry of combos aside from special abilities such as a Bloodflame Slash and his Gravity attacks. After being reduced to 65% of his health, this will trigger a cutscene leading to Phase 2.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
In this phase, Radahn's previous attacks are improved and he gains new powerful abilities. Most of them are Holy-powered and have a wider AoE. Overall, while his attacks become more lethal, Radahn is now faster in speed, now capable of creating mirror images to attack and using strong Holy-based abilities, making the boss battle more difficult and challenging. However, despite gaining immense power, Radahn's health has already been reduced to 75%, allowing players to gain a slight edge. It is important to capitalize on the pauses of Radahn's combo attacks, as there are opportunities to strike. Constantly taking advantage of them can deplete his health and because Radahn's attacks can be very punishing if caught off-guard, you have to be prepared to switch between offensive and defensive at times.

While Radahn can still perform similar combos from Phase 1, they have an additional Holy damage explosion at the end. As Miquella is now mounted on his back, he can do a grab attack where he will glow and jump at the player in order to grab them. If successful, Radahn will bring them close to Miquella, who will then place the player under a charm. While this doesn't deal any damage, if Radahn successfully grabs the player a second time while they are charmed, this will ultimately result in instant death. Using Miquella's Great Rune will undo the charm.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: The arena consists of a very wide area, with a rough white surface filled with gray-white decomposed corpses, which can be found sticking from the ground. At the other end of the arena, stands the Gate of Divinity itself, where Miquella will step out in divine aspect in the second phase.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- General Radahn and his foot soldiers engaged Margit, the Fell Omen during an undisclosed battle of the Shattering.
- Starscourge Radahn's feet have been eaten away by the scarlet rot.
- Promised Consort Radahn has Omen horns and casts Blood Oath Incantations because he inhabits Mohg's body.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Radahn is the only Shardbearer boss with no spoken dialogue or cinematic introduction immediately before his battle (excluding the cutscene triggered by speaking with Castellan Jerren) or during his phase transition.
  - Although Radahn remains silent in the DLC, unused voice lines suggest he once had an introductory monologue.
- The  description of the Longtail Cat Talisman referenced Radahn owning a pet cat, though this detail was later removed.
- Hidetaka Miyazaki has cited Radahn's first battle as his personal favorite boss fight, praising the character's design and the duel's bittersweet tone.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sorcerer Rogier** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He is first encountered as an optional summon against Margit, the Fell Omen, and is later found within a church searching for knowledge in Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
A Tarnished dedicated to investigating the fateful Night of Black Knives, Rogier familiarized himself with D, Hunter of the Dead and Fia, Deathbed Companion at the Roundtable Hold. He and Fia discussed at length the Black Knifeprints left by the Black Knife Assassin. He hasn't seen the Guidance of Grace for a long time.

He later left the Hold to search for clues at Stormveil Castle, where he offered to teach the Tarnished his magical combat arts, warning them of Godrick's Tarnished hunters. While exploring the lower reaches of the castle, Rogier discovered a cadaver of the Prince of Death and was infected with Death Blight.

Back at the Roundtable and immobilized by his condition, Rogier imparted his knowledge of the plot and Those Lost in Death to the Tarnished. If Rogier receives a Black Knifeprint from the Tarnished, he deduces that the one who enchanted the assassins' weapons was Ranni the Witch. He urges the Tarnished to seek Ranni and enter her service in order to learn more. However, he soon succumbs to the Deathroot, leaving behind a note informing the Tarnished of the whereabouts of D's inseparable twin, Devin.

Fia later summons Rogier as one of her Champions at the Prince of Death's Throne in Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Stormveil Castle
  - *(Optional)* Exhaust his dialogue in Stormveil Castle encounter. He can be found in the chapel past the Rampart Tower Site of Grace.
  - Witness his bloodstain after killing the Ulcerated Tree Spirit in the lower section of Stormveil Castle. Doing so before defeating Godrick will cause him to disappear from Stormveil, regardless of whether you have done step 1.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Meet him at Roundtable Hold after defeating Godrick. Tell him that you have defeated Godrick and then ask about the corpse below Stormveil.
  - Speak to Fia to learn about the Black Knifeprint.
1. Black Knife Catacombs
  - Obtain the Black Knifeprint from the wounded Black Knife Assassin in Black Knife Catacombs in Liurnia.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Give Rogier the Black Knifeprint.
  - *(Optional)* Ask Fia about Rogier.
  - Reload the area and speak to Rogier. He will ask you to investigate Ranni.
1. Three Sisters (Ranni's Rise)
  - Head to Ranni's Rise and speak to Ranni. She will be dismissive and ask you to leave.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Return to Roundtable Hold and tell Rogier about Ranni. He will ask that you enter her service to further the investigation.
1. Three Sisters (Ranni's Rise)
  - Return to Ranni's Rise and agree to serve Ranni.
1. Roundtable Hold
  - Return to Roundtable Hold and speak to Rogier. He will tell you that his condition is worsening.
  - Reload the area and Rogier will be unresponsive. Any unseen dialogue options will be locked and his shop will be unavailable.
  - Reload the area again and Rogier will be dead, leaving behind his gear, bell bearing and a letter.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Spellblade's Pointed Hat marks Rogier as a heretical sorcerer and features a light-blue feather, likely plucked from a Glintstone Dragon or Gravebird.
- Rogier foreshadows the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince.

**Spells** in Elden Ring come in two types: sorceries and incantations.

Spells are equipped at Sites of Grace. Each spell takes up one or more Memory Slots, the number of which may be increased by collecting Memory Stones.

Casting spells requires a catalyst and consumes FP and Stamina, unless noted otherwise.

Note, for the on-weapon enchantments to work such as Poison Armament, the weapon you intend to enchant needs to be active in the right hand and the spellcasting implement active in the left, and then the enchantment can be cast.

sections.text: The **Stranded Graveyard** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
After their death at the Chapel of Anticipation, the Tarnished washed up in the Stranded Graveyard, where they are chosen by Torrent and Melina to receive the Sacred Flasks.

The Stranded Graveyard is a small, damp cavern filled with coffins below the Fringefolk Hero's Grave in Limgrave. It contains a small illusory tree and the deeper Cave of Knowledge. Fringefolk Hero's Grave is also accessed from this area, the entrance to which is locked by an imp statue requiring a Stonesword Key.

The cave may be reached by descending the elevator at the Fringefolk Hero's Grave and passing through a large door. It may also be accessed from a beach on the southwestern coast of Limgrave, where the Haligdrake Talisman can be picked up.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sorceress Sellen** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring. She is initially found in Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave and is eager to share her glintstone sorceries.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Sellen was considered to be the most promising glintstone sorceress to ever attend the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Her first teacher at the academy was the sorcerer Azur, one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and originator of the Karolos Conspectus. Azur, along with Lusat, was banished from the academy due to their study of the Primeval Current, a study Sellen wished to pursue. However, following accusations of unspeakable treatment of her fellow scholars under the name of the Graven Witch, Sellen too was expelled from the academy. Sellen had sought to restore the Primeval Current, desiring glintstone sorceries unbound by terrestrial taboos and the pedantry of the Carian Royal Family.

Sellen was also an acquaintance of Preceptor Seluvis, and a frequent visitor to his underground cellar, where he kept his collection of puppets. When Sellen was expelled, Seluvis helped her in some capacity, for which she owes him.

At some point following her banishment, Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, bound by the Academy's shackles. She managed to manifest a projection of herself in the Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave. It is here that she meets the Tarnished, who becomes her apprentice, learning glintstone sorceries from her. When she learns that the Tarnished has found Master Azur on Mt. Gelmir, she requests that they seek out Master Lusat, speculating that he returned to his home of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. The Tarnished discovers Lusat, in a near-inorganic state much like Azur, in Sellia Hideaway, and reports back to Sellen.

sections.heading: Freeing Sellen
sections.text:
Much like Ranni the Witch, Sellen's fate is tied to the stars, and with the defeat of Starscourge Radahn, Sellen becomes dispossessed of her immortality. This makes her a target of Jerren, a friend of the Carian Royal Family who once made a promise to exterminate the witch. Sellen reveals to the Tarnished that the form they have been speaking to is a projection, and that her true body resides in Witchbane Ruins. The Tarnished meets with Sellen's true body, shackled in the ruin's cellar, and she asks them to remove her Primal Glintstone, beseeching them to look after it. Jerren arrives to find Sellen's previous body already perished. The Tarnished later places Sellen's Primal Glintstone into a puppet in Seluvis's basement, which bears a striking resemblance to Sellen's old body.

Sellen, now in her new, more youthful body, returns to the Academy and displaces Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. She has the bodies of Azur and Lusat moved back to the Academy, so that she can finally hone the Primeval Current. She offers her support to the Tarnished in their mission to become Elden Lord, and requests that when the time comes, they illuminate her about the secrets of life which course the Elden Ring Before long, however, Jerren finally catches up to her.  Should the Tarnished aid her in beating back Jerren, she will continue her research. When the Tarnished next sees her, she has transformed into a Graven Mass.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.text:
1. Waypoint Ruins
  - Sellen can be found in the cellar of Waypoint Ruins after defeating the Mad Pumpkin Head. Talk to Sellen and then select "I wish to learn glintstone sorceries" to receive the "Nod in Thought" Gesture, and to unlock her sorcery shop.
  - *(Optional)* If the Radahn Festival has not commenced, Sellen will have dialogue about it if you have Seluvis's Introduction in your inventory. This is obtained by progressing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline and speaking to Seluvis about Nokron prior to initiating the Festival.
1. Waypoint Ruins
  - Find Primeval Sorcerer Azur, located beyond the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir, to obtain Comet Azur. Return to Sellen and select the "Show Azur's Sorcery" dialogue option. After listening to this dialogue, select the "Tell me your story" option, and then select "Let us journey together". Next, select "I have a favor to ask" to obtain the Sellian Sealbreaker.
  - The Sellian Sealbreaker can be used to open a sealed tunnel in Sellia Hideaway, behind which is Primeval Sorcerer Lusat. Interact with him to receive Stars of Ruin. It is now possible to select the "Lusat's location" dialogue option when talking to Sellen, which will reward you with a Starlight Shards. This option can be avoided until later in the questline.
1. Witchbane Ruins
  - After Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, talk to Sellen to learn that her true body is in Witchbane Ruins. Travel there and speak to the shackled Sellen to obtain Sellen's Primal Glintstone.
  - Reload the area and return to find Castellan Jerren. In order for him to appear, you must have spoken to him in Redmane Castle after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
1. Three Sisters
  - Travel to the Three Sisters and go to the ruined structure north-east of Ranni's Rise. Roll or attack the ground to reveal a hidden staircase leading to a basement full of immobile puppets. Pass through the illusory wall on the far end of the room to find a puppet duplicate of Sellen. Interact with the puppet to insert Sellen's Primal Glintstone, resurrecting Sellen in her new body.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
  - There will now be two summon signs outside the door to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library; one red and one gold. To progress Sellen's questline, select the gold summon sign. You will be summoned as a co-operator to assist Sellen in defeating Witch-Hunter Jerren. Defeat Jerren to receive the Eccentric's Set.
  - This step can only be completed if Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon has been defeated.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
  - After defeating Jerren, Sellen can be found where Rennala is usually based. Speak to her to receive the Glintstone Kris. If you have not done so already, find Primeval Sorcerer Lusat in Sellia Hideaway and speak to Sellen to select "Lusat's location" and receive Starlight Shards.
  - It is also possible to obtain Azur and Lusat's armour sets by returning to their respective locations at this point.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
  - Reload the area after telling Sellen about Lusat. Sellen, now in the form of a Graven Mass, can be found  to the side of the room. The Witch's Glintstone Crown can be obtained here. It is still possible to purchase sorceries from her and to offer her scrolls.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Portraits of Sellen are hung around the Academy of Raya Lucaria, notably the Debate Parlor.
- Sellen may be summoned as a cooperator against the Red Wolf of Radagon if her Primal Glintstone has been inserted in the doll body from Seluvis's Cellar. Given that this requires both reaching the top of Mt. Gelmir and defeating Starscourge Radahn before you have made significant progress in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, this is rather unlikely to happen naturally.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Sellen's body in the Waypoint Ruins and the doll body in Seluvis's cellar have some differences, with the doll body having a smaller head as well as paler skin and its hair is brown instead of the original's black hair.
- Per the description of the Primal Glintstone Blade, sorcerers would slice open their hearts to imbue primal glintstone with their soul, killing them. As Sellen is already in possession of a Primal Glintstone, it is possible that she has already died, and that the body imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins is not her original body.
- Both Sellens in Limgrave are protected by enemies that bring down a cascade of energy. The Miranda Blossom at Waypoint Ruins calls down Holy light, while the Graven Mass at Witchbane Ruins triggers a cascade of starry Magic.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sword of Night and Flame** is a Legendary melee armament and straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
In a locked room at Caria Manor, Liurnia of the Lakes, which the Tarnished can jump into from above on the walkways where the Raya Lucaria Soldier puppets appear.

More specifically, starting from the Manor Lower Level Site of Grace walk out onto the stone walkways and take a left when they path splits in two. Follow the path as it turn to the right and look to the left when halfway across the last walkway. Search for a nearby roof to jump onto and then walk forward to find another roof further down. In one of the corners should be a ladder leading down into the inside of a tower with a chest containing the sword as well as a door leading outside.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- This weapon possess one of the strongest skills in the game, Night-and-Flame Stance. While holding the stance, the user is able to perform either a miniature Comet Azur with a light attack or a flame wave resembling the skill Flame of the Redmanes with a heavy attack.
  - Since both Magic damage and Fire damage have specialized ways to increase their damage (their respective Shrouding Cracked Tear, as well as Terra Magica for Magic and Flame, Grant Me Strength for Fire) it may be best to think ahead and try to specialize if you are about to challenge a touch foe or boss.
- One of the main weaknesses of this weapon is the relative lack of other equipment that scales well with both Intelligence and Faith, which pretty much only the Golden Order Seal being a strong option. The Prince of Death's Staff (and the much harder to get Gelmir Glintstone Staff) has rather subpar returns for Sorcery Scaling when the two stats are below 60, making it only relatively good with Death Sorceries and rather bad with everything else.
- It's possible to invest primarily in only one of the two stats, but it's ill-advised to do this beyond the early and early-to-mid sections of the game. This is because, while doing so lets you potentially hyper-specialize in one of the attacks and more easily overcome flat defences early on, it will also lock you into one element, and both the sword's own damage and the skill's damage doesn't scales all that well past 54 in the associated stat.
- Just meeting the sword's requirements means that you will have the Intelligence to cast the Magic-boosting Terra Magic and the Fire-boosting Flame, Grant Me Strength, and just 1 more points in Faith will let the wielder cast the Golden Vow spell (which also boosts the skill since it's based of weapon Attack Power).

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Despite the skill's description that the light attack follow-up casts Night Comet it actually casts Comet Azur.
- Patch 1.07 increased attack power, the attack direction may now be adjusted up and down when using a normal attack, added damage detection to the weapon part.
  - This is in regard to the skill.
  - Increased the damage of the light attack follow-up from 100%, 150%, and 180% of weapon Magic Attack Power (1,180% in total) to 108%, 162%, and 194% of Magic Attack Power (1,274% in total).
  - Increased the damage of the heavy attack follow-up from 700% of weapon Fire Attack Power to 800% of Fire Attack Power.
- Patch 1.03 decreased weapon skill, Sword of Night and Flame’s damage.
- The Chinese and Korean  release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "*A magical sword forged to celebrate Rennala's wedding. The cold crystal symbolizing the Queen of Raya Lucaria and the Giantsflame symbolizing her husband, Radagon, are enshrined on each side of the blade.*"

At the same time, the Intelligence-scaling is largely useless due to being the weakest scaling (maxing out at 36% versus Strength's 50% and Dexterity's 72%) and scaling the much, much weaker Magic damage.
  - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 542 AP, 80 Dexterity grants 533 AP, and 45 Dexterity and 45 Intelligence grants 490 AP.
  - While it can technically match the strongest Keen Straight Swords (Longsword and Broadsword) in terms of pure Attack Power, the fact that a considerable part of that is Magic damage (about 20% on a pure Dexterity build) hampers the damage a bit.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Scholar** is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign, one of the two playable Nightfarer classes included in the  DLC.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Scholar is the perfect choice for a precise and technical playstyle. He specializes in crowd control, debuffs, and team utility, making him especially valuable in coordinated group play.

Scholar favors Thrusting Swords, which focus on pokes, counters, and spacing rather than brute force, and they synergize extremely well with his presumed reliance on Arcane as his highest stat. His movement also appears more refined than most Nightfarers, incorporating smooth sidesteps, backstep feints, and flowing motion chains that allow him to control distance while maintaining pressure.

Much like the Executor, Scholar appears to benefit heavily from status effects—however, he applies them differently. For example, pairing his Arcane scaling with a weapon like the Antspur Rapier (which applies Scarlet Rot) could lead to highly efficient status infliction across multiple enemies, especially when combined with his unique skills.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text: Stats displayed below are for character at level 15.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.text:
Bagcraft — *"Store additional resources. Level up the power or effect of items by using them."*

Increased item stack limit for consumable Tools, which can be leveled up twice during an Expedition. The Scholar can level up items by repeatedly using the item. Leveling up doesn't focus on individual items but instead on the item category. For example, if a player frequently uses a throwable pot, all throwable pots will benefit from the effect.

Increased stack limits for consumable Tools, which can be upgraded twice during an Expedition. The Scholar upgrades items through repeated use, and upgrades apply to the whole item category. If a player often uses a Throwing Pot, every Throwable Pot becomes stronger.

**Bagcraft**
- Item-handling level up [2] - Improves the effectiveness.
- Item-handling level up [3] -  Adds a secondary effect to the item.

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.text:
Analyze — *"Study your enemies. The longer you observe, the better your combat advantage."*

The Scholar's awareness and ability to make observations on the battlefield are his primary strengths. **Analyze** applies debuffs to enemies and buffs to himself and nearby allies. Activating the ability creates a large circle that marks all targets inside it. Focusing on a target triggers a red gauge that fills over time; the longer the analysis, the stronger the resulting buff or debuff. Once the indicator is complete, press the assigned button to apply the effect.

Analysis speed is distance-based: close targets fill quickly, while distant ones take longer. The Scholar is exposed during this process because he lowers his weapon, so the skill is safest to use when enemies are not pressuring him.

- Best used when multiple targets are lined up on-screen, including enemies and allies.

**Analyze Buff and Debuff Effects**
- Level 1 Buff - Increased Stamina
- Level 3 Buff - Conjure a shield that releases a shockwave when hit.
- Level 1 Debuff - Decreases attack.
- Level 3 Debuff - Take extra damage on the next hit received.

sections.heading: Ultimate Art
sections.text:
Communion — *"Taboo Knowledge: Damage is shared by linked enemies and can heal threaded allies."*

The Scholar's ultimate ability binds together all nearby foes and allies in an area of effect. Any damage inflicted on one linked enemy is mirrored across all others. For allies, each connected member benefits from any single source of healing.

- The Scholar is invulnerable to damage while casting Communion.
- Most effective against clustered enemies and multi-target bosses to enhance both damage output.
- Most effective when cast on both allies, significantly boosting team survivability.

sections.text: The **Sealing Tree** is an object in Elden Ring, included in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Sealing Tree in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh generates the thorns and shadows that shroud Enir-Ilim, the hornsents' sacred spiral tower. Queen Marika placed this seal to bar any other Empyrean from accessing the Gate of Divinity. It can be burned only with the Kindling of her Demigod son, Messmer the Impaler.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Sealing Tree stands on an unenclosed stone platform that extends from the Church of the Bud in western Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Romina, Saint of the Bud blocks the path to the tree and must be defeated to progress.
