  - The player Tarnished warps to Enir-Ilim.
  - A ladder in the  Theatre of the Divine Beast allows access to a secret section of Enir-Ilim.

sections.heading: Note
sections.text:
- The Sealing Tree is identical in form to the twisted Scadutree trunk, though much smaller in scale.
- Burning the Sealing Trees is similar to the Cardinal Sin. Both actions transport the player to a previously inaccessible area where it is permanently daytime, clear away thorns, and inaugurate new Ages and Elden Lords. As with the Sealing Tree, the Erdtree can burn only with special kindling—a maiden who bears a vision of fire. Finger Maiden Hyetta and Melina, Messmer's younger sister who presently exists in spirit form, can commit the Cardinal Sin.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Silver** is a metal associated with Arcane power in Elden Ring. It is closely tied to the Night and the artificial and mutable forms of life connected to the Eternal Cities, including Silver Tears and Albinaurics, as well as concepts of rebirth, mimicry, and hidden wealth.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
]]

A blessing believed to have invited riches, silver was valued in the Lands Between for its practical and mystical properties. It was used by many factions to forge a wide range of armor, weapons, and sacred objects throughout the ages.

The Nox of the Eternal Cities used silver to create artificial lifeforms. Silver Tears were formless creatures that mimicked objects and other living things. Although their liquid metal bodies could be tempered into flowing weapons, silver tears had wills of their own. Like Silver Tears, Albinaurics were arcane creatures that possessed silvery cores housing their life essence.

Silver mist also had life-sapping properties, as utilized by Nox Nightmaidens.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Terra Magica** is a spell in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Creates a large, stationary sigil inside of a circle, centered on where the caster stands that lasts for 30 seconds and grants a +35% (+20% in PvP) increase to all Magic damage dealt while standing inside of it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
Since all Magic damage, not only that from Sorceries, is increased, other powerful sources of Magic damage such as the incantation Glintstone Breath and the unique skill Sorcery of the Crozier from the Watchdog's Staff Colossal Weapon benefit greatly from it.

The buff is unique, meaning it stacks with any other buff used. Additionally, since the buff only matters at the time the damage is inflicted, the damage increase is granted even if the spell, skill, or consumable is used outside of the affected area as long as the caster stands in the sigil when it hits.

Due to the limited area of effect where the buff is granted it can be difficult to make use of the effect except in ambushes and the starting moments of a fight.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The ground-bound sigil of this is Sorcery is the same as the one created when casting basic Glintstone Sorceries such as Glintstone Pebble and Glintstone Arc.
- This spell's name was Terra Magicus upon release but was changed to Terra Magica at a later date.
- The buffs is applied through what is basically an attack that deals 0 damage, as can be seen if the Golden Epitaph unique skill Last Rites is used in the vicinity of an already created Terra Magica. This is because the unique skill grants a small amount of flat Holy damage which Terra Magica thereafter applies on each attack.

- Magic Scorpion Charm, talisman that grants +12% (+8% in PvP) Magic damage at the cost of +10% (+15% in PvP) Physical damage taken.

Summonwater Village is a seemingly abandoned settlement in the eastern region of Limgrave. The village is flooded and inhabited by Those Who Live in Death, led by a Tibia Mariner.

In the southeastern part of the village is a cellar, sealed by an imp statue, in which a number of turtles dwell.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Spear Talisman** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Obtained from a chest in Lakeside Crystal Cave, in southern Liurnia of the Lakes.
  - The chest can be found in a demi-human campsite found by following the path in the cave without dropping down, past two braziers through a smaller cave in the back.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Strengthens Guard Counters from Piercing attacks by 15%.

As the damage bonus for Guard Counters with Piercing attacks is already 30%, this stacks with that bonus for a total damage boost of 50%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- As with the regular Guard Counter damage bonus, this damage bonus is only applied if a target is attack in the middle of an attack animation.
- Note that the important bit is not that the attack made is a thrust, but that the damage it deals is Pierce damage.
  - This leads to some seemingly unexpected synergy with the Lucerne, Pickaxe, Rusted Anchor, and Warpick as all their attacks deal Pierce damage despite not looking the part.
- Skills such as Giant Hunt deal heavy Pierce damage, giving synergy with the Shard of Alexander and the like, and many weapons also reserve their Pierce damage for their heavy attacks, giving some combination potential with the Axe Talisman.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - The icon is that of a Godrick Soldier Helm or Leyndell Soldier Helm and an unknown Spear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Talismans** are special items in Elden Ring. They can be equipped to provide a variety of effects.

Note that talismans with variants (like +1 or +2 after the name) will only allow one of these to be equipped at a time, so one can't equip both Arsenal Charm and Arsenal Charm +1, even if one has enough talisman slots for both.

You begin the game with the ability to equip 1 talisman at a time. This number can be increased by acquiring Talisman Pouches.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Surge, O Flame!** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Fire Monk incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for  5,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Fire Monks' Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
  - <font color="red">WARNING:</font> Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Produces a continuous stream of Fire with an Attack Power equal to 51% of Incantation Scaling, hitting once per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  1 FP per cast and continues to quickly drain FP in 1-point increments as long as it is maintained.
- Costs  2 Stamina every time FP is consumed.
- Deals 1 Stance damage per hit.
- Can be cast while moving.
- Cannot be charged, but holding the button sustains the fire stream until FP is depleted.
- Resets the Frostbite status effect.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- This spell has limited damage potential due to its low Attack Power multiplier and extremely high rate of FP consumption.
- It can be cast continuously when paired with the Cerulean Hidden Tear.
- Frostbite builds can use this spell as a relatively quick and inexpensive method to clear the Frostbite ailment from targets, allowing them to reapply it for additional damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- In Update 1.07, the continuous FP drain was reduced from 1 to 0, effectively lowering the FP cost from 1(1) to 1(0).
  - In Update 1.07.1, the change was reverted, increasing the continuous FP drain from 0 back to 1.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Stormhawk Deenh** is a spirit ash in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: Found in the Chapel of Anticipation. After returning to the area via the portal at The Four Belfries, go through the previously locked door near the main entrance, and follow the staircase into the upper level of the chapel to find the ashes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.
- Summons a brown Stormhawk.
- Deals Standard damage.
- Will immediately let out a war cry that functions as an Aura Buff to strengthen itself and its summoner by increasing all Physical damage, Stamina damage against blocking, and Stance damage by 20% for 60 seconds. This war cry will periodically be reused.
- While it has fairly low health, the evasiveness of its flying and its tendency to use divebomb attacks instead of simply hanging around in melee range causes Deenh to actually have pretty good survivability.
  - This divebomb attack can actually deflect projectiles (if only very rarely) and will knock human-sized enemies over.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Patch 1.13: Increased HP and physical attack power. Will no longer stagger as easily. Increased duration of effect to increase the attack power given to allies.
  - Increased the duration of the Aura Buff from 30 seconds to 60 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Sorcerer Thops** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A former student of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, Thops was considered a "bluntstone", lacking any talent for sorcery, yet he looked up to Sorceress Sellen prior to her expulsion from the Academy.

When the Shattering broke out, the Academy declared that they would not interfere with the conflict, and the scholars cast repelling seals on the gates. Thops was outside the Academy's grounds when the seals were cast, and thus found himself unable to return.

Thops encounters the Tarnished at the Church of Irith in Liurnia of the Lakes, just beyond Stormveil Castle. He offers to share his limited knowledge of sorceries with them in return for a small donation, and advises them to seek out an Academy Glintstone Key so that they can access the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Should the Tarnished find a second Glintstone Key, they may offer it to Thops, allowing him to finally return to the Academy. Shortly after returning, he passes away hunched over a desk, however he leaves behind a sorcery which may one day form the basis of a new Conspectus.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Church of Irith
  - Thops can be found at the Church of Irith in Liurnia of the Lakes. Speak to him and agree to donate 10 Runes to unlock his shop.
1. Church of Irith
  - After obtaining the Academy Glintstone Key from within the Academy of Raya Lucaria, return to Thops and hand it to him in order to receive the "Erudition" Gesture. Note that he will not accept the Academy Glintstone Key found near Glintstone Dragon Smarag in north-western Liurnia, as this one is required for you to gain entry to the Academy.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
  - Thops's corpse can be found sitting at a desk outside the room containing the Schoolhouse Classroom Site of Grace. Loot his body to obtain Thops's Barrier, an Academy Glintstone Staff, and Thops's Bell Bearing. Ash of War: Thops's Barrier can now be obtained from a scarab at the Church of Irith.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Unlike other sorcery instructors in the game, Thops cannot be given scrolls to expand his shop inventory.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Unlike many other characters associated with the Academy of Raya Lucaria, most of which have blue eyes, Thops has golden eyes, indicating he has the grace of gold. It's unknown if this has any relation to his status as an outcast of the academy.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: Increases Magic damage negation by 15% (10% in PvP) for 120 seconds upon consumption. This counts as a Body Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Compared to Magic Fortification:
  - In PvE there is a tradeoff, the Liver has greater duration (120 seconds vs 90 seconds) and much lower FP cost (0 FP versus 20 FP) while the Fortification has greater Magic damage negation (35% versus 15%).
  - In PvP the Liver is stronger, since these effects have the same strength but the Liver has a greater duration and no FP cost.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Stats and Attributes** determine the player character's gameplay-relevant properties. They can be inspected at the Character Status page, where the game separates them into the following categories:

sections.heading: Attributes
sections.text: These are the 8 attributes that can be increased by leveling up. Some affect base stats.

sections.heading: Attack Power
sections.text:
Depending on the weapon or shield wielded, a specific type of damage is done.

Note that Attack Power and damage dealt is not the same thing, with the latter depending how the former compares with defense. More specifically, if Attack Power is more than eight times as large as defense then damage dealt is equal to 90% of Attack Power while if Attack Power is less than an eighth of defense damage dealt is equal to 10% of Attack Power. If Attack Power is in between these breakpoints damage dealt falls somewhere between these two numbers.

sections.heading: Guard Damage Negation
sections.text: A weapon or shield's ability to reduce incoming damage when blocking.

sections.heading: Damage Negation
sections.text: **Damage Negation** (obtained through armor or items) reduces the damage of incoming attacks. Each Damage Type has a corresponding defense stat and damage negation stat that governs its mitigation.

sections.heading: Defense
sections.text: **Defense** (obtained through stats) also reduces the damage of incoming attacks.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text: Determine the character's defense against Status Effects. Can by increased by armors, Talismans, and items.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Tanith is the consort of Praetor Rykard and the leader of the Recusants, a band of Tarnished who have taken up arms against the Erdtree and vowed to hunt down their own kind. She sits on a throne in the Volcano Manor, located on the summit of Mt. Gelmir.

When Tanith first met Rykard, she was working as a dancer in a foreign land, but soon she became his consort. She became truly charmed by Rykard when he swore himself to blasphemy, being the only human to remain by his side when he was devoured by the great serpent, even refusing to imbibe a Tonic of Forgetfulness offered to her by Rykard, believing there to be no greater distress than to forget him.

Tanith is the adoptive mother of Rya, although Rya believes her to be her true mother, having been told that she was born of the grace of a glorious king. Although they are not biologically related, Tanith professes to care for Rya, whose true name is Zorayas.

The Tarnished first meets Tanith in the entrance chamber of Volcano Manor, accompanied by her Crucible Knight bodyguard, where she offers them the opportunity to join the Recusants. Should the Tarnished accept, they are tasked with hunting down several other Tarnished. After tracking down and killing two Tarnished, Tanith divulges the truth about Volcano Manor, and about Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy.

After the Tarnished slays Rykard, Tanith thanks them, as their victory proved Rykard to yet be weak. She announces that she will leave Volcano Manor, however she instead moves to Rykard's audience chamber, where she can be found devouring the corpse of her lord, wishing to become his serpent so that they can devour the gods together.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
Defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy at any point during Tanith's questline will cause all subsequent steps in the questline to become locked.#Upon entering Volcano Manor, Tanith can be found to the right of the Site of Grace. Speak to her and agree to join the family. Tanith will give you the Drawing Room Key.
1. Go into the corridor to the right of Tanith and open the first door on the left. Pick up the Letter from Volcano Manor on the table as well as the Recusant Finger.
1. Travel to the entrance to the colosseum in Stormhill and interact with the invasion sign to fight Old Knight Istvan. After defeating him, report back to Tanith to obtain Magma Shot.
1. Go back to the drawing room and pick up the Letter from Volcano Manor. Travel to Altus Plateau and find an invasion sign at the bottom of the gorge leading to Shaded Castle. Interact with the sign to fight Rileigh the Idle. After defeating him, talk to Tanith to obtain the Serpentbone Blade.
1. *(Optional)* If you have advanced Rya's questline and met her in serpent form, and rested at a Site of Grace in the main dungeon area of Volcano Manor, speak to Tanith to obtain the Tonic of Forgetfulness. This step will be locked if you kill Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood, before giving Rya the Serpent's Amnion.
1. Pick up the Red Letter from the drawing room, and travel to the Shack of the Lofty in the Mountaintops of the Giants. Interact with the invasion sign to fight Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood. Report back to Tanith to obtain the Taker's Cameo.
1. Tanith will now offer to send you directly to Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, bypassing the rest of the Volcano Manor. Defeat Rykard and return to Tanith and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Travel to the Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy Site of Grace to find Tanith eating the remains of Rykard.
1. *(Optional)* After obtaining the Dancer's Castanets from Patches in Shaded Castle, offer them to Tanith. There is no reward for doing so, however the Dancer's Castanets will be removed from your inventory.
1. *(Optional)* Attacking Tanith will cause her to die in a single hit. You will then be invaded by Tanith's Knight. Defeating the knight will reward you with Aspects of the Crucible: Breath and the Consort's Set.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Her name is a tribute to British author Tanith Lee, a friend and colleague of George R.R. Martin's. In her 1978 novel, *Night's Master*, one segment focuses on a girl named Zorayas, who was the child of a dictator, raised unaware of her origins.[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanith Lee]

sections.text: **The Four Belfries** is a location and Site of Grace in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Four Belfries sit atop a hill in western Liurnia of the Lakes, north of the Minor Erdtree and south of Caria Manor. Constructed by the civilization that created the imps, catacombs, and Stonesword Keys, the great Belfries are adorned with baldachins and images of the nameless bearded god of the Ancient Dynasty. They are protected by Headless Troll Knights, not unlike the Mausoleum Knights who guard the Wandering Mausoleums.

Three of the belfries host Sending Gates which will allow access to remote regions of the Lands Between, and must be unlocked using Imbued Sword Keys. One such key can be found in a treasure chest at the foot of the northernmost belfry.

A sign is posted outside each sending gate, teasing its destination. The sending gates lead to these locations:

- Chapel of Anticipation (*"Precipice of Anticipation"*): The area where the game began. The player may return to defeat the Grafted Scion if they did not at the start, as well as obtain The Stormhawk King and Stormhawk Deenh.
- Crumbling Farum Azula (*"Crumbling Lands"*): An isolated section of Farum Azula, where the player may obtain a Pearldrake Talisman.
- Siofra River (*"Night Sky Unceasing"*): A cliff overlooking Nokron, Eternal City. The player may fight a Crucible Knight and find a Mottled Necklace.

sections.text: Found at the bottom of the hill, to the south.

sections.text:

  - It may also be the old man found in the stone coffins.
- It is unconfirmed whether these belfries were rung to beckon spirits in a manner similar to Wandering Mausoleums, Spirit Calling Bell, Spiritcaller Snail, and Wraith Calling Bell.
- There is a Fifth Belfry on the Scadu Altus behind Castle Ensis. It leads to a hidden area within the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.

sections.text: The **snowy crone**, also known as the **snow witch**, is an unseen character in Elden Ring. She was the secret mentor of Ranni the Witch.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The snowy crone was a heretical witch who practiced forbidden magic deep within the woods. She taught these cold sorceries to Lunar Princess Ranni in secret, and warned the young Carian to beware the dark moon.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: The snowy crone was described as an elderly woman dressed in clothing as white as the snow itself. She wore a heavy cloak of gray furs and a frozen hat with a wide brim and pointed tip. The blue, four-armed doll inhabited by Ranni's soul was modeled after the crone's likeness.

- The icy, wide-brimmed hat and white robes Ranni wears once belonged to the snow witch.
  - After Ranni resumes her empyrean journey, the Snow Witch set may be found in Renna's Rise.
  - When initially encountered at the Church of Elleh, Ranni will introduce herself as Renna the witch.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Swamp of Aeonia** is a subregion of Caelid.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Before it was the scarlet rot Swamp of Aeonia, the heart of Caelid contained the Street of Sages, a western extension of Sellia, Town of Sorcery, where great sorcerers practiced Gravity Sorcery. Alongside peers Gaea and Gaius, young Radahn learned this potent form of magic from an ancient Alabaster Lord. However, it was fate that the stars would destroy Sellia. After learning all he could from his master, Radahn confronted the stars and prevailed. Following the Starscourge Conflict, the Red Lion was the renowned Starscourge.

The area was later known as the site of the last battle of the Shattering—the Battle of Aeonia. The Redmane forces of General Radahn clashed the invading cleanrot forces of Miquella of the Haligtree. The mightiest Demigods and greatest champions of the era—Starscourge Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella fought each other to a standstill. Unable to match Radahn's measure, Malenia snapped the Unalloyed Gold Needle that suppressed her curse, producing her first-ever bloom of her Scarlet Aeonia. She unleashed her Aeonian Butterflies and gained wings of strength.

In the aftermath, Miquella himself rescued Redmane Freyja, who was striken with rot. He drained the disease from her body, earned her loyalty, and vanished, abandoning Commander O'Neil, Malenia, and her Cleanrot army. Over time, the area was scarlet rot formed a vast red bog that gave rise to ancient Rot Disciples and contemporary Kindred of Rot. A great scarlet rotflower tree grew, and rot ate away at the land like a vicious plague. Later, young Scarlet Buds, offshoots of Malenia, were born of the rot. Sage Gowry cultivates them, taking care they blossomed into beautiful Scarlet Valkyries.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **The Shattering** (破砕戦争, *Hasai Sensō*) refers to the devastating and widespread war that broke out between Queen Marika the Eternal's offspring, and her demigod step-children, after the Elden Ring was shattered.

sections.heading: The Night of Black Knives
sections.text:
During the Golden Age of the Erdtree, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen by Lunar Princess Ranni, who used it to forge godslaying Black Knives. These knives were used by the Black Knife Assassins who, one night, entered Leyndell and assassinated Godwyn the Golden. As the assassins fled the capital, an assassin named Tiche was killed protecting her mother Alecto, the leader of the assassins.

Ranni slew body at the moment of Godwyn's death, causing the Cursemark to break into two half-wheels rather than form a circle. While Ranni died in the flesh, Godwyn's soul alone perished, sentencing him to live in death. His body was interred in the Erdtree's roots beneath Leyndell, where it mutated and warped. Later, the Rune of Death began to spread through the roots in the form of Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death.

In preparation for the fallout of the Night of Black Knives, earlier that same night, Ranni met with her elder brother and co-conspirator, Praetor Rykard. She gifted him a slab of rock inscribed with traces of the Rune of Death, which was to serve as a last-resort foil to Maliketh, the Black Blade, in case a battle between Rykard and Maliketh came to pass.

sections.heading: The Shattering of the Elden Ring
sections.text:
The Night of Black Knives became the catalyst for the Shattering. In response to Godwyn's death, Queen Marika the Eternal used her hammer to shatter the Elden Ring. Elden Lord Radagon, her other half, attempted to repair the Elden Ring, but in vain. As punishment for her offense, Marika (alongside Radagon) was imprisoned within the Erdtree.

Consequently, the shattering of the Elden Ring corrupted the Golden Order, and led to a Great War that would leave the Lands Between in ruin.

sections.heading: The Shardbearers
sections.text:
The shards of the Elden Ring, known as Great Runes, were inherited by Marika's Demigod offspring. Tainted by the strength of the Great Runes, the Demigods warred, with the conflict becoming known as the Shattering.

Morgott, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage who was born as a graceless Omen, inherited a Great Rune known as the anchor ring which houses the base, proving his pedigree as a member of the Golden Lineage and as the Lord of Leyndell. Taking on the moniker of the "veiled lord", Morgott ruled over Leyndell, slaughtering countless champions in defence of the Erdtree under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.

Praetor Rykard, whose noble ambitions had turned to gluttonous depravity, fed himself to the blasphemous serpent after obtaining his Great Rune. His consort, Tanith, established the recusants of Volcano Manor, waging a war against the Erdtree in his stead.

Godrick, a distant relation of Marika whose blood was sorely diluted, escaped the capital by hiding amongst the womenfolk, bringing with him a multitude of treasures including the Mimic's Veil. He hid from General Radahn in Stormveil Castle, and later insulted Malenia, only to grovel for mercy after he himself was defeated at her hands. He turned to the act of grafting in order to attain power, so that one day he could return to the capital.

General Radahn, famed as the scourge of the stars, led the Redmane Knights during the Shattering. They were met in battle by Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and her undefeated army of Cleanrot Knights. They fought to a standstill, until Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot, ending the duel inconclusively. Radahn was driven mad by the rot and was forced to wander the battlefield as a mindless beast, devouring the corpses of those who died during the conflict, whether they be a friend or foe. Malenia, who became comatose, was carried back to the Haligtree of her brother Miquella by Cleanrot Knight Finlay, one of the few survivors of the battle.

Ranni, the instigator of the Night of Black Knives, is said to have cast aside her Great Rune, and its present whereabouts are unknown.

Mohg, known only as the Lord of Blood, began building his dynasty underground in secret. To this end he abducted Miquella from his resting place in the Haligtree, wishing to raise the Empyrean to full godhood and become his consort.However, Miquella never responded to Mohg, no matter how hard the omen tried, and continued to remain asleep in his cocoon.

sections.heading: The First Defense of Leyndell
sections.text:
march upon the Royal Capital|232x232px]]

The First Defense of Leyndell was precipitated by the deterioration of a sovereign alliance. Godefroy the Grafted was captured by Ancient Dragon Knight Kristoff during this conflict, earning the latter the honor of Erdtree Burial. The belligerents of said conflict are not confirmed; however, Godefroy's involvement may suggest that the remnants of the Golden Lineage were the attackers.

sections.heading: The Second Defense of Leyndell
sections.text:
During the Second Defense of Leyndell, Morgott, in the guise of Margit the Fell Omen, slaughtered many heroes in his defense of the Erdtree and engaged in conflict with Radahn.

Whether Morgott actually defeated Radahn is unclear, as his description as the mightiest hero of the demigods would suggest not. Regardless, while the walls of Leyndell did not fall, Radahn survived, and his forces were repelled. Alongside what were apparently Radahn's forces, soldiers of Godrick and Stormveil Castle also took part in the battle.

sections.heading: The Assault on Volcano Manor
sections.text: Said to have been the most appalling battle in the Shattering, the conflict took place on Mt. Gelmir, seemingly between Praetor Rykard's army and the forces of Leyndell. The squalid, the sick, and the blasphemous are said to have participated in this battle, which went on without end. The attackers brought the Jar Cannon to the assault; however, it was discovered that nobody knew how to use it. Most of the soldiers in Leyndell's army eventually became afflicted by Frenzy and seemingly resorted to cannibalism, consuming the bodies of the dead. Rykard's own men deserted him following this conflict, no longer able to abide the consequences of his blasphemy.

sections.heading: Godrick vs Malenia
sections.text: Scarcely deserving of being considered a balanced conflict on her journey to face Radahn in the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia and her Cleanrot Knights marched past Stormveil Castle, where Godrick the Grafted and his own forces had been cowering from the Red Lion general. Apparently, Godrick did something to insult Melania, sparking a fight between the pair. Godrick was defeated, and rather than choosing to die in battle, he begged Malenia for mercy. Godrick was spared, and Malenia pressed on to meet Radahn.

sections.heading: The Battle of Aeonia
sections.text: The final act of the Shattering was the Battle of Aeonia, a conflict between General Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella. It occured in the area south of Sellia, Town of Sorcery in Caelid, in a region now known as the Swamp of Aeonia. Malenia and her army of Cleanrot Knights marched southward before arriving in Caelid, where they met Radahn's Redmane Knights in battle. The battle ended in a stalemate after Malenia unleashed her scarlet rot, driving the Redmane Knights to defeat. At the same time, their leader was infected with the rot, which drove Radahn into becoming a mindless beast.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text: Ultimately, none of the Demigods succeeded in becoming Elden Lord, and they were abandoned by the Greater Will. Instead, the guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who were called to the Lands Between to claim the Great Runes, become Elden Lord, and restore the Golden Order.

sections.heading: *Nightreign*
sections.text:
The events of the Shattering in the alternate timeline are likely the same, though the aftermath is entirely different in comparison. In the aftermath of the civil war, a primordial cataclysm known as simply the Night and its harbingers Heolstor and the Nightlords emerged and descended on the Lands Between. As Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring and the Shattering had destroyed order itself, the Night, through the Night's Tide, began plunging the Lands Between into darkness and chaos, drawing forth all manner of monsters and beasts from different realms and eras as perpetual rain threatened to wash away everything.

As the world was alternated and consumed by the Night, the Golden Order ceased to exist. Queen Marika seemed to have disappeared completely from the Lands Between, as she and the Elden Ring are no longer prayed to, though a few churches remained standing. Meanwhile, the Erdtree itself had vanished entirely from the Lands Between, and its golden, radiant hues are no longer visible. Its disappearance, along with the Grace of Gold, prevented the Tarnished from being beckoned by its call to return. The fate of many of the demigods is unknown, but they presumably died out during the Shattering, while only very few, namely Morgott, Godrick and Mohg, were left alive. In response to the growing darkness, a group of warriors from other lands known as the Nightfarers chose to stay in the Limveld to slay the Nightlords and end the Night.

sections.text:
Rykard and his forces were those who wished to oppose all the Erdtree stood for. His armies were assisted by legions of automatons like the Abductor Virgins, the Marrionettes and the Avionettes. After Rykard's transformation into the Lord of Blasphemy, almost all of his non-automaton forces abandoned him, no longer able to abide by the depravity his once rebellious ambitions had become. In their place, to support his gluttonous cause, the sacrilegious union of Rykard and the God-Devouring Serpent brought about the emergence of the Man-Serpents.

sections.text:
Radahn's soldiers were a revered and well trained fighting force that served their lord with unfailing loyalty. Unlike their contemporaries, Radahn's armies were very linear, in the sense they were entirely Redmane soldiers, and were supported by little to no other different forces. However, in the event of the battle of the Second Defense of Leyndell, they were apparently able to coordinate with the forces of Stormveil Castle and Godrick.

Stranded Souls can be found throughout the Lands Between, offering short pieces of dialogue which serve to add context to the lore and story.  These spirits are translucent, and they take on a variety of appearances based on the inhabitants of the Lands Between, such as commoners and Noble Sorcerers.

The Stranded Souls always face directly toward whatever it is they are speaking about.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Localisation Notes
  - Rather than "unwanted child", the soulless demigod(s) of the mausoleum is referred to as Queen Marika's "ugly bastard" or "ugly spawn." (醜い落とし子, *Minikui otoshi-ko*.)
  - The verb used to describe the sun not being "swallowed" in Castle Sol is 蝕まれませ (*Mushibama remase*) which can mean "to be eaten by worms", or more generally "to spoil, to undermine, to gnaw at." This may be a play on words, as 蝕ま (*Mushibama*) is written with kanji that also denotes an eclipse, 蝕.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Sword Monuments** are unmarked locations found throughout the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The sword monuments are clusters of great stone swords verically embedded in the earth, often found near ancient battlegrounds. They were erected to memorialize important events in the history of the Lands Between, inscribed on the largest blades.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The swords that are used in the Sword Monuments are strikingly similar to the Stone-Sheathed Sword, which may be transformed into either the Sword of Light or Sword of Darkness.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Localization Notes
  - The two Liurnian Wars and the Routing of the Ancient Dragons are referred to as 戦役 (*Sen'eki*), which can be read "military campaign" and  "battle", as well as "war."
  - The second line in the First Liurnian War monument says less ambiguously "red-haired Radagon becomes a hero." (赤髪のラダゴン、英雄となる, *Akagami no Radagon, eiyū to naru*.)
  - The "siege" of Caria Manor is referred to as 防衛戦 (*Kōjō-sen*) meaning "defensive battle", the same kanji used to refer to the First and Second Defenses of Leyndell.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
<noinclude>
**Straight Swords** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
They boast decently quick attack speeds, with reasonable range and area coverage for said speed. Their movesets are consistently very versatile and easy to use, particularly when one-handed and dual-wielded. Two-handing may be slightly less reliable compared to the other ways of using them, but its increased poise-damage still gives it uses in certain situations.

Overall straight swords pair exceptionally well with shields and most other weapon classes in general, as their regular attack's wide and fast horizontal swings help cover for potential shortcomings that other weapon movesets might face.

They also have exclusive access to the Ash of War: Square Off, a strong and versatile stance skill that easily breaks open blocks with its light attack version and that quickly breaks enemy Stance with its heavy attack version, leaving even bosses open for a Critical Attack within 2 or 3 hits.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.text:
The moveset mostly consists of slashes, with thrusts on every odd one-handed heavy attack, light rolling attack, every third dual wield attack, and dual wield backstep attacks.

It's important to know when to use one-handed or two-handed light attacks, as the one-handed ones wide, horizontal swings makes catching evasive foes or hitting multiple ones easier, while the two-handed ones more vertical approach lets them hit slightly above the wielder and are much easier to use in close environments where other attacks might bounce off walls.

Some straight swords have different standing heavy attacks: the Short Sword always makes thrusts instead of alternating between thrusts and slashes, the Broadsword and Cane Sword has only slashes on their heavy attacks (and their rolling light attack, which most notably also comes out slightly quicker than normal), the Warhawk's Talon that hits twice with its first heavy attack (both the first and second if charged), the Lazuli Glintstone Sword and Carian Knight's Sword both can block when making or charging their heavy attack in exchange for weaker Stance damage, and the Miquellan Knight's Sword has a dashing slash which goes further when charged.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Stray dogs** are enemies in Elden Ring. They tend to gather around groups of humanoids throughout the world of Elden Ring, adding some challenge to certain encounters.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Strays, like normal canines, often acompany humanoids or form packs. They could potentially be victims of Scarlet rot (Their appearance and prominence in Caelid being a clue) or some form of neglect or extreme metabolism. They are almost always eating some kind of corpse, and are incredibly hostile to the tarnished.

Nonetheless, they have managed to make appearances from Limgrave to Castle Sol being a more common enemy among others. They more than likely serve the same purpose as regular dogs, serving as protectors, companions (of enemies), or both.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Strays (Often just called "Dogs") are canine-like enemies with fast attacks but poor health. They often appear to be either incredibly malnourished or decomposing, often found in Caelid and Crumbling Farum Azula (This "Rotting" appearance is similar to Giant Dogs, perhaps a relation between the two.) They have two major variants, the Stray and the more appealing Noble variant, Although the only major differences are stats and appearance. Two more uncommon variants would be the Bloodied, and Messmer Fire variants.

Their attack patterns can be quite deadly in groups, incredibly fast and punishing if you don't deal with them quickly. They share some similarities to many Wolf variants.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
Stray dogs are found throughout the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, often near human dwellings.

Otherwise they are often found in these areas;

- Caelid
- Crumbling Farum Azula
- Forbidden Lands (Entrance Area and further)
- Altus Plateau/ Leyndell (Both ashen and regular)
- Limgrave
- MountainTops of the Giants. (Castle Sol, otherwise spread out.)
- Consecrated Snowfield

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
Stray's are almost always consuming something, before being interrupted by hostiles or the tarnished. They almost never can be found just wandering.

Despite their grotesque appearance Stray's have strangely normal sounds, easily recognizable despite their condition.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Strength** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Strength stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Strength scaling. In addition, leveling Strength will also increase the Tarnished's Physical Defense.

The Tarnished can level Strength by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Strength has soft caps for raising Physical Defense at 30, 40 and 60 points. Soft caps for Strength scaling weapons varies by weapon type and affinities.

When two-handing a weapon Strength is increased by 50%, rounded up, for the purpose of scaling and meeting weapon requirements. A partial exception to this is paired weapons, such as all Fists and Claws, and the Ornamental Straight Sword, who will not get the boost to scaling. The Starscourge Greatsword, however, still receives the Strength bonus in spite of being a paired weapon.

Note that this Strength-boost also can be applied to Incantations via the Clawmark Seal, but that it doesn't apply to skills with a separate "bullet" attack that scales with Strength, such as Flame of the Redmanes, Ground Slam, or Storm Blade.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Sorceries** (魔術, *Majutsu*) are a medium of spells in Elden Ring.

All sorceries require some FP to be cast and the majority of them require a heavy investment into the Intelligence stat, however, there are still some Faith and Arcane-based sorceries to be found. Sorceries can only be manifested through the use of Staves acting as a catalyst.

The actual damage or effect per casting of a Sorcery is based on a unique stat of Staves called Sorcery Scaling, or SS. The value of this stat for any staff depends on the quality of the staff, its Strengthening level, and a combination of your relevant Stats and Attributes combined with the staff's Grade Ratio for those attributes (primarily focusing on Intelligence). Individual spells will have their Power ratio represented as % SS (such as POWER: 75% SS), which represents the percentage of an equipped staff's Sorcery Scaling value that is used for each shot. Do note that enemy resistances will factor into how much damage you see an enemy take; the Power % shown for attack spells is based on calculations done on unarmored neutral critters in the starting zones.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **St. Trina**, also known as the **saint of sleep**, is an NPC character in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
A pale young girl, delicately swaddled within the nurturing petals of a motherly deep-purple flower, rests her cherubic head on folded arms as she slumbers within her tranquil garden. Purple blood seeps from an unhealed wound on the left side of St. Trina's head, and her plant-like lower body twists into a dark stalk that roots her to the earth. A silvery-white streak graces her flowing purple hair, and the sweet, poisonous nectar she secretes grants eternal rest to those who partake of it.

Her earlier form was that of an alluring young woman with two long braids, yet her destined adult form was considered unsettling. Crowned by a flower with eight petals, this cyclopean deity was expected to a awaken a third eye and eight wild braids of hair that coiled into eddy-like spirals.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: St. Trina is found in a small cave within the Garden of Deep Purple at the bottom of the Stone Coffin Fissure.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
An enigmatic and fleeting individual who held dominion over sleep, some say she is a comely young girl, others are sure he is a boy. The only certainty is that their appearance was as sudden as their disappearance. She was the other half of Miquella, the aspect of his love thanks to his Empyrean nature. The Empyrean and aspect inhabit the same body, much like Queen Marika and Lord Radagon. As Miquella they appeared a small, golden-haired boy; as Trina, a prepossessing young woman with silver, light-purple hair.

St. Trina's love was boundless, offering gentle, intoxicating rest to those she visited in dreams. Some inhabitants of the Lands Between were so enamored that they formed a cult. Light-purple water lilies on the verge of wilting numbed the senses and prevented agitation, symbolizing faith in Trina. Seeking to find her again in their sleep, Trina's followers developed poisonous concoctions to elicit deeper slumber, and some priests were rumored to use sleep-inducing arrows for ritual purposes. Dolores the Sleeping Arrow and Thiollier were among her greatest devotees.

In the final act of the Shattering, Miquella and Malenia mustered an army of Cleanrot Knights and departed the Haligtree for Caelid to confront General Radahn regarding the vow. The ensuing Battle of Aeonia culminated in a duel between Radahn and Malenia, who snapped Miquella's Needle to break the stalemate, unleashing her first scarlet rot bloom. Although she gained wings of strength, fierce Malenia, Blade of Miquella, soon fell into a deep slumber.

sections.heading: Shadow of the Erdtree
sections.text:
wings.]]

During Miquella's pilgrimage through the Realm of Shadow, he stopped at the Cerulean Coast and traveled downward into the Stone Coffin Fissure. Deep underground, the Empyrean stood atop the largest stone coffin and divested himself of his love and adoring other self, casting Trina into the chasm's darkest depths. Liberated from his fate and eternal childhood, he sealed the Fissure and resumed his injurious path to godhood.

St. Trina survived her fall; wounded, flowers burgeoned where her nectar-like blood pooled. Her faint, light-purple slumber mists concentrated into an intoxicating deep-purple fog. Trina blossomed, manifesting deep-purple water lilies and forming her Garden of Deep Purple. The congealed, arcane putrescence of ancient heroes imbibed her poisonous nectar, received velvety eternal rest, and became her gallant Putrescent Knight.

Trina's love for Miquella never wavered, even after her abandonment. Unable to speak directly, her singular wish was to grant Miquella forgiveness in death, knowing that godhood would become his prison. If her wish is granted, Trina withers and dies, leaving behind a single harmless water lily.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.text:
The cult of St. Trina had a presence at Summonwater Village, Forsaken Ruins, and Academy Gate Town. Trina's Lilies grow in abundance at these locations.

sections.text:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- St. Trina was a young adult woman in the story trailer, but appears as a young girl in-game. Miquella was a boy during his flashback, but returns a young man at the Gate of Divinity.
- Her roots are purple, but her eyebrows and eyelashes are white.
- The white in Trina's hair is reflected in Nectarblood Burgeon and St. Trina's Blossom
- Trina's fall displays on-screen while Needle Knight Leda mentions Miquella abandoning his fate in the story trailer.
- The woodland creatures that followed Trina into the Fissure received eternal sleep at the spot from which she fell, arranged in uniform rows, as if herded by Ancestral Followers.
- Horned Owls drop Deep-Purple Lilies.
- Fresh buds also sprout from blood shed by her siblings.
- The path to Trina is protected by * Bloodfiends, Gravebirds, Sentry Stones, and Putrescent Skeletons. In addition to his seal, Miquella left behind the golden spirit of a Misbegotten Warrior.
- The close relationship between Trina and Miquella was teased prior to the release of *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*:
  - St. Trina and Miquella are youthful and elusive figures with complementary water lilies: Miquella's Lily and Trina's Lily.
  - [[Fevor's Cookbook 3|Fevor's Cookbook [3]]] contains the recipe for Bewitching Branches. Blessed with an incantation of Unalloyed Gold, these twigs compel affection.
  - Guarding the approach to Miquella's Haligtree, Albinauric Archers in the Consecrated Snowfield have lily motifs on their Blue Silver Mail Armor and can drop St. Trina's Arrows. Latenna the Albinauric and her wolf companion, Lobo, rest at the Slumbering Wolf's Shack.
  - Cleanrot Knights can drop both Miquella and Trina's Lilies.
  - Slumbering Eggs foreshadowed the Cocoon of the Empyrean and associated nascency with sleep.
- Sleep is often equated with Death.
- St. Trina's unnerving adult form shares many traits with the cyclopian Fell God.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- *Trina* is a feminine inflection of the Latin *trīnus* ("three" or "triple"), affirming her status as a triplet.
- The unmarked location in Altus Plateau where the Amber Starlight is found is internally referred to as "St. Trina's Hideaway", and features a statue of Miquella and his twin, Malenia.
- An additional voiceline was cut from *Shadow of the Erdtree*. If the player visited Trina and drank her nectar after defeating Promised Consort Radahn she would have thanked the player for their deed before finally withering.
- Several early iterations of St. Trina were cut from *Elden Ring* during development.
  - In the  files, **St. Trina of the Cradlesong** sang a lullaby to the Nomadic Merchants, granting them succour by alleviating the Frenzied Flame and allowing them to sleep. After the singer vanished, the merchants left their prison, and soothed themselves by playing the song on their instruments. Later, Merchant Kalé asked the player to collect Slumber Fog with St. Trina's Crystal Ball so he could recreate the effect.
  - In a later version, Reeling Rico used Slumber Fog to produce Dreambrew, an alcoholic potion that revealed secrets. His questline would have concluded at the Cocoon of the Empyrean, where he would have discovered St. Trina was Miquella all along.
  - Intriguingly, the Network Test files lacked Miquella's Lilies to match Trina's Lilies, the  Chinese and Korean versions of St. Trina's Torch describes her as active since ancient times, and there is no reference to apparent gender fluidity in Sword of St. Trina, suggesting that her textual connection to Miquella had yet to be implemented at this point of development.
- Quella, a young boy whose emblem was a sacred tree, was the god of dreams in *Dark Souls II*.

A derelict castle sinking into a poisonous mire in the north of Altus Plateau. For generations, the Shaded Castle was ruled over by House Marais, who served as both executioners and castellans. Maleigh Marais, born sickly like all sons of House Marais, became beguiled by Malenia, claiming to feel her presence when he held the Valkyrie's Prosthesis

Elemer of the Briar, an infamous killer of instructors and merchants, was held in the castle for execution. However, he managed to steal the executioner's sword of House Marais and furnished it with the battle skills of his home of Eochaid, thus avoiding execution. Elemer succeeded in taking over the castle, bringing about the ruin of House Marais. Maleigh Marais can be found wandering the craggy wasteland to the west of the castle.

sections.text: The **Subterranean Shunning-Grounds** are a legacy dungeon in Elden Ring. This area is not drawn on any maps.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Subterranean Shunning-Grounds are connected to Leyndell, Royal Capital and the Deeproot Depths. The entrance to the Leyndell Catacombs can be found within the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. It is in the room with the Giant Crayfish.

An intricate system of sewers and dungeons that spreads out below the capital. It is crawling with all kinds of shunned creatures, most notably the Omen, who are imprisoned there unbeknownst to anyone. The layout is disorienting due to the multitude of tunnels, waterways, and chambers. Deep within the dungeon is a cathedral, where an encounter with Mohg, the Omen occurs. The altar at the back of the cathedral is illusory, and hides a passage which can only be unsealed by killing Morgott, the Omen King in the city above. The passage leads to a catacomb which plunges deep into the earth. It is here that a nomadic tribe was once entombed so as to bury a maddening disease that followed them, and where, in their despair, they summoned the flame of frenzy. The Three Fingers can be met behind a door at the lowest level of the catacomb, provided one removes all of their equipment first.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Starcaller**s, also known as **Meteorite Scavengers** and **Meteorite Seekers**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Starcallers are hooded scavengers who search for rocks imbued with gravity magic left behind by meteor strikes. They are commonly found around craters, digging into the earth with crude pickaxes, which double as their primary weapons. Starcallers also utilize Gravity Stone Fans and gravity-infused Ashes of War in combat.

Their attire consists of filthy hooded robes and simple leather shoes. Multi-colored Rainbow Stones are strung like beads along their waists and embedded in their robes, while a sack of loose netting filled with similar stones is slung over their backs and secured with rope. Equipped with their rudimentary pickaxes, the starcallers work tirelessly to harvest fallen stars and the remnants of their power.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The starcallers were practitioners of gravity-based glintstone sorcery. They traveled to meteor impact sites to harvest rocks imbued with gravitational energy.

After learning gravity sorcery from an Alabaster Lord, Radahn confronted the stars and defended Sellia during the Starscourge Conflict. In the time that followed, falling stars were rare in the Lands Between. For this reason, the starcallers were desperate to scavenge what precious few gravity stone chunks they could find.

  - They've lost access to their own internet and can't regain access.
  - Their PSN or XBOX Live subscription expires and they can't renew it.
  - Or after Elden Ring's online matchmaking servers ultimately shut down.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Sorcery Scaling** is an attack power stat in Elden Ring.

Sorcery Scaling is a stat unique to Glintstone Staves, and increases the amount of damage caused by Sorceries cast by the staff used. The Tarnished must meet the required attribute stats to wield the weapon, or the Sorcery Scaling will be reduced. On the other hand, exceeding the Intelligence requirement will increase the Sorcery Scaling of the staff used. Sorcery Scaling can also be increased by upgrading the Glintstone Staves.

Sorcery Scaling only affects the damage of the spells cast by the staff, and has no effect on the duration of buffs or other sorceries. The Sorcery Scaling of the staff used to attack is the only Sorcery Scaling used to determine the effectiveness of the attack. Having a second staff equipped will not affect Sorcery Scaling on the first staff.

A related and often confused effect is that a very few passive buffs, such as the 30% Gravity Magic damage boost of the Meteor Staff and the 30% damage boost to Invisibility Magic from the Staff of Loss, will apply when the staff with the buff is equipped in the non-casting hand. This increases the damage of the buffed type of magic from the casing staff but does not increase the Sorcery Scaling of the casting staff. The damage buff is applied after the calculation that uses the Sorcery Scaling of the casting staff. This is easily verified by experiment.

sections.text: **Stone Astrolabes** (星見台, *Hoshimidai*, lit. Star Viewing Pedestal) are recurring objects in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Stone astrolabes are hemicyclium sundials—concave, bowl-shaped sundials, resembling a quarter of a sphere—set upon pedestals in areas with an open view of the night sky. They were used by astrologers and their descendants to study the stars, and Starlight Shards often accumulate at their base.

sections.heading: Note
sections.text:
- Most information about Stone Astrolabes is conjectural, based on its visual details and context.
  - The name "Stone Astrolabe" appears in the Messages system among a list of gameplay objects and landmark features. Although the nameless Starlight Shard collection basins don't meet the real-world definition for "stone astrolabe", they're the only recurring objects that fit the general description of an otherwise missing gameplay feature. Their Japanese name, 星見台 (*Hoshimidai*, lit. Star Viewing Pedestal) more accurately reflects their purpose.
- Astrologers and Fire Giants being friends may be explained by the fact that both found common ground in the Sun, one group studying the star closest to the Lands Between with their sundials, the other looking at it through the lens of faith.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Stone Astrolabes were inspired by real-world hemicycliums made from stone.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **The Pit** (also colloquially known as *"The Hungry-Hungry Hole"*) is an unmarked location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
It is a bottomless pit that instantly kills anything that falls into it and is the only one of its kind amongst the surface world of the Lands Between, as every other lethal fall is either tied to coastal waters or mountainous cliffs. It can be found in Limgrave, southeast of the First Step Site of Grace.

Notable for its surprisingly high count of fatalities, the pit is visually distinguished by its eleven crucifixes, three breakable carts, and several flying Man-Bats patrolling its surroundings. The main source of its fatalities is caused by the north and western edges of the hole being geographically higher compared to the rest of the surroundings, obscuring its presence to anyone nearby on its north and western sides, the hazard only being made clear when the player gets dangerously close to the edge.

It is possible to exploit this obscurity in PvP. If one player gets another to chase them, they can bait the chasing player to follow them to the northern edges of the hole and then jump across to the southern side. If the chaser is unaware of the hole's geography, they may either jump too early or too late in their attempt to catch up to the running player, causing them to fall down into the hole and die.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **The Heroic Concept** is a design philosophy followed by Hidetaka Miyazaki and the development team at FromSoftware that shapes the characteristics and themes of certain characters found within Elden Ring's story, primarily the Shardbearers in particular.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The philosophy places focus on characters carrying noble or heroic aspects that become warped and twisted into something malign due the circumstances they've been placed in. Whether it be an inability to handle the power received from their respective great rune, coping with the trauma of a unfortunate event or their fundamental noble principles getting pushed to such an extreme that it transforms into a vice. Either way the source of their personal downfall usually does not stem far away from their once respectable traits.

sections.heading: *Godrick the Golden*
sections.text:
Born a small, frail child amongst his far stronger kin. From his very birth, Godrick was destined for an endless uphill battle for relevancy. From a young age Godrick has beem yearning to prove his worth as a true heir to the Golden Lineage and so he would pursue great varieties of ways to improve himself and his lordsworn army.

However his primary manner of bolstering himself would quickly devolve into piteous scavenging for old relics and stealing and grafting body parts of less fortunate people and creatures alike on to himself and his closest assets.

sections.heading: *Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon*
sections.text:
Once a great Carian queen who led a military that could resist the (at the time) unstoppable armies of the Golden Order. Queen Rennala was intelligent, strong, beautiful and certainly not least, loving.

Her unmatched love would be her downfall though, as Radagon's departure would leave her broken from grief, her unconditional love and dedication to the frail, transient Juvenile Scholars entrapping her within the Grand Library.

sections.heading: *General Radahn*
sections.text:
In his prime, General Radahn was one of the most powerful demigods in the Lands Between, being equally matched in combat against his half-sister Malenia. Most importantly, Radahn was known for his charisma, skill and intelligence in military leadership and battle. Being a noble commander of honor, he inspired confidence in and valued his Redmane soldiers and Knights, which is what earned him their respect in the first place.

However, during the Shattering, the great power of his Great Rune alongside the other Great Runes of the other Shardbearers, drove him to go to war against his fellow kin. This would eventually lead to a battle against Malenia, which ultimately ended in a stalemate when Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot, which drove Radahn to madness, turning into a mindless and feral beast who would feast on the corpses of both friends and foes alike.

sections.heading: *Praetor Rykard*
sections.text:
Once a ruthless justiciar who led an army of inquisitors to ruthlessly hunt and torture heretics, Praetor Rykard descended into blasphemy following the discovery of ancient spells of a long-forgotten snake-worshipping religion on Mt. Gelmir. His increasingly heretic tendencies led him to assist his sister Ranni in the Night of Black Knives, in which Godwyn the Golden was assassinated.

During the Shattering, he became strongly disillusioned with the Erdtree and the Golden Order, finding that the Gods demanding the demigods to fight over the Great Runes (whom he refers to as "miserly scraps of power") as nothing but debasing. Thus, he launched a blasphemous campaign against the Golden Order, establishing the rule of taking by force and the belief that the Gods are no different.

Despite his heresy, many followers were drawn by his ambition, as they also became disillusioned with the Golden Order, and they came to see Rykard's intentions as noble. They then waged war against the armies of Leyndell in Rykard's name, though the results were costly and appalling.

Praetor Rykard eventually lost his sanity and fed himself to the Blasphemous/God-devouring serpent, merging himself with the creature. With his ambition descending into gluttonous depravity, the now-monstrous Rykard began engaging in cannibalism, where he would devour his greatest champions, thus making them a part of his "family".

sections.heading: *Morgott, the Omen King*
sections.text:
Born an Omen, Morgott came to renounce his accursed blood and would seal it away within a blade, which was then concealed within his wooden staff. Following Queen Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring, Morgott secured power over Leyndell, Royal Capital and devoted himself to protecting the capital and the Erdtree from his other siblings, as he considers them traitors to the Golden Order for going against it in favor of their own ambitions.

Despite his deeds, unfortunately, they weren't recognized by many even the Golden Order, who reviled as an accursed fiend. Despite this, Morgott remained steadfastly loyal, as he considers loyalty to be a reward in its own right, and despite knowing that the Erdtree wouldn't admit anyone, not even himself, to claim the title of Elden Lord. However, his devotion and loyalty towards the Golden Order proved to be his downfall as he met defeat at the hands of a Tarnished of no renown.

sections.heading: *Mohg, Lord of Blood*
sections.text:
Like his brother Morgott, Mohg was accursed at birth. Unlike the former, who renounced his Omen blood, Mohg came to embrace it. After an encounter with an Outer God known as the Formless Mother, he established a cult, where he and his followers would perform blood-associated rituals as her servants. Seeking to become Elden Lord, and while recruiting and kidnapping many followers to his cause, Mohg plots to overthrow the Golden Order in favor of his own dynasty, which he calls the Mohgwyn Dynasty.

As he has a strong obsession of his half-brother Miquella, Mohg believes the young Empyrean has the potential of ascending to Godhood, he plans to make him his puppet and rule alongside him as his consort. And so he abducts Miquella from the Haligtree to have him facilitated with blood for his awakening. However, no matter how hard Mohg tried to interact with him, the slumbering Miquella never responded.

sections.text: **Spiritcaller Snail** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Pale, serpentine snails possessing the ability to summon spirits by emitting a ringing sound, akin to a Spirit Calling Bell. They possess limited offensive capabilities of their own, relying on their spirits to protect them. In some cases, they can teleport or turn themselves invisible.

Spiritcaller Snails can summon the following enemies:
- Leyndell Foot Soldier (Leyndell Catacombs)
- Leyndell Soldier (Leyndell Catacombs)
- Wolf (Spiritcaller Cave)
- Inaba, Disciple of Okina (Spiritcaller Cave)
- Crystalian (Miquella's Haligtree)

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: A Spiritcaller Snail encountered at the end of Road's End Catacombs in Liurnia of the Lakes. It summons the spirits of Crucible Knights to defend it. It can only summon one at a time, and will alternate between sword and spear varieties. The snail itself is effectively invisible, but can be detected by looking for a glowing patch on the ground. It will teleport to another part of the room after being hit a few times. It can be killed without engaging with the Crucible Knight summons, by pursuing the snail.

**Smoldering Walls** are perpetually burning stone walls found throughout Caelid. Constructed by the Redmanes after the Battle of Aeonia in an effort to suppress the spread of the Scarlet Rot.

They are lined in several layers throughout the land, with several walls barricading the entrances to Fort Gael and Redmane Castle. One extremely long wall can be found crossing the entire midsection of the western countryside and across the southern edges of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Another smaller wall found west of Rotview Balcony, marking the border between Limgrave and Caelid and acting as an ominous warning to outsiders of the dangers lurking within the rot-infested land.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Guilty**, also known as **exiled criminals**, are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Guilty are convicted criminals of the Lands Between. They are often punished through crucifixion, imprisonment, exile, execution and most iconic of all, marked with briars that coil around their bodies, many having their eyes gouged out by their razor-sharp thorns. Several of these blinded subjects eventually discovered the blood star as they lived in their eternal darkness.

sections.heading: The Crucified
sections.text:
Crucified subjects can be found all over the Lands Between, though most notably in Limgrave and Altus Plateau. Mimicking the subjugation of Queen Marika, they have their hands nailed to a wooden board in the shape of a Rune Arc for an undisclosed (if not infinite) amount of time. They usually either wear a simple plain garb and trousers along with a hood with a collar made of sharpened branches. Or no clothes at all, their bodies visibly burned and charred. The former being sentenced for lesser, petty crimes and the latter likely for more severe indictments. Queen Marika has also been sentenced to this punishment, though she has been strung up to an actual, enormous rune arc.

The crucified of Limgrave are completely inert during daytime, but spring to life with horrific cries of pain and agony during the night.

While the crucifixes near Dominula don't have anyone hanging on them, they have been uniquely decorated with pink flowers by the local inhabitants. Due to their allegiance to the local Godskin Apostle it's likely done in mockery of the Queen's image and and may serve as a celebration of her suffering.

sections.heading: Briars of Sin
sections.text:
While briars are used as a means of punishment conducted by a figure of authority. They do curiously seem to appear on their own in environments inhabited by either a great number of criminals or by a single criminal convicted of a particularly heinous sin.

Notable locations infested by briars include:
- Stormveil Castle, with it's myriad of Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights likely serving as their penal colony with it's location at the fringes of the Lands Between.
- Flame Peak with it's graveyard of fallen Fire Giants and serving as the site that would allow for the commitment of the Golden Order's first cardinal sin, the burning of the Erdtree.
- The entrance of the Erdtree itself, which serves as the prison of Queen Marika for her crime of shattering the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: The Blood Star
sections.text: An unknown entity perceived by those blinded by thorns. It's powers appears to manifest in the form of bloodthorn sorceries and the creation of red glintstone through the blood of sacrifices, allowing staves infused with such stones to scale with one's Faith at the complete abandonment of Intelligence. Earning its practitioners of Aberrant Sorceries the ire of the academy scholars as well.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Stormveil** was a faction mentioned in Elden Ring. Not to be confused with the stronghold of the same name, the members of Stormveil were the ancient, original inhabitants and operators of Stormveil Castle. Known for the development of their unique storm-based battle arts, channeling the power of the ceaseless winds that encircled their home.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
, before receiving its current decor]]
Long ago, when Stormveil's winds were unmatched, its people allied with mighty Stormhawks—formidable warriors shaped by the raging cyclones around them. The cries of their strongest hawks emboldened comrades in battle, while the winds they carried could tear through foes. The faction was led by the proud and revered Stormhawk King and later by the Storm Lord, though these entities may be the same. From their fortress on Stormhill, they oversaw all of Limgrave and the Weeping Peninsula.

During the Age of the Erdtree, the armies of the Golden Order attacked Stormveil. The Storm Lord was ultimately defeated in solo combat by Lord Godfrey. Stormveil Castle was later claimed by the Golden Order and repurposed as a penal colony for Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights. These outcasts attempted to continue the castle's traditions, but lacked the skill of its original masters. Their stormhawks and even the castle's surrounding winds weakened over time. Unable to train the birds in storm arts, they resorted to grafting weapons onto them—a practice that killed many.

The castle's condition worsened further under the rule of Godrick the Grafted.

Nepheli Loux, Warrior can claim the title of Lord of Limgrave.

There is a variant that looks like an inflated balloon. When aggressors come too close, it expands and explodes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Starscourge Conflict** refers the clash between General Radahn and the stars of the night sky. Commonly described as a completely one-sided battle in Radahn's favor, the conclusion of this confrontation would earn the young warrior the title of "Starscourge" (星砕きの *"Hoshi-Kudaki"* literally meaning "star crusher" or "star smasher"), secure the safety of the town of sorcery, Sellia and would fetter the very movement of the stars, halting the fates they'd ordain for their subjects, which would include the fate of Lunar Princess Ranni, Radahn's own sister. From this day onward, only when Radahn has fully perished, will the stars ever dare to resume their movements.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Found in a treasure chest in the western Ancient Ruins.

If you have the Ancient Ruins, Grand Stairway Site of Grace unlocked, start there and take the nearby lift down; then, enter the square passage towards the south by using Torrent's double jump, using the adjacent pile of rocks to gain enough height to do so. Through the passage is a room containing the treasure chest.

If you only have the Rauh Ancient Ruins, West grace unlocked, start there and enter the tunnel to the southwest. Follow the tunnel's left wall until you reach a lift; take it up and then round the corner to the left. Below the cliff is a walkable lattice structure; jump down onto it and follow the path. At the intersection, enter the room to your left, which contains the aforementioned square passage and the elevator to the Grand Stairway grace.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Somber Smithing Stones** (also simply known as *Somberstones*) are Bolstering Materials in Elden Ring, of which 10 variants exist. They are rarer counterparts of ordinary Smithing Stones required for upgrading certain special Weapons.

They can be used by Smithing Master Hewg or War Counselor Iji to incrementally upgrade such special Weapons in exchange for runes, up to +10, consuming one stone in the process. Each "tier" of Somber Smithing Stone can upgrade an armament once, to the same level as the number in their name. Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones are the sole exception to this naming scheme, being the equivalent of a Somber Smithing Stone 10.

However, for ordinary armaments, regular Smithing Stones are needed instead; such armaments can be upgraded all the way to +25, and require 12 stones per 3 upgrades, except for the final one which only requires 1 Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

They can be found scattered through both the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, sometimes looted from certain enemies when killed, or purchased from some Merchants in usually limited quantity. However, excepting Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones, they can be purchased in unlimited quantity from the Twin Maiden Husks after giving them Somberstone Miner's Bell Bearings, of which 4 are scattered throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Sword of Darkness** is a melee armament in Elden Ring, included in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
- Take the Stone-Sheathed Sword or Sword of Light to an altar at either Fog Rift Catacombs or Ruins of Unte.
  - <font color="red">**WARNING**</font>: Once either the Sword of Darkness or Sword of Light has been acquired, though the two forms can be freely switched between by traveling to their assigned altars, the Stone-Sheathed Sword itself cannot be reacquired until you enter the next new game cycle.
  - See the page for the Stone-Sheathed Sword for all 3 altar locations.
  - If the Stone-Sheathed Sword was taken from Fog Rift Catacombs or Ancient Ruins of Rauh, the altar at Ruins of Unte should be used. If it was taken from Ruins of Unte, the altar at Fog Rift Catacombs should be used.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The unique skill, Darkness, sprays streams of Holy darkness in a rotating circle around the user. This takes about 4 seconds to cast and reduces the Holy damage negation for any enemies hit by 20% for 60 seconds. Since this casts quite slowly, taking about 4 seconds to complete, it's best used in an ambush to strengthen any Holy damage attacks used afterwards.
  - The debuff inflicted does not stack with any other defence or attack debuff, except Frostbite. This includes the two moon sorceries Rennala's Full Moon and Ranni's Dark Moon, the Shriek of Milos of the Sword of Milos, Acid Spraymist, and the Soul Stifler skill of the Winged Greathorn.
  - Since the Sword of Light's skill, Light, works as a Body Buff, these two skills work well together to raise the damage of Holy attacks significantly.
- Has identical statistics to the Sword of Light. Only their unique skills and appearances distinguish one from the other.
- A single sword switched between Sword of Darkness, Sword of Light, and Stone-Sheathed Sword forms always has the same level.
  - This means that if the Stone-Sheathed Sword is upgraded to +3 before switching to Sword of Darkness, you will gain a Sword of Darkness +3. If it's then upgraded to +7 it will become a Sword of Light +7 when switched.
- Incredibly bad damage negation when blocking, even for a Straight Sword.
- Note that all swords currently held in one's inventory switch forms when the respective altar is interacted with. Thus, keeping one sword in the item box allows for the dual-wielding of the Sword of Darkness and Sword of Light.
- Scales the best with a pure Strength build but due to scaling becoming less effective when stats are leveled above 54 a hybrid Strength/Faith build performs almost as well. The second, hybrid build will also deal more damage with the skill.
  - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 638 Attack Power (AP), and 45 Strength and 45 Faith grants 622 AP.
  - Note that the high levels of Faith required to wield the sword, a hybrid Strength/Faith build, effectively have 14 more levels to work with. These could either be put in other stats, such as Endurance for more Equip Load or Stamina, or Mind for more FP, but they could also be put into Strength and Faith for more AP. Doing this would put both stats at 52 and grant 642 AP.
