sections.heading: Recreating
sections.text:
Though this beta origin is mostly available in the form of the release version of the Warrior, some equipment has been changed.

The weapons, shield, and ash of war are acquirable in Limgrave: Scimitars can be gained by killing Scimitar-wielding Skeletons at a 2% drop rate (Deathtouched Catacombs is the earliest farming spot) or 1 can be bought from Twin Maiden Husks for  600 Runes or 2 are held by the Warrior Origin as starting equipment, Buckler can be gained by buying it from Gatekeeper Gostoc for  1,500 Runes or by starting as a Bandit, and 1 Ash of War: Storm Blade can be bought from Bernahl at Warmaster's Shack (getting a second one requires a Lost Ashes of War, easiest gained by buying from either the Isolated Merchant at the Isolated Merchant's Shack (Weeping Peninsula) or the Isolated Merchant hidden in Academy of Raya Lucaria).

The Blue Cloth Set can be gained by either starting as a Warrior or bought from the Isolated Merchant hidden in Academy of Raya Lucaria and found by going around the eastern transportation sigil at the  Main Academy Gate Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Suitable Origins
sections.text:
The Warrior is obviously extremely suitable, seeing as it only lacks the Buckler and Ash of War: Storm Blade to have the whole kit.

The Bandit Origin has the shield starting out, can gain the rest of the important equipment relatively easily, and has the stats to use all of it.

The Prisoner, Samurai, and Vagabond Origins also have the stats to use the equipment by default.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
**Unalloyed Gold** is a type of metal in Elden Ring. It was produced and employed by the demigod and empyrean, Miquella, the Unalloyed.

After observing that Golden Order Fundamentalism could not alleviate his sister's sickness, Miquella began pursuing other means of treating her condition. One of these pursuits leading to the creation of Unalloyed Gold, a substance that Miquella would make into a primary design element in the equipment of his army and closest companions.

Repeatedly used as a medium to compel affection and raise faith, one of the primary inventions that enforced the pursuit of this metal were the many prototypes of Miquella's Needle. An artifact that when inserted into ones flesh, had the ability to ward away the meddling of the outer gods. However, even the latest and most advanced model of these needles are still considered incomplete, and could only accomplish this fully if inserted into the flesh while standing in a location that has been untouched by time, the only currently known location being the heart of the storm found in Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Relevant Items
sections.text: **Items related to or referencing Unalloyed Gold**

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - For a metal to be considered to be unalloyed, it needs to have no alloys. An alloy is a collection of minerals that are mixed into a metal's recipe in order to alter it's properties. In other words, unalloyed gold is pure gold that has not been mixed with other metals.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Thiollier** is an NPC merchant in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
A Tarnished, Thiollier was an isolated young man who encountered St. Trina, just once, and was granted the sweet repose of velvety sleep. The remainder of his days would be spent in search of the means to recapture it, despite Miquella's enchantment. He views himself as utterly weak and useless, though he is, in secret, an expert in the realm of mixing poisons. He wears a mask with a tranquil sleeping face carved on it, its silver hair is arranged in the same style as St. Trina's, increasing arcane. Additionally, he has sewn countless needles onto the exterior of his garb for a talismanic effect.

Thiollier touched Miquella's withered arm at the Cocoon of the Empyrean and, alongside other followers of Miquella, entered the Realm of Shadow after the death of Mohg, Lord of Blood. The player Tarnished can help Thiollier create a condensed, somniferous elixir, purported to be capable of putting even an ancient dragon to sleep, although fatal for any mortal. Should his questline be completed, Thiollier can see St. Trina once more in the Garden of Deep Purple.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Thiollier sits by himself, quite some distance from his compatriots, at the  Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace, located on the northeastern border of the Gravesite Plain. He later moves to the Garden of Deep Purple. Thiollier can be summoned as a cooperator against Putrescent Knight, Miquella's Followers, and Promised Consort Radahn.

sections.heading: Shop Inventory
sections.text: Thiollier acts as a merchant and sells various items that hint at Trina's origin.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
**WARNING:** Coming too close to the entrance of the Shadow Keep will lock you out of the first step of his quest, and you will miss the Spirit Ash of Ancient Dragon Florissax.

1. Gravesite Plain
  - Speak with Moore outside Belurat, Tower Settlement.
  - Find and speak with Thiollier at the  Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace.
  - Speak with Moore again and he will give you Black Syrup for Thiollier.
  - Find Thiollier again and he will give you Thiollier's Concoction.
  - After all this is done, approach the Shadow Keep, and you will get an ominous message on the screen. Find Thiollier once more, and after exhausting his dialogue, reload the area, and he'll state he is heading south.
1. Stone Coffin Fissure
  - Make your way to the southernmost point of the Cerulean Coast, where you'll find a pit. When facing south towards the pit, turn to the right; there are steps leading into it. Follow the given path, and you'll come across the Stone Coffin Fissure.
  - Beat the Putrescent Knight, a boss found at the end of this Legacy Dungeon, and in the corner of the arena, you'll find both the  Garden of Deep Purple Site of Grace and Thiollier, in front of St. Trina.
  - Exhaust Thiollier's Dialogue and then reset the area using the nearby Grace. Return and Thiollier will have new dialogue, exhaust it again, and then imbibe St. Trina's nectar, repeating this step (6 times) until St. Trina speaks to you.
  - Once that is complete, pass on St. Trina's words to Thiollier, who will be reluctant to believe these words, and choose to try passing on St. Trina's words again and exhaust his dialogue.
  - After this, return to the Grace. Here you will immediately be invaded by Thiollier, so defeat him and enter St. Trina's garden. Speak to Thiollier, then imbibe St. Trina's nectar again until she speaks. Here you can tell Thiollier of what she has said and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Enir-Ilim
  - Thiollier will now be available to summon for the two final fights of the *Shadow of The Erdtree*'s story, where his quest finishes.

sections.text:

- Thiollier is friends with Moore.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Unique Skill: Darkness** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Sword of Darkness.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Lifts up the sword and sprays mists of darkness in a large, clockwise circle that starts from the left, to deal 310 base Holy damage.

Any enemies hit have their Holy damage negation reduced by a flat 20%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Faith.
- Takes about 1 second to start and then makes one lap of the circle over the course of about 3 seconds.
  - Due to this slowness the skill is somewhat difficult to use in combat and is best used on unalert enemies.
- The debuff inflicted does not stack with any other defence or attack debuff, with the exception of Frostbite. This includes the two moon sorceries Rennala's Full Moon and Ranni's Dark Moon, the Shriek of Milos of the Sword of Milos, Acid Spraymist, and the Soul Stifler skill of the Winged Greathorn.
  - The debuff is applied AFTER the skill hits, meaning it will only benefit from the decrease to Damage Negation if the skill has been used recently on the same opponent.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Velvet Sword of St. Trina** is a melee armament and straight sword in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: From the  Fissure Cross Site of Grace in Cerulean Coast, head north and drop down two stone platforms to a cliff lower down. Inside a Putrescent Rotmound-infested cave to the south is the sword, furthest in.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.text:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: <font color="red">red</font> for Fire damage, <font color="yellow">yellow</font> for Lightning damage, <font color="orange">orange</font> for Holy damage, and <font color="cyan">cyan</font> for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The skill, Mists of Eternal Sleep, has two parts. The first is a fine, purple mist that inflicts 112 Eternal Sleep build-up per second for two seconds, that is also paired with a swing of the weapon. The second is a Weapon Buff that increases the sword's innate Eternal Sleep build-up by 15 for 30 seconds.
  - Since both of these parts happen simultaneously, hitting both the sword and the mist on an enemy immediately causes 169 Eternal Sleep build-up.
- Similar damage and scaling as the Sword of St. Trina, and since they both inflict Sleep buildup, they pair quite well together for dual-wielding.
- Scales best with Dexterity, but unlike with the Sword of St. Trina the Strength- and Intelligence-scaling isn't far behind, and its base Magic damage is far greater. This means that the sword deals roughly equal amounts of damage on a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, a pure Dexterity build, and a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence build.
  - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 534 AP, 80 Dexterity grants 534 AP, and 45 Dexterity and 45 Intelligence grants 522 AP.
- The hilt features a St. Trina carving.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Sword of St. Trina, a version of this sword that hasn't been stained purple

sections.page: Unique Skill: Mists of Eternal Sleep

sections.text: Strikes out to deal damage equal to 160% of weapon Attack Power and throw out a mist that inflicts 112 Eternal Sleep build-up and lasts for slightly more than two seconds, and coats the sword in a Weapon Buff that lasts for 30 seconds adds 15 Eternal Sleep build-up to its strikes.

- Since the Sword of St. Trina already has a base 42 Sleep build-up on its strikes, it gains a total amount of 57 Sleep build-up with the Weapon Buff.
  - The buff is applied before the mist is thrown out, meaning a total amount of 169 Eternal Sleep build-up is applied in the first second if a target both get hits by the swing and is caught in the mist.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **War of the Ancient Dragons**, refers to the conflict in the Lands Between between the forces of Leyndell and the Ancient Dragons.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
During the reign of Queen Marika the Eternal and Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, at some point after the end of the Age of Plenty the royal capital of Leyndell was attacked by Ancient Dragon Gransax.

The immense dragon wielding a giant golden spear managed to fell the walls of Leyndell for the first time in recorded history and wreck havoc upon the city until it was finally defeated, his massive corpse left lying between the Fortified Manor and the lower city. Gransax's assault marked the beginning of the War against the Ancient Dragons.

For the battles to come, the priests of the Erdtree would develop incantations to protect the knights of Leyndell against the lightning of the dragons.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.text:
The dragon's attack on the capital caused some among the Tree Sentinels, the guardians of the Erdtree, to have an epiphany; According to them, the only way to protect the Erdtree was to become dragons themselves. Thus, some of the Sentinels began to emulate the Ancient Dragons in order to provide proper protection for the Erdtree against the new threat. They adorned their armor with dragon imagery and wielding weapons and shields imbued with red lightning, crafted whittling from the claws of great dragon that fell on their city. From then on, these grotesque Tree Sentinels are referred to as Draconic Tree Sentinels.

The last battle of the war happened in the Altus Plateau, outside the outer walls of Leyndell. Godwyn the Golden, the son of Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey, engaged in conflict against Ancient Dragon Fortissax, who had stood out during the war for its usage of twin red lightning stakes and was known as the "mightiest boulderstone".

Fighting with courage, Godwyn triumphed over Fortissax before eventually befriending him and sparing his life. This event marked the end of the war against the Ancient Dragons and their integration into the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.text:
Through his friendship with Fortissax, Godwyn learned to channel golden lightning. and their bond gave rise to the Ancient Dragon Cult in Leyndell. The dragon cult worshiped the ancient dragons and their incantations channeled lightning instead of the power of the Erdtree, but these practices were sanctioned by the Golden Order, as lightning and the Gravel Stones of the dragons were imbued with gold.

The cultists devotedly worshipped the Ancient Dragons and prayed for their golden lightning incantations thus adding another great power to Leyndell's arsenal, although the red-hued incantations remained a secret of Farum Azula, as its prayerbooks never reached the rest of the Lands Between.

Ancient Dragon Lansseax, the sister of Fortissax, assumed a human form and became the priestess for the Dragon Cult of Leyndell to interact with its knights.  Only those loved by the dragons could receive the blessing of their lightning and survive their lightning, with Vyke the Dragonspear being the most favored by Lansseax and able to imbue his body even with red lightning.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- It is possible that during the war, battles between Leyndell forces and Dragons happened even in Crumbling Farum Azula.
  - The Golden Lightning Fortification incantation used during the war is obtained from a scarab rolling the ashes left on the ruined city
  - Golden Runes from 9 to 12, those of people born at the foot of the Erdtree and those of people that first served it, can be found on the ruined city.
  - Two Crucible Knights can still be found fighting Beastmen in the ruined city.
- It is possible that, in the last battle of the war, Demigods or nobles closely affiliated with the Golden Lineage fought and died.
  - The Sainted Hero's Grave, built close to the site of the last battle, implies that champions of holy status were buried in the catacomb.
    - The banners found on the Sainted Hero's Grave display the symbol of the Golden Lineage.
      - Godwyn was the first Demigod to die in "recorded history".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Thorn sorceries**, also known as **aberrant sorceries**, are a type of sorcery in Elden Ring. These Faith-based spells damage the caster to summon cursed Briars of Sin that deal Magic damage and inflict Blood Loss upon their targets. Drawn from the heretical blood star and the forsaken Scadutree, thorn sorceries reflect the agonizing woe of those who wield them.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Thorn sorceries, encompassing both bloodthorn hexes and impenetrable thorn sorceries, embody the torment of their casters. Bloodthorn hexes summon spiraling tendrils of blood, born from the suffering of those who beheld the blood star after their eyes were crushed by the Briars. These guilty sorcerers use smoldering saplings as a catalyst to transform sacrificial blood into red glintstone, a practice reviled by the sorcerers of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Impenetrable thorn sorceries, in contrast, are tied to the holiness of the sacred Scadutree. They were created by those who abandoned incantations after their devout Faith led only to despair. Both forms of thorn sorcery channel the anguish of those condemned by Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Boosting thorn sorceries
sections.text:
Briars of Punishment, Briars of Sin, and Impenetrable Thorns:
- Alberich's Bracers, Alberich's Robe, Alberich's Pointed Hat, and Alberich's Pointed Hat (Altered) each boost the effectiveness of Briars of Punishment, Briars of Sin, and Impenetrable Thorns by 6%.
- Staff of the Guilty boosts the Attack Power of Briars of Punishment, Briars of Sin, and Impenetrable Thorns by 20%.
- Magic Scorpion Charm increases Magic Attack Power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear increases Magic Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes.
- Albinauric Staff and Maternal Staff provide a scaling bonus to Blood Loss buildup based on the caster's Arcane attribute.
- Azur's Glintstone Staff reduces the casting time of sorceries.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Alberich's Robe (Altered) and Alberich's Trousers do not provide a bonus to thorn sorceries.
- Mantle of Thorns does not benefit from effects that boost thorn sorceries but provides considerable damage when rolling, especially when combined with the Briar Armor set.
- Thorn sorceries do not produce a spell sigil when cast.
- Wielded by the Guilty and the mysterious Scadutree Avatars.
- Thorn sorceries impale their targets from below.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- There are four thorn sorceries in total.
- Mad Tongue Alberich was tormented into madness by his fellows at the Roundtable Hold long ago. He wielded cold sorceries and devoted himself to the red glintstone.
- The Man-Serpents of Mt. Gelmir use their faith to cast lava sorcery with red glintstone as the catalyst.
- The Briars of Sin had a different icon during the Closed Network Test for Elden Ring. It featured the spell sigil for Giants' Flame Incantations.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: This page lists **Trees** in Elden Ring, Shadow of the Erdtree, and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Trees held deep symbolic and spiritual importance to the people of the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, particularly to groups like the Woodfolk. The greatest of these trees were suffused with profound holiness, bestowing sacred blessings in the form of soaring grace, Golden Dew, and blessed sap, which dripped from their boughs and hardened into Crystal Tears and treasured amber. These great trees typically grew from potent sources of life energy. For example, Queen Marika used the Crucible to create her Erdtree, and Miquella watered the doomed Haligtree with his divine Empyrean blood. Certain trees manifested stylized avatars to protect themselves and their offspring in times of need. The Erdtree could rebirth or renew its followers through esoteric death rites like Erdtree Burial.

Some individuals gained the power of trees by channeling aspects of the Crucible or by entering pacts with great trees. For example, the Tree Guardians received eternal life to defend the Erdtree and its offspring; the end of their service was said to approach when their buds bloom into blood-red flowers, beginning their slow transformation into trees.

However, the all-female, blind shamans—spirited-away denizens of another world—and their descendants, the Numen, inherently possessed the greatest arboreal affinity in all the Lands Between. Their founding Grandmother formed a small yet significant tree at the Shaman Village, Marika's home, long ago. The flesh of shamans was later prized for its ability to graft and meld harmoniously with that of others. Many maidens were dismembered to create jar saints, while others bulged from inside trees around Enir-Ilim.

Feminine forms likewise manifested in other trees related to Marika or her people, including the motherly womb at the Haligtree Roots and the praying maiden bound by a Cord End inside a blossom sealed within Limveld's secret cave. Just as dried prunings from the Erdtree were snapped in lieu of death, the Cutting-Gifted Tribe atoned for learning the original sin by offering up their young maidens to become Sacrificial Twigs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Many trees on the Mountaintops of the Giants have become spirits.
- The bodies and souls of warriors who receive Erdtree Burial are absorbed by the Erdtree. Art in the catacombs suggests this practice causes new or reborn life to later sprout from the Erdtree.
- There is a unique "root tree" in the courtyard of the Shadow Keep, Church District.
- Bleached willow trees are commonly found throughout the realm of shadow, especially in areas associated with the hornsent.
- , such as those found in Altus Plateau, can regrow their bark once peeled off. The Secret Rite Scroll, which details the Gate of Divinity's workings, was recorded on birch bark.
- Fallen red oak and maple leaves blanket the land at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree and the Scadutree Chalice.
- Fallen oak leaves litter the Deeproot Depths, especially around the hollowed-out tree guarded by Crucible Knight Siluria.
- The Cutting-Gifted Tribe converted their maidens to Sacrificial Twigs to atone for learning the Erdtree's Original Sin. The bound figure in Limveld's secret room is possibly connected to the divine Spirit Shelter.

__NOTOC__

**Weapons**, also known as **Armaments**, are equipment items in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

Weapons scale in power based on the player's attributes. Several weapons can be wielded two-handed, affecting their attack strength and animation patterns. For keyboard controls, the command to switch to two-handed mode is to hold **E** and then click the attack button of the weapon in question.

There are two types of Armaments: generic weapons that are upgraded with Smithing Stones and unique weapons, which are bolstered with Somber Smithing Stones. Armaments may be improved by interacting with Smithing Master Hewg, Smithing Master Iji, or the Smithing Table at the Church of Elleh. Armaments of both types fall into one of four categories: Melee Armaments, Ranged Armaments, Catalysts, and Shields.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **White Mask Varré** (白面のヴァレー) is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Varré is an enigmatic man who dresses as a war surgeon. War Surgeons, despite their name, are not surgeons or doctors. They act as mercy killers on battlefields, putting dying soldiers out of their misery as quickly as possible by delivering final blows. Varré was a war surgeon prior to his association with Mohg.

Varré was abducted by Mohg against his will along with various other war surgeons, however it was noted that Varré was particularly talented with blood incantations, and that of all the war surgeons abducted he was the only one able to "tame" Mohg's cursed blood. Somewhere along the way Varré came to genuinely worship Mohg. If game data is accessed to remove his mask, you can see Mohg's emblem painted on his forehead.

Varré is generally regarded as enticing but deceitful. He is eloquent and is kind to the Tarnished at first, but this appears to be a front as his personality can change dramatically if elicited by disobedience. For example: He will try to suggest he is helping the Tarnished, and refers to them with the pet name "Lambkin", but if provoked he consequently will refer to them as a "runt" and "low born". If the tarnished refuses Varré's offer to join Mohg, then he will indignantly remark that they must have misheard his request, and that he will wait "for your ears to clean out."

Varré seems to also harbor some level of sadism, or in the least, an indifference to the pain of others. He asks the Tarnished to soak a cloth in a finger maiden's blood and remarks that since they have no maiden of their own, "any maiden will do". When he injects the tarnished with royal blood and they scream in pain, he chuckles in a shocked tone and says "clench your teeth, or something". When the ritual is completed he will remark that the tarnished as "the sweetest scream".  If attacked at the Rose church he will remark upon killing the tarnished that "materials of quality are so hard to find these days", revealing that he only ever thought of the Tarnished as a material or tool.

sections.heading: Events in Game
sections.text:
The Tarnished first encounters him in Limgrave, after exiting the Stranded Graveyard, where he offers them guidance, noticing that they are not accompanied by a Finger Maiden. He advises the Tarnished to journey to Stormveil Castle and challenge Godrick the Grafted for his Great Rune, and recommends that they visit the Roundtable Hold.

The Tarnished encounters him again in Liurnia of the Lakes, outside the Rose Church. Here, he tests the Tarnished's dedication to the Two Fingers, expressing his own doubts about the veracity of their words. If the Tarnished shares his concerns, he reveals himself to be a loyal disciple of Mohg, Lord of Blood, and offers the Tarnished the opportunity to join his new dynasty. After the Tarnished completes their initiation, by soaking a cloth in the blood of a maiden, Varré awards them with a medal which will grant them audience with Mohg when the time is right. He also injects the Tarnished's finger with noble blood, allowing them to invade other worlds.

The Tarnished journeys to Mohgwyn Palace where they encounter Varré for the final time, invading his world and defeating him. Varré dies on the ground of Mohgwyn Palace after blessing Mohg's dynasty.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
- Limgrave (The First Step)

Just past the Site of Grace. Will leave a message in his spot after talking with Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold.

- Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)

At the entrance of the Rose Church, to the west of the Site of Grace.

- Mohgwyn Palace (Dynasty Mausoleum Entrance)

His invasion sign is located in the hallway before the Dynasty Mausoleum Midpoint Site of Grace. After defeating him, Varré will be found laying on the floor close to where the sign previously was.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.text:
1. Limgrave (The First Step)
  - *(Optional)* Talk to Varré next to The First Step Site of Grace.
  - *(Optional)* After visiting the Roundtable Hold, return to Varré and exhaust his dialogue.
  - *(Optional)* After obtaining a Great Rune, return to Varré and exhaust his dialogue.
  - *(Optional)* After talking to Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold, read the message he leaves behind to receive the "Bravo!" Gesture.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)
  - As he moves at the entrance of the Rose Church after speaking with Enia, talk to him, selecting **They didn't seem right**, and exhaust his dialogues to receive Festering Bloody Finger x5.
1. Altus Plateau (Road of Iniquity Side Path)
  - Interact with the invasion sign of Magnus the Beast Claw, found at the Writheblood Ruins south-west of the Site of Grace, and either defeat him or simply invade him three times. Invading actual players with the Festering Bloody Fingers three times is also enough to progress Varré's questline.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)
  - Return to Varré to receive the Lord of Blood's Favor, which needs to be coated in a maiden's blood. The followings options are available:
    - The corpse of your Finger Maiden in the Chapel of Anticipation, which requires using an Imbued Sword Key at the Four Bellfries of Liurnia.
    - Vyke's Finger Maiden in the Church of Inhibition of Liurnia.
    - Killing Irina of Morne or, if already deceased, Lightseeker Hyetta at any of their locations.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)
  - Return to Varré to receive the Bloody Finger, then talk to him again to receive the Pureblood Knight's Medal.
1. Mohgwyn Palace (Dynasty Mausoleum Entrance)
  - Reaching Mohgwyn Palace either through the Pureblood Knight's Medal or the Waygate in Consacrated Snowfield, interact with Varré's invasion sign in the hallway right before Dynasty Mausoleum Midpoint Site of Grace. Once defeated, he'll drop Festering Bloody Finger x6, Rune Arc x1 and Furlcalling Finger Remedy x1.
  - Talk to him near where his invasion sign was and, exhausting his dialogues, he'll die dropping Varré's Bouquet.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: They are roving beasts that may attack in packs. The common wolf is widespread throughout the wilds of the Lands Between, almost always encountered in packs and forewarned by its characteristic howl. Their packs are usually led by a tougher specimen distinguished by their color. They are hostile but relatively easy to avoid. They cannot be outrun on foot.

sections.heading: Wolf
sections.text: Grey wolves, the most common variety found in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: White Wolf
sections.text: Larger wolves with white fur. They are often found among packs of standard grey wolves.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Occasionally, wolves can be encountered attacking other entities. Notably, in a gorge near the Third Church of Marika, a large pack of them can be found swarming a Runebear. The wolves will lose handily if the Tarnished does not intervene.
- Three wolves of the regular variety can be summoned using the Lone Wolf Ashes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Wolves that drop from the sky in a gust at specific areas are a literal howling wind.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Wing of Astel** is a Curved Sword, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Found inside a chest in Uhl Palace Ruins above a Withered Astel, located in Ainsel River and only reachable from Ainsel River Main.

More specifically, from  Ainsel River Main site of grace and head down the tunnel. Take the left split in the road, guarded by a Hardhead Giant Ant, and follow the cliffside path to a stone structure with the chest.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Has a 20% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies.
- Standing regular and charged heavy attacks, and dodging while charging a heavy attack also throws out one and two and one Magic beams respectively, in addition to the normal parts of a heavy attack. Since both parts can hit the same enemy, this weapon deals greatly increase damage and Stance damage on hit, at no FP cost.
- This weapon's variant of Unique Skill: Nebula is different from Bastard's Stars.
- The skill's damage is increased by Spellblade's Set (though not the heavy attack beams).
- Cannot be buffed or infused with Ashes of War.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: - Patch 1.09 increased the Attribute scaling of this weapon.

sections.heading: See Also
sections.text:

- Bastard's Stars, the other weapon with Unique Skill: Nebula.
- Founding Rain of Stars, a spell that also creates a dark cloud of stars.
- Frozen Needle, another weapon with a ranged heavy attack.
- Meteorite of Astel, another power of Astel.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Winged Greathorn** is a Greataxe, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Trade the Remembrance of the Regal Ancestor, obtained by defeating the Regal Ancestor Spirit, with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate it (only one can be obtained per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Winged Greathorns are wielded by certain Ancestral Follower Warriors.
- Winged Greathorns are used in spirit worshipping practices of the ancestral followers.
- Likely references Twinbird, Death Rite Birds, Giant Crows, or Ancient Dragons, which all outstretch their wings in this manner. White-Winged Maidens may also be represented here.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Winged Scythe** is a Reaper and Melee Armament in Elden Ring

sections.heading: Unique Skill
sections.text:
- Angel's Wings
  - Jump and imbue the wing-blade of the armament with light, then deliver a slashing attack on the enemy.
  - The white wings impede recovery actions using a Flask of Crimson Tears.
  - The skill only disables using the Flask of Crimson Tears of other players and player-style NPC invaders. Non-player-style enemies, such as Haligtree Knights and Depraved Perfumers, can still heal using their flasks.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
**Location**: Tombsward Ruins
- The Winged Scythe is found in a treasure chest in the underground cellar at the Tombsward Ruins, located on the western Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Winged Scythe can be strengthened to **+10** with Somber Smithing Stones.
- It scales best with Dexterity and Faith, with the latter having stronger scaling. However, it gains 3% more AR on a split Dexterity/Faith build, if somewhat more split between damage types.
- The Battle Art generates sacred White light and soft white feathers.
- An uneven pair of white-feathered wings affixed to an octagonal pole, the Winged Scythe features carved reliefs of bearded elders, possibly depicting the Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues. Robed, bald-headed men, seen elsewhere on Ancient Dynasty stelae and obelisks, stand side-by-side to form a band just below the wing-like blades. Positioned above them is a different bearded figure, his features obscured beneath his dark, shadowy hood, similar to the certain skeleton statues found in catacombs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The skill produces unique white feather visual effects.
- This weapon is superficially similar to the shape of the Ancestral Followers' Greathorn Hammers, horns carved with tree ring-like markings.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Weeping Peninsula** is a subregion located to the south of Limgrave in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Weeping Peninsula is a crescent-shaped landmass at the southernmost tip of the Lands Between. It is named for its unceasing rainfall, which gives the impression of a land in perpetual lament. The landscape is marked by steep cliffs, deep ravines, poison swamps, and a mournful atmosphere.

To the northeast, the Bridge of Sacrifice connects the peninsula to Limgrave proper. A Rosus Statue overlooks the bridge from the east, guiding the dead to the Impaler's Catacombs on the northeastern shore. Nearby, the Forest Lookout Tower monitors the Demi-Human Forest Ruins, and south of Rosus lies both an area struck by starfall and the sorcerous Oridys's Rise.

At the center of the peninsula is a plateau dominated by a minor Erdtree and Radagon's Church of Pilgrimage. The area is home to a Erdtree Guardians and Miranda Blossoms. Rows of ancient black stone ruins flank the plateau, while fallen ruins are embedded in the earth throughout the region.

West of the plateau is Tombsward, where a Wandering Mausoleum tolling solemnly on the plain. This area, and the Fourth Church of Marika, are guarded by a group of Mausoleum Soldiers. A large number of Putrid Corpses aimlessly wander the littered western beach. The Tower of Return rises from the southwest, offering safe passage to the base of Erdtree.

The south is home to Castle Morne, located at the peninsula’s southernmost tip. The road to the castle passes through a demolished stone rampart before reaching its gates. Castle Morne was once the site of a storied battle between a lone revenger and Godfrey, First Elden Lord. Today, it is under the stewardship of Castellan Edgar, appointed by Godrick the Grafted. However, the castle has fallen into disarray following a revolt by its Misbegotten workers.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Undertaker** is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign, one of the two playable Nightfarer classes included in the  DLC.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text: Stats displayed below are for the character at level 15.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.text:
: Confluence — *"Ally's execution of art enables additional art activation regardless of gauge."*

The Ultimate Art Gauge fills and glows purple for **5 seconds** after an ally activates their Ultimate Art. The Undertaker can activate her Ultimate Art during this window, even if her Gauge was previously empty.

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.text:
: Trance — *"Bloodletting triggers the power of the loathsome hex"* (Cooldown duration: **14 seconds**)

Trance has no startup animation and can be activated at any time, even during an animation. Upon activation, Trance instantly applies a self-buff that lasts for eight (8) seconds with the following effects:
- Fully replenishes  Stamina
- +35% to all Damage Negation stats
- +10% Attack Power
- Successive Attacks increase Attack Power by +10% for the remaining duration of the ability (required number of hits varies with Weapon Class).
- Increased  Poise
- Sprint faster and at no Stamina cost
- Quick Dodge — Undertaker can act faster after dodging, but her invincibility during each dodge is reduced. At 30 FPS, her dodge animations have two fewer invincibility and recovery frames when the ability is activated.

Empowered Trance: If the Ultimate Art Gauge is full, Undertaker can fully consume it to empower Trance by holding down the Character Skill input or by pressing both L2 and R2 while holding Triangle (L1+R1+Y on Xbox). Empowered Trance adds the following effects:
- Extends duration from 8 to 15 seconds
- Attack Power significantly increased
- Automatically Dodge

The skill icon drains to indicate the remaining time for Trance. The 14-second cooldown begins when it ends. Reactivating Trance ends the effect early, reducing the effective cooldown duration.

sections.heading: Ultimate Art
sections.text:
: Loathsome Hex — *"Pull out uncanny bone from body, speed toward target, and strike."*

The Undertaker pulls a long spine from her mouth and surges toward her target, dealing damage to anything in her way. This ability allows her to reach her target from great distances quickly and can be activated even mid-air.

The damage dealt by Loathsome Hex scales with player level:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Traitorous Straghess**, also known as the **Dreglord**, is one of the Nightlord bosses included in the  expansion for Elden Ring Nightreign. When its health is depleted, it gains a second health bar by transforming into **Pure Impulse Straghess**.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
Traitorous Dreglord Straghess is a large, staff-wielding humanoid boss formed from discarded corpses. The fight opens with slow, clearly telegraphed attacks, allowing consistent windows for evasion and counterattacks. At roughly 50% health, Straghess enters its second phase. It begins using attacks and spells that inflict  Scarlet Rot and control space or block movement, sharply increasing the difficulty. Straghess also summons Putrid Corpses and Rotmounds that impede and trap the players.

Upon depletion of its health bar, **Traitorous Straghess** gains a second health bar and transforms into **Pure Impulse Straghess**, initiating the third and most demanding phase. Still applying  Scarlet Rot, it becomes a markedly agile and erratic melee attacker, punishing players who overextend or fail to adjust to the faster tempo. Pure Impulse Straghess frequently disengages before re-entering with high-speed lunges and unrelenting attack combos, making sustained pressure difficult to maintain. It enters the fourth phase at approximately half health, at which point it summons pillars of flesh throughout the arena. These obstructions conceal its approach and allow it to trigger a wide explosive attack, forcing players to track its position while remaining constantly mobile.

sections.text: **Valiant Gargoyle** and **Valiant Gargoyle (Twinblade)** are a duo Boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text: A pair of Valiant Gargoyles encountered at the Siofra Aqueduct in Siofra River. One wields a Greatsword and Halberd, whilst the other wields a Great Axe and Twinblade. The latter emerges from the waterfall when the former falls below half its health. They are unable to perform Beast's Roar, instead coughing out a poisonous mist from their bodies.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: The Valiant Gargoyle duo is found at the Siofra Aqueduct, located east of Nokron, Eternal City and the Ancestral Woods. They protect one of two entrances to Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text:
- 30,000 runes
- Gargoyle's Greatsword
- Gargoyle's Twinblade

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text:
- HP: 5,671 (each)
- Defense: ?
- Stance: 110
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to  Strike damage
- Weak spot: Head
- Immune to all Status Effects

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
Since the second one only drops in from the cliffs above once the second gets low on health, it is best to draw the first Gargoyle to the entrance so that it takes a few seconds longer for them to gang up on you.

The poison breath is very hard to see and also quickly causes Physical damage, but it only affects a conal area in front of the gargoyle, so it can be avoided by quickly heading behind it, running away a bit if close enough.

The Putrid Corpse Ashes are very useful for this fight, as even upgraded to just +4, they will keep the attention of the second gargoyle, provided that they are summoned around at around 60% health of the first gargoyle. They are quite tanky, draw aggro very well, and will be summoned at the summoning monument instead of at your side, meaning they will be in the perfect spot to distract #2.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Winged Sword Insignia** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: - Obtained from Stillwater Cave in southern Liurnia of the Lakes, by defeating the Cleanrot Knight boss.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
Increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 3%/5%/10%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point.

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hit towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive).
  - These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land.
  - For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive.
- For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count.
- Can be worn together with the Millicent's Prosthesis to stack the effect, but not with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia.
- Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy.
  - An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice.
  - This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

That is, in some scenarios, performing an additional attack within a sequence would cause attack power to decrease, rather than increase. This could be observed when using the Dagger and Short Sword weapons. This effect could be observed for the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia as well.

sections.text: **Whirl, O Flame!** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Fire Monk incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

**Loot:** Caelid
- Dropped by a Teardrop Scarab in northern Caelid, between the Caelem Ruins and the Rotview Balcony sites of grace. The scarab is located right behind the black carriage containing the Greatsword.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Produces a spiraling stream of fire with a Fire Attack Power equal to 96% of Incantation Scaling. It can hit up to 4 times and pierces foes (though not Guarded Damage Negation).

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 121% of Incantation Scaling and doubles its range.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Costs  19 FP per cast.
- Costs  26 Stamina per cast. Charging increases the cost to 34 points.
- Costs 1 Memory Slot to equip.
- Deals 1.85 Stance damage per hit (7.4 if all hits land). Charging increases Stance damage to 2.8 per hit (11.2 if all hits land).
- The spell can pierce through multiple enemies but is blocked by walls and other solid obstacles.
- If it hits a Guarding foe the damage will be lowered by Guarded Damage Negation but will still hit enemies behind the first one.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.text:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
  - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 26%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 45%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- Effective for hitting multiple enemies due to its piercing effect.
- Large or immobile enemies are much easier to hit multiple times, as they are much more unlikely to move out of the way of the fire stream.
- Deals very low Stamina damage to Guarding enemies, as it will only deal 52 Stamina damage to an enemy Guarding with a 50 Guard Boost shield and all 4 hits land.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Update 1.07: Reduced FP consumption. Increased stamina attack power against guarding enemies. Increased ability to stagger enemies.
  - FP cost was reduced from 21 to 19.
  - Stamina Attack Power per hit was increased from 15 to 20 for the uncharged version, and from 20 to 26 for the charged version.
    - Against players the Stamina Attack Power per hit was increased from 15 to 25 for the uncharged version, and from 20 to 32 for the charged version.
  - Stance damage per hit was increased from 1 to 1.85 for the uncharged version, and from 1.85 to 2.8 for the charged version.
- Update 1.04: Increased damage, decreased recovery time.
  - The Attack Power of the uncharged version was increased from 91% of Incantation Scaling to 96% of the same, and from 106% of Incantation Scaling to 121% of the same for the charged version.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
Scaling is a mechanic in Elden Ring. Most weapons possess scaling values, which cause the weapon's effectiveness to increase in accordance with an associated stat. Weapons can scale with Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith or Arcane. Scaling affinity with each stat is signified by a letter icon on the weapon's information.

Attribute scaling impacts:

- Attack Power
- Sorcery Scaling and Incantation Scaling, with the *base damage* calculated as 100 since the actual damage varies by spell
- Poison, Blood Loss, Sleep, and Madness, if the weapon has Arcane attribute scaling

Scaling doesn't affect poise damage or stamina damage.

sections.heading: Scaling Values
sections.text:
The letter grades that are used to represent a weapon's scaling affinity is only a rough guide of a weapon's potential. These grades are derived from a scaling value, which is an invisible number that determines the exact amount of damage you receive from scaling. The scaling values that each letter can represent are:

- E: < 0.25
- D: 0.25 - 0.5999
- C: 0.6 - 0.8999
- B: 0.9 - 1.3999
- A: 1.4 - 1.75
- S: > 1.75

The formula for calculating a weapon's scaling damage is:

<math>
Scaling value*Base damage\left ( \frac{stat scaling}{100} \right )</math>

*Base damage* is the damage of the weapon before any scaling is applied, and *stat scaling* is a value that is gained by increasing the relevant attribute. Increasing both of these values will also increase the bonus damage received from scaling, which means that a weapon with lower base damage but a higher scaling value will not necessarily gain more scaling.

sections.heading: Attribute Requirements
sections.text:
Most weapons have a minimum requirement for each attribute they scale with. If that requirement is not met, anything that scales with that attribute receives no scaling, and instead takes a -40% penalty.

For example, the Club has 103 base Physical Attack Power, and Strength scaling with a requirement of 10. A character with only 9 Strength would have 61 Physical Attack Power (103 - 42).

sections.heading: Stat Scaling
sections.text:
This value increases as the associated stat increases, varying somewhat depending on if the used affinity is physical (Standard, Heavy, Keen, Quality, or Occult) or non-physical (Fire, Flame Art, Lightning, Sacred, Magic, Cold, Blood, or Poison).

;Physical affinity values
- Stat at 10: 15
- Stat at 20: 35
- Stat at 30: 46.5
- Stat at 40: 57.5
- Stat at 50: 67.5
- Stat at 60: 75
- Stat at 70: 82.5
- Stat at 80: 90
- Stat at 90: 92.5
- Stat at 99: 96

As can be seen, for physical affinities the biggest increase is from increasing a stat from 10 to 20, before falling of bit-by-bit from 20 to 40, then 40 to 50, and then 50 to 80, until it finally slows down to a crawl from 80 to 99.

;Non-physical affinity values
- Stat at 10: 19
- Stat at 20: 40
- Stat at 30: 53
- Stat at 40: 66.5
- Stat at 50: 80
- Stat at 60: 85
- Stat at 70: 90
- Stat at 80: 95
- Stat at 90: 97.5
- Stat at 99: 100

For non-physical affinities, however, the increase is more steady. It still falls of heavily after the 10 to 20 stretch but after that remains steady with the scaling (most notably reaching the same amount of scaling by 50 as physical affinities don't get until almost reaching 70) until reaching 50, where after the scaling slows down to less than half until the stat reaches 80 and halves against for the final stretch to reach 99.

;Spell tools
Spell tools (Staves and Sacred Seals) uses one of three different scaling rates depending on whether or not they scale with only one stat, scales with more than one stat, or if it's the Demi-Human Queen's Staff. The exception to this is the Prince of Death's Staff (PDS) which despite being a Staff that scales with more than one stat uses the more backloaded "one stat" scaling, making it require a large amount of both Intelligence and Faith to attain good results.

More specifically, those that scales with one stat (and the PDS) start strong and gain stronger scaling after reaching 25 in the stat and then again after reaching 60, until finally dropping off hard upon eventually reaching 80 in that stat.

Scaling with more than one stat initially scales rather poorly before skyrocketing to being much, much stronger in scaling for a stat upon getting to 15 in that stat until 30, were after it falls to more normal, "one stat" levels of scaling and then increases become insignificant after reaching 45 in that stat.

The Demi-Human Queen's Staff is effectively the inverse of regular "one stat" scaling with exceptional scaling prior to reaching 20 in Intelligence and then being weaker until it reaches 40 and after that it becomes even weaker.

;Status Effects scaling

sections.heading: Increasing Scaling Values
sections.text:
All weapons increase their scaling values by being upgraded. All weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones gain an extra 8% of their base scaling per upgrade level, while other weapons gain 2% by default.

Weapons that can be infused with ashes of war can gain affinities which alter both the base damage and the scaling values, affecting how different stats increase scaling damage. There is no universal formula for how infusion changes the values of a weapon and different weapons are changed by an infusion in different, seemingly arbitrary ways.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Withered Astels**, also known as **Malformed Stars**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Malformed Stars are insect-like creatures with long bodies comprised of spheres. They have spindly, multi-jointed limbs that end with six-digited hands, translucent wings, and humanoid skulls. Visually, they are almost identical to Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, but the spheres composing their torsos are grey.

Born in a lightless abyss in the far beyond, they arrived to the Lands Between on falling stars. Withered Astels are typically found hanging from the ceilings of caves, and will fire rocks at the player from a distance with Gravity Sorceries.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The Astel in Perfumer's Grotto is also visible from Altus Tunnel and will attack there.

- Very low Stance, easily broken with one or two heavy jumping attacks.

- For the one in Perfumer's Grotto and Altus Tunnel, the former location has direct access to it for either melee or ranged attacks while the latter can only reach it with very long ranged weapons such as Bows. The fight isn't very complicated, with almost no cover and in the Altus Tunnel one can still run up and down the branches while surviving its assault.

- For Uhl Palace Ruins stick close to the walls if taking the lower paths, so its attacks can hit. To reach the platform the Malformed Star is on, head up some fallen pillars to the right and then the cliffside.

- Ainsel River Main is similar to the Uhl Palace Ruins location, except the Malformed Star is already reachable from ground level and does not require any platforming.

- The Fallingstar Beasts are likely another variant of Astel. They have the same face and tails, but the ferromagnetic beasts are covered in stone and iron filings.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Winged Crystal Tear** is a key item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text:
Found at a sap collection basin on top of some cliffs west of Capital Outskirts' Minor Erdtree and east of Hermit Merchant's Shack.
It is guarded by a group of Skeletal Slugs along with an additional Deathbird at night.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: When mixed into the Flask of Wondrous Physick and used, greatly increases the user's equip load by 450% for 3 minutes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- A 450% increase in equip load is effectively the same as multiplying maximum equip load with 5.5.
- Potentially very useful in that it let's the Tarnished combine their heaviest armor with their heaviest armaments while still keeping at a medium load, but also carries the danger of getting stuck in Heavy Load - or worse, Overloaded - should it run out at an inopportune moment.
  - Even with the Prophet Origin's low Endurance of 8 this will boost its maximum equip load from 45 to 247.5, and therefore increase the thresholds for its light and medium loads from 13.5 and 31.5 to 74.25 and 173.25. This makes it possible to carry the heavy Bull-Goat Set and its 63 weight while still keeping a light load and its much longer rolls, if not with a lot of weight to spare.
  - Be wary that unless equip load is kept under 15.6% of the maximum while under the effect of this tear, its effect expiring will send the user straight into heavy load. Additionally, being above 22.2% of maximum equipment load while under the tear's effect leads to being overloaded when it ends.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Yuri** was a character mentioned in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Yuri, the treasured son of a renowned sorcerer, died at a young age and was laid to rest in the quiet cemetery beside the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. Despite his passing, his grief-stricken father, Count Ymir, continued to speak of him as though he still ran about the church grounds. Ymir believed a rotten, tangled mass haunted Yuri’s dreams, and often visited his grave to soothe the nightmares.

Consumed by loss, Count Ymir sought Yuri’s rebirth, attempting to replicate the power of Metyr, Mother of Fingers. Should Ymir become a Mother of Fingers, he ultimately fails in his efforts to restore Yuri’s life.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Yuri's grave is found in the small graveyard attached to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, assemble via the cathedral entrance near Jolán, Swordhand of Night.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Yuri's dreams were troubled a tangled horror. Similar nightmares plagued the Omen.
- They might be a Fingercreeper

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **white-winged maidens** were a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: According to legend, angelic, white-winged maidens were divine messengers of Death. Their holy light delivered a gentler form of death, producing white feathers that impede the restorative power of Sacred Flasks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- They contrast the twinbird and its malevolent, black-feathered offspring.
- The Winged Scythe represents their wings. An asymmetrical pair of white-feathered wings affixed to an octagonal pole, the Winged Scythe features carved reliefs of bearded elders, possibly depicting the Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues. Robed, bald-headed men, seen elsewhere on Ancient Dynasty stelae and obelisks, stand side-by-side to form a band just below the wing-like blades. Positioned above them is a different bearded figure, his features obscured beneath his dark, shadowy hood, similar to the certain skeleton statues found in catacombs.
- They may still exist in the world.
- They might be connected to Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia, the Balancers.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The winged serpents were ever-present companions of Messmer the Impaler that suppressed the power of the base serpent. They were with Messmer when Marika replaced his eye with a seal of Grace. After his eternal exile in the Realm of Shadow, they shared in his terrible fate.

During the Crusade, the winged serpents served as wise guardians and were the token creature of the Fire Knights and Messmer's army. Their likeness is echoed in Messmer's Flame incantations and Fire Knight skills such as *Fire Serpent* and *Flare, O Serpent*.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The winged serpents appear during the boss fight with Messmer the Impaler at the Shadow Keep.
- The Fire Knights highly valued the winged serpents.
- Messmer's Helm is adorned with the image of winged serpents.
- Statues of winged serpents can be found around Prison Town on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Wylder** is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign. He is one of the ten playable Nightfarer classes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Wylder is a Nightfarer tasked with defeating the Night Lord to prevent an impending tragedy in the land of Limveld. His collector card reveals he is a swordsman long in pursuit of the Night Lord.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Armed with a greatsword and a buckler, the Wylder also relies on a wrist-mounted stake driver, capable of launching a grappling hook and priming an explosive stake.  The Wylder wears a blue tunic adorned with arcane sigils over sleek, medium armor. The wing motifs flanking his helmet mark him as a swift and resourceful champion.
- His preferred weapon type is Greatswords, with which he has a unique moveset.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.text: Stats displayed below are for character at level 15.

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.text: The Wylder is a generalist who can fulfill different roles. He is designed for all-around performance, offering balanced defense, offense, and speed stats, making him an ideal choice for beginner players.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.text:
- Passive Ability: Sixth Sense – *"Cheat death a single time."*
  - Wylder performs a special dodge upon taking damage that would reduce his HP to 0; ability refreshes when resting at Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.text:
- Character Skill: Claw Shot – *"Launching grappling claw to rope foes in or move swiftly by retracting."*
  - The Wylder can pull foes in closer with a wrist-mounted grappling hook or quickly avoid attacks.

sections.heading: Ultimate Art
sections.text:
- Ultimate Art: Onslaught Stake – *"Powerful single attack that launches an iron stake with a great explosion."*
  - The Wylder primes a heavy metal explosive stake on his wrist and thrusts it into an enemy. He can also charge it to add a massive explosion for much more damage and stun, as well as hitting multiple enemies.

sections.heading: Starting Equipment
sections.text: The Wylder starts each Expedition with Wylder's Greatsword and Wylder's Small Shield.

sections.heading: Unique Relic Effects
sections.text:

- [Wylder] Art activation spreads fire in the area
- [Wylder] Standard attacks enhanced with fiery follow-ups when using Character Skill (greatsword only)
- [Wylder] +1 additional character skill use
- [Wylder] Character Skill inflicts Blood Loss (Deep Relic)
- [Wylder] Improved Intelligence and Faith, Reduced Strength and Dexterity (Deep Relic)
- [Wylder] Improved Mind, Reduced Vigor (Deep Relic)

- [Wylder] +1 additional Character Skill use

**The Will of the Balancers**

**Grand Luminous Scene**

sections.text:
The following effects are listed in preferred order. Two or more effects on a single relic should be prioritized. If an effect is listed as "Stacks" it means it may be applied to more than one relic and still work.

- Partial HP Restoration upon Post-Damage Attacks
- Taking attacks improves attack power

- Improved Poise & Damage Negation When Knocked Back by Damage

- HP restoration after Greatsword attacks
- Flask also heals nearby allies

sections.heading: Best Deep Relic Effects

- Max HP increased for each great enemy defeated at a Great Church

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: If the Wylder is not selected as the player character, he will be present at the Roundtable Hold. He speaks in a similar accent to the Duchess.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The Wylder and Duchess both have matching characteristics for their starting Chalices (red, red, blue).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Wylder is the mascot for *Nightreign*. He appears prominently on the box art and in marketing materials.
- The Wylder was one of the four heroes initially revealed on December 12th, 2024.
- The winged helmet is evocative of , the Roman god , and Malenia, Blade of Miquella.
- Wylder has several details painted on his clothes, most of which seem Norse inspired:
  - Around the neck is what appears to be a red wolf on a blue forest.
  - Around his thighs is a viking boat.
  - Many runes spread throughout.
- Unlike the other Nightfarers, the Wylder has no crafted appearance beneath his helmet.
  - In fact, among them, he is the only one to not show any ounce of his unarmored self in any of his skins.
  - However, according to the Iron Menial, Wylder resembles the Duchess.
- The color scheme and details on Wylder's Darkness skin appear to be based on Heolstor the Nightlord.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Zamor Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Zamor Knights are tall, slender humanoids with long, silver hair, and ornate masks, who move with elegance and cloak themselves in icy gales. This clan of warriors resides in the Zamor Ruins on the Mountaintops of the Giants and wield rimed curved swords imbued with frost.

They deal  Slash damage and apply  Frostbite buildup. They are vulnerable to  Fire and  Lightning damage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The knights of Zamor have long practiced cold sorceries on the snowy northern mountaintops in devotion to winter. Since time immemorial, they have waged an enduring and bitter feud with the Fire Giants over the Flame Peak. They fought heroically alongside Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey in the War Against the Giants, some of them continuing to serve him, becoming guardians of the Hero's Graves of the Mountaintops and Altus, after the War of the Ancient Dragons. A single Ancient Heroes of Zamor was punished by Radagon and imprisoned close to the beach from where the Tarnished would leave the Lands Between. While the majority of Zamor Knights remained to protect their ancestral home, their Town of Zamor would be ultimately destroyed at some point.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Zamor Knights can be parried and riposted.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Wings of the Storm** were a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Wings of the Storm were Engvall and Oleg, a pair of departed Banished Knights who were known as heroes in the Lands Between. They gained notoriety during the Shattering, their efforts earning them clemency from Morgott, the Omen King, who invited them to join his ranks.

The Grace-Given Lord's offer ultimately split the heroic Stormveil duo. Oleg accepted the opportunity, and slaughtered a hundred enemies under the Erdtree's banner. His glorious accolades warranted Erdtree Burial and, upon his death, an exception was made to grant his spiritual return to the Erdtree. Conversely, Engvall refused, choosing to remain in banishment. He instead became a fringefolk hero, and spent his days running a lordless castle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
The Witch of the Wheel was a practitioner of ancient magic who once dwelled in the Deep Woods beyond the Lands Between. Known for her cunning and deceit, she relied upon guile as both weapon and shield. She was an old companion of the Recluse, sharing in the same arts and knowledge, and in time became the nurse of the Infant summoned by her counterpart. The newborn being devoured without end, and the Witch was tasked with appeasing its insatiable hunger.

During a later clash of armies, the two witches unleashed the Infant as a weapon. The monstrous creature overran the enemy but soon turned upon its summoners. The Recluse failed to offer comfort or embrace to the frightened child, and the Witch of the Wheel was slain in the chaos. Her shadow was shorn away and her essence subsumed, leaving behind a lifeless body.

The Witch of the Wheel was later restored to life at the Roundtable Hold through the power of the Nightlord. In this state, she attacked the Iron Menial and locked him in the crypt, taking his likeness to move freely within the Hold. Her activities drew the suspicion of the Recluse, who eventually detected the Witch’s magic within the Vestige of Night. The Witch's old companion sought her out to atone for her death.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
The Witch of the Wheel appears in the Realm of Remembrance at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold during the third chapter of Recluse's Remembrance Quest. She has disguised herself as the Iron Menial, and is polishing a sword at the Sparring Grounds. Attack and slay the puppet, prompting her to mimic the Recluse's appearance.

She appears again after defeating Heolstor the Nightlord. Visit the bed area where the Vestige of Night was in the ashen Roundtable Hold and embrace the crying Infant. Return to the bed area after the ending. The Witch of the Wheel thanks the Recluse for choosing to love their infant Night.

sections.text:
- Wears the Recluse's Remembrance Garb
- The Witch of the Wheel's magic binds the Night Aspect.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia**, also known as the **Balancers** and **Salvation's Standard-Bearers**, are one of the Nightlord bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign, included in the  expansion.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.text:
The Balancers are pallid maidens wielding victorious weapons. Their armor resembles white flowers. Their faces are similar to Trina's and have white clothes as wings.

However, Everdark Harmonia is drenched in blood. Their clothes are red rather than white, while the wings are very rose-like and bloody. In their final form they emerge as a giant worm-like creature drenched in blood. The worm has the corpses of balancers all over its body, with one in the middle of its face that has a spear.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
Young Harmonia fled into the forest to seek help when ruthless marauders terrorized her small farming settlement. The village girl prayed to a statue of a guardian deity with a weapon raised overhead, and was granted great power. By the end, the village was steeped in red and settled in silence. Harmonia, drenched in blood, stood with a vacant stare and a heroic weapon in her grip.

She became the Balancers, seven white-winged valkyries of the heavens, sent to purify chaos and restore balance to the world.

sections.text:
- HP: 14,160 (solo)
- HP: 28,320 (duo)
- HP: 42,480(trio)
- Stance:
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack when put to  Sleep or after its Stance is broken.
- Nearly all non-empowered attacks can be Parried with relative ease. A single parry triggers a Stagger.
- Weakness:  Strike damage,  Sleep

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.text:
- Damage Types
  - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
  - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
  - A negative value (  ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
  - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
  - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
- The  Sleep status effect is Harmonia's greatest weakness. It is easily inflicted on the valkyries, causing them to fall into a deep slumber that lasts for an extended duration, comparable to that of Godskins. This serves as a means to control their numbers, tipping the scales. Sleeping Balancers are also vulnerable to Critical Attacks.
- Parrying is a valid strategy for Wylder against Harmonia because most of her attacks can be Parried.

- Divine Beast Warrior & Curseblade

**Night 2**:

- Lord of Blood

; **Everdark**

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Open for a critical strike should their stance be broken.
- Vulnerable to shield parries.
- Harmonia's boss clear message is "**Balance Disrupted**."
- Defeating Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia for the first time unlocks the Dreglord expedition. The Balancers kept Traitorous Straghess at bay.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Internal names.
  - Valkyries: **AngelsDaughters**.
- Harmonia's Tree Spirit form (ID: 4641) is a modified Ulcerated Tree Spirit (ID: 4640).
- When resurrected, the Harmonia are held up by their weapons in a manner akin to puppets.
- Harmonia is fully modeled beneath their armor. Their sleeping, cherubic faces strongly resemble St. Trina's, whose eyelids also appear to be bruised.
- Salvation Harmonia's cranial cavity houses a dark seed surrounded by six glowing sprouts—one for each of her clones—during Phase 3. It blossoms into a magnificently red bloodflower during Phase 4, transforming Harmonia into a Tree Spirit in full bloom.
  - Miranda and Malenia, Goddess of Rot also share Harmonia's ability to duplicate and bloom.
- Harmonia's name and botanical nature tacitly imply a Numen Shaman lineage: *"The flesh of shamans was said to meld harmoniously with others."*
- They may be connected to the Formless Mother, since the Lord of Blood is one of her Night 2 bosses. Her Standard-Bearer armor is identical to Varré's Bouquet.
- Their screech attack uses the same sound as the Grafted Scion.
- Salvation Harmonia's grand bloodflower bloom unfurls in the divine "eight around one" pattern.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.text:
- In Japanese, their title is written as 英雄武器の娘たち, which roughly translates to "Daughters/Girls of Heroic Weapons". The term used for them as a group coincides with their young faces.
- In Brazilian Portuguese, their boss name is rendered **Harmonia, Arma Legada**, roughly meaning "Legacy Weapon Harmonia". Here, the title makes it seem that the name refers to the weapons and not the valkyries.
